declarations.name: reflection_principle
declarations.doc:
**Reflection principle, formula by formula.** Given a finite family of set-theory
formulas `φᵢ` with `n` free variables and any set `M₀`, there is a limit
ordinal `α` such that `M₀ ⊆ V_α` and for every parameter tuple in `V_α` and
every `i`, the relativization `φᵢ^{V_α}` agrees with `φᵢ` on the full universe.
Here `V_ α = ZFSet.vonNeumann α` is the von Neumann hierarchy from Mathlib.
declarations.statement:
theorem reflection_principle
    (n m : ℕ) (φ : Fin m → SetFormula n) (M₀ : ZFSet.{u}) :
    ∃ α : Ordinal.{u}, Order.IsSuccLimit α ∧ M₀ ⊆ V_ α ∧
      ∀ (x : Fin n → ZFSet),
        (∀ j, x j ∈ V_ α) →
        ∀ i : Fin m,
          (φ i).realizeIn (V_ α) x ↔ (φ i).realize x
declarations.comment: each formula separately, with `M = V_α`

declarations.name: exists_superset_forall_realizeIn_iff_forall_realize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000G — Reflection principle.** Given a finite family `φ₁, …, φₘ` of formulas of
set theory in the free variables `x₁, …, xₙ` and a set `M₀`, there is a set `M` with
`M₀ ⊆ M` such that for all `x₁, …, xₙ ∈ M`, the conjunction of the relativizations `φᵢ^M`
holds if and only if the conjunction of the `φᵢ` holds in the universe of sets; moreover
`M = V_α` for a limit ordinal `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_superset_forall_realizeIn_iff_forall_realize
    (n m : ℕ) (φ : Fin m → SetFormula n) (M₀ : ZFSet.{u}) :
    ∃ M : ZFSet.{u}, M₀ ⊆ M ∧
      (∀ x : Fin n → ZFSet.{u}, (∀ j, x j ∈ M) →
        ((∀ i : Fin m, (φ i).realizeIn M x) ↔ ∀ i : Fin m, (φ i).realize x)) ∧
      ∃ α : Ordinal.{u}, Order.IsSuccLimit α ∧ M = V_ α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_family_iso_of_size_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000I** (Lemma 3.9.1). For every cardinal `κ` there is a set of schemes such that
every scheme `S` with `size S ≤ κ` is isomorphic to a member of it: here the set is a family
`A : ι → Scheme.{u}` indexed by a type `ι : Type u`.

No hypothesis on `κ` is needed: the schemes of size at most `κ` are among those of size below
`Order.succ (max κ ℵ₀)`, which is uncountable, so `essentiallySmall_schemeSizeBelow` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_family_iso_of_size_le (κ : Cardinal.{u}) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (A : ι → Scheme.{u}), ∀ S : Scheme.{u}, S.size ≤ κ →
      ∃ i, Nonempty (A i ≅ S)
declarations.comment:
The set `A` of schemes is a family indexed by a type in the universe of the
schemes, and `X ≅ S` is an isomorphism of schemes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_size_cutoff
declarations.doc:
For every set `S₀` of schemes there is an uncountable strong limit cardinal `κ` of uncountable
cofinality such that every member of `S₀` has size below `κ`, that is, the collection
`Sch_κ = {S | size S < κ}` contains `S₀`. This is item (1) of Stacks 000J; the complete statement,
with the countable limits and colimits of items (3) and (4), is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeBelow_countable_limits_colimits`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_size_cutoff (S₀ : Set Scheme.{u}) [Small.{u} S₀] :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, ℵ₀ < κ ∧ Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ ∧ ℵ₀ < κ.ord.cof ∧
      ∀ S ∈ S₀, S.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_le_stacksBound
declarations.doc:
If `S` is an object of `Sch_κ` and `T` is a scheme of size at most `Bound(size S)`, then `T` is
an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_le_stacksBound {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ)
    (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ) {S T : Scheme.{u}} (hS : S.size < κ)
    (hT : T.size ≤ Cardinal.stacksBound S.size) : T.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeBelow_countable_limits_colimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000J.** Let `S₀` be a set of schemes. There is an uncountable strong limit cardinal
`κ` of uncountable cofinality such that the full subcategory `Sch_κ = SchemeBelow κ` of schemes of
size below `κ` has the following properties.
1. `S₀ ⊆ Ob(Sch_κ)`.
2. For any `S ∈ Ob(Sch_κ)` and any scheme `T` with `size(T) ≤ Bound(size(S))` there is
   `S' ∈ Ob(Sch_κ)` with `T ≅ S'`.
3. For any countable category `J` (countably many objects and morphisms) and any functor
   `F : J ⥤ Sch_κ`, the limit of `F` exists in `Sch_κ` if and only if the limit of `F` exists in
   `Sch`, and in this case the natural morphism between them is an isomorphism.
4. The same holds for colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_schemeBelow_countable_limits_colimits (S₀ : Set Scheme.{u}) [Small.{u} S₀] :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, ℵ₀ < κ ∧ IsStrongPrelimit κ ∧ ℵ₀ < κ.ord.cof ∧
      (∀ S ∈ S₀, schemeSizeBelow κ S) ∧
      (∀ (S : SchemeBelow κ) (T : Scheme.{u}), T.size ≤ stacksBound S.obj.size →
        ∃ S' : SchemeBelow κ, Nonempty (T ≅ S'.obj)) ∧
      (∀ (J : Type v) [Category.{w} J] [CountableCategory J] (F : J ⥤ SchemeBelow κ),
        (HasLimit F ↔ HasLimit (F ⋙ schemeBelowInclusion κ)) ∧
        ∀ [HasLimit F] [HasLimit (F ⋙ schemeBelowInclusion κ)],
          IsIso (limit.post F (schemeBelowInclusion κ))) ∧
      (∀ (J : Type v) [Category.{w} J] [CountableCategory J] (F : J ⥤ SchemeBelow κ),
        (HasColimit F ↔ HasColimit (F ⋙ schemeBelowInclusion κ)) ∧
        ∀ [HasColimit F] [HasColimit (F ⋙ schemeBelowInclusion κ)],
          IsIso (colimit.post F (schemeBelowInclusion κ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000P.** Let `S` be an affine scheme and `R = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`. Then
`size S = max ℵ₀ #R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_of_isAffine (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] :
    S.size = max ℵ₀ #Γ(S, ⊤)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_le_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
If `S : I → X.Opens` is an open cover of `X` indexed by a nonempty type `I`, then
`size X ≤ max #I (⨆ i, size (S i))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_le_of_iSup_eq_top {X : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} [Nonempty I]
    (S : I → X.Opens) (hcov : ⨆ i, S i = ⊤) :
    Scheme.size X ≤ max #I (⨆ i, Scheme.size (S i : Scheme))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_pullback_lt
declarations.doc:
The fibre product of two objects of `Sch_κ` over any base, which need not lie in `Sch_κ`, is
again an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_pullback_lt {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (hX : X.size < κ) (hY : Y.size < κ) : (pullback f g).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt
declarations.doc:
If `κ` is uncountable of uncountable cofinality, the coproduct of an at most countable family
of objects of `Sch_κ` is again an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) (hcof : ℵ₀ < κ.ord.cof) {ι : Type u}
    (hι : #ι ≤ ℵ₀) (Y : ι → Scheme.{u}) (hY : ∀ i, (Y i).size < κ) : (∐ Y).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_mono_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
The source of a quasi-compact monomorphism into an object of `Sch_κ` is an object of
`Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_mono_quasiCompact {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f]
    [QuasiCompact f] (hY : Y.size < κ) : X.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_mono_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
The source of a monomorphism locally of finite presentation into an object of `Sch_κ` is an
object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_mono_locallyOfFinitePresentation {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Mono f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hY : Y.size < κ) : X.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc: The source of an open immersion into an object of `Sch_κ` is an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_isOpenImmersion {U S : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ S)
    [IsOpenImmersion f] (hS : S.size < κ) : U.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: The source of a closed immersion into an object of `Sch_κ` is an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_isClosedImmersion {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    [IsClosedImmersion f] (hS : S.size < κ) : T.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_openCover
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme with an open covering `S = ⋃ i, U i` and let `T` be an object of `Sch_κ`
such that the index type and every member of the covering are bounded by `size(T) ^ ℵ₀`. Then `S`
is an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_openCover (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} [Nonempty I] (U : I → S.Opens) (hcov : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (hT : T.size < κ) (hI : #I ≤ T.size ^ ℵ₀)
    (hU : ∀ i, (↑(U i) : Scheme.{u}).size ≤ T.size ^ ℵ₀) : S.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
The source of a finite type morphism (locally of finite type and quasi-compact) into an object
of `Sch_κ` is an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_of_quasiCompact {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hS : S.size < κ) : T.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_of_affineCover
declarations.doc:
Let `f : T ⟶ S` be locally of finite type with `S` an object of `Sch_κ`, and suppose `T` has an
affine open covering indexed by a type of cardinality at most `size(S) ^ ℵ₀`. Then `T` is an object
of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_of_affineCover (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ)
    (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ) {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] {I : Type u} [Nonempty I] (V : I → T.affineOpens)
    (hcov : ⨆ i, (V i).1 = ⊤) (hI : #I ≤ S.size ^ ℵ₀) (hS : S.size < κ) : T.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_isAffine_of_mk_le
declarations.doc:
An affine scheme `S` whose ring of global sections has cardinality at most
`Bound(size T) = size(T) ^ ℵ₀` for some object `T` of `Sch_κ` is itself an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_isAffine_of_mk_le (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ)
    (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ) {S T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] (hT : T.size < κ)
    (h : Cardinal.mk Γ(S, ⊤) ≤ T.size ^ ℵ₀) : S.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_mk_le
declarations.doc:
If `#R ≤ Bound(size T) = size(T) ^ ℵ₀` for some object `T` of `Sch_κ`, then `Spec R` is an
object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_mk_le (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ)
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) {T : Scheme.{u}} (hT : T.size < κ)
    (h : Cardinal.mk R ≤ T.size ^ ℵ₀) : (Spec R).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
For an object `Spec R` of `Sch_κ` and a finite type `R`-algebra `A`, the scheme `Spec A` is an
object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_finiteType (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ)
    (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ) (R A : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (hR : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).size < κ) :
    (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
For an object `Spec R` of `Sch_κ` and a localization `A` of `R` at a submonoid, the scheme
`Spec A` is an object of `Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_isLocalization (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ)
    (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ) {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : Submonoid R)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization M A]
    (hR : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).size < κ) : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_subring
declarations.doc:
For an object `Spec R` of `Sch_κ` and a subring `R' ⊆ R`, the scheme `Spec R'` is an object of
`Sch_κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_Spec_lt_of_subring (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ)
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (R' : Subring R)
    (hR : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).size < κ) : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R')).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_Spec_adicCompletion_lt
declarations.doc:
For an object `Spec R` of `Sch_κ` and an ideal `I ⊆ R`, the spectrum of the completion
`R^* = lim_n R/I^n` is an object of `Sch_κ`. As a set `R^*` is the image of a map from a subset of
`R^ℕ`, so `#R^* ≤ #R ^ ℵ₀ ≤ size(Spec R) ^ ℵ₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_Spec_adicCompletion_lt (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ)
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hR : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).size < κ) :
    (Spec (CommRingCat.of (AdicCompletion I R))).size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_lt_of_finiteType_of_mk_le_power
declarations.doc:
For an object `Spec R` of `Sch_κ`, any scheme `X` of finite type over a ring `A` with
`#A ≤ #R ^ ℵ₀` is an object of `Sch_κ`: `Spec A` lies in `Sch_κ` by (9), and then so does `X`
by (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_lt_of_finiteType_of_mk_le_power (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ)
    (hsl : Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ) {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    (hR : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).size < κ) (hA : Cardinal.mk A ≤ Cardinal.mk R ^ ℵ₀)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] : X.size < κ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt_of_lt_cof
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000R (2)** at an arbitrary index type. The coproduct of a family of objects of
`Sch_κ` indexed by a type smaller than the cofinality of `κ` is again an object of `Sch_κ`.

The hypothesis on the index type is what bounds the supremum of the sizes; the index type's own
cardinality is then below `κ` because the cofinality of an ordinal is at most the ordinal.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt_of_lt_cof (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) {ι : Type u} (hι : #ι < κ.ord.cof)
    (Y : ι → Scheme.{u}) (hY : ∀ i, (Y i).size < κ) : (∐ Y).size < κ
declarations.comment: (2), index type below the cofinality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt_of_forall_size_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000R (2) for a family of uniformly bounded size.** The coproduct of a family of
objects of `Sch_κ` indexed by a type of cardinality below `κ` is again an object of `Sch_κ` as
soon as the sizes of its members admit *one* bound below `κ`.

The cofinality hypothesis of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt_of_lt_cof` is there only
to bound the supremum `⨆ i, size (Y i)`, and a uniform bound does that directly. This is the
form needed by a family indexed by the points of a scheme of the site — a set of size below `κ`
whose cardinality need not be below `cof κ` — whose members are cut out of affine opens of one
fixed scheme, so that their sizes are bounded in terms of that one scheme's.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_sigmaObj_lt_of_forall_size_le (hκ : ℵ₀ < κ) {ι : Type u} (hι : #ι < κ)
    (Y : ι → Scheme.{u}) (c : Cardinal.{u}) (hc : c < κ) (hY : ∀ i, (Y i).size ≤ c) :
    (∐ Y).size < κ
declarations.comment: (2), uniformly bounded family at an index type below the cutoff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_spec_tensorProduct
declarations.doc: The spectrum of a tensor product of two contained spectra is contained.
declarations.statement:
theorem contains_spec_tensorProduct (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) {R A C : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R C]
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (hC : B.Contains (Spec (.of C))) :
    B.Contains (Spec (.of (A ⊗[R] C)))
declarations.comment: (9), for a tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_spec_algebraicClosure
declarations.doc: The spectrum of an algebraic closure of a contained field is contained.
declarations.statement:
theorem contains_spec_algebraicClosure (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K))) :
    B.Contains (Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure K)))
declarations.comment: (9), for an algebraic closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_spec_residueField_atPrime
declarations.doc: The spectrum of the residue field of a prime of a contained spectrum is contained.
declarations.statement:
theorem contains_spec_residueField_atPrime (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
    B.Contains (Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime p))))
declarations.comment: (9), for the residue field of a prime

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_spec_algebraicClosure_residueField_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
For algebras `A` and `C` over `R` whose spectra are objects of the site and a prime `𝔰` of
`A ⊗_R C`, the spectrum of an algebraic closure of the residue field of `𝔰` is an object of the
site.
declarations.statement:
theorem contains_spec_algebraicClosure_residueField_tensorProduct (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    {R A C : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R C]
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (hC : B.Contains (Spec (.of C)))
    (s : Ideal (A ⊗[R] C)) [s.IsPrime] :
    B.Contains (Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime s)))))
declarations.comment:
(9), for the algebraic closure of the residue field of a prime of a tensor
product

declarations.name: Sk_of_le_power_aleph0
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000U (2).** For an admissible cutoff `κ`, if `S` is an object of `G-Sets_α`
and `T` is a `G`-set with `size T ≤ Bound(size S) = size(S) ^ ℵ₀`, then `T` is an object of
`G-Sets_α`. This is condition `B2` of `AdmissibleBound` read through `Sk`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_of_le_power_aleph0 {G : Type u} {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ)
    {S T : Type u} (hS : Sk G κ S) (hT : gsetSize G T ≤ gsetSize G S ^ ℵ₀) : Sk G κ T

declarations.name: exists_gsetsBelowCutoff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000U.** For every group `G` and every family `S₀` of `G`-sets there is an admissible
cutoff `κ`, a strong limit cardinal (the counterpart of the source's limit ordinal `α`), such
that the full subcategory `G-Sets_α = gsetsBelowCutoff G κ` of `G-Sets = Action (Type u) G`
satisfies:
1. every member of `S₀` and the left regular `G`-set `{}_G G` are objects of `G-Sets_α`;
2. every `G`-set `T` with `size T ≤ Bound(size S) = size(S) ^ ℵ₀` for some object `S` of
   `G-Sets_α` is an object of `G-Sets_α`;
3. for every countable index category `J`, every functor `J ⥤ G-Sets_α` has a limit and a
   colimit in `G-Sets_α`, and the inclusion into `G-Sets` preserves them.

Objects of `G-Sets_α` are modelled up to isomorphism, by their size, since Mathlib has no
cumulative hierarchy `V_α`; in particular clause (1) holds up to isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_gsetsBelowCutoff (G : Type u) [Group G] {ι : Type u}
    (S₀ : ι → Action (Type u) G) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, Cardinal.IsStrongPrelimit κ ∧ AdmissibleBound G κ ∧
      (∀ i, gsetsBelowCutoff G κ (S₀ i)) ∧ gsetsBelowCutoff G κ (Action.ofMulAction G G) ∧
      (∀ S T : Action (Type u) G, gsetsBelowCutoff G κ S →
        gsetSize G T.V ≤ gsetSize G S.V ^ ℵ₀ → gsetsBelowCutoff G κ T) ∧
      ∀ (J : Type v) [Category.{w} J] [CountableCategory J],
        HasLimitsOfShape J (gsetsBelowCutoff G κ).FullSubcategory ∧
          HasColimitsOfShape J (gsetsBelowCutoff G κ).FullSubcategory ∧
          PreservesLimitsOfShape J (gsetsBelowCutoff G κ).ι ∧
          PreservesColimitsOfShape J (gsetsBelowCutoff G κ).ι

declarations.name: Sk_leftRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (1)**. The left regular `G`-set `{}_G G` is an object of `G-Sets_α`, since
its size is `max {ℵ₀, #G}`, which is below the cutoff by `B1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_leftRegular (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) :
    Sk G κ G

declarations.name: Sk_prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (2)**. The product `S × T` of two `G`-sets below the cutoff, with the
diagonal `G`-action, is again below it: `#(S × T) = #S * #T ≤ max {max {#S, #T}, ℵ₀} < κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_prod (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (S T : Type u) [MulAction G S] [MulAction G T]
    (hS : Sk G κ S) (hT : Sk G κ T) :
    Sk G κ (S × T)

declarations.name: Sk_sum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (2)**. The coproduct `S ⊕ T` of two `G`-sets below the cutoff, with the
disjoint-union `G`-action, is again below it:
`#(S ⊕ T) = #S + #T ≤ max {max {#S, #T}, ℵ₀} < κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_sum (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (S T : Type u) [MulAction G S] [MulAction G T]
    (hS : Sk G κ S) (hT : Sk G κ T) :
    Sk G κ (S ⊕ T)

declarations.name: Sk_fibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (2)**. For `G`-sets `S`, `T`, `R` below the cutoff and equivariant maps
`f : S → R`, `h : T → R`, the fibre product `S ×_R T = {p : S × T // f p.1 = h p.2}` is
below the cutoff, being a subtype of `S × T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_fibreProduct (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (S T R : Type u)
    [MulAction G S] [MulAction G T] [MulAction G R]
    (hS : Sk G κ S) (hT : Sk G κ T)
    (f : S → R) (h : T → R) :
    Sk G κ { p : S × T // f p.1 = h p.2 }

declarations.name: Sk_pushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (2)**. For `G`-sets `S`, `T`, `R` below the cutoff and equivariant maps
`f : R → S`, `h : R → T`, the pushout of `S ← R → T` is below the cutoff, being a quotient
of `S ⊕ T`. The pushout is modelled as the quotient of `S ⊕ T` by the equivalence relation
generated by `inl (f r) ~ inr (h r)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_pushout (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (S T R : Type u)
    [MulAction G S] [MulAction G T] [MulAction G R]
    (hS : Sk G κ S) (hT : Sk G κ T)
    (f : R → S) (h : R → T) :
    Sk G κ
      (Quotient
        (Relation.EqvGen.setoid
          (fun a b : S ⊕ T =>
            ∃ r : R, a = Sum.inl (f r) ∧ b = Sum.inr (h r))))

declarations.name: Sk_sigma
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (2)**. For an at-most-countable index type `ι` and a family of `G`-sets
`S i` below the cutoff, the coproduct `Σ i, S i` with the fibrewise `G`-action is below the
cutoff: `#(Σ i, S i) = Σ i, #(S i) ≤ #ι * ⨆ i, #(S i)`, and a supremum of at most `ℵ₀` many
cardinals below `κ` is below `κ` because `κ.ord` has uncountable cofinality (`B3`).
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_sigma (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (ι : Type u) (hι : #ι ≤ ℵ₀)
    (S : ι → Type u) [∀ i, MulAction G (S i)] (hS : ∀ i, Sk G κ (S i)) :
    Sk G κ (Σ i, S i)

declarations.name: Sk_pi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (2)**. For an at-most-countable index type `ι` and a family of `G`-sets
`S i` below the cutoff, the product `Π i, S i` with the pointwise `G`-action is below the
cutoff: writing `s = ⨆ i, #(S i)`, which is below `κ` by `B3`, one has
`#(Π i, S i) = Π i, #(S i) ≤ s ^ #ι ≤ s ^ ℵ₀ < κ` by `B2`. If `s = 0` the bound is instead
the trivial `s ^ #ι ≤ 1 < ℵ₀ < κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_pi (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (ι : Type u) (hι : #ι ≤ ℵ₀)
    (S : ι → Type u) [∀ i, MulAction G (S i)] (hS : ∀ i, Sk G κ (S i)) :
    Sk G κ (∀ i, S i)

declarations.name: Sk_subtype
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000V (3)**. For a `G`-set `U` below the cutoff and a `G`-stable subset `O ⊆ U`,
the induced `G`-set on `{x : U // x ∈ O}` is below the cutoff, being a subtype of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sk_subtype (G : Type u) [Group G] (κ : Cardinal.{u})
    (hκ : AdmissibleBound G κ) (U : Type u) [MulAction G U]
    (hU : Sk G κ U) (O : Set U) :
    Sk G κ { x : U // x ∈ O }

declarations.name: exists_covTrunc_isSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 000X**. Let `IsCov` be a site on `C` and let `Cov₀` be a set of coverings in it.
Then there are an (infinite) cardinal `κ` and a small collection `𝒯` of index types, standing for
the stage `V_α` of the von Neumann hierarchy, such that the class `Cov(C)_{κ, 𝒯}` of coverings in
`IsCov` with index set in `𝒯` of cardinality at most `κ` is a *set*, contains `Cov₀`, satisfies
the site axioms, and contains a combinatorially equivalent copy of every covering in `IsCov`.

The collection `𝒯` does the work of the limit ordinal `α`: it is closed under the one-point type
and under `Σ`-types of families of its members, which is what the composition and isomorphism
axioms need. The index sets live in a universe `Type (max u v w)` at least as large as that of the
objects and morphisms of `C`; `w = 0` is the case `Type (max u v)` of `exists_covBounded_isSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_covTrunc_isSite
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (IsCov : Covering.{u, v, max u v w} C → Prop)
    (hSite : IsSite IsCov)
    (Cov₀ : Set (Covering.{u, v, max u v w} C))
    [Small.{max u v w} Cov₀]
    (hCov₀ : ∀ 𝒰 ∈ Cov₀, IsCov 𝒰) :
    ∃ (κ : Cardinal.{max u v w}) (𝒯 : Set (Type (max u v w))),
      ℵ₀ ≤ κ ∧ Small.{max u v w} 𝒯 ∧
      Small.{max u v w} {𝒰 // CovTrunc IsCov κ 𝒯 𝒰} ∧
      (∀ 𝒰 ∈ Cov₀, CovTrunc IsCov κ 𝒯 𝒰) ∧
      IsSite (CovTrunc IsCov κ 𝒯) ∧
      (∀ 𝒰 : Covering C, IsCov 𝒰 →
        ∃ 𝒰' : Covering C, CovTrunc IsCov κ 𝒯 𝒰' ∧ Covering.CombEquiv 𝒰 𝒰')
declarations.comment:
The stage `V_α` of the von Neumann hierarchy is modelled by a small collection `𝒯`
of index types closed under the one-point type and `Σ`-types, as a Lean type has no rank; the
truncated class is proved `Small`.

declarations.name: exists_small_abelian_subcategory_with_enough_injectives
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0010**. Let `𝒜` be an abelian category with enough injectives and
`A : S → 𝒜` a family of objects. There is an object property `P` whose full subcategory
`𝒜' = P.FullSubcategory` has a set of objects, contains every `A s`, and admits an
abelian structure for which the inclusion `P.ι` is additive and exact, `𝒜'` has enough
injectives, and an object of `𝒜'` is injective there if and only if it is injective
in `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_abelian_subcategory_with_enough_injectives (A : S → 𝒜) :
    ∃ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒜),
      Small.{max v w} P.FullSubcategory ∧
      (∀ s, P (A s)) ∧
      ∃ (_ : Abelian P.FullSubcategory),
        P.ι.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (PreservesFiniteLimits P.ι) ∧
        Nonempty (PreservesFiniteColimits P.ι) ∧
        EnoughInjectives P.FullSubcategory ∧
        ∀ X : P.FullSubcategory, Injective X ↔ Injective (P.ι.obj X)

A subcategory of a category `C`: a set `obj` of objects of `C` and a set `hom` of arrows of
`C` such that the source and target of every arrow in `hom` lie in `obj`, the identity of every
object in `obj` lies in `hom`, and `hom` is closed under composition.

declarations.comment:

source and target among the objects, containing the identities of its objects and closed under

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_iff_pullback_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0023** (Equivalent definitions of representable presheaf morphisms).
A morphism of presheaves `a : F ⟶ G` on `𝒞` is relatively representable along the Yoneda embedding
if and only if for every object `U : 𝒞` and every section `ξ ∈ G(U)` the pullback presheaf
`h_U ×_G F` is representable.
declarations.statement:
lemma CategoryTheory.yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_iff_pullback_representable
  {F G : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (a : F ⟶ G) :
  yoneda.relativelyRepresentable a ↔
  ∀ (U : 𝒞) (ξ : G.obj (op U)), (pullback (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ) a).IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: Equivalent definitions of representable presheaf morphisms

  the yoneda functor

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_diag_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0024**.
For a presheaf `F` on a category `𝒞` with binary products and pullbacks, the following are
equivalent:
1. the diagonal `Δ : F ⟶ F × F` is representable along Yoneda;
2. for every `U : 𝒞` and every `ξ ∈ F(U)`, the morphism `yonedaEquiv.symm ξ : h_U ⟶ F` is
   representable along Yoneda;
3. for every pair `U, V : 𝒞` and sections `ξ ∈ F(U)`, `ξ' ∈ F(V)`, the pullback presheaf
   `h_U ×_F h_V` is representable.
declarations.statement:
lemma CategoryTheory.yoneda_relativelyRepresentable_diag_tfae
    (F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) [HasBinaryProducts 𝒞] [HasPullbacks 𝒞] : List.TFAE
    [
      yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag F),
      ∀ (U) (ξ : F.obj (op U)), yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ),
      ∀ (U V) (ξ : F.obj (op U)) (ξ' : F.obj (op V)),
        (pullback (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ) (yonedaEquiv.symm ξ')).IsRepresentable
    ]

**Stacks 002M**, curried form: if each `F.obj i` has a colimit, then `uncurry.obj F` has a
colimit if and only if `i ↦ colim_j F(i, j)` has one.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimit_uncurry_iff [∀ i, HasColimit (F.obj i)] :
    HasColimit (uncurry.obj F) ↔ HasColimit (pointwiseColim F)
declarations.comment: curried form: given each colim_j, total colimit exists iff iterated one does

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.colimitUncurryIsoColimitPointwiseColim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 002M**, curried form: when they exist, the colimit of `uncurry.obj F` is the
colimit of `i ↦ colim_j F(i, j)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colimitUncurryIsoColimitPointwiseColim [∀ i, HasColimit (F.obj i)]
    [HasColimit (uncurry.obj F)] [HasColimit (pointwiseColim F)] :
    colimit (uncurry.obj F) ≅ colimit (pointwiseColim F)
declarations.comment: curried form: the total and iterated colimits agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimit_iff_hasColimit_pointwiseColim_curry
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 002M**: for `G : I × J ⥤ C` such that `colim_j G(i, j)` exists for every `i`, the
functor `G` has a colimit if and only if `i ↦ colim_j G(i, j)` has one.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimit_iff_hasColimit_pointwiseColim_curry
    [∀ i, HasColimit ((curry.obj G).obj i)] :
    HasColimit G ↔ HasColimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj G))
declarations.comment: given each colim_j M_{i,j}, M has a colimit iff M_{-,∞} has one

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.colimitIsoColimitPointwiseColimCurry
declarations.doc: **Stacks 002M**: when they exist, `colim_{(i,j)} G(i, j) ≅ colim_i colim_j G(i, j)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colimitIsoColimitPointwiseColimCurry [∀ i, HasColimit ((curry.obj G).obj i)]
    [HasColimit G] [HasColimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj G))] :
    colimit G ≅ colimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj G))
declarations.comment: when they exist, the colimits of M and of M_{-,∞} agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimit_pointwiseColim_curry_swap_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 002M**: if `colim_j G(i, j)` exists for every `i` and `colim_i G(i, j)` exists for
every `j`, then `colim_i colim_j G(i, j)` exists if and only if `colim_j colim_i G(i, j)` does.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimit_pointwiseColim_curry_swap_iff [∀ i, HasColimit ((curry.obj G).obj i)]
    [∀ j, HasColimit ((curry.obj (Prod.swap J I ⋙ G)).obj j)] :
    HasColimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj (Prod.swap J I ⋙ G))) ↔
      HasColimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj G))
declarations.comment: given colimits in both variables, colim_i colim_j exists iff colim_j colim_i does

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.pointwiseColimCurrySwapIso
declarations.doc: **Stacks 002M**: when they exist, `colim_j colim_i G(i, j) ≅ colim_i colim_j G(i, j)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointwiseColimCurrySwapIso [∀ i, HasColimit ((curry.obj G).obj i)]
    [∀ j, HasColimit ((curry.obj (Prod.swap J I ⋙ G)).obj j)]
    [HasColimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj G))]
    [HasColimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj (Prod.swap J I ⋙ G)))] :
    colimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj (Prod.swap J I ⋙ G))) ≅
      colimit (pointwiseColim (curry.obj G))
declarations.comment: colim_j colim_i = colim_i colim_j, given colimits in both variables

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.hasLimit_iff_hasLimit_pointwiseLim_curry

declarations.doc: **Stacks 002M** for limits: when they exist, `lim_j lim_i G(i, j) ≅ lim_i lim_j G(i, j)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiltered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 002V.** A diagram `M : I ⥤ C` is *filtered* (or *directed*) if
`I` is nonempty, every pair of objects of `I` admits morphisms into a common
object, and every pair of parallel morphisms of `I` is equalized, after
applying `M`, by composition with a further morphism.
declarations.statement:
structure Functor.IsFiltered {I : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} I] {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C]
    (M : I ⥤ C) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiltered_id_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 002V.** An index category `I` is filtered in the sense of Stacks —
the identity diagram `𝟭 I` is a filtered diagram — exactly when it is filtered
in the sense of Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.IsFiltered`. Since `(𝟭 I).map f = f`,
condition (3) for `𝟭 I` reads `a ≫ c = b ≫ c` in `I`, so both directions are a
repackaging of the same data.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isFiltered_id_iff (I : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} I] :
    (𝟭 I).IsFiltered ↔ _root_.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered I

registrations.name: PreservesFiniteColimits
registrations.comment: Prop-valued typeclass for right exact functors

registrations.name: leftExactFunctor
registrations.comment:
Part (1), left exact functors: the property `leftExactFunctor C D` of a functor
  `F : C ⥤ D`, which is `PreservesFiniteLimits F` (`leftExactFunctor_iff`); left exact functors
  form the full subcategory `C ⥤ₗ D`.

registrations.name: rightExactFunctor
registrations.comment:
Part (2), right exact functors: the property `rightExactFunctor C D` of a
  functor `F : C ⥤ D`, which is `PreservesFiniteColimits F` (`rightExactFunctor_iff`); right
  exact functors form the full subcategory `C ⥤ᵣ D`.

registrations.name: exactFunctor
registrations.comment:
Part (3), exact functors: the property `exactFunctor C D` of a functor
  `F : C ⥤ D`, which is `PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F`, i.e. both left and
  right exact (`exactFunctor_iff`, `exactFunctor_le_leftExactFunctor`,
  `exactFunctor_le_rightExactFunctor`); exact functors form the full subcategory `C ⥤ₑ D`.

registrations.name: exactFunctor_iff
registrations.comment:
Part (3): a functor is exact iff it preserves finite limits and finite
  colimits.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae_of_hasFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
A functor out of a category with finite limits is left exact if and only if it preserves
finite products and equalizers, if and only if it preserves the terminal object and pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_tfae_of_hasFiniteLimits [HasFiniteLimits C] (F : C ⥤ D) :
    List.TFAE [PreservesFiniteLimits F,
      PreservesFiniteProducts F ∧ PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair F,
      PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete.{0} PEmpty) F ∧ PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan F]
declarations.comment:
Left exactness is `PreservesFiniteLimits`; `(2) → (1)` is Mathlib's
`preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesEqualizers_and_finiteProducts` and `(3) → (1)` is
`preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesTerminal_and_pullbacks`, while `(1) → (2)` and `(1) → (3)`
hold because finite products, equalizers, the empty limit and pullbacks are finite limits.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.NatTrans.vcomp_hcomp_formal_properties
declarations.statement:
theorem vcomp_hcomp_formal_properties :
    -- (1) associativity of `≫`
    (∀ {F G H K : A ⥤ B} (a : F ⟶ G) (b : G ⟶ H) (c : H ⟶ K),
      (a ≫ b) ≫ c = a ≫ b ≫ c) ∧
    -- (1) associativity of `◫`
    (∀ {F F' : A ⥤ B} {G G' : B ⥤ C} {H H' : C ⥤ D}
      (t : F ⟶ F') (s : G ⟶ G') (r : H ⟶ H'), (t ◫ s) ◫ r = t ◫ (s ◫ r)) ∧
    -- (2) `𝟙 F` is a unit for `≫`
    (∀ {F G : A ⥤ B} (t : F ⟶ G), 𝟙 F ≫ t = t ∧ t ≫ 𝟙 G = t) ∧
    -- (3) `𝟙 (𝟭 A)` is a unit for `◫`
    (∀ {F F' : A ⥤ B} (t : F ⟶ F'), 𝟙 (𝟭 A) ◫ t = t ∧ t ◫ 𝟙 (𝟭 B) = t) ∧
    -- (3) `𝟙 (𝟭 A)` is a unit for `≫`
    (∀ {G : A ⥤ A} (u : 𝟭 A ⟶ G) (w : G ⟶ 𝟭 A), 𝟙 (𝟭 A) ≫ u = u ∧ w ≫ 𝟙 (𝟭 A) = w) ∧
    -- (4) the interchange law
    (∀ {F F' F'' : A ⥤ B} {G G' G'' : B ⥤ C}
      (t : F ⟶ F') (t' : F' ⟶ F'') (s : G ⟶ G') (s' : G' ⟶ G''),
      (t ≫ t') ◫ (s ≫ s') = (t ◫ s) ≫ (t' ◫ s'))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.IsTwoOneCategory
declarations.doc:
A *(strict) `(2,1)`-category* is a `2`-category — that is, a strict bicategory — in which
every `2`-morphism is an isomorphism, the latter spelled as Mathlib's
`Bicategory.IsLocallyGroupoid`, i.e. each hom-category `a ⟶ b` is a groupoid.
declarations.statement: def IsTwoOneCategory (B : Type u) [Bicategory.{w, v} B] : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.isTwoOneCategory_pith_cat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003K.** The `2`-category `Cat` of categories, functors and morphisms of functors
(Stacks 003J) becomes a `(2,1)`-category once only the *isomorphisms* of functors are allowed as
`2`-morphisms. The resulting `2`-category is `Bicategory.Pith Cat`; that its `2`-morphisms are
precisely the isomorphisms of functors is `Pith.homEquivIso`.
declarations.statement: lemma isTwoOneCategory_pith_cat : IsTwoOneCategory (Pith Cat.{v, u})

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.TwoCommSq
declarations.doc:
A **2-commutative cone** over the cospan `(f, g)`: an object `pt` together with
1-morphisms `fst : pt ⟶ x`, `snd : pt ⟶ y` and an invertible 2-morphism
`iso : fst ≫ f ≅ snd ≫ g` filling the square.

**Stacks 003O.** These are the objects of the 2-category of 2-commutative diagrams over
the cospan `(f, g)`.
declarations.statement: structure TwoCommSq (f : x ⟶ z) (g : y ⟶ z)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.TwoCommSq.PreHom
declarations.doc:
A **pre-morphism of cones** `T ⟶ S`: a 1-morphism `hom : T.pt ⟶ S.pt` together with
invertible comparison 2-cells `isoFst : T.fst ≅ hom ≫ S.fst`, `isoSnd : T.snd ≅ hom ≫ S.snd`
subject to the Stacks 003O compatibility square.

**Stacks 003O.** These are the 1-morphisms of the 2-category of 2-commutative diagrams
(`TwoCommSqBicat.bicategory`), before passing to classes modulo the 2-cell equivalence
`TwoCommSq.PreHom.Rel`; the 2-morphisms between them are `TwoCommSq.PreHom.Hom₂`.
declarations.statement: structure TwoCommSq.PreHom (T S : TwoCommSq f g)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.TwoCommSqBicat.bicategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003O.** The 2-category of 2-commutative diagrams over the cospan `(f, g)`:
objects are the 2-commutative squares `(w, a, b, φ)`, 1-morphisms are the triples
`(k, α, β)` satisfying the compatibility square (`TwoCommSq.PreHom`), composed by
`TwoCommSq.PreHom.comp`, and 2-morphisms are the 2-morphisms `δ : k₁ ⟶ k₂` compatible with the
comparison 2-cells (`TwoCommSq.PreHom.Hom₂`), composed vertically and horizontally as in `B`.
Since `B` is a bicategory, this is a bicategory, whose associators and unitors are those of `B`;
it is a strict 2-category when `B` is.
declarations.statement: instance TwoCommSqBicat.bicategory : Bicategory (TwoCommSqBicat f g)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.IsBiterminal
declarations.doc:
A *final object* of a `(2,1)`-category `B`, defined as an object `T` such that every
hom-category `X ⟶ T` has a terminal object. In a locally groupoidal `B` this says that every
object admits a `1`-morphism to `T`, and any two such are isomorphic by a unique `2`-morphism
(`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.isBiterminal_iff`).
declarations.statement: def IsBiterminal (T : B) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.IsFinalTwoCommSq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003Q.** A 2-commutative square `P` over `(f, g)` is a **2-fibre product** of `f`
and `g`: a final object, in the sense of Stacks 003P, of the 2-category of 2-commutative
diagrams over `(f, g)` of Stacks 003O. That is, (1) every 2-commutative square `Q` has a
1-morphism `preHom Q : Q ⟶ P`, and (2) any two 1-morphisms `F G : Q ⟶ P` are related by a
unique 2-morphism `F ⟶ G` of Stacks 003O (4), which is then invertible
(`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.IsFinalTwoCommSq.hom₂Iso`), so `F` and `G` are isomorphic by a
unique 2-morphism. The `fst`, `snd` and `iso` fields of `P` are the projections `p`, `q` and
the invertible `ψ : f ∘ p ⟶ g ∘ q` of the source.
declarations.statement: structure IsFinalTwoCommSq (P : TwoCommSq f g)
declarations.comment: final object of the 2-category of 2-commutative diagrams (003O, 003P), with the uniqueness of the 2-isomorphism of 003P (2)

registrations.comment: Both conditions: `exists_lift` is (1), the existence of a lift with prescribed target of every base morphism; `unique_lift` is (2), the unique fill-in `χ` with `p.map χ = f` and `χ ≫ φ = ψ`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.iff_isFibered_and_fiber_isGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003V (Lemma 4.35.2).** A functor `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` is fibred in groupoids
if and only if it is a fibred category all of whose fibres are groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem iff_isFibered_and_fiber_isGroupoid :
    p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ↔ p.IsFibered ∧ ∀ S, IsGroupoid (p.Fiber S)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInGroupoids_iff_and_isStronglyCartesian_and_isGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003V.** For a functor `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮`:

1. `p` is fibred in groupoids if and only if `p` is a fibred category and every fibre category
   `p.Fiber S` is a groupoid;
2. moreover, if `p` is fibred in groupoids then every morphism `φ` of `𝒳` is strongly cartesian
   (over `p.map φ`), and for every choice of morphisms `f^* x ⟶ x` lying over `f`, for all
   `f : V ⟶ U` and all `x` over `U`, the data `(U ↦ 𝒳_U, f ↦ f^*, α_{g,f}, α_U)` of Stacks 02XO
   form a pseudofunctor `𝒮ᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat` (`ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor`) every value of which is a
   groupoid, i.e. a pseudofunctor into the `(2, 1)`-category of groupoids.

The pseudofunctor is that of `ChoiceOfPullbacks.ofIsFiberedInGroupoids`; its value at `f` is the
pullback functor `f^*` of the given lifts (`ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_map`), and its unitor
and compositor are characterised by `ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_mapId_hom_app`,
`ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_fac` and
`ChoiceOfPullbacks.pseudofunctor_mapComp_hom_app_unique`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInGroupoids_iff_and_isStronglyCartesian_and_isGroupoid (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) :
    (p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ↔ p.IsFibered ∧ ∀ S, IsGroupoid (p.Fiber S)) ∧
      ∀ hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids,
        (∀ {x y : 𝒳} (φ : y ⟶ x), p.IsStronglyCartesian (p.map φ) φ) ∧
        ∀ (obj : ∀ {V U : 𝒮} (_f : V ⟶ U), p.Fiber U → p.Fiber V)
          (map : ∀ {V U : 𝒮} (f : V ⟶ U) (x : p.Fiber U), (obj f x).1 ⟶ x.1)
          (isHomLift : ∀ {V U : 𝒮} (f : V ⟶ U) (x : p.Fiber U), p.IsHomLift f (map f x))
          (U : LocallyDiscrete 𝒮ᵒᵖ),
          IsGroupoid
            ((ChoiceOfPullbacks.ofIsFiberedInGroupoids hp obj map isHomLift).pseudofunctor.obj U)
declarations.comment: the equivalence (1) ⇔ (2), every morphism strongly cartesian, and the groupoid-valued pseudofunctor of Lemma 02XO attached to any choice of lifts
