declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.faithful_iff_forall_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003Z (1).** `G` is faithful if and only if for every object `U` of `C` the
induced functor `G_U : S_U ⥤ S'_U` on fibres is faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.faithful_iff_forall_fiber (p : S ⥤ C) (p' : S' ⥤ C)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hp' : p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (G : S ⥤ S')
    (hG : G ⋙ p' = p) : G.Faithful ↔ ∀ U : C, (Fiber.mapOfComp p p' G hG U).Faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.full_and_faithful_iff_forall_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003Z (1).** `G` is full and faithful if and only if for every object `U` of `C` the
induced functor `G_U : S_U ⥤ S'_U` on fibres is full and faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.full_and_faithful_iff_forall_fiber (p : S ⥤ C) (p' : S' ⥤ C)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hp' : p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (G : S ⥤ S')
    (hG : G ⋙ p' = p) : (G.Full ∧ G.Faithful) ↔
      ∀ U : C, ((Fiber.mapOfComp p p' G hG U).Full ∧ (Fiber.mapOfComp p p' G hG U).Faithful)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.isEquivalence_iff_forall_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003Z (1).** `G` is an equivalence of categories if and only if for every object
`U` of `C` the induced functor `G_U : S_U ⥤ S'_U` on fibres is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.isEquivalence_iff_forall_fiber (p : S ⥤ C) (p' : S' ⥤ C)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hp' : p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (G : S ⥤ S')
    (hG : G ⋙ p' = p) :
    G.IsEquivalence ↔ ∀ U : C, (Fiber.mapOfComp p p' G hG U).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.isEquivalence_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003Z (2).** If `G` is an equivalence of categories, then `G` is an equivalence
in the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over `C`: there are a functor
`F : S' ⥤ S` over `C` (that is, `F ⋙ p = p'`) and natural isomorphisms `G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 S` and
`F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 S'` all of whose components lie over identity morphisms of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.isEquivalence_over (p : S ⥤ C) (p' : S' ⥤ C)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hp' : p'.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (G : S ⥤ S') (hG : G ⋙ p' = p) (hGequiv : G.IsEquivalence) :
    ∃ (F : S' ⥤ S) (_ : F ⋙ p = p') (η : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 S) (ε : F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 S'),
      (∀ x : S, p.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj x)) (η.hom.app x)) ∧
      (∀ x' : S', p'.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p'.obj x')) (ε.hom.app x'))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fibreIso
declarations.doc:
Clause (1) of Stacks 0040: the comparison isomorphism `φ` of an object `(U, x, y, φ)` is an
isomorphism `F x ≅ G y` *in the fibre category* `𝒮_U`. Both `F x` and `G y` lie over `U` because
`F` and `G` are 1-morphisms over `𝒞`, and `φ` is vertical by construction.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.lift
declarations.doc:
The mediating 1-morphism `γ : W ⥤ 𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴` of Stacks 0040, sending `w` to the quadruple
`(pW w, H w, K w, t w)`. That `H` and `K` are 1-morphisms over `𝒞` is what makes the two components
of `γ h` lie over the common base morphism `pW h`, and the comparison square is the naturality
of `t`.
declarations.statement: def lift : W ⥤ TwoFibreProductOver p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.lift_comp_structureFunctor
declarations.doc:
The mediating 1-morphism is a 1-morphism of categories over `𝒞`: it sends `w` to an object
lying over `pW w`, and a morphism to one lying over `pW h`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lift_comp_structureFunctor :
    lift p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht ⋙ structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G = pW

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.liftCompFst_hom_app_isHomLift
declarations.doc: The first comparison isomorphism is a 2-morphism over `𝒞`: its components are vertical.
declarations.statement:
theorem liftCompFst_hom_app_isHomLift (w : W) :
    p𝒳.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) ((liftCompFst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht).hom.app w)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.liftCompSnd_hom_app_isHomLift
declarations.doc: The second comparison isomorphism is a 2-morphism over `𝒞`: its components are vertical.
declarations.statement:
theorem liftCompSnd_hom_app_isHomLift (w : W) :
    p𝒴.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) ((liftCompSnd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht).hom.app w)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.lift_whiskerRight_psi
declarations.doc:
The factorisation is compatible with the given isomorphism `t`: whiskering the 2-cell `ψ` into
`γ` and correcting by the two comparison isomorphisms recovers `t`. This is the commuting square of
2-morphisms which makes `γ` a factorisation of the test cone `(H, K, t)`, rather than merely a
1-morphism with the right two projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem lift_whiskerRight_psi :
    Functor.whiskerRight (liftCompFst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht).hom F ≫ t.hom =
      Functor.whiskerLeft (lift p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht) (psiIso p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).hom ≫
        Functor.whiskerRight (liftCompSnd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht).hom G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.natTrans_ext
declarations.doc:
Two 2-morphisms into the 2-fibre product that agree after projecting to `𝒳` and to `𝒴` are
equal, so the mediating 2-morphism supplied by `liftIso` is the only one.
declarations.statement:
theorem natTrans_ext {γ δ : W ⥤ TwoFibreProductOver p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G} {α β : γ ⟶ δ}
    (h₁ : Functor.whiskerRight α (fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) =
      Functor.whiskerRight β (fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G))
    (h₂ : Functor.whiskerRight α (snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) =
      Functor.whiskerRight β (snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G)) : α = β

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.liftIso
declarations.doc:
Any other factorisation of the test cone `(H, K, t)` through the 2-fibre product is
2-isomorphic over `𝒞` to the mediating 1-morphism `lift`. Together with `natTrans_ext` this is the
uniqueness half of the 2-universal property: the factorisation is unique up to a unique
2-isomorphism over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def liftIso (γ : W ⥤ TwoFibreProductOver p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G)
    (a : γ ⋙ fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ≅ H) (b : γ ⋙ snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ≅ K)
    (ha : ∀ w, p𝒳.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (a.hom.app w))
    (hb : ∀ w, p𝒴.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (b.hom.app w))
    (hab : Functor.whiskerRight a.hom F ≫ t.hom =
      Functor.whiskerLeft γ (psiIso p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight b.hom G)
    (hH : H ⋙ p𝒳 = pW) (hK : K ⋙ p𝒴 = pW)
    (ht : ∀ w, p𝒮.IsHomLift (𝟙 (pW.obj w)) (t.hom.app w)) :
    γ ≅ lift p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G pW H K hH hK t ht

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq
declarations.doc: The first projection is strictly over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement: lemma fst_comp_eq : fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ⋙ p𝒳 = structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.snd_comp_eq
declarations.doc: The second projection is strictly over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement: lemma snd_comp_eq : snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ⋙ p𝒴 = structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.psiIso
declarations.doc:
The 2-cell `ψ : π₁ ⋙ F ≅ π₂ ⋙ G` filling the square, with component at
`(U, x, y, φ)` the comparison isomorphism `φ` itself.
declarations.statement:
def psiIso (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮) :
    (fst p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ⋙ F) ≅ (snd p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G ⋙ G)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.psiIso_hom_vertical
declarations.doc: Every component of the 2-cell `ψ` is vertical over `𝒞`: it lies over an identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma psiIso_hom_vertical (P : TwoFibreProductOver p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G) :
    p𝒮.IsHomLift (𝟙 P.base) ((psiIso p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).hom.app P)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0041.** The 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞` has 2-fibre
products, given by the construction of Stacks 0040: if `p𝒳`, `p𝒴`, `p𝒮` are fibred in groupoids
and `F`, `G` are strictly over `𝒞`, then the structure functor of `𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴` is fibred in
groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInGroupoids (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮)
    (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h𝒮 : p𝒮.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hF : F ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒳) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒴) :
    (structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInSets_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0043.** A functor is fibred in sets, i.e. every morphism of the base has a unique
lift with a prescribed target, if and only if it is fibred in groupoids and all of its fibre
categories are discrete. The right-hand side is Stacks' definition of a category fibred in sets
(a category fibred in discrete categories); a category is discrete (`CategoryTheory.IsDiscrete`)
when its only morphisms are identities.
declarations.statement:
lemma Functor.isFiberedInSets_iff (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) :
    p.IsFiberedInSets ↔ p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ ∀ U : 𝒞, IsDiscrete (p.Fiber U)
declarations.comment: The defining property: `p` is fibred in sets iff it is fibred in groupoids (003T) and every fibre category `p.Fiber U` is discrete.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInSets
registrations.comment: Stated through the equivalent unique-lift property; `Functor.isFiberedInSets_iff` identifies it with Stacks' definition: fibred in groupoids with discrete fibre categories.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.overEquivElementsOp
declarations.doc:
**`C/X` is the category of elements of `h_X`.** The slice category `C/X` is equivalent to
the category `S_{h_X} = ((h_X).Elements)ᵒᵖ` attached to the representable presheaf
`h_X = Mor_C(-, X)`.

Both round trips are the identity functor on the nose, so the unit and counit are
identities.
declarations.statement: def overEquivElementsOp : Over X ≌ ((yoneda.obj X).Elements)ᵒᵖ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.overEquivElementsOpForget
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of `overEquivElementsOp` is an equivalence over `C`.** It carries the
structure functor `C/X → C` to the structure functor `S_{h_X} → C`, which is
`(Functor.Elements.π h_X).leftOp`. This is the sense in which `C/X` is *canonically
equivalent over `C`* to `S_{h_X}`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.eq_of_hom_left_id
declarations.doc:
**The fibre categories of `C/X → C` have only identities (existence part).** If there is
a morphism `Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk g` of `C/X` lying over the identity of `U`, then `f = g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_hom_left_id {U : C} {f g : U ⟶ X} (φ : Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk g)
    (hφ : φ.left = 𝟙 U) : f = g

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.hom_eq_id_of_left_id
declarations.doc:
**The fibre categories of `C/X → C` have only identities (uniqueness part).** A morphism
of `C/X` from an object to itself lying over the identity is the identity. Together with
`CategoryTheory.Over.eq_of_hom_left_id` this says that the fibre category of `C/X → C` over
`U` has the morphisms `h : U ⟶ X` as objects and only identities as morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_eq_id_of_left_id {U : C} {f : U ⟶ X} (φ : Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk f)
    (hφ : φ.left = 𝟙 U) : φ = 𝟙 (Over.mk f)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.Equivalence.isFiberedInSetoids_of_isFiberedInSets
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0045 (1)(a).** Let `𝒞` be a category and let `𝒳` be a category over `𝒞`. If `𝒳` is
equivalent over `𝒞` to a category `𝒴` fibred in sets over `𝒞`, then `𝒳` is fibred in setoids
over `𝒞`.

Both fibre conditions are transported backwards along the equivalence: a category fibred in sets
is fibred in groupoids with discrete, hence thin, fibres (Stacks 0043), and being fibred in
groupoids and having thin fibres each transport.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInSetoids_of_isFiberedInSets (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴)
    (h : 𝒴.p.IsFiberedInSets) : 𝒳.p.IsFiberedInSetoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.Equivalence.fiberMap_identifiesIsoClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0045 (1)(b).** Let `𝒞` be a category, let `𝒳` be a category over `𝒞` and let `e` be
an equivalence over `𝒞` from `𝒳` to a category `𝒴` fibred in sets over `𝒞`. For every object `U`
of `𝒞` the induced map `Ob(𝒳_U) → Ob(𝒴_U)` on the objects of the fibres identifies its target
with the set of isomorphism classes of its source: it is surjective, and two objects of `𝒳_U`
have the same image exactly when they are isomorphic in `𝒳_U`.

The same content packaged as a bijection `Ob(𝒳_U)/≅ ≃ Ob(𝒴_U)` is
`CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.Equivalence.fiberQuotientEquiv`; as there, the two categories over
`𝒞` are taken in one pair of universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberMap_identifiesIsoClasses {𝒳 𝒴 : BasedCategory.{v₂, u₂} 𝒞}
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴)
    (h : 𝒴.p.IsFiberedInSets) (U : 𝒞) :
    Function.Surjective (e.fiberMap (U := U)) ∧
      ∀ x y : 𝒳.p.Fiber U, e.fiberMap x = e.fiberMap y ↔ IsIsomorphic x y

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInSets_isoClassElementsProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0045 (2)**, the category produced is fibred in sets. The lift of `f : V ⟶ U` at
`(U, ξ)` is `(V, f^*ξ)`, with the restriction map of the presheaf of isomorphism classes as the
morphism, and it is the only one: a lift of `f` with target `(U, ξ)` has its underlying morphism
of `𝒞` forced to be `f`, and then the class at its source is forced to be `f^*ξ`.
declarations.statement:
instance isFiberedInSets_isoClassElementsProj (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFibered] :
    (isoClassElementsProj p).IsFiberedInSets
declarations.comment: (2), the category fibred in sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.basedEquivalenceIsoClassElements
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0045 (2)**, the equivalence. Let `𝒞` be a category and let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` be a category
fibred in setoids. Then `can : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'` is an equivalence over `𝒞` onto the category of elements
of the presheaf of isomorphism classes, which is fibred in sets by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInSets_isoClassElementsProj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def basedEquivalenceIsoClassElements (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFiberedInSetoids] :
    BasedCategory.Equivalence (BasedCategory.ofFunctor p)
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (isoClassElementsProj p))
declarations.comment: (2), the equivalence over the base

declarations.name: StacksRepresentableCFG.IsRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0046.** `p : S ⥤ C` is *representable* if it is representable by some object `X` of
`C`: there are an object `X` of `C` and an equivalence `j : S → C/X` over `C`
(`StacksRepresentableCFG.RepresentableBy`), i.e. strict 1-morphisms over `C` in both directions
with unit and counit 2-isomorphisms over `C`.

The predicate is stated for an arbitrary category `p : S ⥤ C` over `C`; Stacks applies it to
categories fibred in groupoids. For those it is exactly the source's notion: `C/X` is fibred in
groupoids, and the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over `C` (Stacks 02XS) has as
1-morphisms the functors strictly over `C` and as 2-morphisms the transformations lying over
identities, as in the 2-category of categories over `C` (Stacks 003Y), so an equivalence in it
is exactly an equivalence over `C` between `S` and `C/X`.
declarations.statement: def IsRepresentable (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) : Prop
declarations.comment: stated for any category over C; Stacks' case is p fibred in groupoids, where an equivalence over C is an equivalence in the 2-category of groupoids over C (02XS)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInSets.twoFibreProd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0047 (Lemma 4.38.4).** The 2-category of categories fibred in sets over `𝒞` has
2-fibre products: if `𝒳`, `𝒴`, `𝒮` are fibred in sets over `𝒞` and `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮`, `G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮`
are 1-morphisms over `𝒞`, then the 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴` of Stacks `0040`, with its
structure functor, is again fibred in sets over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.IsFiberedInSets.twoFibreProd
    [pX.IsFiberedInSets] [pY.IsFiberedInSets] [pS.IsFiberedInSets]
    (hF : F ⋙ pS = pX) (hG : G ⋙ pS = pY) :
    (TwoFibreProd.proj pX pY pS F G).IsFiberedInSets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isFiberedInGroupoids_presheafOfGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0049.**
The category `𝒮_F` attached to a presheaf of groupoids `F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grpd` is fibred in groupoids
over `𝒞`: every morphism of `𝒞` lifts, and every fill-in problem has a unique solution.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInGroupoids_presheafOfGroupoids :
    (presheafOfGroupoids F).p.IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isFibredEquivalenceOver_presheafOfCategories
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004A.**
Every fibred category `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` is equivalent, in the 2-category of fibred categories over `𝒞`,
to the category `𝒮_F` (Stacks 02XV, `CategoryTheory.presheafOfCategories`) attached to a
contravariant functor `F : 𝒞 ⥤ Cat`; in other words, every fibred category is equivalent to a
split one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFibredEquivalenceOver_presheafOfCategories :
    ∃ (F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat.{v₂, max u₁ u₂ v₁}) (Φ : 𝒳 ⥤ (presheafOfCategories F).obj),
      IsFibredEquivalenceOver p (presheafOfCategories F).p Φ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation
declarations.doc:
The evaluation functor `ev : Mor_{Cat/C}(C/U, S) ⥤ S_U` of the 2-Yoneda lemma.

On objects it sends a functor over `C`, `G : C/U ⥤ S` (packaged as a based functor),
to `G(id_U) = G(Over.mk (𝟙 U))`, which lies in the fibre over `U` since
`p ∘ G = π_U` and `π_U (Over.mk (𝟙 U)) = U`.

On a 2-morphism `η : G ⟶ G'` (a based natural transformation) it returns the
component `η_{(U, 𝟙 U)}`, which lies over `𝟙 U` and is therefore a morphism of `S_U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation (p : S ⥤ C) (U : C) :
    (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (Over.forget U) ⥤ᵇ BasedCategory.ofFunctor p) ⥤ p.Fiber U

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The 2-Yoneda lemma (Stacks 004B).**
Let `p : S ⥤ C` be fibred in groupoids and let `U` be an object of `C`. Then the
evaluation functor `ev : Mor_{Cat/C}(C/U, S) ⥤ S_U`, `G ↦ G(id_U)`, is an equivalence
of categories.

It is faithful, full and essentially surjective by
`Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation_faithful`, `Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation_full` and
`Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation_essSurj`, and a functor with these three properties is an
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation_isEquivalence (p : S ⥤ C) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (U : C) : (Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation p U).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.TwoYoneda.liftBasedEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004B**, essential surjectivity as data. The functor over `C` on the slice `C/U`
assembled from the chosen cartesian lifts of an object `x` of the fibre of `p` over `U` evaluates
at the terminal object to an object canonically isomorphic to `x`: the chosen lift at `𝟙 U` is an
arrow of the fibre, and the fibre of a category fibred in groupoids is a groupoid.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def liftBasedEvaluationIso (p : S ⥤ C) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (U : C)
    (x : p.Fiber U) :
    (Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation p U).obj (liftBased p hp U x) ≅ x
declarations.comment: essential surjectivity of evaluation, as data

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.TwoYoneda.hom₂OfFiberHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004B**, fullness as data. The 2-morphism of functors over `C` on the slice `C/U`
representing a morphism of the fibre objects they evaluate to.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hom₂OfFiberHom
    (φ : (Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation p U).obj G ⟶ (Functor.twoYonedaEvaluation p U).obj G') :
    G ⟶ G'
declarations.comment: fullness of evaluation, as data

declarations.name: refine_open_cover_by_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004Q.** A basis refines any open covering of an open set: given a topological basis
`ℬ` of `X` and an open covering `𝓤` of an open `U ⊆ X`, the set `V` of basis elements contained in
some `𝓤 i` satisfies `⋃₀ V = U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem refine_open_cover_by_basis
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {ℬ : Set (Set X)} (hℬ : TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis ℬ)
    {U : Set X}
    {I : Type*} (𝓤 : I → Set X) (h𝓤 : ∀ i, IsOpen (𝓤 i)) (hU : U = ⋃ i, 𝓤 i) :
    ∃ V : Set (Set X),
      V ⊆ ℬ ∧
      ⋃₀ V = U ∧
      ∀ v ∈ V, ∃ i, v ⊆ 𝓤 i

registrations.name: connectedComponent_eq
registrations.comment: (3), (4): uniqueness

registrations.name: connectedComponent_disjoint
registrations.comment: (4): disjointness

declarations.name: isGenericPoint_iff
declarations.doc: A point `ξ` lies in `Z` with `Z = closure {ξ}` exactly when `ξ` is a generic point of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGenericPoint_iff (Z : Set X) (ξ : X) :
    (ξ ∈ Z ∧ Z = closure {ξ}) ↔ IsGenericPoint ξ Z
declarations.comment: generic point

declarations.name: kolmogorov_iff
declarations.doc:
A space in which any two distinct points are separated by a closed set is exactly a
`T0Space`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kolmogorov_iff :
    (∀ x x' : X, x ≠ x' →
        ∃ C : Set X, IsClosed C ∧ ((x ∈ C) ↔ x' ∉ C)) ↔ T0Space X
declarations.comment: Kolmogorov

declarations.name: local_quasiSober_iff
declarations.doc:
A space in which every irreducible closed subset `Z` admits some `ξ ∈ Z` with `Z = closure {ξ}`
is exactly a `QuasiSober` space.
declarations.statement:
theorem local_quasiSober_iff :
    (∀ Z : Set X, IsIrreducible Z → IsClosed Z →
        ∃ ξ ∈ Z, Z = closure {ξ}) ↔ QuasiSober X
declarations.comment: quasi-sober

declarations.name: StacksSober
declarations.doc: A space is sober when every irreducible closed subset has a *unique* generic point.
declarations.statement: def StacksSober (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop
declarations.comment: sober

declarations.name: isIrreducible_iff_singleton_of_t2
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004Y** (subset irreducible iff singleton).
A subset `s` of a Hausdorff space `X` is irreducible if and only if `s` is a singleton.
declarations.comment: subset irreducible iff singleton

declarations.name: irreducibleSpace_iff_univ_singleton_of_t2
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004Y** (space irreducible iff singleton).
A Hausdorff space `X` is irreducible as a space if and only if its underlying set is a
singleton.
declarations.comment: space irreducible iff singleton

declarations.name: sober_of_t2
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004Y** (Hausdorff implies sober).
A Hausdorff space is `T0` and quasi-sober, that is, sober.
declarations.statement:
theorem sober_of_t2 (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] :
    T0Space X ∧ QuasiSober X
declarations.comment: Hausdorff implies sober

declarations.name: irreducibleSpace_of_continuous_of_dense_isIrreducible_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 004Z**.
Let `f : X → Y` be a continuous map of topological spaces. Assume that (a) `Y` is irreducible,
(b) `f` is open, and (c) there exists a dense collection of points `y ∈ Y` such that `f ⁻¹' {y}`
is irreducible. Then `X` is irreducible.

The continuity hypothesis (a) is recorded here because the source states it; the proof does not
use it, see `irreducibleSpace_of_isOpenMap_of_dense_isIrreducible_fiber`.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_of_continuous_of_dense_isIrreducible_fiber
    [IrreducibleSpace Y] {f : X → Y} (_hfcont : Continuous f) (hfopen : IsOpenMap f)
    (hfib : Dense {y : Y | IsIrreducible (f ⁻¹' {y})}) :
    IrreducibleSpace X

declarations.name: noetherianSpace_iff_wellFoundedLT_closeds
declarations.doc:
A topological space is Noetherian if and only if its lattice of closed subsets is
well-founded for the strict order.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_iff_wellFoundedLT_closeds
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    NoetherianSpace X ↔ WellFoundedLT (Closeds X)
declarations.comment:
Part (1): a space is Noetherian iff the descending chain condition holds for its
  closed subsets; part (2) is `isLocallyNoetherianSpace_iff_forall_exists_mem_nhds`.

declarations.name: isLocallyNoetherianSpace_iff_forall_exists_mem_nhds
declarations.doc:
A topological space is locally Noetherian, i.e. every point has a Noetherian open
neighbourhood, if and only if every point has a neighbourhood (a subset containing an open set
containing the point) which is Noetherian in the induced topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherianSpace_iff_forall_exists_mem_nhds
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X ↔ ∀ x : X, ∃ N ∈ nhds x, NoetherianSpace N
declarations.comment:
Part (2): the definition of a locally Noetherian space, with Stacks'
  neighbourhoods (any subset containing an open set containing the point).

declarations.name: topologicalKrullDim_eq_bot_iff_isEmpty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0055 (3).** The Krull dimension of `X` is `-∞` exactly when `X` is empty; for a
nonempty space `closure {x}` is an irreducible closed subset, so the supremum is taken over a
nonempty family.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_bot_iff_isEmpty :
    topologicalKrullDim X = ⊥ ↔ IsEmpty X

declarations.name: topologicalKrullDimAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0055 (4).** The Krull dimension of `X` at a point `x`: the infimum of the Krull
dimensions of the open neighbourhoods of `x`. It is a minimum, by
`topologicalKrullDimAt_isLeast`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def topologicalKrullDimAt (x : X) : WithBot ℕ∞

declarations.name: topologicalKrullDimAt_isLeast
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0055 (4).** `topologicalKrullDimAt X x` is the *least* element of the set of
Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods of `x`, which is Stacks' phrasing of part (4) as a
minimum. The infimum is attained because `WithBot ℕ∞` is well-founded.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_isLeast (x : X) :
    IsLeast
      {d : WithBot ℕ∞ |
        ∃ U : Set X, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpen U ∧ d = topologicalKrullDim (↥U)}
      (topologicalKrullDimAt X x)

declarations.name: topologicalKrullDim_euclideanSpace_eq_zero
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0056.** The Krull dimension of the Euclidean space `ℝ^n` is `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_euclideanSpace_eq_zero (n : ℕ) :
    topologicalKrullDim (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) = 0

declarations.name: isOpen_upperSet_fin_two_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0057.** The two-point example: with the upper-set topology on `Fin 2` (so `s = 0`
and `η = 1`), the open sets are exactly `∅`, `{η}` and the whole space.

declarations.name: exists_finite_space_of_krullDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0057.** For every `n : ℕ` there is a topological space with `n + 1` points whose
Krull dimension is `n`, namely `Fin (n + 1)` with the upper-set topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_space_of_krullDim (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (_ : Fintype X),
      Fintype.card X = n + 1 ∧ topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional
declarations.doc:
A topological space `X` is *equidimensional* if every irreducible component of `X` has the same
dimension, i.e. the same topological Krull dimension as a subspace.
declarations.statement: def TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop

declarations.name: compactSpace_iff_finite_subcover
declarations.doc:
**Quasi-compact spaces.** A topological space is compact (Mathlib's `CompactSpace`, with no
separation axiom) if and only if every open covering of it has a finite subcover: for every
family `𝒰` of open subsets with `⋃₀ 𝒰 = univ` there is a finite `𝒱 ⊆ 𝒰` with `⋃₀ 𝒱 = univ`.

The forward direction is `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image` for `univ`; the converse is
`isCompact_generateFrom`, the topology being generated by its open sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_iff_finite_subcover {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] :
    CompactSpace X ↔ ∀ 𝒰 : Set (Set X), (∀ U ∈ 𝒰, IsOpen U) → ⋃₀ 𝒰 = univ →
      ∃ 𝒱 ⊆ 𝒰, 𝒱.Finite ∧ ⋃₀ 𝒱 = univ
declarations.comment: (1): a space is quasi-compact if every open covering has a finite subcover

registrations.name: CompactSpace
registrations.comment:
(1): a quasi-compact topological space is `CompactSpace`; see
  `compactSpace_iff_finite_subcover` for the open-cover characterization

registrations.name: IsClosed.isCompact
registrations.comment: a closed subset of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact

registrations.name: CompactSpace.iInter_nonempty
registrations.comment: the finite intersection property in a quasi-compact space

registrations.name: IsClosed.exists_closed_singleton
registrations.comment: the case of the whole space, which is closed and assumed nonempty

declarations.name: connectedComponent_eq_iInter_isClopen_of_compactSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a topological space that is quasi-compact, admits a basis of quasi-compact open
sets, and is such that the intersection of any two quasi-compact open sets is quasi-compact. Then
for every `x : X` the connected component of `x` equals the intersection of all clopen subsets of
`X` containing `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedComponent_eq_iInter_isClopen_of_compactSpace
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
    {B : Set (Set X)} (hB : IsTopologicalBasis B)
    (hBqc : ∀ U ∈ B, IsCompact U)
    (hqcInter :
      ∀ ⦃U V : Set X⦄, IsOpen U → IsCompact U → IsOpen V → IsCompact V → IsCompact (U ∩ V))
    (x : X) :
    connectedComponent x = ⋂ Z : { Z : Set X // IsClopen Z ∧ x ∈ Z }, (Z : Set X)

declarations.name: Topology.isConstructible_iff_exists_finset_biUnion_inter_compl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005G(1)**.
A subset `s` of a topological space `X` is constructible if and only if it is a finite union of
subsets of the form `U ∩ Vᶜ` with `U, V ⊆ X` open and retrocompact in `X`. The finite union is
encoded by a `Finset` of pairs `(U, V)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Topology.isConstructible_iff_exists_finset_biUnion_inter_compl {s : Set X} :
    Topology.IsConstructible s ↔
      ∃ t : Finset (Set X × Set X),
        (∀ p ∈ t, IsOpen p.1 ∧ IsRetrocompact p.1 ∧ IsOpen p.2 ∧ IsRetrocompact p.2) ∧
        s = ⋃ p ∈ t, p.1 ∩ p.2ᶜ

declarations.name: IsConstructibleStratified.iUnion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005H** (finite unions).
A finite union of subsets of `X` that are each a finite union of sets `U ∩ Vᶜ` with `U, V`
open and retrocompact in `X` is again such a finite union.
declarations.comment: finite unions of constructible sets, in the normal form of 005G(1)

declarations.name: IsConstructibleStratified.iInter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005H** (finite intersections).
A finite intersection of subsets of `X` that are each a finite union of sets `U ∩ Vᶜ` with
`U, V` open and retrocompact in `X` is again such a finite union.
declarations.comment: finite intersections of constructible sets, in the normal form of 005G(1)

declarations.name: IsConstructibleStratified.compl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005H** (complements).
The complement of a finite union of sets `U ∩ Vᶜ` with `U, V` open and retrocompact in `X` is
again such a finite union.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsConstructibleStratified.compl {s : Set X} (hs : IsConstructibleStratified s) :
    IsConstructibleStratified sᶜ
declarations.comment: complements of constructible sets, in the normal form of 005G(1)

registrations.name: Topology.IsConstructible.iUnion
registrations.comment: a finite union of constructible sets is constructible

registrations.name: Topology.IsConstructible.iInter
registrations.comment: a finite intersection of constructible sets is constructible

registrations.name: Topology.IsConstructible.compl
registrations.comment: the complement of a constructible set is constructible

declarations.name: Topology.IsConstructible.exists_isOpen_inter_closure_singleton_subset
declarations.doc:
Every point of a constructible set has an open neighbourhood whose intersection with
the closure of the point lies in the set.
declarations.comment: constructible case, (3) ⇒ (1)

declarations.name: open_dense_iff_dense
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005K**.
For irreducible `Z` and `E` a finite union of locally closed subsets, the intersection
`E ∩ Z` contains an open dense subset of `Z` if and only if it is dense in `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem open_dense_iff_dense
    {Z : Set X} (hZ : IsIrreducible Z)
    {E : Set X} (hE : IsFiniteUnionLocallyClosed E) :
    (∃ V : Set X, IsOpenDenseSubsetOf V Z ∧ V ⊆ E ∩ Z) ↔ Z ⊆ closure (E ∩ Z)

declarations.name: tfae_with_generic_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005K**.
For irreducible `Z` with generic point `ξ` and `E` a finite union of locally closed subsets,
the existence of an open dense subset of `Z` inside `E ∩ Z`, the density of `E ∩ Z` in `Z`,
and the membership `ξ ∈ E` are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_with_generic_point
    {Z : Set X} (hZ : IsIrreducible Z)
    {E : Set X} (hE : IsFiniteUnionLocallyClosed E)
    {ξ : X} (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z) :
    [ (∃ V : Set X, IsOpenDenseSubsetOf V Z ∧ V ⊆ E ∩ Z),
      Z ⊆ closure (E ∩ Z),
      ξ ∈ E ].TFAE

declarations.name: constructible_iff_finite_union_locally_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005L.** In a Noetherian topological space `X`, a subset `E ⊆ X` is constructible if
and only if it is a finite union of locally closed subsets of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem constructible_iff_finite_union_locally_closed
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X] (E : Set X) :
    IsConstructibleSet E ↔ IsFiniteUnionLocallyClosed E

registrations.name: generalized_tube_lemma
registrations.comment: the tube lemma for a product of two quasi-compact subsets

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Topology.IsBourbakiProperMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005O (2).** `f` is *Bourbaki-proper* if `Z × X → Z × Y` is closed for every
topological space `Z`. As in Mathlib's `isProperMap_iff_universally_closed`, `Z` is quantified
over one universe at a time; `IsProperMap.isBourbakiProperMap` below supplies the statement in
every universe at once.
declarations.statement: def IsBourbakiProperMap (f : X → Y) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Topology.IsQuasiProperMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005O (3).** `f` is *quasi-proper* if the inverse image of every quasi-compact
subset of `Y` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: def IsQuasiProperMap (f : X → Y) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Topology.IsUniversallyClosedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005O (4).** `f` is *universally closed* if for every continuous `g : Z → Y` the
base change `f' : Z ×_Y X → Z` is a closed map.
declarations.statement: def IsUniversallyClosedMap (f : X → Y) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Topology.IsProperMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005O (5).** `f` is *proper* if it is separated and universally closed. Separatedness
is Mathlib's `IsSeparatedMap`, which Stacks 0CY1 defines by the diagonal `X → X ×_Y X` being a
closed map; `isSeparatedMap_iff_isClosedMap` is that equivalence.
declarations.statement: def IsProperMap (f : X → Y) : Prop

registrations.name: IsClosedMap
registrations.comment: (1) A map is closed if the image of every closed subset is closed.

declarations.name: compactSpace_iff_forall_isClosedMap_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005P**.
A topological space `X` is quasi-compact (`CompactSpace X`) if and only if, for every
topological space `Z`, the first projection `Prod.fst : Z × X → Z` is a closed map.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_iff_forall_isClosedMap_fst (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    CompactSpace X ↔
      ∀ (Z : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Z], IsClosedMap (Prod.fst : Z × X → Z)

declarations.name: isClosedMap_fst_of_compactSpace_and_compactSpace_of_forall_isClosedMap_fst
declarations.doc:
The two ingredients of Stacks Lemma 005P, which Stacks Remark 005Q attributes to Bourbaki
(General Topology, I, p. 75, Lemme 1 and p. 76, Corollaire 1).

1. If `X` is quasi-compact, then for every topological space `Z` (in any universe) the
   projection `Prod.fst : Z × X → Z` is a closed map.
2. Conversely, if the projection `Prod.fst : Z × X → Z` is a closed map for every topological
   space `Z` in the universe of `X`, then `X` is quasi-compact.

Lemma 005P (`compactSpace_iff_forall_isClosedMap_fst`) is their combination, as the remark
says; see `compactSpace_iff_isClosedMap_fst`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedMap_fst_of_compactSpace_and_compactSpace_of_forall_isClosedMap_fst
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    (CompactSpace X →
        ∀ (Z : Type v) [TopologicalSpace Z], IsClosedMap (Prod.fst : Z × X → Z)) ∧
      ((∀ (Z : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Z], IsClosedMap (Prod.fst : Z × X → Z)) →
        CompactSpace X)
declarations.comment: the remark is bibliographic: it says Lemma 005P combines two results of Bourbaki. Formalized as the two directions of 005P stated separately, the forward one for every universe of `Z`; their combination is `compactSpace_iff_isClosedMap_fst`.

declarations.name: isProperMap_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005R**.
Let `f : X → Y` be a continuous map between topological spaces. The following four
conditions are equivalent:

1. `f` is quasi-proper and closed.
2. `f` is Bourbaki-proper.
3. `f` is universally closed.
4. `f` is closed and the fibre `f⁻¹{y}` is quasi-compact for every `y : Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperMap_tfae {X Y : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    (f : X → Y) (hf : Continuous f) :
    [IsQuasiProper f ∧ IsClosedMap f,
     IsBourbakiProperMap.{u, u, u} f,
     IsUniversallyClosed f,
     IsClosedMap f ∧ ∀ y : Y, IsQuasiCompactSubset (f ⁻¹' {y})].TFAE

declarations.name: jacobson_check_irreducible_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005V**. Let `X` be a topological space and `X₀` its set of closed
points. If for every point `x` the intersection `X₀ ∩ closure {x}` is dense in
`closure {x}` (equivalently, `closure (closedPoints X ∩ closure {x}) = closure {x}`),
then `X` is a Jacobson space.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobson_check_irreducible_closed
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (h : ∀ x : X, closure (closedPoints X ∩ closure ({x} : Set X)) = closure ({x} : Set X)) :
    JacobsonSpace X

declarations.name: jacobsonSpace_iff_of_isOpenCover
declarations.doc:
For an open covering `U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X` of a topological space `X`, the space
`X` is Jacobson if and only if each `U i`, with the subspace topology, is Jacobson.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_iff_of_isOpenCover
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {ι : Type*} {U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X}
    (hU : TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover U) :
    JacobsonSpace X ↔ ∀ i, JacobsonSpace (U i)

declarations.name: closedPoints_eq_iUnion_image_closedPoints_of_isOpenCover
declarations.doc:
For an open covering `U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X` of a Jacobson space `X`, the set of
closed points of `X` is the union over `i` of the images of the closed points of `U i` under the
inclusion `Subtype.val : ↥(U i) → X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPoints_eq_iUnion_image_closedPoints_of_isOpenCover
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {ι : Type*} {U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X}
    (hU : TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover U)
    [JacobsonSpace X] :
    closedPoints X = ⋃ i, (Subtype.val : ↥(U i) → X) '' closedPoints ↥(U i)

declarations.name: jacobson_of_iUnion_isLocallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005X**. A (possibly infinite) union of locally closed subsets of a Jacobson space
is Jacobson, and its closed points are closed in the ambient space.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobson_of_iUnion_isLocallyClosed
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [JacobsonSpace X]
    {ι : Type v} {L : ι → Set X} (hL : ∀ i, IsLocallyClosed (L i)) :
    JacobsonSpace (⋃ i, L i : Set X) ∧
      (closedPoints (⋃ i, L i : Set X) ⊆ Subtype.val ⁻¹' closedPoints X)

declarations.name: jacobson_of_isLocallyClosed
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
theorem jacobson_of_isLocallyClosed

    {T : Set X} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    JacobsonSpace T ∧ (closedPoints T ⊆ Subtype.val ⁻¹' closedPoints X)

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: JacobsonSpace.isConstructible_restrictToClosedPoints
declarations.doc:
The correspondence of Stacks 005Y is well defined: for a constructible subset `E` of a
Jacobson space `X`, the subset `E ∩ X₀` of the space of closed points is constructible.

Restriction to the closed points is continuous and preserves retrocompactness of opens, so this
is Mathlib's `Topology.IsConstructible.preimage`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstructible_restrictToClosedPoints [JacobsonSpace X] {E : Set X}
    (hE : IsConstructible E) : IsConstructible (restrictToClosedPoints E)
declarations.comment: well-defined

declarations.name: JacobsonSpace.subset_iff_restrictToClosedPoints_subset
declarations.doc:
The correspondence of Stacks 005Y reflects inclusions: constructible subsets `E, F` of a
Jacobson space satisfy `E ⊆ F` if and only if `E ∩ X₀ ⊆ F ∩ X₀`.

Only the backward direction has content: `E \ F` is constructible, so if it is nonempty it
contains a closed point, which then witnesses the failure of `E ∩ X₀ ⊆ F ∩ X₀`.
declarations.comment: inclusion-preserving

declarations.name: JacobsonSpace.restrictToClosedPoints_bijective
declarations.doc:
Stacks 005Y: on a Jacobson space `X`, restriction to the closed points is a bijection from
the constructible subsets of `X` onto the constructible subsets of `X₀ = closedPoints X`.

Injectivity is the inclusion-reflecting property applied twice. Surjectivity is proved by the
Boolean induction `Topology.IsConstructible.empty_union_induction`: a retrocompact open of `X₀` is
the restriction of an open of `X`, which is retrocompact by
`JacobsonSpace.isRetrocompact_iff_isRetrocompact_restrictToClosedPoints`, and restriction
commutes with unions and complements.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictToClosedPoints_bijective [JacobsonSpace X] :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun E : {E : Set X // IsConstructible E} =>
        (⟨restrictToClosedPoints E.1, isConstructible_restrictToClosedPoints E.2⟩ :
          {F : Set (closedPoints X) // IsConstructible F}))
declarations.comment: bijective correspondence

declarations.name: JacobsonSpace.isOpen_and_isRetrocompact_iff_on_closedPoints
declarations.doc:
Stacks 005Y: the correspondence matches the retrocompact opens of `X` with the retrocompact
opens of `X₀`. A constructible subset `E` of a Jacobson space is a retrocompact open if and only
if `E ∩ X₀` is a retrocompact open of the space of closed points.

The backward direction writes `E ∩ X₀` as the restriction of an open `U ⊆ X`, which is
retrocompact and hence constructible; both `U` and `E` are then constructible with the same
restriction, so `U = E` by `JacobsonSpace.subset_iff_restrictToClosedPoints_subset`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_and_isRetrocompact_iff_on_closedPoints [JacobsonSpace X] {E : Set X}
    (hE : IsConstructible E) :
    (IsOpen E ∧ IsRetrocompact E) ↔
      (IsOpen (restrictToClosedPoints E) ∧ IsRetrocompact (restrictToClosedPoints E))
declarations.comment: preserves retrocompact opens

declarations.name: JacobsonSpace.isOpen_compl_and_isRetrocompact_compl_iff_on_closedPoints
declarations.doc:
Stacks 005Y: the correspondence matches the complements of retrocompact opens of `X` with the
complements of retrocompact opens of `X₀`. This is the previous statement applied to `Eᶜ`, which
is constructible, together with the fact that restriction to the closed points commutes with
complementation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_compl_and_isRetrocompact_compl_iff_on_closedPoints [JacobsonSpace X] {E : Set X}
    (hE : IsConstructible E) :
    (IsOpen Eᶜ ∧ IsRetrocompact Eᶜ) ↔
      (IsOpen (restrictToClosedPoints E)ᶜ ∧ IsRetrocompact (restrictToClosedPoints E)ᶜ)
declarations.comment: preserves complements of retrocompact opens

declarations.name: jacobsonSpace_locallyClosed_bijection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 005Z**. Let `X` be a Jacobson topological space, and let `X₀ = closedPoints X`
carry the subspace topology. There exists a bijection `Φ` between the finite unions of locally
closed subsets of `X` and of `X₀`, given by pullback `E ↦ Subtype.val ⁻¹' E`, that is,
`E ↦ E ∩ X₀`, which preserves inclusion in both directions and restricts to bijections on the
locally closed, the open, and the closed subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_locallyClosed_bijection
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [JacobsonSpace X] :
    ∃ Φ : {s : Set X // IsFiniteUnionLocallyClosed s} ≃
          {s : Set ↥(closedPoints X) // IsFiniteUnionLocallyClosed s},
      (∀ E, (Φ E).1 = Subtype.val ⁻¹' E.1) ∧
      (∀ E E', E.1 ⊆ E'.1 ↔ (Φ E).1 ⊆ (Φ E').1) ∧
      (∀ E, IsLocallyClosed E.1 ↔ IsLocallyClosed (Φ E).1) ∧
      (∀ E, IsOpen E.1 ↔ IsOpen (Φ E).1) ∧
      (∀ E, IsClosed E.1 ↔ IsClosed (Φ E).1)

ega.comment: a′ ⇒ c and c′, a′ ⇒ c″

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.tensorPresheafHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of the tensor product presheaf.** For presheaves of commutative rings
`α : O ⟶ O'` on `X`, a presheaf of `O`-modules `F` and a presheaf of `O'`-modules `M`, the
morphisms `O' ⊗_{p,O} F ⟶ M` of presheaves of `O'`-modules are in canonical bijection with the
morphisms `F ⟶ M_O` of presheaves of `O`-modules. The bijection sends `Φ` to `m ↦ Φ(1 ⊗ m)` and its
inverse sends `g` to the sectionwise lift `s ⊗ m ↦ s • g(m)`. This is Stacks 006R
(Lemma 6.6.2); the bijection is natural in both variables, being the hom-set bijection of the
adjunction `tensorPresheafAdjunction`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorPresheafHomEquiv :
    (tensorPresheafOfModules O O' α F ⟶ M) ≃ (F ⟶ restrictPresheaf O O' α M)
declarations.comment: hom-set bijection `Hom_{O'}(O' ⊗_{p,O} G, F) ≃ Hom_O(G, F_O)` on the explicit sectionwise tensor product presheaf, presheaves on a topological space; natural in both variables via `tensorPresheafAdjunction`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.tensorPresheafAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 006R (Lemma 6.6.2), adjunction form.** For a morphism `α : O ⟶ O'` of presheaves of
commutative rings on a topological space `X`, the change of rings functor
`O' ⊗_{p,O} (-) : PMod(O) ⥤ PMod(O')` on the sectionwise tensor product presheaf is left adjoint
to restriction of scalars `(-)_O : PMod(O') ⥤ PMod(O)`. Its hom-set bijection is
`tensorPresheafHomEquiv` (`tensorPresheafAdjunction_homEquiv`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorPresheafAdjunction :
    tensorPresheafFunctor O O' α ⊣ PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars (ringPresheafMap O O' α)
declarations.comment: adjunction form: `O' ⊗_{p,O} (-) ⊣ (-)_O` on the explicit sectionwise tensor product presheaf `U ↦ O'(U) ⊗_{O(U)} G(U)`, presheaves on a topological space; its hom-set bijection is `tensorPresheafHomEquiv`

the dependent product `∀ x : U, A x`, i.e. Mathlib's `TopCat.presheafToTypes X A`), with
restriction sending `(a_x)_{x ∈ U}` to `(a_x)_{x ∈ V}` for `V ⊆ U`, is a sheaf of sets.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: directSumOverPointsPresheaf_not_isSheaf_in_general_and_isSheaf_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 006Y.** Let `X` be a topological space and `M_x` an abelian group for each
`x ∈ X`, and let `F` be the presheaf `U ↦ ⨁_{x ∈ U} M_x`. Then
(a) `F` is not a sheaf in general: there are a space `X` and a family `M` for which `F` is not a
sheaf (an infinite discrete space with `M_x = ℤ`);
(b) if every open subset of `X` is quasi-compact, then `F` is a sheaf, for every family `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem directSumOverPointsPresheaf_not_isSheaf_in_general_and_isSheaf_of_isCompact :
    (∃ (X : TopCat.{u}) (M : X → Type u) (_ : ∀ x, AddCommGroup (M x)),
      ¬ (directSumOverPointsPresheaf (X := X) M).IsSheaf) ∧
    ∀ X : TopCat.{u}, (∀ U : Opens X, IsCompact (U : Set X)) →
      ∀ (M : X → Type u) [∀ x, AddCommGroup (M x)], (directSumOverPointsPresheaf M).IsSheaf

registrations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp
registrations.comment:
an abelian presheaf is a sheaf exactly when its underlying presheaf of

registrations.name: TopCat.Sheaf
registrations.comment:
Sheaves of abelian groups on `X` are the objects of
  `TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat X`; Mathlib states the sheaf condition for a general target

sga.comment: Fiber of E over a scheme

The category structure on `Ab(X) = TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat X`,

registrations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.SheafConditionEqualizerProducts.diagram
registrations.comment: the equalizer diagram `F(U) → ∏ F(Uᵢ) ⇉ ∏ F(U_{i₀} ∩ U_{i₁})`

registrations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheafEqualizerProducts

registrations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafEqualizerProducts

declarations.name: presheafC0_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
The presheaf of (commutative) `ℝ`-algebras of continuous real-valued
functions on a topological space `X` is a sheaf of `ℝ`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafC0_isSheaf (X : TopCat.{0}) :
    (presheafC0 X).IsSheaf

declarations.name: forget_topCat_not_reflectsIsomorphisms_and_presheafToDiscreteTypes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0075.** The forgetful functor `Top → Sets` is faithful and commutes with
limits, in particular with products and equalizers (Mathlib's instances `(forget C).Faithful`
and `TopCat.forget_preservesLimits`), but it does not reflect isomorphisms; and the analogue of
Lemma 0073 fails for `Top`. Namely, let `X = ℕ` with the discrete topology and let `A i`,
`i ∈ ℕ`, be discrete spaces. Then `F(U) = ∏_{i ∈ U} A i` with the discrete topology is a
presheaf of topological spaces whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf (Example 006X); if
each `A i` has at least two elements, it is not a sheaf of topological spaces; and putting the
product topology on each `F(U)` instead does give a sheaf of topological spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem forget_topCat_not_reflectsIsomorphisms_and_presheafToDiscreteTypes :
    (forget TopCat.{0}).Faithful ∧ Limits.PreservesLimits (forget TopCat.{0}) ∧
      ¬ (forget TopCat.{0}).ReflectsIsomorphisms ∧
      ∀ (A : TopCat.of ℕ → Type) [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (A i)] [∀ i, DiscreteTopology (A i)],
        TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf (presheafToDiscreteTypes (TopCat.of ℕ) A ⋙ forget TopCat) ∧
        ((∀ i, Nontrivial (A i)) → ¬ (presheafToDiscreteTypes (TopCat.of ℕ) A).IsSheaf) ∧
        (presheafToPiTop (TopCat.of ℕ) fun i => TopCat.of (A i)).IsSheaf
