declarations.name: isSheafOnBasis_iff_forall_mem_cofinalSystem
declarations.doc:
**Cofinal systems of coverings and the sheaf condition on a basis.** Let `B` be a basis for
the topology of `X`, let `C` be a cofinal system of coverings (`C U ⊆ Cov_B(U)` for each `U ∈ B`),
and for each covering `𝒰 : U = ⋃ Uᵢ` in `C U` let `ch U hU 𝒰 h𝒰` be given coverings
`Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ = ⋃ Uᵢⱼₖ` by basis elements. A presheaf of sets `F` on `B` is a sheaf on `B` (Stacks 009J,
the condition `(**)` for every covering and every choice of the `Uᵢⱼₖ`) iff `(**)` holds for every
`U ∈ B` and every `𝒰 ∈ C U` with the given coverings `ch U hU 𝒰 h𝒰`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafOnBasis_iff_forall_mem_cofinalSystem
    {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) (C : CofinalSystem B)
    (ch : ∀ (U : Opens X) (hU : U ∈ B) (𝒰 : BasisCovering B U), 𝒰 ∈ C.cov U hU →
      IntersectionCoverings B 𝒰)
    (F : BasisPresheaf B) :
    IsSheafOnBasis hB F.toPresheafOnBasisOpenStruct ↔
      ∀ (U : Opens X) (hU : U ∈ B) (𝒰 : BasisCovering B U) (h𝒰 : 𝒰 ∈ C.cov U hU),
        SheafConditionStarStar F hU 𝒰 (ch U hU 𝒰 h𝒰)
declarations.comment: both directions; the sheaf on B is the Stacks 009J notion, over every choice of intersection coverings, and the coverings of the intersections are given for the coverings in C

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOnBasis.sheaf_iff_cofinal_sheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009L.** Let `B` be a family of subsets closed under intersection of pairs of its
members lying in a common member, and for each `U ∈ B` let `C U` be a cofinal system of coverings
of `U` by members of `B`. Then a presheaf of sets on `B` is a sheaf on `B` if and only if gluing
holds for the coverings in `C U` with compatibility tested on the intersections `Uᵢ ∩ Uⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_iff_cofinal_sheaf {B : Set (Set X)} (hB_inter : ClosedUnderInter B)
    (C : ∀ U ∈ B, Set (Covering.{u, v} B U)) (hC : IsCofinalSystem B C) (F : Presheaf.{u, w} B) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf.{u, v, w} F ↔ F.IsSheafOnCofinal hB_inter C

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.BasisPresheaf.germMap_bijection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project 009M (bijection form).** The germ map `Φ_U` induces
a bijection between `F.obj U hU` and the set of `(*)`-families of germs
over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem germMap_bijection {B : Set (Set X)} (hB : IsTopologicalBasis B)
    (F : PresheafOnBasisOpenSet B) (hF : F.IsSheaf) {U : Set X} (hU : U ∈ B) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun s : F.obj U hU =>
        (⟨germMap F hU s, by
          rw [← germMap_range_eq_conditionStar hB F hF hU]; exact ⟨s, rfl⟩⟩ :
          {f : ∀ x : U, Stalk F x.1 // ConditionStar F f}))

declarations.name: Stacks.BasisExtension.sheaf_extension_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009N.** *Existence.* Given a sheaf `F` of sets on a basis `B`, there exists a sheaf
`Fext` of sets on `X` together with bijections `Fext(U) ≃ F(U)` for `U ∈ B`, compatible with the
restriction maps.

Uniqueness of the extension is `sheaf_extension_unique`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_extension_exists {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (F : BasisPresheaf B) (hF : F.IsSheaf) :
    ∃ (Fext : OpensPresheaf X) (_ : Fext.IsSheaf),
      Nonempty (BasisPresheaf.Iso (Fext.restrictToBasis B) F)

declarations.name: Stacks.BasisExtension.sheaf_extension_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009N.** *Uniqueness.* Any two sheaves on `X` extending the same sheaf `F` on the
basis `B` are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism intertwining the comparison bijections.

Existence of an extension is `sheaf_extension_exists`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_extension_unique {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (F : BasisPresheaf B)
    (Fext : OpensPresheaf X) (hFext : Fext.IsSheaf)
    (ι : BasisPresheaf.Iso (Fext.restrictToBasis B) F)
    (G : OpensPresheaf X) (hG : G.IsSheaf)
    (ι' : BasisPresheaf.Iso (G.restrictToBasis B) F) :
    ∃! Φ : OpensPresheaf.Iso Fext G,
      ∀ (U : B) (s : Fext.obj (U : Opens X)),
        ι'.toEquiv U (Φ.toEquiv (U : Opens X) s) = ι.toEquiv U s

declarations.name: Stacks.OpensBasis.restrictFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009O.** The restriction-to-basis functor
`r : Sh(X) ⥤ Sh(B)`, sending a sheaf on `X` to its restriction to the basis
elements.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def restrictFunctor (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) X ⥤ SheafOnBasis B

declarations.name: Stacks.OpensBasis.restrictFunctor_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009O.** Let `X` be a topological space and let `B` be a basis for
the topology on `X`. The restriction-to-basis functor `r : Sh(X) ⥤ Sh(B)` is an
equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictFunctor_isEquivalence (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) :
    (restrictFunctor (X := X) B hB).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: SheafOnBasis.PresheafOnBasis
declarations.doc:
A presheaf with values in `C` on the basis `B` (Stacks 009P (1)): a functor on the members of
`B` ordered by reverse inclusion.
declarations.statement:
abbrev PresheafOnBasis (B : Basis X) (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] :
    Type max v u

declarations.name: SheafOnBasis.MorphismOnBasis
declarations.doc:
A morphism of presheaves with values in `C` on the basis `B` (Stacks 009P (2)): a natural
transformation.
declarations.statement:
abbrev MorphismOnBasis {B : Basis X} {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (F G : PresheafOnBasis B C) : Type _

declarations.name: SheafOnBasis.underlyingPresheafOnBasis
declarations.doc:
The underlying set-valued presheaf on the basis `B` of a presheaf with values in `C`
(Stacks 009P (3)), obtained by post-composing with a forgetful functor `F₀ : C ⥤ Type v`.
declarations.statement:
def underlyingPresheafOnBasis {B : Basis X} {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (F₀ : C ⥤ Type v) (F : PresheafOnBasis B C) : PresheafOnBasis B (Type v)

declarations.name: SheafOnBasis.SheafOnBasisStruct
declarations.doc:
A sheaf with values in `C` on the basis `B` (Stacks 009P (4)): a presheaf with values in `C`
on `B` together with the sheaf condition on its underlying sets.
declarations.statement:
structure SheafOnBasisStruct (B : Basis X) (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]
    (F₀ : C ⥤ Type v)

declarations.name: Stacks.BasisExtension.extension_of_sheaf_on_basis
declarations.doc:
**Extension of a sheaf on a basis (Stacks 009Q / Lemma 6.30.9).**

Let `(C, F)` be a type of algebraic structure, `B` a basis for `X`, and `F` a sheaf with
values in `C` on `B`.  Then there is a sheaf `Fᵉˣᵗ` with values in `C` on `X`, unique up to
unique isomorphism, whose restriction to `B` is isomorphic to `F`.

* *Existence*: there is a sheaf `Fext` on `X` together with an isomorphism
  `θ : Fext|_B ≅ F.presheaf`.
* *Uniqueness*: any sheaf `G` on `X` equipped with an isomorphism `η : G|_B ≅ F.presheaf`
  admits a unique isomorphism `Φ : G ≅ Fext` compatible with the identifications over `B`,
  i.e. `(restrictIso Φ) ≪≫ θ = η`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extension_of_sheaf_on_basis
    (A : AlgebraicStructureType.{u, w}) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (F : CSheafOnBasis A hB) :
    ∃ (Fext : CSheaf A X)
      (θ : restrictToBasis A B Fext.presheaf ≅ F.presheaf),
      ∀ (G : CSheaf A X) (η : restrictToBasis A B G.presheaf ≅ F.presheaf),
        ∃! Φ : G.presheaf ≅ Fext.presheaf,
          restrictIso A B Φ ≪≫ θ = η

declarations.name: restrictBasisEquivalenceStructures
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a topological space, let `B : ι → Opens X` be a family of opens whose inclusion
into `Opens X` is cover-dense, and let `C` be a category with enough limits. Then restriction
along the inclusion of `B` into `Opens X` is an equivalence from sheaves on `X` with values in
`C` to sheaves with values in `C` on the site `B` with the topology induced from
`Opens.grothendieckTopology X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictBasisEquivalenceStructures
    {X : TopCat.{w}} {ι : Type w} (B : ι → Opens X)
    [(inducedFunctor B).IsCoverDense (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)]
    (C : Type v) [Category.{u} C]
    [∀ Y, Limits.HasLimitsOfShape
        (CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow Y (inducedFunctor B).op) C] :
    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) C ≌
      Sheaf ((inducedFunctor B).inducedTopology
              (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)) C

declarations.name: PresheafOfModulesOnBasis
declarations.doc:
A presheaf of `O`-modules on a basis `B` (Stacks 009S).

Given a presheaf of rings `O` on `B`, a presheaf of `O`-modules on `B` is
a presheaf `F` of abelian groups on `B` together with an `O(U)`-module
structure on `F(U)` for each `U ∈ B`, compatible with restriction in the
sense that `res(r • m) = (res r) • (res m)`.
declarations.statement:
structure PresheafOfModulesOnBasis {B : Set (Set X)}
    (O : PresheafOfRingsOnBasis.{u, w₁} B)
declarations.comment: (1): presheaf of O-modules on a basis

declarations.name: PresheafOfModulesOnBasis.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of presheaves of `O`-modules on `B`.

A morphism `φ : F → G` is a family of `O(U)`-module homomorphisms
`φ(U) : F(U) → G(U)` commuting with restriction.
declarations.comment: (2): morphism of presheaves of O-modules on a basis

declarations.name: SheafOfModulesOnBasis
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of `O`-modules on a basis `B` (Stacks 009S, part 3).

For a sheaf of rings `O` on `B`, a sheaf of `O`-modules on `B` is a presheaf of `O`-modules on
`B` whose underlying presheaf of abelian groups satisfies the sheaf condition.
declarations.statement:
structure SheafOfModulesOnBasis {B : Set (Set X)}
    (O : SheafOfRingsOnBasis.{u, w₁} B)
declarations.comment: (3): sheaf of O-modules on a basis, for a sheaf of rings O

declarations.name: BasesSheaves.exists_moduleStructure_on_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009T (Lemma 6.30.11), the module structure on the extension.**

Let `X` be a topological space, `B` a basis for its topology, `𝒪` a sheaf of rings on `X`
(playing the role of `O^ext`, the extension of a sheaf of rings `O` on `B`), and `N` a sheaf of
`𝒪|_B`-modules on `B` (the sheaf `F`).

Then there is a sheaf of `𝒪`-modules `M` on `X` — its scalar action `𝒪 × M → M` being the
asserted map `O^ext × F^ext → F^ext` — together with an isomorphism
`basis_iso : M|_B ≅ N` of sheaves of `𝒪|_B`-modules, i.e. the module structure agrees with the
given one over elements of `B`. The map is canonical: for any other sheaf of `𝒪`-modules `M'`
with an identification `M'|_B ≅ N` there is a *unique* isomorphism `M ≅ M'` inducing it.

That the underlying abelian sheaf of `M` is `F^ext` is `restrictToSheaf_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_moduleStructure_on_extension {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (𝒪 : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat X) (N : ModuleSheafOnBasis hB 𝒪) :
    ∃ (M : SheafOfModules.{u} 𝒪) (basis_iso : (restrictModuleSheaf hB 𝒪).obj M ≅ N),
      ∀ (M' : SheafOfModules.{u} 𝒪) (θ : (restrictModuleSheaf hB 𝒪).obj M' ≅ N),
        ∃! Φ : M ≅ M', (restrictModuleSheaf hB 𝒪).mapIso Φ ≪≫ θ = basis_iso
declarations.comment: the canonical module structure, agreeing with the given one over elements of B

declarations.name: BasesSheaves.restrictToSheaf_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009T (Lemma 6.30.11), the module structure lives on `F^ext`.**

An isomorphism `M|_B ≅ N` of sheaves of `𝒪|_B`-modules induces an isomorphism of the underlying
abelian sheaves on `B`. Hence the module structure produced by
`exists_moduleStructure_on_extension` is carried by an abelian sheaf on `X` whose restriction to
`B` is the underlying abelian sheaf of `N` — that is, by an extension of `F` off `B`, which by
the uniqueness in Stacks 009Q is `F^ext`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictToSheaf_iso {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (𝒪 : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat X) (M : SheafOfModules.{u} 𝒪) (N : ModuleSheafOnBasis hB 𝒪)
    (basis_iso : (restrictModuleSheaf hB 𝒪).obj M ≅ N) :
    ((basisInclusion B).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat
          (basisGrothendieckTopology hB) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf 𝒪).obj M) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj N
declarations.comment: the module structure is carried by the abelian extension F^ext of F

declarations.name: Stacks.BasisRestriction.restrictModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
The restriction-to-`B` functor on sheaves of `𝒪`-modules.

This is defined as the pushforward along the inclusion `B ↪ Opens X`, applied to
sheaves of modules. The ring-level pushforward sends `𝒪` to its restriction
`𝒪|_B`, so the module-level pushforward goes from `SheafOfModules 𝒪` to
`SheafOfModules (𝒪|_B)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictModuleSheaf {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (𝒪 : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat X) :
    SheafOfModules.{max u w} 𝒪 ⥤ ModuleSheafOnBasis hB 𝒪

declarations.name: Stacks.BasisRestriction.isEquivalence_restrictModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009U.** The restriction-to-`B` functor

  `r : SheafOfModules 𝒪 ⥤ SheafOfModules (𝒪|_B)`,
  `F ↦ F|_B`,

is an equivalence of categories, where `𝒪|_B` is the restriction of the sheaf of
rings `𝒪` to the basis category `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_restrictModuleSheaf {B : Set (Opens X)} (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (𝒪 : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat X) :
    (restrictModuleSheaf (X := X) hB 𝒪 : SheafOfModules.{max u w} 𝒪 ⥤ _).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: fMap_basis_unique_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009V.** Let `B : ι → Opens Y` be a family of opens whose range is a basis of `Y`.
Then every compatible family of basis-level morphisms `φ i : G(B i) ⟶ (f_* F)(B i)` extends to a
unique `f`-map `ψ : G ⟶ f_* F`, i.e. a unique sheaf morphism whose component at each `B i` is
`φ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fMap_basis_unique_extension
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {FC : C → C → Type _} {CC : C → Type v}
    [∀ (X Y : C), FunLike (FC X Y) (CC X) (CC Y)]
    [ConcreteCategory C FC]
    [HasLimits C] [HasColimits C]
    [PreservesLimits (forget C)] [PreservesFilteredColimits (forget C)]
    [(forget C).ReflectsIsomorphisms]
    {X Y : TopCat} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf C X) (G : TopCat.Sheaf C Y)
    {ι : Type w} (B : ι → Opens Y) (hB : Opens.IsBasis (Set.range B))
    (φ : BasisCompatibleFamily f G F B) :
    ∃! ψ : FMapParameterizedC f G F, ∀ i : ι, ψ.hom.app (op (B i)) = φ.app (op i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.existsUnique_fMap_of_basis
declarations.doc:
Unique $f$-map extension from basis-compatible module maps.

Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, $\mathcal{G}$ a sheaf
of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules, and $\mathcal{B}$ a basis for the topology on $Y$.
For every basis-indexed compatible system of $\mathcal{O}_Y(V)$-module homomorphisms
$\varphi_V : \mathcal{G}(V) \to \mathcal{F}(f^{-1}V)$ for $V \in \mathcal{B}$,
there exists a unique $f$-map $\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ whose
basis-restricted family equals $\{\varphi_V\}_{V \in \mathcal{B}}$.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_fMap_of_basis {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (G : ModuleSheaf Y) (F : ModuleSheaf X)
    (B : Set (Opens Y.carrier))
    (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (φ : FMapOnBasis f G F B) :
    ∃! (Φ : FMapModuleSheaf f G F), Φ.restrictToBasis B = φ

declarations.name: main_theorem009X
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 009X (main theorem).** Given a compatible basis family, there is
a unique `f`-map extending it.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem009X (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]
    {FC : C → C → Type*} {CC : C → Type w} [(X Y : C) → FunLike (FC X Y) (CC X) (CC Y)]
    [ConcreteCategory.{w} C FC]
    [HasLimits C]
    [PreservesLimits (CategoryTheory.forget C)]
    [(CategoryTheory.forget C).ReflectsIsomorphisms]
    {X Y : TopCat.{w}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf C X) (G : TopCat.Sheaf C Y)
    (BX : Set (Opens X)) (BY : Set (Opens Y))
    (hBX : Opens.IsBasis BX) (hBY : Opens.IsBasis BY)
    (Φ : CompatibleBasisFamily C f F G BX BY) :
    ∃! (φ : FMapValPresheaf C f F G),
      ∀ (V : Opens Y) (hV : V ∈ BY) (U : Opens X) (hU : U ∈ BX)
        (hfU : U ≤ (Opens.comap f.hom) V),
        Φ.φ V hV U hU hfU = φ.app (op V) ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE hfU).op

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.existsUnique_fMap_of_bases
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 009Y.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of ringed spaces, `F` a sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules, `G` a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules, and `BX`, `BY` bases of the topologies of `X`
and `Y`. Then a compatible system `φ` of maps `G(V) → F(U)`, indexed by the pairs of basis
opens with `U ≤ f⁻¹ V`, extends to a unique `f`-map `ψ : G → F`, and each `φ_V^U` is
recovered from `ψ` as the composite `G(V) → F(f⁻¹ V) → F(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_fMap_of_bases
    {X Y : RingedSpace.{v, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : SheafOfModulesOnRingedSpace X) (G : SheafOfModulesOnRingedSpace Y)
    (BY : Set (Opens Y.carrier)) (BX : Set (Opens X.carrier))
    (hBY : Opens.IsBasis BY) (hBX : Opens.IsBasis BX)
    (φ : BasisCompat f F G BX BY) :
    ∃! ψ : FMapAddGroupHom f F G,
      ∀ {V : Opens Y.carrier} (hV : V ∈ BY)
        {U : Opens X.carrier} (hU : U ∈ BX) (hUV : U ≤ (Opens.map f.hom.base).obj V)
        (g : G.sections V),
        φ.basisApp hV hU hUV g = F.restrict hUV (ψ.app V g)

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.presheaf_pullback_iso_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (1).** For a presheaf of sets `G` on `X`, the presheaf pullback
`j_p G` (the colimit-based left adjoint of `j_*`) is canonically isomorphic to
the naive restriction `V ↦ G(j V)`:
`(j_p G) ≅ restrictPresheaf hj G`.
Componentwise, for every open `V ⊆ U`, the canonical colimit map
`G(j V) → (j_p G)(V)` is a bijection (the colimit defining `(j_p G)(V)`
collapses to its value at the largest neighbourhood `j V = V`). The
isomorphism is exhibited as honest data: it is Mathlib's canonical
`IsOpenMap.pullbackObjIso`, whose `V`-component is the canonical comparison
`pullbackObjObjOfImageOpen`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheaf_pullback_iso_restriction (G : X.Presheaf (Type u)) :
    (Presheaf.pullback (Type u) j).obj G ≅ restrictPresheaf j hj G

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.sheaf_pullback_iso_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (2).** For a sheaf of sets `G` on `X`, the sheaf pullback
`j⁻¹ G` (sheafification of `j_p G`) is canonically isomorphic, as a *sheaf on
`U`*, to the restriction sheaf `restrictSheaf hj G` (no sheafification is needed,
by the sheaf condition built into `restrictSheaf`). The isomorphism lives in the
category `U.Sheaf (Type u)`. It is exhibited as honest data: the `G`-component of
Mathlib's canonical natural isomorphism `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.sheafPullbackIso`
(note `(hj.sheafPullback _).obj G = restrictSheaf hj G` by definition).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheaf_pullback_iso_restriction (G : X.Sheaf (Type u)) :
    (Sheaf.pullback (Type u) j).obj G ≅ restrictSheaf j hj G

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.stalk_sheaf_pullback_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (3).** For a sheaf of sets `G` on `X` and a point `u ∈ U`, the
stalk of the sheaf pullback `j⁻¹ G` at `u` is canonically isomorphic to the
stalk of `G` at `j u`:
`(j⁻¹ G)_u ≅ G_{j u}`.
This is the special case `f = j` of the canonical stalk identity
`(f⁻¹ G)_x ≅ G_{f x}`. It is exhibited as honest data, built from the canonical
comparison maps: the underlying presheaf of `j⁻¹ G` is canonically isomorphic to
the presheaf pullback `j_p (G^♭)` (via clause (2) and
`IsOpenMap.pullbackObjIso`), and `Presheaf.stalkPullbackIso` identifies the
stalk of the presheaf pullback at `u` with the stalk of `G` at `j u`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalk_sheaf_pullback_iso (G : X.Sheaf (Type u)) (u : U) :
    Presheaf.stalk ((Sheaf.pullback (Type u) j).obj G).obj u
      ≅ Presheaf.stalk G.obj ((ConcreteCategory.hom j) u)

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.presheaf_pullback_pushforward_counit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (4).** On the category `PSh(U)` of presheaves of sets on `U`,
the *canonical* natural transformation `j_p ∘ j_* ⟶ id` — namely the counit of
the adjunction `j_p ⊣ j_*` (`pullback ⊣ pushforward`) — is a natural
isomorphism. Equivalently, for every presheaf of sets `F` on `U` and every open
`V ⊆ U`, the canonical map `(j_p j_* F)(V) → F(V)` is a bijection, naturally in
`F`. This exhibits the canonical natural isomorphism `j_p ∘ j_* ≅ id_{PSh(U)}`.
The open-embedding hypothesis `hj` is required: for an arbitrary continuous `j`
this counit need not be an isomorphism.

Proof: A counit of an adjunction `L ⊣ R` is an isomorphism whenever the right
adjoint `R` is fully faithful (`Adjunction.counit_isIso_of_R_fully_faithful`).
Here `R = j_* = Presheaf.pushforward (Type u) j`, which is fully faithful for the
open embedding `j` by `presheafPushforwardFullyFaithful`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_pullback_pushforward_counit_isIso
    (j : U ⟶ X) (hj : Topology.IsOpenEmbedding (ConcreteCategory.hom j)) :
    IsIso (Presheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Type u) j).counit

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.sheaf_pullback_pushforward_counit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (5).** On the category `Sh(U)` of sheaves of sets on `U`, the
*canonical* natural transformation `j⁻¹ ∘ j_* ⟶ id` — namely the counit of the
adjunction `j⁻¹ ⊣ j_*` (`Sheaf.pullback ⊣ Sheaf.pushforward`) — is a natural
isomorphism. Equivalently, for every sheaf of sets `F` on `U` and every open
`V ⊆ U`, the canonical map `(j⁻¹ j_* F)(V) → F(V)` is a bijection, naturally in
`F`. This exhibits the canonical natural isomorphism `j⁻¹ ∘ j_* ≅ id_{Sh(U)}`.
The open-embedding hypothesis `hj` is required: for an arbitrary continuous `j`
this counit need not be an isomorphism.

Proof: As for clause (4), the counit of `Sheaf.pullback ⊣ Sheaf.pushforward`
is an isomorphism because its right adjoint `j_* = Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) j`
is fully faithful for the open embedding `j`
(`sheafPushforwardFullyFaithful`), via
`Adjunction.counit_isIso_of_R_fully_faithful`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_pullback_pushforward_counit_isIso
    (j : U ⟶ X) (hj : Topology.IsOpenEmbedding (ConcreteCategory.hom j)) :
    IsIso (Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Type u) j).counit

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.restrictPresheafAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (1), for presheaves with values in any category `A`.** The restriction
`G ↦ (V ↦ G(V))` of presheaves along the open embedding `j : U ⟶ X` is left adjoint to the
pushforward `j_* = TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward A j`. Since Stacks defines `j_p` as the left
adjoint of `j_*` (Stacks 008C), this says that `j_p G` is given by `V ↦ G(V)` for `V ⊆ U` open.
No hypothesis on `A` is needed. The adjunction is the whiskering of the opposite of the
adjunction `hj.functor ⊣ Opens.map j` of posets of opens.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictPresheafAdjunction :
    restrictPresheafFunctor A j hj ⊣ Presheaf.pushforward A j
declarations.comment:
(1) for presheaves with values in any category: restriction is left adjoint to
  `j_*`, i.e. is `j_p`; see `presheafPullbackIsoRestrict` for Mathlib's colimit-built `j_p`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.presheafPullbackIsoRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (1), Mathlib's `j_p`.** When `A` has colimits, Mathlib's presheaf pullback
`TopCat.Presheaf.pullback A j` (the left Kan extension, computed by colimits) is isomorphic to
the restriction. This is Mathlib's `IsOpenMap.pullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheafPullbackIsoRestrict [HasColimits A] :
    Presheaf.pullback A j ≅ restrictPresheafFunctor A j hj
declarations.comment: (1) for Mathlib's colimit-built `j_p` (Mathlib `IsOpenMap.pullbackIso`)

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.isIso_restrictPresheafAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (4), for presheaves with values in any category `A`.** The counit
`j_p j_* ⟶ 𝟭` of `restrictPresheafAdjunction` is an isomorphism: its component at `F` and `V`
is `F` applied to the isomorphism `V ≅ j⁻¹(j V)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_restrictPresheafAdjunction_counit :
    IsIso (restrictPresheafAdjunction A j hj).counit
declarations.comment: (4) for presheaves with values in any category

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.isIso_presheafPullbackPushforwardAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (4), Mathlib's adjunction.** When `A` has colimits, the counit of Mathlib's
adjunction `TopCat.Presheaf.pullback A j ⊣ TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward A j` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_presheafPullbackPushforwardAdjunction_counit [HasColimits A] :
    IsIso (Presheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction A j).counit
declarations.comment: (4) for Mathlib's `j_p ⊣ j_*`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.restrictSheafAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (2), for sheaves with values in any category `A`.** The restriction
`hj.sheafPullback A : Sh(X, A) ⥤ Sh(U, A)`, `G ↦ (V ↦ G(V))` — a sheaf as it stands, with no
sheafification — is left adjoint to the pushforward `j_* = TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward A j`.
Since Stacks defines `j⁻¹` on sheaves as the left adjoint of `j_*` (Stacks 008C), this says
that `j⁻¹ G` is given by `V ↦ G(V)` for `V ⊆ U` open. No hypothesis on `A` is needed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictSheafAdjunction :
    hj.sheafPullback A ⊣ Sheaf.pushforward A j
declarations.comment:
(2) for sheaves with values in any category: restriction is left adjoint to
  `j_*`, i.e. is `j⁻¹`; see `sheafPullbackIsoRestrict` for Mathlib's sheafified `j⁻¹`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.isIso_restrictSheafAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (5), for sheaves with values in any category `A`.** The counit
`j⁻¹ j_* ⟶ 𝟭` of `restrictSheafAdjunction` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_restrictSheafAdjunction_counit :
    IsIso (restrictSheafAdjunction A j hj).counit
declarations.comment: (5) for sheaves with values in any category

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.restrictStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (3), for presheaves with values in any category `A`.** For a presheaf `G` on
`X` and `u ∈ U`, if the stalk `G_{j u}` (the colimit of `G` over the open neighbourhoods of
`j u`) exists, then so does the stalk at `u` of the restriction `V ↦ G(V)`
(`hasColimit_restrict_nhds`) and the two are canonically isomorphic: the neighbourhoods of
`j u` of the form `j V` are cofinal. No colimits are assumed in `A`. This is the argument of
Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.restrictStalkIso`, which needs `HasColimits A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictStalkIso (G : X.Presheaf A) (u : U)
    [HasColimit ((OpenNhds.inclusion (j u)).op ⋙ G)] :
    haveI := hasColimit_restrict_nhds A j hj G u
    colimit ((OpenNhds.inclusion u).op ⋙ (restrictPresheafFunctor A j hj).obj G) ≅
      colimit ((OpenNhds.inclusion (j u)).op ⋙ G)
declarations.comment: (3) for presheaves with values in any category, stalk of the restriction

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.sheafPullbackIsoRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (2), Mathlib's `j⁻¹`.** Under the hypotheses for which Mathlib constructs the
sheaf pullback `TopCat.Sheaf.pullback A j` (the sheafification of the presheaf pullback), it is
isomorphic to the restriction `hj.sheafPullback A`. This is Mathlib's
`Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.sheafPullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackIsoRestrict :
    Sheaf.pullback A j ≅ hj.sheafPullback A
declarations.comment:
(2) for Mathlib's sheafified `j⁻¹` (Mathlib
  `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.sheafPullbackIso`)

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.isIso_sheafPullbackPushforwardAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (5), Mathlib's adjunction.** The counit of Mathlib's adjunction
`TopCat.Sheaf.pullback A j ⊣ TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward A j` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafPullbackPushforwardAdjunction_counit :
    IsIso (Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction A j).counit
declarations.comment: (5) for Mathlib's `j⁻¹ ⊣ j_*`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.sheafPullbackStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (3), Mathlib's `j⁻¹`.** For a sheaf `G` on `X` and `u ∈ U`, the stalk of
Mathlib's sheaf pullback `j⁻¹ G` at `u` is the stalk of `G` at `j u`:
`(j⁻¹ G)_u ≅ (G|_U)_u ≅ G_{j u}`, through clause (2) and `restrictStalkIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackStalkIso (G : X.Sheaf A) (u : U) :
    Presheaf.stalk ((Sheaf.pullback A j).obj G).obj u ≅
      Presheaf.stalk G.obj ((ConcreteCategory.hom j) u)
declarations.comment: (3) for Mathlib's sheafified `j⁻¹`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.restrictPresheafOfModulesAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (1), for presheaves of modules.** Restriction of presheaves of `R`-modules
along the open embedding `j`, `G ↦ (V ↦ G(V))` as a presheaf of `R|_U`-modules, is left adjoint
to the pushforward `j_*` (with `R`-module structure through `R ⟶ j_* (R|_U)`). Since `j_p` on
presheaves of modules is the left adjoint of `j_*` (Stacks 008U), this says that `j_p G` is
given by `V ↦ G(V)`. Its underlying adjunction of presheaves of abelian groups is
`restrictPresheafAdjunction Ab j hj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictPresheafOfModulesAdjunction :
    restrictPresheafOfModules.{v} j hj R ⊣ pushforwardPresheafOfModules.{v} j hj R
declarations.comment:
(1) for presheaves of modules: restriction is left adjoint to `j_*`, i.e. is
  `j_p`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.isIso_restrictPresheafOfModulesAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (4), for presheaves of modules.** The counit `j_p j_* ⟶ 𝟭` on presheaves of
`R|_U`-modules is an isomorphism: on underlying presheaves of abelian groups it is the counit of
`restrictPresheafAdjunction Ab j hj`, an isomorphism by `isIso_restrictPresheafAdjunction_counit`,
and the forgetful functor to presheaves of abelian groups reflects isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_restrictPresheafOfModulesAdjunction_counit :
    IsIso (restrictPresheafOfModulesAdjunction.{v} j hj R).counit
declarations.comment: (4) for presheaves of modules

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.restrictPresheafOfModulesIsoPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (1), for presheaves of modules, Mathlib's pullback.** Mathlib's
`PresheafOfModules.pullback` along `R ⟶ j_* (R|_U)` — the left adjoint of `j_*` — is the
restriction `G ↦ (V ↦ G(V))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictPresheafOfModulesIsoPullback :
    restrictPresheafOfModules.{v} j hj R ≅
      PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} (ringHomPushforwardRestrict j hj R)
declarations.comment: (1) for presheaves of modules, Mathlib's `PresheafOfModules.pullback`

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.isIso_restrictSheafOfModulesAdj_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (5), for sheaves of modules.** The counit `j⁻¹ j_* ⟶ 𝟭` of the adjunction
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.restrictSheafOfModulesAdj` between restriction of sheaves of modules
along the open embedding `f` and `j_*` is an isomorphism: its component at `F` and `V` is
restriction along the equality `V = f⁻¹(f V)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_restrictSheafOfModulesAdj_counit :
    IsIso (restrictSheafOfModulesAdj.{v} hf R).counit
declarations.comment: (5) for sheaves of modules

declarations.name: OpenImmersionSheaves.restrictSheafOfModulesIsoPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A0 (2), for sheaves of modules.** For a sheaf of `R`-modules `G`, `j⁻¹ G` — the
pullback of sheaves of modules along `R ⟶ j_* (R|_U)`, i.e. the left adjoint of `j_*` (Mathlib's
`SheafOfModules.pullback`, Stacks 008Y) — is given by the rule `V ↦ G(V)`: it is isomorphic to
the restriction `Stacks.SheafOfModules.restrictSheafOfModules hf R`, whose underlying presheaf
is `V ↦ G(f V)` and needs no sheafification.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictSheafOfModulesIsoPullback :
    restrictSheafOfModules.{v} hf R ≅
      SheafOfModules.pullback.{v} (pushforwardSheafOfRingsHom hf R)
declarations.comment: (2) for sheaves of modules: Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.pullback` is restriction

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.stalkRestrictIso
registrations.comment:
(3) for sheaves of modules: the stalk of the restriction of a sheaf of
  modules at `z` is its stalk at `f z`, semilinearly over the identification of stalks of rings

declarations.name: restrictPresheaf
declarations.doc:
Restriction of a presheaf to an open subset: precomposition with the
opposite of the open-embedding functor on opens.
declarations.statement:
def restrictPresheaf
    {C : Type*} [Category C] {X : TopCat}
    (G : TopCat.Presheaf C X) (U : Opens X) :
    TopCat.Presheaf C ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U)

declarations.name: local_restrictSheaf
declarations.doc: Restriction of a sheaf to an open subset, via the open-embedding sheaf pullback.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def local_restrictSheaf
    {A : Type*} [Category A] {X : TopCat}
    (G : TopCat.Sheaf A X) (U : Opens X) :
    TopCat.Sheaf A ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U)

declarations.name: openSubspace
declarations.doc: Open subspace of a ringed space `(X, 𝒪)` associated to an open `U ⊆ X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def openSubspace
    (X : SheafedSpace CommRingCat) (U : Opens X) :
    SheafedSpace CommRingCat

declarations.name: restrictPresheafOfModules
declarations.doc:
Restriction of a presheaf of `𝒪`-modules to an open subset, via
`PresheafOfModules.pushforward` along the open-embedding functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictPresheafOfModules
    {X : TopCat} (𝒪 : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat) (U : Opens X) :
    PresheafOfModules 𝒪 ⥤ PresheafOfModules (restrictPresheaf 𝒪 U)

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitial
declarations.doc:
**Extension by an initial object.** For `j : U → X` the inclusion of an open subset,
`C` a category with initial object `e`, and `F` a presheaf on `U` with values in `C`, this is
the presheaf `j_{p!}F` on `X` with `j_{p!}F(V) = F(V)` for `V ⊆ U` and `j_{p!}F(V) = e`
otherwise, with the obvious restriction maps.

When `C` is a category of algebraic structures its zero object is initial, so this is the
classical extension by zero of an abelian presheaf; and the initial object of `Type` is the
empty type, so this is also the extension by the empty set of a presheaf of sets.

The other clauses of Stacks 00A4 are registered on: `extendByInitialSheafify` and
`extendByInitialSheaf` (2), the sheafification of `j_{p!}` for abelian sheaves;
`AlgebraicStructureType.extendByInitialSheaf` (4), for sheaves of algebraic structures, whose
sheafification is constructed rather than assumed; `extendByZeroPresheafOfModules` (5) and
`extendByZeroSheafOfModules` (6), for (pre)sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitial (F : Presheaf C (sp U)) : Presheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialFunctor
declarations.doc: **Extension by an initial object, as a functor.** `j_{p!} : PSh(U) ⥤ PSh(X)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitialFunctor : Presheaf C (sp U) ⥤ Presheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheafify
declarations.doc:
**Extension by an initial object for sheaves.** The extension `j_! F` of a sheaf `F` on
`U` is the sheafification of the presheaf `j_{p!}F`.

For a category of algebraic structures the initial object is the zero object, so this is the
classical extension by zero of a sheaf; for `C = Type` the initial object is the empty type, so
this is the extension by the empty set.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialSheafify :
    Presheaf C (sp U) ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Extension by an initial object, as a functor on sheaves.** `j_! : Sh(U) ⥤ Sh(X)` sends a
sheaf `F` on `U` to the sheafification of `j_{p!}F`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitialSheaf : TopCat.Sheaf C (sp U) ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction, presheaf level.** For `j : U → X` the
inclusion of an open subset, `j_{p!}` is a left adjoint of the restriction functor `j_p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialAdjunction :
    extendByInitialFunctor (C := C) U ⊣ restrictToOpen U
declarations.comment: (1) j_{p!} is a left adjoint to the restriction functor j_p

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.restrictExtendByInitialIso
declarations.doc:
**`j_p j_{p!} = id`.** The extension by an initial object of a presheaf on `U` restricts
back to that presheaf, naturally in the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictExtendByInitialIso :
    extendByInitialFunctor (C := C) U ⋙ restrictToOpen U ≅ 𝟭 (Presheaf C (sp U))
declarations.comment: (4) on presheaves on U we have j_p j_{p!} = id

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheafAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction, sheaf level.** `j_!` is a left adjoint of
the restriction functor `j^{-1} : Sh(X) ⥤ Sh(U)`, i.e.
`Mor_{Sh(X)}(j_!F, G) = Mor_{Sh(U)}(F, G|_U)` bifunctorially.

Here `j^{-1}` is `TopologicalSpace.Opens.sheafRestrict U`, which is `G ↦ (W ↦ G(j(W)))` with no
sheafification.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialSheafAdjunction :
    extendByInitialSheaf U ⊣ Opens.sheafRestrict (C := C) U
declarations.comment: (2) j_! is a left adjoint to restriction on sheaves

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.restrictExtendByInitialSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**`j^{-1} j_! = id`.** The extension by an initial object of a sheaf on `U` restricts back
to that sheaf, naturally in the sheaf. This is the unit of `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}`, inverted.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictExtendByInitialSheafIso :
    extendByInitialSheaf U ⋙ Opens.sheafRestrict (C := C) U ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: (5) on sheaves on U we have j^{-1} j_! = id

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.isInitialStalkExtendByInitialSheafify
declarations.doc:
The stalk of `j_!F` at a point `x ∉ U` is an initial object.
For sheaves of sets the initial object is `∅`, so this is `(j_!F)_x = ∅`; for abelian sheaves
it is the zero object.
declarations.comment: (3) the stalk of j_!F at x ∉ U is initial (∅ for sheaves of sets)

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.stalkExtendByInitialSheafifyIso
declarations.doc: The stalk of `j_!F` at a point `j(x)` with `x ∈ U` is the stalk of `F` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkExtendByInitialSheafifyIso (F : Presheaf C (sp U)) (x : sp U) :
    ((extendByInitialSheafify U).obj F).presheaf.stalk (U.inclusion' x) ≅ F.stalk x
declarations.comment: (3) the stalk of j_!F at a point of U is the stalk of F

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.isEmpty_stalk_extendByInitialSheafify
declarations.doc:
For a presheaf of sets `F` on `U`, the stalk of `j_!F` at a point outside `U` is empty:
`(j_!F)_x = ∅`. This gives the inclusion of the essential image of `j_!` in the sheaves with
empty stalks outside `U`; the complete Stacks 00A8 is
`TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheaf_full_faithful_and_mem_essImage_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_stalk_extendByInitialSheafify {X : TopCat.{u}} (U : Opens X)
    (F : Presheaf (Type u) (sp U)) {x : X} (hx : x ∉ U) :
    IsEmpty (stalk ((extendByInitialSheafify U).obj F).presheaf x)
declarations.comment: (3) for sheaves of sets: (j_!F)_x = ∅ for x ∉ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.extendByInitialSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Extension by the initial object of a sheaf of algebraic structures.** For `(C, F)` a type
of algebraic structure such that `C` has an initial object `e`, the extension `j_!𝓕` by `e` of a
sheaf `𝓕` of algebraic structures on `U` is the sheafification of the presheaf `j_{p!}𝓕`, as a
functor `Sh(U, C) ⥤ Sh(X, C)`. The sheafification is `sheafifyFunctor`, the plus construction
applied twice, which exists for every type of algebraic structure, so no sheafification
hypothesis on `C` is made.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitialSheaf : TopCat.Sheaf S.C (sp U) ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf S.C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitial
declarations.doc:
**Extension by an initial object.** For `j : U → X` the inclusion of an open subset,
`C` a category with initial object `e`, and `F` a presheaf on `U` with values in `C`, this is
the presheaf `j_{p!}F` on `X` with `j_{p!}F(V) = F(V)` for `V ⊆ U` and `j_{p!}F(V) = e`
otherwise, with the obvious restriction maps.

When `C` is a category of algebraic structures its zero object is initial, so this is the
classical extension by zero of an abelian presheaf; and the initial object of `Type` is the
empty type, so this is also the extension by the empty set of a presheaf of sets.

The other clauses of Stacks 00A4 are registered on: `extendByInitialSheafify` and
`extendByInitialSheaf` (2), the sheafification of `j_{p!}` for abelian sheaves;
`AlgebraicStructureType.extendByInitialSheaf` (4), for sheaves of algebraic structures, whose
sheafification is constructed rather than assumed; `extendByZeroPresheafOfModules` (5) and
`extendByZeroSheafOfModules` (6), for (pre)sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitial (F : Presheaf C (sp U)) : Presheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialFunctor
declarations.doc: **Extension by an initial object, as a functor.** `j_{p!} : PSh(U) ⥤ PSh(X)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitialFunctor : Presheaf C (sp U) ⥤ Presheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheafify
declarations.doc:
**Extension by an initial object for sheaves.** The extension `j_! F` of a sheaf `F` on
`U` is the sheafification of the presheaf `j_{p!}F`.

For a category of algebraic structures the initial object is the zero object, so this is the
classical extension by zero of a sheaf; for `C = Type` the initial object is the empty type, so
this is the extension by the empty set.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialSheafify :
    Presheaf C (sp U) ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Extension by an initial object, as a functor on sheaves.** `j_! : Sh(U) ⥤ Sh(X)` sends a
sheaf `F` on `U` to the sheafification of `j_{p!}F`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByInitialSheaf : TopCat.Sheaf C (sp U) ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf C X

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByZeroPresheafOfModules
declarations.doc:
**Extension by zero of a presheaf of modules** (Stacks 00A4 (5)). Let `𝒪` be a presheaf of
rings on `X` and `ℱ` a presheaf of `𝒪|_U`-modules, where `𝒪|_U` is the presheaf `W ↦ 𝒪(j(W))`
on `U`. The extension by zero `j_{p!}ℱ` is the presheaf of `𝒪`-modules which is equal to the
extension by zero `j_{p!}ℱ` of the underlying abelian presheaf of `ℱ`
(`extendByZeroPresheafOfModules_presheaf`), endowed with the multiplication
`𝒪 × j_{p!}ℱ → j_{p!}ℱ`: over an open `V ⊆ U` a section of `𝒪` acts on `ℱ(j⁻¹ V)` through
its restriction to `𝒪|_U(j⁻¹ V)` (`extendByZeroPresheafOfModules_smul_of_le`), and over an open
`V ⊄ U` the sections form the zero module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByZeroPresheafOfModules (F : PresheafOfModules.{v} ((imF U).op ⋙ O)) :
    PresheafOfModules.{v} O

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByZeroSheafOfModules
declarations.doc:
**Extension by zero of a sheaf of modules** (Stacks 00A4 (6)). Let `𝒪` be a sheaf of rings
on `X` and `ℱ` a sheaf of `𝒪|_U`-modules. The extension by zero `j_!ℱ` is the sheaf of
`𝒪`-modules which is equal to the extension by zero `j_!ℱ` of the underlying abelian sheaf of
`ℱ`, i.e. the sheafification of `j_{p!}ℱ` (`extendByZeroSheafOfModules_val_presheaf`), endowed
with the multiplication `𝒪 × j_!ℱ → j_!ℱ` induced by that of `j_{p!}ℱ`: the sheafification map
`j_{p!}ℱ ⟶ j_!ℱ` is `𝒪`-linear (`toExtendByZeroSheafOfModules`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByZeroSheafOfModules
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Opens.sheafRestrict U).obj O)) :
    SheafOfModules.{u} O

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction, presheaf level.** For `j : U → X` the
inclusion of an open subset, `j_{p!}` is a left adjoint of the restriction functor `j_p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialAdjunction :
    extendByInitialFunctor (C := C) U ⊣ restrictToOpen U

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.restrictExtendByInitialIso
declarations.doc:
**`j_p j_{p!} = id`.** The extension by an initial object of a presheaf on `U` restricts
back to that presheaf, naturally in the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictExtendByInitialIso :
    extendByInitialFunctor (C := C) U ⋙ restrictToOpen U ≅ 𝟭 (Presheaf C (sp U))

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheafAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction, sheaf level.** `j_!` is a left adjoint of
the restriction functor `j^{-1} : Sh(X) ⥤ Sh(U)`, i.e.
`Mor_{Sh(X)}(j_!F, G) = Mor_{Sh(U)}(F, G|_U)` bifunctorially.

Here `j^{-1}` is `TopologicalSpace.Opens.sheafRestrict U`, which is `G ↦ (W ↦ G(j(W)))` with no
sheafification.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialSheafAdjunction :
    extendByInitialSheaf U ⊣ Opens.sheafRestrict (C := C) U

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.restrictExtendByInitialSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**`j^{-1} j_! = id`.** The extension by an initial object of a sheaf on `U` restricts back
to that sheaf, naturally in the sheaf. This is the unit of `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}`, inverted.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictExtendByInitialSheafIso :
    extendByInitialSheaf U ⋙ Opens.sheafRestrict (C := C) U ≅ 𝟭 _

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.isZero_stalk_extendByInitialSheafify
declarations.doc:
When the value category has a zero object — as the categories of abelian groups and of
modules do — the stalk of `j_!F` at a point `x ∉ U` is a *zero* object.

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.stalkExtendByInitialSheafifyIso
declarations.doc: The stalk of `j_!F` at a point `j(x)` with `x ∈ U` is the stalk of `F` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkExtendByInitialSheafifyIso (F : Presheaf C (sp U)) (x : sp U) :
    ((extendByInitialSheafify U).obj F).presheaf.stalk (U.inclusion' x) ≅ F.stalk x

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.extendByInitialAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A6 (1).** On presheaves of algebraic structures, the extension by the initial
object `j_{p!}` is a left adjoint of the restriction functor `j_p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialAdjunction :
    extendByInitialFunctor (C := S.C) U ⊣ restrictToOpen U
declarations.comment: (1) j_{p!} is a left adjoint to the restriction functor j_p

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.restrictExtendByInitialIso
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00A6 (4).** On presheaves of algebraic structures on `U`, `j_p j_{p!} = id`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictExtendByInitialIso :
    extendByInitialFunctor (C := S.C) U ⋙ restrictToOpen U ≅ 𝟭 (TopCat.Presheaf S.C (sp U))
declarations.comment: (4) on presheaves of algebraic structures on U we have j_p j_{p!} = id

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.extendByInitialSheafAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A6 (2).** `j_!` is a left adjoint of the restriction `j^{-1} : Sh(X, C) ⥤ Sh(U, C)`,
`𝓖 ↦ 𝓖|_U`: `Mor(j_!𝓕, 𝓖) = Mor(𝓕, 𝓖|_U)` bifunctorially in `𝓕` and `𝓖`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendByInitialSheafAdjunction :
    S.extendByInitialSheaf U ⊣ Opens.sheafRestrict (C := S.C) U
declarations.comment: (2) j_! is a left adjoint to restriction on sheaves, bifunctorially

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.restrictExtendByInitialSheafIso
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00A6 (5).** On sheaves of algebraic structures on `U`, `j^{-1} j_! = id`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictExtendByInitialSheafIso :
    S.extendByInitialSheaf U ⋙ Opens.sheafRestrict (C := S.C) U ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment: (5) on sheaves of algebraic structures on U we have j^{-1} j_! = id

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.isInitialStalkExtendByInitialSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A6 (3), points outside `U`.** For a sheaf `𝓕` of algebraic structures on `U`
and `x ∉ U`, the stalk `(j_!𝓕)_x` is the initial object `e`.
declarations.comment: (3) the stalk of j_!F at a point x ∉ U is the initial object e

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.stalkExtendByInitialSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A6 (3), points of `U`.** For a sheaf `𝓕` of algebraic structures on `U` and
`x ∈ U`, the stalk `(j_!𝓕)_x` is the stalk `𝓕_x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkExtendByInitialSheafIso (F : TopCat.Sheaf S.C (sp U)) {x : X}
    (hx : x ∈ U) :
    (CategoryStalk.stalkFunctor S.C x).obj ((S.extendByInitialSheaf U).obj F).obj ≅
      (CategoryStalk.stalkFunctor S.C (⟨x, hx⟩ : sp U)).obj F.obj
declarations.comment: (3) the stalk of j_!F at a point x ∈ U is the stalk F_x

declarations.name: ExtensionByZeroModules.extendByZeroAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A7 (1).** The explicit extension by zero `j_{p!}` of presheaves of modules
(`V ↦ F(V)` for `V ⊆ U`, `V ↦ 0` otherwise, `ExtensionByZeroModules.extendByZero`) is left adjoint
to the restriction functor `PMod(𝒪) ⥤ PMod(𝒪|_U)`, `G ↦ G|_U`: `Hom(j_{p!}F, G) = Hom(F, G|_U)`,
naturally in `F` and `G`. The bijection sends `φ` to `t ↦ φ(t)` over opens of `U`, and `ψ` to
the map which is `ψ` over opens `V ⊆ U` and zero over the other opens.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendByZeroAdjunction : extendByZero U O ⊣ jpStar U O
declarations.comment: (1): `j_{p!}` is the explicit extension by zero of presheaves of modules

declarations.name: ExtensionByZeroModules.jShriekExplicitAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A7 (2).** Extension by zero `j_!` of sheaves of modules, the sheafification of the
explicit `j_{p!}`, is left adjoint to the restriction functor `Mod(𝒪) ⥤ Mod(𝒪|_U)`:
`Hom(j_!F, G) = Hom(F, G|_U)`, naturally in `F` and `G`. It is obtained from the adjunction of (1)
and the sheafification adjunction, through the identification `jShriekExplicitIso`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jShriekExplicitAdjunction : jShriekExplicit U O ⊣ jStar U O
declarations.comment: (2): `j_!` is the sheafification of the explicit `j_{p!}`

declarations.name: ExtensionByZeroModules.isZero_stalk_jShriekExplicit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A7 (3), points outside `U`.** For a sheaf `F` of `𝒪|_U`-modules and `x ∉ U`, the
stalk `(j_!F)_x` is zero. The statement is about the underlying abelian group of the
`𝒪_{X,x}`-module `(j_!F)_x`, which vanishes exactly when the module does.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_stalk_jShriekExplicit (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O)) (x : X) (hx : x ∉ U) :
    IsZero (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (X := X) ((jShriekExplicit U O).obj F).val.presheaf x)
declarations.comment: (3), the stalk of `j_!F` at `x ∉ U` is zero

declarations.name: ExtensionByZeroModules.jShriekExplicitCompJStarIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A7 (4).** `j^{-1} j_! = id` on sheaves of `𝒪|_U`-modules: restricting the extension
by zero of `F` back to `U` gives `F`, naturally in `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jShriekExplicitCompJStarIso :
    jShriekExplicit U O ⋙ jStar U O ≅ 𝟭 (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O))
declarations.comment: (4): `j^{-1} j_! ≅ id` on sheaves of `𝒪|_U`-modules

declarations.name: ExtensionByZeroModules.stalkJShriekExplicitLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A7 (3), points of `U`.** For a sheaf `F` of `𝒪|_U`-modules and a point `x ∈ U`
(written `x = j u` with `u` the point `x` of the subspace `U`), the stalk `(j_!F)_x` is `F_x` as
modules. The stalk `(j_!F)_x` is an `𝒪_{X,x}`-module, `F_x` is an
`𝒪|_U,x`-module, and the identification is linear along the canonical isomorphism
`𝒪_{X,x} ≅ 𝒪|_U,x` (`stalkResRingIso`): it is an isomorphism of `𝒪_{X,x}`-modules from
`(j_!F)_x` to `F_x` with scalars restricted along that ring isomorphism. Its underlying additive
map is `stalkJShriekExplicitAddIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkJShriekExplicitLinearEquiv (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O))
    (u : Usp U) :
    TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (X := X)
        ((jShriekExplicit U O).obj F).val.presheaf (U.inclusion' u) ≃ₗ[
          TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := RingCat.{u}) (X := X) O.obj (U.inclusion' u)]
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (stalkResRingIso U O u).hom.hom).obj
        (ModuleCat.of
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := RingCat.{u}) (X := Usp U) (resRing U O).obj u)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (X := Usp U) F.val.presheaf u))
declarations.comment: (3), the stalk of `j_!F` at `x ∈ U` is `F_x`, linearly over `𝒪_{X,x} ≅ 𝒪|_U,x`

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.extendByInitialSheaf_full_faithful_and_mem_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A8.** Let `j : U → X` be the inclusion of an open subset. The functor
`j_! : Sh(U) ⥤ Sh(X)` on sheaves of sets is fully faithful, and its essential image consists
exactly of the sheaves `G` on `X` with `G_x = ∅` for all `x ∈ X \ U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extendByInitialSheaf_full_faithful_and_mem_essImage_iff :
    (extendByInitialSheaf (C := Type u) U).Full ∧
      (extendByInitialSheaf (C := Type u) U).Faithful ∧
      ∀ G : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) X,
        (extendByInitialSheaf U).essImage G ↔ ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → IsEmpty (G.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: ExtensionByZero.jExt_full
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A9 (1).** The extension by zero functor `j_!` is full: every morphism
`j_! F ⟶ j_! F'` of sheaves on `X` comes from a morphism `F ⟶ F'` of sheaves on `U`.
declarations.statement: theorem jExt_full : (jExt U).Full

declarations.name: ExtensionByZero.jExt_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A9 (1).** The extension by zero functor `j_!` is faithful: a morphism of sheaves
on `U` is determined by the morphism it induces on the extensions by zero.
declarations.statement: theorem jExt_faithful : (jExt U).Faithful

declarations.name: ExtensionByZero.jExt_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00A9 (2), description of the essential image.** An abelian sheaf `G` on `X` lies in
the essential image of `j_!` if and only if the stalk `G_x` is the zero abelian group for every
point `x ∈ X` not belonging to `U`.

For "only if", an isomorphism `G ≅ j_! F` induces an isomorphism of stalks, and the stalk of
`j_! F` at a point outside `U` is zero. For "if", the vanishing hypothesis makes the counit
`j_! (j⁻¹ G) ⟶ G` an isomorphism, which exhibits `G` in the essential image.
declarations.statement:
theorem jExt_essImage (G : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X) :
    (jExt U).essImage G ↔ ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → IsZero (G.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicStructureType.extendByInitialSheaf_full_faithful_and_mem_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AA.** Let `X` be a topological space, `j : U → X` the inclusion of an open
subset, and `(C, F)` a type of algebraic structure (Stacks 007L) such that `C` has an initial
object `e`. Then `j_! : Sh(U, C) ⥤ Sh(X, C)` is fully faithful, and its essential image
consists exactly of the sheaves `𝓖` with `𝓖_x = e` (that is, `𝓖_x` initial) for all
`x ∈ X ∖ U`.

The homs of `C` live in the universe of `X` and its objects in any universe, so `C` may be
`Type v`, `Ab.{v}`, `CommRingCat.{v}`, …; nothing beyond 007L and the initial object is
assumed. `j_!` is `extendByInitialSheaf`, the sheafification of the source's `j_{p!}`, and
the stalk is the filtered colimit of Stacks 007H.
declarations.statement:
theorem extendByInitialSheaf_full_faithful_and_mem_essImage_iff :
    (S.extendByInitialSheaf U).Full ∧ (S.extendByInitialSheaf U).Faithful ∧
      ∀ G : TopCat.Sheaf S.C X, (S.extendByInitialSheaf U).essImage G ↔
        ∀ x : X, x ∉ U →
          Nonempty (IsInitial ((CategoryStalk.stalkFunctor S.C x).obj G.obj))

declarations.name: ExtensionByZeroModules.full_and_faithful_and_essImage_jShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AB.** Let `(X, 𝒪)` be a ringed space and let `j : (U, 𝒪|_U) → (X, 𝒪)` be an open
subspace. The extension-by-zero functor `j_! : Mod(𝒪|_U) ⥤ Mod(𝒪)` is fully faithful, and its
essential image consists exactly of those sheaves `G` of `𝒪`-modules with `G_x = 0` for all
`x ∈ X ∖ U`.

The stalk `G_x` is a module over the stalk `𝒪_x` whose underlying abelian group is the stalk of
the underlying abelian sheaf of `G` (Mathlib's `PresheafOfModules.instModuleStalk`), and a module
is zero exactly when its underlying group is; so `G_x = 0` is expressed here as vanishing of that
abelian group. The sheaf of rings is allowed to be non-commutative, which is more general than
the ringed spaces of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_and_faithful_and_essImage_jShriek :
    (jShriek U O).Full ∧ (jShriek U O).Faithful ∧
      ∀ G : SheafOfModules.{u} O, (jShriek U O).essImage G ↔
        ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → IsZero (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (X := X) G.val.presheaf x)

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.isEmpty_isTerminal_extendByInitialSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AC, first half.** For `U ≠ X` the sheaf `j_!F` is not a final object of
`Sh(X, Type)`, whatever the sheaf `F` on `U` is. In particular `j_!` does not transform a final
object of `Sh(U)` into a final object of `Sh(X)`.

A final object of a category of sheaves of sets has a one-point set of sections over every open,
because `Sheaf.forget` and evaluation at an open both preserve limits; but the global sections of
`j_!F` are empty by `isEmpty_sections_extendByInitialSheafify`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_isTerminal_extendByInitialSheaf (hU : U ≠ ⊤)
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (sp U)) :
    IsEmpty (IsTerminal ((extendByInitialSheaf U).obj F))
declarations.comment: j_! does not transform a final object of Sh(U) into a final object of Sh(X)

declarations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.not_preservesFiniteLimits_extendByInitialSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AC.** For `U ≠ X` the functor `j_! : Sh(U, Type) ⥤ Sh(X, Type)` does not preserve
finite limits, i.e. it is not left exact.

The final object is the limit of the empty diagram, so a functor preserving finite limits would
send the final object of `Sh(U, Type)` to a final object of `Sh(X, Type)`, contradicting
`isEmpty_isTerminal_extendByInitialSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_preservesFiniteLimits_extendByInitialSheaf (hU : U ≠ ⊤) :
    ¬ PreservesFiniteLimits
      (extendByInitialSheaf U : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (sp U) ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) X)
declarations.comment: j_! is not left exact as a functor between the categories of sheaves of sets

declarations.name: ClosedImmersionSheaves.isTerminalStalkPushforwardOfNotMemRange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AE, the stalks of `i_* F` away from `Z`.** For `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed embedding,
`F` a sheaf on `Z` and `x ∈ X` not in the image of `i`, the stalk `(i_* F)_x` is a terminal
object of the target category: a singleton for sheaves of sets, `0` for abelian sheaves, a
final object for sheaves of algebraic structures.

The complement of the (closed) image is an open neighbourhood `W` of `x` with `i⁻¹(W) = ∅`,
so `pushforwardStalkIsoOfEmptyPreimage` identifies the stalk with the terminal object
`(i_* F)(W) = F(∅)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTerminalStalkPushforwardOfNotMemRange
    (hi : IsClosedEmbedding (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) (x : X)
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) :
    IsTerminal (stalk (i _* F) x)

declarations.name: ClosedImmersionSheaves.sheaf_pullback_pushforward_counit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AE, `i⁻¹ i_* = id`.** For an inducing `i : Z ⟶ X` — in particular for the
inclusion of a closed subset — the counit `i⁻¹ i_* ⟶ 𝟭` of the adjunction
`i⁻¹ ⊣ i_*` between categories of sheaves is a natural isomorphism, because its right
adjoint `i_*` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_pullback_pushforward_counit_isIso
    (hi : IsInducing (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) :
    IsIso (Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction A i).counit

registrations.name: TopCat.Presheaf.stalkPushforward.stalkPushforward_iso_of_isInducing
registrations.comment:
The stalk of `i_* F` at a point `i z` of the closed subset `Z` is
  `F_z`, via the canonical comparison map `stalkPushforward`. Mathlib proves this for any
  inducing map, and a closed embedding is inducing.

declarations.name: pushforward00AF_fullyFaithful_and_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AF.** For the inclusion `i : Z → X` of a closed subset, the functor
`i_* : Sh(Z) → Sh(X)` on sheaves of sets is fully faithful, and its essential image consists
exactly of the sheaves `G` with `G_x = {*}` for all `x ∈ X \ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward00AF_fullyFaithful_and_essImage_iff (X : TopCat.{u}) {Z : Set X}
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    (pushforward00AF X Z).Full ∧ (pushforward00AF X Z).Faithful ∧
      ∀ G : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) X,
        (pushforward00AF X Z).essImage G ↔ ∀ x : X, x ∉ Z → StalkIsSingleton X G x
declarations.comment:
Full faithfulness holds for any subset `Z`; closedness is used for the
  essential image.

declarations.name: closedInclusion_pushforward_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AG, faithfulness.** The pushforward of sheaves of abelian groups along a closed
embedding is a faithful functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedInclusion_pushforward_faithful
    (Z X : TopCat.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i.hom) :
    (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).Faithful

declarations.name: closedInclusion_pushforward_full
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AG, fullness.** The pushforward of sheaves of abelian groups along a closed
embedding is a full functor: every morphism `i_* 𝒜 ⟶ i_* ℬ` is `i_*` of a morphism `𝒜 ⟶ ℬ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedInclusion_pushforward_full
    (Z X : TopCat.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i.hom) :
    (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).Full

declarations.name: closedInclusion_pushforward_essImage_stalk_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AG, essential image.** If a sheaf `G` of abelian groups on `X` lies in the
essential image of the pushforward along a closed embedding `i`, then the stalk of `G` vanishes
at every point outside the range of `i`. The converse is
`Stacks.ClosedImmersion.essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_forall_stalk_isZero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedInclusion_pushforward_essImage_stalk_isZero
    (Z X : TopCat.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i.hom)
    (G : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X)
    (hG : (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).essImage G) :
    ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range i.hom → IsZero (Presheaf.stalk G.obj x)

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.closedInclusionPushforward_full_faithful_and_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AG.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed embedding of topological spaces. The
pushforward `i_* : Ab(Z) ⥤ Ab(X)` on sheaves of abelian groups is fully faithful, and its
essential image consists exactly of the sheaves `G` with `G_x = 0` for every `x ∈ X` outside
the image of `i`.

Fullness and faithfulness are `closedInclusion_pushforward_full` and
`closedInclusion_pushforward_faithful`; the description of the essential image, in both
directions, is `essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_forall_stalk_isZero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedInclusionPushforward_full_faithful_and_essImage_iff
    (hi : IsClosedEmbedding i.hom) :
    (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).Full ∧ (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).Faithful ∧
      ∀ G : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X, (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).essImage G ↔
        ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range i.hom → IsZero (G.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: Stacks.full_and_faithful_sheafPushforward_subsetInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AH, part 1, in its general form.** For `X : TopCat.{u}`, any subset
`Z ⊆ X` with inclusion `i : Z ↪ X`, and any type of algebraic structure `(C, F)`
whose objects live in an arbitrary universe `w` (so that `CommRingCat.{u}`, `Ab.{u}`,
… are instances), the pushforward functor `i_* : Sh(Z, C) ⥤ Sh(X, C)` is full and
faithful. The proof only uses that `Opens.map i` is surjective on opens, so `Z` may
be an arbitrary subset (Stacks takes `Z` closed); closedness is needed only for
`essImage_sheafPushforward_subsetInclusion_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_and_faithful_sheafPushforward_subsetInclusion (X : TopCat.{u}) (Z : Set X)
    (S : AlgebraicStructureType.{u, w}) :
    (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward S.C (subsetInclusion X Z)).Full ∧
      (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward S.C (subsetInclusion X Z)).Faithful
declarations.comment: fully faithful part; holds for any subset `Z`

declarations.name: Stacks.essImage_sheafPushforward_subsetInclusion_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AH, part 2, in its general form.** Let `X : TopCat.{u}`, let `Z ⊆ X`
be closed with inclusion `i : Z ↪ X`, and let `(C, F)` be a type of algebraic structure
with a final object `0`, whose objects live in an arbitrary universe `w` (so that
`CommRingCat.{u}`, `Ab.{u}`, … are instances). A sheaf `G ∈ Sh(X, C)` lies in the
essential image of `i_* : Sh(Z, C) ⥤ Sh(X, C)` exactly when its stalk `G_x` at every
point `x ∉ Z` is isomorphic in `C` to `0`.

The stalk `G_x` is written as the colimit of `G` over the open neighbourhoods of `x`,
which is a filtered colimit and so exists by 007L. This is literally the definition of
Mathlib's `TopCat.Presheaf.stalk G.obj x`; that API is not used directly because it
requires `HasColimits C`, more than 007L provides. Whenever `C` has all colimits the two
are definitionally equal (see `essImage_pushforward_subsetInclusion_iff`).
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_sheafPushforward_subsetInclusion_iff (X : TopCat.{u}) (Z : Set X)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) (S : AlgebraicStructureType.{u, w}) (Sfinal : S.WithFinal)
    (G : TopCat.Sheaf S.C X) :
    (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward S.C (subsetInclusion X Z)).essImage G ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∉ Z →
        Nonempty (colimit ((OpenNhds.inclusion x).op ⋙ G.obj) ≅ Sfinal.zero)
declarations.comment: essential image part

declarations.name: ClosedImmersionSheaves.not_preservesColimitsOfShape_sheafPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AI, first half.** For `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed embedding and `x ∈ X` outside the image
of `i`, the pushforward `i_* : Sh(Z, Type) ⥤ Sh(X, Type)` does not preserve binary coproducts, i.e.
it is not right exact.

Take `F` to be the final sheaf `*` on `Z`. Stacks 00AE makes the stalk at `x` of `i_*G` terminal
for *every* sheaf `G` on `Z`, in particular for `G = F` and for `G = F ⨿ F`. Taking stalks of
sheaves is a left adjoint, so it preserves the coproduct; if `i_*` preserved it too, the terminal
set `(i_*(F ⨿ F))_x` would be the coproduct of the terminal set `(i_*F)_x` with itself, which
`isEmpty_isTerminal_coprod_self` forbids.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_preservesColimitsOfShape_sheafPushforward
    (hi : IsClosedEmbedding (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) (x : X)
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) :
    ¬ PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) (Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) i)
declarations.comment: i_* is not right exact as a functor between categories of sheaves of sets

declarations.name: ClosedImmersionSheaves.not_isLeftAdjoint_sheafPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AI, second half.** For `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed embedding and `x ∈ X` outside the image
of `i`, the pushforward `i_* : Sh(Z, Type) ⥤ Sh(X, Type)` has no right adjoint: a functor with a
right adjoint preserves all colimits, and `i_*` does not preserve binary coproducts.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isLeftAdjoint_sheafPushforward
    (hi : IsClosedEmbedding (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) (x : X)
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range (ConcreteCategory.hom i)) :
    ¬ (Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) i).IsLeftAdjoint
declarations.comment: in particular i_* cannot have a right adjoint

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.GlueData.glued
declarations.doc: The sheaf of sets on `X` glued from the glueing data `D`.
declarations.statement: def glued (D : GlueData X U) : X.Sheaf (Type u)

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.GlueData.sectionsEquiv
declarations.doc: The comparison isomorphism `φ i : F|_{U i} ≅ F_i` on sections over an open `V ≤ U i`.
declarations.statement:
def sectionsEquiv (D : GlueData X U) (i : ι) {V : Opens X} (hV : V ≤ U i) :
    D.Sections V ≃ (D.sheaf i).obj V hV

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.GlueData.sectionsEquiv_map
declarations.doc:
The comparison isomorphism `φ i` commutes with the restriction maps, i.e. it is an
isomorphism of sheaves on `U i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionsEquiv_map (D : GlueData X U) (i : ι) {V W : Opens X} (hV : V ≤ U i) (hWV : W ≤ V)
    (s : D.Sections V) :
    D.sectionsEquiv i (hWV.trans hV) (D.sectionsMap hWV s)
      = (D.sheaf i).map hWV (D.sectionsEquiv i hV s)

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.GlueData.trans_sectionsEquiv
declarations.doc: The commuting diagram `φ i j ∘ φ i = φ j` over the overlaps.
declarations.statement:
theorem trans_sectionsEquiv (D : GlueData X U) (i j : ι) {V : Opens X} (hi : V ≤ U i)
    (hj : V ≤ U j) (s : D.Sections V) :
    D.trans i j hi hj (D.sectionsEquiv i hi s) = D.sectionsEquiv j hj s

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.AddGlueData.gluedAddPresheaf_forget

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OModuleGlueData.chartLinearEquiv_restrict
declarations.doc:
The comparison isomorphism `φ i` commutes with the restriction maps, i.e. it is an isomorphism
of sheaves of modules on `U i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartLinearEquiv_restrict (D : OModuleGlueData O U) (i : ι) {V W : Opens X}
    (hV : V ≤ U i) (h : W ≤ V) (s : D.sectionsSubmodule V) :
    D.chartLinearEquiv i (h.trans hV) (D.sectionsMap h s)
      = (D.sheaf i).map h (D.chartLinearEquiv i hV s)
declarations.comment: sheaves of O-modules, the comparison isomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.OModuleGlueData.trans_chartLinearEquiv
declarations.doc: The commuting triangle `φ i j ∘ φ i = φ j` over the overlaps.
declarations.statement:
theorem trans_chartLinearEquiv (D : OModuleGlueData O U) (i j : ι) {V : Opens X} (hi : V ≤ U i)
    (hj : V ≤ U j) (s : D.sectionsSubmodule V) :
    D.trans i j hi hj (D.chartLinearEquiv i hi s) = D.chartLinearEquiv j hj s
declarations.comment: sheaves of O-modules, compatibility of the comparisons

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ModulesGlueData.glued
declarations.doc: The sheaf of modules on `S` glued from `D`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev glued (D : ModulesGlueData S f) : S.Modules
declarations.comment: sheaves of O-modules on a scheme, the glued module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ModulesGlueData.chartIso
declarations.doc: The glued module restricts along each chart to the sheaf of modules it was glued from.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartIso (D : ModulesGlueData S f) (i : ι) :
    D.glued.restrict (f i) ≅ D.mod i
declarations.comment: sheaves of O-modules on a scheme, the comparison isomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ModulesGlueData.trans_chartSectionsIso
declarations.doc:
**The commuting triangle `φ i j ∘ φ i = φ j` on sections over an open contained in two
charts.** Reading a section of the glued module on the `i`-th chart and comparing it with the
`j`-th chart gives the same thing as reading it on the `j`-th chart directly. This is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.OModuleGlueData.trans_chartLinearEquiv` phrased with `chartSectionsIso`,
so that it elaborates outside this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem trans_chartSectionsIso (D : ModulesGlueData S f) (i j : ι) {V : S.Opens}
    (hi : V ≤ (f i).opensRange) (hj : V ≤ (f j).opensRange)
    (x : ToType (D.glued.val.obj (op V))) :
    D.trans i j hi hj ((D.chartSectionsIso i hi).hom x) = (D.chartSectionsIso j hj).hom x
declarations.comment: sheaves of O-modules on a scheme, the comparisons related by the transitions

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.sheafEquivGlueData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AN, sheaves of sets.** For an open covering `X = ⋃ i, U i`, restriction to the
members of the covering is an equivalence between the category of sheaves of sets on `X` and the
category of glueing data with respect to the covering.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sheafEquivGlueData (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤) : X.Sheaf (Type u) ≌ GlueData X U
declarations.comment: sheaves of sets

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.sheafOfModulesEquivGlueData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AN, sheaves of `𝒪`-modules.** Let `𝒪` be a sheaf of rings on a topological space
`X` and let `X = ⋃ i, U i` be an open covering. Restriction to the members of the covering is an
equivalence between the category of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules on `X` and the category of glueing
data of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules with respect to the covering.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafOfModulesEquivGlueData (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤) :
    SheafOfModules.{u} 𝒪 ≌ OModuleGlueData 𝒪.obj U
declarations.comment: sheaves of O-modules

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.addSheafEquivGlueData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AN, abelian sheaves.** For an open covering `X = ⋃ i, U i`, restriction to the
members of the covering is an equivalence between the category of abelian sheaves on `X` and the
category of glueing data of abelian sheaves with respect to the covering.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def addSheafEquivGlueData (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤) :
    X.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≌ ValuedGlueData (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u}) U
declarations.comment: abelian sheaves

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.algebraicStructureSheafEquivGlueData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00AN, sheaves of algebraic structures.** Let `(C, F)` be a type of algebraic
structure (Stacks 007M). For an open covering `X = ⋃ i, U i`, restriction to the members of the
covering is an equivalence between the category of sheaves of algebraic structures of type
`(C, F)` on `X` and the category of glueing data of such sheaves with respect to the covering.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def algebraicStructureSheafEquivGlueData (S : AlgebraicStructureType.{u, w})
    (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤) : X.Sheaf S.C ≌ ValuedGlueData S.F U
declarations.comment: sheaves of algebraic structures

declarations.name: Stacks.Localization.existsUnique_ringHom_comp_algebraMap_eq
declarations.doc:
The universal property of localization: if a ring map `f : R →+* P` sends every element of
`M` to a unit of `P`, there is a unique ring map `g : S →+* P` out of the localization
`S = M⁻¹R` with `g ∘ (R → S) = f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_ringHom_comp_algebraMap_eq {f : R →+* P} (hf : ∀ y : M, IsUnit (f y)) :
    ∃! g : S →+* P, g.comp (algebraMap R S) = f
declarations.comment: Stated for any localization `S` of `R` at `M`, in particular `Localization M`.

declarations.name: LocalizedModule.equivAwayColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00CR.** `S⁻¹M = colim_{f ∈ S} M_f`: the localization of `M` at `S` is the
directed colimit of the away-localizations `M_f` over `f ∈ S` with the divisibility
preorder, with transition maps `M_f → M_g` for `f ∣ g` induced by the universal
property.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def equivAwayColimit : LocalizedModule S M ≃ₗ[R] AwayColimit S M

declarations.name: IsLocalization.quotientEquiv
declarations.doc:
Localization commutes with quotients: for any localization
`Q` of `A/I` at the image `S̄` of `S`, there is a canonical algebra (in particular ring)
isomorphism `S̄⁻¹(A/I) ≅ S⁻¹A/S⁻¹I`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def quotientEquiv : Q ≃ₐ[A ⧸ I] A_S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A A_S)

declarations.name: TensorProduct.existsUnique_linearEquiv_compr₂_eq_of_universal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00CX** (uniqueness). If `(T, g)` and `(T', g')` are two pairs of an `R`-module and an
`R`-bilinear map `M × N → _` which both have the universal property (every bilinear map `f` to an
`R`-module `P` is `f̃ ∘ g` for a unique linear `f̃`), then there is a unique `R`-linear isomorphism
`j : T ≃ T'` with `j ∘ g = g'`. The universal property is quantified over modules `P` in the
universe of `T` and `T'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_linearEquiv_compr₂_eq_of_universal {T T' : Type w} [AddCommGroup T]
    [Module R T] [AddCommGroup T'] [Module R T'] (g : M →ₗ[R] N →ₗ[R] T)
    (g' : M →ₗ[R] N →ₗ[R] T')
    (hg : ∀ (P : Type w) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] (f : M →ₗ[R] N →ₗ[R] P),
      ∃! f' : T →ₗ[R] P, g.compr₂ f' = f)
    (hg' : ∀ (P : Type w) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] (f : M →ₗ[R] N →ₗ[R] P),
      ∃! f' : T' →ₗ[R] P, g'.compr₂ f' = f) :
    ∃! j : T ≃ₗ[R] T', g.compr₂ j.toLinearMap = g'
declarations.comment:
Uniqueness: two universal pairs `(T, g)`, `(T', g')` admit a unique isomorphism
`j : T ≃ T'` with `j ∘ g = g'`; the universal property quantifies over modules in the universe of
`T` and `T'`.

declarations.name: IsTensorProduct.existsUnique_linearEquiv_compr₂_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00CX** (uniqueness, for `IsTensorProduct`). If `g : M × N → T` and `g' : M × N → T'`
are bilinear maps exhibiting `T` and `T'` as tensor products of `M` and `N` (Mathlib's
`IsTensorProduct`), then there is a unique `R`-linear isomorphism `j : T ≃ T'` with
`j ∘ g = g'`.
declarations.comment:
Uniqueness, for pairs exhibited as tensor products by `IsTensorProduct`: there is
a unique isomorphism `j : T ≃ T'` with `j ∘ g = g'`.
