declarations.name: PiTensorProduct.existsUnique_linearEquiv_of_universal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00CZ.** The tensor product is unique up to unique isomorphism: if a module `T`
and a multilinear map `g : Π i, s i → T` have the universal property (every multilinear map
`f` to a module `P` factors as `f' ∘ g` for a unique linear `f'`), then there is a unique
linear isomorphism `e : (⨂[R] i, s i) ≃ₗ[R] T` with `e ∘ tprod R = g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_linearEquiv_of_universal (T : Type t) [AddCommMonoid T] [Module R T]
    (g : MultilinearMap R s T)
    (hg : ∀ (P : Type (max u v w t)) [AddCommMonoid P] [Module R P] (f : MultilinearMap R s P),
      ∃! f' : T →ₗ[R] P, f'.compMultilinearMap g = f) :
    ∃! e : (⨂[R] i, s i) ≃ₗ[R] T, e.toLinearMap.compMultilinearMap (tprod R) = g
declarations.comment:
Uniqueness clause: such a `T` is unique up to unique isomorphism; the existence
of `(T, g)` with the universal property is `PiTensorProduct.lift` with
`PiTensorProduct.lift.unique`.

declarations.name: PiTensorProduct.tmulTmulLeftEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D0**, the map `f`: the isomorphism `(M ⊗_R N) ⊗_R P ≅ M ⊗_R N ⊗_R P` from the
iterated tensor product to the threefold tensor product of Stacks 00CZ, with
`f ((x ⊗ y) ⊗ z) = x ⊗ y ⊗ z` (`tmulTmulLeftEquiv_tmul`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tmulTmulLeftEquiv : ((M 0 ⊗[R] M 1) ⊗[R] M 2) ≃ₗ[R] ⨂[R] i, M i
declarations.comment:
the map `f`; the three modules are the family `M 0`, `M 1`, `M 2` and the
threefold tensor product is `PiTensorProduct` over `Fin 3`

declarations.name: PiTensorProduct.tmulTmulRightEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D0**, the map `g`: the isomorphism `M ⊗_R N ⊗_R P ≅ M ⊗_R (N ⊗_R P)` from the
threefold tensor product of Stacks 00CZ to the iterated tensor product, with
`g (x ⊗ y ⊗ z) = x ⊗ (y ⊗ z)` (`tmulTmulRightEquiv_tprod`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tmulTmulRightEquiv : (⨂[R] i, M i) ≃ₗ[R] M 0 ⊗[R] (M 1 ⊗[R] M 2)
declarations.comment:
the map `g`; the three modules are the family `M 0`, `M 1`, `M 2` and the
threefold tensor product is `PiTensorProduct` over `Fin 3`

declarations.name: PiTensorProduct.tmulTmulLeftEquiv_trans_tmulTmulRightEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D0**, the composite: `g ∘ f` is the associator
`TensorProduct.assoc : (M ⊗_R N) ⊗_R P ≅ M ⊗_R (N ⊗_R P)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tmulTmulLeftEquiv_trans_tmulTmulRightEquiv :
    tmulTmulLeftEquiv R M ≪≫ₗ tmulTmulRightEquiv R M = TensorProduct.assoc R (M 0) (M 1) (M 2)
declarations.comment: the composite `g ∘ f` is `TensorProduct.assoc`

registrations.name: TensorProduct.assoc_tmul
registrations.comment: the composite g ∘ f, on pure tensors

declarations.name: DistribMulAction.commute_toAddMonoidEnd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D1.** In an `(A, B)`-bimodule multiplication by `a : A` and multiplication by
`b : B` commute, as additive endomorphisms of `N`: this is the source's own phrasing of the
bimodule condition, an equation in `AddMonoid.End N`.

The condition itself is `SMulCommClass A B N`, whose field `smul_comm` is the pointwise identity
`a • b • n = b • a • n`; commuting of the operators is the form consumed by
`Algebra.TensorProduct.liftEquiv`, hence by `TensorProduct.Algebra.module`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem DistribMulAction.commute_toAddMonoidEnd {A B N : Type*} [Monoid A] [Monoid B]
    [AddMonoid N] [DistribMulAction A N] [DistribMulAction B N] [SMulCommClass A B N] (a : A)
    (b : B) :
    Commute (DistribMulAction.toAddMonoidEnd A N a) (DistribMulAction.toAddMonoidEnd B N b)
declarations.comment: The source's condition, that multiplication by `a` and multiplication by `b` commute, at the level of the multiplication operators: an equation in `AddMonoid.End N`. The condition as a class on the two actions is `SMulCommClass`, tagged below.

registrations.name: SMulCommClass
registrations.comment: An `(A, B)`-bimodule is a type with `[Module A N] [Module B N] [SMulCommClass A B N]`: the source's data is the two module structures, and its one condition, that the actions commute, is this class, `smul_comm` being `a • b • n = b • a • n`, the source's `b (a n) = a (b n)` read from the other side. The class asks only for two `SMul`s, so this covers semirings acting on an additive commutative monoid as well as the source's rings acting on an abelian group. Writing the `B`-action on the right is the source's notation, not a further condition; the genuine right-action form is this class at `Bᵐᵒᵖ`, the bimodule set-up of `Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Bimodule.lean`.

declarations.name: TensorProduct.smulCommClass_bimoduleAssoc_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D2**, the bimodule structure on `(M ⊗_A N) ⊗_B P`: here `B` acts on `M ⊗_A N`
through `N`, and `A` and `B` act on the outer tensor product through its left factor.
declarations.statement: theorem smulCommClass_bimoduleAssoc_left : SMulCommClass A B ((M ⊗[A] N) ⊗[B] P)
declarations.comment: The `(A, B)`-bimodule structure on `(M ⊗_A N) ⊗_B P`: `A` acts through `M`, `B` through `N` (`TensorProduct.rightModule`), and the two actions commute.

declarations.name: TensorProduct.smulCommClass_bimoduleAssoc_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D2**, the bimodule structure on `M ⊗_A (N ⊗_B P)`: here `A` and `B` act on
`N ⊗_B P` through `N`, `A` acts on the outer tensor product through `M` and `B` through
`N ⊗_B P`.
declarations.statement: theorem smulCommClass_bimoduleAssoc_right : SMulCommClass A B (M ⊗[A] (N ⊗[B] P))
declarations.comment: The `(A, B)`-bimodule structure on `M ⊗_A (N ⊗_B P)`: `A` acts through `M`, `B` through `N` (`TensorProduct.rightModule`), and the two actions commute.

declarations.name: TensorProduct.bimoduleAssoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D2**: for an `A`-module `M`, a `B`-module `P` and an `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`,
`(M ⊗_A N) ⊗_B P ≅ M ⊗_A (N ⊗_B P)` via `(m ⊗ n) ⊗ p ↦ m ⊗ (n ⊗ p)`, an `A`-linear isomorphism.
The same map is `B`-linear: `TensorProduct.bimoduleAssocRight`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bimoduleAssoc : ((M ⊗[A] N) ⊗[B] P) ≃ₗ[A] M ⊗[A] (N ⊗[B] P)
declarations.comment: The isomorphism `(M ⊗_A N) ⊗_B P ≅ M ⊗_A (N ⊗_B P)` for an `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`, with no ring map between `A` and `B`, as an `A`-linear isomorphism; the same map as a `B`-linear isomorphism is `TensorProduct.bimoduleAssocRight`.

declarations.name: TensorProduct.bimoduleAssocRight
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D2**: `bimoduleAssoc` as a `B`-linear isomorphism; its underlying map is that of
the `A`-linear `bimoduleAssoc` (`bimoduleAssocRight_toAddEquiv`), so the two triple tensor
products are isomorphic as `A`-modules and as `B`-modules via the same mapping.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bimoduleAssocRight : ((M ⊗[A] N) ⊗[B] P) ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[A] (N ⊗[B] P)
declarations.comment: The isomorphism `(M ⊗_A N) ⊗_B P ≅ M ⊗_A (N ⊗_B P)` as a `B`-linear isomorphism; its underlying additive equivalence is that of the `A`-linear `TensorProduct.bimoduleAssoc`.

registrations.name: IsDirectedOrder
registrations.comment:
Directed sets. Note that unlike stacks, mathlib does not require directed sets
  to be nonempty.

declarations.name: Module.ColimitQuotient.existsUnique_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 10.8.2**: for a system `(M_i, μ_ij)` of modules over a preordered set `I`,
the quotient `(⨁ i, M i) / Q` together with the maps `φ_i = π ∘ ι_i` is the colimit:
for every module `Y` and maps `ψ_i : M_i → Y` with `ψ_j ∘ μ_ij = ψ_i`, there is a unique
`g : (⨁ i, M i) / Q → Y` with `g ∘ φ_i = ψ_i` for all `i`. The compatibility
`φ_j ∘ μ_ij = φ_i` is `ColimitQuotient.of_comp`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ColimitQuotient.existsUnique_comp_eq {Y : Type*} [AddCommGroup Y] [Module R Y]
    (ψ : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] Y) (hψ : ∀ (i j : ι) (h : i ≤ j), ψ j ∘ₗ μ i j h = ψ i) :
    ∃! g : ColimitQuotient M μ →ₗ[R] Y, ∀ i, g ∘ₗ ColimitQuotient.of M μ i = ψ i
declarations.comment: The identities `μ_ii = id` and `μ_ik = μ_jk ∘ μ_ij` of a system are not needed.

declarations.name: ModuleCat.isColimitDirectLimitSigmaCocone
declarations.doc:
**The colimit of a directed system of modules is the disjoint union modulo eventual
equality.** Over a nonempty directed preorder `ι`, the module `_root_.DirectLimit G f`, the
quotient of `Σ i, G i` by `m ∼ m' ↔ μ_{ij} m = μ_{i'j} m'` for some `j ≥ i, i'`, together with
the maps `φ_i : x ↦ ⟦⟨i, x⟩⟧`, is a colimit of the system in `ModuleCat R`.
declarations.statement: def isColimitDirectLimitSigmaCocone : IsColimit (directLimitSigmaCocone G f)
declarations.comment: the module `Σ i, G i` modulo eventual equality, with the maps `φ_i`, is the colimit

declarations.name: ModuleCat.colimitDirectLimitSigmaIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism between the colimit of `ModuleCat.directLimitDiagram G f` and
the explicit module `_root_.DirectLimit G f`, over a nonempty directed preorder.
declarations.statement:
def colimitDirectLimitSigmaIso :
    colimit (directLimitDiagram G f) ≅ of R (_root_.DirectLimit G f)
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism of the colimit with `Σ i, G i` mod eventual equality

declarations.name: DirectLimit.mk_eq_mk_iff
declarations.doc:
In the direct limit over a directed preorder, the classes of `m ∈ G i` and `m' ∈ G i'`
agree exactly when `μ_{ij} m = μ_{i'j} m'` for some `j ≥ i, i'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {i i' : ι} (m : G i) (m' : G i') :
    (⟦⟨i, m⟩⟧ : DirectLimit G f) = ⟦⟨i', m'⟩⟧ ↔
      ∃ (j : ι) (hij : i ≤ j) (hi'j : i' ≤ j), f i j hij m = f i' j hi'j m'
declarations.comment: item (1): the equivalence relation on `Σ i, G i`

declarations.name: DirectLimit.mk_add_mk
declarations.doc:
In the direct limit over a directed preorder, the sum of the classes of `m ∈ G i` and
`m' ∈ G i'` is the class of `μ_{ij} m + μ_{i'j} m'`, for any `j ≥ i, i'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_add_mk {i i' j : ι} (hij : i ≤ j) (hi'j : i' ≤ j) (m : G i) (m' : G i') :
    (⟦⟨i, m⟩⟧ : DirectLimit G f) + ⟦⟨i', m'⟩⟧ = ⟦⟨j, f i j hij m + f i' j hi'j m'⟩⟧
declarations.comment: item (2): the addition, through any common upper bound

registrations.name: DirectLimit.smul_def
registrations.comment: item (3): the scalar multiplication `x • ⟦⟨i, m⟩⟧ = ⟦⟨i, x • m⟩⟧`

declarations.name: ModuleCat.ker_hom_comp_inl_and_ker_hom_inl_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring and let `M = colim M_i` be the colimit of a system of
`R`-modules over the poset `{a < b, a < c}`, that is, the pushout of a span
`M_b ← M_a → M_c` of `R`-modules, with canonical maps `inl : M_b → M` and `inr : M_c → M`. Then the
kernel of the canonical map `M_a → M` is `Ker(μ_ab) + Ker(μ_ac)`, and the kernel of `inl` is the
image of `Ker(μ_ac)` under `μ_ab`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ModuleCat.ker_hom_comp_inl_and_ker_hom_inl_of_isPushout {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {Ma Mb Mc M : ModuleCat.{v} R} {μab : Ma ⟶ Mb} {μac : Ma ⟶ Mc} {inl : Mb ⟶ M} {inr : Mc ⟶ M}
    (h : IsPushout μab μac inl inr) :
    LinearMap.ker (μab ≫ inl).hom = LinearMap.ker μab.hom ⊔ LinearMap.ker μac.hom ∧
      LinearMap.ker inl.hom = Submodule.map μab.hom (LinearMap.ker μac.hom)
declarations.comment:
The poset `{a < b, a < c}` is the span shape, so the colimit of a system over it is
a pushout in `ModuleCat R`, taken here abstractly rather than through the model
`Coker(μ_ab ⊕ -μ_ac)`; that the pushout is that cokernel is Mathlib's
`CategoryTheory.IsPushout.isColimitCokernelCofork`. The mirror `Ker(inr) = μ_ac(Ker(μ_ab))` is this
statement applied to `h.flip`.

declarations.name: Module.IsSystemHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00D9.** Let `(M i, μ i j)` and `(N i, ν i j)` be systems of `R`-modules over the same
preordered set `ι`. A family of `R`-linear maps `φ i : M i →ₗ[R] N i` is a *homomorphism of
systems* from `(M, μ)` to `(N, ν)` when every transition square commutes, that is, when
`φ j ∘ₗ μ i j = ν i j ∘ₗ φ i` for all `i ≤ j`; equivalently, when `φ` is a natural transformation
between the associated diagrams `ι ⥤ ModuleCat R`. The axioms making `μ` and `ν` systems are not
needed to state the condition and are not assumed.
declarations.statement:
def IsSystemHom {R : Type*} [Semiring R] {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι]
    {M : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
    (μ : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → M i →ₗ[R] M j)
    {N : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommMonoid (N i)] [∀ i, Module R (N i)]
    (ν : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → N i →ₗ[R] N j)
    (φ : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N i) : Prop
declarations.comment: Stated as a `Prop`-valued predicate on the family `φ`, in the unbundled language of `Module.DirectLimit`, so that `Module.DirectLimit.map φ h` is the induced map on colimits of Lemma 00DA. The axioms of a system (`DirectedSystem`) are not assumed, the commuting squares not referring to them, and `R` is only a semiring acting on additive commutative monoids.

declarations.name: Module.DirectLimit.existsUnique_comp_of_eq_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DA.** Let `(M i, μ i j)` and `(N i, ν i j)` be systems of `R`-modules over the same
preordered set `ι`. A homomorphism of systems `φ i : M i →ₗ[R] N i` (so
`φ j ∘ₗ μ i j = ν i j ∘ₗ φ i` for all `i ≤ j`) induces a unique `R`-linear map
`ψ : colim M →ₗ[R] colim N` such that the square `ψ ∘ₗ of i = of i ∘ₗ φ i` commutes for every
`i`; the map is `Module.DirectLimit.map φ hφ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comp_of_eq_of_comp (φ : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N i)
    (hφ : ∀ i j h, φ j ∘ₗ μ i j h = ν i j h ∘ₗ φ i) :
    ∃! ψ : DirectLimit M μ →ₗ[R] DirectLimit N ν,
      ∀ i, ψ ∘ₗ of R ι M μ i = of R ι N ν i ∘ₗ φ i
declarations.comment: Existence and uniqueness of the induced map `Module.DirectLimit.map φ hφ`, from Mathlib's `Module.DirectLimit.map_apply_of` (the squares commute) and `Module.DirectLimit.hom_ext` (uniqueness). Stated in the generality of `Module.DirectLimit`: `R` a semiring acting on additive commutative monoids, and the system axioms of `μ` and `ν` not assumed, neither part depending on them.

declarations.name: Module.DirectLimit.comp_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
public lemma Module.DirectLimit.comp_eq_zero :
    Module.DirectLimit.map g' hg' ∘ₗ Module.DirectLimit.map g hg = 0
declarations.comment: part 1

declarations.name: Module.DirectLimit.homologyColimitEquiv
declarations.doc: Homology intertwines with direct limits.
declarations.statement:
public def Module.DirectLimit.homologyColimitEquiv
    [Nonempty ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
    [DirectedSystem M fun i j h ↦ ⇑(f' i j h)]
    [DirectedSystem N fun x1 x2 x3 ↦ ⇑(l x1 x2 x3)] :
    Module.DirectLimit (hObj g g') (hMap g hg g' hg') ≃ₗ[R] homologyLimit g hg g' hg'
declarations.comment: part 2

declarations.name: ModuleCat.not_injective_hom_of_isColimit_binaryCofan_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
Taking colimits is not exact in general: let `R` be a ring, let `M` be the
colimit of a system `(A, B, C, μ_ab, μ_ac)` of `R`-modules over the poset `{a < b, a < c}`, that
is, the pushout of the span `B ← A → C`, and let `L` be the colimit `B ⊔ C` of the sub-system
`(0, B, C, 0, 0)`. If one of `μ_ab`, `μ_ac` is nonzero, then the induced map of colimits
`ψ : L → M` is not injective, even though the morphism of systems `(0 → A, 𝟙 B, 𝟙 C)` is
injective on each object.
declarations.comment:
The poset `{a < b, a < c}` is the span shape, so the colimit of a system over it is
a pushout in `ModuleCat R` and the colimit of the sub-system with apex the zero module is the
coproduct `B ⊔ C`; the morphism of systems `(0 → A, 𝟙 B, 𝟙 C)` is injective on each object, and
`ψ` is pinned by the two commuting squares of `Stacks 00DA`. Stated for an arbitrary nonzero span
over an arbitrary ring instead of the source's `(0, ℤ, ℤ, 0, 0) → (ℤ, ℤ, ℤ, 1, 1)`.

declarations.name: tensorRight_not_preserve_exactness
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorRight_not_preserve_exactness :
    ¬ ∀ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (M₁ : Type v)
      (M₂ M₃ : Type v') (N : Type w)
      (_ : AddCommGroup M₁) (_ : Module R M₁)
      (_ : AddCommGroup M₂) (_ : Module R M₂)
      (_ : AddCommGroup M₃) (_ : Module R M₃)
      (_ : AddCommGroup N) (_ : Module R N)
      (f : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃),
      Function.Exact f g →
      Function.Exact (f.rTensor N) (g.rTensor N)

declarations.name: TensorProduct.not_injective_rTensor_zmod_two_lsmul_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DI**.
Multiplication by `2` is an injective map of `ℤ`-modules `ℤ → ℤ`, but the induced map
`ℤ ⊗[ℤ] ℤ/2 → ℤ ⊗[ℤ] ℤ/2` is the zero map and hence not injective, `ℤ ⊗[ℤ] ℤ/2` being nonzero.
So tensoring does not preserve injectivity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem TensorProduct.not_injective_rTensor_zmod_two_lsmul_two :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ ℤ (2 : ℤ)) ∧
      (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ ℤ (2 : ℤ)).rTensor (ZMod 2) = 0 ∧
      ¬ Function.Injective ((LinearMap.lsmul ℤ ℤ (2 : ℤ)).rTensor (ZMod 2))

declarations.name: IsLocalization.tensorLocalizeEquivTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DL.** Localization commutes with tensor product: for any localization `P` of
`M ⊗[R] N` at `S`, there is a canonical `Rₛ`-linear isomorphism `M' ⊗[Rₛ] N' ≃ P`. Taking
`Rₛ = S⁻¹R`, `M' = S⁻¹M`, `N' = S⁻¹N` and `P = S⁻¹(M ⊗_R N)` gives the isomorphism
`S⁻¹M ⊗_{S⁻¹R} S⁻¹N ≅ S⁻¹(M ⊗_R N)` of the Stacks project.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsLocalization.tensorLocalizeEquivTensor
    [IsLocalizedModule S f] [IsLocalizedModule S g] [IsLocalizedModule S h] :
    M' ⊗[Rₛ] N' ≃ₗ[Rₛ] P

declarations.name: exteriorPower_free
declarations.doc:
If `M` is a free `R`-module, then for every `n ≥ 0` the `n`-th exterior power `⋀^n(M)` is a
free `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_free
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Free R M] (n : ℕ) :
    Module.Free R (ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower R n M)

declarations.name: symmetricPower_free_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Symmetric powers of a free module are free.** Let `R` be a commutative ring in any universe
and `M` a free `R`-module. For every finite index type `ι` the symmetric power `Sym[R] ι M` is a
free `R`-module; with `ι = ULift (Fin n)` this is the `n`-th symmetric power `Symⁿ(M)` for every
`n ≥ 0`. The exterior powers are `exteriorPower_free`.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetricPower_free_of_finite (R ι : Type u) [CommSemiring R] [Finite ι] (M : Type*)
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] :
    Module.Free R (SymmetricPower R ι M)

declarations.name: symmetric_and_exterior_power_presentation
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let
`M₂ --g--> M₁ --f--> M → 0` be an exact sequence of `R`-modules (`f` surjective and
`range g = ker f`).  With `n = k + 1 ≥ 1`, both presentation sequences are exact:

* symmetric: `M₂ ⊗ Sym^k(M₁) --α--> Sym^{k+1}(M₁) --Sym^{k+1}(f)--> Sym^{k+1}(M) → 0`;
* exterior:  `M₂ ⊗ ∧^k(M₁) --β--> ∧^{k+1}(M₁) --∧^{k+1}(f)--> ∧^{k+1}(M) → 0`.

In each case the right-hand map is surjective and the image of the left-hand connecting
map equals the kernel of the right-hand map.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetric_and_exterior_power_presentation
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {M M₁ M₂ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
    [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
    (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₁) (f : M₁ →ₗ[R] M)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hexact : LinearMap.range g = LinearMap.ker f)
    (k : ℕ) :
    (Function.Surjective (symMap (k + 1) f) ∧
        LinearMap.range (symMulMap k g) = LinearMap.ker (symMap (k + 1) f)) ∧
      (Function.Surjective (exteriorPower.map (k + 1) f) ∧
        LinearMap.range (beta k g) = LinearMap.ker (exteriorPower.map (k + 1) f))

declarations.name: exists_presentation_exteriorPower_and_symmetricPower_univ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00DP.** Let `M` be a module over a commutative ring `R` (in any universe) with a
generating system `x : I → M`, and let `n + 2 ≥ 2`. There are canonical exact sequences

  `(⊕_{j₁<j₂} ⊕_{i₁,i₂} Tⁿ(M)) ⊕ (⊕_{j₁<j₂} ⊕_{i} Tⁿ(M)) → Tⁿ⁺²(M) → ⋀ⁿ⁺²(M) → 0`   and
  `(⊕_{j₁<j₂} ⊕_{i₁,i₂} Tⁿ(M)) → Tⁿ⁺²(M) → Symⁿ⁺²(M) → 0`,

where a pure tensor `⨂ₜ f` in the `(j₁, j₂, i₁, i₂)` summand maps to the tensor with `x_{i₁}`,
`x_{i₂}` in slots `j₁, j₂` and `f` in the remaining slots, plus (exterior side) or minus
(symmetric side) the same tensor with `x_{i₁}` and `x_{i₂}` swapped; a pure tensor in the
`(j₁, j₂, i)` summand maps to the tensor with `x_i` in both slots `j₁, j₂`; and the projections
send `⨂ₜ f` to `ιMulti f` and to `⨂ₛ f`. The symmetric power is
`SymmetricPower R (ULift (Fin (n + 2))) M`, indexed by `n + 2` slots in the universe of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_presentation_exteriorPower_and_symmetricPower_univ {I : Type*} [DecidableEq I]
    (x : I → M) (hx : Submodule.span R (Set.range x) = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ (Φ : DirectSum ((SlotPair n × I × I) ⊕ (SlotPair n × I)) (fun _ => ⨂[R]^n M)
              →ₗ[R] ⨂[R]^(n + 2) M)
       (π : ⨂[R]^(n + 2) M →ₗ[R] ⋀[R]^(n + 2) M),
        (∀ (jp : SlotPair n) (i₁ i₂ : I) (f : Fin n → M),
          Φ (DirectSum.lof R _ _ (Sum.inl (jp, i₁, i₂)) (⨂ₜ[R] k, f k))
            = (⨂ₜ[R] k, insTwo jp.1.1 jp.1.2 jp.2 (x i₁) (x i₂) f k)
              + (⨂ₜ[R] k, insTwo jp.1.1 jp.1.2 jp.2 (x i₂) (x i₁) f k)) ∧
        (∀ (jp : SlotPair n) (i : I) (f : Fin n → M),
          Φ (DirectSum.lof R _ _ (Sum.inr (jp, i)) (⨂ₜ[R] k, f k))
            = (⨂ₜ[R] k, insTwo jp.1.1 jp.1.2 jp.2 (x i) (x i) f k)) ∧
        (∀ f : Fin (n + 2) → M, π (⨂ₜ[R] k, f k) = exteriorPower.ιMulti R (n + 2) f) ∧
        Function.Exact Φ π ∧ Function.Surjective π) ∧
    (∃ (Ψ : DirectSum (SlotPair n × I × I) (fun _ => ⨂[R]^n M) →ₗ[R] ⨂[R]^(n + 2) M)
       (ρ : ⨂[R]^(n + 2) M →ₗ[R] SymmetricPower R (ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 2))) M),
        (∀ (jp : SlotPair n) (i₁ i₂ : I) (f : Fin n → M),
          Ψ (DirectSum.lof R _ _ (jp, i₁, i₂) (⨂ₜ[R] k, f k))
            = (⨂ₜ[R] k, insTwo jp.1.1 jp.1.2 jp.2 (x i₁) (x i₂) f k)
              - (⨂ₜ[R] k, insTwo jp.1.1 jp.1.2 jp.2 (x i₂) (x i₁) f k)) ∧
        (∀ f : Fin (n + 2) → M, ρ (⨂ₜ[R] k, f k) = ⨂ₛ[R] k, f k.down) ∧
        Function.Exact Ψ ρ ∧ Function.Surjective ρ)
declarations.comment: Both exact sequences, for a ring in any universe; `n + 2` plays Stacks' `n ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: LinearMap.exists_sub_one_mem_and_map_surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (5)**: if `φ : N →ₗ[R] M` has `N/IN → M/IM` surjective and `M` is finite, then
some `r ∈ 1 + I` makes `φ` surjective after localizing at the powers of `r`.

Stated against arbitrary localization witnesses `fN`, `fM`, so it applies to any model of
`N_r` and `M_r`. For the concrete `LocalizedModule` reading see
`LinearMap.exists_sub_one_mem_and_localizedMap_surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ`.

Dropping the hypothesis `I ≤ rad(R)` of `LinearMap.surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ` (part (6))
costs surjectivity of `φ` itself; inverting one element of `1 + I` recovers it.
declarations.statement:
theorem LinearMap.exists_sub_one_mem_and_map_surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ
    (I : Ideal R) (φ : N →ₗ[R] M) [Module.Finite R M]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ ∘ₗ φ)) :
    ∃ r : R, r - 1 ∈ I ∧ ∀ {Nᵣ Mᵣ : Type*} [AddCommGroup Nᵣ] [Module R Nᵣ]
      [AddCommGroup Mᵣ] [Module R Mᵣ] (fN : N →ₗ[R] Nᵣ) (fM : M →ₗ[R] Mᵣ)
      [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers r) fN] [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers r) fM],
      Function.Surjective (IsLocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers r) fN fM φ)

declarations.name: LinearMap.exists_sub_one_mem_and_localizedMap_surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (5)**, in the concrete `LocalizedModule` model: the tag's literal
"`N_f → M_f` is surjective".

This is `LinearMap.exists_sub_one_mem_and_map_surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ` at the canonical
witnesses `LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem LinearMap.exists_sub_one_mem_and_localizedMap_surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ
    (I : Ideal R) (φ : N →ₗ[R] M) [Module.Finite R M]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ ∘ₗ φ)) :
    ∃ r : R, r - 1 ∈ I ∧
      Function.Surjective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers r) φ)

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_span_image_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (7)**: if `s` generates `M/IM` and `M` is finite, then some `r ∈ 1 + I` makes
`s` generate `M` after localizing at the powers of `r`.

"`s` generates `M/IM`" is taken literally, as `s` spanning the quotient `M ⧸ I • ⊤`. Internally
that is converted to the `Submodule.span R s ⊔ I • ⊤ = ⊤` form which part (3) consumes, by
`span_sup_smul_top_eq_top_of_span_image_mk_eq_top`. Stated against arbitrary localization
witnesses `S`, `fM`; for the concrete reading see
`Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_span_image_mkLinearMap_eq_top`.

The tag writes a finite list `x₁, …, xₙ`, but finiteness of the generating set is not used —
only finiteness of `M`. Take `s := Set.range x` to recover the tag's form.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_span_image_eq_top
    (I : Ideal R) [Module.Finite R M] (s : Set M)
    (hs : Submodule.span R
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk '' s : Set (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = ⊤) :
    ∃ r : R, r - 1 ∈ I ∧ ∀ {S Mᵣ : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
      [AddCommGroup Mᵣ] [Module R Mᵣ] [Module S Mᵣ] [IsScalarTower R S Mᵣ]
      [IsLocalization (Submonoid.powers r) S] (fM : M →ₗ[R] Mᵣ)
      [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers r) fM],
      Submodule.span S (fM '' s) = ⊤

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_span_image_mkLinearMap_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (7)**, in the concrete `LocalizedModule` model: the tag's literal
"`x₁, …, xₙ` generate `M_f` over `R_f`".
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_span_image_mkLinearMap_eq_top
    (I : Ideal R) [Module.Finite R M] (s : Set M)
    (hs : Submodule.span R
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk '' s : Set (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = ⊤) :
    ∃ r : R, r - 1 ∈ I ∧
      Submodule.span (Localization (Submonoid.powers r))
        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers r) M '' s) = ⊤

declarations.name: Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00DV (9)**: if `N ≤ I • N` and `I` is nilpotent, then `N = ⊥`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_isNilpotent (I : Ideal R) (N : Submodule R M)
    (hI : IsNilpotent I) (hN : N ≤ I • N) : N = ⊥

declarations.name: Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (10)**: if `N' ≤ N ⊔ I • N'` and `I` is nilpotent, then `N' ≤ N`.

The nilpotent counterpart of `Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot` (part (4)), which
assumes `I ≤ jacobson ⊥` and `N'.FG` instead; as everywhere in this block the finiteness goes.

This is (9) read in `M ⧸ N`: mapping the hypothesis through `N.mkQ` kills the `N` summand
(`Submodule.mkQ_map_self`) while `Submodule.map_smul''` carries `I • N'` across, leaving
`map N.mkQ N' ≤ I • map N.mkQ N'` — exactly (9)'s hypothesis on the quotient.

The tag words it as `M = N + I N'`; that is the case `N' := ⊤`, reached from the tag's hypothesis
via `I • N' ≤ I • ⊤`. Parts (11) and (12) are both this lemma at `N' := ⊤`, with `N` taken to be
`range φ` and `span R s` respectively.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_isNilpotent {I : Ideal R} {N N' : Submodule R M}
    (hI : IsNilpotent I) (hNN : N' ≤ N ⊔ I • N') : N' ≤ N

declarations.name: LinearMap.surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (11)**: if `φ : N →ₗ[R] M` has `N/IN → M/IM` surjective and `I` is nilpotent,
then `φ` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem LinearMap.surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ_of_isNilpotent
    (I : Ideal R) (φ : N →ₗ[R] M) (hI : IsNilpotent I)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ ∘ₗ φ)) :
    Function.Surjective φ

declarations.name: Submodule.span_eq_top_of_span_image_mkQ_eq_top_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (12)**: if `s` generates `M/IM` and `I` is nilpotent, then `s` generates `M`.

The nilpotent counterpart of part (8), and (10) at `N := span R s`, `N' := ⊤`. As in part (7) the
hypothesis is taken literally — `s` spans the quotient `M ⧸ I • ⊤` — and nothing requires `s` to
be finite, so the tag's `{xα}` is an arbitrary `s : Set M`. Unlike (7), `M` need not be finite
either.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.span_eq_top_of_span_image_mkQ_eq_top_of_isNilpotent
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsNilpotent I) (s : Set M)
    (hs : Submodule.span R
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk '' s : Set (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = ⊤) :
    Submodule.span R s = ⊤

declarations.name: Submodule.span_eq_top_of_span_image_mkQ_eq_top_of_le_jacobson_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (8)**: if `M` is finite, `I ≤ rad(R)`, and the image of `s` spans `M ⧸ I • ⊤`,
then `s` spans `M`.

The hypothesis "`s` generates `M/IM`" is taken literally, as `s` spanning the quotient
`M ⧸ I • ⊤`. Finiteness of `s` is not used, so `s` is an arbitrary set; the tag's
`x₁, …, xₙ` is `s := Set.range x`, see
`Submodule.span_range_eq_top_of_span_range_mkQ_eq_top_of_le_jacobson_bot`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.span_eq_top_of_span_image_mkQ_eq_top_of_le_jacobson_bot
    [Module.Finite R M] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥) (s : Set M)
    (hs : Submodule.span R
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk '' s : Set (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = ⊤) :
    Submodule.span R s = ⊤
declarations.comment:
(8): elements of a finite module `M` generating `M/IM`, with `I ⊆ rad(R)`,
  generate `M`; stated for an arbitrary set `s`.

declarations.name: Submodule.span_range_eq_top_of_span_range_mkQ_eq_top_of_le_jacobson_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00DV (8)**, for a finite family: if `M` is finite, `I ≤ rad(R)`, and the images of
`x₁, …, xₙ` generate `M ⧸ I • ⊤`, then `x₁, …, xₙ` generate `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.span_range_eq_top_of_span_range_mkQ_eq_top_of_le_jacobson_bot
    [Module.Finite R M] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥) {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → M)
    (hx : Submodule.span R
      (Set.range fun i ↦ (Submodule.Quotient.mk (x i) : M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = ⊤) :
    Submodule.span R (Set.range x) = ⊤
declarations.comment: (8): the tag's literal form, for a family `x : Fin n → M`.

registrations.name: LinearMap.surjective_of_surjective_comp_mkQ
registrations.comment:
(6): `N → M` with `N/IN → M/IM` surjective, `M` finite and
  `I ⊆ rad(R)` forces `N → M` surjective. Mathlib swaps the names of source and target.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_eq_top_iff_isUnit
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_eq_top_iff_isUnit {f : R} :
    basicOpen f = ⊤ ↔ IsUnit f

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_eq_of_unit_mul
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_eq_of_unit_mul {f f' u : R} (hu : IsUnit u) (h : f = u * f') :
    basicOpen f = basicOpen f'

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_basicOpen_disjoint_zeroLocus
PrimeSpectrum.iUnion_basicOpen_eq_compl_zeroLocus
declarations.statement:
theorem iUnion_basicOpen_eq_compl_zeroLocus {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R) :
    (⋃ i, (basicOpen (f i) : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))) = (zeroLocus (Set.range f))ᶜ

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E4**: for `S` a localization of `R` away from `f` (such as `R_f`), the map
`Spec S → Spec R` induced by `R → S` is a homeomorphism onto the standard open `D(f)`.

The forward map is `comap (algebraMap R S)` (`localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen_apply_coe`)
and the inverse sends `𝔭` to `𝔭 · S` (`localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen_symm_apply_asIdeal`).
It is assembled from Mathlib's `localization_away_isOpenEmbedding` (a homeomorphism onto the
range) and `localization_away_comap_range` (the range is `D(f)`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R) [IsLocalization.Away f S] : PrimeSpectrum S ≃ₜ basicOpen f
declarations.comment: the homeomorphism `Spec(R_f) → D(f)`

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen_symm_apply_asIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E4**, the inverse: the inverse of `Spec S → D(f)` sends `𝔭 ∈ D(f)` to the prime
`𝔭 · S`, the ideal of `S` generated by the image of `𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen_symm_apply_asIdeal (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S]
    [Algebra R S] (f : R) [IsLocalization.Away f S] (p : basicOpen f) :
    ((localizationAwayHomeomorphBasicOpen S f).symm p).asIdeal =
      Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (p : PrimeSpectrum R).asIdeal
declarations.comment: the inverse is `𝔭 ↦ 𝔭 · R_f`

declarations.name: Ideal.primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E5**: the quotient map `R → R ⧸ I` induces, via `PrimeSpectrum.comap`, a
homeomorphism `Spec (R ⧸ I) ≃ₜ V(I)`. The forward map is `comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)`
(`Ideal.coe_primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus_apply`), and the inverse sends `𝔭` to
`𝔭 / I = 𝔭.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)`
(`Ideal.primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus_symm_apply`).

The underlying bijection is Mathlib's `Ideal.primeSpectrumQuotientOrderIsoZeroLocus`; it is a
homeomorphism because `comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)` is an embedding
(`PrimeSpectrum.isEmbedding_comap_of_surjective`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus :
    PrimeSpectrum (R ⧸ I) ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (R := R) I

declarations.name: Ideal.coe_primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E5**, the forward map: the homeomorphism `Spec (R ⧸ I) ≃ₜ V(I)` is induced by the
quotient map `R → R ⧸ I` via the functoriality of `Spec`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus_apply (p : PrimeSpectrum (R ⧸ I)) :
    (I.primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus p : PrimeSpectrum R) =
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (Quotient.mk I) p
declarations.comment: the map is `comap` of the quotient map

declarations.name: Ideal.primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E5**, the inverse: the inverse of `Spec (R ⧸ I) ≃ₜ V(I)` sends `𝔭 ⊇ I` to
`𝔭 / I`, the image of `𝔭` in `R ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus_symm_apply
    (p : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (R := R) I) :
    (I.primeSpectrumQuotientHomeomorphZeroLocus.symm p).asIdeal =
      p.1.asIdeal.map (Quotient.mk I)
declarations.comment: the inverse is `𝔭 ↦ 𝔭 / I`

declarations.name: Ideal.nontrivial_fiber_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E7**, clause (2) ⇔ clause (3): the fibre `κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S` is nonzero if and only if
`S_𝔭 / 𝔭 S_𝔭` is nonzero.

Both are ways of saying the fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` over `𝔭` is nonempty; for the link to
clause (1), that `𝔭` lies in the image, see `PrimeSpectrum.nontrivial_iff_mem_rangeComap`
(tagged in `StacksCore.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.RingHom`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nontrivial_fiber_iff :
    Nontrivial (p.Fiber S) ↔ Nontrivial (Sp ⧸ p.map (algebraMap R Sp))

declarations.name: Ideal.nontrivial_quotient_localization_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E7**, clause (3) ⇔ clause (4): `S_𝔭 / 𝔭 S_𝔭` is nonzero if and only if
`(S/𝔭S)_𝔭` is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem nontrivial_quotient_localization_iff :
    Nontrivial SpS ↔ Nontrivial (Sp ⧸ p.map (algebraMap R Sp))

registrations.name: PrimeSpectrum.mem_range_comap_iff
registrations.comment: (1) ⇔ (5): `𝔭` is in the image of `Spec S → Spec R` iff `𝔭 = φ⁻¹(𝔭S)`.

registrations.name: PrimeSpectrum.nontrivial_iff_mem_rangeComap
registrations.comment:
(1) ⇔ (2): `𝔭` is in the image of `Spec S → Spec R` iff the fibre
  `κ(𝔭) ⊗[R] S` is nonzero. The tag writes the tensor product in the other order.

declarations.name: isLocalRing_iff_exists_maximal_isUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E9**, clause (1) ⇔ (3): a ring is local if and only if it has a maximal ideal
`m` such that every element outside `m` is a unit.

The forward direction takes `m` to be `IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R`, where being outside `m` is
*definitionally* being a unit (`IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal`). The reverse direction cannot
use `IsLocalRing.of_unique_max_ideal` directly — that wants uniqueness, which is not assumed —
so it goes through `IsLocalRing.of_nonunits_add`: the hypothesis says every nonunit lies in `m`,
and `m` is closed under addition. Nontriviality comes from `m ≠ ⊤`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalRing_iff_exists_maximal_isUnit {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] :
    IsLocalRing R ↔ ∃ m : Ideal R, m.IsMaximal ∧ ∀ x : R, x ∉ m → IsUnit x

declarations.name: isLocalRing_iff_existsUnique_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00E9**, clause (1) ⇔ (2): a ring is local if and only if its spectrum has exactly
one closed point.

The clause is genuinely topological, so it is stated that way rather than as uniqueness of a
maximal ideal. `PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_singleton_iff_isMaximal` is what converts between the
two, in both directions; the rest is transport between `PrimeSpectrum R` and `Ideal R` along
`PrimeSpectrum.ext`.

No nontriviality hypothesis is needed: for the zero ring the spectrum is empty, so it has no
closed point at all and clause (2) fails on its own.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalRing_iff_existsUnique_isClosed_singleton {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] :
    IsLocalRing R ↔ ∃! p : PrimeSpectrum R, IsClosed ({p} : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self
registrations.comment: (1) ⇒ (4): in a local ring, `x` or `1 - x` is a unit.

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.of_isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self
registrations.comment:
(4) ⇒ (1): a nontrivial ring in which `x` or `1 - x` is always a unit is
  local.

declarations.name: localization_eq_of_unique_prime_over
declarations.doc:
If `p` is a prime of `R` with a unique prime `q` of `S` lying over it, and `R → S`
satisfies going up (or going down together with injectivity of contraction on primes),
then the localization of `S` at the image of `R ∖ p` is also a localization of `S` at
the complement of `q`; that is, `S_p = S_q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_eq_of_unique_prime_over
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    (huniq : ∀ q' : Ideal S, q'.IsPrime → q'.LiesOver p → q' = q)
    (h2 :
      (∀ (p₁ p₂ : Ideal R) (q₁ : Ideal S), p₁.IsPrime → p₂.IsPrime → q₁.IsPrime →
          p₁ ≤ p₂ → q₁.under R = p₁ →
            ∃ q₂ : Ideal S, q₂.IsPrime ∧ q₁ ≤ q₂ ∧ q₂.under R = p₂) ∨
      (Algebra.HasGoingDown R S ∧
        ∀ (q₁ q₂ : Ideal S), q₁.IsPrime → q₂.IsPrime →
          q₁.under R = q₂.under R → q₁ = q₂)) :
    IsLocalization q.primeCompl
      (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S p.primeCompl))

registrations.name: PrimeSpectrum.sigmaToPiHomeo
registrations.comment: for an arbitrary finite product

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.preconnectedSpace_iff_mul_eq_zero_add_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EF**, in its most general form. Over a semiring the statement must be phrased with
*complementary pairs* rather than idempotents: an idempotent need not have a complement, so
"every idempotent is `0` or `1`" is strictly stronger than preconnectedness there. Mathlib's own
example, on `PrimeSpectrum.mulZeroAddOneEquivClopens`, is the semiring `{0, 0.5, 1}` with `⊔ = +`
and `⊓ = *`, in which `0.5` is idempotent and uncomplemented.

Pairs `e * f = 0`, `e + f = 1` are exactly what index the clopens of `Spec R`, which is why this
is the level at which the equivalence is true.
declarations.statement:
theorem preconnectedSpace_iff_mul_eq_zero_add_eq_one :
    PreconnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) ↔
      ∀ e f : R, e * f = 0 → e + f = 1 → e = 0 ∨ f = 0
declarations.comment: for a semiring, phrased with complementary pairs

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.preconnectedSpace_iff_isIdempotentElem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EF** without the nonzero hypothesis. Over a ring every idempotent `e` has the
complement `1 - e`, so the pair formulation collapses to the familiar one.

This form needs no `Nontrivial R`: for the zero ring `Spec R` is empty, hence preconnected, and
the right-hand side holds vacuously. It is `ConnectedSpace` — which bundles nonemptiness — that
forces the hypothesis, see `connectedSpace_iff_isIdempotentElem`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preconnectedSpace_iff_isIdempotentElem :
    PreconnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) ↔ ∀ e : R, IsIdempotentElem e → e = 0 ∨ e = 1
declarations.comment: without the nonzero hypothesis, for `PreconnectedSpace`

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.connectedSpace_iff_isIdempotentElem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EF**: for a nonzero ring, `Spec R` is connected if and only if `R` has no
nontrivial idempotents.

The `Nontrivial R` hypothesis is load-bearing and not merely inherited from the tag's wording:
for the zero ring the right-hand side holds vacuously while `Spec R` is empty, so `ConnectedSpace`
fails. Dropping it would make the statement false, not weaker.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_iff_isIdempotentElem [Nontrivial R] :
    ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) ↔ ∀ e : R, IsIdempotentElem e → e = 0 ∨ e = 1

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_connectedComponent_eq_zeroLocus_span_isIdempotentElem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00EG.** For any commutative ring `R` and any point `x` of
`Spec R`, the connected component of `x` is `V(I)` for an ideal `I` generated by
idempotents such that every idempotent of `R` maps to `0` or `1` in `R/I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.exists_connectedComponent_eq_zeroLocus_span_isIdempotentElem
    (x : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    ∃ I : Ideal R,
      connectedComponent x = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R) ∧
      I = Ideal.span {e : R | e ∈ I ∧ IsIdempotentElem e} ∧
      ∀ e : R, IsIdempotentElem e →
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk I e = 0 ∨ Ideal.Quotient.mk I e = 1)

declarations.name: IsLocalization.Away.quotient_span_singleton_of_isIdempotentElem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EH**, clause (2), in the tag's orientation: for an idempotent `e`, the quotient
`R ⧸ (e)` is the localization of `R` away from `1 - e`.

This is `IsLocalization.Away.quotient_of_isIdempotentElem` with `e` replaced by `1 - e`, but that
substitution cannot be performed by rewriting: the offending `1 - (1 - e)` occurs as a *type index*
of the quotient, so `simp` and `▸` both fail on the motive. Going through
`IsLocalization.away_of_isIdempotentElem` instead puts the kernel equation in hypothesis position,
where `simp` reaches it.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalization.Away.quotient_span_singleton_of_isIdempotentElem {e : R}
    (he : IsIdempotentElem e) : IsLocalization.Away (1 - e) (R ⧸ Ideal.span {e})

declarations.name: IsLocalization.Away.quotientAlgEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EH**, clause (2), as the isomorphism the tag states. Mathlib carries only the
`IsLocalization.Away` predicate, never a bundled map, so this records `R ⧸ (e) ≅ R_{1 - e}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsLocalization.Away.quotientAlgEquiv {e : R} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
    (R ⧸ Ideal.span {e}) ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away (1 - e)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isClopen_zeroLocus_of_isIdempotentElem_of_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EH**, clause (3): the vanishing locus of a finitely generated idempotent ideal is
open as well as closed.

Only one implication holds. `I.FG` cannot be dropped — in a rank-one non-discrete valuation ring
the maximal ideal satisfies `m * m = m` without being finitely generated, and `V(m)` is closed but
not open — and there is no converse: for `I = (x)` in `k[x]/(x²)` the set `V(I)` is all of
`Spec R`, hence clopen, while `I * I = 0 ≠ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClopen_zeroLocus_of_isIdempotentElem_of_fg {I : Ideal R} (hfg : I.FG)
    (h : IsIdempotentElem I) : IsClopen (zeroLocus (I : Set R))

declarations.name: alphaLin_injective
declarations.doc: If `f` generates the unit ideal, then `α` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem alphaLin_injective (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) :
    Function.Injective (alphaLin R n f)
declarations.comment: exactness at `R`, i.e. injectivity of `α`

declarations.name: ker_betaLin_eq_range_alphaLin
declarations.doc: If `f` generates the unit ideal, then the kernel of `β` equals the range of `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_betaLin_eq_range_alphaLin (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) :
    LinearMap.ker (betaLin R n f) = LinearMap.range (alphaLin R n f)
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term, i.e. `ker β = im α`

declarations.name: IsLocalizedModule.Away.injective_pi_and_exact_of_span_range_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative semiring, let `f : ι → R` be a family of elements generating the unit
ideal and let `M` be an `R`-module. Let `Mf i` be the localization of `M` away from `f i`, with
localization map `g i`, and let `Mff i j` be the localization of `M` away from `f i * f j`,
reached from `Mf i` by `l i j` and from `Mf j` by `r i j`. Then the sequence
`0 → M → ∏ i, Mf i → ∏ (i, j), Mff i j`
is exact, the first map being `m ↦ (g i m)` and the second
`(m i) ↦ (l i j (m i) - r i j (m j))`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_pi_and_exact_of_span_range_eq_top
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (hlr : ∀ i j, (l i j).comp (g i) = (r i j).comp (g j)) :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.pi g) ∧
      Function.Exact (LinearMap.pi g) (LinearMap.pi fun p : ι × ι ↦
        (l p.1 p.2).comp (LinearMap.proj p.1) - (r p.1 p.2).comp (LinearMap.proj p.2))

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_ringEquiv_prod_of_isOpen_of_isCompl
declarations.doc:
A disjoint open cover of `Spec R` yields a product decomposition of `R`.

Let `R` be a commutative ring with `Spec(R) = U ⊔ V` for two open subsets `U, V`.
Then there is an idempotent `e ∈ R` such that, setting `R₁ := R⧸(1-e)` and
`R₂ := R⧸e`:

* the canonical ring map `φ := RingHom.quotientProdOneSub e : R →+* R₁ × R₂` lifts to a
  ring isomorphism `R ≃+* R₁ × R₂`;
* `Spec(R₁)` is homeomorphic to `U` (as a subspace of `Spec R`) and `Spec(R₂)`
  is homeomorphic to `V`, with both homeomorphisms realised by the canonical maps
  of the product decomposition, i.e. via `PrimeSpectrum.primeSpectrumProdHomeo`;
* each factor is simultaneously a quotient and a localization of `R`:
  the quotient maps make `R₁` a localization at `e` and `R₂` a localization at `1 - e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.exists_ringEquiv_prod_of_isOpen_of_isCompl
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {U V : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hV : IsOpen V)
    (h : IsCompl U V) :
    ∃ e : R, IsIdempotentElem e ∧
      ∃ φ : R ≃+* (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set R)) ×
                  (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({e} : Set R)),
        (φ : R →+* (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set R)) ×
                   (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({e} : Set R))) = RingHom.quotientProdOneSub e ∧
        (∃ eU : PrimeSpectrum (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set R)) ≃ₜ U,
          ∀ p, (eU p).1 =
            PrimeSpectrum.comap
              (φ : R →+* (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set R)) ×
                         (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({e} : Set R)))
              (PrimeSpectrum.primeSpectrumProdHomeo.symm (Sum.inl p))) ∧
        (∃ eV : PrimeSpectrum (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({e} : Set R)) ≃ₜ V,
          ∀ p, (eV p).1 =
            PrimeSpectrum.comap
              (φ : R →+* (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set R)) ×
                         (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({e} : Set R)))
              (PrimeSpectrum.primeSpectrumProdHomeo.symm (Sum.inr p))) ∧
        IsLocalization.Away e (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set R)) ∧
        IsLocalization.Away (1 - e) (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({e} : Set R))

declarations.name: Module.subsingleton_of_localizationSpan_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (1).** If each canonical localisation
`LocalizedModule (powers (f i)) M` is the zero module and the `f i` generate the
unit ideal, then `M` itself is the zero module.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.subsingleton_of_localizationSpan_range
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, Subsingleton (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) M)) :
    Subsingleton M

declarations.name: Module.Finite.of_localizationSpan_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (2).** If each canonical localisation `M_{f i}` is finite over
`R_{f i}` and the `f i` generate the unit ideal, then `M` is a finite `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Finite.of_localizationSpan_range
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, Module.Finite (Localization.Away (f i))
                            (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) M)) :
    Module.Finite R M

declarations.name: bijective_of_localized_span_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (4).** If `φ : M →ₗ[R] N` is bijective after canonical
localisation at each `f i` and the `f i` generate the unit ideal, then `φ` is
bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_of_localized_span_range
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    {M N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N)
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (hiso : ∀ i, Function.Bijective
                  (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (f i)) φ)) :
    Function.Bijective φ

declarations.name: shortExact_of_localized_span_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (5).** Let `g : M'' →ₗ[R] M` and `h : M →ₗ[R] M'` be linear maps.
If `0 → M''_{f i} → M_{f i} → M'_{f i} → 0` is exact for each `i` and the `f i`
generate the unit ideal, then `0 → M'' → M → M' → 0` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_of_localized_span_range
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    {M'' M M' : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid M''] [Module R M'']
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M']
    (g : M'' →ₗ[R] M) (h : M →ₗ[R] M')
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (hexact : ∀ i,
      Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (f i)) g) ∧
      Function.Exact (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (f i)) g)
        (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (f i)) h) ∧
      Function.Surjective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (f i)) h)) :
    Function.Injective g ∧ Function.Exact g h ∧ Function.Surjective h

declarations.name: IsNoetherianRing.of_localizationSpan_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (6).** If each canonical `R_{f i} = Localization.Away (f i)`
is Noetherian and the `f i` generate the unit ideal, then `R` is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsNoetherianRing.of_localizationSpan_range
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (Localization.Away (f i))) :
    IsNoetherianRing R

declarations.name: Algebra.FiniteType.of_localizationSpan_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (7).** If each canonical `S_{f i}` is a finite-type
`R_{f i}`-algebra and the `f i` generate the unit ideal, then `S` is a
finite-type `R`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FiniteType.of_localizationSpan_range
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap R S) (f i)).FiniteType) :
    Algebra.FiniteType R S

declarations.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_localizationSpan_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (8).** If each canonical `S_{f i}` is of finite presentation
over `R_{f i}` and the `f i` generate the unit ideal, then `S` is a finitely
presented `R`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_localizationSpan_range
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (f i))
                              (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S (f i))) :=
                (IsLocalization.Away.map (Localization.Away (f i))
                  (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S (f i)))
                  (algebraMap R S) (f i)).toAlgebra
              Algebra.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away (f i))
                                         (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S (f i)))) :
    Algebra.FinitePresentation R S

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentation.of_localizationSpan_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EO (3).** If each canonical localisation `M_{f i}` is finitely
presented over `R_{f i}` and the `f i` generate the unit ideal, then `M` is
finitely presented over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.FinitePresentation.of_localizationSpan_range
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {ι : Type*} (f : ι → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away (f i))
                                       (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) M)) :
    Module.FinitePresentation R M

declarations.name: ModuleGluingData.psi_apply_of_mem_gluedModule
declarations.doc: For `m ∈ gluedModule`, the gluing relation holds: `ψ i j (m_i/1) = m_j/1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma psi_apply_of_mem_gluedModule
    (D : ModuleGluingData ι f) (m : D.gluedModule) (i j : ι) :
    D.ψ i j (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (f j))
              (D.M i) ((m : D.DirectSumM) i)) =
      LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (f i)) (D.M j) ((m : D.DirectSumM) j)
declarations.comment: moreover clause: `ψ i j (m/1) = m/1` for `m` in the glued module

declarations.name: ModuleGluingData.proj_isLocalizedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00EQ (localization comparison).** For finite module gluing data, projection to the
`i`-th component is the localization map at the powers of `f i`. Thus the induced canonical map
from the localization of the glued module to `D.M i` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem proj_isLocalizedModule (D : ModuleGluingData ι f) (i : ι) :
    IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) (D.proj i)
declarations.comment: localization comparison

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_and_isIrreducible_iff_exists_isPrime_eq_zeroLocus
declarations.doc:
A subset of `Spec R` is closed and irreducible if and only if it is `V(p)` for a prime
ideal `p` of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_and_isIrreducible_iff_exists_isPrime_eq_zeroLocus {s : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} :
    IsClosed s ∧ IsIrreducible s ↔ ∃ p : Ideal R, p.IsPrime ∧ s = zeroLocus (p : Set R)
declarations.comment: (2) the irreducible closed subsets of Spec R are exactly the V(p), p prime

registrations.name: PrimeSpectrum.closure_singleton
registrations.comment: (1) the closure of {p} is V(p)

registrations.name: PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_minimalPrimes
registrations.comment: (3) the irreducible components of Spec R are exactly the V(p), p minimal

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.irreducibleClosedThroughEquiv
declarations.doc:
Part (1): The irreducible closed subsets of `Spec(R)` passing through `𝔭`
correspond to the prime ideals of any localization `S` of `R` at `𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
def irreducibleClosedThroughEquiv :
    irreducibleClosedThrough R 𝔭 ≃ { q : Ideal S // q.IsPrime }

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.irreducibleComponentsThroughEquiv
declarations.doc:
Part (2): The irreducible components of `Spec(R)` passing through `𝔭`
correspond to the minimal prime ideals of any localization `S` of `R` at `𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
def irreducibleComponentsThroughEquiv :
    irreducibleComponentsThrough R 𝔭 ≃ minimalPrimes S

registrations.name: Ring.KrullDimLE.of_isLocalization
registrations.comment: localization at a minimal prime is zero-dimensional

registrations.name: Ring.KrullDimLE.isNilpotent_iff_mem_maximalIdeal
registrations.comment: maximal ideal consists of nilpotents

registrations.name: Ring.KrullDimLE.isField_of_isReduced
registrations.comment: reduced case: the localization is a field

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_disjoint_basicOpen_of_mem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
Let `𝔭` be a minimal prime of `R` and let `W ⊆ Spec R` be a quasi-compact open not containing
`𝔭`. Then some `f ∉ 𝔭` has `D(f)` disjoint from `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.exists_disjoint_basicOpen_of_mem_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    {𝔭 : Ideal R} (h𝔭min : 𝔭 ∈ minimalPrimes R)
    {W : TopologicalSpace.Opens (PrimeSpectrum R)}
    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)))
    (h𝔭W : (⟨𝔭, h𝔭min.isPrime⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R) ∉ W) :
    ∃ f ∉ 𝔭,
      Disjoint (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
        (W : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))

declarations.name: isField_localizationAtPrime_of_minimal
declarations.doc: The localization of a reduced ring at a minimal prime is a field.
declarations.statement:
lemma isField_localizationAtPrime_of_minimal (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsReduced R]
    (p : Ideal R) (hp : p ∈ minimalPrimes R) :
    haveI : p.IsPrime := hp.isPrime
    IsField (Localization.AtPrime p)
declarations.comment: 2, the factors are fields

declarations.name: localizationProdMap_injective
declarations.doc:
The map `R → ∏_{p minimal} R_p` from a reduced commutative ring to the product of localizations
at minimal primes is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationProdMap_injective (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] :
    Function.Injective (localizationProdMap R)
declarations.comment: 2, injectivity; the factors are fields by isField_localizationAtPrime_of_minimal

declarations.name: exists_injective_ringHom_pi_field
declarations.doc:
A reduced commutative ring embeds into a product of fields, indexed by a type in the universe
of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_ringHom_pi_field.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsReduced R] :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (K : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
      (f : R →+* (∀ i, K i)), Function.Injective f

declarations.name: iUnion_minimalPrimes_eq_zeroDivisors
declarations.doc:
The union of the minimal primes of a reduced commutative ring equals its set of zero
divisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem iUnion_minimalPrimes_eq_zeroDivisors (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] :
    (⋃ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, (p : Set R)) = zeroDivisorSet R

declarations.name: IntXSqSubFour.isPrime_iff
declarations.doc:
**Classification of `Spec(R)` (Stacks Tag 00EY).**
An ideal `p` of `R = ℤ[x]/(x² - 4)` is prime if and only if it is one of the
listed ideals: `(2, x̄)`, or `(q, x̄ - 2)`/`(q, x̄ + 2)` for some odd prime `q`,
or one of the two generic primes `(x̄ - 2)`, `(x̄ + 2)`.

A prime contains `x̄ - 2` or `x̄ + 2`, since their product is `0`. The evaluations
`R → ℤ`, `x̄ ↦ ±2`, are surjective with kernels `(x̄ ∓ 2)`, so the primes containing
`x̄ ∓ 2` are the preimages of the primes `(0)` and `(q)` of `ℤ`; for `q = 2` both
preimages are `(2, x̄)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPrime_iff (p : Ideal IntXSqSubFour) :
    p.IsPrime ↔
      (p = p2 ∨
       (∃ q : ℕ, q.Prime ∧ Odd q ∧ (p = pMinus q ∨ p = pPlus q)) ∨
       p = gMinus ∨ p = gPlus)

declarations.name: Polynomial.isPrime_int_trichotomy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00EZ** (Description of `Spec(ℤ[x])`).

Every prime ideal `𝔭` of `ℤ[x]` has one of the following forms:
* `𝔭 = (0)`;
* `𝔭 = (f)` with `f` irreducible in `ℤ[x]`; this covers the nonzero primes with
  `𝔭 ∩ ℤ = (0)` and the primes `(q)` (take `f = q`) for a prime number `q`;
* `𝔭 = (q, f)` for a prime number `q` and `f` irreducible in `ℤ[x]` whose reduction modulo `q`
  is irreducible in `(ℤ/qℤ)[x]`.

The Stacks text omits the primes `(q)`, which lie over `(q)` without being of the third form.
declarations.statement:
theorem Polynomial.isPrime_int_trichotomy
    (𝔭 : Ideal ℤ[X]) (h𝔭 : 𝔭.IsPrime) :
    𝔭 = ⊥ ∨
    (∃ f : ℤ[X], Irreducible f ∧ 𝔭 = Ideal.span {f}) ∨
    (∃ (q : ℕ) (f : ℤ[X]), q.Prime ∧
        Irreducible f ∧
        Irreducible (f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod q))) ∧
        𝔭 = Ideal.span {(C (q : ℤ)), f})

declarations.name: Polynomial.isPrime_iff_eq_bot_or_eq_span_or_eq_span_pair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00F0**, both directions: the prime ideals of `R[X]`, for `R` a principal ideal
domain. The tag is the case `R = k[x]` for a field `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPrime_iff_eq_bot_or_eq_span_or_eq_span_pair [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]
    (P : Ideal R[X]) :
    P.IsPrime ↔ P = ⊥ ∨ (∃ f : R[X], Irreducible f ∧ P = span {f}) ∨
      (∃ (p : R) (f : R[X]), Irreducible p ∧
        Irreducible (Ideal.Quotient.mk (span {C p}) f) ∧ P = span {C p, f})
declarations.comment: for `R[X]` over any principal ideal domain `R`; the tag is the case `R = k[x]`

declarations.name: NodalCubicAffineOpen.isOpenEmbedding_comap_inclRToRa
declarations.doc:
The inclusion `R ↪ R_a` induces an open embedding
`θ : Spec R_a → Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenEmbedding_comap_inclRToRa (a : ℚ)
    (ha0 : a ≠ 0) (ha1 : a ≠ 1) :
    Topology.IsOpenEmbedding
      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (inclRToRa a ha0 ha1).toRingHom)

declarations.name: NodalCubicAffineOpen.range_comap_inclRToRa
declarations.doc:
The image of `θ : Spec R_a → Spec R` is exactly the complement of the
closed point `𝔪_a` in `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_comap_inclRToRa (a : ℚ)
    (ha0 : a ≠ 0) (ha1 : a ≠ 1) :
    Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (inclRToRa a ha0 ha1).toRingHom) =
      {p : PrimeSpectrum R | p ≠ mRPoint a}
declarations.comment: the image of `θ` is `Spec R ∖ {𝔪_a}`

declarations.name: NodalCubicAffineOpen.range_comap_inclRToRa_ne_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
The image of `θ : Spec R_a → Spec R` is **not** the basic open `D(f)` of any
element `f ∈ R`. Hence `Spec R_a ⊂ Spec R` is an affine open which is not standard /
principal.

This is an extra observation, not a claim of the Stacks example: it is used below
to show that `R_a` is not a localization of `R`, where the source argues with units
instead.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_comap_inclRToRa_ne_basicOpen (a : ℚ)
    (ha0 : a ≠ 0) (ha1 : a ≠ 1) (ha12 : a ≠ 1 / 2) (f : R) :
    Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (inclRToRa a ha0 ha1).toRingHom) ≠
      (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
declarations.comment: extra observation: the image of `θ` is not a basic open of `Spec R`

declarations.name: NodalCubicAffineOpen.not_exists_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
`R_a` is **not** a localization of `R`: there is no submonoid `S ⊆ R`
for which `R_a` becomes the localization `S⁻¹ R` via `inclRToRa`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_exists_isLocalization (a : ℚ)
    (ha0 : a ≠ 0) (ha1 : a ≠ 1) (ha12 : a ≠ 1 / 2) :
    let _ : Algebra R (Ra a ha0 ha1) := (inclRToRa a ha0 ha1).toAlgebra
    ¬ ∃ (S : Submonoid R), IsLocalization S (Ra a ha0 ha1)
declarations.comment: `R_a` is not a localization of `R`

declarations.name: NodalCubicAffineOpen.adjoin_genA_genB_genW_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The functions `z² - z`, `z³ - z` and `(a² - a)/(z - a) + z` generate `R_a` as a
`ℚ`-algebra. The source assumes `a ∉ {0, ½, 1}`; only `a ≠ 0, 1` is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem adjoin_genA_genB_genW_eq_top (a : ℚ) (ha0 : a ≠ 0) (ha1 : a ≠ 1) :
    Algebra.adjoin ℚ {genA a ha0 ha1, genB a ha0 ha1, genW a ha0 ha1} = ⊤
declarations.comment:
`z² - z`, `z³ - z` and `(a² - a)/(z - a) + z` generate `R_a` as a
`ℚ`-algebra

declarations.name: RingHom.finiteType_finitePresentation_comp_and_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00F4 (Lemma 10.6.2).** Let `f : R →+* S'` and `g : S' →+* S` be ring maps.
1. If `f` and `g` are of finite type, so is `g.comp f` (`RingHom.FiniteType.comp`).
2. If `f` and `g` are of finite presentation, so is `g.comp f`
   (`RingHom.FinitePresentation.comp`).
3. If `g.comp f` is of finite type, so is `g` (`RingHom.FiniteType.of_comp_finiteType`).
4. If `g.comp f` is of finite presentation and `f` is of finite type, then `g` is of finite
   presentation (`RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_comp_finiteType`).
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteType_finitePresentation_comp_and_of_comp {R : Type u} {S' : Type v} {S : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S'] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S') (g : S' →+* S) :
    (f.FiniteType → g.FiniteType → (g.comp f).FiniteType) ∧
      (f.FinitePresentation → g.FinitePresentation → (g.comp f).FinitePresentation) ∧
      ((g.comp f).FiniteType → g.FiniteType) ∧
      ((g.comp f).FinitePresentation → f.FiniteType → g.FinitePresentation)
declarations.comment: the four parts of the lemma

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isCompact_preimage_comap_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
Stacks 00F7 (first assertion): for a ring map `φ : R → S`, the induced
continuous map `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is quasi-compact, i.e. the preimage of
every quasi-compact open of `Spec(R)` is quasi-compact in `Spec(S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.isCompact_preimage_comap_of_isOpen
    {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (V : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) (hV : IsOpen V) (hVc : IsCompact V) :
    IsCompact ((PrimeSpectrum.comap φ) ⁻¹' V)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isConstructible_preimage_comap
declarations.doc:
Stacks 00F7 (second assertion): for a ring map `φ : R → S` and any
constructible subset `E ⊆ Spec(R)`, the preimage `(comap φ)⁻¹(E)` is
constructible in `Spec(S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.isConstructible_preimage_comap
    {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (E : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) (hE : Topology.IsConstructible E) :
    Topology.IsConstructible ((PrimeSpectrum.comap φ) ⁻¹' E)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_range_eq_of_isConstructible_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00F8.** Every constructible subset of `Spec R` is the image of `Spec S` for a
finitely presented `R`-algebra `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_range_eq_of_isConstructible_finitePresentation {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {s : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} (hs : IsConstructible s) :
    ∃ (S : Type u) (_ : CommRing S) (f : R →+* S),
      f.FinitePresentation ∧ Set.range (comap f) = s

declarations.name: Polynomial.image_comap_C_basicOpen_eq_biUnion_basicOpen_coeffs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00FB**, second part. Let `R` be a ring and `f ∈ R[x]`. The image of the standard open
`D(f) ⊆ Spec(R[x])` under the map `Spec(R[x]) → Spec(R)` is the union of the standard opens `D(a)`,
`a` running over the coefficients of `f`; in particular it is a quasi-compact open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem image_comap_C_basicOpen_eq_biUnion_basicOpen_coeffs {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (f : R[X]) :
    PrimeSpectrum.comap (C : R →+* R[X]) '' (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R[X])) =
      ⋃ a ∈ f.coeffs, (basicOpen a : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
declarations.comment: Second part

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isNilpotent_baseChange_mulLeft_iff_mem_zeroLocus
declarations.doc:
For `A` free of rank `n` over `R` and `f : A`, the set of primes `p` at which
multiplication by `f` becomes nilpotent over the residue field is the zero locus of the first
`n` coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.isNilpotent_baseChange_mulLeft_iff_mem_zeroLocus
    {R A : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (n : ℕ) (e : A ≃ₗ[R] (Fin n → R))
    (f : A) (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    IsNilpotent
        (LinearMap.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (LinearMap.mulLeft R f)) ↔
      p ∈ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
        ((fun i : Fin n =>
            (charPolyOfEquiv e (LinearMap.mulLeft R f)).coeff i) '' Set.univ)

declarations.name: image_comap_C_basicOpen_inter_zeroLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00FD.** Let `R` be a ring and `f, g ∈ R[x]` polynomials whose
leading coefficient of `g` is a unit of `R`. Then the image of `D(f) ∩ V(g)`
under the structure map `Spec(R[x]) → Spec(R)` is a finite union of standard
opens: there exist `r_1, …, r_n ∈ R` with image `= ⋃ᵢ D(rᵢ)`.

Since the leading coefficient of `g` is a unit, `g` is associate to the monic
polynomial `g' = (leadingCoeff g)⁻¹ • g`, so `V(g) = V(g')`. For monic `g'`,
`R[x]/(g')` is finite free over `R`, and Mathlib's
`Polynomial.exists_image_comap_of_monic` produces a finite set `t ⊆ R` with
image `= (V(t))ᶜ = ⋃_{r ∈ t} D(r)`, which we reindex by `Fin n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_comap_C_basicOpen_inter_zeroLocus
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f g : R[X]) (hg : IsUnit g.leadingCoeff) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n → R),
      comap (C : R →+* R[X]) ''
          ((basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R[X])) ∩ zeroLocus {g}) =
        ⋃ i, (basicOpen (r i) : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))

declarations.name: GenericFinitePresentation.generic_finite_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Generic finite presentation.** An inclusion of domains of finite type admits nonzero
`f ∈ R` and `g ∈ S` such that `R[1/f] → S[1/(fg)]` is of finite presentation.
The domain hypothesis on `R` follows from injectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem GenericFinitePresentation.generic_finite_presentation
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) :
    ∃ (f : R) (g : S), f ≠ 0 ∧ g ≠ 0 ∧ (awayMapMul f g).FinitePresentation

declarations.name: image_constructible_contains_open_dense_in_closure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00FH (Lemma 10.30.2).**  Let `φ : R →+* S` be a ring map of finite type, let
`E ⊆ Spec S` be constructible, and let `ξ ∈ Spec R` lie in the image `f(E)` of `E` under
`f = PrimeSpectrum.comap φ`.  Then `closure {ξ} ∩ f(E)` contains a subset `D` that is open and
dense in the subspace `closure {ξ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_constructible_contains_open_dense_in_closure
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : φ.FiniteType)
    (E : Set (PrimeSpectrum S)) (hE : Topology.IsConstructible E)
    (ξ : PrimeSpectrum R)
    (hξ : ξ ∈ PrimeSpectrum.comap φ '' E) :
    ∃ D : Set (closure {ξ} : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)),
      IsOpen D ∧ Dense D ∧
      (Subtype.val '' D) ⊆ closure {ξ} ∩ (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ '' E)

declarations.name: main_equivalence
declarations.doc: Main equivalence: conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_equivalence
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) :
    (SpecSurjective φ ↔ RadicalContractionEq φ) ∧
    (RadicalContractionEq φ ↔ RadicalIdealContractionEq φ) ∧
    (RadicalIdealContractionEq φ ↔ PrimeContractionEq φ) ∧
    (PrimeContractionEq φ ↔ SpecSurjective φ)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1), (2), (3) and (4); the base change assertion is `base_change_preserves_specSurjective`, `base_change_preserves_radicalContractionEq`, `base_change_preserves_radicalIdealContractionEq` and `base_change_equivalence`

declarations.name: base_change_preserves_specSurjective
declarations.doc: Base change preserves Spec-surjectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem base_change_preserves_specSurjective
    {R S R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R']
    (φ : R →+* S) (ψ : R →+* R') :
    letI : Algebra R S := φ.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra R R' := ψ.toAlgebra
    SpecSurjective φ →
    SpecSurjective (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
      R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S)
declarations.comment: base change: property (1) of `R → S` passes to `R' → R' ⊗_R S` for every ring map `R → R'`

declarations.name: base_change_preserves_radicalContractionEq
declarations.doc: Condition (2) is stable under base change along `ψ : R →+* R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem base_change_preserves_radicalContractionEq
    {R S R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R']
    (φ : R →+* S) (ψ : R →+* R') :
    letI : Algebra R S := φ.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra R R' := ψ.toAlgebra
    RadicalContractionEq φ →
    RadicalContractionEq (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
      R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S)
declarations.comment: base change: property (2) of `R → S` passes to `R' → R' ⊗_R S` for every ring map `R → R'`

declarations.name: base_change_preserves_radicalIdealContractionEq
declarations.doc: Condition (3) is stable under base change along `ψ : R →+* R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem base_change_preserves_radicalIdealContractionEq
    {R S R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R']
    (φ : R →+* S) (ψ : R →+* R') :
    letI : Algebra R S := φ.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra R R' := ψ.toAlgebra
    RadicalIdealContractionEq φ →
    RadicalIdealContractionEq (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
      R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S)
declarations.comment: base change: property (3) of `R → S` passes to `R' → R' ⊗_R S` for every ring map `R → R'`

declarations.name: base_change_equivalence
declarations.doc: Conditions (1), (2), (3) are equivalent for the base-changed map.
declarations.statement:
theorem base_change_equivalence
    {R S R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R']
    (φ : R →+* S) (ψ : R →+* R') :
    letI : Algebra R S := φ.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra R R' := ψ.toAlgebra
    (SpecSurjective (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
        R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S) ↔
      RadicalContractionEq (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
        R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S)) ∧
    (RadicalContractionEq (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
        R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S) ↔
      RadicalIdealContractionEq (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
        R' →+* TensorProduct R R' S))
declarations.comment: base change: (1), (2) and (3) are equivalent for `R' → R' ⊗_R S`

declarations.name: domain_image_dense_set_points_generic_point_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a domain and `φ : R →+* S` a ring map. Then the following are equivalent:
1. `φ` is injective.
2. The range of the induced map `PrimeSpectrum.comap φ` is dense in `PrimeSpectrum R`.
3. There exists a prime `q` of `S` whose preimage under `φ` is the zero ideal of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem domain_image_dense_set_points_generic_point_tfae :
    List.TFAE
      [ Function.Injective φ
      , Dense (Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ))
      , ∃ q : PrimeSpectrum S, (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ q).asIdeal = ⊥ ]

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.tfae_isNilpotent_ker_minimalPrimes_denseRange_comap
declarations.doc:
For a ring map `f : R →+* S` the following are equivalent: every element of the kernel of `f`
is nilpotent; every minimal prime of `R` is in the image of `comap f : Spec S → Spec R`; the image
of `comap f` is dense in `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isNilpotent_ker_minimalPrimes_denseRange_comap :
    List.TFAE [∀ x ∈ RingHom.ker f, IsNilpotent x,
      ∀ I (h : I ∈ minimalPrimes R), ⟨I, h.1.1⟩ ∈ Set.range (comap f),
      DenseRange (comap f)]
declarations.comment: The three conditions of the lemma, in the order (1), (2), (3).

declarations.name: exists_monic_aeval_not_bijective_of_rank_lt_card
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and `V` a nonzero `k`-vector space with `dim_k V < |k|` (as cardinals).
Then for every `k`-linear operator `T : V → V` there is a monic polynomial `P` of degree `≥ 1`
such that `P(T)` is not bijective (i.e. not invertible).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_aeval_not_bijective_of_rank_lt_card
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [Nontrivial V]
    (h : Cardinal.lift.{u} (Module.rank k V) < Cardinal.lift.{v} (Cardinal.mk k))
    (T : V →ₗ[k] V) :
    ∃ P : k[X], P.Monic ∧ 1 ≤ P.natDegree ∧ ¬ Function.Bijective (aeval T P)

declarations.name: Stacks.HilbertNullstellensatz.module_finite_quotient_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Hilbert Nullstellensatz**, part (1), for a finite type algebra: if `A` is a `k`-algebra of
finite type over a field `k` and `𝔪 ⊆ A` is a maximal ideal, then the residue field
`κ(𝔪) = A ⧸ 𝔪` is a finite extension of `k`.

The quotient `A ⧸ 𝔪` is a field by `Ideal.Quotient.field`, and it is of finite type over `k`
because `A` is, so Zariski's lemma over the Jacobson ring `k` applies.
declarations.statement:
public theorem module_finite_quotient_of_finiteType (k A : Type*) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] (𝔪 : Ideal A) [𝔪.IsMaximal] :
    Module.Finite k (A ⧸ 𝔪)
declarations.comment: part (1), for an arbitrary finite type algebra over the field

declarations.name: Stacks.HilbertNullstellensatz.eq_sInf_isMaximal_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Hilbert Nullstellensatz**, part (2), for a finite type algebra: a radical ideal `I` of a
`k`-algebra `A` of finite type over a field `k` is the infimum of the maximal ideals of `A`
containing `I`.

A finite type algebra over a field is a Jacobson ring, and in a Jacobson ring a radical ideal
equals its Jacobson radical, which is by definition that infimum.
declarations.comment: part (2), for an arbitrary finite type algebra over the field

declarations.name: Stacks.HilbertNullstellensatz.module_finite_quotient_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Hilbert Nullstellensatz**, part (1): for a field `k`, finitely many variables `ι` and a
maximal ideal `𝔪` of the polynomial ring `k[x_i : i ∈ ι]`, the residue field
`κ(𝔪) = k[x_i : i ∈ ι] ⧸ 𝔪` is a finite extension of `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem module_finite_quotient_mvPolynomial (k : Type*) [Field k] (ι : Type*) [Finite ι]
    (𝔪 : Ideal (MvPolynomial ι k)) [𝔪.IsMaximal] :
    Module.Finite k (MvPolynomial ι k ⧸ 𝔪)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.HilbertNullstellensatz.eq_sInf_isMaximal_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Hilbert Nullstellensatz**, part (2): for a field `k` and finitely many variables `ι`, a
radical ideal `I` of the polynomial ring `k[x_i : i ∈ ι]` is the infimum of the maximal ideals
containing `I`.
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.HilbertNullstellensatz.coe_eq_iInter_isMaximal_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Hilbert Nullstellensatz**, part (2), as an equality of sets: a radical ideal `I` of the
polynomial ring `k[x_i : i ∈ ι]` over a field `k` in finitely many variables is, as a subset of
the polynomial ring, the intersection of the maximal ideals containing `I`.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: jacobson_quotient
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Jacobson ring and `I ⊆ R` an ideal. Then `R ⧸ I` is Jacobson, and
maximal ideals of `R ⧸ I` correspond (via `Ideal.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)`) to
maximal ideals of `R` containing `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobson_quotient
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsJacobsonRing R] (I : Ideal R) :
    IsJacobsonRing (R ⧸ I) ∧
      ∃ e : {M : Ideal (R ⧸ I) // M.IsMaximal} ≃
            {J : Ideal R // J.IsMaximal ∧ I ≤ J},
        ∀ (M : {M : Ideal (R ⧸ I) // M.IsMaximal}),
          (e M).1 = Ideal.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) M.1
