declarations.name: comap_image_subspaceClosedPoints_and_mem_comap_image_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00GD.** Let `R` be a Jacobson ring and `S` a finite type `R`-algebra (hence also
Jacobson, Stacks 00GB); write `X = Spec R`, `Y = Spec S` and `f : Y → X` for the induced map.
Let `E ⊆ Y` be constructible, and denote with a subscript `₀` the set of points of a subset
that are closed in it (`subspaceClosedPoints`; `X₀ = closedPoints X`). Then
1. `f(E)₀ = f(E₀) = X₀ ∩ f(E)`;
2. a point `ξ ∈ X` lies in `f(E)` if and only if `closure {ξ} ∩ f(E₀)` is dense in
   `closure {ξ}`, written `closure {ξ} ⊆ closure (closure {ξ} ∩ f(E₀))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_image_subspaceClosedPoints_and_mem_comap_image_iff :
    (subspaceClosedPoints (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) '' E) =
        PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) '' subspaceClosedPoints E ∧
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) '' subspaceClosedPoints E =
        closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum R) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) '' E) ∧
    ∀ ξ : PrimeSpectrum R, ξ ∈ PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) '' E ↔
      closure {ξ} ⊆ closure (closure {ξ} ∩
        PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) '' subspaceClosedPoints E)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_commSq_constructible_restrictToClosedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00GE.** Let `R` be a Noetherian Jacobson ring and `φ : R → S` a ring map of
finite type, with `f : Y = Spec S → X = Spec R`, and write `X₀`, `Y₀` for the spaces of closed
points. There is a commutative square
```
Constr(Y)  --E ↦ E₀-->  Constr(Y₀)
   |                       |
 f(·)                    f(·)
   v                       v
Constr(X)  --E ↦ E₀-->  Constr(X₀)
```
whose horizontal arrows are the bijections `E ↦ E ∩ X₀` of Stacks 005Y
(`JacobsonSpace.restrictToClosedPoints_bijective`) and whose vertical arrows take images under
`f` and under its restriction `Y₀ → X₀` (`mapsTo_comap_closedPoints`). Here `S` is Jacobson as
a finite-type algebra over a Jacobson ring, so 005Y applies to both `X` and `Y`.

The statement records the full content of the lemma: each of the four arrows is pinned down by
its action on underlying sets (so both vertical arrows are well defined, i.e. land in
constructible sets), both horizontal arrows are bijective, and `right ∘ top = bot ∘ left`, which
on underlying sets is `f(E)₀ = f(E₀)`.

The left arrow is well defined by Chevalley's theorem
(`isConstructible_comap_image_of_finiteType`, via Stacks 00FP and 00FE); commutativity is
`restrictToClosedPoints_comap_image` (part (1) of Stacks 00GD); the right arrow is then well
defined because every constructible subset of `Y₀` is some `E₀`, whose image `f(E₀) = f(E)₀` is
constructible.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_commSq_constructible_restrictToClosedPoints [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsJacobsonRing R] (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : φ.FiniteType) :
    ∃ (left : {E : Set (PrimeSpectrum S) // IsConstructible E} →
          {E : Set (PrimeSpectrum R) // IsConstructible E})
      (right : {F : Set (closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum S)) // IsConstructible F} →
          {F : Set (closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum R)) // IsConstructible F})
      (top : {E : Set (PrimeSpectrum S) // IsConstructible E} →
          {F : Set (closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum S)) // IsConstructible F})
      (bot : {E : Set (PrimeSpectrum R) // IsConstructible E} →
          {F : Set (closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum R)) // IsConstructible F}),
      (∀ E, (left E).1 = comap φ '' E.1) ∧
      (∀ F, (right F).1 = (mapsTo_comap_closedPoints hφ).restrict (comap φ) _ _ '' F.1) ∧
      (∀ E, (top E).1 = JacobsonSpace.restrictToClosedPoints E.1) ∧
      (∀ E, (bot E).1 = JacobsonSpace.restrictToClosedPoints E.1) ∧
      Function.Bijective top ∧ Function.Bijective bot ∧
      right ∘ top = bot ∘ left
declarations.comment: the full square: both vertical arrows well defined, horizontal arrows the bijections of 005Y, and f(E)₀ = f(E₀)

declarations.name: idempotent_matrices_classified_by_rank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00GG** (example of idempotent matrices).

Let `K` be a field and consider the affine scheme of `n × n` idempotent matrices,
i.e. the spectrum of `R = K[{t_{ij}}] / 𝔞` where `𝔞` is the ideal generated by the
entries of `T² - T`. Its `K`-points are exactly the matrices `M` with
`M * M = M`.

The example asserts that, by linear algebra, each idempotent matrix `M` is
conjugate (under the `GLₙ`-action `g, T ↦ g T g⁻¹`) to a diagonal matrix
`diag(1, …, 1, 0, …, 0)` with `r = rank M` ones, and that an idempotent is
*classified up to conjugation by its rank*. Consequently distinct ranks give
distinct conjugation orbits — these are precisely the irreducible components of
the scheme, and orbits of different rank are disjoint.

We record the linear-algebra heart of the example: for idempotent `M, N`,

* `M` and `N` are conjugate iff they have the same rank (classification by rank,
  which makes distinct-rank orbits disjoint), and
* `M` is conjugate to the standard idempotent `diag(1, …, 1, 0, …, 0)` carrying
  `rank M` ones (existence of the diagonal normal form).

This holds over every commutative local ring; the field in the example is a special case.

The geometric statements of the example (the orbit loci are the irreducible components of
`Spec R`, pairwise disjoint, and are separated by polynomial functions: the trace in
characteristic `0`, `tr(⋀³ T)` for `n = 3`) are in
`StacksFrontier.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.IdempotentMatrices`.

Here `IsConj M N` unfolds to `∃ g : (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)ˣ, g * M = N * g`,
i.e. `g * M * g⁻¹ = N`, which is exactly the `GLₙ`-conjugation action of the
statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem idempotent_matrices_classified_by_rank
    (M N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) (hM : M * M = M) (hN : N * N = N) :
    (IsConj M N ↔ M.rank = N.rank) ∧
      IsConj M (Matrix.diagonal (fun i : Fin n => if (i : ℕ) < M.rank then (1 : K) else 0))
declarations.comment: an idempotent matrix is conjugate to diag(1, …, 1, 0, …, 0), and idempotents are conjugate iff they have the same rank

declarations.name: Matrix.trace_eq_rank_of_isIdempotentElem
declarations.doc:
The trace of an idempotent matrix over a commutative local ring is its rank, cast to the
ring. In characteristic zero, distinct ranks therefore give distinct traces.
declarations.statement:
lemma Matrix.trace_eq_rank_of_isIdempotentElem (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
    (hM : IsIdempotentElem M) : M.trace = (M.rank : K)
declarations.comment: the trace of an idempotent matrix is its rank

declarations.name: StacksDraft.IdempotentMatrices.irreducibleComponents_eq
declarations.doc:
**The irreducible components of the scheme of idempotent matrices.** The irreducible
components of `Spec R` are exactly the `n + 1` rank loci `rankLocus k n r`, `0 ≤ r ≤ n`; each
is the image of `GLₙ` under the orbit map (`range_comap_orbitHom`), and they are open, closed and
pairwise disjoint (`isClopen_rankLocus`, `disjoint_rankLocus`).
declarations.comment: the irreducible components of Spec R are the n + 1 orbit loci of diag(1, …, 1, 0, …, 0), pairwise disjoint

declarations.name: StacksDraft.IdempotentMatrices.point_mem_rankLocus_iff
declarations.doc:
**The orbits are the `k`-points of the components.** The `k`-point of an idempotent matrix
`M` lies in the component `rankLocus k n r` exactly when `M` is in the `GLₙ(k)`-orbit
`{g D g⁻¹}` of the standard idempotent `D = diag(1, …, 1, 0, …, 0)` with `r` ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem point_mem_rankLocus_iff {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k} (hM : M * M = M) {r : ℕ}
    (hr : r ≤ n) : point k n hM ∈ rankLocus k n r ↔ IsConj M (stdIdem k n r)
declarations.comment: the k-points of the component rankLocus k n r form the GLₙ(k)-orbit of diag(1, …, 1, 0, …, 0) with r ones

declarations.name: StacksDraft.IdempotentMatrices.charpoly_separates
declarations.doc:
The coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of `T`, which are polynomials in the
`t_{ij}`, separate the components in every characteristic: on `rankLocus k n r` the polynomial
`charpoly T` takes the value `(X - 1)ʳ Xⁿ⁻ʳ`, and these values are distinct for distinct
`r ≤ n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem charpoly_separates {r s : ℕ} (hr : r ≤ n) (hs : s ≤ n) (hrs : r ≠ s) :
    (∀ p ∈ rankLocus k n r, ∀ i,
      (genericIdem k n).charpoly.coeff i - (stdCharpoly (IdemRing k n) n r).coeff i ∈ p.asIdeal) ∧
    stdCharpoly k n r ≠ stdCharpoly k n s
declarations.comment: in every characteristic the components are separated by polynomial functions, the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of T

declarations.name: StacksDraft.IdempotentMatrices.trace_separates_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
In characteristic `0` the trace `f = t₁₁ + ⋯ + tₙₙ` separates the components: it takes the
value `r` on `rankLocus k n r` and the value `s` on `rankLocus k n s`, and `r ≠ s` in `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_separates_of_charZero [CharZero k] {r s : ℕ} (hrs : r ≠ s)
    {p q : PrimeSpectrum (IdemRing k n)} (hp : p ∈ rankLocus k n r) (hq : q ∈ rankLocus k n s) :
    (genericIdem k n).trace - algebraMap k (IdemRing k n) r ∈ p.asIdeal ∧
      (genericIdem k n).trace - algebraMap k (IdemRing k n) s ∈ q.asIdeal ∧ (r : k) ≠ (s : k)
declarations.comment: in characteristic 0 the trace takes the distinct values r on the distinct components

declarations.name: StacksDraft.IdempotentMatrices.trace_exteriorPower_three_separates
declarations.doc:
For `n = 3`, the function `tr(⋀³ T)` takes the value `1` on the component of `diag(1, 1, 1)`
and `0` on the other components, in every characteristic and in particular in characteristic
`3`, where the trace `tr T` vanishes on the component of `diag(1, 1, 1)` as on that of `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_exteriorPower_three_separates {r : ℕ} (hr : r ≤ 3)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum (IdemRing k 3)) (hp : p ∈ rankLocus k 3 r) :
    LinearMap.trace (IdemRing k 3) _ (exteriorPower.map 3 (Matrix.toLin' (genericIdem k 3))) -
      (if r = 3 then 1 else 0) ∈ p.asIdeal
declarations.comment: for n = 3, tr(⋀³T) is 1 on the component of diag(1, 1, 1) and 0 on the others, in every characteristic, in particular in characteristic 3

declarations.doc:
For a domain `R`, an element `g` of the fraction field is almost integral over `R` if and
only if there is a nonzero `r ∈ R` with `r • g ^ n` in the image of `R` for all `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlmostIntegral_iff (g : FractionRing R) :
    IsAlmostIntegral R g ↔
      ∃ r : R, r ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ n, r • g ^ n ∈ (algebraMap R (FractionRing R)).range

declarations.name: RingHom.IsIntegralElemOverIdeal
declarations.doc:
An element `g ∈ S` is *integral over the ideal `I ⊂ R`* with respect to the
ring map `φ : R →+* S` if there exists a monic polynomial `P ∈ R[X]` of degree
`d` such that every coefficient `P.coeff j` lies in `I ^ (d - j)`, and `P`
evaluated at `g` via `φ` is zero in `S`.

Since `P` is monic with `d = P.natDegree`, the leading coefficient `P.coeff d`
equals `1 ∈ I ^ 0 = ⊤`, and the coefficients above the degree vanish, so the
condition `∀ j, P.coeff j ∈ I ^ (d - j)` is exactly the Stacks requirement on
the non-leading coefficients `a_j ∈ I ^ (d - j)` for `j < d`.
declarations.statement:
def IsIntegralElemOverIdeal {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [Ring S]
    (φ : R →+* S) (I : Ideal R) (g : S) : Prop

declarations.name: isIntegralElemOverIdeal_iff_isIntegralElem
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 00H3].** Let `φ : R →+* S` be a ring map and `I ⊆ R` an ideal, and let
`A = reesAlgebra I = ∑ Iⁿ Xⁿ ⊆ R[X]`, mapped to `S[X]` along the coefficientwise extension of `φ`.
An element `s : S` is integral over `I` if and only if `C s · X ∈ S[X]` is integral over `A`.

Both directions are proved: `isIntegralElem_of_isIntegralOverIdeal` (forward) and
`isIntegralElemOverIdeal_of_isIntegralElem` (converse, by taking the `X ^ d` coefficient).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralElemOverIdeal_iff_isIntegralElem (φ : R →+* S) (I : Ideal R) (s : S) :
    φ.IsIntegralElemOverIdeal I s ↔ (reesToPolyS φ I).IsIntegralElem (C s * X)

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_submodule_and_mul_isIntegralElemOverIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 00H4].** Let `S` be an `R`-algebra and `I ⊆ R` an ideal. The elements of `S`
integral over `I` form an `R`-submodule of `S`; furthermore, if `s ∈ S` is integral over `R` and
`g ∈ S` is integral over `I`, then `s * g` is integral over `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ideal.exists_submodule_and_mul_isIntegralElemOverIdeal (I : Ideal R) :
    (∃ M : Submodule R S, ∀ g, g ∈ M ↔ (algebraMap R S).IsIntegralElemOverIdeal I g) ∧
      ∀ s g : S, IsIntegral R s → (algebraMap R S).IsIntegralElemOverIdeal I g →
        (algebraMap R S).IsIntegralElemOverIdeal I (s * g)

declarations.name: Polynomial.isIntegral_coeff_and_coeff_mem_radical_of_monic_dvd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00H6.** Let `K` be a field, and let `g = xⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + a₀` divide
`f = xᵐ + bₘ₋₁xᵐ⁻¹ + ⋯ + b₀` in `K[x]`. Then
1. the `aᵢ` are integral over any subring `R₀ ⊆ K` containing the `bⱼ`, and
2. each `aᵢ` lies in `√((b₀, …, bₘ₋₁)R)` for any subring `R ⊆ K` containing the `aᵢ` and the
   `bⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_coeff_and_coeff_mem_radical_of_monic_dvd {f g : K[X]} (hf : f.Monic)
    (hg : g.Monic) (hgf : g ∣ f) :
    (∀ R₀ : Subring K, (∀ j, f.coeff j ∈ R₀) → ∀ i, IsIntegral R₀ (g.coeff i)) ∧
    (∀ R : Subring K, (∀ j, f.coeff j ∈ R) → ∀ hgR : ∀ i, g.coeff i ∈ R,
      ∀ i < g.natDegree, (⟨g.coeff i, hgR i⟩ : R) ∈
        (Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ j < f.natDegree, (x : K) = f.coeff j}).radical)
declarations.comment: (1) is Mathlib's `Polynomial.isIntegral_coeff_of_dvd`; (2) proved here

declarations.name: Module.exists_linearEquiv_directLimit_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Every `R`-module `M` is the colimit of a directed system of finitely
presented `R`-modules in the universe of `M`, provided `R` is small in that universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_linearEquiv_directLimit_finitePresentation
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    ∃ (ι : Type v) (_ : Preorder ι) (_ : IsDirectedOrder ι) (_ : Nonempty ι)
      (_ : DecidableEq ι)
      (G : ι → Type v) (_ : (i : ι) → AddCommGroup (G i))
      (_ : (i : ι) → Module R (G i))
      (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → (G i →ₗ[R] G j))
      (_ : DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => f i j h)),
      -- each module in the system is finitely presented
      (∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation R (G i)) ∧
      -- and M is isomorphic to the colimit of the system
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] Module.DirectLimit G f)

declarations.name: Module.exists_linearEquiv_directLimit_finitePresentation_max
declarations.doc:
Every module is a directed colimit of finitely presented modules in the maximum of the
universes of the ring and the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_linearEquiv_directLimit_finitePresentation_max
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    ∃ (ι : Type (max u v)) (_ : Preorder ι) (_ : IsDirectedOrder ι) (_ : Nonempty ι)
      (_ : DecidableEq ι)
      (G : ι → Type (max u v)) (_ : (i : ι) → AddCommGroup (G i))
      (_ : (i : ι) → Module R (G i))
      (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → (G i →ₗ[R] G j))
      (_ : DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => f i j h)),
      (∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation R (G i)) ∧
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] Module.DirectLimit G f)
declarations.comment: no smallness assumption on the ring

declarations.name: tensor_flat_quotient_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `0 → F'' → F' → F → 0` be a short exact sequence of modules over a commutative ring `R`:
`a : F'' → F'` is injective, the sequence is exact at `F'` and `b : F' → F` is surjective. If `F`
is flat, then for every `R`-module `G` the tensored sequence `0 → F'' ⊗ G → F' ⊗ G → F ⊗ G → 0`
is short exact: `a ⊗ 1` is injective, the sequence is exact at `F' ⊗ G`, and `b ⊗ 1` is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensor_flat_quotient_shortExact
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {F'' F' F : Type*} [AddCommGroup F''] [AddCommGroup F'] [AddCommGroup F]
    [Module R F''] [Module R F'] [Module R F]
    (a : F'' →ₗ[R] F') (b : F' →ₗ[R] F)
    (ha : Function.Injective a) (hexact : Function.Exact a b)
    (hb : Function.Surjective b)
    (hFflat : Module.Flat R F)
    (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [Module R G] :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.rTensor G a) ∧
      Function.Exact (LinearMap.rTensor G a) (LinearMap.rTensor G b) ∧
      Function.Surjective (LinearMap.rTensor G b)

declarations.name: flat_tor_zero
declarations.doc:
If `0 → M'' → M' → M → 0` is a short exact sequence of `R`-modules whose quotient
term `M` is flat, then tensoring with an arbitrary `R`-module `N` leaves the sequence
short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_tor_zero
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {M'' M' M N : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M''] [AddCommGroup M'] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module R M''] [Module R M'] [Module R M] [Module R N]
    [Module.Flat R M]
    (f : M'' →ₗ[R] M') (g : M' →ₗ[R] M)
    (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.lTensor N f) ∧
    Function.Exact (LinearMap.lTensor N f) (LinearMap.lTensor N g) ∧
    Function.Surjective (LinearMap.lTensor N g)

declarations.name: flat_of_flat_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Part 1: In a short exact sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` of `R`-modules,
if `M'` and `M''` are flat, then `M` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_flat_of_flat
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {M' M M'' : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M'] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup M'']
    [Module R M'] [Module R M] [Module R M'']
    (f : M' →ₗ[R] M) (g : M →ₗ[R] M'')
    (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    [Module.Flat R M'] [Module.Flat R M''] :
    Module.Flat R M

declarations.name: flat_of_flat_of_flat_quotient
declarations.doc:
Part 2: In a short exact sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` of `R`-modules,
if `M` and `M''` are flat, then `M'` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_flat_of_flat_quotient
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {M' M M'' : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M'] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup M'']
    [Module R M'] [Module R M] [Module R M'']
    (f : M' →ₗ[R] M) (g : M →ₗ[R] M'')
    (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hfg : Function.Exact f g)

    [Module.Flat R M] [Module.Flat R M''] :

declarations.name: faithfullyFlat_tfae00HQ
declarations.doc:
For a flat ring map `f : R →+* S`, faithful flatness is equivalent to surjectivity of
`Spec(S) → Spec(R)`, and to every closed point of `Spec(R)` lying in the image of that
map.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlat_tfae00HQ
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) (hf : RingHom.Flat f) :
    List.TFAE
      [ RingHom.FaithfullyFlat f,
        Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap f),
        ∀ x : PrimeSpectrum R, IsClosed ({x} : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) →
          x ∈ Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap f) ]

declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_forall_flat_atPrime
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      ∀ (P : Ideal R) (_ : P.IsPrime),

declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_flat_localizedModule_atMaximal
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) (_ : m.IsMaximal),
        haveI : m.IsPrime := Ideal.IsMaximal.isPrime ‹_›

declarations.comment: part4

declarations.name: flat_iff_forall_flat_localizedModule_away
declarations.doc:
Stacks 00HT (5). Let `R → A` be a ring map, `M` an `A`-module and `g₁, …, gₘ ∈ A` elements
generating the unit ideal of `A`. Then `M` is flat over `R` if and only if each localization
`M_{gᵢ}` is flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_forall_flat_localizedModule_away
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
    {m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → A) (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤) :
    Module.Flat R M ↔ ∀ i, Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.Away (g i) M)

declarations.name: flat_iff_forall_flat_localizedModule_atPrime_comap
declarations.doc:
Stacks 00HT (6). Let `R → A` be a ring map and `M` an `A`-module. Then `M` is flat over `R` if
and only if `M_𝔮` is flat over `R_𝔭`, with `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, for every prime `𝔮` of `A`. The reverse
implication is `flat_of_flat_atPrime`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_forall_flat_localizedModule_atPrime_comap
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔ ∀ (Q : Ideal A) (_ : Q.IsPrime),
        letI : (Q.comap (algebraMap R A)).IsPrime := Ideal.comap_isPrime _ _
        letI : Q.LiesOver (Q.comap (algebraMap R A)) := ⟨rfl⟩
        letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (algebraMap R A)))
                       (Localization.AtPrime Q) :=
          Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver _ _
        letI : Module (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (algebraMap R A)))
                      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime Q M) :=
          Module.compHom _ (algebraMap _ (Localization.AtPrime Q))
        Module.Flat
          (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (algebraMap R A)))
          (LocalizedModule.AtPrime Q M)

declarations.name: flat_iff_forall_flat_localizedModule_atMaximal_comap
declarations.doc:
Stacks 00HT (7). Let `R → A` be a ring map and `M` an `A`-module. Then `M` is flat over `R` if
and only if `M_𝔪` is flat over `R_𝔭`, with `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔪`, for every maximal ideal `𝔪` of `A`. The
reverse implication is `flat_of_flat_localizedModule_maximal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_forall_flat_localizedModule_atMaximal_comap
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔ ∀ (m : Ideal A) (_ : m.IsMaximal),
        letI : m.IsPrime := Ideal.IsMaximal.isPrime ‹_›
        letI : (m.comap (algebraMap R A)).IsPrime := Ideal.comap_isPrime _ _
        letI : m.LiesOver (m.comap (algebraMap R A)) := ⟨rfl⟩
        letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime (m.comap (algebraMap R A)))
                       (Localization.AtPrime m) :=
          Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver _ _
        letI : Module (Localization.AtPrime (m.comap (algebraMap R A)))
                      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime m M) :=
          Module.compHom _ (algebraMap _ (Localization.AtPrime m))
        Module.Flat
          (Localization.AtPrime (m.comap (algebraMap R A)))
          (LocalizedModule.AtPrime m M)

declarations.name: RingHom.GoingUp
declarations.doc:
A ring map `φ : R → S` satisfies **going up** if for all primes
`p ⊆ p'` of `R` and every prime `q` of `S` lying over `p` (that is,
`Ideal.comap φ q = p`), there exists a prime `q'` of `S` with `q ⊆ q'`
lying over `p'`.
declarations.statement: def RingHom.GoingUp (φ : R →+* S) : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.GoingDown
declarations.doc:
A ring map `φ : R → S` satisfies **going down** if for all primes
`p ⊆ p'` of `R` and every prime `q'` of `S` lying over `p'` (that is,
`Ideal.comap φ q' = p'`), there exists a prime `q` of `S` with `q ⊆ q'`
lying over `p`.
declarations.statement: def RingHom.GoingDown (φ : R →+* S) : Prop

declarations.name: goingDown_iff_liftsGeneralizations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00HW (1).** A ring map `φ : R → S` satisfies going down if and only if
generalizations lift along `Spec(S) → Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem goingDown_iff_liftsGeneralizations (φ : R →+* S) :
    RingHom.GoingDown φ ↔
      LiftsGeneralizations (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ)

declarations.name: goingUp_iff_liftsSpecializations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00HW (2).** A ring map `φ : R → S` satisfies going up if and only if
specializations lift along `Spec(S) → Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem goingUp_iff_liftsSpecializations (φ : R →+* S) :

declarations.name: RingHom.hasGoingDown_and_hasGoingUp_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00HX.** If the ring maps `f : R →+* S` and `g : S →+* T` satisfy going down, then so
does `g ∘ f`; likewise for going up.
declarations.comment:
Both assertions, for a composite of ring maps. For a tower of algebras they are
  `Algebra.HasGoingDown.trans` and `Algebra.HasGoingUp.trans`, which carry this tag as well.

declarations.name: goingUp_iff_isClosedMap_comap

declarations.name: not_isReduced_of_not_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00I3** (part 1). If `R ⊗[k] S` is nonreduced, then there exist finitely generated
subalgebras `R' ⊆ R`, `S' ⊆ S` such that `R' ⊗[k] S'` is not reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isReduced_of_not_isReduced (h : ¬ IsReduced (R ⊗[k] S)) :
    ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), R'.FG ∧ S'.FG ∧
      ¬ IsReduced (R' ⊗[k] S')
declarations.comment: nonreduced

declarations.name: exists_zerodivisor_of_exists_zerodivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00I3** (part 2). If `R ⊗[k] S` contains a nonzero zerodivisor, then there exist
finitely generated subalgebras `R' ⊆ R`, `S' ⊆ S` such that `R' ⊗[k] S'` contains a nonzero
zerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_zerodivisor_of_exists_zerodivisor
    (h : ∃ x : R ⊗[k] S, x ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ y : R ⊗[k] S, y ≠ 0 ∧ x * y = 0) :
    ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), R'.FG ∧ S'.FG ∧
      ∃ x : R' ⊗[k] S', x ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ y : R' ⊗[k] S', y ≠ 0 ∧ x * y = 0
declarations.comment: zerodivisor

declarations.name: exists_idempotent_of_exists_idempotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00I3** (part 3). If `R ⊗[k] S` contains a nontrivial idempotent, then there exist
finitely generated subalgebras `R' ⊆ R`, `S' ⊆ S` such that `R' ⊗[k] S'` contains a nontrivial
idempotent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idempotent_of_exists_idempotent
    (h : ∃ e : R ⊗[k] S, e * e = e ∧ e ≠ 0 ∧ e ≠ 1) :
    ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), R'.FG ∧ S'.FG ∧
      ∃ e : R' ⊗[k] S', e * e = e ∧ e ≠ 0 ∧ e ≠ 1
declarations.comment: idempotent

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.of_perfectField
declarations.doc: Over a perfect field `k`, every reduced `k`-algebra is geometrically reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.of_perfectField (k S : Type*) [Field k]
    [PerfectField k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [IsReduced S] :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k S
declarations.comment:
Clause (1): over a perfect field `k` every reduced `k`-algebra is geometrically
  reduced, stated with Mathlib's `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced` (equivalent to the source's
  Definition 030S by Lemma 030V); the source's form, reducedness of `K ⊗[k] S` for every field
  extension `K/k`, is `PerfectField.isReduced_tensorProduct_field`.

declarations.name: PerfectField.isReduced_tensorProduct
declarations.doc: Over a perfect field `k`, the tensor product of two reduced `k`-algebras is reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem PerfectField.isReduced_tensorProduct (k R S : Type*) [Field k] [PerfectField k]
    [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsReduced R] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [IsReduced S] :
    IsReduced (R ⊗[k] S)
declarations.comment:
Clause (2): over a perfect field `k` the tensor product `R ⊗[k] S` of two reduced
  `k`-algebras is reduced.

declarations.name: PerfectField.isReduced_tensorProduct_field
declarations.doc:
Over a perfect field `k`, a reduced `k`-algebra `S` is geometrically reduced in the sense of
Definition 030S: `K ⊗[k] S` is reduced for every field extension `K/k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem PerfectField.isReduced_tensorProduct_field (k S : Type*) [Field k] [PerfectField k]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [IsReduced S] (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    IsReduced (K ⊗[k] S)
declarations.comment:
Clause (1) in the source's Definition 030S of geometric reducedness: over a perfect
  field `k`, for a reduced `k`-algebra `S`, the ring `K ⊗[k] S` is reduced for every field extension
  `K/k`.

declarations.name: irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_of_isOpenMap_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00I6** (algebraic form, more general statement). Let `R → S` be a
ring map. Assume:
* `Spec R` is irreducible;
* the induced map `Spec S → Spec R` is open;
* the topological fibres of `Spec S → Spec R` are irreducible for `p` in a
  dense subset of `Spec R`.

Then `Spec S` is irreducible.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_of_isOpenMap_comap
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)]
    (hopen : IsOpenMap (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S)))
    (D : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) (hD : Dense D)
    (hfib : ∀ p ∈ D,
      IrreducibleSpace
        {q : PrimeSpectrum S // PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q = p}) :
    IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum S)
declarations.comment: general form

declarations.name: irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_of_flat_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00I6** (flat + finite-presentation form). Let `R → S` be a flat
ring map of finite presentation. If `Spec R` is irreducible and the
topological fibres of `Spec S → Spec R` are irreducible for `p` in a dense
subset of `Spec R`, then `Spec S` is irreducible.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_of_flat_finitePresentation
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)]
    [Module.Flat R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) (hD : Dense D)
    (hfib : ∀ p ∈ D,
      IrreducibleSpace
        {q : PrimeSpectrum S // PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q = p}) :
    IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum S)

declarations.name: dominates_iff
declarations.doc:
Part (1). For local subrings `A`, `B` of a field `K`, the domination order
`A ≤ B` of `LocalSubring K` holds iff `A ⊆ B` (as subrings) and, for every
`a ∈ A`, the element `a` lies in the maximal ideal of `A` exactly when its image
in `B` lies in the maximal ideal of `B`. The latter is the literal Stacks
condition `𝔪_A = A ∩ 𝔪_B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dominates_iff {A B : LocalSubring K} :
    A ≤ B ↔ ∃ h : A.toSubring ≤ B.toSubring,
      ∀ a : A.toSubring,
        a ∈ maximalIdeal A.toSubring ↔
          Subring.inclusion h a ∈ maximalIdeal B.toSubring

declarations.name: IsValuationRing
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement: def IsCenteredOn (A : ValuationSubring K) (R : Subring K) : Prop

declarations.name: ValuationRing.isDiscreteValuationRing_iff_nonempty_mulEquiv_int
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00IE (3)**: a valuation ring `A` with fraction field `K` is a discrete valuation
ring (a local principal ideal domain which is not a field) if and only if its value group
`Γ = Kˣ/Aˣ`, here `(ValuationRing.ValueGroup A K)ˣ`, is isomorphic to `ℤ`.

The isomorphism is one of groups. Stacks writes `Γ ≅ ℤ` and remarks that there is then a unique
such isomorphism with `1 ≥ 0`, so any group isomorphism is order preserving up to the sign of
`ℤ`; the proof below works with a generator of `Γ` which is `< 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_iff_nonempty_mulEquiv_int :
    IsDiscreteValuationRing A ↔ Nonempty ((ValueGroup A K)ˣ ≃* Multiplicative ℤ)
declarations.comment: (3) a valuation ring is a DVR (Mathlib's IsDiscreteValuationRing) iff its value group (ValuationRing.ValueGroup A K)ˣ = Kˣ/Aˣ is isomorphic to ℤ (as a group, written multiplicatively).

declarations.name: StacksValuation.isValuationRing_valueGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00IG** (`lemma-valuation-valuation-ring`).
Let `(Γ, ≥)` be a totally ordered abelian group, `K` a field, and `v : Kˣ → Γ` a
group homomorphism with `v(a + b) ≥ min (v a) (v b)` for `a, b, a + b` nonzero.
Then `A = {x ∈ K | x = 0 ∨ v x ≥ 0}` is a valuation ring with value group
`Im(v) ⊆ Γ`, with maximal ideal `m = {x ∈ K | x = 0 ∨ v x > 0}` and group of units
`A* = {x ∈ Kˣ | v x = 0}`.

The value group of `A` (Stacks 00ID/00IE) is `Kˣ/A*`; in the library it is the
nonzero part `(ValuationRing.ValueGroup A K)ˣ` of `K / A*`, written multiplicatively
and ordered by `[x] ≤ [y] ↔ x / y ∈ A` (the reverse of the additive order `≥` of
Stacks). The last clause gives a group isomorphism `e : Kˣ/A* ≅ Im(v)` induced by `v`
(it sends the class of `x` to `v x`), which is an isomorphism of ordered groups for
these conventions. Here `A` is `sv.valuationSubring`, whose underlying subring is
`sv.integerSubring`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isValuationRing_valueGroup :
    -- `A` is a valuation ring.
    ValuationRing sv.integerSubring ∧
    -- The group of units of `A` is `{x | v x = 0}`.
    (∀ x : sv.integerSubring, IsUnit x ↔ sv.addVal (x : K) = 0) ∧
    -- The maximal ideal of `A` is `m = {x | v x > 0}`.
    (∀ x : sv.integerSubring,
      x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal sv.integerSubring ↔ 0 < sv.addVal (x : K)) ∧
    -- `sv.valuationSubring` is `A`, as a valuation subring of `K`.
    sv.valuationSubring.toSubring = sv.integerSubring ∧
    -- The value group `Kˣ/A*` of `A` is isomorphic to `Im(v) ⊆ Γ` as an ordered group,
    -- by the isomorphism induced by `v`.
    ∃ e : sv.valuationSubring.ValueGroupˣ ≃* Multiplicative sv.valueSubgroup,
      (∀ x : Kˣ, ((Multiplicative.toAdd
          (e (Units.map (sv.valuationSubring.valuation : K →* sv.valuationSubring.ValueGroup)
            x)) : sv.valueSubgroup) : Γ) = sv.toFun x) ∧
      ∀ a b : sv.valuationSubring.ValueGroupˣ,
        a ≤ b ↔ Multiplicative.toAdd (e b) ≤ Multiplicative.toAdd (e a)
declarations.comment: The value group Kˣ/A* is (ValuationRing.ValueGroup A K)ˣ, multiplicative and ordered by [x] ≤ [y] iff x/y ∈ A; the isomorphism with Im(v) sends the class of x to v x.

declarations.name: ideals_correspond_to_valueGroupIdeals
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 00IH.**  Let `A` be a valuation ring with fraction field `K`
and value group `Γ = ValueGroup A K`.  The ideals of `A` are in
inclusion-preserving bijection with the ideals of `Γ` (`IsIdealGamma`), via
`Φ(𝔞) = v(𝔞 \ {0})`, and this bijection carries prime ideals to prime ideals
(and reflects them).
declarations.statement:
theorem ideals_correspond_to_valueGroupIdeals :
    ∃ e : Ideal A ≃ {I : Set (Gamma A K) // IsIdealGamma A K I},
      (∀ 𝔞 𝔟 : Ideal A, 𝔞 ≤ 𝔟 ↔ (e 𝔞).1 ⊆ (e 𝔟).1) ∧
        (∀ 𝔞 : Ideal A, 𝔞.IsPrime ↔ IsPrimeIdealGamma A K (e 𝔞).1)

theorem valuation_ring_noetherian_iff_dvr_or_field

    IsNoetherianRing A ↔ IsDiscreteValuationRing A ∨ IsField A

declarations.name: artin_rees
declarations.doc:
**Artin–Rees lemma.** For a Noetherian ring `R`, an ideal `I ⊆ R` and a submodule `N` of a
finite `R`-module `M`, there is a constant `c > 0` with `I^n M ⊓ N = I^(n-c) • (I^c M ⊓ N)` for
every `n ≥ c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem artin_rees
    {R : Type*} {M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (N : Submodule R M) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ c,
      (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⊓ N
        = I ^ (n - c) • ((I ^ c • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⊓ N)

declarations.name: exists_comap_smul_eq_and_range_inf_le
declarations.doc:
**Map version of Artin–Rees.** For an exact sequence `0 → K → M → N` of
finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring `R` and an ideal `I`, there is
a constant `c` such that for all `n ≥ c`,
`f⁻¹(IⁿN) = K + Iⁿ⁻ᶜ · f⁻¹(IᶜN)` and `f(M) ∩ IⁿN ⊆ f(Iⁿ⁻ᶜ M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_comap_smul_eq_and_range_inf_le
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (I : Ideal R) :
    ∃ c, ∀ n ≥ c,
      Submodule.comap f (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R N)) =
        LinearMap.ker f +
          I ^ (n - c) • Submodule.comap f (I ^ c • (⊤ : Submodule R N)) ∧
      LinearMap.range f ⊓ (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R N)) ≤
        Submodule.map f (I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule R M))

declarations.name: exists_notMem_localized_krullIntersection_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
For every prime ideal `p` containing `I`, there exists `f ∈ R` with
`f ∉ p` such that the localization of `N = ⋂_n I^n M` at the submonoid
generated by `f` is the zero submodule.

theorem exists_notMem_localized_krullIntersection_eq_bot
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (hIp : I ≤ p) :
    ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧
      (krullIntersection M I).localized (Submonoid.powers f) = ⊥

declarations.name: Algebra.FiniteType.pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00IT.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `f : A →ₐ[R] B`
and `g : C →ₐ[R] B` be `R`-algebra maps. If `A` and `C` are of finite type over
`R`, `f` is surjective, and `g` is a finite morphism (that is, `B` is finitely
generated as a `C`-module), then the fibre product `A ×_B C` is of finite type
over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FiniteType.pullback [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R C] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : C →ₐ[R] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (hBC : g.Finite) : Algebra.FiniteType R (f.pullback g)

declarations.name: Module.length_le_length_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
For a ring map `φ : R → S` and an `S`-module `M`, viewed as an `R`-module by restriction of
scalars along `φ`, the length over `R` is at least the length over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.length_le_length_restrictScalars
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] :
    letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M φ
    Module.length S M ≤ Module.length R M

declarations.name: length_restrictScalars_eq_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
For a surjective ring map `φ : R → S` and an `S`-module `M`, viewed as an `R`-module by
restriction of scalars along `φ`, the length over `R` equals the length over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_restrictScalars_eq_of_surjective
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] :
    letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M φ
    Module.length R M = Module.length S M

declarations.name: length_eq_rank_of_maximal_smul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Length of `M` as an `R`-module equals the dimension of `M` as an
`R ⧸ m`-vector space, when `m M = 0` for a maximal ideal `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_eq_rank_of_maximal_smul_eq_zero
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : ∀ r ∈ m, ∀ x : M, r • x = 0) :
    letI hTors : Module.IsTorsionBySet R M (m : Set R) :=
      fun x a => hM a.1 a.2 x
    letI : Module (R ⧸ m) M := hTors.module
    Module.length R M = Cardinal.toENat (Module.rank (R ⧸ m) M)

declarations.name: length_lt_top_iff_finite_of_smul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The length of `M` is finite if and only if `M` is a finite `R`-module,
when `m M = 0` for a maximal ideal `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_lt_top_iff_finite_of_smul_eq_zero
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : ∀ r ∈ m, ∀ x : M, r • x = 0) :
    Module.length R M < ⊤ ↔ Module.Finite R M

declarations.name: Module.length_localizedModule_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00IZ.** Let `R` be a ring, `M` an `R`-module, and `S ⊆ R` a multiplicative
subset. Then `length_R(M) ≥ length_{S⁻¹R}(S⁻¹M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.length_localizedModule_le :
    Module.length (Localization S) (LocalizedModule S M) ≤ Module.length R M

declarations.name: length_lt_top_of_pow_smul_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00J0.** Let `R` be a commutative ring with finitely generated maximal ideal `m`.
If `M` is a finite `R`-module with `m ^ n • M = 0` for some `n`, then `length_R M < ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_lt_top_of_pow_smul_eq_bot
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal] (hm : m.FG)
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : m ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊥) :
    Module.length R M < ⊤
