declarations.name: length_eq_and_subQuot_isSimpleModule_and_exists_quot_maximal_and_ncard_eq_length
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00J3**. Let `M` be an `R`-module and `0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M` a maximal
chain of submodules with `M_i ≠ M_{i-1}`. Then

1. `n = length_R(M)`;
2. each successive quotient `M_{i+1}/M_i` is simple;
3. each successive quotient is isomorphic to `R/𝔪_i` for some maximal ideal `𝔪_i`;
4. for any choice of such maximal ideals `𝔪_i` (part (3)) and every maximal ideal `𝔪` of `R`,
   `#{i | 𝔪_i = 𝔪} = length_{R_𝔪}(M_𝔪)`.

The source assumes `M` has finite length; this is not needed as a hypothesis, since a finite
maximal chain forces it (and part (1) records it). The length in part (1) is `Module.length`
in `ℕ∞`, and `M_𝔪`, `R_𝔪` are `LocalizedModule 𝔪.primeCompl M` and
`Localization.AtPrime 𝔪`. In part (4) the ideal `𝔪_i` is in fact determined by `M_{i+1}/M_i`
(it is its annihilator), so the count does not depend on the choice.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_eq_and_subQuot_isSimpleModule_and_exists_quot_maximal_and_ncard_eq_length
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {n : ℕ} (M' : Fin (n + 1) → Submodule R M) (hchain : IsMaximalChainPrime M') :
    (n : ℕ∞) = Module.length R M ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, IsSimpleModule R (subQuot M' i)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, ∃ (𝔪 : Ideal R) (_ : 𝔪.IsMaximal),
        Nonempty (subQuot M' i ≃ₗ[R] R ⧸ 𝔪)) ∧
      ∀ 𝔪s : Fin n → Ideal R,
        (∀ i : Fin n, (𝔪s i).IsMaximal ∧ Nonempty (subQuot M' i ≃ₗ[R] R ⧸ 𝔪s i)) →
        ∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) [𝔪.IsMaximal],
          ({i | 𝔪s i = 𝔪}.ncard : ℕ∞) =
            Module.length (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪) (LocalizedModule 𝔪.primeCompl M)

registrations.name: monotone_stabilizes_iff_artinian
registrations.comment: the descending chain condition, as stabilization of monotone chains

declarations.name: finite_dimensional_algebra_is_artinian
declarations.doc: A finite-dimensional algebra over a field is an Artinian ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_dimensional_algebra_is_artinian
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (R : Type*) [Ring R] [Algebra K R]
    [FiniteDimensional K R] : IsArtinianRing R

declarations.name: MaximalSpectrum.algebraMap_pi_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00JA and 00JB** (the product decomposition).
A commutative semiring with discrete prime spectrum — in particular an Artinian ring — is the
product of its localizations at its (finitely many) maximal ideals: for any family `Rₘ` of
localizations of `R` at the maximal ideals of `R`, the canonical map `R → ∀ 𝔪, Rₘ 𝔪` is
bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem algebraMap_pi_bijective (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R]
    [DiscreteTopology (PrimeSpectrum R)]
    (Rₘ : MaximalSpectrum R → Type*) [∀ m, CommSemiring (Rₘ m)] [∀ m, Algebra R (Rₘ m)]
    [∀ m, IsLocalization.AtPrime (Rₘ m) m.asIdeal] :
    Function.Bijective (algebraMap R (∀ m, Rₘ m))
declarations.comment: The product decomposition, for an arbitrary family of localizations. Discreteness of `Spec R` is the tag's own hypothesis, by `PrimeSpectrum.discreteTopology_iff_finite_isMaximal_and_sInf_le_nilradical`.

declarations.name: nonempty_ringEquiv_pi_localization_and_isMaximal
declarations.doc:
A ring with finitely many maximal ideals whose Jacobson radical is contained in the
nilradical is isomorphic to the product of its localizations at its maximal ideals, and
every prime ideal of it is maximal.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_ringEquiv_pi_localization_and_isMaximal (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [Finite
  (MaximalSpectrum R)]
    (h : Ring.jacobson R ≤ nilradical R) :
    Nonempty (R ≃+* (Π m : MaximalSpectrum R, Localization.AtPrime m.asIdeal)) ∧
    (∀ p : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → p.IsMaximal)

declarations.name: MaximalSpectrum.algebraMap_pi_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00JA and 00JB** (the product decomposition).
A commutative semiring with discrete prime spectrum — in particular an Artinian ring — is the
product of its localizations at its (finitely many) maximal ideals: for any family `Rₘ` of
localizations of `R` at the maximal ideals of `R`, the canonical map `R → ∀ 𝔪, Rₘ 𝔪` is
bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem algebraMap_pi_bijective (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R]
    [DiscreteTopology (PrimeSpectrum R)]
    (Rₘ : MaximalSpectrum R → Type*) [∀ m, CommSemiring (Rₘ m)] [∀ m, Algebra R (Rₘ m)]
    [∀ m, IsLocalization.AtPrime (Rₘ m) m.asIdeal] :
    Function.Bijective (algebraMap R (∀ m, Rₘ m))
declarations.comment: The final assertion, under discreteness of `Spec R` in place of Artinian-ness

declarations.name: isArtinianRing_iff_isFiniteLength_and_isNoetherianRing_and_toPiLocalization_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Artinian rings have finite length, and decompose.** A commutative ring `R` is Artinian if
and only if it has finite length as a module over itself; and any Artinian ring `R` is also
Noetherian, has all of its prime ideals maximal, has only finitely many maximal ideals, and is
the product of its localizations at them, in the sense that the canonical `R`-algebra map
`R → ∀ 𝔪 : MaximalSpectrum R, Localization.AtPrime 𝔪` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    isArtinianRing_iff_isFiniteLength_and_isNoetherianRing_and_toPiLocalization_bijective
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    (IsArtinianRing R ↔ IsFiniteLength R R) ∧
      (IsArtinianRing R → IsNoetherianRing R ∧ (∀ p : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → p.IsMaximal) ∧
        Finite (MaximalSpectrum R) ∧
        Function.Bijective (MaximalSpectrum.toPiLocalization R))
declarations.comment: All four assertions: the finite-length criterion, Noetherianness, maximality of the primes, and the product decomposition, the last as bijectivity of the canonical map.

declarations.name: length_K0prime_hom_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00JD.** If `R` is an Artinian local ring then the length
function defines an abelian group homomorphism `K'_0(R) →+ ℤ` sending the
class of each presentation `P` to its integer length.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_K0prime_hom_exists (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsArtinianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] :
    ∃ φ : K0prime R →+ ℤ,
      ∀ P : FGPres R, φ (K0prime.mk P) = lengthOfPresℤ R P

declarations.name: K0toK0'_field_bijective_and_isoZ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Example 00JE.** Let `k` be a field. Then `K₀(k) = K'₀(k) ≅ ℤ`, the
isomorphism being given by the dimension function, which is also the length function.
Precisely:
* the canonical map `K0toK0' k : K₀(k) → K'₀(k)` is bijective;
* there is an isomorphism `K'₀(k) ≃+ ℤ` sending the class `[M]` of every finite
  `k`-module `M` to `dim_k M`;
* there is an isomorphism `K₀(k) ≃+ ℤ` sending the class `[M]` of every finite
  (projective) `k`-module `M` to `dim_k M`;
* for every finite `k`-module `M`, `length_k M = dim_k M`.

Here `K'₀(k) = K0PrimeOfFinPres k` and `K₀(k) = K0OfProjGen k` are the Grothendieck
groups of finite, resp. finite projective, `k`-modules modulo short exact sequences,
built as in Stacks Section 00JC.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0toK0'_field_bijective_and_isoZ (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Function.Bijective (K0toK0' k) ∧
    (∃ e : K0PrimeOfFinPres k ≃+ ℤ, ∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M]
        [Module.Finite k M], e (K0PrimeOfFinPres.mkM k M) = Module.finrank k M) ∧
    (∃ e : K0OfProjGen k ≃+ ℤ, ∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M]
        [Module.Finite k M], e (K0OfProjGen.mkM k M) = Module.finrank k M) ∧
    ∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] [Module.Finite k M],
      Module.length k M = Module.finrank k M
declarations.comment: K0(k) → K'0(k) bijective, K'0(k) ≅ ℤ and K0(k) ≅ ℤ via dimension, dimension equals length

declarations.name: K0_polynomial_isoZ
declarations.doc:
`K0(k[x]) ≅ ℤ`, exhibited by an explicit isomorphism that sends
the class `[k[x]]` of the rank-1 free module to `1`.  (The rank map.)
declarations.statement:
theorem K0_polynomial_isoZ (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ∃ e : K0OfProjGen (Polynomial k) ≃+ ℤ,
      e (K0OfProjGen.mk (Polynomial k) (K0Gen.free1 (Polynomial k))) = 1
declarations.comment: K0(k[x]) ≅ ℤ

declarations.name: K0'_polynomial_isoZ
declarations.doc:
`K0'(k[x]) ≅ ℤ`, exhibited by an explicit isomorphism that sends
the class `[k[x]]` to `1` (the rank of the free part).  Every torsion finite
module has class `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0'_polynomial_isoZ (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ∃ e : K0PrimeOfFinPres (Polynomial k) ≃+ ℤ,
      e (K0PrimeOfFinPres.mk (Polynomial k) (K0'Gen.free1 (Polynomial k))) = 1

declarations.name: K0toK0'_polynomial_bijective
declarations.doc:
The canonical homomorphism `ι : K0(k[x]) → K0'(k[x])` is an
isomorphism (it is bijective).

Argument: `rankHom ∘ K0toK0' = rankHomK0` (definitionally, `rankHomK0`), and
both `rankHom` (D6) and `rankHomK0` (D9) are bijective.  Therefore
`K0toK0' = rankHom.symm ∘ rankHomK0` (as maps), a composite of bijections,
hence bijective.  Formally: `K0toK0'` is injective because
`rankHom ∘ K0toK0' = rankHomK0` is injective; it is surjective because
`rankHom` is bijective and `rankHomK0 = rankHom ∘ K0toK0'` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0toK0'_polynomial_bijective (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    Function.Bijective (K0toK0' (Polynomial k))

declarations.name: nodeRing_K0_addEquiv_and_K0prime_addEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Example 10.55.5 (tag `00JG`).** Let `k` be a field and
`R = {f ∈ k[x] ∣ f(0) = f(1)}`. Then `K₀(R) ≅ k^* ⊕ ℤ`, but `K'₀(R) ≅ ℤ`.

Here `K₀(R)` (`K0OfProjGen`) and `K'₀(R)` (`K0PrimeOfFinPres`) are the Grothendieck groups of
finite projective, respectively finite, `R`-modules, with relations from short exact sequences,
and `k^*` is written additively. The isomorphisms are `NodeRing.exists_K0_addEquiv` (sending
`[R]` to `(1, 1)` and the line bundle `L_u = {f ∣ f(1) = u f(0)}` to `(u, 1)`) and
`NodeRing.exists_K0prime_addEquiv_int` (the rank, sending `[R]` to `1`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nodeRing_K0_addEquiv_and_K0prime_addEquiv (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    Nonempty (K0OfProjGen (nodeRing k) ≃+ Additive kˣ × ℤ) ∧
      Nonempty (K0PrimeOfFinPres (nodeRing k) ≃+ ℤ)
declarations.comment: `K₀(R) ≅ k^* ⊕ ℤ` and `K'₀(R) ≅ ℤ` for `R = {f ∈ k[x] ∣ f(0) = f(1)}`

declarations.name: K0_product
declarations.doc:
For a product ring `R = R₁ × R₂`, the natural
homomorphism `K₀(R) → K₀(R₁) × K₀(R₂)`, given on generators by
`[M] ↦ ([M ⊗_R R₁], [M ⊗_R R₂])` (base change along the two projections), is an
isomorphism of abelian groups.

The product map is characterized by its values on the generating classes
`K0.mk M`; since these generate `K0 (R₁ × R₂)`, the additive isomorphism `e`
below is unique with the stated property, so this faithfully expresses that the
product map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0_product (R1 R2 : Type u) [CommRing R1] [CommRing R2] :
    ∃ e : K0 (R1 × R2) ≃+ (K0 R1 × K0 R2),
      ∀ M : FGProj (R1 × R2),
        e (K0.mk M) =
          ( K0.mk (M.baseChangeHom (RingHom.fst R1 R2)),
            K0.mk (M.baseChangeHom (RingHom.snd R1 R2)) )

declarations.name: K0prime_prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00JH, `K'_0` half.** Let `R = R₁ × R₂` be a product of two commutative
rings (no further hypothesis). Then the natural homomorphism
`K'₀(R) → K'₀(R₁) × K'₀(R₂)`, given on generators by
`[M] ↦ ([M ⊗_R R₁], [M ⊗_R R₂])`, is an isomorphism of abelian groups.

As for the `K_0` half (`K0_product`), the classes `K0prime.mk M` generate
`K0prime (R₁ × R₂)`, so the additive isomorphism `e` is uniquely determined by the
stated property.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0prime_prod (R1 R2 : Type u) [CommRing R1] [CommRing R2] :
    ∃ e : K0prime (R1 × R2) ≃+ (K0prime R1 × K0prime R2),
      ∀ M : FGPres (R1 × R2),
        e (K0prime.mk M) =
          ( K0prime.baseChangeMk (RingHom.fst R1 R2) M.module,
            K0prime.baseChangeMk (RingHom.snd R1 R2) M.module )
declarations.comment: K'_0 half, for arbitrary commutative rings R_1, R_2; the K_0 half is K0_product

declarations.name: K0prime.lengthHom_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00JI.** Let `R` be an Artinian local ring. The length homomorphism
`length_R : K'_0(R) → ℤ` of Stacks 00JD (`lengthHom R`, sending the class of a finite module
to its length) is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem lengthHom_isIso : ∃ e : K0prime R ≃+ ℤ, ⇑e = lengthHom R

declarations.name: finite_projective_is_finite_free
declarations.doc:
Over a local ring, every finitely generated projective module is free, and
admits a linear equivalence to `Fin n → R` for some `n`. This is the first half
of Stacks 00JJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_projective_is_finite_free
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M] :
    Module.Free R M ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] (Fin n → R))
declarations.comment: every finite projective module over a local ring is finite free

declarations.name: K0.rank_isIso
declarations.doc:
Over a local ring, the rank map `K_0(R) → ℤ` is an isomorphism. Combined
with `finite_projective_is_finite_free`, this gives the full statement of
Stacks 00JJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem K0.rank_isIso
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] :
    ∃ e : K0 R ≃+ ℤ, ⇑e = K0.rank R
declarations.comment: the rank map `[M] ↦ rank_R(M)` is a well-defined isomorphism `K_0(R) ≃+ ℤ`

declarations.name: K0.toK0prime_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00JK.** Let `R` be a local Artinian ring. The diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
K_0(R) & \to & K_0'(R) \\
\text{rank}_R \downarrow & & \downarrow \text{length}_R \\
\mathbf{Z} & \xrightarrow{\text{length}_R(R)} & \mathbf{Z}
\end{array}
$$
commutes, and its vertical maps are isomorphisms: `K0.rank R` and `lengthHom R` are bijective,
and `length_R ∘ (K_0(R) → K'_0(R)) = length_R(R) · rank_R`.

Here `K_0(R)` (`K0 R`) is presented by direct-sum relations; since short exact sequences of
projective modules split, these are the relations of the Stacks definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem toK0prime_comm [IsLocalRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] :
    Function.Bijective (K0.rank R) ∧ Function.Bijective (lengthHom R) ∧
      (lengthHom R).comp (toK0prime R) =
        (AddMonoidHom.mulLeft ((Module.length R R).toNat : ℤ)).comp (K0.rank R)

declarations.name: Proj
declarations.doc:
The homogeneous spectrum `Proj 𝒜` of a graded ring: the set of homogeneous prime
ideals `𝔭` of `A` with `𝒜₊ ⊄ 𝔭`, topologized by the subspace topology from `Spec A`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Proj : Type _

declarations.name: gradedPrimesComparison_isHomeomorph
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a `ℤ`-graded ring containing a homogeneous invertible
element of positive degree. Then the comparison map `Φ : G → Spec(S₀)`,
`q ↦ q ∩ S₀`, from the space of `ℤ`-graded primes of `S` (with the subspace topology) to
`Spec(S₀)`, is a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem gradedPrimesComparison_isHomeomorph
    (hf : HasHomogeneousUnitOfPosDegree 𝒜) :
    IsHomeomorph (gradedPrimesComparison 𝒜)

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.exists_homeomorph_awayGradedPrimes
declarations.doc:
For `f` homogeneous of positive degree, the ring maps `A → A_f ← A₍f₎` induce homeomorphisms
`D₊(f) ← {ℤ-graded primes of A_f} → Spec A₍f₎`, each sending a prime to its pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homeomorph_awayGradedPrimes {f : A} {m : ℕ} (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m) (hm : 0 < m) :
    ∃ (e₁ : awayGradedPrimes 𝒜 f m ≃ₜ basicOpen 𝒜 f)
      (e₂ : awayGradedPrimes 𝒜 f m ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum (HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)),
      (∀ q, (e₁ q).1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal = q.1.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A (Away f))) ∧
      ∀ q, (e₂ q).asIdeal =
        q.1.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap (HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f) (Away f))
declarations.comment: Assertion (6): for `f` homogeneous of positive degree, `S → S_f ← S_(f)` induce homeomorphisms `D₊(f) ← {ℤ-graded primes of S_f} → Spec(S_(f))`; the second is the first composed with Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.projIsoSpecTopComponent`.

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.exists_not_compactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00JP (7).** There is a graded ring `S` whose homogeneous spectrum `Proj S` is not
quasi-compact, namely `ℤ[X₀, X₁, …]` graded by total degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_compactSpace :
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : CommRing S) (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule ℤ S) (_ : GradedRing 𝒜),
      ¬ CompactSpace (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜)
declarations.comment: Assertion (7): there is a graded ring `S` with `Proj(S)` not quasi-compact, namely `S = ℤ[X₁, X₂, …]` (`not_compactSpace_mvPolynomial`).

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.isOpen_basicOpen_of_mem
declarations.doc: A standard open `D₊(f)`, for `f` homogeneous of positive degree, is open in `Proj 𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_basicOpen_of_mem {f : A} {d : ℕ} (_hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (_hd : 0 < d) :
    IsOpen (basicOpen 𝒜 f : Set (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜))
declarations.comment: Assertion (1): the sets `D₊(f)`, `f` homogeneous of positive degree, are open (Mathlib's `ProjectiveSpectrum.isOpen_basicOpen`).

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen_mul_of_mem
declarations.doc: For `f`, `f'` homogeneous of positive degree, `D₊(ff') = D₊(f) ∩ D₊(f')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_mul_of_mem {f f' : A} {d d' : ℕ} (_hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (_hd : 0 < d)
    (_hf' : f' ∈ 𝒜 d') (_hd' : 0 < d') :
    basicOpen 𝒜 (f * f') = basicOpen 𝒜 f ⊓ basicOpen 𝒜 f'
declarations.comment: Assertion (2): `D₊(ff') = D₊(f) ∩ D₊(f')` (Mathlib's `ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen_mul`).

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen_eq_basicOpen_proj_zero_sup_iSup
declarations.doc:
For `g ∈ A` with homogeneous components `gᵢ = proj i g`, the set `D(g) ∩ Proj 𝒜` of relevant
homogeneous primes not containing `g` is `(D(g₀) ∩ Proj 𝒜) ∪ ⋃_{i ≥ 1} D₊(gᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_eq_basicOpen_proj_zero_sup_iSup (g : A) :
    basicOpen 𝒜 g = basicOpen 𝒜 (GradedRing.proj 𝒜 0 g) ⊔
      ⨆ (i : ℕ) (_ : 0 < i), basicOpen 𝒜 (GradedRing.proj 𝒜 i g)
declarations.comment: Assertion (3): `D(g) ∩ Proj(S) = (D(g₀) ∩ Proj(S)) ∪ ⋃_{i ≥ 1} D₊(gᵢ)` for `g = ∑ gᵢ` with `gᵢ ∈ Sᵢ`; derived from Mathlib's `ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen_eq_union_of_projection`.

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen_eq_iSup_basicOpen_mul_of_mem_zero
declarations.doc: For `g₀` homogeneous of degree `0`, `D(g₀) ∩ Proj 𝒜 = ⋃_{f ∈ 𝒜 d, d ≥ 1} D₊(g₀ f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_eq_iSup_basicOpen_mul_of_mem_zero {g₀ : A} (_hg₀ : g₀ ∈ 𝒜 0) :
    basicOpen 𝒜 g₀ = ⨆ (d : ℕ) (_ : 0 < d) (f : A) (_ : f ∈ 𝒜 d), basicOpen 𝒜 (g₀ * f)
declarations.comment: Assertion (4): `D(g₀) ∩ Proj(S) = ⋃_{f ∈ S_d, d ≥ 1} D₊(g₀ f)` for `g₀ ∈ S₀`.

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basicOpen_of_pos
declarations.doc:
The standard opens `D₊(f)`, for `f` homogeneous of positive degree, form a basis of the
topology of `Proj 𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTopologicalBasis_basicOpen_of_pos :
    TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis
      {U : Set (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜) |
        ∃ (d : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < d ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 d ∧ U = basicOpen 𝒜 f}
declarations.comment: Assertion (5): the opens `D₊(f)`, `f` homogeneous of positive degree, form a basis of the topology of `Proj(S)`.

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus_homogeneousIdeal
declarations.doc: For a homogeneous ideal `I`, the set `V₊(I)` is closed in `Proj 𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_zeroLocus_homogeneousIdeal (I : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜) :
    IsClosed (zeroLocus 𝒜 (I : Set A))
declarations.comment: Assertion (8): the sets `V₊(I)`, `I` homogeneous, are closed (Mathlib's `ProjectiveSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus`).

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.exists_homogeneousIdeal_eq_zeroLocus_of_isClosed
declarations.doc: Every closed subset of `Proj 𝒜` is `V₊(I)` for some homogeneous ideal `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homogeneousIdeal_eq_zeroLocus_of_isClosed {T : Set (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜)}
    (hT : IsClosed T) : ∃ I : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜, T = zeroLocus 𝒜 (I : Set A)
declarations.comment: Assertion (9): every closed `T ⊆ Proj(S)` is `V₊(I)` for a homogeneous ideal `I`, namely `I = ProjectiveSpectrum.vanishingIdeal T` (Mathlib's `ProjectiveSpectrum.zeroLocus_vanishingIdeal_eq_closure`).

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.zeroLocus_empty_iff_irrelevant_le_radical
declarations.doc:
The projective zero locus `V₊(I)` of a homogeneous ideal `I` of a graded ring `A` is empty if
and only if the irrelevant ideal `𝒜₊` is contained in the radical of `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroLocus_empty_iff_irrelevant_le_radical (I : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜) :
    zeroLocus 𝒜 (I : Set A) = ∅ ↔ HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜 ≤ I.radical
declarations.comment: Assertion (10): for a homogeneous ideal `I`, `V₊(I) = ∅` if and only if `S₊ ⊆ √I`.

declarations.name: projToSpec_isHomeomorph
declarations.doc: The natural map `Proj(R[X]) → Spec(R)` is a bijection and a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem projToSpec_isHomeomorph : IsHomeomorph (projToSpec R)

declarations.name: HomogeneousLocalization.isLocalizedModule_atPrime
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a graded ring, let `M` be a graded `A`-module, let `𝔭` be a homogeneous prime ideal
of `A`, and let `f ∈ A` be homogeneous of positive degree with `f ∉ 𝔭`. Let `𝔭'` be the prime of the
degree-zero localization `A⁰_f` consisting of the fractions `a/fⁿ` with `a ∈ 𝔭`. Then the
`A⁰_f`-module `M_(𝔭)` of degree-zero fractions `y/g` with `g ∉ 𝔭` homogeneous is the localization of
the `A⁰_f`-module `M_(f)` of degree-zero fractions `y/fⁿ` at `𝔭'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalizedModule_atPrime {σ τ A M : Type*} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A]
    [AddSubgroupClass σ A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [SetLike τ M] [AddSubmonoidClass τ M]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (ℳ : ℤ → τ) [DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ]
    (hℳ : ∀ (i : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (a : A) (y : M), a ∈ 𝒜 i → y ∈ ℳ j → a • y ∈ ℳ (i + j)) (𝔭 : Ideal A)
    [𝔭.IsPrime] (h𝔭 : 𝔭.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) {f : A} {m : ℕ} (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 m) (hm : 0 < m) (hf𝔭 : f ∉ 𝔭)
    (𝔭' : Ideal (Away 𝒜 f)) [𝔭'.IsPrime]
    (h𝔭' : ∀ z : NumDenSameDeg 𝒜 (Submonoid.powers f), mk z ∈ 𝔭' ↔ (z.num : A) ∈ 𝔭) :
    letI : Module (Away 𝒜 f) (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap (Away 𝒜 f) (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)))
    letI : Module (Away 𝒜 f) (LocalizedModule 𝔭.primeCompl M) :=
      Module.compHom _
        ((algebraMap (AtPrime 𝒜 𝔭) (Localization 𝔭.primeCompl)).comp
          (mapId 𝒜 (Submonoid.powers_le.mpr hf𝔭)))
    ∃ φ :
      ↥(Submodule.span (Away 𝒜 f)
            {z : LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M |
              ∃ (i : ℕ) (y : M) (g : Submonoid.powers f),
                y ∈ ℳ (i : ℤ) ∧ (g : A) ∈ 𝒜 i ∧ z = .mk y g}) →ₗ[Away 𝒜 f]
        ↥(Submodule.span (Away 𝒜 f)
            {z : LocalizedModule 𝔭.primeCompl M |
              ∃ (i : ℕ) (y : M) (g : 𝔭.primeCompl), y ∈ ℳ (i : ℤ) ∧ (g : A) ∈ 𝒜 i ∧ z = .mk y g}),
      (∀ z,
          (φ z : LocalizedModule 𝔭.primeCompl M) =
            LocalizedModule.liftOfLE _ _ (Submonoid.powers_le.mpr hf𝔭) (z : _)) ∧
        IsLocalizedModule 𝔭'.primeCompl φ
declarations.comment:
The module equality `M_(𝔭) = (M_(f))_{𝔭'}`; the ring equality
`S_(𝔭) = (S_(f))_{𝔭'}` is `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.isLocalization_atPrime`.

declarations.name: graded_silly
declarations.doc:
Graded prime avoidance: if `p₁, …, p_r` are homogeneous prime ideals of a graded ring and
`I` is a homogeneous ideal contained in the irrelevant ideal with `¬ I ≤ pᵢ` for every `i`,
then `I` contains a homogeneous element of positive degree lying outside every `pᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem graded_silly
    {r : ℕ} (p : Fin r → HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜) (hp : ∀ i, (p i).toIdeal.IsPrime)
    (I : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜) (hI : I ≤ HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜)
    (hIp : ∀ i, ¬ I ≤ p i) :
    ∃ x : S, x ∈ I.toIdeal ∧ (∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ x ∈ 𝒜 d) ∧ ∀ i, x ∉ (p i).toIdeal

registrations.name: Ideal.homogeneousCore
registrations.comment: the homogeneous ideal generated by the homogeneous elements of `𝔭`

declarations.name: Ideal.IsHomogeneous.isHomogeneous_of_mem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
Part (2): Given a homogeneous ideal `I`, any minimal prime over `I` is
homogeneous.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ideal.IsHomogeneous.isHomogeneous_of_mem_minimalPrimes
    {I p : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hp : p ∈ I.minimalPrimes) :
    p.IsHomogeneous 𝒜
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: GradedRing.isHomogeneous_of_mem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
Part (1): Any minimal prime of a graded ring is a homogeneous ideal. This
is the special case of part (2) where `I = ⊥`.
declarations.statement:
theorem GradedRing.isHomogeneous_of_mem_minimalPrimes
    {p : Ideal A} (hp : p ∈ minimalPrimes A) :
    p.IsHomogeneous 𝒜
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: GradedRing.isNoetherianRing_iff_isNoetherianRing_gradeZero_and_irrelevant_fg
declarations.doc:
A graded ring `A = ⨁_d 𝒜 d` is Noetherian if and only if its degree-zero subring `𝒜 0`
is a Noetherian ring and its irrelevant ideal `⨁_{d > 0} 𝒜 d` is finitely generated as an
ideal of `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNoetherianRing_iff_isNoetherianRing_gradeZero_and_irrelevant_fg
    (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] :
    IsNoetherianRing A ↔
      IsNoetherianRing (𝒜 0) ∧ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal.FG

declarations.name: IsNumericalPolynomial
declarations.doc:
A function `f : ℤ → A` (with `A` an additive abelian group) is a
*numerical polynomial* if there exist `r : ℕ` and elements
`a : Fin (r + 1) → A` such that
`f n = ∑_{i = 0}^{r} (n choose i) • a i` holds for all sufficiently large
integers `n`.
declarations.statement: def IsNumericalPolynomial (f : ℤ → A) : Prop

declarations.name: numerical_polynomial_functorial
declarations.doc:
Numerical polynomials are functorial: if `φ : A →+ A'` is a homomorphism of abelian groups
and `f : ℤ → A` is a numerical polynomial, then `n ↦ φ (f n)` is a numerical polynomial valued in
`A'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem numerical_polynomial_functorial
    {A A' : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [AddCommGroup A']
    (φ : A →+ A') (f : ℤ → A) (hf : IsNumericalPolynomial f) :
    IsNumericalPolynomial (fun n => φ (f n))

declarations.name: main_00JZ
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian group and `f : ℤ → A`. If the backward difference
`n ↦ f n - f (n - 1)` is a numerical polynomial, then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_00JZ {A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] (f : ℤ → A)
    (hdiff : IsNumericalPolynomial (fun n => f n - f (n - 1))) :
    IsNumericalPolynomial f

declarations.name: graded_module_pieces_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00K0**.
Let `S = ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝒜 n` be a graded ring and `M = ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℳ n` a graded `S`-module, with
`S_d · M_e ⊆ M_{d+e}`. If `M` is finitely generated as an `S`-module and `S` is finitely
generated as an `𝒜 0`-algebra, then every graded piece `ℳ n` is a finite `𝒜 0`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem graded_module_pieces_finite (ℳ : ℤ → Submodule (𝒜 0) M) [DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ]
    (hsmul : ∀ (d : ℕ) (e : ℤ) (s : S), s ∈ 𝒜 d → ∀ m : M, m ∈ ℳ e → s • m ∈ ℳ ((d : ℤ) + e))
    (hM : Module.Finite S M)
    (hS : Algebra.FiniteType (𝒜 0) S) : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite (𝒜 0) (ℳ n)

declarations.name: hilbertFun_isNumericalPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Main statement (Stacks Tag 00K1, Proposition 10.58.7).**
Let `S` be a Noetherian graded ring with degree-zero ring `S_0 = ↥(𝒮 0)`, graded
nonnegatively (`𝒮 d = 0` for `d < 0`), and let `M` be a finite graded `S`-module.
Assume the irrelevant ideal `S_+` is generated by elements of degree `1`
(`GeneratedInDegreeOne 𝒮`).  Then the Hilbert function
`n ↦ [M_n] ∈ K'_0(S_0)` is a numerical polynomial.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertFun_isNumericalPolynomial (hneg : ∀ d : ℤ, d < 0 → 𝒮 d = ⊥)
    (hgen : GeneratedInDegreeOne 𝒮) : IsEventualNumericalPolynomial (hilbertFun 𝒮 ℳ hneg)

declarations.name: Stacks.HilbertFunction.PolynomialQuotient.hilbertFunction_degree_lt
declarations.doc:
**Main Theorem (Stacks Lemma 10.58.10, Tag 00K3).**
Let `k` be a field, `d ≥ 1`, and `S = k[X_1, …, X_d]` with the standard grading.
Let `I ⊆ S` be a *nonzero* graded ideal and set `M = S / I`. Then the Hilbert
function `H_M(n) = dim_k(M_n)` is, for large `n`, given by a rational polynomial
`P` whose degree is strictly less than `d - 1`.

Concretely: there exist `P ∈ ℚ[T]` with `deg P < d - 1` and an integer `N` such
that `dim_k(M_n) = P(n)` for all `n ≥ N`. The degree bound `deg P < d - 1` is
expressed using `Polynomial.degree : ℚ[X] → WithBot ℕ`, which sends the zero
polynomial to `⊥`; thus `deg P < d - 1` automatically allows `P = 0` (the case
`-∞ < d - 1`), and when `d = 1` it forces `P = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertFunction_degree_lt (hd : 1 ≤ d) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k))
    (hI_hom : Ideal.IsHomogeneous (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin d) k) I)
    (hI_ne : I ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ (P : Polynomial ℚ) (N : ℕ),
      P.degree < ((d - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → (hilbertFunction I n : ℚ) = P.eval (n : ℚ)

declarations.name: chi_bounds_of_quotient_finiteLength
declarations.doc:
Let `(R, m, k)` be a Noetherian local ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal of definition, and
`M' ⊆ M` finite `R`-modules with `M / M'` of finite length. Then there are
constants `c₁, c₂ ∈ ℕ` such that for all `n ≥ c₂`,
`c₁ + χ_{I,M'}(n - c₂) ≤ χ_{I,M}(n) ≤ c₁ + χ_{I,M'}(n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chi_bounds_of_quotient_finiteLength
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (M' : Submodule R M) (hlen : Module.length R (M ⧸ M') < ⊤) :
    ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, c₂ ≤ n →
      (c₁ : ℕ∞) + chi I M' (n - c₂) ≤ chi I M n ∧
      chi I M n ≤ (c₁ : ℕ∞) + chi I M' n

declarations.name: additivity_of_characteristic_and_hilbert_functions
declarations.doc:
Given a short exact sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` of finite `R`-modules over a
Noetherian local ring `(R, m)` and an ideal `I` with `√I = m`, there are a submodule
`N ⊆ M'` of finite colength `l = length_R (M'/N)` and an integer `c ≥ 0` such that for
all `n ≥ c`
  `χ_{I,M}(n) = χ_{I,M''}(n) + χ_{I,N}(n - c) + l`  and
  `φ_{I,M}(n) = φ_{I,M''}(n) + φ_{I,N}(n - c)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem additivity_of_characteristic_and_hilbert_functions
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.radical = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (M' M M'' : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module.Finite R M']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M''] [Module.Finite R M'']
    (f : M' →ₗ[R] M) (g : M →ₗ[R] M'')
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (hfg : Function.Exact f g) :
    ∃ (N : Submodule R M') (c : ℕ) (l : ℕ),
      Module.length R (M' ⧸ N) = (l : ℕ∞) ∧
      (∀ n ≥ c, charFn R I M n = charFn R I M'' n + charFn R I N (n - c) + (l : ℕ∞)) ∧
      (∀ n ≥ c, hilbertFn R I M n = hilbertFn R I M'' n + hilbertFn R I N (n - c))

declarations.name: chi_change_ideal_of_definition
declarations.doc:
Let `(R, m)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `I, I'` be two ideals of definition
of `R`, and let `M` be a finite `R`-module. Then there exists a positive integer
`a` such that
  `χ_{I,M}(n) ≤ χ_{I',M}(a·n)` for all `n ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chi_change_ideal_of_definition
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I I' : Ideal R) (hI : IsIdealOfDefinition' I) (hI' : IsIdealOfDefinition' I') :
    ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → hilbertSamuel_chi I M n ≤ hilbertSamuel_chi I' M (a * n)

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_eventually_length_quotient_smul_pow_eq_sum_choose_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00K8.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal of definition
(`I.radical` is the maximal ideal of `R`) and let `M` be a finite `R`-module. Then the Hilbert
function `n ↦ length_R (I ^ n • M / I ^ (n + 1) • M)` and the function
`n ↦ length_R (M / I ^ (n + 1) • M)` are numerical polynomials: each takes finite values which,
for all `n ≫ 0`, are given by a `ℤ`-linear combination of the binomial coefficients
`n choose 0, …, n choose r`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.exists_eventually_length_quotient_smul_pow_eq_sum_choose_mul
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : I.radical = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (a b : ℕ → ℤ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      (∃ p : ℕ, Module.length R (↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⧸
            (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).submoduleOf (I ^ n • ⊤)) = p ∧
          (p : ℤ) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r + 1), (n.choose i : ℤ) * a i) ∧
      (∃ q : ℕ, Module.length R (M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = q ∧
          (q : ℤ) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r + 1), (n.choose i : ℤ) * b i)

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_degree_eq_of_eventually_eval_eq_length_quotient_smul_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00K9.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and let `M` be a finite `R`-module. Then
there are `d e : WithBot ℕ`, depending on `R` and `M` only, such that for every ideal of
definition `I ⊆ R` (that is, `I.radical = m`): every polynomial `P ∈ ℚ[t]` agreeing with the
Hilbert function `φ_{I,M}(n) = length_R (I ^ n M / I ^ (n + 1) M)` for all `n ≫ 0` has degree
`d`, and every polynomial `P ∈ ℚ[t]` agreeing with `χ_{I,M}(n) = length_R (M / I ^ (n + 1) M)`
for all `n ≫ 0` has degree `e`. That is, the degrees of the numerical polynomials `φ_{I,M}` and
`χ_{I,M}` are independent of the ideal of definition `I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.exists_degree_eq_of_eventually_eval_eq_length_quotient_smul_pow
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    ∃ d e : WithBot ℕ, ∀ I : Ideal R, I.radical = maximalIdeal R → ∀ P : ℚ[X],
      ((∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ p : ℕ,
            Module.length R (↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⧸
              (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).submoduleOf (I ^ n • ⊤)) = p ∧
            P.eval (n : ℚ) = (p : ℚ)) → P.degree = d) ∧
      ((∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ q : ℕ,
            Module.length R (M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = q ∧
            P.eval (n : ℚ) = (q : ℚ)) → P.degree = e)
declarations.comment:
The degree of a numerical polynomial is spelled as the degree of any rational
polynomial computing it at all large `n`, and independence of `I` as the two degrees being
quantified outside the ideal of definition. Part (1) of the tag is the first conjunct, part (2)
the second.

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertSamuelDegree
declarations.doc:
The degree, an element of `{-∞, 0, 1, 2, …} = WithBot ℕ`, of the numerical polynomial
`χ_{I,M}(n) = length_R (M / I ^ (n + 1) M)`: the degree of a polynomial `P ∈ ℚ[t]` with
`P(n) = χ_{I,M}(n)` for all `n ≫ 0`, and `-∞` if there is no such polynomial.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def Ideal.hilbertSamuelDegree {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : WithBot ℕ
declarations.comment:
Definition 00KA is the case `I = maximalIdeal R`, spelled
`Module.hilbertSamuelDegree`. The definition is stated for an arbitrary ideal because that is the
generality of the surrounding section, and because Lemma 00K9(2) is the assertion that this value
is the same for all ideals of definition.

declarations.name: Module.hilbertSamuelDegree
declarations.doc:
The invariant `d(M) ∈ {-∞, 0, 1, 2, …} = WithBot ℕ` of a module `M` over a local ring
`(R, m)`: the degree of the numerical polynomial `χ_M(n) = length_R (M / m ^ (n + 1) M)`, that is
`Ideal.hilbertSamuelDegree` at the maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev Module.hilbertSamuelDegree (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : WithBot ℕ
declarations.comment:
The `d(M)` of the definition. Case (1) is not a separate branch: for `M = 0` the
polynomial computing `χ_M` is `0`, whose degree is `-∞ = ⊥`, and conversely a computing
polynomial of degree `-∞` forces `M = m ^ n M` for `n ≫ 0`, hence `M = 0` by Nakayama. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: HilbertSamuel.degree_sub_lt
declarations.doc:
Let `(R, m)` be a Noetherian local ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal of definition, and `M`
a finite `R`-module which does not have finite length.  Let `M' ⊆ M` be a
submodule with finite colength, and let `χ_{I,M}`, `χ_{I,M'} ∈ Q[t]` be the
Hilbert–Samuel polynomials of `M` and `M'`.  Then the difference
`χ_{I,M} - χ_{I,M'}` has degree strictly less than the degree of each of the two
Hilbert–Samuel polynomials.
declarations.statement:
theorem degree_sub_lt
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (hM : ¬ HasFiniteLength R M)
    (M' : Submodule R M) (hM' : HasFiniteColength M')
    (χM χM' : ℚ[X])
    (hχM : IsHilbertSamuelPoly I M χM)
    (hχM' : IsHilbertSamuelPoly I (↥M') χM') :
    (χM - χM').degree < χM.degree ∧ (χM - χM').degree < χM'.degree

declarations.name: Ideal.max_degree_eq_degree_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00KC.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal of definition
(`I.radical` is the maximal ideal of `R`) and let `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` be a short exact
sequence of finite `R`-modules, given by `f : M' →ₗ[R] M` injective, `g : M →ₗ[R] M''`
surjective and `Function.Exact f g`. Then

1. if `M'` does not have finite length, then `χ_{I,M} - χ_{I,M''} - χ_{I,M'}` is a numerical
   polynomial of degree `<` the degree of `χ_{I,M'}`,
2. `max {deg χ_{I,M'}, deg χ_{I,M''}} = deg χ_{I,M}`, and
3. `max {d(M'), d(M'')} = d(M)`, for the invariant `d(-)` of Definition 00KA — the case
   `I = m` of the last conjunct, since `d(N) = (maximalIdeal R).hilbertSamuelDegree N`.

Here `P'`, `P`, `P''` are the numerical polynomials `χ_{I,M'}`, `χ_{I,M}`, `χ_{I,M''}`, that is,
the polynomials with `P'(n) = length_R (M' / I ^ (n + 1) M')` for all `n ≫ 0` and likewise for
`M` and `M''`, and `Ideal.hilbertSamuelDegree I N` is the degree of `χ_{I,N}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.max_degree_eq_degree_of_exact
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.radical = maximalIdeal R)
    {M' M M'' : Type*} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module.Finite R M']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M''] [Module.Finite R M'']
    {f : M' →ₗ[R] M} {g : M →ₗ[R] M''} (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    (∀ P' P P'' : ℚ[X],
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ p : ℕ,
          Module.length R (M' ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M'))) = p ∧
            P'.eval (n : ℚ) = (p : ℚ)) →
        (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ p : ℕ,
          Module.length R (M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = p ∧
            P.eval (n : ℚ) = (p : ℚ)) →
        (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ p : ℕ,
          Module.length R (M'' ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M''))) = p ∧
            P''.eval (n : ℚ) = (p : ℚ)) →
        (¬ IsFiniteLength R M' → (P - P'' - P').degree < P'.degree) ∧
          max P'.degree P''.degree = P.degree) ∧
      max (I.hilbertSamuelDegree M') (I.hilbertSamuelDegree M'') =
        I.hilbertSamuelDegree M
declarations.comment:
The first conjunct is parts (1) and (2) of the tag, for polynomials computing the
three Hilbert–Samuel functions as in Tags 00K8 and 00K9, so `χ_{I,M} - χ_{I,M''} - χ_{I,M'}` is
`P - P'' - P'`; that this is again a numerical polynomial is inherited from the hypotheses on
the three polynomials, and the degree bound is the content. The second conjunct is part (2) for
the invariant of Definition 00KA, and part (3) of the tag is its case `I = maximalIdeal R`. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.ringKrullDim_eq_zero_iff_hilbertSamuelDegree_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local ring has dimension zero exactly when its Hilbert–Samuel degree `d(R)`
is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_eq_zero_iff_hilbertSamuelDegree_eq_zero :
    ringKrullDim R = 0 ↔ Module.hilbertSamuelDegree R R = 0
declarations.comment:
The source reads this off from `d(R) = 0` if and only if `R` has finite length;
here it is read off from `d(M) = dim Supp(M)` (Lemma 00L8) for `M = R`.

registrations.comment: dimension zero implies d=0

registrations.name: isArtinianRing_iff_isFiniteLength
registrations.comment: d=0 characterization

declarations.name: isArtinianRing_tfae_hilbertSamuelDegree
declarations.doc:
**Characterizations of Artinian rings.** For a commutative ring `R` the following are
equivalent: (1) `R` is Artinian; (2) `R` is Noetherian of Krull dimension at most zero; (3) `R`
has finite length as a module over itself; (4) `R` is a finite product of Artinian local rings;
(5) `R` is Noetherian and `Spec(R)` is a finite discrete space; (6) `R` is a finite product of
Noetherian local rings of Krull dimension `0`; (7) `R` is a finite product of Noetherian local
rings `R_i` with Hilbert–Samuel degree `d(R_i) = 0`; (8) `R` is a finite product of Noetherian
local rings with nilpotent maximal ideals; (9) `R` is Noetherian with finitely many maximal
ideals and nilpotent Jacobson radical; and (10) `R` is Noetherian with no strict inclusions among
its prime ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem isArtinianRing_tfae_hilbertSamuelDegree (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsArtinianRing R,
        IsNoetherianRing R ∧ Ring.KrullDimLE 0 R,
        IsFiniteLength R R,
        ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (S : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (S i))
          (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (S i)), (∀ i, IsArtinianRing (S i)) ∧ Nonempty (R ≃+* ∀ i, S i),
        IsNoetherianRing R ∧ Finite (PrimeSpectrum R) ∧ DiscreteTopology (PrimeSpectrum R),
        ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (S : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (S i))
          (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (S i)), (∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (S i) ∧ ringKrullDim (S i) = 0) ∧
            Nonempty (R ≃+* ∀ i, S i),
        ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (S : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (S i))
          (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (S i)),
          (∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (S i) ∧ Module.hilbertSamuelDegree (S i) (S i) = 0) ∧
            Nonempty (R ≃+* ∀ i, S i),
        ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (S : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (S i))
          (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (S i)),
          (∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (S i) ∧ IsNilpotent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (S i))) ∧
            Nonempty (R ≃+* ∀ i, S i),
        IsNoetherianRing R ∧ Finite (MaximalSpectrum R) ∧ IsNilpotent (Ring.jacobson R),
        IsNoetherianRing R ∧ ∀ p q : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → q.IsPrime → p ≤ q → p = q ]
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(10) in the source's order. Item (2) reads `dim(R) = 0` as
`ringKrullDim R ≤ 0` (`Ring.KrullDimLE 0 R`), which is the literal equality for every nonzero
ring (`isArtinianRing_iff_isNoetherianRing_and_ringKrullDim_eq_zero`) and the correct form for
the zero ring, whose dimension is `-∞` by Topology, Definition 0055. In (7), `d(R_i)` is
`Module.hilbertSamuelDegree` of Definition 00KA. A finite product of local rings is a finite
index type and a ring isomorphism `R ≃+* ∀ i, S i`.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Noetherian local rings of dimension one.** For a Noetherian local ring `(R, m)` the
following are equivalent: `dim(R) = 1`; `d(R) = 1`; there is a non-nilpotent `x ∈ m` with
`V(x) = {m}`; there is a non-nilpotent `x ∈ m` with `m = √(x)`; some ideal of definition is
generated by one element, and the ideal `(0)` generated by zero elements is not an ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_eq_one_tfae :
    List.TFAE
      [ringKrullDim R = 1,
        Module.hilbertSamuelDegree R R = 1,
        ∃ x ∈ maximalIdeal R, ¬ IsNilpotent x ∧ zeroLocus {x} = {closedPoint R},
        ∃ x ∈ maximalIdeal R, ¬ IsNilpotent x ∧ (Ideal.span {x}).radical = maximalIdeal R,
        (∃ x : R, (Ideal.span {x}).radical = maximalIdeal R) ∧
          (⊥ : Ideal R).radical ≠ maximalIdeal R]
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(5), in the source's order. The ideal generated by zero elements is
`⊥`; an ideal of definition is an ideal with radical `m`.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.ringKrullDim_eq_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Dimension of a Noetherian local ring.** For a Noetherian local ring `(R, m)` and a natural
number `d` the following are equivalent: `dim(R) = d`; the Hilbert–Samuel function
`n ↦ length_R (R / m ^ (n + 1))` is eventually a `ℤ`-combination
`∑_{i ≤ d} (n choose i) * a i` of binomial coefficients with `a d ≠ 0`, i.e. `d(R) = d`; and `d`
is the least number of generators of an ideal of definition of `R`, i.e. some ideal of definition
is generated by `d` elements and none is generated by fewer.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.ringKrullDim_eq_tfae {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] (d : ℕ) :
    List.TFAE
      [ringKrullDim R = d,
        ∃ a : ℕ → ℤ,
          a d ≠ 0 ∧
            ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
              ∃ p : ℕ,
                Module.length R (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ (n + 1)) = p ∧
                  (p : ℤ) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (d + 1), (n.choose i : ℤ) * a i,
        IsLeast {n : ℕ | ∃ I : Ideal R, I.radical = maximalIdeal R ∧ I.spanFinrank = n} d]
declarations.comment: Items (1)-(3); see the module docstring for the form of (2) and (3).

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsSystemOfParameters
declarations.doc:
**System of parameters of a local ring**. A sequence `rs` of elements of a local ring `(R, m)`
is a *system of parameters* of `R` if it generates an ideal of definition of `R`, that is an ideal
with radical `m`, and has `dim R` entries. Over a Noetherian local ring this is the source's
notion: `dim R` elements of `m` generating an ideal of definition, `dim R` being the least number
of generators an ideal of definition can have. A *regular* system of parameters is one generating
`m` itself, `IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParametersList`; the rings admitting one are the regular
local rings, `IsLocalRing.HasRegularSystemOfParameters` (Mathlib's `IsRegularLocalRing`).
declarations.statement:
public def IsLocalRing.IsSystemOfParameters {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (rs : List R) : Prop
declarations.comment:
Item (1). Item (2) is `IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParametersList` (a regular
system of parameters) and `IsLocalRing.HasRegularSystemOfParameters` (a regular local ring), the
latter equivalent over a Noetherian local ring to Mathlib's `IsRegularLocalRing` by
`IsLocalRing.isRegularLocalRing_iff_hasRegularSystemOfParameters`.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParametersList
declarations.doc:
**Regular system of parameters** (Stacks 00KU, item (2)). A sequence `rs` of elements of a
local ring `(R, m)` is a *regular system of parameters* of `R` if it generates the maximal ideal
`m` and has `dim R` entries. Its entries then lie in `m`.
declarations.statement: def IsRegularSystemOfParametersList (rs : List R) : Prop
declarations.comment: Item (2), the sequence notion: a regular system of parameters, `m = (x_1, …, x_d)` with `d = dim R`.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.HasRegularSystemOfParameters
declarations.doc:
**Regular local ring, Stacks' definition** (Stacks 00KU, item (2)). A local ring `R` is
regular in the sense of the source if it admits a regular system of parameters, i.e. its maximal
ideal is generated by `dim R` elements. Over a Noetherian local ring this is Mathlib's
`IsRegularLocalRing`, see `IsLocalRing.isRegularLocalRing_iff_hasRegularSystemOfParameters`.
declarations.statement: def HasRegularSystemOfParameters : Prop
declarations.comment: Item (2), the predicate on the ring: there exist `x_1, …, x_d ∈ m` with `m = (x_1, …, x_d)`, `d = dim R`. Equivalent to Mathlib's `IsRegularLocalRing` over a Noetherian local ring by `isRegularLocalRing_iff_hasRegularSystemOfParameters`.

declarations.name: Ideal.height_le_one_of_mem_minimalPrimes_span_singleton_and_not_lt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00KV.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `x ∈ R`.
1. If a prime `p` is minimal over `(x)`, then `p` has height `0` or `1`, that is, height `≤ 1`.
2. If `p` is a prime and the prime `q` is minimal over `(p, x)`, then there is no prime strictly
   between `p` and `q`: no prime `r` satisfies `p < r < q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.height_le_one_of_mem_minimalPrimes_span_singleton_and_not_lt {R : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (x : R) :
    (∀ p ∈ (Ideal.span {x}).minimalPrimes, p.height ≤ 1) ∧
      ∀ p q : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → q ∈ (p ⊔ Ideal.span {x}).minimalPrimes →
        ∀ r : Ideal R, r.IsPrime → p < r → ¬r < q
declarations.comment: Item (1) is Mathlib's Krull principal ideal theorem `Ideal.height_le_one_of_isPrincipal_of_mem_minimalPrimes` applied to `Ideal.span {x}`; item (2) is `Ideal.not_lt_of_lt_of_mem_minimalPrimes_sup_span_singleton`.

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_le_quotient_span_singleton_add_one_and_eq_of_notMem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00KW.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and `x ∈ 𝔪`. Then
`dim R ≤ dim R/xR + 1`, and if `x` is contained in no minimal prime of `R` then
`dim R/xR + 1 = dim R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_le_quotient_span_singleton_add_one_and_eq_of_notMem_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {x : R}
    (hx : x ∈ maximalIdeal R) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ ringKrullDim (R ⧸ span {x}) + 1 ∧
      ((∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, x ∉ p) → ringKrullDim (R ⧸ span {x}) + 1 = ringKrullDim R)
declarations.comment: both the inequality and the equality when x avoids the minimal primes

declarations.name: isJacobsonRing_of_forall_isMaximal_or_infinite_setOf_isPrime
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring in which every prime ideal is either maximal or contained in infinitely
many prime ideals is a Jacobson ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJacobsonRing_of_forall_isMaximal_or_infinite_setOf_isPrime (R : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (h : ∀ p : Ideal R, p.IsPrime →
      p.IsMaximal ∨ {q : Ideal R | p ≤ q ∧ q.IsPrime}.Infinite) :
    IsJacobsonRing R

declarations.name: Module.Finite.exists_relSeries_isQuotientEquivQuotientCyclic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00KZ**.
Let `R` be a ring and `M` a finite `R`-module. Then `M` admits a finite filtration
`0 = M₀ ≤ M₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ Mₙ = M`, packaged as a `RelSeries` of
`Submodule.IsQuotientEquivQuotientCyclic`, whose terms are finitely generated and whose successive
quotients `Mᵢ₊₁ ⧸ Mᵢ` are cyclic, i.e. each isomorphic to `R ⧸ Iᵢ` for some ideal `Iᵢ`.

The quotients are cyclic but not necessarily simple, so this is a filtration rather than a
composition series in the sense of `CompositionSeries` (which requires simple quotients, hence
finite length).
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Finite.exists_relSeries_isQuotientEquivQuotientCyclic (R M : Type*) [Ring R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    ∃ X : RelSeries {(N₁, N₂) | N₁.IsQuotientEquivQuotientCyclic N₂},
      X.head = (⊥ : Submodule R M) ∧ X.last = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, Module.Finite R (X i)

registrations.name: Module.isClosed_support
registrations.comment: the support of a finite module is closed

declarations.name: support_submodule_subset
declarations.doc: The support of a submodule is contained in the support of the ambient module.
declarations.statement:
theorem support_submodule_subset
    {R : Type*} {M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (N : Submodule R M) :
    Module.support R N ⊆ Module.support R M

declarations.name: support_eq_iUnion_zeroLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00L4, main statement.** With the filtration data of Stacks 00L0,
the support of `M` is the union of the closed sets `V(𝔭ᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem support_eq_iUnion_zeroLocus
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Module.Finite A M]
    (s : RelSeries {(N₁, N₂) : Submodule A M × Submodule A M |
          N₁.IsQuotientEquivQuotientPrime N₂})
    (hhead : s.head = ⊥) (hlast : s.last = ⊤)
    (p : Fin s.length → PrimeSpectrum A)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin s.length,
      Nonempty (((s.toFun i.succ) ⧸ (s.toFun i.castSucc).submoduleOf (s.toFun i.succ))
        ≃ₗ[A] A ⧸ (p i).asIdeal)) :
    Module.support A M
      = ⋃ i : Fin s.length, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ((p i).asIdeal : Set A)

declarations.name: mem_support_of_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime_series
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00L4, "in particular".** Each prime `𝔭ᵢ` lies in the support of
`M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_support_of_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime_series
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Module.Finite A M]
    (s : RelSeries {(N₁, N₂) : Submodule A M × Submodule A M |
          N₁.IsQuotientEquivQuotientPrime N₂})
    (hhead : s.head = ⊥) (hlast : s.last = ⊤)
    (p : Fin s.length → PrimeSpectrum A)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin s.length,
      Nonempty (((s.toFun i.succ) ⧸ (s.toFun i.castSucc).submoduleOf (s.toFun i.succ))
        ≃ₗ[A] A ⧸ (p i).asIdeal)) :
    ∀ i : Fin s.length, p i ∈ Module.support A M

declarations.name: support_point
declarations.doc:
Stacks 00L5. Over a Noetherian local ring `R` with maximal ideal `m`, a nonzero
finite `R`-module `M` has support equal to the singleton `{m}` if and only if `M`
has finite length over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem support_point {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M] :
    Module.support R M = {IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} ↔ IsFiniteLength R M

declarations.name: main_theorem_00l6
declarations.doc:
For a finite module `M` over a Noetherian ring `R` and an ideal `I ⊆ R`,
some power of `I` annihilates `M` if and only if the support of `M` is contained
in the zero locus of `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_00l6 {R : Type*} {M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R M] (I : Ideal R) :
    (∃ n : ℕ, (I ^ n) • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊥) ↔
      Module.support R M ⊆ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R)

declarations.name: Module.setOf_minimal_range_eq_setOf_minimal_support_and_ncard_eq_length
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00L7**.
Let `R` be a ring, `M` an `R`-module, and let `0 = N₀ ⊆ N₁ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Nₙ = M` be a filtration whose
successive quotients are `Nᵢ₊₁ ⧸ Nᵢ ≅ R ⧸ 𝔭ᵢ` for primes `𝔭ᵢ = p i` of `R`, as produced by
Stacks 00L0. Then the minimal elements of the set `{𝔭ᵢ}` are exactly the minimal elements of
`Supp(M)`, and each minimal `𝔭 ∈ Supp(M)` occurs among the `𝔭ᵢ` exactly
`length_{R_𝔭} M_𝔭` times.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setOf_minimal_range_eq_setOf_minimal_support_and_ncard_eq_length {R M : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {n : ℕ} (N : Fin (n + 1) → Submodule R M)
    (p : Fin n → PrimeSpectrum R) (hle : ∀ i : Fin n, N i.castSucc ≤ N i.succ)
    (hquot : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Nonempty ((↥(N i.succ) ⧸ (N i.castSucc).submoduleOf (N i.succ)) ≃ₗ[R] R ⧸ (p i).asIdeal))
    (hbot : N 0 = ⊥) (htop : N (Fin.last n) = ⊤) :
    {q | Minimal (· ∈ Set.range p) q} = {q | Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q} ∧
      ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum R, Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) q →
        ({i | p i = q}.ncard : ℕ∞) =
          Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl M)

declarations.name: Module.hilbertSamuelDegree_eq_supportDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00L8**.
Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and let `M` be a finite `R`-module. Then the Hilbert–Samuel
degree `d(M)` of Definition 00KA equals the dimension of the support of `M`, that is, the Krull
dimension of `Supp(M) ⊆ Spec(R)`.

The equation is stated in `WithBot ℕ∞`, where `dim Supp(M)` lives, with `d(M) : WithBot ℕ`
transported along the order embedding `WithBot.map (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℕ∞)`; it therefore also
asserts that `dim Supp(M)` is finite. Both sides are `⊥ = -∞` exactly when `M = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hilbertSamuelDegree_eq_supportDim (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    (hilbertSamuelDegree R M).map (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℕ∞) = supportDim R M

declarations.name: IsAssociatedPrimeStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00LA**.
A prime ideal `p` of `R` is associated to the `R`-module `M` when it is the
annihilator of a single element of `M`.
declarations.statement: def IsAssociatedPrimeStacks (p : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: ass_subset_of_filtration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00LB.** If `M` admits a finite filtration by `R`-submodules
`0 = M_0 ⊆ M_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ M_n = M` whose successive quotients `M_i / M_{i-1}` are
isomorphic to `R / p_i` for prime ideals `p_i`, then every associated prime of
`M` is among the `p_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ass_subset_of_filtration
    (R M : Type*) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (n : ℕ) (Mfil : Fin (n + 1) → Submodule R M)
    (hbot : Mfil 0 = ⊥) (htop : Mfil (Fin.last n) = ⊤)
    (hmono : Monotone Mfil)
    (p : Fin n → Ideal R)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin n, (p i).IsPrime)
    (hquot : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Nonempty (((Mfil i.succ) ⧸ (Submodule.comap (Mfil i.succ).subtype (Mfil i.castSucc)))
        ≃ₗ[R] (R ⧸ p i))) :
    assPrimes R M ⊆ Set.range p

declarations.name: regularSequence_xyz_one_sub_x
declarations.doc: The sequence `x, y(1-x), z(1-x)` is a regular sequence on `k[x, y, z]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularSequence_xyz_one_sub_x (k : Type) [Field k] :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (mvPolyRingFin3 k)
      ([X 0, X 1 * (1 - X 0), X 2 * (1 - X 0)] : List (mvPolyRingFin3 k))

declarations.name: Module.depth
declarations.doc:
The `I`-depth of an `R`-module `M`, for `I` an ideal of `R`: the supremum in
`ℕ∞ = {0, 1, 2, …, ∞}` of the lengths of the `M`-regular sequences with all terms in `I`,
except that the depth is `⊤` when `I • M = M` (which happens for instance when `M = 0`).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def Module.depth (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : ℕ∞

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.isRegular_of_perm
registrations.comment: for a Noetherian module over a local ring

declarations.name: Module.depth_le_supportDim
declarations.doc:
**Depth is at most the dimension of the support.** If `M` is a finite `R`-module and `I` is
an ideal of `R` with `I • M ≠ M`, then `depth_I(M) ≤ dim(Supp(M))`. For `R` Noetherian local,
`I` the maximal ideal and `M` nonzero, this is `depth(M) ≤ dim(Supp(M))`.

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_mem_isSMulRegular_iff_forall_associatedPrimes_not_le
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `M` an `R`-module with finitely many associated primes and
`I ⊆ R` an ideal. Then `I` contains an element that is a nonzerodivisor on `M` if and only if `I`
is contained in no associated prime of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.exists_mem_isSMulRegular_iff_forall_associatedPrimes_not_le {R : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : (associatedPrimes R M).Finite) :
    (∃ x ∈ I, IsSMulRegular M x) ↔
      ∀ 𝔮 ∈ associatedPrimes R M, ¬ I ≤ 𝔮

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.isRegular_map_algebraMap_iff_of_faithfullyFlat_of_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring, `M` an `R`-module, `S` a faithfully flat `R`-algebra and
`f : M →ₗ[R] N` a base change of `M` to `S`. Then a sequence `rs` in `R` is `M`-regular if and
only if its image in `S` is `N`-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_map_algebraMap_iff_of_faithfullyFlat_of_isBaseChange
    {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : IsBaseChange S f) (rs : List R) :
    IsRegular N (rs.map (algebraMap R S)) ↔ IsRegular M rs

**Statement 2.** An `M`-regular sequence (Mathlib's `IsRegular`, i.e. the

declarations.name: exists_free_resolution
declarations.doc:
**(Existence of a free resolution.)** For any commutative ring `R` and any
`R`-module `M`, there exists an exact complex of `R`-modules
`... → F₂ → F₁ → F₀ → M → 0` in which every `Fᵢ` is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_free_resolution
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    ∃ P : FreeResolutionData R M, P.IsExact ∧ P.IsFree

declarations.name: exists_finite_free_resolution
declarations.doc:
**(Finite free resolution in the Noetherian finite case.)** If `R` is a Noetherian
commutative ring and `M` is a finite `R`-module, then there exists an exact complex of
`R`-modules `... → F₂ → F₁ → F₀ → M → 0` in which every `Fᵢ` is finite free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_free_resolution
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    ∃ P : FreeResolutionData R M, P.IsExact ∧ P.IsFiniteFree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.LeftResolution
declarations.doc:
A `P.LeftResolution Z` consists of a bundled `ℕ`-indexed chain complex whose terms lie in the
class `P`, along with a quasi-isomorphism to the complex consisting of just `Z` supported in
degree `0`; equivalently, an exact complex `… → F₁ → F₀ → Z → 0` with all `Fᵢ` in `P`.
declarations.statement: public structure LeftResolution (P : ObjectProperty C) (Z : C)

declarations.name: ModuleResolution
declarations.doc:
A (left) *resolution* `F_• → M` of an `R`-module `M`: an exact chain complex
`… → F₂ → F₁ → F₀ → M → 0` of `R`-modules, encoded as an ℕ-indexed chain
complex together with a quasi-isomorphism to `M` in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
structure ModuleResolution (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
declarations.comment: resolution

declarations.name: FreeModuleResolution
declarations.doc:
A *resolution of `M` by free `R`-modules*: a resolution `F_• → M` such that
every `F_i` is a free `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
structure FreeModuleResolution (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] extends ModuleResolution R M
declarations.comment: free resolution

declarations.name: FiniteFreeModuleResolution
declarations.doc:
A *resolution of `M` by finite free `R`-modules*: a resolution `F_• → M`
such that every `F_i` is a free and finitely generated `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
structure FiniteFreeModuleResolution (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] extends FreeModuleResolution R M
declarations.comment: finite free resolution

declarations.name: exists_lift_along_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1): Existence of a lift.** Let `φ : M → N` be a map of `R`-modules, let
`C` be an (arbitrary) resolution of `N`, and let `F` be a complex over `M` whose terms are
all free `R`-modules. Then there exists a map of complexes `α : F → C` lifting `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_along_resolution {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module R N]
    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) (F : ComplexOver R M) (C : ComplexOver R N)
    (hC : IsResolution C) (hF : IsFreeComplex F) :
    ∃ α : ∀ i, F.obj i →ₗ[R] C.obj i, IsLift φ F C α

declarations.name: lift_unique_up_to_homotopy
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2): Uniqueness up to homotopy.** Any two maps of complexes `α, β : F → C`
lifting the same `φ` are chain homotopic.
declarations.statement:
theorem lift_unique_up_to_homotopy {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) (F : ComplexOver R M) (C : ComplexOver R N)
    (hC : IsResolution C) (hF : IsFreeComplex F)
    (α β : ∀ i, F.obj i →ₗ[R] C.obj i)
    (hα : IsLift φ F C α) (hβ : IsLift φ F C β) :
    HomotopicComplexOver F C α β

declarations.name: ModuleCat.homologyMap_linearYoneda_eq_and_isIso_and_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00LT.** Let `R` be a ring, let `M₁`, `M₂`, `N` be `R`-modules, let `F` be a free
resolution of `M₁`, let `G` be a free resolution of `M₂`, let `φ : M₁ → M₂` be a module map and
let `α : F_• → G_•` be a map of complexes inducing `φ`. Then, for every `i`, the map
`H^i(α) : H^i(Hom_R(G_•, N)) → H^i(Hom_R(F_•, N))` is independent of the choice of `α`; it is an
isomorphism if `φ` is one; and a map `F_• → F_•` inducing the identity of `M₁` induces the
identity on `H^i(Hom_R(F_•, N))`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homologyMap_linearYoneda_eq_and_isIso_and_eq_id {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat.{v} R} (N : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    (F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution (fun P : ModuleCat.{v} R => Module.Free R P) M₁)
    (G : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution (fun P : ModuleCat.{v} R => Module.Free R P) M₂)
    (φ : M₁ ⟶ M₂) (α : F.complex ⟶ G.complex)
    (hα : α ≫ G.π = F.π ≫ (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{v} R)).map φ) (i : ℕ) :
    (∀ β : F.complex ⟶ G.complex,
        β ≫ G.π = F.π ≫ (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{v} R)).map φ →
        homologyMap ((opFunctor _ _ ⋙
            ((linearYoneda R (ModuleCat.{v} R)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex _).map β.op) i =
          homologyMap ((opFunctor _ _ ⋙
            ((linearYoneda R (ModuleCat.{v} R)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex _).map α.op) i) ∧
      (IsIso φ → IsIso (homologyMap ((opFunctor _ _ ⋙
          ((linearYoneda R (ModuleCat.{v} R)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex _).map α.op) i)) ∧
      (∀ γ : F.complex ⟶ F.complex, γ ≫ F.π = F.π →
        homologyMap ((opFunctor _ _ ⋙
          ((linearYoneda R (ModuleCat.{v} R)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex _).map γ.op) i
            = 𝟙 _)
declarations.comment:
A free resolution is an `ObjectProperty.LeftResolution` for the class of free
modules (00LQ) and `Hom_R(F_•, N)` is the image of `F_•` under
`(linearYoneda R (ModuleCat R)).obj N`, so `H^i(α)` is a `homologyMap`. The source's display has
the two cohomology groups interchanged, since `Hom_R(-, N)` is contravariant; see the module
docstring.

declarations.name: ext_annihilated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00LV**.
If `x` annihilates `N` or `x` annihilates `M`, then `x` annihilates every Ext group
$\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, N)$.
declarations.statement:
theorem ext_annihilated (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (x : R)
    (h : x ∈ Module.annihilator R N ∨ x ∈ Module.annihilator R M) (i : ℕ) :
    ∀ ξ : extModule M N i, x • ξ = 0

declarations.name: depth_eq_least_nonzero_ext
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00LW (Lemma 10.72.5).** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring with
maximal ideal `𝔪`, residue field `κ = R/𝔪`, and let `M` be a nonzero finite
`R`-module. Then there is a least index `n` for which `Ext^n_R(κ, M)` is nonzero,
and the depth of `M` equals this index `n`:
`depth(M) = min { i | Ext^i_R(κ, M) ≠ 0 }`.
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_eq_least_nonzero_ext {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (hM : Nontrivial M) :
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      IsLeast
          {i : ℕ |
            Nontrivial
              (Ext (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) (ModuleCat.of R M) i)}
          n ∧
        Module.depthSup R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) M = (n : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Module.min_depth_le_depth_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Depth in a short exact sequence.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal, and let
`0 → N' → N → N'' → 0` be a short exact sequence of finite `R`-modules, given by `f : N' →ₗ[R] N`
injective, `g : N →ₗ[R] N''` surjective and `Function.Exact f g`. Then

1. `min {depth_I(N'), depth_I(N'')} ≤ depth_I(N)`,
2. `min {depth_I(N), depth_I(N') - 1} ≤ depth_I(N'')`,
3. `min {depth_I(N), depth_I(N'') + 1} ≤ depth_I(N')`,

the subtraction being the truncated one of `ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem min_depth_le_depth_of_exact {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) {N' N N'' : Type*} [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R N'] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module R N] [AddCommGroup N''] [Module R N''] [Module.Finite R N] {f : N' →ₗ[R] N}
    {g : N →ₗ[R] N''} (h : Function.Exact f g) (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    min (depth R I N') (depth R I N'') ≤ depth R I N ∧
      min (depth R I N) (depth R I N' - 1) ≤ depth R I N'' ∧
      min (depth R I N) (depth R I N'' + 1) ≤ depth R I N'

declarations.name: FreeResolution.torMap_isLift_properties
declarations.doc:
Let `F` and `G` be free resolutions of `M₁` and `M₂`, let `φ : M₁ ⟶ M₂` and let `N` be a
module. Then the maps `H_i(α) : H_i(F ⊗ N) ⟶ H_i(G ⊗ N)` induced by chain maps `α` lifting `φ`
are independent of the choice of `α`; if `φ` is an isomorphism, so are all the maps `H_i(α)`;
and if `F = G` and `φ` is the identity, all the maps `H_i(α)` are the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem torMap_isLift_properties {M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat R} (F : FreeResolution M₁)
    (G : FreeResolution M₂) (N : ModuleCat R) (φ : M₁ ⟶ M₂) :
    (∀ (α β : F.complex ⟶ G.complex), IsLift F G φ α → IsLift F G φ β → ∀ i,
        torMap F G N α i = torMap F G N β i) ∧
      (IsIso φ → ∀ (α : F.complex ⟶ G.complex), IsLift F G φ α → ∀ i,
        IsIso (torMap F G N α i)) ∧
      (∀ (α : F.complex ⟶ F.complex), IsLift F F (𝟙 M₁) α → ∀ i, torMap F F N α i = 𝟙 _)
declarations.comment: All three assertions: independence of the lift, the isomorphism case, and the identity case (`M₁ = M₂`, `F = G`, `φ = 𝟙`).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.exists_Tor'_one_composableArrows_exact_and_epi
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `M` be an `R`-module and let
`S : 0 → N' → N → N'' → 0` be a short exact sequence of `R`-modules. Then there is a connecting
homomorphism `δ : Tor₁(M, N'') ⟶ M ⊗ N'` making

  `Tor₁(M, N') → Tor₁(M, N) → Tor₁(M, N'') →δ M ⊗ N' → M ⊗ N → M ⊗ N''`

exact, and `M ⊗ N → M ⊗ N''` is surjective. Here `Tor₁(M, -)` is `(Tor' (ModuleCat R) 1).obj M`,
the first left derived functor of `- ⊗ N` evaluated at `M`, and the maps other than `δ` are the
functorial ones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_Tor'_one_composableArrows_exact_and_epi {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)} (hS : S.ShortExact) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (∃ δ : ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj M).obj S.X₃ ⟶ M ⊗ S.X₁,
        (ComposableArrows.mk₅ (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj M).map S.f)
          (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj M).map S.g) δ (M ◁ S.f) (M ◁ S.g)).Exact) ∧
      Epi (M ◁ S.g)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tor.DoubleComplex.statement1
declarations.doc:
For a double complex `A` whose rows are resolutions of the horizontal cokernels and whose
columns are resolutions of the vertical cokernels, there is an isomorphism of `R`-modules
`H_i(R(A)_•) ≅ H_i(U(A)_•)` for every `i ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1 (A : DoubleCx R) (hrow : A.RowResolution) (hcol : A.ColResolution)
    (i : ℕ) : Nonempty (A.RHom i ≃ₗ[R] A.UHom i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tor.DoubleComplex.statement2
declarations.doc:
The isomorphisms `H_i(R(A)_•) ≅ H_i(U(A)_•)` can be chosen naturally in `A`: there is an
assignment, to every double complex `A` satisfying the resolution hypotheses and every `i`, of an
isomorphism `e A : H_i(R(A)_•) ≅ H_i(U(A)_•)`, such that `H_i(U(Ψ)) ∘ e A = e B ∘ H_i(R(Ψ))` for
every morphism `Ψ : A → B` of such double complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2 :
    ∃ e : ∀ (A : DoubleCx R), A.RowResolution → A.ColResolution → ∀ i,
        (A.RHom i ≃ₗ[R] A.UHom i),
      ∀ (A B : DoubleCx R) (hrowA : A.RowResolution) (hcolA : A.ColResolution)
        (hrowB : B.RowResolution) (hcolB : B.ColResolution)
        (Ψ : DCxHom A B) (i : ℕ),
        (Ψ.UHomMap i).comp (e A hrowA hcolA i : A.RHom i →ₗ[R] A.UHom i) =
          ((e B hrowB hcolB i : B.RHom i →ₗ[R] B.UHom i)).comp (Ψ.RHomMap i)

declarations.name: tor_symm_canonically_iso
declarations.doc:
For every `i ≥ 0` the two functors `(M, N) ↦ Tor_i^R(M, N)` and `(M, N) ↦ Tor_i^R(N, M)` are
canonically isomorphic: there is a natural isomorphism between the bifunctor
`Tor (ModuleCat R) i` and the swap bifunctor `(Tor (ModuleCat R) i).flip` in the functor category
`ModuleCat R ⥤ ModuleCat R ⥤ ModuleCat R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tor_symm_canonically_iso (i : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i ≅ (Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).flip)

declarations.name: swap_eigenspace_dim
declarations.doc:
Eigenspace dimensions in characteristic `≠ 2`.
Assume `char k ≠ 2` and `dim_k V = n`. Then the `+1`-eigenspace of the swap
map has dimension `(n^2 + n)/2` and the `-1`-eigenspace has dimension
`(n^2 - n)/2`.

Argument: the `-1`-eigenspace has dimension `(n^2 − n)/2` by
`swap_finrank_antisymm`. Since `E₊₁` and `E₋₁` are complementary
(`swap_isCompl_eigenspaces`), their dimensions add to
`finrank (V ⊗ V) = n * n = n^2` (`Submodule.finrank_add_eq_of_isCompl` and
`Module.finrank_tensorProduct`). The remaining `+1`-dimension is then
`n^2 − (n^2 − n)/2 = (n^2 + n)/2`, a nat-arithmetic identity (both `n^2 ± n`
are even).

This is the eigenvalue count of the example in Stacks, Remark 00M4. The remark itself, about
the self-map of `Tor_0(V, V)` given by the symmetry of Tag 00M3, is
`torSymm_zero_self_ne_one_and_ne_neg_one`, which identifies that self-map with `swapMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem swap_eigenspace_dim
    (hk : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) (hn : Module.finrank k V = n) :
    Module.finrank k (swapEigenspace k V (1 : k)) = (n ^ 2 + n) / 2 ∧
    Module.finrank k (swapEigenspace k V (-1 : k)) = (n ^ 2 - n) / 2
declarations.comment: supporting part: the eigenspace dimensions of the switch map in the example; the Tor statement is torSymm_zero_self_ne_one_and_ne_neg_one

declarations.name: swap_not_isDiagonalizable
declarations.doc:
Non-diagonalizability in characteristic `2`.
Assume `char k = 2` and `dim_k V ≥ 2`. Then the swap map is not
diagonalizable.

Argument: if `σ` were diagonalizable then `⨆ λ, eigenspace λ = ⊤`. But in
characteristic `2` every eigenspace is contained in `eigenspace 1`
(`swap_eigenspace_le_one_char2`), so `⨆ λ, eigenspace λ ≤ eigenspace 1`, whence
`eigenspace 1 = ⊤`, i.e. `σ x = x` for all `x`. This contradicts `swap_ne_id`,
which produces a tensor moved by `σ`.

This is the characteristic `2` sentence of the example in Stacks, Remark 00M4; the remark itself
is `torSymm_zero_self_ne_one_and_ne_neg_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem swap_not_isDiagonalizable
    (hk : (2 : k) = 0) (hn : 2 ≤ Module.finrank k V) :
    ¬ IsDiagonalizable (swapMap k V)
declarations.comment: supporting part: the switch map of the example is not diagonalizable in characteristic 2; the Tor statement is torSymm_zero_self_ne_one_and_ne_neg_one

declarations.name: torSymm_zero_self_ne_one_and_ne_neg_one
declarations.doc:
Stacks, Remark 00M4: for `M = N` the canonical isomorphism of Tag 00M3 gives a self-map of
`Tor_i^R(M, M)`, and this self-map is not the identity, already for `i = 0`; changing its sign
does not help either. Concretely, let `V` be a vector space of dimension at least `2` over a
field `k`. Under `torZeroIso` the self-map of `Tor_0^k(V, V)` given by `torSymm` is the switch
map `swapMap k V` of `V ⊗_k V` (whose eigenspaces have dimensions `(n² + n)/2` and `(n² − n)/2`
in characteristic `≠ 2`, `swap_eigenspace_dim`, and which is not diagonalizable in
characteristic `2`, `swap_not_isDiagonalizable`), and it is neither the identity nor minus the
identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem torSymm_zero_self_ne_one_and_ne_neg_one (k : Type u) [Field k] (V : ModuleCat.{u} k)
    (hn : 2 ≤ Module.finrank k V) :
    (torZeroIso k V V).inv ≫ ((torSymm k 0).hom.app V).app V ≫ (torZeroIso k V V).hom
        = ModuleCat.ofHom (swapMap k V) ∧
      ((torSymm k 0).hom.app V).app V ≠ 𝟙 _ ∧
      ((torSymm k 0).hom.app V).app V ≠ -𝟙 _
declarations.comment: the degree-0 self-map of the 00M3 symmetry on Tor_0(V, V) is the switch map, and is neither 1 nor -1 when dim V ≥ 2

declarations.name: Module.Flat.tfae_isZero_Tor'
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `M` be an `R`-module. The following are equivalent:
(1) `M` is flat over `R`; (2) for all `i > 0` the functor `Tor_i(M, -)` is zero; (3) the functor
`Tor₁(M, -)` is zero; (4) `Tor₁(M, R/I) = 0` for all ideals `I ⊆ R`; (5) `Tor₁(M, R/I) = 0` for
all finitely generated ideals `I ⊆ R`. Here `Tor_i(M, -)` is `(Tor' (ModuleCat R) i).obj M`, the
`i`-th left derived functor of `- ⊗ N` evaluated at `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isZero_Tor' {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    List.TFAE
      [Module.Flat R M,
        ∀ i, 0 < i → IsZero ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj M),
        IsZero ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj M),
        ∀ I : Ideal R,
          IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj M).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))),
        ∀ I : Ideal R, I.FG →
          IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj M).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I)))]

declarations.name: isIso_torBaseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
**Flat base change for `Tor`** (Stacks 00M8). Let `R → R'` be a flat homomorphism of
commutative rings and let `M`, `N` be `R`-modules. Then for every `i` the natural `R'`-linear map
`Tor_i^R(M, N) ⊗_R R' ⟶ Tor_i^{R'}(M ⊗_R R', N ⊗_R R')`, the `R'`-linear extension of the
change-of-rings map of Stacks 00M7 (2), is an isomorphism.

The map `torBaseChangeComparison` is defined for every `R → R'`, from `torBaseChangeMap`;
flatness is used only here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_torBaseChangeComparison [Module.Flat R R'] (i : ℕ) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    IsIso (torBaseChangeComparison R' i M N)

registrations.name: AdicCompletion.map_injective
registrations.comment: (1), and the injectivity half of (2)

registrations.name: AdicCompletion.map_surjective
registrations.comment: (2): surjectivity of the completed second map

registrations.name: AdicCompletion.map_exact
registrations.comment: (2): exactness in the middle of the completed sequence

declarations.name: adicCompletion_shortExact
declarations.doc:
For a Noetherian ring $R$, every short exact sequence $0 \to M' \to M \to M'' \to 0$ of
$R$-modules with $M$ finitely generated completes to a short exact sequence
$0 \to (M')^\wedge \to M^\wedge \to (M'')^\wedge \to 0$.
declarations.statement:
theorem adicCompletion_shortExact {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    {M' M M'' : Type u} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M'']
    {f : M' →ₗ[R] M} {g : M →ₗ[R] M''} (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    Function.Injective (AdicCompletion.map I f) ∧
    Function.Surjective (AdicCompletion.map I g) ∧
    Function.Exact (AdicCompletion.map I f) (AdicCompletion.map I g)

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.faithfullyFlat_of_le_ringJacobson
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `R` and let `R^∧` be the `I`-adic completion of `R`.
If `I` is contained in the Jacobson radical of `R`, then the ring map `R → R^∧` is faithfully flat.
In particular, if `(R, 𝔪)` is a Noetherian local ring, then the completion `lim_n R/𝔪ⁿ` is
faithfully flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem AdicCompletion.faithfullyFlat_of_le_ringJacobson {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Ring.jacobson R) :
    Module.FaithfullyFlat R (AdicCompletion I R)
declarations.comment:
Stated as the class `Module.FaithfullyFlat R (AdicCompletion I R)`, the shape of the
flatness half `AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian`; the `in particular` is the case `I = 𝔪`. See
the module docstring.
