declarations.name: Module.Flat.injective_and_flat_quotient_range_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal_of_isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ME.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings with `S` Noetherian, let
`𝔪` be the maximal ideal of `R`, let `M` be a flat `R`-module, let `N` be a finite `S`-module and
let `u : N → M` be a map of `R`-modules. If the induced map `ū : N/𝔪N → M/𝔪M` is injective, then
`u` is injective and `M/u(N)` is flat over `R`.

Here `N/𝔪N` is `N ⧸ 𝔪 • ⊤` and `ū` is the canonical `Submodule.mapQ`, which sends the class of `x`
to the class of `u x`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem
    Module.Flat.injective_and_flat_quotient_range_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal_of_isNoetherianRing
    {R S N M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [Module.Finite S N]
    (u : N →ₗ[R] M)
    (hu : Function.Injective (Submodule.mapQ (maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R N))
      (maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) u
      (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal R) u))) :
    Function.Injective u ∧ Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range u)
declarations.comment:
`N/𝔪N` is `N ⧸ 𝔪 • (⊤ : Submodule R N)` and `ū` the canonical `Submodule.mapQ` of
`u`. The cokernel `M/u(N)` is `M ⧸ LinearMap.range u`, and the two conclusions are conjoined; see
the module docstring. The non-Noetherian generalization is 046Y.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_and_flat_quotient_span_singleton_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MF.** Let `R → S` be a flat and local ring homomorphism of Noetherian local rings,
let `𝔪` be the maximal ideal of `R`, and let `f ∈ S` be a nonzerodivisor in `S/𝔪S`. Then `f` is a
nonzerodivisor in `S` and `S/fS` is flat over `R`.

Here `S/𝔪S` is the ring quotient `S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)`,
the image of `f` in it is pinned as `Ideal.Quotient.mk`, and `S/fS` is `S ⧸ Ideal.span {f}` with
its canonical `R`-algebra structure; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem
    mem_nonZeroDivisors_and_flat_quotient_span_singleton_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors_maximalIdeal
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Flat R S]
    {f : S}
    (hf : Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) f ∈
      nonZeroDivisors (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    f ∈ nonZeroDivisors S ∧ Module.Flat R (S ⧸ Ideal.span {f})
declarations.comment:
"Nonzerodivisor" is `nonZeroDivisors` at the level of rings, as in the source:
`𝔪S` is `Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)` and `S/fS` is
`S ⧸ Ideal.span {f}`. The two conclusions are conjoined, in the order of the sibling lemmas 00ME
and 046Z rather than the source's. `IsNoetherianRing R` is redundant (faithful flatness descends
the ascending chain condition) but is part of the tag's hypotheses; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.isRegular_and_flat_quotient_ofList_take_of_isRegular_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MG.** Let `R → S` be a flat and local ring homomorphism of Noetherian local rings,
let `𝔪` be the maximal ideal of `R`, and let `f₁, …, f_c` be elements of `S` whose images form a
regular sequence in `S/𝔪S`. Then `f₁, …, f_c` is a regular sequence in `S` and each of the
quotients `S/(f₁, …, f_i)` is flat over `R`.

Here `S/𝔪S` is the ring quotient `S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)`, the
images are pinned as `Ideal.Quotient.mk`, and `S/(f₁, …, f_i)` is `S ⧸ Ideal.ofList (fs.take i)`
with its canonical `R`-algebra structure; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.isRegular_and_flat_quotient_ofList_take_of_isRegular_maximalIdeal
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Flat R S]
    {fs : List S}
    (hfs : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular
      (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))
      (fs.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))))) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular S fs ∧
      ∀ i, Module.Flat R (S ⧸ Ideal.ofList (fs.take i))
declarations.comment:
"Regular sequence" is `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, which is Definition 00LF
verbatim, nonvanishing clause included, and the sequence is a `List S`. The fibre is
`S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)` and `S/(f₁, …, f_i)` is
`S ⧸ Ideal.ofList (fs.take i)`, quantified over all `i : ℕ` since `List.take` saturates.
`IsNoetherianRing R` and `IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)` are both redundant here but are part of the
tag's hypotheses; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.free_and_flat_of_free_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MH.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, let `𝔪` be the
maximal ideal of `R`, and let `M` be a nonzero finite `S`-module. If `M/𝔪M` is a free
`S/𝔪S`-module and `M` is flat over `R`, then `M` is free over `S` and `S` is flat over `R`.

Here `S/𝔪S` is the ring quotient `S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)` and
`M/𝔪M` is the quotient `M ⧸ 𝔪S • (⊤ : Submodule S M)` with its canonical `S/𝔪S`-module structure;
see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_and_flat_of_free_maximalIdeal
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    [Nontrivial M] [Module.Flat R M]
    (hM : Module.Free (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))
      (M ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S M))) :
    Module.Free S M ∧ Module.Flat R S
declarations.comment:
"Nonzero" is `Nontrivial M`. The fibre ring is
`S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)` and `M/𝔪M` is
`M ⧸ 𝔪S • (⊤ : Submodule S M)`, whose `S/𝔪S`-module structure is
`Module.instQuotientIdealSubmoduleHSMulTop`. The two conclusions are conjoined, in the source's
order: `M` is free over `S`, `S` is flat over `R`. `IsNoetherianRing R` is unused but is part of
the tag's hypotheses; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.exactAt_and_flat_cokernel_of_exactAt_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MI.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, let `𝔪` be the
maximal ideal of `R`, and let `0 → F_e → F_{e-1} → ⋯ → F_0` be a finite complex of finite
`S`-modules, presented as a chain complex `C` of `S`-modules with `C.X i = 0` for `i > e`. Assume
that every `F_i` is flat over `R` and that the reduced complex `0 → F_e/𝔪F_e → ⋯ → F_0/𝔪F_0` is
exact. Then `0 → F_e → ⋯ → F_0` is exact, and `Coker(F_1 → F_0)` is flat over `R`.

Reduction modulo `𝔪` is base change along `S → S/𝔪S`, `Coker(F_1 → F_0)` is the categorical
cokernel, and flatness over `R` is flatness after restricting scalars along `algebraMap R S`; see
the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.exactAt_and_flat_cokernel_of_exactAt_maximalIdeal
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max w v} S) ℕ) [∀ i, Module.Finite S (C.X i)] (e : ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ i, e < i → IsZero (C.X i))
    (hflat : ∀ i, Module.Flat R ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (C.X i)))
    (hexact : ∀ i, 0 < i →
      (((ModuleCat.extendScalars
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R)))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj C).ExactAt i) :
    (∀ i, 0 < i → C.ExactAt i) ∧
      Module.Flat R ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (cokernel (C.d 1 0)))
declarations.comment:
The complex is a `ChainComplex (ModuleCat S) ℕ` vanishing above `e`, as in 00N0, so
that `ExactAt e` is the leading `0 →`; exactness is assumed and concluded at every positive index,
which above `e` is automatic. `F_i/𝔪F_i` is the base change
`(S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R)) ⊗[S] F_i` of `ModuleCat.extendScalars`, applied
to `C` as a complex, and `Coker(F_1 → F_0)` is `cokernel (C.d 1 0)`. `IsNoetherianRing R` is
unused but is part of the tag's hypotheses; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.isZero_Tor'_one_of_isFiniteLength
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MJ.** Let `R` be a local ring with residue field `κ` and let `M` be an `R`-module.
If `Tor₁(κ, M) = 0`, then `Tor₁(N, M) = 0` for every `R`-module `N` of finite length. Here
`Tor₁(N, M)` is `((Tor' (ModuleCat R) 1).obj N).obj M`, the first left derived functor of
`- ⊗ M` evaluated at `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_Tor'_one_of_isFiniteLength {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (hM : IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R))).obj M))
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (hN : IsFiniteLength R N) :
    IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj N).obj M)

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_isZero_Tor'_one_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MK** (local criterion for flatness). Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of
Noetherian local rings, let `κ` be the residue field of `R` and let `M` be a finite `S`-module.
If `Tor₁^R(κ, M) = 0`, then `M` is flat over `R`. Here `Tor₁^R(κ, M)` is
`((Tor' (ModuleCat R) 1).obj κ).obj M`, the first left derived functor of `- ⊗_R M` at `κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem of_isZero_Tor'_one_residueField {R : Type u} (S : Type v) (M : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (hTor : IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj
      (ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R))).obj (ModuleCat.of R M))) :
    Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment:
`Tor₁^R(κ, M)` is `Tor'`, the left derived functor of `- ⊗_R M` evaluated at `κ`;
forming it in `ModuleCat R` puts `M` in the universe of `R`.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_rTensor_subtype_injective_of_flat_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ML** (variant of the local criterion for flatness). Let `R → S` be a local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, let `I ≠ R` be an ideal of `R` and let `M` be a finite
`S`-module. If `Tor₁^R(M, R/I) = 0` and `M/IM` is flat over `R/I`, then `M` is flat over `R`.
Here the Tor hypothesis appears in the form of Remark 00M6, as the injectivity of
`I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M`, and `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤` with its canonical `R ⧸ I`-module structure.
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_rTensor_subtype_injective_of_flat_quotient {R : Type u} (S : Type v) (M : Type w)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Finite S M] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≠ ⊤)
    (hTor : Function.Injective (I.subtype.rTensor M))
    (hflat : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))) : Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment:
The hypothesis `Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0` is stated in the form Remark 00M6 identifies
it with, the injectivity of `I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M`; this is the form the source's own second proof
of the lemma assumes, and unlike `Tor_1` it puts `R` and `M` in no common universe. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.TorOneBaseChange.tor_baseChange_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00MM (Lemma 10.99.12).**

Let `R → R' → R''` be ring maps and let `M` be an `R`-module with a chosen projective
resolution `P` over `R`.  If the `R'`-module `M ⊗ᴿ R'` is flat over `R'`, then the
natural base-change map

  `Φ : R'' ⊗_{R'} Tor₁ᴿ(M, R') → Tor₁ᴿ(M, R'')`

(equivalently `Tor₁ᴿ(M, R') ⊗_{R'} R'' → Tor₁ᴿ(M, R'')`), characterized by `phi_apply_mk`,
is surjective. Here `Tor₁ᴿ` is the resolution model `H₁(P ⊗ᴿ -)`; `Φ` is *not* identified
with the canonical base-change natural transformation on derived functors (see the caveat
on `exists_baseChange_eq_phi`).

The reduction to `cycles_baseChange_surjective` runs as follows.
`Tor1 R'' = K''/B''` is a quotient of `K'' = cycles R'' d₁`, so by surjectivity of the
quotient map `Submodule.Quotient.mk` it suffices to hit every class `⟦c⟧` with
`c ∈ K''`.  By the crux `cycles_baseChange_surjective`, `c = cyclesBC z` for some
`z ∈ R'' ⊗_{R'} K'`, where `cyclesBC = AlgebraTensorModule.lift (cyclesMap d₁)`.  Pushing
`z` through `lTensor R'' (mkQ : K' → Tor1 R')` gives an element of `R'' ⊗_{R'} Tor1 R'`,
and the square
  `phi ∘ (id ⊗ mkQ)  =  mkQ'' ∘ cyclesBC`
commutes on generators `r'' ⊗ k` by `phi_apply_mk` (both sides are `⟦cmpBil r'' k⟧`).
Hence `phi (lTensor mkQ z) = mkQ''(cyclesBC z) = ⟦c⟧`, proving surjectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem tor_baseChange_surjective
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (P : ProjectiveResolution M)
    -- flatness hypothesis: `M ⊗ᴿ R'`, as an `R'`-module, is flat over `R'`.
    -- We use `R' ⊗ᴿ M`, the standard Mathlib orientation with `R'` on the left,
    -- which is canonically `R'`-isomorphic to `M ⊗ᴿ R'`.
    (hflat : Module.Flat R' (R' ⊗[R] (M : Type u))) :
    Function.Surjective
      (phi (R := R) (R' := R') (R'' := R'')
        (P.complex.d 2 1).hom (P.complex.d 1 0).hom)
declarations.comment: Proved for the resolution model Tor1 S = H₁(P ⊗ᴿ S); the map is the explicit phi, not identified with the canonical derived base-change natural transformation.

declarations.name: TorSurjective.surjective_on_tor_one_trivial
declarations.doc:
**The Stacks lemma (tag [0BPB]).**  With `N = R'/I'` and `M' = M ⊗_R R'`, the
natural map
  `Tor_1^R(R'/I', M) → Tor_1^{R'}(R'/I', M')`
(constructed via the Stacks data `S`: the pushed-forward `R`-free resolution, the
genuine `R'`-resolution `D` differing only by an added free summand in degree `2`,
and the comparison chain map `φ` that is the identity in degrees `0, 1`) is
**surjective**, i.e. an epimorphism of abelian groups.

Equivalently, the map `naturalMap f S (R'/I')` induced on degree-`1` homology is
an epimorphism (see `surjective_on_tor_one_trivial'`).

Scope of what is proved. `torNaturalMap` is `naturalMap` conjugated by
`Classical.choice` of the `Nonempty` correctness isomorphisms
`naturalMap_src_iso` / `naturalMap_tgt_iso`. Since `Epi` is invariant under
pre- and post-composition with isomorphisms, the epimorphism conclusion between
the genuine Tor objects `torOneRestrict` and `torOneExtend` is real, and the
module `N = quotIdeal f I = R'/IR'` is exactly the module Stacks 00MN is stated
for. What is *not* established is that `torNaturalMap` is the canonical
base-change natural transformation on derived functors: because the two
isomorphisms are extracted by choice, the map is not canonically determined.
Pinning that down requires turning `naturalMap_src_iso` / `naturalMap_tgt_iso`
into `def`s and identifying the composite with a `NatTrans` built independently
of this construction.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_on_tor_one_trivial (I : Ideal R) (M : ModuleCat R)
    (F : ProjectiveResolution M) (S : StacksData f F) :
    Epi (torNaturalMap f S (quotIdeal f I))
declarations.comment: Epi holds between the genuine Tor objects for N = R'/IR', but the comparison map is naturalMap conjugated by Classical.choice isomorphisms, so it is not identified with the canonical derived base-change natural transformation.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_flat_quotient_of_tor_one_map_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MO.** Let `S ← R → R' → S'`, `S → S'` be a commutative square of ring maps with
`R`, `R'`, `S'` local, `R'` and `S'` Noetherian and `R → R'`, `R' → S'` local, let `I ⊆ R` be a
proper ideal, let `M` be a finite `S`-module and let `f : M → M'` be the base change of `M` to an
`S'`-module. Assume `S'` is a localization of `S ⊗_R R'`. If `M/IM` is flat over `R/I` and the
canonical map `Tor_1^R(M, R/I) → Tor_1^{R'}(M', R'/I')` is zero, then `M'` is flat over `R'`.

By Remark 00M6 the source `Tor_1^R(M, R/I)` is `Ker(I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M)` and the target is a
submodule of `I' ⊗_{R'} M'` for `I' = IR'`, so the last hypothesis is that the canonical map
`I ⊗_R M → I' ⊗_{R'} M'`, the unique `R`-linear map with `a ⊗ x ↦ a ⊗ f x`, vanishes on that
kernel; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_flat_quotient_of_tor_one_map_eq_zero {R R' S S' M M' : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing R'] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing R'] [IsNoetherianRing R']
    [IsLocalRing S'] [IsNoetherianRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S']
    [Algebra R' S'] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R' S')]
    [Algebra (S ⊗[R] R') S'] [IsScalarTower S (S ⊗[R] R') S']
    (hR' :
      (algebraMap (S ⊗[R] R') S').comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : R' →ₐ[R] S ⊗[R] R').toRingHom =
        algebraMap R' S')
    (T : Submonoid (S ⊗[R] R')) [IsLocalization T S'] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Finite S M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module S M']
    [Module R' M'] [Module S' M'] [IsScalarTower R S M'] [IsScalarTower R R' M']
    [IsScalarTower S S' M'] [IsScalarTower R' S' M'] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≠ ⊤) (f : M →ₗ[S] M')
    (hf : IsBaseChange S' f) (hflat : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (htor :
      LinearMap.ker (I.subtype.rTensor M) ≤
        LinearMap.ker
          (TensorProduct.lift
            (((TensorProduct.mk R' ↥(I.map (algebraMap R R')) M').restrictScalars₁₂ R R).compl₁₂
              ((Algebra.linearMap R R').restrict (p := I) (q :=
                (I.map (algebraMap R R')).restrictScalars R) fun _ hx => Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hx)
              (f.restrictScalars R)))) :
    Module.Flat R' M'
declarations.comment:
`Tor₁` is spelled through Remark 00M6 as `Ker(I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M)`, and the
hypothesis that `Tor_1^R(M, R/I) → Tor_1^{R'}(M', R'/I')` is zero as the vanishing on that kernel
of the canonical map `I ⊗_R M → I' ⊗_{R'} M'`. `M'` and `S'` are abstract (`IsBaseChange`,
`IsLocalization`). The unused hypotheses `R` Noetherian, `S` local Noetherian, `R → S` local and
`S → S'` local are dropped; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.flat_and_flat_of_flat_quotient_maximalIdeal_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Critère de platitude par fibres, Noetherian local case**. Let `R → S → S'` be local
homomorphisms of Noetherian local rings, let `𝔪 ⊆ R` be the maximal ideal of `R`, and let `M` be an
`S'`-module whose `S`- and `R`-module structures come from the two ring maps. If `M` is finite over
`S'`, nonzero, `M/𝔪M` is flat over `S/𝔪S` and `M` is flat over `R`, then `S` is flat over `R` and
`M` is flat over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.flat_and_flat_of_flat_quotient_maximalIdeal_of_flat
    {R S S' M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsLocalRing S']
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S']
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S S')]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [Module S' M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [IsScalarTower S S' M]
    [Module.Finite S' M] [Nontrivial M]
    [Module.Flat (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
      (M ⧸ ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))]
    [Module.Flat R M] :
    Module.Flat R S ∧ Module.Flat S M
declarations.comment:
The composite `R → S'` is not assumed: the two scalar towers on `M` already pin
the `R`-action to the restriction along `R → S → S'`. `𝔪M` is written as `𝔪S • ⊤` over `S`, so
that the quotient carries the `S/𝔪S`-structure; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.baseChange_and_of_flat_baseChange_of_isPushout_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00MQ**, parts (1) and (2). Let `S ← R → R'` be ring maps, let `T` be the pushout
`S ⊗_R R'`, let `S'` be a localization of `T` at a submonoid `W`, and let `f : M →ₗ[S] M'` realize
`M'` as the base change `S' ⊗_S M` of an `S`-module `M`. Then (1) if `M` is flat over `R` then
`M'` is flat over `R'`, and (2) if moreover `S` and `S'` are local with `S → S'` a local
homomorphism, then `M'` flat over `R'` and `R → R'` flat imply `M` flat over `R`.

Part (1) holds for an arbitrary such square: the source's local rings and local homomorphisms are
used only in part (2), and only for `S`, `S'` and `S → S'`, so they are bound inside the second
conjunct instead of in the signature.

Parts (3) and (4) of the source, that `S` flat over `R` implies `S'` flat over `R'` and that
`R' → S'` and `R → R'` flat imply `S` flat over `R`, are the instance `M := S`, `M' := S'`,
`f := Algebra.linearMap S S'`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChange_and_of_flat_baseChange_of_isPushout_of_isLocalization
    (R : Type*) {S R' T S' M M' : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing T] [CommRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R T] [Algebra S T] [Algebra R' T]
    [IsScalarTower R S T] [IsScalarTower R R' T] [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' T]
    [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra T S']
    [IsScalarTower S T S'] [IsScalarTower R' T S']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module S M'] [Module R' M'] [Module S' M']
    [IsScalarTower S S' M'] [IsScalarTower R' S' M']
    (W : Submonoid T) [IsLocalization W S'] (f : M →ₗ[S] M') (hf : IsBaseChange S' f) :
    (Module.Flat R M → Module.Flat R' M') ∧
      (∀ [IsLocalRing S] [IsLocalRing S'] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S S')],
        Module.Flat R' M' → Module.Flat R R' → Module.Flat R M)
declarations.comment:
Parts (1) and (2). Of the source's eight locality assumptions only `IsLocalRing S`,
`IsLocalRing S'` and `IsLocalHom (algebraMap S S')` are used, by part (2) alone, and they are bound
inside the second conjunct together with `Module.Flat R R'`, so that part (1) is stated for an
arbitrary commutative square; the rest are dropped. "`S'` is a localization of `S ⊗_R R'`" is
`IsLocalization W S'` over an abstract pushout `Algebra.IsPushout R S R' T`, as in the siblings
00P4 and 00RJ, and `M' = S' ⊗_S M` is `IsBaseChange S' f`, as in 00MO. Parts (3) and (4) are the
instance `M := S`, `M' := S'` and are not separate declarations. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: BoundedFreeComplex
declarations.doc:
A complex `0 → R^{n_e} → R^{n_{e-1}} → ⋯ → R^{n_0}` of finite free `R`-modules, as in
Stacks Situation 10.102.1 (tag 00MS). The ranks are given by `n : ℕ → ℕ` with `n i = 0` for
`i > e`, and the differential `R^{n_{i+1}} → R^{n_i}` by the matrix
`φ i : Matrix (Fin (n i)) (Fin (n (i + 1))) R`.
declarations.statement: structure BoundedFreeComplex (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

declarations.name: exists_splitOff_elementaryComplex_of_hasInvertibleCoeff
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring and `C` a complex of finite free `R`-modules `C_j = R^{n_j}`. If the
differential `φ_i` has an invertible matrix coefficient, then `n_i ≥ 1`, `n_{i-1} ≥ 1`, and there
is a complex of finite free `R`-modules `C'` with the ranks decremented at degrees `i` and `i-1`
(and unchanged elsewhere) together with an isomorphism of complexes
`C ≅ C' ⊕ T^{(i)}`, where `T^{(i)}` is the elementary identity complex of `elementaryComplex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_splitOff_elementaryComplex_of_hasInvertibleCoeff {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (C : FreeComplex R) (i : ℤ) (h : HasInvertibleCoeff C i) :
    1 ≤ C.n i ∧ 1 ≤ C.n (i - 1) ∧
    ∃ C' : FreeComplex R,
      (∀ j, C'.n j = if j = i then C.n i - 1 else if j = i - 1 then C.n (i - 1) - 1 else C.n j) ∧
      Nonempty (C.toComplex ≅ C'.toComplex ⊞ (elementaryComplex R i).toComplex)

declarations.name: LinearMap.exists_trivialDecomposition_of_injective_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**An exact complex of finite free modules over an Artinian local ring is a direct sum of
trivial complexes.** Let `R` be an Artinian local ring and let
`0 → R^{n_{e+1}} →[φ e] R^{n_e} → ⋯ → R^{n_1} →[φ 0] R^{n_0}` be a complex of finite free
`R`-modules which is exact at `R^{n_{e+1}}, …, R^{n_1}`. Then there are multiplicities `c j` and
`R`-linear bijections `g i : R^{n_i} ≃ R^{c_i} × R^{c_{i+1}}` in the degrees `i ≤ e + 1`, with
`c (e + 2) = 0`, carrying each differential `φ i` to `(x, y) ↦ (0, x)`; that is, the complex is
isomorphic to the direct sum of `c_j` copies, for each `0 ≤ j ≤ e + 1`, of the trivial complex
with the identity map of `R` in degrees `j` and `j - 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LinearMap.exists_trivialDecomposition_of_injective_of_exact
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (e : ℕ) (n : ℕ → ℕ)
    (φ : ∀ i, (Fin (n (i + 1)) → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin (n i) → R))
    (hφ : ∀ k < e, φ k ∘ₗ φ (k + 1) = 0)
    (htop : Function.Injective (φ e))
    (hex : ∀ k < e, Function.Exact (φ (k + 1)) (φ k)) :
    ∃ (c : ℕ → ℕ) (g : ∀ i, (Fin (n i) → R) →ₗ[R] ((Fin (c i) → R) × (Fin (c (i + 1)) → R))),
      c (e + 2) = 0 ∧ (∀ i ≤ e + 1, Function.Bijective (g i)) ∧
        (∀ i ≤ e, g i ∘ₗ φ i = LinearMap.inr R _ _ ∘ₗ LinearMap.fst R _ _ ∘ₗ g (i + 1))

declarations.name: Stacks.DeterminantalRank.exteriorRank
declarations.doc:
The rank of `φ = mulVecLin A`: the largest `r ≤ min m n` such that the `r`-th exterior
power `⋀^r φ` is nonzero. Since `⋀^r φ = 0` for `r > min m n`, and `⋀^0 φ = id ≠ 0` for
nontrivial `R`, this is the largest `r` with `⋀^r φ ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def exteriorRank (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R) : ℕ

declarations.name: Stacks.DeterminantalRank.detIdeal
declarations.doc:
The determinantal ideal `I(φ)`: the ideal generated by the `rank × rank` minors of `A`.
When `rank = 0` the only minor is the empty minor `det (A.submatrix _ _) = 1`, so `I(φ) = R`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def detIdeal (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R) : Ideal R

declarations.name: StacksComplex.rank_eq_rIndex
declarations.doc:
If the complex is isomorphic to a direct sum of trivial complexes,
then for `1 ≤ i ≤ e` the rank of `φ_i` (which is `d (i-1)`, or equivalently `d k` with
`k = i-1` ranging over `0 ≤ k ≤ e-1`) equals `r_i = ∑_{l=i}^e (-1)^{l-i} n_l`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rank_eq_rIndex (C : Complex R e) (hC : IsoToSumOfTrivials C)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k < e) :
    (rank (C.d k) : ℤ) = rIndex C (k + 1)

declarations.name: StacksComplex.rank_add_rank
declarations.doc:
If the complex is isomorphic to a direct sum of trivial complexes, then for `1 ≤ i ≤ e-1`,
`rank(φ_{i+1}) + rank(φ_i) = n_i`. In the indexing `d j = φ_{j+1}`, with `k = i-1`
ranging over `0 ≤ k ≤ e-2`, this reads `rank (d (k+1)) + rank (d k) = n (k+1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rank_add_rank (C : Complex R e) (hC : IsoToSumOfTrivials C)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k + 1 < e) :
    rank (C.d (k + 1)) + rank (C.d k) = C.n (k + 1)

declarations.name: StacksComplex.minorIdeal_eq_top
declarations.doc:
If the complex is isomorphic to a direct sum of trivial complexes, then for `1 ≤ i ≤ e`,
the ideal `I(φ_i)` is the unit ideal `R`. In the indexing `d k = φ_{k+1}` with `0 ≤ k ≤ e-1`,
this is `I(d k) = ⊤`.
declarations.statement:
theorem minorIdeal_eq_top (C : Complex R e) (hC : IsoToSumOfTrivials C)
    (k : ℕ) :
    minorIdeal (C.d k) = ⊤

declarations.name: exists_trivial_iso_of_exact
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal `m` is an associated prime of `R`, i.e.
`R` has depth `0`. Then every complex of finite free `R`-modules
`0 → R^{n_e} → ⋯ → R^{n_0}` which is exact at `R^{n_e}, …, R^{n_1}` is isomorphic to a complex
of the same length and ranks all of whose differentials are partial permutation matrices, that
is, to a direct sum of trivial complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_trivial_iso_of_exact
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hdepth : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ∈ associatedPrimes R R)
    (C : BoundedFreeComplex R) (hC : C.Exact) :
    ∃ D : BoundedFreeComplex R, ∃ _ : C.Iso D,
      D.e = C.e ∧ (∀ i, D.n i = C.n i) ∧ D.IsTrivial

declarations.name: tag_00MZ
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal `m`, and let
`φ : R^{n (•+1)} → R^{n •}` be a complex of finite free modules ending at position
`e` (so `n (e+1) = 0`).  If the complex is exact at positions `1, ..., e` and
`x ∈ m` is a nonzerodivisor of `R`, then the reduced complex `φ mod x` is exact at
positions `2, ..., e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tag_00MZ (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (e : ℕ) (n : ℕ → ℕ)
    (φ : (i : ℕ) → Matrix (Fin (n i)) (Fin (n (i + 1))) R)
    (hcomplex : IsMatrixComplex n φ)
    (x : R)
    (hxnzd : ∀ r : R, x * r = 0 → r = 0)
    (hexact : ∀ i, i < e → ExactAtSucc n φ i) :
    ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i < e → ExactAtSucc n (reduceMat x n φ) i

declarations.name: Module.one_le_depth_homology_of_forall_le_depth_of_isGreatest_not_exactAt
declarations.doc:
**Acyclicity lemma.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and let
`0 → M_e → M_{e-1} → ⋯ → M_0` be a complex of finite `R`-modules, presented as a chain complex
`C` of `R`-modules with `C.X j = 0` for `j > e`. Assume `depth(M_i) ≥ i` for `i ≤ e`. If `i` is
the largest index at which `C` fails to be exact and `i > 0`, then
`Ker(M_i → M_{i-1})/Im(M_{i+1} → M_i)` has depth at least `1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.one_le_depth_homology_of_forall_le_depth_of_isGreatest_not_exactAt
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℕ) [∀ j, Module.Finite R (C.X j)] (e : ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ j, e < j → IsZero (C.X j))
    (hdepth : ∀ j ≤ e, (j : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (C.X j))
    {i : ℕ} (hi : IsGreatest {j : ℕ | ¬ C.ExactAt j} i) (hi0 : 0 < i) :
    1 ≤ Module.depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (C.homology i)

declarations.name: LinearMap.injective_and_exact_iff_forall_rank_eq_and_le_depth_minors
declarations.doc:
**Buchsbaum–Eisenbud exactness criterion.** A complex
`0 → R^{n_{e+1}} →[φ e] R^{n_e} → ⋯ → R^{n_1} →[φ 0] R^{n_0}` of finite free modules over a
local Noetherian ring is exact at `R^{n_{e+1}}, …, R^{n_1}` if and only if, for every `k ≤ e`,
the rank of `φ k` — the largest `r` with `⋀^r (φ k) ≠ 0` — is the alternating sum
`n_{k+1} - n_{k+2} + ⋯ ± n_{e+1}`, and the ideal generated by the `r × r` minors of the matrix
of `φ k` has depth at least `k + 1`, that is, it is `R` or contains a regular sequence of
length `k + 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LinearMap.injective_and_exact_iff_forall_rank_eq_and_le_depth_minors
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (e : ℕ) (n : ℕ → ℕ)
    (φ : ∀ i, (Fin (n (i + 1)) → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin (n i) → R))
    (hφ : ∀ k < e, φ k ∘ₗ φ (k + 1) = 0) :
    (Function.Injective (φ e) ∧ ∀ k < e, Function.Exact (φ (k + 1)) (φ k)) ↔
      ∀ k ≤ e, ∃ r : ℕ,
        (r : ℤ) = ∑ t ∈ Finset.range (e + 1 - k), (-1) ^ t * (n (k + 1 + t) : ℤ) ∧
        IsGreatest {j : ℕ | exteriorPower.map j (φ k) ≠ 0} r ∧
        ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (Ideal.span {x : R |
          ∃ (ρ : Fin r → Fin (n k)) (γ : Fin r → Fin (n (k + 1))),
            ((LinearMap.toMatrix' (φ k)).submatrix ρ γ).det = x}) R

declarations.name: Module.IsCohenMacaulayAtMaximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Cohen–Macaulay module over a local ring.** A module `M` over a local ring `(R, 𝔪)` is
*Cohen–Macaulay* if the dimension of its support equals its depth,
`dim(Supp(M)) = depth_𝔪(M)`, the equality being read in `WithBot ℕ∞` where `Module.supportDim`
lives.
declarations.statement:
public def Module.IsCohenMacaulayAtMaximalIdeal (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop
declarations.comment: Stated without the Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses, as in tags 00LI, 00NF and 0AAH; the equation is oriented `depth_𝔪(M) = dim Supp(M)`, the spelling of Cohen–Macaulayness already used by tags 00LK, 00NF, 0AAG, 0AAH and 0C6G. The name records that the depth is taken at the maximal ideal, `Module.IsCohenMacaulay` being Definition 0AAH for a not necessarily local ring. See the module docstring.

registrations.name: IsCohenMacaulayModule
registrations.comment: the definition of a Cohen-Macaulay module

declarations.name: isCohenMacaulayModule_quotient_of_isGoodElement
declarations.doc:
(Stacks 00N4, Lemma 10.103.2.) Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring with maximal
ideal `m`, let `M` be a Cohen-Macaulay finite `R`-module, and let `f_1, ..., f_d ∈ m`
(here `d = f.length`) be an `M`-regular sequence with `d = dim(Supp(M))`. Assume
`d ≥ 1` and let `g ∈ m` be good with respect to `(M, f_1, ..., f_d)`. Then:
(a) `g` is a nonzerodivisor on `M`;
(b) `M/gM` is Cohen-Macaulay, the images of `f_1, ..., f_{d-1}` form an
    `(M/gM)`-regular sequence, and this sequence is maximal, equivalently
    `dim(Supp(M/gM)) = depth(M/gM) = d - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulayModule_quotient_of_isGoodElement {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] {M : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayModule R M)
    (f : List R) (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M f)
    (hfm : ∀ x ∈ f, x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hd : (f.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = Module.supportDim R M) (hd1 : 1 ≤ f.length) (g : R)
    (hg : g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hgood : IsGoodElement M f g) :
    -- (a) g is a nonzerodivisor on M
    IsSMulRegular M g ∧
      -- (b) M/gM is Cohen-Macaulay
      IsCohenMacaulayModule R (M ⧸ (Ideal.span {g}) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ∧
      -- the images of f_1, ..., f_{d-1} form an (M/gM)-regular sequence
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (M ⧸ (Ideal.span {g}) • (⊤ : Submodule R M))
        (f.take (f.length - 1)) ∧
      -- maximality: dim(Supp(M/gM)) = depth(M/gM) = d - 1 (the depth equality is the
      -- Cohen-Macaulay conclusion above; here we record the common value is d - 1)
      Module.supportDim R (M ⧸ (Ideal.span {g}) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) =
        ((f.length - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: isSMulRegular_and_isCohenMacaulayModule_quotSMulTop_of_supportDim_drop
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00N5.** Let `M` be a Cohen-Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring `R`, of
support dimension `e ≥ 1`, and let `g ∈ m` be such that
`dim (Supp M ∩ V(g)) = dim (Supp M) - 1`, i.e. `dim (Supp (M/gM)) = e - 1`. Then

* (a) `g` is a nonzerodivisor on `M`, and
* (b) `M/gM` is Cohen-Macaulay, of depth one less than the depth of `M`.

The hypothesis `1 ≤ e` is the Stacks hypothesis that the dimension actually drops: `e - 1` is
truncated subtraction in `ℕ`, and for `e = 0` the displayed condition of the source has no
solutions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSMulRegular_and_isCohenMacaulayModule_quotSMulTop_of_supportDim_drop
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayModule R M)
    (e : ℕ) (he : Module.supportDim R M = ((e : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hpos : 1 ≤ e)
    {g : R} (hg : g ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hdrop : Module.supportDim R (QuotSMulTop g M) = (((e - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    IsSMulRegular M g ∧ IsCohenMacaulayModule R (QuotSMulTop g M) ∧
      Module.depthSup R (maximalIdeal R) (QuotSMulTop g M) + 1
        = Module.depthSup R (maximalIdeal R) M

declarations.name: cohenMacaulay_regularSequence_extend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00N6 (Proposition 10.103.4).**
Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal `m`, and let `M` be a finite,
nonzero, Cohen-Macaulay `R`-module with `dim(Supp(M)) = d`. If `g_1, ..., g_c ∈ m`
(here `gs`, with `gs.length = c` and `c ≤ d`) satisfy
`dim(Supp(M/(g_1,...,g_c)M)) = d - c`, then:
1. `gs` is an `M`-regular sequence, and
2. `gs` extends to a maximal `M`-regular sequence of length `d` (`= depth M`): there is
   a list `gs'` of elements of `m` with `(gs ++ gs').length = d` such that `gs ++ gs'`
   is a maximal `M`-regular sequence.

The hypothesis `dim(Supp(M)) = d` with `d : ℕ` already forces `M ≠ 0` (since
`dim(Supp(0)) = ⊥`); this is recorded by `[Nontrivial M]`. The hypothesis `hcd : c ≤ d`
ensures the truncated subtraction `(d - c : ℕ)` agrees with the intended integer `d - c`,
which is forced to be nonnegative by the mathematical hypothesis on dimensions.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohenMacaulay_regularSequence_extend
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (d c : ℕ) (hcd : c ≤ d) (hd : Module.supportDim R M = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulay R M)
    (gs : List R) (hgs_len : gs.length = c)
    (hgs_mem : ∀ g ∈ gs, g ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hdim : Module.supportDim R (M ⧸ (Ideal.ofList gs • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))
      = ((d - c : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    IsRegular M gs ∧
    ∃ gs' : List R, (∀ g ∈ gs', g ∈ maximalIdeal R) ∧
      (gs ++ gs').length = d ∧
      IsMaximalRegularSequence R M (gs ++ gs')

declarations.name: IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local ring `R` is called *Cohen–Macaulay* if it is
Cohen–Macaulay as a module over itself.
declarations.statement:
def IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] :
    Prop

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.length_eq_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Maximal chains of primes in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local
Cohen–Macaulay ring, that is `depth_𝔪(R) = dim(R)`. Then every maximal chain of primes of `R` —
one whose steps are covering pairs `𝔭_i ⋖ 𝔭_{i + 1}`, starting at a minimal prime and ending at
the maximal ideal — has length `dim(R)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.length_eq_ringKrullDim
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R)
    (s : RelSeries {(p, q) : PrimeSpectrum R × PrimeSpectrum R | p ⋖ q})
    (hmin : IsMin s.head) (hmax : IsMax s.last) :
    (s.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of the Noetherian local ring `R` is the predicate
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R` (Definition 00N8, i.e. `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R`); a maximal chain
of primes is a `RelSeries` for the covering relation `⋖` on `PrimeSpectrum R` whose head is
minimal and whose last is maximal; the source's name `d` for `dim R` is dropped. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.ringKrullDim_eq_height_add_ringKrullDim_quotient
declarations.doc:
**The dimension formula in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring.** If `R` is a Noetherian local
Cohen–Macaulay ring, that is `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R`, then every prime `𝔭` of `R` satisfies
`dim R = dim R_𝔭 + dim R/𝔭`, the dimension of the localisation `R_𝔭` being written as the
height of `𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.ringKrullDim_eq_height_add_ringKrullDim_quotient
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ringKrullDim R = p.height + ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p)
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of `R` is the hypothesis `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R`,
i.e. `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R` (Definition 00N8); `dim(R_𝔭)` is written `𝔭.height`; the source's name
`d` for `dim R` is dropped.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.of_isLocalization_atPrime
declarations.doc:
**Cohen–Macaulayness localizes at a prime.** If `R` is a Noetherian local Cohen–Macaulay
ring, that is `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R`, then for every prime `𝔭` of `R` the local ring `R_𝔭` is
Cohen–Macaulay: `depth_{𝔭R_𝔭}(R_𝔭) = dim R_𝔭`. The localization is any `R`-algebra `Rₚ` with
`IsLocalization.AtPrime Rₚ p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.of_isLocalization_atPrime {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R) (p : Ideal R)
    [p.IsPrime] (Rₚ : Type*) [CommRing Rₚ] [Algebra R Rₚ] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rₚ p]
    [IsLocalRing Rₚ] : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay Rₚ Rₚ
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of a Noetherian local ring is the predicate
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay S S`, i.e. `depth_{𝔪_S}(S) = dim S` (Definition 00N8); the
localization is an abstract `IsLocalization.AtPrime`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsCohenMacaulayRing
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring `R` is *Cohen–Macaulay* if every localisation `R_𝔭` at a
prime ideal `𝔭` is a Cohen–Macaulay local ring.
declarations.statement: def IsCohenMacaulayRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.of_isLocalization_atPrime_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**A polynomial algebra over a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is Cohen–Macaulay.** Let `R` be
a Noetherian ring all of whose local rings `R_𝔭` are Cohen–Macaulay, and let `σ` be finite. Then
for every prime `𝔮` of `R[x_i : i ∈ σ]`, every localization `S` of `R[x_i : i ∈ σ]` at `𝔮` is a
Cohen–Macaulay local ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.of_isLocalization_atPrime_mvPolynomial {R : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (hR :
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime p))
    {σ : Type*} [Finite σ] (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ R)) [q.IsPrime] (S : Type*) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial σ R) S] [IsLocalization.AtPrime S q] [IsLocalRing S] :
    Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay S S
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of a Noetherian local ring is `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay S S`
(Definition 00N8); that of a Noetherian ring (Definition 00NC) is spelled out as a condition on
its localizations at primes, the hypothesis at the concrete `Localization.AtPrime` and the
conclusion at an abstract `IsLocalization.AtPrime`; `R[x_1, …, x_n]` is `MvPolynomial σ R` for
finite `σ`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.depth_lt_depth_or_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Depth of a syzygy module over a Cohen–Macaulay local ring.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian
local Cohen–Macaulay ring, that is `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R`, let `F` be a finite free `R`-module and
let `0 → K → F → M → 0` be a short exact sequence of `R`-modules, given by `f : K →ₗ[R] F`
injective, `g : F →ₗ[R] M` surjective and `Function.Exact f g`, with `M` nonzero. Then either
`depth_𝔪(M) < depth_𝔪(K)`, or `depth_𝔪(K) = depth_𝔪(M) = dim R`, i.e. both `K` and `M` are
maximal Cohen–Macaulay.

The source states the third alternative as `depth(K) = depth(M) = d` and the middle term as
`R^{⊕n}`, and lists `M = 0` as a first alternative in place of the hypothesis
`[Nontrivial M]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.depth_lt_depth_or_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_of_exact
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hR : IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R) {K F M : Type*} [AddCommGroup K] [Module R K]
    [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] [Module.Free R F] [Module.Finite R F] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Nontrivial M] {f : K →ₗ[R] F} {g : F →ₗ[R] M} (h : Function.Exact f g)
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    depth R (maximalIdeal R) M < depth R (maximalIdeal R) K ∨
      (IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R K ∧ IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R M)
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of the Noetherian local ring `R` is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R`, i.e. `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R` (Definition 00N8); `R^{⊕n}` is an
arbitrary finite free module `F`; the alternative `M = 0` is the hypothesis `[Nontrivial M]`;
and `depth(K) = depth(M) = d` is maximal Cohen-Macaulayness of `K` and of `M`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Maximal Cohen–Macaulay module.** A module `M` over a local ring `(R, 𝔪)` is *maximal
Cohen–Macaulay* if its depth along `𝔪` equals the Krull dimension of `R`,
`depth_𝔪(M) = dim(R)`, which for `R` Noetherian is the largest value the depth of a nonzero
finite `R`-module can take. The
source states this for `R` Noetherian and `M` finite; neither hypothesis is needed to state the
condition, so both are left to the lemmas, and under them this is the source's condition. The
depth is that of Tag 00LI, so the zero module has depth `∞` and, `dim(R)` being finite for a
Noetherian local ring, is not maximal Cohen–Macaulay, as in the source.
declarations.statement:
public def Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop
declarations.comment: Stated without the Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses, which the lemmas assume where needed; under them this is the source's condition, with the depth of Tag 00LI. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.exists_composableArrows_exact_free_and_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_left
declarations.doc:
**Finite free complexes with a maximal Cohen–Macaulay kernel.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian
local Cohen–Macaulay ring, that is `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R`, of dimension `d`, and let `M` be a
finite `R`-module of depth `e`. Then there is an exact complex

  `0 → K → F_{d-e-1} → ⋯ → F₀ → M → 0`

of `R`-modules with the `d - e` modules `Fᵢ` finite free and `K` maximal Cohen–Macaulay. The
complex is a `ComposableArrows (ModuleCat R) (d - e + 1)` with rightmost object `M`, whose
exactness at the interior objects `Fᵢ` is `S.Exact` and whose outer two exactness conditions are
`Mono (S.map' 0 1)` and `Epi (S.map' (d - e) (d - e + 1))`; the module `K` is its leftmost
object `S.left`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_composableArrows_exact_free_and_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_left {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R M] {d e : ℕ} (hd : ringKrullDim R = d)
    (he : Module.depth R (maximalIdeal R) M = e) :
    ∃ S : ComposableArrows (ModuleCat.{u} R) (d - e + 1),
      S.right = M ∧ S.Exact ∧ Mono (S.map' 0 1) ∧ Epi (S.map' (d - e) (d - e + 1)) ∧
        (∀ i, Module.Finite R (S.obj i)) ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < d - e), Module.Free R (S.obj' (i + 1))) ∧
        Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R S.left
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of the Noetherian local ring `R` is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R`, i.e. `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R` (Definition 00N8); the complex is a
`ComposableArrows (ModuleCat R) (d - e + 1)` whose rightmost object is `M`, its interior exactness
being `Exact` and the outer two conditions `Mono` and `Epi` as in `ShortComplex.ShortExact`. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: Ring.IsCatenary
declarations.doc:
A commutative ring `R` is **catenary** if for every pair of prime ideals `p ⊆ q` there is an
integer bounding the lengths of the finite chains of primes from `p` to `q`, and all non-refinable
such chains have the same length. Chains are `LTSeries` in `PrimeSpectrum R`, and
non-refinability of a chain with fixed endpoints is the condition that each of its steps be a
covering pair `⋖`.
declarations.statement: public def Ring.IsCatenary (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: localization_isCatenary
declarations.doc: A localization of a catenary ring is catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_isCatenary
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization S A]
    (h : IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum R)) :
    IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum A)
declarations.comment: first part, stated for catenarity of the spectrum

declarations.name: localization_isUniversallyCatenary
declarations.doc: A localization of a Noetherian universally catenary ring is universally catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_isUniversallyCatenary
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (S : Submonoid R)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization S A]
    (h : IsUniversallyCatenary R) :
    IsUniversallyCatenary A
declarations.comment: second part

declarations.name: Ring.isCatenary_and_isUniversallyCatenary_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a multiplicative subset of a ring `R` and `A = S⁻¹R`. If `R` is catenary, then so
is `A`; if `R` is Noetherian and universally catenary, then `A` is Noetherian and universally
catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenary_and_isUniversallyCatenary_of_isLocalization {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (S : Submonoid R) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization S A] :
    (IsCatenary R → IsCatenary A) ∧
      (IsNoetherianRing R → IsUniversallyCatenary R →
        IsNoetherianRing A ∧ IsUniversallyCatenary A)

declarations.name: Ring.isCatenary_and_isUniversallyCatenary_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
If `f : A →+* B` is surjective, then `B` is catenary if `A` is, and `B` is universally catenary
if `A` is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ring.isCatenary_and_isUniversallyCatenary_of_surjective {A B : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] {f : A →+* B} (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (Ring.IsCatenary A → Ring.IsCatenary B) ∧
      (Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary A → Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary B)

declarations.name: Ring.IsCatenary.of_surjective
declarations.doc: If `f : A →+* B` is surjective and `A` is catenary, then so is `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ring.IsCatenary.of_surjective {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    {f : A →+* B} (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hA : Ring.IsCatenary A) : Ring.IsCatenary B

declarations.name: Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary.of_surjective
declarations.doc: If `f : A →+* B` is surjective and `A` is universally catenary, then so is `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary.of_surjective {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    {f : A →+* B} (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hA : Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary A) :
    Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary B

declarations.name: Ring.IsUniversallyCatenaryNoetherian
declarations.doc:
A ring `R` is **universally catenary** if `R` is Noetherian and every `R`-algebra of finite
type is catenary. The finite-type algebras range over the universe of `R`; this is no restriction,
since every finite-type `R`-algebra is isomorphic to a quotient of a polynomial ring
`R[X₁, …, Xₙ]` (`Ring.isUniversallyCatenary_iff_forall_finiteType`).
declarations.statement: public def Ring.IsUniversallyCatenaryNoetherian (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop
declarations.comment: Noetherianity is a conjunct of the definition, as in the source

declarations.name: Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary.of_isCohenMacaulay_of_support_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**A Noetherian ring with a Cohen–Macaulay module of full support is universally catenary.**
If `R` is Noetherian and `M` is a finite Cohen–Macaulay `R`-module (Definition 0AAH) with
`Supp(M) = Spec(R)`, then every `R`-algebra of finite type is catenary. Taking `M = R`, where the
support condition is automatic, this says that a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is universally
catenary. The universes of `R` and `M` are independent: the localisations the hypothesis speaks
of are named inside Definition 0AAH, which puts `M_𝔭` in `Type (max u v)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary.of_isCohenMacaulay_of_support_eq_univ {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (hM : Module.IsCohenMacaulay R M)
    (hsupp : Module.support R M = Set.univ) :
    Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary R
declarations.comment:
The source's `M` Cohen-Macaulay with `Supp(M) = Spec(R)` is
`Module.IsCohenMacaulay R M` (Definition 0AAH) together with `Module.support R M = Set.univ`, the
spelling of the companion Tag 0AAE; the Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses, which the source keeps
inside Definitions 00N3 and 0AAH, are assumed explicitly; and the first sentence of the tag is the
case `M = R`, where the support condition holds for every ring. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.gradedRing_maximalIdeal_isPolynomialAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00NO, in the form of a graded-ring isomorphism.** Let `(R, 𝔪, κ)` be a regular local
ring of dimension `d` and let `xs = x_1, …, x_d` be a minimal set of generators of `𝔪`, that is, a
list generating `𝔪` whose length is the minimal number of generators of `𝔪` (which equals `dim R`).
Then the canonical map of graded rings
`κ[X_1, …, X_d] → ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝔪^n/𝔪^(n+1)`, `X_i ↦ x_i mod 𝔪^2`,
is bijective (first clause) and carries the homogeneous polynomials of degree `n` onto the
degree-`n` part `𝔪^n/𝔪^(n+1)` (second clause). Together: the graded ring
`⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝔪^n/𝔪^(n+1)` is the graded polynomial algebra `κ[X_1, …, X_d]` over the residue
field, as graded rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gradedRing_maximalIdeal_isPolynomialAlgebra
    (hxs : Ideal.ofList xs = maximalIdeal R)
    (hmin : xs.length = (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank)
    (hx : ∀ i : Fin xs.length, xs[i] ∈ maximalIdeal R) :
    Function.Bijective
        (AssociatedGraded.polyGradedHom (maximalIdeal R) (fun i : Fin xs.length => xs[i]) hx) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : AssociatedGraded.gradedRing (maximalIdeal R)),
        y ∈ AssociatedGraded.grading (maximalIdeal R) n ↔
          ∃ p : MvPolynomial (Fin xs.length) (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R), p.IsHomogeneous n ∧
            AssociatedGraded.polyGradedHom (maximalIdeal R)
              (fun i : Fin xs.length => xs[i]) hx p = y
declarations.comment: The graded-RING form: the canonical ring map `κ[X_1, …, X_d] → ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝔪^n/𝔪^(n+1)`, `X_i ↦ x_i mod 𝔪^2`, of a minimal generating sequence of the maximal ideal is bijective, and carries the degree-`n` homogeneous polynomials exactly onto `𝔪^n/𝔪^(n+1)`; that is the source's isomorphism of the graded ring with the graded polynomial algebra, with the isomorphism pinned to the source's own map rather than merely asserted. See also `IsRegularLocalRing.isQuasiRegular` for the graded-module form (Tag 061N/061P).

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.isQuasiRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00NO.** Let `(R, m, κ)` be a regular local ring of dimension `d` and let
`xs = x_1, …, x_d` be a minimal set of generators of `m`, that is, a list generating `m` whose
length is the minimal number of generators of `m` (which equals `dim R`). Then `xs` is a
quasi-regular sequence: the canonical map of graded `κ[X_1, …, X_d]`-modules
`κ[X_1, …, X_d] ⊗_κ (R/m) → ⨁_{n ≥ 0} m^n/m^(n + 1)`, `X^e ⊗ 1 ↦ x^e mod m^(|e| + 1)`, is
bijective. Equivalently, the graded ring `⨁_{n ≥ 0} m^n/m^(n + 1)` is the graded polynomial
algebra `κ[X_1, …, X_d]` over the residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.isQuasiRegular {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R]
    (xs : List R) (hxs : Ideal.ofList xs = maximalIdeal R)
    (hmin : xs.length = (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular R xs
declarations.comment: Stated as quasi-regularity (Tag 061P) of a minimal generating sequence of the maximal ideal, which is exactly the assertion that the source's graded surjection `κ[X_1, …, X_d] → ⨁ m^n/m^(n+1)`, `X_i ↦ x_i mod m^2`, is an isomorphism. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.isDomain
declarations.doc:
**A regular local ring is a domain.** If the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring `R` can
be generated by `dim R` elements, then `R` has no zero divisors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.isDomain (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] :
    IsDomain R

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.isWeaklyRegular_of_span_range_eq_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Two generators of the maximal ideal of a regular local ring of dimension two form a regular
sequence.** A family of two elements spanning `𝔪` has the minimal length
`(𝔪).spanFinrank = dim A = 2`, so Tag 00NQ applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyRegular_of_span_range_eq_maximalIdeal (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (x : Fin 2 → A)
    (hspan : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A = Ideal.span (Set.range x)) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular A [x 0, x 1]
declarations.comment: for a two-dimensional regular local ring and a two-element generating family of the maximal ideal

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.isRegular_and_isRegularLocalRing_quotient_and_isMaximalCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**A minimal set of generators of the maximal ideal of a regular local ring is a regular
sequence.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a regular local ring. Then every list `xs = x₁, …, x_d` generating
`𝔪` of the minimal length `d = (𝔪).spanFinrank` is a regular sequence on `R`, and each initial
quotient `R/(x₁, …, x_c)` is a regular local ring of dimension `d - c`; in particular `R` is
Cohen-Macaulay, that is, maximal Cohen-Macaulay over itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_and_isRegularLocalRing_quotient_and_isMaximalCohenMacaulay
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] :
    (∀ xs : List R, Ideal.ofList xs = maximalIdeal R →
        xs.length = (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank →
        RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R xs ∧
          ∀ c ≤ xs.length, IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (xs.take c)) ∧
            ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (xs.take c)) + c = ringKrullDim R) ∧
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R
declarations.comment: Cohen-Macaulayness is the named predicate `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R` (Definition 00NF), the equality `depth_𝔪(R) = dim R`; the minimal generating sequence is bound inside the clause that uses it, so the `in particular` is a statement about `R` alone. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.exists_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_length_eq_spanFinrank_and_ofList_take_eq
declarations.doc:
**An ideal of a regular local ring with regular quotient is generated by part of a minimal
set of generators of the maximal ideal.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a regular local ring and let `I` be an
ideal of `R` such that `R ⧸ I` is a regular local ring as well. Then there is a list
`xs = x₁, …, x_d` generating `𝔪` of the minimal length `d = (𝔪).spanFinrank` and a `c ≤ d` with
`I = (x₁, …, x_c)`; moreover `dim (R ⧸ I) + c = dim R`, i.e. `c = dim R - dim (R ⧸ I)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_length_eq_spanFinrank_and_ofList_take_eq
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ I)) :
    ∃ xs : List R, Ideal.ofList xs = maximalIdeal R ∧
      xs.length = (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank ∧
      ∃ c ≤ xs.length, Ideal.ofList (xs.take c) = I ∧
        ringKrullDim (R ⧸ I) + c = ringKrullDim R
declarations.comment: A minimal set of generators of `𝔪` is a list generating it whose length is `(𝔪).spanFinrank`, and `(x₁, …, x_c)` is the ideal generated by the length-`c` prefix of that list, as in Tag 00NQ. The source's existentially bound `c` is pinned by the dimension equation `dim (R ⧸ I) + c = dim R` proved along with it. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: free_mod_x
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00NS.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal
`m`, and let `x ∈ m`. Let `M` be a finite `R`-module on which `x` is a
nonzerodivisor and such that `M / xM` is free over `R / xR`. Then `M` is free
over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_mod_x
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (x : R) (hx : x ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hnzd : IsSMulRegular M x)
    (hfree : Module.Free (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})
      (M ⧸ (Ideal.span {x} • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))) :
    Module.Free R M

declarations.name: regular_mcm_free
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 00NT (Lemma 10.106.6): over a regular local ring, any nonzero
finitely generated maximal Cohen-Macaulay module is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_mcm_free
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    (hM : IsMaxCM R M) : Module.Free R M

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00NU**, regular sequence case. Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, and
`rs` a regular sequence such that `R / (rs)` is a regular local ring. Then `R` is a
regular local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_isRegular (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherian R R]
    (rs : List R) (hrs : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R rs)
    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList rs)) :
    IsRegularLocalRing R
declarations.comment: regular sequence

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_of_nonZeroDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00NU**, single nonzerodivisor case. Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring,
and `x` a nonzerodivisor such that `R / xR` is a regular local ring. Then `R` is a
regular local ring.

This is the special case `rs = [x]` of `isRegularLocalRing_of_isRegular`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_nonZeroDivisor (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherian R R]
    (x : R) (hx : x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})) :
    IsRegularLocalRing R
declarations.comment: single element

declarations.name: Module.IsLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
`M` is a **locally free** `R`-module: there is a family `f : ι → R` whose
basic opens cover `Spec R` (equivalently, generate the unit ideal) and such that
each localization `M_{f i}` is a free `R_{f i}`-module.
declarations.statement:
def Module.IsLocallyFree (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.IsFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
`M` is a **finite locally free** `R`-module: as above, but each localization
`M_{f i}` is in addition finitely generated (hence finite free) over `R_{f i}`.
declarations.statement:
def Module.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
`M` is **finite locally free of rank `r`**: there is a covering family
`f : ι → R` of `Spec R` such that each localization `M_{f i}` is free of rank `r`
over `R_{f i}`, i.e. has a basis indexed by `Fin r`.
declarations.statement:
def Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (r : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: Module.finite_projective_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Characterizations of finite projective modules.** For a module `M` over a commutative ring
`R` the following are equivalent: (1) `M` is finitely presented and flat; (2) `M` is finite
projective; (3) `M` is a direct summand of a finite free module; (4) `M` is finitely presented and
free at every prime; (5) `M` is finitely presented and free at every maximal ideal; (6) `M` is
finite and locally free; (7) `M` is finite locally free; (8) `M` is finite, free at every prime,
and its rank function `ρ_M = Module.rankAtStalk M` is locally constant on `Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.finite_projective_tfae (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    List.TFAE
      [Module.FinitePresentation R M ∧ Module.Flat R M,
       Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M,
       ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (g : M →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)), f ∘ₗ g = LinearMap.id,
       Module.FinitePresentation R M ∧ Module.freeLocus R M = Set.univ,
       Module.FinitePresentation R M ∧ ∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) (_ : 𝔪.IsMaximal),
         Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪) (LocalizedModule 𝔪.primeCompl M),
       Module.Finite R M ∧ ∃ s : Set R, Ideal.span s = ⊤ ∧
         ∀ f ∈ s, Module.Free (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M),
       ∃ s : Set R, Ideal.span s = ⊤ ∧ ∀ f ∈ s,
         Module.Free (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M) ∧
           Module.Finite (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M),
       Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.freeLocus R M = Set.univ ∧
         IsLocallyConstant (Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) M)]

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteFlatNotProjective.quotientModule_isLocalization_finite_flat_not_projective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00NY.** Over `R = C^∞(ℝ)`, with `m` the ideal of functions vanishing at `0` and `I`
the ideal of functions vanishing on a neighbourhood of `0`, the module `M = R/I` is the
localization `R_m`, and it is a finite flat `R`-module which is not projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientModule_isLocalization_finite_flat_not_projective :
    IsLocalization.AtPrime QuotientModule vanishAtZero ∧
      Module.Finite SmoothFunReal QuotientModule ∧
      Module.Flat SmoothFunReal QuotientModule ∧
      ¬ Module.Projective SmoothFunReal QuotientModule

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteProjective.MapLocus.isOpen_injLocus_and_localized
declarations.doc:
**(Injectivity locus.)** The injectivity locus `U` is open, and for every
`f` with `D(f) ⊆ U`:
(a) the localized map `φ_f` is injective; and
(b) `Coker(φ)_f` is finite projective over `R_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_injLocus_and_localized
    (φ : P₁ →ₗ[R] P₂) [Module.Finite R P₁] [Module.Projective R P₁]
    [Module.Finite R P₂] [Module.Projective R P₂] :
    IsOpen (injLocus φ) ∧
    ∀ f : R, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ⊆ injLocus φ →
      Function.Injective (localizedMap φ f) ∧
      Module.Finite (Localization.Away f)
        (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] (P₂ ⧸ LinearMap.range φ)) ∧
      Module.Projective (Localization.Away f)
        (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] (P₂ ⧸ LinearMap.range φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteProjective.MapLocus.isOpen_surjLocus_and_localized
declarations.doc:
**(Surjectivity locus.)** The surjectivity locus `W` is open, and for every
`f` with `D(f) ⊆ W`:
(a) the localized map `φ_f` is surjective; and
(b) `Ker(φ)_f` is finite projective over `R_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_surjLocus_and_localized
    (φ : P₁ →ₗ[R] P₂) [Module.Finite R P₁] [Module.Projective R P₁]
    [Module.Finite R P₂] [Module.Projective R P₂] :
    IsOpen (surjLocus φ) ∧
    ∀ f : R, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ⊆ surjLocus φ →
      Function.Surjective (localizedMap φ f) ∧
      Module.Finite (Localization.Away f)
        (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] (LinearMap.ker φ)) ∧
      Module.Projective (Localization.Away f)
        (Localization.Away f ⊗[R] (LinearMap.ker φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteProjective.MapLocus.isOpen_isoLocus_and_localized
declarations.doc:
**(Isomorphism locus.)** The isomorphism locus `V` is open, and for every
`f` with `D(f) ⊆ V`, the localized map `φ_f` is bijective.

Formal consequence of Theorems 1 and 2: `isoLocus φ = injLocus φ ∩ surjLocus φ`
(`isoLocus_eq`), so it is open as an intersection of two opens; and on
`D(f) ⊆ isoLocus φ ⊆ injLocus φ` (resp. `⊆ surjLocus φ`) the localized map is both
injective (`injective_localizedMap_of_subset`) and surjective
(`surjective_localizedMap_of_subset`), hence bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_isoLocus_and_localized
    (φ : P₁ →ₗ[R] P₂) [Module.Finite R P₁] [Module.Projective R P₁]
    [Module.Finite R P₂] [Module.Projective R P₂] :
    IsOpen (isoLocus φ) ∧
    ∀ f : R, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ⊆ isoLocus φ →
      Function.Bijective (localizedMap φ f)

declarations.name: finite_projective_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00O1 (Lemma 10.78.6).** Let `R → S` be a flat local homomorphism of
local rings, and let `M` be a finite `R`-module. Then `M` is finite projective
over `R` if and only if `M ⊗_R S` is finite projective over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_projective_iff_baseChange {R : Type*} {S : Type*} {M : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    [Module.Flat R S]
    [Module.Finite R M] :
    (Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M) ↔
      (Module.Finite S (S ⊗[R] M) ∧ Module.Projective S (S ⊗[R] M))

declarations.name: schanuel
declarations.doc:
**Schanuel's Lemma (Stacks Tag 00O3).**
Given two short exact sequences `0 → K → P₁ → M → 0` and `0 → L → P₂ → M → 0`
with `P₁`, `P₂` projective, there are `R`-linear isomorphisms
`φ : K × P₂ ≃ P₁ × L` and `ψ : P₁ × P₂ ≃ P₁ × P₂` fitting into a commutative
diagram of short exact sequences whose right-hand vertical map is the identity
on `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schanuel
    {R : Type*} [Ring R]
    {K L P₁ P₂ M : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup P₁] [AddCommGroup P₂] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R K] [Module R L] [Module R P₁] [Module R P₂] [Module R M]
    (c₁ : K →ₗ[R] P₁) (p₁ : P₁ →ₗ[R] M) (c₂ : L →ₗ[R] P₂) (p₂ : P₂ →ₗ[R] M)
    (hP₁ : Module.Projective R P₁) (hP₂ : Module.Projective R P₂)
    -- first short exact sequence `0 → K → P₁ → M → 0`
    (hc₁ : Function.Injective c₁) (hp₁ : Function.Surjective p₁)
    (hex₁ : Function.Exact c₁ p₁)
    -- second short exact sequence `0 → L → P₂ → M → 0`
    (hc₂ : Function.Injective c₂) (hp₂ : Function.Surjective p₂)
    (hex₂ : Function.Exact c₂ p₂) :
    ∃ (φ : (K × P₂) ≃ₗ[R] (P₁ × L)) (ψ : (P₁ × P₂) ≃ₗ[R] (P₁ × P₂)),
      let topLeft : (K × P₂) →ₗ[R] (P₁ × P₂) := c₁.prodMap LinearMap.id
      let topRight : (P₁ × P₂) →ₗ[R] M := LinearMap.coprod p₁ 0
      let botLeft : (P₁ × L) →ₗ[R] (P₁ × P₂) := LinearMap.id.prodMap c₂
      let botRight : (P₁ × P₂) →ₗ[R] M := LinearMap.coprod 0 p₂
      -- (1) both rows are short exact sequences
      (Function.Injective topLeft ∧ Function.Surjective topRight ∧
        Function.Exact topLeft topRight) ∧
      (Function.Injective botLeft ∧ Function.Surjective botRight ∧
        Function.Exact botLeft botRight) ∧
      -- (3a) left square commutes: `(id, c₂) ∘ φ = ψ ∘ (c₁, id)`
      (botLeft.comp φ.toLinearMap = ψ.toLinearMap.comp topLeft) ∧
      -- (3b) right square commutes: `(0, p₂) ∘ ψ = (p₁, 0)`
      (botRight.comp ψ.toLinearMap = topRight)

declarations.name: Module.projectiveDimension
declarations.doc:
The **projective dimension** of an `R`-module `M`: the least `d` with `Ext^i(M, -) = 0` for
all `i > d`. For `R` small in `M`'s universe this is the source's invariant, the least `d` for
which there is an exact sequence `0 → P_d → ⋯ → P_0 → M → 0` with all `P_i` projective (00O5,
0CXC), and `M` then has *finite projective dimension* in the sense of the source exactly when
this is `≠ ⊤` (`CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension_ne_top_iff`). It is `⊥` for the zero module,
whose projective dimension in the source is `0`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev Module.projectiveDimension (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : WithBot ℕ∞

declarations.name: pd_syzygy_projective_of_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00O5 / Lemma 10.109.3.** Let `M` have projective dimension at most `d` and let
`F_e → ⋯ → F_0 → M → 0` be exact with every `F_i` projective and `d ≤ e + 1`. Then the
leftmost syzygy `Ker(F_e → F_{e-1})`, or `Ker(F_0 → M)` when `e = 0`, is projective.

The source assumes `pd(M) = d` for its minimal-resolution projective dimension (00O4), under
which the zero module has projective dimension `0`; the library's projective dimension of the zero
module is `⊥` instead. The hypothesis `projectiveDimension M ≤ d` covers the source's hypothesis
in both cases (for `M ≠ 0` the two invariants coincide, and for `M = 0` the value `⊥` is `≤ d`),
so this is the source's statement, in a slightly more general form.
declarations.statement:
theorem pd_syzygy_projective_of_le (d e : ℕ)
    -- the truncated sequence `F_e → ⋯ → F_0 → M → 0`
    (S : ComposableArrows (ModuleCat R) (e + 2))
    -- `M`, the object at position `e + 1`, has projective dimension at most `d`
    (hpd : projectiveDimension (S.obj ⟨e + 1, by omega⟩) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    -- the hypothesis `e ≥ d - 1`, equivalently `d ≤ e + 1`
    (hde : d ≤ e + 1)
    -- exactness at every internal object (in particular `F_0 → M` is surjective);
    -- note exactness is NOT imposed at the leftmost object `F_e`
    (hexact : S.Exact)
    -- the rightmost object (position `e + 2`) is the zero module
    (hzero : Limits.IsZero (S.obj (Fin.last (e + 2))))
    -- each `F_i` (positions `0, …, e`) is projective
    (hproj : ∀ i : Fin (e + 1), Projective (S.obj i.castSucc.castSucc)) :
    -- the leftmost syzygy `Ker(F_e → F_{e-1})` (or `Ker(F_0 → M)` when `e = 0`)
    -- is projective
    Projective (Limits.kernel (S.map' 0 1))
declarations.comment: The source's hypothesis `pd(M) = d` is relaxed to `projectiveDimension M ≤ d`, which also covers the zero module, of projective dimension `0` in the source and `⊥` here.

declarations.name: ringGlobalDimension
declarations.doc:
The **global dimension** of a ring `R`: the supremum of the projective dimensions of all
`R`-modules, an element of `WithBot ℕ∞`. It is `≤ n` exactly when every `R`-module admits a
resolution of length `≤ n` by projective modules (00O5, 0CXC), so it is the source's minimal such
`n`, and `R` has *finite global dimension* exactly when `ringGlobalDimension R ≠ ⊤`. It is `⊥`
for the zero ring.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable abbrev ringGlobalDimension (R : Type u) [Ring R] : WithBot ℕ∞
declarations.comment:
The global dimension is the supremum `⨆ M, projectiveDimension M` over the
`R`-modules in `R`'s own universe; `R` has finite global dimension iff this is `≠ ⊤`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.RegularLocalRing.ShortFreeResolution.solution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00O7.** Let `R` be a regular local ring of dimension at most `d`. Every finite
`R`-module `M` whose `𝔪`-depth is at least `e` has a resolution `0 → F_{d-e} → ⋯ → F_0 → M → 0`
by finite free `R`-modules, and every `R`-module has projective dimension at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem solution {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] {d : ℕ}
    (hd : ringKrullDim R ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    (∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R M] (e : ℕ),
        (e : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (maximalIdeal R) M →
        ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution
            (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} R => Module.Free R N ∧ Module.Finite R N) M,
          ∀ i, d - e < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)) ∧
      ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d
declarations.comment:
Stated with `ringKrullDim R ≤ d` and `e ≤ depth_𝔪(M)`; see the module docstring of
the statement file.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.exists_leftResolution_free_finite_and_hasProjectiveDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00O7.** Let `R` be a regular local ring of dimension at most `d`. Every finite
`R`-module `M` whose `𝔪`-depth is at least `e` has a resolution `0 → F_{d-e} → ⋯ → F_0 → M → 0`
by finite free `R`-modules, and every `R`-module has projective dimension at most `d`; that is,
`R` has global dimension at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.exists_leftResolution_free_finite_and_hasProjectiveDimensionLE
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] {d : ℕ}
    (hd : ringKrullDim R ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    (∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R M] (e : ℕ),
        (e : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (maximalIdeal R) M →
        ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution
            (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} R => Module.Free R N ∧ Module.Finite R N) M,
          ∀ i, d - e < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)) ∧
      ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d
declarations.comment:
Stated with `ringKrullDim R ≤ d` and `e ≤ depth_𝔪(M)`; the length `d - e` of the
resolution is the vanishing of its terms in degrees `> d - e`, and `R` having global dimension
`≤ d` is `∀ M, HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.projectiveDimension_localizedModule_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00O8 (1).** Let `R` be a ring, `M` an `R`-module and `S ⊆ R` a multiplicative
subset. If `M` has projective dimension `≤ n`, then `S⁻¹M` has projective dimension `≤ n` over
`S⁻¹R`. Projective dimension is the library's `Module.projectiveDimension` (Stacks 00O4); the
module `M` lives in any universe in which `R` is small, the hypothesis under which that invariant
is the source's minimal length of a projective resolution (00O5, 0CXC). The localization `S⁻¹M`
is `LocalizedModule S M` itself, in its own universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.projectiveDimension_localizedModule_le {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (S : Submonoid R) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ)
    (hM : Module.projectiveDimension R M ≤ n) :
    Module.projectiveDimension (Localization S) (LocalizedModule S M) ≤ n

declarations.name: ringGlobalDimension_localization_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00O8 (2).** Let `R` be a ring and `S ⊆ R` a multiplicative subset. If `R` has
finite global dimension `≤ n`, then so does `S⁻¹R`. Global dimension is the library's
`ringGlobalDimension` (Stacks 00O6), the supremum of the projective dimensions of all modules,
which is `≤ n` exactly when every module has a projective resolution of length `≤ n`. The proof
is the source's: every `S⁻¹R`-module `M'` is its own localization `S⁻¹M'`, so (1) applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringGlobalDimension_localization_le {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R) (n : ℕ)
    (hR : ringGlobalDimension R ≤ n) : ringGlobalDimension (Localization S) ≤ n

declarations.name: Ring.forall_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_forall_isLocalization_maximal
declarations.doc:
**Global dimension of a Noetherian ring is detected at the maximal ideals.** For a Noetherian
ring `R` and `n : ℕ`, every `R`-module has projective dimension `≤ n` if and only if, for every
maximal ideal `𝔪` of `R`, every module over the localization `R_𝔪` has projective dimension `≤ n`.
Taking `∃ n` on both sides gives the source's statement that `R` has finite global dimension iff
the global dimensions of the `R_𝔪` are bounded.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ring.forall_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_forall_isLocalization_maximal
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (n : ℕ)
    (Rₘ : (𝔪 : Ideal R) → [𝔪.IsMaximal] → Type v)
    [∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) [𝔪.IsMaximal], CommRing (Rₘ 𝔪)]
    [∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) [𝔪.IsMaximal], Algebra R (Rₘ 𝔪)]
    [∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) [𝔪.IsMaximal], IsLocalization.AtPrime (Rₘ 𝔪) 𝔪] :
    (∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, HasProjectiveDimensionLE M n) ↔
      ∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) [𝔪.IsMaximal] (M : ModuleCat.{v} (Rₘ 𝔪)),
        HasProjectiveDimensionLE M n

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.finrank_cotangentSpace_le_projectiveDimension_residueField
declarations.doc:
**The projective dimension of the residue field bounds the embedding dimension.** For a
Noetherian local ring `(R, 𝔪, κ)`, the projective dimension of `κ` as an `R`-module is at least
`dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪²`, the dimension of the cotangent space of `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finrank_cotangentSpace_le_projectiveDimension_residueField
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    (Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
      projectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R))
declarations.comment:
`dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪²` is the `finrank` of `IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace R` over
