`IsLocalRing.ResidueField R`, and `pd_R κ` is `CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension` of `κ` in
`ModuleCat R`, valued in `WithBot ℕ∞`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.projectiveDimension_le_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Finite projective dimension is bounded by the dimension.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian
local ring and let `M` be a finite `R`-module of finite projective dimension. Then
`pd_R M ≤ dim R`. The source states the case `M = κ`, for which the inequality is an equality
(Proposition 00OC).
declarations.statement:
public theorem projectiveDimension_le_ringKrullDim {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (hM : projectiveDimension R M ≠ ⊤) :
    projectiveDimension R M ≤ ringKrullDim R
declarations.comment:
Stated for an arbitrary finite module `M` rather than only for `κ`, the source's
proof using nothing else; `pd_R M` is `Module.projectiveDimension` (Tag 00O4) and finiteness of
it is `≠ ⊤`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Serre's characterisation of regular local rings** (Stacks 00OC). For a Noetherian local
ring `(R, 𝔪, κ)` the following are equivalent: (1) `κ` has finite projective dimension over `R`;
(2) `R` has finite global dimension; (3) `R` is a regular local ring; (4) the global dimension of
`R` is `dim R`; (5) the global dimension of `R` is `dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪²`. Items (4) and (5) are the
source's final sentence, and together they give `gl dim R = dim R = dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪²`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularLocalRing_tfae {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    List.TFAE
      [projectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R (ResidueField R)) ≠ ⊤,
       (⨆ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, projectiveDimension M) ≠ ⊤,
       IsRegularLocalRing R,
       (⨆ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, projectiveDimension M) = ringKrullDim R,
       (⨆ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, projectiveDimension M) =
         (Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) : WithBot ℕ∞)]
declarations.comment:
Global dimension is the supremum of the projective dimensions of all `R`-modules
(Mathlib has no name for it) and "finite" is `≠ ⊤`; `dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪²` is the `finrank` of
`IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace R` over `IsLocalRing.ResidueField R`. The source's two "moreover"
equalities are items (4) and (5) of the list, each of which implies the other three. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularRing.isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**A localization of a regular ring at a prime is a regular local ring** (Stacks 00OD). A
Noetherian ring `R` is *regular* when all of its localizations `R_𝔭` at primes are regular local
rings; read for an arbitrary model `S` of `R_𝔭`, that is the statement below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularRing.isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsRegularRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime S p] : IsRegularLocalRing S
declarations.comment:
Definition 00OD is Mathlib's class `IsRegularRing`, which is the source's sentence
verbatim (`IsNoetherianRing R` plus `IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)` for every prime
`p`), so no predicate is redefined here. Its defining field pins the concrete model
`Localization.AtPrime p`, while the source says "the localizations `R_𝔭`"; this is the definition
in that model-independent form, universe-polymorphic in the localization. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: isRegularRing_tfae
declarations.doc:
**A Noetherian ring has global dimension `n` if and only if it is regular of dimension `n`**
(Stacks 00OE). For a Noetherian ring `R` and `n : ℕ` the following are equivalent: (1) the global
dimension of `R` is `n`; (2) `R` is a regular ring and `dim R = n`; (3) every localization `R_𝔪` at
a maximal ideal is a regular local ring of dimension `≤ n`, with `dim R_𝔪 = n` for at least one
`𝔪`; (4) the same for the localizations at all primes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRing_tfae {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (n : ℕ) :
    List.TFAE
      [(⨆ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, projectiveDimension M) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞),
       IsRegularRing R ∧ ringKrullDim R = (n : WithBot ℕ∞),
       (∀ 𝔪 : Ideal R, ∀ _ : 𝔪.IsMaximal, IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪) ∧
            ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
         ∃ 𝔪 : Ideal R, ∃ _ : 𝔪.IsMaximal,
           ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞),
       (∀ 𝔭 : Ideal R, ∀ _ : 𝔭.IsPrime, IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭) ∧
            ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
         ∃ 𝔭 : Ideal R, ∃ _ : 𝔭.IsPrime,
           ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)]
declarations.comment:
Stated for a fixed `n : ℕ`: the source re-quantifies `n` existentially in items (3)
and (4), but "with equality for at least one `𝔪`" pins it, and `exists_congr` on `n` recovers the
source's reading. Global dimension is the supremum of the projective dimensions of all `R`-modules,
Mathlib having no name for it; "regular" is `IsRegularRing` (Definition 00OD) and dimensions are
`ringKrullDim`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.of_flat_of_isLocalHom
declarations.doc:
**Regularity descends along a flat local homomorphism** (Stacks 00OF). Let `R → S` be a local
homomorphism of local Noetherian rings. If it is flat and `S` is regular, then `R` is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.of_flat_of_isLocalHom {R : Type u} (S : Type v) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsRegularLocalRing S] : IsRegularLocalRing R
declarations.comment:
The source's "local Noetherian and regular" for `S` is the single class
`IsRegularLocalRing S` (Definition 00KU), which extends `IsLocalRing` and `IsNoetherianRing`; the
homomorphism is `algebraMap R S`, flat as `Module.Flat R S` and local as
`IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)`, the hypothesis pair of `Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom`.
See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_le_of_goingUp
declarations.doc:
**Going-up version.**
If `φ : R → S` satisfies going up and the induced map `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is
surjective, then `dim(R) ≤ dim(S)`.

This follows from `chain_lift_goingUp` through `krullDim_le_of_chain_lift`, since
`ringKrullDim R` is `krullDim (PrimeSpectrum R)` by definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_le_of_goingUp (φ : R →+* S) (hup : GoingUp_00oh φ)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ)) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ ringKrullDim S

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_le_of_goingDown
declarations.doc:
**Going-down version.**
If `φ : R → S` satisfies going down and the induced map `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is
surjective, then `dim(R) ≤ dim(S)`.

This follows from `chain_lift_goingDown` through `krullDim_le_of_chain_lift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_le_of_goingDown (φ : R →+* S) (hdown : GoingDown_00oh φ)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ)) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ ringKrullDim S

declarations.name: comap_isMaximal_of_goingUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00OI.** If `φ : R → S` satisfies going up and `q ⊆ S` is a maximal
ideal, then its contraction `φ⁻¹(q)` is a maximal ideal of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_isMaximal_of_goingUp (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : GoingUp φ)
    (q : Ideal S) (hq : q.IsMaximal) :
    (Ideal.comap φ q).IsMaximal

declarations.name: integral_dim_up
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00OJ.** If `f : R → S` is a ring map making `S` integral over `R`,
then `ringKrullDim S ≤ ringKrullDim R` and every closed point of `Spec(S)` contracts
to a closed point of `Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem integral_dim_up
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
    (hf : f.IsIntegral) :
    ringKrullDim S ≤ ringKrullDim R ∧
    ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, IsClosed ({q} : Set (PrimeSpectrum S)) →
      IsClosed ({PrimeSpectrum.comap f q} : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))

declarations.name: Algebra.IsIntegral.ringKrullDim_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OK.** If `S` is an integral `R`-algebra whose structure map `R → S` is injective
(for instance an integral ring extension `R ⊆ S`), then `R` and `S` have the same Krull
dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsIntegral.ringKrullDim_eq (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] [FaithfulSMul R S] :
    ringKrullDim R = ringKrullDim S
declarations.comment:
The source's ring inclusion `R ⊆ S` is stated as an `R`-algebra `S` with
`algebraMap R S` injective, spelled `FaithfulSMul R S`; see the module docstring.

registrations.name: Ideal.Fiber
registrations.comment: the fibre ring S ⊗_R κ(p) (written κ(p) ⊗_R S)

registrations.name: PrimeSpectrum.primesOverOrderIsoFiber
registrations.comment: primes q of S lying over p = primes of the fibre ring (inverse: comap along S -> κ(p) ⊗_R S)

registrations.name: Ideal.Fiber.localizationAlgEquivQuotient
registrations.comment: (S ⊗_R κ(p))_q = S_q / p S_q, with q the prime of S under the fibre prime

registrations.name: Localization.AtPrime.isLocalRing
registrations.comment: the localization at a prime is a local ring

declarations.name: maximal_ideal_generated_by_n
declarations.doc: A maximal ideal `m` of `k[x_1, …, x_n]` is generated by at most `n` elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem maximal_ideal_generated_by_n
    {k : Type*} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (m : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (hm : m.IsMaximal) :
    GeneratedByAtMost n m

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_localization_atPrime_eq
declarations.doc:
Part 2 of tag 00OP: the localization of `k[x_1, …, x_n]` at a maximal ideal has Krull
dimension `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_localization_atPrime_eq
    {k : Type*} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (m : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (hm : m.IsMaximal) :
    haveI : m.IsPrime := hm.isPrime
    ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime m) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_localization_atPrime
declarations.doc: The localization of `k[x_1, …, x_n]` at a maximal ideal is a regular local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_localization_atPrime
    {k : Type*} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (m : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (hm : m.IsMaximal) :
    haveI : m.IsPrime := hm.isPrime
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.isRegularRing_and_iSup_projectiveDimension_eq_and_isRegularLocalRing_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OQ.** A polynomial algebra `k[ι]` in finitely many variables over a field is a
regular ring; its global dimension, the supremum of the projective dimensions of its modules, is
the number `Nat.card ι` of variables; and every localization of `k[ι]` at a maximal ideal is a
regular local ring of dimension `Nat.card ι`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRing_and_iSup_projectiveDimension_eq_and_isRegularLocalRing_localization
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (ι : Type v) [Finite ι] :
    IsRegularRing (MvPolynomial ι k) ∧
      (⨆ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} (MvPolynomial ι k), projectiveDimension M) =
        (Nat.card ι : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
      ∀ (𝔪 : Ideal (MvPolynomial ι k)) [𝔪.IsMaximal] (A : Type w) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra (MvPolynomial ι k) A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A 𝔪],
        IsRegularLocalRing A ∧ ringKrullDim A = (Nat.card ι : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment:
The number of variables is `Nat.card ι` for an arbitrary finite index type `ι`,
the global dimension is the supremum of the projective dimensions of all modules (Mathlib has no
name for it), and the localization at a maximal ideal is an abstract `IsLocalization.AtPrime`.
See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularRing.height_last_eq_length_add_height_head
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OR.** In a regular ring, every maximal chain of primes between `𝔭` and `𝔮` — a
chain from `𝔭` to `𝔮` no two consecutive members of which admit a prime strictly between them —
has length `height 𝔮 - height 𝔭`, stated as `height 𝔮 = length + height 𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularRing.height_last_eq_length_add_height_head {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsRegularRing R] (s : RelSeries {(p, q) : PrimeSpectrum R × PrimeSpectrum R | p ⋖ q}) :
    s.last.asIdeal.height = s.length + s.head.asIdeal.height
declarations.comment:
Stated for an arbitrary regular ring, of which a polynomial algebra in finitely
many variables over a field is an instance (the source's ring, via Proposition 00OQ); a maximal
chain between `𝔭` and `𝔮` is a `RelSeries` for the covering relation `⋖` on `PrimeSpectrum R`
with the given head and last, and the formula is stated additively. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FiniteType.ringKrullDim_eq_height_of_isMaximal_and_length_eq_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OS.** Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra which is a
domain. Then `dim S = dim S_𝔪 = height 𝔪` for every maximal ideal `𝔪` of `S`, and every maximal
chain of primes of `S` — one starting at a minimal prime, ending at a maximal ideal, and with all
steps covering pairs — has length `dim S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_eq_height_of_isMaximal_and_length_eq_ringKrullDim (k : Type*)
    [Field k] (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] :
    (∀ (𝔪 : Ideal S) [𝔪.IsMaximal], ringKrullDim S = (𝔪.height : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
      ∀ s : RelSeries {(p, q) : PrimeSpectrum S × PrimeSpectrum S | p ⋖ q},
        IsMin s.head → IsMax s.last → (s.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim S
declarations.comment:
`dim(S_𝔪)` is written `𝔪.height`, the Krull dimension of any model of the local
ring at `𝔪`; the source's "in words" clause is kept as a second conjunct, a maximal chain of
primes being a `RelSeries` for the covering relation `⋖` on `PrimeSpectrum S` whose head is
minimal and whose last is maximal. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.localKrullDim_eq_iSup_irreducibleComponents_and_eq_iInf_height
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OT.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `X = Spec S`,
and let `x ∈ X` be a point, with prime ideal `𝔭 = x.asIdeal`. Then the dimension of `X` at `x` is
both the largest dimension of an irreducible component of `X` through `x` and the smallest of the
dimensions `dim S_𝔪 = height 𝔪` over the maximal ideals `𝔪 ⊇ 𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localKrullDim_eq_iSup_irreducibleComponents_and_eq_iInf_height
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (x : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    (TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) x =
        ⨆ Z ∈ {Z ∈ irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum S) | x ∈ Z}, topologicalKrullDim Z) ∧
      (TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) x =
        ⨅ 𝔪 ∈ {𝔪 : Ideal S | 𝔪.IsMaximal ∧ x.asIdeal ≤ 𝔪}, (𝔪.height : WithBot ℕ∞))
declarations.comment:
`dim_x X` is `TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim`, Topology Definition 0055 (4);
`dim(S_𝔪)` is `𝔪.height`; the components are `irreducibleComponents` and their dimension is
`topologicalKrullDim`, and the source's `max`/`min` are `iSup`/`iInf` in `WithBot ℕ∞`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.localKrullDim_eq_ringKrullDim_localization_of_isMaximal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OU.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, and let `𝔪 ⊆ S` be
a maximal ideal, with associated closed point `x` of `X = Spec S`. Then `dim_x X = dim S_𝔪`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localKrullDim_eq_ringKrullDim_localization_of_isMaximal (k : Type*) [Field k]
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (𝔪 : Ideal S)
    [h𝔪 : 𝔪.IsMaximal] :
    TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) ⟨𝔪, h𝔪.isPrime⟩ =
      ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪)
declarations.comment:
`X = Spec S` is `PrimeSpectrum S`, `x` is the point `⟨𝔪, _⟩`, `dim_x X` is the
topological local dimension `TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim` of Topology, Definition 0055 (4), and
`dim(S_𝔪)` is `ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪)`. The same statement on the scheme `Spec S`
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.topologicalLocalKrullDim_specClosedPoint`.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isLocallyConstant_localKrullDim_and_equidimensional_fiber_and_exists_algEquiv_pi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OV.** Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a Cohen-Macaulay finite type `k`-algebra.
Then `Spec S` is the disjoint union of the level sets `T_d` of its local dimension; these are
open and closed, there are finitely many nonempty ones, and `T_d` is equidimensional of
dimension `d`. Equivalently, `S` is a product of rings `S_d`, `d = 0, …, dim S`, such that every
maximal ideal of `S_d` has height `d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    isLocallyConstant_localKrullDim_and_equidimensional_fiber_and_exists_algEquiv_pi
    {k : Type*} {S : Type v} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (hS : ∀ (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime],
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime p)) :
    IsLocallyConstant (localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S)) ∧
      (∀ d : WithBot ℕ∞,
        Equidimensional ↥(localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) ⁻¹' {d}) ∧
          ((localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) ⁻¹' {d}).Nonempty →
            topologicalKrullDim ↥(localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) ⁻¹' {d}) = d)) ∧
        (Set.range (localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S))).Finite ∧
        ∃ (R : {d : ℕ // (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim S} → Type v)
          (_ : ∀ d, CommRing (R d)) (_ : ∀ d, Algebra k (R d)),
          Nonempty (S ≃ₐ[k] ((d : {d : ℕ // (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim S}) → R d)) ∧
            ∀ d (𝔪 : Ideal (R d)), 𝔪.IsMaximal → 𝔪.height = d.1
declarations.comment:
The family `T_d` is the family of fibers of `TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim`
(Topology Definition 0055 (4)), indexed by `WithBot ℕ∞`; a nonempty fiber has `d` a natural
number at most `dim S`. Disjointness and covering are definitional, `T_d` open and closed is
`IsLocallyConstant.isClopen_fiber`, and finiteness of the union is finiteness of the range. The
product form is the last conjunct, a `k`-algebra isomorphism `S ≃ₐ[k] ∏_{d ≤ dim S} S_d`; it is
built from Mathlib's `PrimeSpectrum.exists_idempotent_basicOpen_eq_of_isClopen` (Lemma 00EM) and
`CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.bijective_pi`. Cohen-Macaulayness of the Noetherian ring `S`
(Definition 00NC) is spelled out over its localizations at primes, as in tags 00ND and 00R9. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.NagataNormalization.exists_isIntegral_aeval
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OX**, in the form the induction uses. If the generators `x 0, …, x n` of a
`k`-algebra `S` satisfy a nonzero polynomial relation `f`, then `S` is integral over the
subalgebra generated by the `n` elements `y i = x (i + 1) - x 0 ^ D ^ (i + 1)`, where
`D = f.totalDegree + 2`; these lie in the `ℤ`-subalgebra generated by the `x i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isIntegral_aeval {k : Type*} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {S : Type*} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] (x : Fin (n + 1) → S) (hx : Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range x) = ⊤)
    {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) k} (hf : f ≠ 0) (hfx : MvPolynomial.aeval x f = 0) :
    ∃ y : Fin n → S, (∀ i, y i ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℤ (Set.range x)) ∧
      (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] S).toRingHom.IsIntegral

declarations.name: exists_finite_inj_aeval_ringKrullDim_eq_of_adjoin_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OY** (Noether normalization). Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a nonzero
commutative `k`-algebra generated by a finite set `s`. Then there are `r : ℕ` and `y : Fin r → S`
with every `y i` in the `ℤ`-subalgebra of `S` generated by `s`, such that the `k`-algebra map
`MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] S` sending `X i` to `y i` is injective and finite; the number `r`
is the Krull dimension of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_inj_aeval_ringKrullDim_eq_of_adjoin_eq_top (k : Type*) {S : Type*}
    [Field k] [CommRing S] [Nontrivial S] [Algebra k S] {s : Set S} (hs : s.Finite)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin k s = ⊤) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (y : Fin r → S), (∀ i, y i ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℤ s) ∧
      Function.Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] S) ∧
      (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] S).Finite ∧
      ringKrullDim S = r
declarations.comment:
Stated for a nonzero `k`-algebra with a finite generating set `s` rather than for a
presentation `k[x_1, …, x_n]/I`, the source's `ℤ`-subalgebra being `Algebra.adjoin ℤ s`; the map
`k[y_1, …, y_r] → S` is pinned as `MvPolynomial.aeval y`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_eq_of_aeval_injective_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00OY**, the clause "in this case the integer `r` is the dimension of `S`": for a field
`k`, a commutative `k`-algebra `S` and `y : Fin r → S` such that the `k`-algebra map
`MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] S` sending `X i` to `y i` is injective and finite, the Krull
dimension of `S` is `r`. So every `r` produced by Noether normalization is `dim S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_eq_of_aeval_injective_of_finite (k : Type*) {S : Type*}
    [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] {r : ℕ} (y : Fin r → S)
    (hinj : Function.Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] S))
    (hfin : (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] S).Finite) :
    ringKrullDim S = r
declarations.comment:
The closing sentence of the lemma: any `r` and `y_1, …, y_r` with
`k[y_1, …, y_r] → S` injective and finite satisfy `dim S = r`. Proved, as in the source, from
Lemma 00OK (`Algebra.IsIntegral.ringKrullDim_eq`) and
`MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_of_isNoetherianRing`; no finite generation hypothesis is needed. The
existence part is `exists_finite_inj_aeval_ringKrullDim_eq_of_adjoin_eq_top`.

declarations.name: noether_normalization_at_point_topologicalKrullDimAt
declarations.doc:
**Noether normalization at a point.** Let `k` be a field, `S` a finite type `k`-algebra,
`X = Spec(S)`, `𝔮` a prime of `S` and `x ∈ X` the corresponding point. There exist `g ∈ S`,
`g ∉ 𝔮`, such that `dim(S_g) = dim_x(X) =: d`, and a finite injective `k`-algebra map
`k[y_1, …, y_d] → S_g`, where `k[y_1, …, y_d] = MvPolynomial (Fin d) k` and `dim_x(X)` is the
Krull dimension of the topological space `X` at `x` (Stacks 0055 (4)),
`topologicalKrullDimAt (PrimeSpectrum S) x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem noether_normalization_at_point_topologicalKrullDimAt
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    ∃ (g : S) (_ : g ∉ q) (d : ℕ)
      (ψ : MvPolynomial (Fin d) k →ₐ[k] Localization.Away g),
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (Localization.Away g) ∧
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞) = topologicalKrullDimAt (PrimeSpectrum S) ⟨q, ‹_›⟩ ∧
      Function.Injective ψ ∧
      ψ.toRingHom.Finite
declarations.comment: dim_x(X) is topologicalKrullDimAt of 0055 (4); finite is ψ.toRingHom.Finite

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_eq_trdeg_and_ringKrullDim_localization_eq_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00P0.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra which is a domain,
and let `K` be its field of fractions. Then the Krull dimension of `S` is the transcendence
degree of `K` over `k`, and the local ring of `S` at every maximal ideal has that same
dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_eq_trdeg_and_ringKrullDim_localization_eq_trdeg
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra k S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra S K] [IsFractionRing S K]
    [Algebra k K] [IsScalarTower k S K] :
    ringKrullDim S = (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg k K) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
      ∀ (𝔪 : Ideal S) [𝔪.IsMaximal] (A : Type x) [CommRing A] [Algebra S A]
          [IsLocalization.AtPrime A 𝔪],
        ringKrullDim A = (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg k K) : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment:
The transcendence degree is compared through `Cardinal.toENat`, the field of
fractions is an abstract `IsFractionRing` and the local ring an abstract
`IsLocalization.AtPrime`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.localKrullDim_eq_height_add_trdeg_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00P1.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `X = Spec S`,
and let `x ∈ X` be a point, with prime ideal `𝔭 = x.asIdeal`. Then the dimension of `X` at `x` —
the least dimension of an open neighbourhood of `x` — is the height of `𝔭` plus the transcendence
degree over `k` of the residue field `κ(𝔭)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localKrullDim_eq_height_add_trdeg_residueField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (x : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) x =
      ((x.asIdeal.height + Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg k x.asIdeal.ResidueField) : ℕ∞) :
        WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment:
`dim_x X` is `TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim`, Definition 0055 (4); `dim(S_𝔭)` is
`𝔭.height`, `κ(𝔭)` is `Ideal.ResidueField`, and the transcendence degree is compared through
`Cardinal.toENat`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.localKrullDim_comap_add_height_eq_localKrullDim_add_height_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00P2.** Let `k` be a field, let `f : S' → S` be a surjection of finite type
`k`-algebras, let `x ∈ Spec S` be a point and let `x' = comap f x` be the corresponding point of
`Spec S'`. Then the dimension of `Spec S'` at `x'` exceeds the dimension of `Spec S` at `x` by
exactly the amount by which the height of `x'` exceeds the height of `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localKrullDim_comap_add_height_eq_localKrullDim_add_height_comap
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {S' : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing S'] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S'] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S'] (f : S' →ₐ[k] S)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (x : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S') (comap f.toRingHom x) +
        (x.asIdeal.height : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) x +
        ((comap f.toRingHom x).asIdeal.height : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment:
`dim_x X` is `TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim`, Definition 0055 (4), and
`height 𝔭` is `Ideal.height`, as in the sibling 00P1; the source's difference of differences is
stated as the equivalent equality of sums, subtraction in `WithBot ℕ∞` being truncated. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.ringKrullDim_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00P3.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a `k`-algebra of finite type and let `K/k` be a
field extension. Then `S` and its base change `T = K ⊗_k S` have the same Krull dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsPushout.ringKrullDim_eq (k K S T : Type*) [Field k] [Field K]
    [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k T] [Algebra K T]
    [Algebra S T] [IsScalarTower k K T] [IsScalarTower k S T] [Algebra.IsPushout k K S T]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] :
    ringKrullDim S = ringKrullDim T
declarations.comment:
The base change `K ⊗_k S` is an arbitrary pushout square of `k`-algebras
`Algebra.IsPushout k K S T`; the source's literal form is `inferInstance` once
`Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra` is a local instance. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.localKrullDim_comap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00P4.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `K/k` be a
field extension and let `T = K ⊗_k S` be the base change, presented as a pushout square. Let
`xK ∈ Spec T` be a point, with prime `q_K`, and let `x = comap (algebraMap S T) xK ∈ Spec S` be
the point of the prime `q = q_K ∩ S` that it lies over. Then `Spec S` has the same dimension at
`x` as `Spec T` has at `xK`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localKrullDim_comap_eq (k K S T : Type*) [Field k] [Field K]
    [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k T] [Algebra K T]
    [Algebra S T] [IsScalarTower k K T] [IsScalarTower k S T] [Algebra.IsPushout k K S T]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (xK : PrimeSpectrum T) :
    TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S)
        (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S T) xK) =
      TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum T) xK
declarations.comment:
`dim_x X` is `TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim`, Definition 0055 (4), as in the
siblings 00P1 and 00P2; the base change `K ⊗_k S` is an arbitrary pushout square of `k`-algebras
`Algebra.IsPushout k K S T`, as in the sibling 00P3; and `q_K` lying over `q` is expressed by
taking `x = PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S T) xK`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: GradedAlgebra.irrelevant_isMaximal_and_ringKrullDim_eq_localKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00P6.** Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a graded `k`-algebra with `S_0 = k` that is
generated over `k` by finitely many elements of degree `1`. Let `P ∈ ℚ[T]` be the polynomial with
`dim_k S_d = P(d)` for all `d ≫ 0`. Then: (1) the irrelevant ideal `m = S_+` is maximal;
(2) every minimal prime of `S` is homogeneous and contained in `S_+`; (3) `dim(S) = deg(P) + 1`,
with `deg(0) = -1`, and `dim(S) = dim_x Spec(S)`, the local dimension of `Spec(S)` at the closed
point `x` given by `m`, which is also `height(m) = dim(S_m)`; (4) the Hilbert function
`d ↦ length_{S_m} (m^d S_m / m^{d + 1} S_m)` of the local ring `S_m` is the Hilbert function
`d ↦ dim_k S_d` of `S`.

The source's `S_0 = k` is `𝒜 0 = 1` together with `Nontrivial S`: `𝒜 0 = 1` alone says that
`𝒜 0` is the image of `k`, which the zero ring also satisfies, and `Nontrivial S` makes `k → S`
injective, so that `S_0 ≅ k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem GradedAlgebra.irrelevant_isMaximal_and_ringKrullDim_eq_localKrullDim
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Nontrivial S] [Algebra k S]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule k S) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (h0 : 𝒜 0 = 1)
    [Module.Finite k ↥(𝒜 1)] (hgen : Algebra.adjoin k (𝒜 1 : Set S) = ⊤)
    (P : ℚ[X]) (hP : ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in Filter.atTop, P.eval (d : ℚ) = Module.finrank k ↥(𝒜 d)) :
    ∃ hm : 𝒜₊.toIdeal.IsMaximal,
      letI := hm.isPrime
      (∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes S, Ideal.IsHomogeneous 𝒜 p ∧ p ≤ 𝒜₊.toIdeal) ∧
      (P = 0 → ringKrullDim S = 0) ∧
      (P ≠ 0 → ringKrullDim S = (P.natDegree + 1 : ℕ)) ∧
      ringKrullDim S = TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) ⟨𝒜₊.toIdeal, hm.isPrime⟩ ∧
      ringKrullDim S = 𝒜₊.toIdeal.height ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, Module.length (Localization.AtPrime (𝒜₊).toIdeal)
          (↥(IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (𝒜₊).toIdeal) ^ d) ⧸
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (𝒜₊).toIdeal) ^ (d + 1)).submoduleOf
              (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (𝒜₊).toIdeal) ^ d))
        = Module.finrank k ↥(𝒜 d)
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(4). `S_0 = k` is `𝒜 0 = 1` with `Nontrivial S`; `dim_x Spec(S)` is
`TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim` at the point given by `S_+`, also shown equal to its height
`dim(S_m)`; the convention `deg 0 = -1` is unfolded into the cases `P = 0`, `P ≠ 0`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_localSubring_isNoetherian_ringKrullDim_eq_one
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_localSubring_isNoetherian_ringKrullDim_eq_one
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (hR : ¬ IsField R) :
    ∃ (R' : LocalSubring K) (hle : LocalSubring.range (algebraMap R K) ≤ R'),
      IsNoetherianRing R'.toSubring ∧
      ringKrullDim R'.toSubring = 1 ∧
      letI : Algebra R R'.toSubring :=
        algebraOfRange R'.toSubring (LocalSubring.le_def.mp hle).choose
      Algebra.EssFiniteType R R'.toSubring

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_finite_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one_of_one_lt_finrank_cotangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**A one-dimensional local ring with non-principal maximal ideal admits a finite
modification.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring of dimension `1` with
`dim_κ(𝔪/𝔪²) > 1`, i.e. with `𝔪` not principal. Then there is a ring map `R → R'` which is
finite, is not an isomorphism, whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of `𝔪`, and
for which `𝔪` is not an associated prime of `R'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    IsLocalRing.exists_finite_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one_of_one_lt_finrank_cotangentSpace
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1)
    (hcotangent : 1 < Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R'), Nontrivial R' ∧
      Module.Finite R R' ∧ ¬ Function.Bijective (algebraMap R R') ∧
      maximalIdeal R ∉ associatedPrimes R R' ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal R ^ n * RingHom.ker (algebraMap R R') = ⊥ ∧
        maximalIdeal R ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R R') ≤
          LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap R R')
declarations.comment:
The conclusion is case (4) of Lemma 0BHZ, spelled the same way there; see the
module docstring for the reading of each of the four conditions. The hypothesis
`dim(𝔪/𝔪²) > 1` is `1 < finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)`.

declarations.name: exists_noetherianLocalDomain_adicCompletion_not_reduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB.** There is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain of positive prime
characteristic whose completion at its maximal ideal is nonreduced, i.e. which is not analytically
unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_noetherianLocalDomain_adicCompletion_not_reduced :
    ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧
      ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : CharP R p) (_ : IsLocalRing R)
        (_ : IsNoetherianRing R) (_ : IsDomain R),
        ringKrullDim R = 1 ∧ ¬ IsAnalyticallyUnramified R
declarations.comment:
The existential form of the tag, which is what Stacks 07NZ consumes: the source's
`k` is any countable field of characteristic two, here `ULift (ZMod 2)`, so that the witness lands
in an arbitrary universe. `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.AnalyticallyUnramified.Examples` carries the
source's other construction, over a field with `[k : k^p] = ∞`.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.isDiscreteValuationRing_finiteCoeffSubring
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00PB: `A` is a discrete valuation ring**, with uniformizer `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_finiteCoeffSubring :
    IsDiscreteValuationRing (finiteCoeffSubring k p)
declarations.comment: The ring `A` is a discrete valuation ring.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.nonempty_algEquiv_adicCompletion_finiteCoeffSubring
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB: the completion of `A` is `k[[x]]`.** The inclusion `A ⊆ k[[x]]` induces an
isomorphism of `A`-algebras from the completion of `A` to `k[[x]]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_algEquiv_adicCompletion_finiteCoeffSubring :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (finiteCoeffSubring k p))
      (finiteCoeffSubring k p) ≃ₐ[finiteCoeffSubring k p] k⟦X⟧)
declarations.comment:
The completion of `A` is `k[[x]]`: an isomorphism of `A`-algebras
`A^ ≃ k[[x]]`.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.isLocalRing_adjoinSubalgebra
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00PB: `R = A[f]` is local.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalRing_adjoinSubalgebra {f : k⟦X⟧} (hf : f ∉ finiteCoeffSubring k p) :
    IsLocalRing (adjoinSubalgebra (p := p) f)
declarations.comment: For `f ∉ A` the ring `R = A[f] ⊆ k[[x]]` is local.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.isNoetherianRing_adjoinSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB: `R = A[f]` is Noetherian.** It is of finite type over the Noetherian ring
`A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherianRing_adjoinSubalgebra (f : k⟦X⟧) :
    IsNoetherianRing (adjoinSubalgebra (p := p) f)
declarations.comment: The ring `R = A[f] ⊆ k[[x]]` is Noetherian.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.ringKrullDim_adjoinSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB: `R = A[f]` has dimension one.** It is integral over `A`, with the same Krull
dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_adjoinSubalgebra {f : k⟦X⟧} (hf : f ∉ finiteCoeffSubring k p) :
    ringKrullDim (adjoinSubalgebra (p := p) f) = 1
declarations.comment: For `f ∉ A` the ring `R = A[f] ⊆ k[[x]]` has Krull dimension one.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.not_isAnalyticallyUnramified_adjoinSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB: the completion of `R = A[f]` is not reduced.** The series `f` is a `p`-th root
of `f ^ p ∈ A` in the completion `k[[x]]` of `A`, while `R = A[T] ⧸ (T ^ p - f ^ p)`; so the
completion of `R` contains the nonzero nilpotent `T - f`
(`AdjoinRoot.not_isReduced_adicCompletion_of_pow_eq`).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isAnalyticallyUnramified_adjoinSubalgebra {f : k⟦X⟧}
    (hf : f ∉ finiteCoeffSubring k p) :
    letI := isLocalRing_adjoinSubalgebra hf
    ¬ IsAnalyticallyUnramified (adjoinSubalgebra (p := p) f)
declarations.comment:
For `f ∉ A` the completion of `R = A[f]` is not reduced, i.e. `R` is not
analytically unramified (Definition 032X).

declarations.name: PowerSeries.isPurelyInseparable_laurentSeries
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB: `k((x))` is purely inseparable over the fraction field of `A`.** The `p`-th
power of `x ^ m g`, `g ∈ k[[x]]`, is `x ^ (p m) g ^ p` with `g ^ p ∈ A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPurelyInseparable_laurentSeries :
    letI := (fractionRingToLaurentSeries (k := k) (p := p)).toAlgebra
    IsPurelyInseparable (FractionRing (finiteCoeffSubring k p)) (LaurentSeries k)
declarations.comment:
The extension `k((x))` of the fraction field of `A` is purely inseparable; that it
has infinite degree is `PowerSeries.not_finiteDimensional_laurentSeries`.

declarations.name: PowerSeries.not_finiteDimensional_laurentSeries
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PB: `k((x))` has infinite degree over the fraction field of `A`**, when
`[k : k^p] = ∞`. The series `f_j = ∑ₙ t_{⟨j, n⟩} xⁿ` built from a `p`-independent sequence
`(tᵢ)` in `k` satisfy `f_m ∉ Frac(A)(f_0, …, f_{m-1})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_finiteDimensional_laurentSeries
    (hk : ¬ FiniteDimensional (pthPowerSubfield k p) k) :
    letI := (fractionRingToLaurentSeries (k := k) (p := p)).toAlgebra
    ¬ FiniteDimensional (FractionRing (finiteCoeffSubring k p)) (LaurentSeries k)
declarations.comment:
The extension `k((x))` of the fraction field of `A` has infinite degree when
`[k : k^p] = ∞`.

declarations.name: isDiscreteValuationRing_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Characterizations of a discrete valuation ring.** For a commutative ring `A` the following
are equivalent: (1) `A` is a discrete valuation ring; (2) `A` is a Noetherian valuation ring and
not a field; (3) `A` is a regular local ring of dimension `1`; (4) `A` is a Noetherian local
domain whose maximal ideal is generated by a single nonzero element; (5) `A` is a Noetherian local
normal domain of dimension `1`; (6) `A` is a local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by a
single nonzero element, and for every generator `π` of the maximal ideal every nonzero `x ∈ A` is
`u * π ^ n` for a unique pair `(n, u)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∃ _ : IsDomain A, IsDiscreteValuationRing A,
        ∃ _ : IsDomain A, ValuationRing A ∧ IsNoetherianRing A ∧ ¬ IsField A,
        IsRegularLocalRing A ∧ ringKrullDim A = 1,
        ∃ _ : IsLocalRing A, IsNoetherianRing A ∧ IsDomain A ∧
          (maximalIdeal A).IsPrincipal ∧ maximalIdeal A ≠ ⊥,
        IsNoetherianRing A ∧ IsLocalRing A ∧ IsDomain A ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed A ∧
          ringKrullDim A = 1,
        ∃ _ : IsLocalRing A, IsDomain A ∧ (maximalIdeal A).IsPrincipal ∧ maximalIdeal A ≠ ⊥ ∧
          ∀ π : A, maximalIdeal A = Ideal.span {π} →
            ∀ x : A, x ≠ 0 → ∃! p : ℕ × Aˣ, x = p.2 * π ^ p.1 ]
declarations.comment:
Item (6) is the source's closing sentence, stated as an item because it is
equivalent to the others: it is item (4) with `IsNoetherianRing` traded for the factorization
property. `0` is excluded there, being of no such form in a domain. See the module docstring for
the spelling of `dimension 1`, of `generated by a single nonzero element` and of `normal`.

declarations.name: length_quotient_span_singleton_lt_top
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Finiteness).** If `R` is a local Noetherian integral domain of Krull
dimension `1` and `x ≠ 0`, then `R / xR` has finite length as an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quotient_span_singleton_lt_top (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) (x : R) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) < ⊤

declarations.name: length_quot_smul_le_mul_length_quot_span
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (Bound).** Let `R` be a local Noetherian integral domain of Krull
dimension `1` with fraction field `K = FractionRing R`. For a non-negative integer `r`,
any `R`-submodule `M` of `K^r = (Fin r → K)`, and any nonzero `x ∈ R`, the length of
`M / xM` is bounded by `r * length (R / xR)`. Here `xM = x • M` and `M / xM` is the
quotient of `M` by the submodule `Submodule.comap M.subtype (x • M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quot_smul_le_mul_length_quot_span
    (r : ℕ) (M : Submodule R (Fin r → FractionRing R)) (x : R) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    Module.length R (M ⧸ Submodule.comap M.subtype (x • M))
      ≤ r * Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})

declarations.name: isFiniteLength_quotSMulTop_of_finiteDimensional
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian domain of Krull dimension at most one with fraction field `K`, let
`V` be a finite-dimensional `K`-vector space and let `M` be an `R`-submodule of `V`. Then for
every nonzero `x ∈ R` the `R`-module `M / xM` has finite length. Note that `M` is not assumed to
be a finitely generated `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLength_quotSMulTop_of_finiteDimensional
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V]
    [Module R V] [IsScalarTower R K V]
    (M : Submodule R V) {x : R} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    IsFiniteLength R (QuotSMulTop x M)
declarations.comment:
For an arbitrary finite-dimensional vector space `V` over the fraction field in
place of `K^{⊕ r}`, and with `dim R = 1` weakened to `Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: krull_akizuki
declarations.doc:
**Krull-Akizuki (Stacks Tag 00PG).** Let `R` be a Noetherian integral domain
of Krull dimension one, with fraction field `K`, and let `L` be a finite field
extension of `K`. Then every intermediate ring `A` with `R ⊆ A ⊆ L` is
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem krull_akizuki
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite K L]
    [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1)
    (A : Subring L) (hA : (algebraMap R L).range ≤ A) :
    IsNoetherianRing A

declarations.name: exists_isDiscreteValuationRing_isFractionRing_of_not_isField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PH.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local domain with fraction field `K` which is not a
field, and let `L/K` be a finitely generated field extension. Then there is an `R`-subalgebra `A`
of `L` which is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field `L` and which dominates `R`, the
last condition being `IsLocalHom (algebraMap R ↥A)`, that is `𝔪_A ∩ R = 𝔪_R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDiscreteValuationRing_isFractionRing_of_not_isField
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    {L : Type*} [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra.EssFiniteType K L]
    [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L] (hR : ¬ IsField R) :
    ∃ A : Subalgebra R L, IsDiscreteValuationRing A ∧ IsFractionRing A L ∧
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap R A)

ega.comment: DVR dom. A, frac field K

declarations.comment:
`A` is produced as a `Subalgebra R L`, so that both inclusions are `algebraMap`s
and domination is `IsLocalHom (algebraMap R ↥A)`. `L/K` finitely generated as a field extension
is `Algebra.EssFiniteType K L`, by `IntermediateField.fg_top_iff`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_singleton_tfae_localizationAtPrime_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PJ.** Let `k` be an artinian ring (for instance a field, the source's hypothesis),
`S` a `k`-algebra of finite type and `𝔮` a prime of `S`. The following are equivalent:
(1) `𝔮` is an isolated point of `Spec S`; (2) `S_𝔮` is finite over `k`; (3) `D(g) = {𝔮}` for
some `g ∉ 𝔮`; (4) `Spec S` has dimension `0` at `𝔮`; (5) `𝔮` is a closed point of `Spec S` and
`dim S_𝔮 = 0`; (6) the residue field `κ(𝔮)` is finite over `k` and `dim S_𝔮 = 0`. In this case
`S = S_𝔮 × S'` as `k`-algebras for a finite type `k`-algebra `S'`, the first component being the
localization map, and every `g ∉ 𝔮` with `D(g) = {𝔮}` has `S_𝔮 = S_g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_singleton_tfae_localizationAtPrime_of_finiteType (k : Type u)
    {S : Type v} [CommRing k] [IsArtinianRing k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime] :
    List.TFAE
        [IsOpen {(⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩ : PrimeSpectrum S)},
          Module.Finite k (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮),
          ∃ g ∉ 𝔮, (basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum S)) = {⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩},
          topologicalKrullDimAt (PrimeSpectrum S) ⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩ = 0,
          IsClosed {(⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩ : PrimeSpectrum S)} ∧ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) = 0,
          Module.Finite k 𝔮.ResidueField ∧ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) = 0] ∧
      (IsOpen {(⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩ : PrimeSpectrum S)} →
        ∃ (S' : Type v) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra k S'), Algebra.FiniteType k S' ∧
          ∃ e : S ≃ₐ[k] Localization.AtPrime 𝔮 × S',
            ∀ x, (e x).1 = algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) x) ∧
      (∀ g ∉ 𝔮, (basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum S)) = {⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩} →
        IsLocalization.Away g (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮))
declarations.comment:
The source's field `k` is generalized to an artinian ring; taking `k` a field gives
the source's statement. `S_𝔮` is `Localization.AtPrime 𝔮`, `κ(𝔮)` is `𝔮.ResidueField`,
`dim_𝔮 Spec S` is `topologicalKrullDimAt` (Stacks 0055 (4)) and `dim S_𝔮` is
`ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)`. The splitting `S = S_𝔮 × S'` is a `k`-algebra
equivalence whose first component is `algebraMap S S_𝔮`, and `S_𝔮 = S_g` is stated as
`IsLocalization.Away g (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)` for every `g ∉ 𝔮` with `D(g) = {𝔮}`.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_singleton_fiber_tfae_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PK.** Let `R → S` be of finite type, let `𝔮` be a prime of `S` lying over a prime
`𝔭` of `R`, let `F = Spec (S ⊗_R κ(𝔭))` be the fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` over `𝔭` and let `q̄`
be the point of `F` corresponding to `𝔮`. The following are equivalent: `q̄` is an isolated
point of `F`; `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` is finite over `κ(𝔭)`; some `g ∉ 𝔮` has `𝔮` as the only prime of
`D(g)` lying over `𝔭`; `dim_q̄ F = 0`; `q̄` is a closed point of `F` and `dim S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮 = 0`;
`κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔭)` is finite and `dim S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮 = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_singleton_fiber_tfae_of_finiteType {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (𝔭 : Ideal R) [𝔭.IsPrime] (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime]
    [𝔮.LiesOver 𝔭] [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭) (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)]
    [IsScalarTower R (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭) (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsOpen (X := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {(⟨𝔭, ‹_›⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R)})
          {⟨⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩, PrimeSpectrum.ext (𝔮.over_def 𝔭).symm⟩},
        Module.Finite 𝔭.ResidueField (𝔭.Fiber (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)),
        ∃ g ∉ 𝔮, {q ∈ 𝔭.primesOver S | g ∉ q} = {𝔮},
        topologicalKrullDimAt
            ↥(PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {(⟨𝔭, ‹_›⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R)})
            ⟨⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩, PrimeSpectrum.ext (𝔮.over_def 𝔭).symm⟩ = 0,
        IsClosed (X := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {(⟨𝔭, ‹_›⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R)})
            {⟨⟨𝔮, ‹_›⟩, PrimeSpectrum.ext (𝔮.over_def 𝔭).symm⟩} ∧
          ringKrullDim (𝔭.Fiber (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) = 0,
        Module.Finite 𝔭.ResidueField 𝔮.ResidueField ∧
          ringKrullDim (𝔭.Fiber (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) = 0]

declarations.name: Algebra.StacksQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PL (1).** For a ring map `R → S` (of finite type, in the source) and a prime `𝔮`
of `S`, `R → S` is quasi-finite at `𝔮` when `𝔮` is an isolated point of its fibre, the subspace
of `Spec S` of the primes lying over `𝔮 ∩ R`: this is condition (1) of Lemma 00PK, equivalent to
the other five by `Algebra.isOpen_singleton_fiber_tfae_of_finiteType`.
declarations.statement: def StacksQuasiFiniteAt (q : PrimeSpectrum S) : Prop
declarations.comment:
(1). The fibre is the subspace `comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {𝔮 ∩ R}` of `Spec S`
and the condition is 00PK (1), `𝔮` isolated in it. For `S` of finite type over `R` this is
Mathlib's `Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R 𝔮`, by `Algebra.stacksQuasiFiniteAt_iff_quasiFiniteAt`.

declarations.name: Algebra.StacksQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PL (2).** A ring map `R → S` is quasi-finite when it is of finite type and
quasi-finite at every prime of `S` in the sense of (1), `Algebra.StacksQuasiFiniteAt`.
declarations.statement: def StacksQuasiFinite : Prop
declarations.comment:
(2). Equivalent to finite type together with Mathlib's `Algebra.QuasiFinite R S`
(which does not include finite type), by `Algebra.stacksQuasiFinite_iff`.

declarations.name: Algebra.stacksQuasiFiniteAt_iff_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PL (1), bridge.** For `R → S` of finite type, `R → S` is quasi-finite at `𝔮` in
the source's sense (`𝔮` isolated in its fibre) iff it is in Mathlib's sense
(`Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt`: `S_𝔮` is quasi-finite over `R`).
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksQuasiFiniteAt_iff_quasiFiniteAt [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (q : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    StacksQuasiFiniteAt R q ↔ Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q.asIdeal
declarations.comment: (1), for `R → S` of finite type, in Mathlib's language.

declarations.name: Algebra.stacksQuasiFinite_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PL (2), bridge.** A ring map `R → S` is quasi-finite in the source's sense (of
finite type and quasi-finite at every prime) iff it is of finite type and quasi-finite in
Mathlib's sense (every fibre `κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S` finite over `κ(𝔭)`).
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksQuasiFinite_iff :
    StacksQuasiFinite R S ↔ Algebra.FiniteType R S ∧ Algebra.QuasiFinite R S
declarations.comment: (2), in Mathlib's language: `Algebra.QuasiFinite` together with finite type.

declarations.name: forall_quasiFiniteAt_iff_forall_finite_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PM.** Let `R → S` be a finite type ring map. Then `R → S` is quasi-finite, i.e.
quasi-finite at every prime `q` of `S` (Stacks 00PL), if and only if for every prime `p` of `R`
the fibre ring `S ⊗_R κ(p)` is finite over `κ(p)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_quasiFiniteAt_iff_forall_finite_fiber
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    (∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q) ↔
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], Module.Finite p.ResidueField (p.Fiber S)
declarations.comment:
Quasi-finiteness at `q` is `Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q`, which for a finite type
map is the 00PK condition `q̄` isolated in its fibre
(`quasiFiniteAt_comap_includeRight_iff_isOpen_singleton`); `S ⊗_R κ(p)` is `p.Fiber S`.
The source's finite type ring map is `[Algebra.FiniteType R S]`, which is also the finite type
part of 00PL's definition. Proved from 0H8X fibre by fibre.

declarations.name: Algebra.stacksQuasiFinite_iff_forall_finite_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00PM.** Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite type. Then `R → S` is quasi-finite (in
the source's sense, Definition 00PL (2)) iff for every prime `𝔭` of `R` the ring `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is
finite over `κ(𝔭)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksQuasiFinite_iff_forall_finite_fiber [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    StacksQuasiFinite R S ↔
      ∀ (𝔭 : Ideal R) [𝔭.IsPrime], Module.Finite 𝔭.ResidueField (𝔭.Fiber S)
declarations.comment:
Stated for the source's notion `Algebra.StacksQuasiFinite`; the fibre
`S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is `𝔭.Fiber S = κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S`.

declarations.name: four_rings_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Four rings lemma.** Given a commutative square of rings
`R → S`, `R → R'`, `R' → S'`, `S → S'` (encoded by `Algebra` instances and the
appropriate `IsScalarTower` data) such that `R → S` is of finite type and the
canonical map `S ⊗_R R' → S'` is surjective, if `R → S` is quasi-finite at the
prime `q := q'.under S` of `S`, then `R' → S'` is quasi-finite at `q'`.

Proof sketch: base change `R → S` quasi-finite at `q'.under S` along
`R → R'`, using `Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.baseChange` with the tensor product
`R' ⊗[R] S`, to obtain quasi-finiteness of `R' → R' ⊗[R] S` at a suitable
prime `P` lying over `q'.under S` and below `q'`. Then push along the
surjective `R'`-algebra map `R' ⊗[R] S →ₐ[R'] S'` using
`Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_surjectiveOnStalks`.
declarations.statement:
theorem four_rings_quasiFiniteAt
    (R S R' S' : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S']
    [IsScalarTower R R' S']
    [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S S')
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R R' S')))
    (q' : Ideal S') [q'.IsPrime]
    [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R (q'.under S)] :
    Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R' q'

declarations.name: Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite type, let `R → R'` be any ring map and set
`S' = R' ⊗[R] S`. Let `𝔮'` be a prime of `S'` and let `𝔮` be its image under the canonical map
`Spec(S') → Spec(S)`. Then `R' → S'` is quasi-finite at `𝔮'` if and only if `R → S` is
quasi-finite at `𝔮`; equivalently, the quasi-finite locus of `Spec(S')` is the inverse image of the
quasi-finite locus of `Spec(S)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_baseChange_iff {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (R' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime] (𝔮' : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)) [𝔮'.IsPrime]
    (h : 𝔮 = 𝔮'.comap Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom) :
    Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R' 𝔮' ↔ Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R 𝔮
declarations.comment:
(1). The canonical map `Spec(S') → Spec(S)` is
`PrimeSpectrum.comap Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom`, so the source's equality of
subsets of `Spec(S')` is this equivalence quantified over `𝔮'`. Quasi-finiteness at a prime
(Definition 00PL) is `Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt`, the source's notion under the finite type
hypothesis. The `←` direction is `Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.baseChange`; `→` is the new content.
Part (2) is `Algebra.quasiFinite_iff_baseChange_of_surjective` and part (3) is Mathlib's
`Algebra.QuasiFinite.baseChange`, tagged 00PP upstream.

declarations.name: Algebra.quasiFinite_iff_baseChange_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite type and let `R → R'` be a ring map such that
`Spec(R') → Spec(R)` is surjective. Then `R → S` is quasi-finite if and only if `R' → R' ⊗[R] S` is
quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.quasiFinite_iff_baseChange_of_surjective {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (R' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    (hR' : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R R'))) :
    Algebra.QuasiFinite R S ↔ Algebra.QuasiFinite R' (R' ⊗[R] S)
declarations.comment:
(2). Surjectivity of `Spec(R') → Spec(R)` is surjectivity of
`PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R R')`. Quasi-finiteness (Definition 00PL) is
`Algebra.QuasiFinite`, which agrees with the source's notion since `R → S`, hence also
`R' → R' ⊗[R] S`, is of finite type. The `→` direction is Mathlib's
`Algebra.QuasiFinite.baseChange` (part (3)); part (1) is `Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_baseChange_iff`.

registrations.name: RingHom.isIntegralElem_leadingCoeff_mul
registrations.comment: scaling by the leading coefficient makes an element integral

registrations.name: RingHom.isIntegralElem_zero
registrations.comment: the degenerate case, where the top coefficient vanishes

declarations.name: StronglyTranscendental
declarations.doc:
An element `x : S` is *strongly transcendental over `R`* if for every
`u : S` and every polynomial `p : R[X]`, the equation `u * p(x) = 0` in `S`
forces `u * (algebraMap R S) (p.coeff i) = 0` for every coefficient index
`i`. This is the algebraic version of the Stacks definition.
declarations.statement:
def StronglyTranscendental (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] (x : S) : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.not_quasiFiniteAt_of_isStronglyTranscendental
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Q2.** Let `R ⊂ S` be an inclusion of reduced rings, let `x ∈ S` be strongly
transcendental over `R`, and assume `S` is finite over `R[x]`. Then `R → S` is not quasi-finite
at any prime `q` of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_quasiFiniteAt_of_isStronglyTranscendental {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsReduced R] [IsReduced S] [Algebra R S] [FaithfulSMul R S] {x : S}
    (hx : IsStronglyTranscendental R x) (hx' : (Polynomial.aeval (R := R) x).toRingHom.Finite)
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] : ¬ QuasiFiniteAt R q
declarations.comment:
`R ⊂ S` is `[FaithfulSMul R S]` with both rings `[IsReduced]`; `S` finite over
`R[x]` is `(Polynomial.aeval x).toRingHom.Finite`; and "not quasi-finite at any prime" is
`¬ Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q` for an arbitrary prime `q` of `S`. The contrapositive is Mathlib's
`Algebra.not_isStronglyTranscendental_of_quasiFiniteAt`, which drops `[IsReduced R]` and
`[FaithfulSMul R S]`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: main_theorem_00q8
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 00Q8 (Lemma 10.123.11). For `S = R[X]/I` monogenic over `R` and a
prime `q ⊂ S` at which `R → S` is quasi-finite, there is an element `g` of the
integral closure `S'` of `R` in `S` with `g ∉ q` such that the induced map
`S'_g → S_g` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_00q8 (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal (R[X]))
    (q : Ideal (R[X] ⧸ I)) [q.IsPrime]
    (hqf : QuasiFiniteAt (R := R) q) :
    ∃ g : integralClosure R (R[X] ⧸ I), (g : R[X] ⧸ I) ∉ q ∧
      Function.Bijective (QF.locMap (R := R) g)

declarations.name: isOpen_quasiFiniteLocus
declarations.doc:
For a finite-type ring map `R → S`, the locus in `Spec(S)` where `S/R` is quasi-finite is
open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_quasiFiniteLocus
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    IsOpen (quasiFiniteLocus R S)

declarations.name: quasiFinite_comap_integralClosure_isOpenEmbedding
declarations.doc:
The map on spectra `Spec(S) → Spec(S')` induced by the inclusion `S' ↪ S` is an open
topological embedding: a homeomorphism of `Spec(S)` onto an open subset of `Spec(S')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFinite_comap_integralClosure_isOpenEmbedding
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFinite R S] :
    IsOpenEmbedding (PrimeSpectrum.comap (integralClosure R S).val.toRingHom)

declarations.name: quasiFinite_awayMap_integralClosure_bijective
declarations.doc:
For every `g ∈ S'` such that the basic open `D(g) ⊆ Spec(S')` is contained in the image of
`Spec(S) → Spec(S')`, the natural ring homomorphism `S'_g → S_g` induced by `S' ↪ S` is
bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFinite_awayMap_integralClosure_bijective
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFinite R S]
    (g : integralClosure R S)
    (hg : (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum (integralClosure R S)))
      ⊆ Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (integralClosure R S).val.toRingHom)) :
    Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap (integralClosure R S).val.toRingHom g)

declarations.name: quasiFinite_exists_finite_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
There is an `R`-subalgebra `S''` of `S`, contained in the integral closure `S'` and finite as
an `R`-module, such that `Spec(S) → Spec(S'')` is an open topological embedding and
`S''_g → S_g` is bijective for every `g ∈ S''` whose basic open `D(g)` lies in the image of that
map.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFinite_exists_finite_subalgebra
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFinite R S] :
    ∃ S'' : Subalgebra R S, S'' ≤ integralClosure R S ∧ Module.Finite R S'' ∧
      IsOpenEmbedding (PrimeSpectrum.comap S''.val.toRingHom) ∧
      ∀ g : S'', (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum S'')) ⊆
          Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap S''.val.toRingHom) →
        Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap S''.val.toRingHom g)

declarations.name: Algebra.relativeDimensionAt
declarations.doc:
The **relative dimension of `S/R` at a prime `𝔮` of `S`**, `dim_𝔮(S/R)`: the dimension of
the fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` through `𝔮` at the point `𝔮`. The fibre is the subspace
`comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {𝔭}` of `Spec S`, where `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, which is homeomorphic to
`Spec (S ⊗_R κ(𝔭))` by `PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def relativeDimensionAt (R : Type*) {S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime] : WithBot ℕ∞
declarations.comment:
The fibre `Spec (S ⊗_R κ(𝔭))` is the homeomorphic subspace
`comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {𝔭}` of `Spec S`, in which the source's point `q̄` is `𝔮` itself,
and `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮` is not an argument; `dim_q̄` is `topologicalKrullDimAt`. The source's finite
type hypothesis is unused by the definition and is left to the lemmas. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.relativeDimension
declarations.doc:
The **relative dimension of `S/R`**, `dim(S/R)`: the supremum of the relative dimensions
`dim_𝔮(S/R)` over all primes `𝔮` of `S`. It is `-∞` exactly when `S` is the zero ring.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def relativeDimension (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] : WithBot ℕ∞
declarations.comment:
The supremum of `Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮` over all primes `𝔮` of `S`,
indexed by `Spec S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: quasiFinite_over_polynomial_of_relativeDimension
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 00QE (Lemma 10.125.2). Let `R → S` be a finite type ring map, `q ⊂ S` a prime
lying over `p = q ∩ R`, with corresponding point `qbar` of the fibre spectrum
`Spec(S ⊗_R κ(p))`. If the relative dimension `dim_q(S/R)` equals `n : ℕ`, then there is
`g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, and an `R`-algebra ring map `φ : R[t_1, …, t_n] → S_g` such that
`S_g = S[1/g]` is finite type and quasi-finite over `R[t_1, …, t_n]` via `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFinite_over_polynomial_of_relativeDimension
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    (p : Ideal R) [hp : p.IsPrime]
    (qbar : PrimeSpectrum (p.Fiber S))
    (hqbar : PrimeSpectrum.comap (fiberMap R S p) qbar = q)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hdim : relativeDimensionAt R S p qbar = (n : ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ (g : S), g ∉ q.asIdeal ∧
      ∃ (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →+* Localization.Away g),
        φ.comp (algebraMap R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) = algebraMap R (Localization.Away g) ∧
        φ.FiniteType ∧ φ.QuasiFinite

declarations.name: Ideal.height_le_height_of_liesOver_of_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QF.** Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `𝔮` be a prime of `S` lying over the prime
`𝔭` of `R`, and assume `R → S` is quasi-finite at `𝔮`. Then `dim(S_𝔮) = 𝔮.height` is at most
`dim(R_𝔭) = 𝔭.height`. The source's finite type hypothesis is not needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.height_le_height_of_liesOver_of_quasiFiniteAt {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (𝔭 : Ideal R) (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔭.IsPrime] [𝔮.IsPrime]
    [𝔮.LiesOver 𝔭] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R 𝔮] : 𝔮.height ≤ 𝔭.height
declarations.comment:
`dim(S_𝔮)` and `dim(R_𝔭)` are `𝔮.height` and `𝔭.height`, model-independently by
`IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height`; quasi-finiteness at `𝔮` (Definition 00PL) is
`Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R 𝔮`, which the source's finite type hypothesis identifies with the
source's notion by `Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber`, and which the conclusion
needs without it. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_le_natCard_of_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QG.** Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a quasi-finite algebra over the polynomial
ring `k[t_i ; i ∈ σ]` in `n = #σ` variables. Then `dim(S) ≤ n`: a quasi-finite cover of
affine `n`-space has dimension at most `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_le_natCard_of_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial (k : Type*) [Field k]
    {σ S : Type*} [Finite σ] [CommRing S] [Algebra (MvPolynomial σ k) S]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite (MvPolynomial σ k) S] : ringKrullDim S ≤ Nat.card σ
declarations.comment:
The source's `k[t_1, …, t_n] ⊂ S` with `S` of finite type over `k` and the map
quasi-finite is weakened to `Algebra.QuasiFinite (MvPolynomial σ k) S` with `Finite σ`, which the
source's hypotheses imply (tag 00PM); neither finite type nor injectivity is used. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_setOf_relativeDimensionAt_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QH.** Let `R → S` be a finite type ring map and let `n : ℕ`. The set of primes `𝔮`
of `S` at which the fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` has dimension at most `n`, that is
`dim_𝔮(S/R) ≤ n`, is open in `Spec S`. Equivalently, every prime `𝔮` with `dim_𝔮(S/R) = n` has an
open neighbourhood `V` in `Spec S` such that `dim_{𝔮'}(S/R) ≤ n` for all `𝔮' ∈ V`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_setOf_relativeDimensionAt_le {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (n : ℕ) :
    IsOpen {𝔮 : PrimeSpectrum S |
      Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮.asIdeal ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)}
declarations.comment:
The source's open neighbourhood `V` of a single prime `𝔮` with `dim_𝔮(S/R) = n` is
pinned as the sublevel set `{𝔮 | dim_𝔮(S/R) ≤ n}`, whose openness the remark following the lemma
in the source gives as an equivalent reading of it; `dim_𝔮(S/R)` is `Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R
𝔮` (tag 00QD). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.relativeDimensionAt_comap_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a finite type ring map, let `R → R'` be any ring map, let `S' = R' ⊗_R S` and
let `f : Spec S' → Spec S` be the induced map on spectra. Then relative dimension is invariant
under this base change: `dim_{𝔮'}(S'/R') = dim_{f(𝔮')}(S/R)` for every prime `𝔮'` of `S'`. In
particular, for `n : ℕ`, the inverse image `f⁻¹({𝔮 | dim_𝔮(S/R) ≤ n})` is
`{𝔮' | dim_{𝔮'}(S'/R') ≤ n}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeDimensionAt_comap_eq (R S R' S' : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R' S']
    [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (𝔮' : PrimeSpectrum S') :
    Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S') 𝔮').asIdeal =
      Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R' 𝔮'.asIdeal
declarations.comment:
The source's equality of sublevel sets, for a bound `n ≥ 0`, is stated as the
pointwise equality `dim_{𝔮'}(S'/R') = dim_{f(𝔮')}(S/R)` of relative dimensions, to which it is
equivalent for all `n` at once; `S' = R' ⊗_R S` is the abstract `Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'`
and `f` is `PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S')`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isCompact_isOpen_setOf_relativeDimensionAt_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QJ.** Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite presentation and let `n : ℕ`. The set
`V_n = {𝔮 ∈ Spec S | dim_𝔮(S/R) ≤ n}` of primes at which the fibre of `Spec S → Spec R` has
dimension at most `n` is a quasi-compact open subset of `Spec S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompact_isOpen_setOf_relativeDimensionAt_le {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] (n : ℕ) :
    IsCompact {𝔮 : PrimeSpectrum S |
        Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮.asIdeal ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)} ∧
      IsOpen {𝔮 : PrimeSpectrum S |
        Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮.asIdeal ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)}
declarations.comment:
"Quasi-compact open" is `IsCompact V ∧ IsOpen V`, in the order and form
`PrimeSpectrum.isCompact_isOpen_iff` consumes; the second conjunct is tag 00QH for the underlying
finite type ring map, the first is the content here. `dim_𝔮(S/R)` is
`Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮` (tag 00QD). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ValuationRing.ringKrullDim_fiber_maximalIdeal_eq_ringKrullDim_fiber_bot_and_equidimensional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QK.** Let `R` be a valuation ring with residue field `k` and fraction field `K`,
and let `S` be a domain containing `R` which is of finite type over `R`. If `S ⊗_R k` is not the
zero ring, then `dim (S ⊗_R k) = dim (S ⊗_R K)`, and in fact `Spec (S ⊗_R k)` is
equidimensional, so that each of its irreducible components has dimension `dim (S ⊗_R K)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_fiber_maximalIdeal_eq_ringKrullDim_fiber_bot_and_equidimensional
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    [Algebra R S] [FaithfulSMul R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (hfib : Nontrivial ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).Fiber S)) :
    ringKrullDim ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).Fiber S) =
        ringKrullDim ((⊥ : Ideal R).Fiber S) ∧
      TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional
        (PrimeSpectrum ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).Fiber S))
declarations.comment:
`S ⊗_R k` is the fibre `(IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).Fiber S` and `S ⊗_R K` the
fibre `(⊥ : Ideal R).Fiber S`, the residue fields `κ(𝔪_R)` and `κ(⊥)` being `k` and `K` because
`R` is a local domain; `dim` is `ringKrullDim` and equidimensionality is Definition 0058. `S` a
domain containing `R` is `[IsDomain S]` with `[FaithfulSMul R S]`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A ring map `f : R →+* S` is *essentially of finite type* if `S` is, as an
`R`-algebra (via `f`), the localization at some submonoid of an `R`-algebra `T`
of finite type.
declarations.statement:
def IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType.{u} (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) : Prop

declarations.name: IsEssentiallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A ring map `f : R →+* S` is *essentially of finite presentation* if `S` is,
as an `R`-algebra (via `f`), the localization at some submonoid of an
`R`-algebra `T` of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
def IsEssentiallyOfFinitePresentation.{u} (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_directedSystem_finitePresentation_lift_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Every algebra is a direct limit of algebras of finite presentation.** For a ring map
`R → A` there is a directed system `G` of `R`-algebras of finite presentation, indexed by a
directed partially ordered set `Λ`, together with a compatible family of `R`-algebra maps
`g l : G l →ₐ[R] A` whose induced map `colim_l G l → A` is bijective. If `A` is of finite type
over `R`, the system can moreover be chosen with all transition maps surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_directedSystem_finitePresentation_lift_bijective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] :
    ∃ (Λ : Type (max u v)) (_ : PartialOrder Λ) (_ : Nonempty Λ) (_ : IsDirectedOrder Λ)
      (G : Λ → Type (max u v)) (_ : ∀ l, CommRing (G l)) (_ : ∀ l, Algebra R (G l))
      (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₐ[R] G j) (_ : DirectedSystem G fun i j h ↦ ⇑(f i j h))
      (g : ∀ l, G l →ₐ[R] A) (hg : ∀ i j h x, g j (f i j h x) = g i x),
      (∀ l, Algebra.FinitePresentation R (G l)) ∧
      (Algebra.FiniteType R A → ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), Function.Surjective (f i j h)) ∧
      Function.Bijective (DirectLimit.Algebra.lift G f A g hg)
declarations.comment:
Both sentences. The second is the implication
`Algebra.FiniteType R A → ∀ i j h, Function.Surjective (f i j h)` inside the same existential,
which is equivalent to stating it separately; `A = colim G l` is bijectivity of
`DirectLimit.Algebra.lift`, which pins the comparison map. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CommRingCat.finitePresentation_tfae_colimit_hom
declarations.doc:
**Algebras of finite presentation are the compact algebras.** For an `R`-algebra `S`, the
following are equivalent: the ring map `R → S` is of finite presentation; for every directed
system `A_λ` of `R`-algebras the canonical map `colim_λ Homᵣ(S, A_λ) → Homᵣ(S, colim_λ A_λ)` is
bijective; for every directed system `A_λ` of `R`-algebras that map is surjective.

A directed system of `R`-algebras is a functor `A : Λ ⥤ Under R` out of a nonempty directed
preordered set `Λ`, `colim_λ A_λ` is the vertex of any colimit cocone `c` on it, and the
canonical map is `colimit.desc` of the image of `c` under the hom functor `Homᵣ(S, -)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_tfae_colimit_hom {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (S : Under R) :
    List.TFAE
      [ S.hom.hom.FinitePresentation,
        ∀ (Λ : Type u) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)]
          (A : Λ ⥤ Under R) (c : Cocone A), IsColimit c →
            Function.Bijective
              (colimit.desc (A ⋙ CategoryTheory.coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op S))
                ((CategoryTheory.coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op S)).mapCocone c)),
        ∀ (Λ : Type u) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)]
          (A : Λ ⥤ Under R) (c : Cocone A), IsColimit c →
            Function.Surjective
              (colimit.desc (A ⋙ CategoryTheory.coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op S))
                ((CategoryTheory.coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op S)).mapCocone c)) ]
declarations.comment:
A directed system of `R`-algebras is a functor `Λ ⥤ Under R` out of a nonempty
directed preordered set, `colim_λ A_λ` is the vertex of any colimit cocone `c`, and the map
`colim_λ Homᵣ(S, A_λ) → Homᵣ(S, colim_λ A_λ)` is `colimit.desc` of `coyoneda.obj (op S)`
applied to `c`.

declarations.name: Algebra.FiniteType.iff_finiteType_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QP**. Being of finite type descends along a faithfully flat base change:
for a faithfully flat `R`-algebra `R'`, an `R`-algebra `S` is of finite type if and only
if `R' ⊗[R] S` is of finite type over `R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FiniteType.iff_finiteType_tensorProduct
    (R S R' : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R R'] :
    Algebra.FiniteType R S ↔ Algebra.FiniteType R' (R' ⊗[R] S)

registrations.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation.baseChange
registrations.comment: a base change of an algebra of finite presentation is of finite presentation

registrations.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
registrations.comment: finite presentation descends along a faithfully flat base change

declarations.name: exists_away_prod_of_localRingHom_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → S` be a ring map of commutative rings, and let `q ⊆ S` be a prime ideal lying over
the prime `p ⊆ R` (i.e. `p = q.comap φ`). Assume `S` is of finite presentation over `R`, and that
the induced map on localizations `φ_p : R_p → S_q` (`Localization.localRingHom`) is bijective.
Then there exist `f : R` with `f ∉ p` and an `R_f`-algebra `C` such that `S_f ≅ R_f × C` as
`R_f`-algebras, where `S_f := Localization.Away (φ f)` is given the `R_f`-algebra structure
induced by `Localization.awayMap φ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_away_prod_of_localRingHom_bijective (R S : Type) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R
  S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R S)) [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (hiso : Function.Bijective (Localization.localRingHom p q (algebraMap R S) hpq)) :
    ∃ f : R,
      f ∉ p ∧
        ∃ (C : Type) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra (Localization.Away f) C),
          letI : Algebra (Localization.Away f) (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S f)) :=
            (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap R S) f).toAlgebra
          Nonempty
            (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S f) ≃ₐ[Localization.Away f]
              (Localization.Away f × C))

declarations.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation.exists_algEquiv_localizationAway_awayLift_eq_of_algEquiv_atPrime
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring, let `S` and `S'` be `R`-algebras of finite presentation, and let
`q ⊆ S`, `q' ⊆ S'` be primes. If `e : S_q ≅ S'_{q'}` is an isomorphism of `R`-algebras,
then there are `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, `g' ∈ S'`, `g' ∉ q'` and an isomorphism of `R`-algebras
`Φ : S_g ≅ S'_{g'}`; moreover `Φ` induces `e` on the local rings: for every `y ∈ S_g`, the image of
`Φ y` under the canonical map `S'_{g'} → S'_{q'}` is `e` of the image of `y` under `S_g → S_q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_algEquiv_localizationAway_awayLift_eq_of_algEquiv_atPrime {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    {S' : Type v'} [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S'] (q : Ideal S)
    [q.IsPrime] (q' : Ideal S') [q'.IsPrime] (Sq : Type w) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [Algebra R Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq] (Sq' : Type w')
    [CommRing Sq'] [Algebra S' Sq'] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq' q'] [Algebra R Sq']
    [IsScalarTower R S' Sq'] (e : Sq ≃ₐ[R] Sq') :
    ∃ g, ∃ hg : g ∉ q, ∃ g', ∃ hg' : g' ∉ q',
      ∃ Φ : Localization.Away g ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away g',
        ∀ y : Localization.Away g,
          Localization.awayLift (algebraMap S' Sq') g'
              (IsLocalization.map_units Sq' (⟨g', hg'⟩ : q'.primeCompl)) (Φ y) =
            e (Localization.awayLift (algebraMap S Sq) g
              (IsLocalization.map_units Sq (⟨g, hg⟩ : q.primeCompl)) y)
declarations.comment:
The local rings `S_q`, `S'_{q'}` are any localizations at the primes
(`IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q` with `IsScalarTower R S Sq`, so that the `R`-algebra structure is
the composite `R → S → Sq`), and `S_g`, `S'_{g'}` are the models `Localization.Away g`,
`Localization.Away g'`, which by uniqueness of localizations costs no generality. Besides the
isomorphism `S_g ≅ S'_{g'}` of the statement, the theorem records that it is compatible with the
given isomorphism `S_q ≅ S'_{q'}`, which the proof in the source produces.

declarations.name: exists_essFiniteType_directedSystem_colimit
declarations.doc:
A local homomorphism `φ : R → S` of local rings is the colimit, over a directed
set `Λ`, of a system of local homomorphisms `ψ_λ : R_λ → S_λ` of local rings
such that each `R_λ` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ` and each `S_λ` is
essentially of finite type over `R_λ` (via `ψ_λ`).

The data is bundled in the existential as:
* `Λ` with a `Preorder`, `Nonempty` and `IsDirectedOrder` instance — the
  directed set;
* `Rl`, `Sl` — the families of local rings, with their `CommRing` and
  `IsLocalRing` structure;
