* `rf`, `sf` — the transition maps, forming directed systems (`dsR`, `dsS`);
* `ψ` — the family of local homomorphisms (`instLH`), commuting with the
  transition maps (`hψ`).

Condition (1) is encoded by the existence of ring isomorphisms
`eR : colim R_λ ≃+* R` and `eS : colim S_λ ≃+* S` identifying the colimit map
`Ring.DirectLimit.map ψ hψ` with `φ`, i.e. `φ ∘ eR = eS ∘ (colim ψ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_essFiniteType_directedSystem_colimit
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    (φ : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom φ] :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (instP : Preorder Λ),
    ∃ (_ : Nonempty Λ) (_ : @IsDirectedOrder Λ instP.toLE)
      (Rl : Λ → Type u) (Sl : Λ → Type u)
      (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (Rl i)) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (Sl i))
      (rf : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → (Rl i →+* Rl j))
      (sf : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → (Sl i →+* Sl j))
      (_ : ∀ i, @IsLocalRing (Rl i) _)
      (_ : ∀ i, @IsLocalRing (Sl i) _)
      (ψ : ∀ i, Rl i →+* Sl i)
      (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalHom (ψ i))
      -- `rf`, `sf` form directed systems of rings
      (_ : @DirectedSystem Λ instP Rl (fun i j h => ⇑(rf i j h)))
      (_ : @DirectedSystem Λ instP Sl (fun i j h => ⇑(sf i j h)))
      -- the squares commute: `ψ` is a morphism of directed systems
      (hψ : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), (ψ j).comp (rf i j h) = (sf i j h).comp (ψ i)),
      -- (1) the colimit of the system `R_λ → S_λ` is equal to `φ : R → S`
      (∃ (eR : Ring.DirectLimit Rl (fun i j h => ⇑(rf i j h)) ≃+* R)
         (eS : Ring.DirectLimit Sl (fun i j h => ⇑(sf i j h)) ≃+* S),
         φ.comp eR.toRingHom = eS.toRingHom.comp (Ring.DirectLimit.map ψ hψ)) ∧
      -- (2) each `R_λ` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ`
      (∀ i, (Int.castRingHom (Rl i)).EssFiniteType) ∧
      -- (3) each `S_λ` is essentially of finite type over `R_λ` (via `ψ_λ`)
      (∀ i, (ψ i).EssFiniteType)

declarations.name: exists_colimit_presentation_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings
which is essentially of finite type.  Then `φ` is a filtered colimit of a system
of local homomorphisms `φ_λ : R_λ → S_λ` of local rings, where each `R_λ` is
essentially of finite type over `ℤ`, each `S_λ` is essentially of finite type
over `R_λ`, and for `λ ≤ μ` the map `S_λ ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ → S_μ` realizes `S_μ` as a
localization of a quotient of `S_λ ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_colimit_presentation_of_essFiniteType
    (R S : Type) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] (hφ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S))
    (hft : Algebra.EssFiniteType R S) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type) (_ : PartialOrder Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty Λ)
      (Rf Sf : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat) (φsys : Rf ⟶ Sf),
      -- each `R_λ`, `S_λ` is a local ring
      (∀ i, IsLocalRing (Rf.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i, IsLocalRing (Sf.obj i)) ∧
      -- each `φ_λ` is a local homomorphism
      (∀ i, IsLocalHom (φsys.app i).hom) ∧
      -- each transition map is a local homomorphism
      (∀ (i j : Λ) (h : i ≤ j), IsLocalHom (Rf.map h.hom).hom) ∧
      (∀ (i j : Λ) (h : i ≤ j), IsLocalHom (Sf.map h.hom).hom) ∧
      -- (1) the colimit of the system is `φ : R → S` (up to canonical isomorphism)
      (∃ (iR : colimit Rf ≅ CommRingCat.of R) (iS : colimit Sf ≅ CommRingCat.of S),
        iR.inv ≫ colimMap φsys ≫ iS.hom = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      -- (2) each `R_λ` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ`
      (∀ i, Algebra.EssFiniteType ℤ (Rf.obj i)) ∧
      -- (3) each `S_λ` is essentially of finite type over `R_λ`
      (∀ i, letI : Algebra (Rf.obj i) (Sf.obj i) := (φsys.app i).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.EssFiniteType (Rf.obj i) (Sf.obj i)) ∧
      -- (4) for `i ≤ j`, `S_j` is the localization of a quotient of `S_i ⊗_{R_i} R_j`
      (∀ (i j : Λ) (h : i ≤ j), Stacks.EssentialFiniteness.LocalColimit.LocalizationOfQuotient φsys
        h)

declarations.name: Stacks.EssentialFiniteness.ColimitPresentation.main_theorem_00qv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 00QV (Lemma 10.127.11).**

Let `φ : R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings. If `S` is essentially of finite
presentation over `R` (via `φ`), then `φ` is a filtered colimit of a directed system of local
homomorphisms `ψ_λ : R_λ → S_λ` between local rings, with local transition maps, such that:
(1) the colimit of the system is `φ`; (2) each `R_λ` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ`;
(3) each `ψ_λ` is essentially of finite type; (4) for `λ ≤ μ`, the canonical base-change map
`S_λ ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ → S_μ` exhibits `S_μ` as a localization of `S_λ ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ` at a prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_00qv
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : IsLocalHom φ)
    (hfp : φ.EssFinitePresentation) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : Preorder Λ) (_ : Nonempty Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·))
      (Robj : Λ → Type u) (Sobj : Λ → Type u)
      (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (Robj i)) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (Sobj i))
      (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (Robj i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (Sobj i))
      (fR : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → Robj i →+* Robj j)
      (fS : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → Sobj i →+* Sobj j)
      (ψ : ∀ i, Robj i →+* Sobj i)
      (comm : ∀ i j (hij : i ≤ j), (ψ j).comp (fR i j hij) = (fS i j hij).comp (ψ i)),
      -- the transition maps form directed systems of rings
      (DirectedSystem Robj (fun i j h => (fR i j h : Robj i → Robj j))) ∧
      (DirectedSystem Sobj (fun i j h => (fS i j h : Sobj i → Sobj j))) ∧
      -- all transition maps and all `ψ_λ` are local homomorphisms
      (∀ i j (hij : i ≤ j), IsLocalHom (fR i j hij)) ∧
      (∀ i j (hij : i ≤ j), IsLocalHom (fS i j hij)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsLocalHom (ψ i)) ∧
      -- (1) the colimit of the system `R_λ → S_λ` recovers `φ : R → S`
      (∃ (eR : Ring.DirectLimit Robj (fun i j h => (fR i j h : Robj i → Robj j)) ≃+* R)
         (eS : Ring.DirectLimit Sobj (fun i j h => (fS i j h : Sobj i → Sobj j)) ≃+* S),
         φ.comp eR.toRingHom = eS.toRingHom.comp (Ring.DirectLimit.map ψ comm)) ∧
      -- (2) each `R_λ` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ`
      (∀ i, Algebra.EssFiniteType ℤ (Robj i)) ∧
      -- (3) each fiber map `ψ_λ` is essentially of finite type
      (∀ i, (ψ i).EssFiniteType) ∧
      -- (4) each transition map is a localization at a prime after base change
      (∀ i j (hij : i ≤ j),
        IsLocalizationAtPrimeOfBaseChange fR fS ψ comm i j hij)

declarations.name: RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation.exists_isColimit_essFiniteType_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00QX.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings which is
essentially of finite presentation and let `M` be a finitely presented `S`-module. Then
there are a nonempty directed set `Λ`, a system `φ : A ⟶ B` of local homomorphisms
`A.obj i → B.obj i` of local rings, and `B.obj i`-modules `N.obj i`, such that (1) the
colimits of `A`, `B` and `N` are `R`, `S` and `M`, compatibly with `algebraMap R S` and
with the `S`-action on `M`; (2) each `A.obj i` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ`;
(3) each `A.obj i → B.obj i` is essentially of finite type; (4) each `N.obj i` is a
finite `B.obj i`-module; (5) for `i ≤ j` the ring `B.obj j` is a localization of
`B.obj i ⊗_{A.obj i} A.obj j` at a prime ideal; (6) for `i ≤ j` the transition map
`N.obj i → N.obj j` exhibits `N.obj j` as the base change of `N.obj i` along
`B.obj i → B.obj j`. Moreover each structure map `A.obj i → R` of the colimit cocone is
a local homomorphism, so that each transition map `A.obj i → A.obj j` is local too and
each `𝔪_{A.obj i}` is the contraction of the maximal ideal of `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation.exists_isColimit_essFiniteType_module
    {R S M : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : Preorder Λ) (_ : Nonempty Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·))
      (A B : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : A ⟶ B) (N : Λ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (_ : ∀ i, Module (B.obj i) (N.obj i))
      (hsmul : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j) (b : B.obj i) (m : N.obj i),
        N.map h (b • m) = B.map h b • N.map h m)
      (ρ : A ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (CommRingCat.of R))
      (σ : B ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (CommRingCat.of S))
      (ν : N ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of M))
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk (CommRingCat.of R) ρ))
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk (CommRingCat.of S) σ))
      (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk (AddCommGrpCat.of M) ν)),
      (∀ i, φ.app i ≫ σ.app i = ρ.app i ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      (∀ (i : Λ) (b : B.obj i) (m : N.obj i),
        (ν.app i (b • m) : M) = HSMul.hSMul (α := S) (β := M) (σ.app i b) (ν.app i m)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsLocalRing (A.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i, IsLocalRing (B.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsLocalHom (φ.app i).hom) ∧
      (∀ i, IsLocalHom (ρ.app i).hom) ∧
      (∀ i, Algebra.EssFiniteType ℤ (A.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ i, (φ.app i).hom.EssFiniteType) ∧
      (∀ i, Module.Finite (B.obj i) (N.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j),
        letI := (pushout.desc (B.map h) (φ.app j) (φ.naturality h).symm).hom.toAlgebra
        ∃ (q : Ideal ↑(pushout (φ.app i) (A.map h))) (_ : q.IsPrime),
          IsLocalization q.primeCompl ↑(B.obj j)) ∧
      (∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j),
        letI : Algebra ↑(B.obj i) ↑(B.obj j) := (B.map h).hom.toAlgebra
        letI : Module ↑(B.obj i) ↑(N.obj j) := Module.compHom _ (B.map h).hom
        letI : IsScalarTower ↑(B.obj i) ↑(B.obj j) ↑(N.obj j) :=
          .of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
        IsBaseChange ↑(B.obj j)
          (⟨(N.map h).hom.toAddHom, hsmul h⟩ :
            ↑(N.obj i) →ₗ[↑(B.obj i)] ↑(N.obj j)))
declarations.comment:
The system is a pair of functors `A B : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat` with a natural
transformation `φ : A ⟶ B`, and a functor `N : Λ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` with `B.obj i`-module
structures compatible with the transition maps; `S_λ ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ` is the pushout in
`CommRingCat` and (6) is `IsBaseChange`. Hypothesis (1) is
`RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation` (Definition 00QM (2)), Mathlib having no such
predicate; (2) and (3) are Mathlib's `EssFiniteType` (Definition 00QM (1)). The
conclusion also asserts that each structure map `ρ_λ : A.obj i → R` is local, which is
the source's "system of local homomorphisms of local rings" read as a system in the
category of local rings; it is realized by the construction of 00QU and is not implied
by (1)–(6). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CommRingCat.exists_colimitPresentation_arrow_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**A ring map is a directed colimit of finite type ring maps between `ℤ`-algebras of finite
type.** Given a ring map `X : R ⟶ S`, there are a nonempty directed poset `Λ` and a diagram of
ring maps `R_λ ⟶ S_λ` over `Λ`, together with a colimit cocone exhibiting `R ⟶ S` as its
colimit, such that each `R_λ` is of finite type over `ℤ` and each `R_λ ⟶ S_λ` is of finite
type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_colimitPresentation_arrow_finiteType (X : Arrow CommRingCat.{u}) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty Λ)
      (pres : ColimitPresentation Λ X), ∀ i : Λ,
        Algebra.FiniteType ℤ (pres.diag.obj i).left ∧ (pres.diag.obj i).hom.hom.FiniteType
declarations.comment:
A ring map is an object of `Arrow CommRingCat`, and the source's item (1) is the
bundled `Limits.ColimitPresentation Λ X` (diagram, cocone, colimiting), colimits in an arrow
category being computed entrywise. The index is the source's nonempty directed poset; Mathlib's
`ObjectProperty.ind` form follows from this one. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_ringHomDirectedSystem_of_finiteType
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringHomDirectedSystem_of_finiteType
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hft : φ.FiniteType) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : Preorder Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty Λ)
      (sys : RingHomDirectedSystem Λ),
      -- (1) the colimit recovers `φ : R → S`
      (∃ (α : sys.colimR ≃+* R) (β : sys.colimS ≃+* S),
        (β : sys.colimS →+* S).comp sys.colimφ = φ.comp (α : sys.colimR →+* R)) ∧
      -- (2) each `R_λ` is of finite type over `ℤ`
      (∀ l, (algebraMap ℤ (sys.R l)).FiniteType) ∧
      -- (3) each `φ_λ` is of finite type
      (∀ l, (sys.φ l).FiniteType) ∧
      -- (4) each base-change map `θ_{λμ}` is surjective
      (∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ≤ j), Function.Surjective (sys.baseChangeMap h))

declarations.name: exists_ringMapSystem_of_finitePresentation
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringMapSystem_of_finitePresentation {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R
  →+* S)
    (hf : f.FinitePresentation) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder Λ) (_ : Nonempty Λ) (_ : IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·))
      (𝓟 : RingMapSystem.{u, u} Λ)
      (eR : 𝓟.source.colimit ≃+* R) (eS : 𝓟.target.colimit ≃+* S),
      -- (1) Colimit: the square commutes (`f ∘ eR = eS ∘ colim ψ`).
      (∀ x, f (eR x) = eS (𝓟.colimitMap x)) ∧
      -- (2) Finite type base: each `R_λ` is of finite type over `ℤ`.
      (∀ i, Algebra.FiniteType ℤ (𝓟.source.R i)) ∧
      -- (3) Finite type fibers: each `ψ_λ` is of finite type.
      (∀ i, (𝓟.ψ i).FiniteType) ∧
      -- (4) Cartesian transitions: the base change maps are isomorphisms.
      (∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (hij : i ≤ j), Function.Bijective (𝓟.baseChange hij))

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_subring_finiteType_int_isPushout_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**A finitely presented algebra with a finitely presented module descends to a subring of
finite type over `ℤ`.** Let `R → S` be of finite presentation and let `M` be a finitely
presented `S`-module. Then there are a subring `R₀ ⊆ R` of finite type over `ℤ`, an `R₀`-algebra
`S₀` of finite type and a finite `S₀`-module `M₀`, together with an algebra map `S₀ → S` and an
`S₀`-linear map `f : M₀ → M`, presenting `S` as `R ⊗_{R₀} S₀` and `M` as `S ⊗_{S₀} M₀`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_subring_finiteType_int_isPushout_isBaseChange
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M] :
    ∃ (R₀ : Subring R) (S₀ M₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀)
      (_ : Algebra S₀ S) (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ S) (_ : AddCommGroup M₀)
      (_ : Module S₀ M₀) (_ : Module S₀ M) (_ : IsScalarTower S₀ S M) (f : M₀ →ₗ[S₀] M),
      Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ Algebra.FiniteType R₀ S₀ ∧ Module.Finite S₀ M₀ ∧
        Algebra.IsPushout R₀ R S₀ S ∧ IsBaseChange S f
declarations.comment:
Stated as a descent along a single subring `R₀ ⊆ R` of finite type over `ℤ`
rather than as a directed system: the six clauses of the source are recovered by taking for `Λ`
the subrings of `R` of finite type over `ℤ` containing `R₀` and base changing `S₀` and `M₀`
along `R₀ → R_λ`, and conversely the source's system gives such an `R₀` as the image of any
`R_λ` in `R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_of_ringKrullDim_eq_add
declarations.doc:
**Miracle flatness, Stacks 00R4.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local
rings with `R` regular and `S` Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. `depth_{𝔪_S}(S) = dim(S)`. If
`dim(S) = dim(R) + dim(S/𝔪_R S)`, then `S` is flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_of_ringKrullDim_eq_add
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    (hS : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay S S)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim S =
      ringKrullDim R + ringKrullDim (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))) :
    Module.Flat R S
declarations.comment:
Regularity of the Noetherian local ring `R` is `IsRegularLocalRing R`;
Cohen-Macaulayness of `S` (Definition 00N8) is `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay S S`, i.e.
`depth_{𝔪_S}(S) = dim S`; and `dim(S/𝔪_R S)` is the Krull dimension of the quotient of `S` by the
image ideal of the maximal ideal of `R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.isMaximalCohenMacaulay_self_and_ringKrullDim_eq_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00R5.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with `R`
Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. `depth_{𝔪_R}(R) = dim(R)`. If `S` is flat over `R` and is either finite over
`R` or of dimension at most `dim(R)`, then `S` is Cohen–Macaulay and `dim(R) = dim(S)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.isMaximalCohenMacaulay_self_and_ringKrullDim_eq_of_flat
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    [Module.Flat R S] (hR : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R)
    (h : Module.Finite R S ∨ ringKrullDim S ≤ ringKrullDim R) :
    Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay S S ∧ ringKrullDim R = ringKrullDim S
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of a Noetherian local ring `A` (Definition 00N8) is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A A`, i.e. `depth_{𝔪_A}(A) = dim A`; the source's two alternatives
are the disjunctive hypothesis `h` over the flatness common to both. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.exists_ge_flat_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
Let `(A i → B i, N i)` be a directed system as in 00QX, with colimits `R → S` and `M`: each
`A i` is essentially of finite type over `ℤ`, each `A i → B i` is a local homomorphism of local
rings essentially of finite type, each transition map `A i → A j` is local, each `N i` is a finite
`B i`-module, each `B j` is a localization of `B i ⊗_{A i} A j` at a prime ideal, and each `N j` is
the base change of `N i` along `B i → B j`. If `M` is flat over `R`, then for every index `i` there
is `j ≥ i` such that `N j` is flat over `A j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ge_flat_of_isColimit
    {R S M : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Flat R M]
    {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)]
    {A B : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}} {φ : A ⟶ B} {N : Λ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}}
    (mod : ∀ i, Module (B.obj i) (N.obj i))
    (hsmul : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j) (b : B.obj i) (m : N.obj i),
      N.map h (b • m) = B.map h b • N.map h m)
    {ρ : A ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (CommRingCat.of R)}
    {σ : B ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (CommRingCat.of S)}
    {ν : N ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of M)}
    (hR : IsColimit (Cocone.mk (CommRingCat.of R) ρ))
    (_hS : IsColimit (Cocone.mk (CommRingCat.of S) σ))
    (hM : IsColimit (Cocone.mk (AddCommGrpCat.of M) ν))
    (hφ : ∀ i, φ.app i ≫ σ.app i = ρ.app i ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S))
    (hν : ∀ (i : Λ) (b : B.obj i) (m : N.obj i),
      (ν.app i (b • m) : M) = HSMul.hSMul (α := S) (β := M) (σ.app i b) (ν.app i m))
    (hAlocal : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (A.obj i)) (hBlocal : ∀ i, IsLocalRing (B.obj i))
    (hφlocal : ∀ i, IsLocalHom (φ.app i).hom)
    (hAmaplocal : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j), IsLocalHom (A.map h).hom)
    (hAft : ∀ i, Algebra.EssFiniteType ℤ (A.obj i))
    (hφft : ∀ i, (φ.app i).hom.EssFiniteType)
    (hNfin : ∀ i, Module.Finite (B.obj i) (N.obj i))
    (hBloc : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j),
      letI := (pushout.desc (B.map h) (φ.app j) (φ.naturality h).symm).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ (q : Ideal ↑(pushout (φ.app i) (A.map h))) (_ : q.IsPrime),
        IsLocalization q.primeCompl ↑(B.obj j))
    (hNbc : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (h : i ⟶ j),
      letI : Algebra ↑(B.obj i) ↑(B.obj j) := (B.map h).hom.toAlgebra
      letI : Module ↑(B.obj i) ↑(N.obj j) := Module.compHom _ (B.map h).hom
      letI : IsScalarTower ↑(B.obj i) ↑(B.obj j) ↑(N.obj j) :=
        .of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
      IsBaseChange ↑(B.obj j)
        (⟨(N.map h).hom.toAddHom, hsmul h⟩ : ↑(N.obj i) →ₗ[↑(B.obj i)] ↑(N.obj j)))
    (i : Λ) :
    ∃ j, i ≤ j ∧
      (letI : Module ↑(A.obj j) ↑(N.obj j) := Module.compHom _ (φ.app j).hom
       Module.Flat ↑(A.obj j) ↑(N.obj j))
declarations.comment:
The system "as in Lemma 00QX" is spelled out as the data and the six
conditions concluded by `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation.exists_isColimit_essFiniteType_module`, together with locality of the transition maps `A i → A j`, which is the source's "system of local homomorphisms of local rings" read as a system in the
category of local rings and is what 00MO needs to know `(𝔪 i) A j` is proper. The
hypotheses of 00QX are not assumed, being either unused or consequences of the system. The
conclusion is the cofinal form (`∀ i, ∃ j ≥ i`), which is what the source's proof produces
and what the dependents use. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.flat_algebra_and_flat_of_flat_quotient_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Critère de platitude par fibres.** Let `R → S → S'` be local homomorphisms of
local rings with `R → S` and `R → S'` essentially of finite presentation, let `𝔪` be the maximal
ideal of `R`, and let `M` be a nonzero `S'`-module of finite presentation over `S'`. If the fibre
`M/𝔪M` is flat over `S/𝔪S` and `M` is flat over `R`, then `S` is flat over `R` and `M` is flat
over `S`.

Here `𝔪S` is `Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R)` and `M/𝔪M` is `M ⧸ 𝔪S • ⊤` taken over
`S`, so that it is a module over `S/𝔪S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.flat_algebra_and_flat_of_flat_quotient_maximalIdeal
    {R S S' M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsLocalRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S S')]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [Module S' M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [IsScalarTower S S' M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S' M] [Nontrivial M]
    [Module.Flat (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
      (M ⧸ ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))]
    [Module.Flat R M]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation)
    (hS' : (algebraMap R S').EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) :
    Module.Flat R S ∧ Module.Flat S M
declarations.comment:
Hypothesis (1) is `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation` (Definition 00QM (2))
applied to `algebraMap R S` and `algebraMap R S'`, Mathlib having no such predicate. The fibre is
`M ⧸ (𝔪S) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)` over the ring `S ⧸ 𝔪S`, as in 06A5, and the two conclusions are
conjoined; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.ringKrullDim_quotient_add_length_eq_and_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00R9.** Let `k` be a field and `S` a finite type `k`-algebra which is Cohen–Macaulay
(every local ring `S_𝔭` satisfies `depth_{𝔪}(S_𝔭) = dim S_𝔭`) and equidimensional of dimension
`d`. Let `f = f₁, …, f_i` be elements of `S` cutting out a nonempty closed subset
`V(f₁, …, f_i)` of `Spec S` of dimension at most `d - i`. Then that dimension is exactly `d - i`,
and `f₁, …, f_i` is a regular sequence in `S_𝔮` for every prime `𝔮 ⊇ (f₁, …, f_i)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_quotient_add_length_eq_and_isRegular
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (hS : ∀ (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime],
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime p))
    (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional (PrimeSpectrum S)) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ringKrullDim S = d) (f : List S) (hf : Ideal.ofList f ≠ ⊤)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (S ⧸ Ideal.ofList f) + f.length ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ringKrullDim (S ⧸ Ideal.ofList f) + f.length = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], Ideal.ofList f ≤ q →
        ∀ (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q],
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular Sq (f.map (algebraMap S Sq))
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of a Noetherian local ring is `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A A`
(Definition 00N8); that of the Noetherian ring `S` (Definition 00NC) is spelled out over its
localizations at primes, as in tag 00ND. `dim V(f₁, …, f_i)` is `ringKrullDim (S ⧸ Ideal.ofList f)`
(`ringKrullDim_quotient`), and `≤ d - i` is written `+ f.length ≤ d` in `WithBot ℕ∞`, the source's
truncating subtraction being false as stated. The extra hypothesis `Ideal.ofList f ≠ ⊤` excludes
the empty locus, where the source's equality fails. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_setOf_isRegular_fiber_of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_of_equidimensional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RA.** Let `R → S` be a finite type ring map and let `d` be such that every
nonempty fibre `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is Cohen–Macaulay (each of its local rings `A` satisfies
`depth_{𝔪_A}(A) = dim A`) and equidimensional of dimension `d`. Let `f = f₁, …, f_i` be elements
of `S`. Then the set of points `𝔮` of `V(f₁, …, f_i)` at which `f₁, …, f_i` is a regular sequence
in `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮`, where `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, is open in `V(f₁, …, f_i)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_setOf_isRegular_fiber_of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_of_equidimensional
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (d : ℕ)
    (hfib : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], Nontrivial (p.Fiber S) →
      (∀ (Q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [Q.IsPrime],
          Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime Q) (Localization.AtPrime Q)) ∧
        TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional (PrimeSpectrum (p.Fiber S)) ∧
        ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (f : List S) :
    IsOpen {q : ↥(PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Ideal.ofList f : Set S)) |
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular
        (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal ⧸
          (q.1.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal)))
        (f.map (algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal ⧸
          (q.1.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q.1.asIdeal)))))}
declarations.comment:
`V(f₁, …, f_i)` is the subspace `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ↑(Ideal.ofList f)` of
`Spec S` and openness is for its subspace topology. `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` is the quotient of
`Localization.AtPrime 𝔮` by the ideal generated by `𝔭 = 𝔮.under R`, which is the fibre
`κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S_𝔮` of tag 00PK by `Ideal.Fiber.ringEquivQuotient` but carries the canonical
`S`-algebra structure. Cohen-Macaulayness of the fibre (Definition 00NC) is spelled out over its
primes at `Localization.AtPrime` and equidimensionality of dimension `d` as Definition 0058 plus
`ringKrullDim = d`, as in tags 00ND and 00R9; the hypothesis is guarded by the fibre being
nonzero, where the source's condition on its components has content. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_setOf_exact_baseChange_fiber_of_flat_of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RB.** Let `R` be Noetherian, let `R → S` be a flat ring map of finite type all of
whose nonempty fibres `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` are Cohen–Macaulay (each of their local rings `A` satisfies
`depth_{𝔪_A}(A) = dim A`) of dimension `d`, and let `0 → F_{e+1} →[φ e] F_e → ⋯ → F_1 →[φ 0] F_0`
be a finite complex of finite free `S`-modules. Then the set of primes `𝔮` of `S` at which the
fibre complex `F̄_{•,𝔮} = F_{•,𝔮} ⊗_R κ(𝔭) = (S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮) ⊗_S F_•`, where `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, is exact
at `F̄_{e+1}, …, F̄_1` is open in `Spec S`.

The fibre hypothesis is not used: the conclusion holds for every flat ring map of finite type over
a Noetherian ring, `isOpen_setOf_exact_baseChange_fiber_of_flat`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_setOf_exact_baseChange_fiber_of_flat_of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Module.Flat R S] (d : ℕ)
    (_hfib :
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        Nontrivial (p.Fiber S) →
          (∀ (Q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [Q.IsPrime],
              Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime Q) (Localization.AtPrime Q)) ∧
            ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (e : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Type*) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (F i)] [∀ i, Module S (F i)]
    [∀ i, Module.Free S (F i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite S (F i)] (φ : ∀ i, F (i + 1) →ₗ[S] F i)
    (hφ : ∀ k < e, φ k ∘ₗ φ (k + 1) = 0) :
    IsOpen
      {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
        Function.Injective
            (LinearMap.baseChange
              (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal ⧸
                (q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)))
              (φ e)) ∧
          ∀ k < e,
            Function.Exact
              (LinearMap.baseChange
                (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal ⧸
                  (q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)))
                (φ (k + 1)))
              (LinearMap.baseChange
                (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal ⧸
                  (q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)))
                (φ k))}
declarations.comment:
The complex is indexed as in 00N1: `φ k : F (k+1) → F k`, read for `k ≤ e`, on
finite free `S`-modules `F i` (the source's `S^{n_i}`), and exactness is injectivity of `φ e` and
exactness at `F_e, …, F_1`. `F_𝔮 ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is the base change of `F` along `S → S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮`, which
is `S_𝔮 ⊗_R κ(𝔭)`. The fibres are Cohen–Macaulay of dimension `d` as in the source: every local
ring of a nonempty fibre is Cohen–Macaulay, and the fibre has Krull dimension `d`; the proof does
not use this hypothesis, going through Theorem 00RC instead of Lemma 00RA.

declarations.name: Module.isOpen_setOf_flat_localizedModule_atPrime
declarations.doc:
For a finitely presented ring map `R → S` and a finitely presented
`S`-module `M`, the locus of primes `q` of `S` at which `M_q` is flat over `R` is open.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.atPrime_iff_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_and_relativeDimensionAt_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RE.** Let `S` be a finite type algebra over a field `k`, let
`φ : k[y_1, …, y_d] → S` be a map of `k`-algebras from a polynomial ring in `d = Nat.card σ`
variables, and let `𝔮` be a prime of `S` at which `φ` is quasi-finite, with localization
`S_𝔮 = Sq`. Then `S_𝔮` is flat over `k[y_1, …, y_d]` if and only if `S_𝔮` is Cohen–Macaulay and
`dim_𝔮(S/k) = d`. Taking `Sq = Localization.AtPrime 𝔮` and `Set.ext`, this is the source's
equality of the flat locus and the Cohen–Macaulay locus of relative dimension `d` inside
`Spec(S)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.atPrime_iff_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_and_relativeDimensionAt_eq
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] {σ : Type*}
    [Finite σ] [Algebra (MvPolynomial σ k) S] [IsScalarTower k (MvPolynomial σ k) S]
    (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt (MvPolynomial σ k) 𝔮] (Sq : Type*)
    [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq 𝔮] [IsLocalRing Sq]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial σ k) Sq] [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial σ k) S Sq] :
    Module.Flat (MvPolynomial σ k) Sq ↔
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay Sq Sq ∧ Algebra.relativeDimensionAt k 𝔮 = Nat.card σ
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of the Noetherian local ring `S_𝔮` (Definition 00N8) is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay Sq Sq`; `k[y_1, …, y_d]` is `MvPolynomial σ k` with
`d = Nat.card σ`; the localization is an abstract `IsLocalization.AtPrime`; and the equality of
subsets of `Spec S` is stated pointwise at `𝔮`, with the source's global quasi-finiteness of `φ`
weakened to quasi-finiteness at `𝔮` (Definition 00PL). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RF.** Let `S` be a finite type algebra over a field `k`. The set of primes `𝔮` of
`S` such that the local ring `S_𝔮` is Cohen–Macaulay is open in `Spec S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_localization (k S : Type*) [Field k]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] :
    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
        (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)}
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of the local ring `S_𝔮` (Definition 00N8) is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay` of `Localization.AtPrime 𝔮` over itself. The proof is the case
`R = k` of Lemma 00RH; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_and_dense_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RG.** Let `S` be a finite type algebra over a field `k`. The set of primes `𝔮` of
`S` at which `S_𝔮` is Cohen–Macaulay is a dense open subset of `Spec S`: it is open by Lemma 00RF
and contains every minimal prime, where the local ring has dimension zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_and_dense_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_localization (k S : Type*)
    [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] :
    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
        Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
          (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)} ∧
      Dense {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
        Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
          (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)}
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of `S_𝔮` is `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay` of
`Localization.AtPrime 𝔮` over itself; "dense open" is the conjunction of `IsOpen` and
`Dense`.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber_and_relativeDimensionAt_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RH.** Let `R → S` be flat of finite presentation and let `d ≥ 0`. The set of
primes `𝔮` of `S` such that, with `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, the fibre ring `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` is Cohen–Macaulay and
`dim_𝔮(S/R) = d` is open in `Spec S`. The fibre ring is spelled as the localization of `S/𝔭S` at
the image of `𝔮`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.isOpen_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber_and_relativeDimensionAt_eq
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] (d : ℕ) :
    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S))))) ∧
        Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R q.asIdeal = d}
declarations.comment:
The fibre ring `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` is `Localization.AtPrime` of the image of `𝔮` in
`S/𝔭S`, `𝔭 = 𝔮.under R`, as in 00RK; Cohen-Macaulayness of a local ring (Definition 00N8) is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A A`, and `dim_𝔮(S/R)` is `Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮`.

declarations.name: Algebra.isOpen_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber_and_dense_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RI.** Let `R → S` be flat of finite presentation. The set `W` of primes `𝔮` of `S`
at which the fibre ring `S_𝔮 ⊗_R κ(𝔭)`, `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, is Cohen–Macaulay is open in `Spec S`, and
for every prime `𝔭` of `R` its trace on the fibre `Spec S ×_{Spec R} {𝔭}` of `Spec S → Spec R` is
dense in that fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.isOpen_setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber_and_dense_fiber
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] :
    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))} ∧
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Dense ((↑) ⁻¹' {q : PrimeSpectrum S |
        Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))} :
        Set (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {p}))
declarations.comment:
The fibre ring is `Localization.AtPrime` of the image of `𝔮` in `S/𝔭S`, as in
00RH and 00RK. The fibre over `𝔭` is the subspace `comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {𝔭}` of `Spec S`
and density is for its subspace topology; openness is asserted in all of `Spec S`, which implies
openness in each fibre. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.isMaximalCohenMacaulay_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `K/k` be a field extension and
let `T = K ⊗_k S` be the base change, presented as a pushout square. Let `𝔮K` be a prime of `T`
lying over the prime `𝔮` of `S`, and let `Sq = S_𝔮` and `TqK = T_{𝔮K}` be the local rings at
them. Then `S_𝔮` is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if `T_{𝔮K}` is Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMaximalCohenMacaulay_iff (k K S T : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [CommRing S]
    [CommRing T] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k T] [Algebra K T] [Algebra S T]
    [IsScalarTower k K T] [IsScalarTower k S T] [Algebra.IsPushout k K S T]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime] (𝔮K : Ideal T) [𝔮K.IsPrime]
    [𝔮K.LiesOver 𝔮] (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq 𝔮]
    [IsLocalRing Sq] (TqK : Type*) [CommRing TqK] [Algebra T TqK]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime TqK 𝔮K] [IsLocalRing TqK] :
    Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay Sq Sq ↔ Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay TqK TqK
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of a Noetherian local ring `A` (Definition 00N8) is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A A` (tag 00NF); the base change `K ⊗_k S` is an arbitrary pushout
square of `k`-algebras `Algebra.IsPushout k K S T`, as in the sibling 00P4; the two local rings
are abstract `IsLocalization.AtPrime`s; and `𝔮_K` lying over `𝔮` is `Ideal.LiesOver`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber_eq_preimage_comap
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be of finite type, let `R → R'` be any ring map and let `S' = R' ⊗_R S`,
presented as a pushout square. Let `f : Spec S' → Spec S` be the map of the ring map `S → S'`.
Then the set `W'` of primes `𝔮'` of `S'` whose fibre ring `S'_{𝔮'} ⊗_{R'} κ(𝔭')`,
`𝔭' = R' ∩ 𝔮'`, is Cohen–Macaulay is the preimage `f ⁻¹' W` of the corresponding set `W` for `S`
over `R`. The fibre ring is the localization of `S/𝔭S` at the prime `𝔮/𝔭S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setOf_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber_eq_preimage_comap (R R' S S' : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra R S'] [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R R' S S'] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    {𝔮' : PrimeSpectrum S' |
        Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
          (Localization.AtPrime (𝔮'.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((𝔮'.asIdeal.under R').map (algebraMap R' S')))))
          (Localization.AtPrime (𝔮'.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((𝔮'.asIdeal.under R').map (algebraMap R' S')))))} =
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S') ⁻¹'
        {𝔮 : PrimeSpectrum S |
          Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
            (Localization.AtPrime (𝔮.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
              ((𝔮.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))
            (Localization.AtPrime (𝔮.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
              ((𝔮.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))}
declarations.comment:
The base change is an arbitrary pushout square `Algebra.IsPushout R R' S S'`, as in
the siblings 00P3, 00P4 and 00SS, so `f` is `PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S')`. The fibre
ring `S_𝔮 ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is `Localization.AtPrime` of the image of `𝔮` in `S/𝔭S`, with `𝔭 = 𝔮.under R`,
as in 00RH and 00RI, and Cohen-Macaulayness of a local ring (Definition 00N8) is
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A A` (tag 00NF). The conclusion is the source's equality of sets of
primes; `Set.ext_iff` gives the pointwise form. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_algEquiv_pi_of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RL.** Let `R → S` be flat, of finite presentation and with Cohen–Macaulay fibres,
that is with every fibre ring `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` Cohen–Macaulay. Then `S ≅ S_0 × ⋯ × S_n` as
`R`-algebras, where each `S_d` is flat, of finite presentation and with Cohen–Macaulay fibres
over `R`, and all fibres of `R → S_d` are equidimensional of dimension `d`: the relative
dimension `dim_𝔮(S_d/R)` is `d` at every prime `𝔮` of `S_d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_algEquiv_pi_of_isMaximalCohenMacaulay_fiber (R : Type u) (S : Type v)
    [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (hCM : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))
          (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R S)))))) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (S' : Fin (n + 1) → Type v) (_ : ∀ d, CommRing (S' d)) (_ : ∀ d, Algebra R (S' d)),
      Nonempty (S ≃ₐ[R] Π d, S' d) ∧ ∀ d, Module.Flat R (S' d) ∧
        Algebra.FinitePresentation R (S' d) ∧
        (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (S' d),
          Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay
            (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
              ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (S' d))))))
            (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
              ((q.asIdeal.under R).map (algebraMap R (S' d))))))) ∧
        ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (S' d), Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R q.asIdeal = (d : ℕ)
declarations.comment:
The fibre ring is `Localization.AtPrime` of the image of `𝔮` in `S/𝔭S`, as in
00RH. "All fibres equidimensional of dimension `d`" is `Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮 = d`
at every prime `𝔮` of `S_d`, which is equivalent over a field by Lemma 00OT. The factors are
indexed by `Fin (n + 1)` and live in the universe of `S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.map_surjective_and_ker_eq_span_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
In a commutative square of rings
```
S --φ--> S'
↑        ↑
|        |
R -----> R'
```
with `φ : S → S'` surjective, the map `Ω[S⁄R] → Ω[S'⁄R']` is surjective and its kernel is the
`S`-submodule generated by the `da` with `a ∈ S` such that `φ(a)` lies in the image of `R'`
(among them the `di` with `i ∈ ker φ`).
declarations.statement:
theorem map_surjective_and_ker_eq_span_of_surjective
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap S S')) :
    Function.Surjective (map R R' S S') ∧
      LinearMap.ker (map R R' S S') =
        Submodule.span S (⇑(D R S) '' {a | algebraMap S S' a ∈ Set.range (algebraMap R' S')})

theorem omega_localization_base

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RW.** The canonical `S`-linear isomorphism from the module of differentials
`Ω_{S/R}`, presented by generators and relations as `(S →₀ S) ⧸ kerTotal R S`, to `J / J²`,
where `J` is the kernel of the multiplication map `S ⊗[R] S → S`. Its formula is
`quotKerTotalEquivCotangent_mk_single`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotKerTotalEquivCotangent :
    ((S →₀ S) ⧸ kerTotal R S) ≃ₗ[S] (ideal R S).Cotangent
declarations.comment: the isomorphism `Ω_{S/R} ≃ J / J²`

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.quotKerTotalEquivCotangent_mk_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00RW**, the formula: the isomorphism `Ω_{S/R} ≃ J / J²` sends `a d b` to the
class of `a ⊗ b - ab ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotKerTotalEquivCotangent_mk_single (a b : S) :
    quotKerTotalEquivCotangent R S ((kerTotal R S).mkQ (Finsupp.single b a)) =
      (ideal R S).toCotangent
        ⟨a ⊗ₜ[R] b - (a * b) ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : S), tmul_sub_mul_tmul_one_mem_ideal R S a b⟩
declarations.comment: the formula `a d b ↦ a ⊗ b - ab ⊗ 1`

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.nlMap_homotopic
declarations.doc:
**Homotopy uniqueness.** Any two morphisms of presentations `varphi, varphi'` from `α` to
`α'` induce homotopic chain maps `NL(varphi), NL(varphi')` (over the source base `S`). The
homotopy is the `S`-linear map `h : Ω_{P/R} ⊗_P S → I'/(I')²`
(`= P.CotangentSpace →ₗ[S] P'.Cotangent`) given by `Algebra.Extension.Hom.sub` of the two
extension homs; the two homotopy relations are `Cotangent.map_sub_map` and
`CotangentSpace.map_sub_map`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nlMap_homotopic (P : Generators R S ι) (P' : Generators R' S' ι') (φ φ' : P.Hom P') :
    Homotopic (nlMap P P' φ) (nlMap P P' φ')

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.nlMapBase_comp_nlMapBase
declarations.doc:
**Compatibility with composition.** Given a commutative diagram of two squares and
compatible morphisms of presentations `varphi : P → P'`, `varphi' : P' → P''`, the composite
`varphi' ∘ varphi` is a morphism of presentations from `α` to `α''` and, viewing everything
over the base ring `S`, `NL(varphi') ∘ NL(varphi) = NL(varphi' ∘ varphi)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nlMapBase_comp_nlMapBase {R'' S'' ι'' : Type*} [CommRing R''] [CommRing S'']
    [Algebra R'' S''] [Algebra R' R''] [Algebra R' S''] [Algebra S' S''] [Algebra S S'']
    [IsScalarTower R' R'' S''] [IsScalarTower R' S' S''] [IsScalarTower S S' S''] [Algebra R R'']
    [Algebra R S''] [IsScalarTower R R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R'' S''] [IsScalarTower R S S'']
    (P : Generators R S ι) (P' : Generators R' S' ι') (P'' : Generators R'' S'' ι'') (φ : P.Hom P')
    (φ' : P'.Hom P'') :
    (nlMapBase S P' P'' φ').comp (nlMapBase S P P' φ) = nlMapBase S P P'' (φ'.comp φ)

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.nlMap_isHomotopyEquiv_and_isQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Isomorphism case.** If `R → R'` and `φ : S → S'` are isomorphisms, then for any morphism
of presentations `varphi` from `α` to `α'` the induced chain map `NL(varphi)` (over `S`) is
both a homotopy equivalence and a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem nlMap_isHomotopyEquiv_and_isQuasiIso (hR : Function.Bijective (algebraMap R R'))
    (hS : Function.Bijective (algebraMap S S')) (P : Generators R S ι) (P' : Generators R' S' ι')
    (φ : P.Hom P') : IsHomotopyEquiv (nlMap P P' φ) ∧ IsQuasiIso (nlMap P P' φ)

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.nlMap_canonical_isQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Comparison with the canonical complex.** Any morphism of presentations `varphi` from a
presentation `α` of `S/R` to the canonical presentation `α_can : R[S] → S` induces a
quasi-isomorphism `NL(α) → NL_{S/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nlMap_canonical_isQuasiIso (P : Generators R S ι) (φ : P.Hom (canonicalGenerators R S)) :
    IsQuasiIso (nlMap P (canonicalGenerators R S) φ)

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.Cotangent.map_ker_baseChange_cotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**The Jacobi-Zariski sequence is exact at `H₁(L_{C/A})`**: let `A → B → C` be ring maps, let
`α : A[x_s, s ∈ S] → B` be a presentation with kernel `I`, let `β : B[y_t, t ∈ T] → C` be a
presentation with kernel `J`, and let `γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C` be the induced presentation of `C`
with kernel `K`. Then the image in `K/K²` of
`H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C) = Ker(I/I² ⊗_B C → Ω_{A[x_s]/A} ⊗ C)`, under the map `I/I² ⊗_B C → K/K²`
induced by `A[x_s] → A[x_s, y_t]`, is the intersection of
`H₁(L_{C/A}) = Ker(K/K² → Ω_{A[x_s, y_t]/A} ⊗ C)` with the kernel of the map `K/K² → J/J²`
induced by `A[x_s, y_t] → B[y_t]`, i.e. with the kernel of `H₁(L_{C/A}) → H₁(L_{C/B})`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem map_ker_baseChange_cotangentComplex (Q : Generators S T ι)
    (P : Generators R S σ) :
    Submodule.map ((Extension.Cotangent.map (Q.toComp P).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange T)
        (LinearMap.ker (P.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T)) =
      LinearMap.ker (Q.comp P).toExtension.cotangentComplex ⊓
        LinearMap.ker (Extension.Cotangent.map (Q.ofComp P).toExtensionHom)
declarations.comment:
Exactness at `H₁(L_{C/A})`, the one node of the six term sequence that is not
in Mathlib; the term on the left is the source's `H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C)`, so no `Tor` vanishing
hypothesis is needed. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact_extension
declarations.doc:
**The Jacobi-Zariski six-term exact sequence over three independently chosen
presentations** (Stacks 00S2 together with Stacks 00S1).  Let `A → B → C` be ring maps, let
`α : A[x_s] → B` be a presentation of `B` over `A`, let `β : B[y_t] → C` be a presentation of
`C` over `B` and let `N` be *any* presentation of `C` over `A`.  Choose morphisms of extensions
`varphi : α ⟶ N` over the square with vertical morphisms `id_A` and `B → C`, and
`psi : N ⟶ β` over the square with vertical morphisms `A → B` and `id_C`.  Then
```
H₁(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₁(NL(N)) → H₁(NL(β)) --δ--> H₀(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₀(NL(N)) → H₀(NL(β)) → 0
```
is exact at each of its five interior nodes, `δ` being
`NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariskiConnecting`.

The two comparison maps do not depend on the choice of `varphi` and `psi`
(`NaiveCotangent.homotopic_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap` and
`NaiveCotangent.homotopic_nlExtensionOverMap`, which are Stacks 00S1 (2)), so the sequence is
canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact_extension (Q : Generators S T ι)
    (P : Generators R S σ) (N : Generators R T τ)
    (φ : P.toExtension.Hom N.toExtension) (ψ : N.toExtension.Hom Q.toExtension) :
    Exact (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) φ).onH₁ (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₁ (jacobiZariskiConnecting Q P) ∧
      Exact (jacobiZariskiConnecting Q P) (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) φ).onH₀ ∧
      Exact (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) φ).onH₀ (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₀
declarations.comment: the six-term exact sequence with its middle column an ARBITRARY presentation of `C` over `A`, rather than the presentation `Q.comp P` induced by the other two, which is what `NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact` gives; the two are compared by Stacks 00S1 (4), which this statement uses but does not state

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact_canonical
declarations.doc:
**The Jacobi-Zariski six-term exact sequence over the canonical presentations** of Stacks
07BL.  For ring maps `A → B → C`,
```
H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H₁(NL_{C/A}) → H₁(NL_{C/B}) --δ--> C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0
```
is exact at each of its five interior nodes, the three complexes being the naive cotangent
complexes of the canonical presentations `A[B] → B`, `A[C] → C` and `B[C] → C`, and the two
comparison maps those attached to any morphisms of extensions between them, on which they do
not depend.

This is `NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact_extension` at the canonical presentation of
`C` over `A`; it is the form in which the stalkwise statements of Stacks 0E1Y need it, the stalk
of the naive cotangent complex being the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation
of the stalk (Stacks 0D09), and the stalk of the canonical map `c₁` of Stacks 0E1Y being
`NaiveCotangent.nlExtensionBaseChangeMap` of a morphism of those canonical presentations
(`Stacks.NaiveCotangentStalkBaseChange.stalkLegZeroLinear_baseChangeNaiveCotangentMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact_canonical
    (φ : (canonicalGenerators R S).toExtension.Hom (canonicalGenerators R T).toExtension)
    (ψ : (canonicalGenerators R T).toExtension.Hom (canonicalGenerators S T).toExtension) :
    Exact (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) φ).onH₁ (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₁
        (jacobiZariskiConnecting (canonicalGenerators S T) (canonicalGenerators R S)) ∧
      Exact (jacobiZariskiConnecting (canonicalGenerators S T) (canonicalGenerators R S))
        (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) φ).onH₀ ∧
      Exact (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) φ).onH₀ (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlExtensionOverMap ψ).onH₀
declarations.comment: the six-term exact sequence between the naive cotangent complexes of the three CANONICAL presentations of Stacks 07BL, rather than of the three presentations of the source's own proof

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_diagram
declarations.doc:
**The Jacobi-Zariski diagram** (Stacks 00S2, first assertion).  Let `A → B → C` be ring maps,
let `α : A[x_s] → B` and `β : B[y_t] → C` be presentations with kernels `I` and `J`, and let
`γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C` be the induced presentation, with kernel `K`.  In the canonical diagram
```
0 ⟶ C ⊗_B Ω_{A[x]/A} ⊗ B ⟶ Ω_{A[x,y]/A} ⊗ C ⟶ Ω_{B[y]/B} ⊗ C ⟶ 0
          ▲                       ▲                  ▲
     C ⊗_B I/I²       ⟶         K/K²       ⟶       J/J²        ⟶ 0
```
the top row is short exact, the bottom row is exact, and both squares commute: the vertical
maps are the differentials of `NL(α) ⊗_B C`, `NL(γ)` and `NL(β)`, and the horizontal ones are
the components of `NaiveCotangent.nlToComp` and `NaiveCotangent.nlOfComp`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem jacobiZariski_diagram (Q : Generators S T ι) (P : Generators R S σ) :
    Injective (nlToComp Q P).f₀ ∧ Exact (nlToComp Q P).f₀ (nlOfComp Q P).f₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp Q P).f₀ ∧ Exact (nlToComp Q P).f₁ (nlOfComp Q P).f₁ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp Q P).f₁ ∧
      (NL (Q.comp P)).d ∘ₗ (nlToComp Q P).f₁ = (nlToComp Q P).f₀ ∘ₗ (nlBaseChange T P).d ∧
      (NL Q).d ∘ₗ (nlOfComp Q P).f₁ = (nlOfComp Q P).f₀ ∘ₗ (NL (Q.comp P)).d
declarations.comment: The canonical commutative diagram with exact rows: the top row is short exact, the bottom row is exact with a surjection at its right end.

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariskiConnecting
declarations.doc:
**The Jacobi-Zariski connecting map** (Stacks 00S2): for ring maps `A → B → C` and
presentations `α : A[x_s] → B`, `β : B[y_t] → C` with induced presentation
`γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C`, the snake-lemma map
`δ : H₁(NL(β)) ⟶ H₀(NL(α) ⊗_B C)`, that is `H₁(L_{C/B}) → C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def jacobiZariskiConnecting (Q : Generators S T ι) (P : Generators R S σ) :
    H₁ (NL Q) →ₗ[T] H₀ (nlBaseChange T P)
declarations.comment:
The connecting map of the six-term sequence, for the naive cotangent
complexes of three presentations as in the source's own proof.

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact
declarations.doc:
**The Jacobi-Zariski six-term exact sequence** (Stacks 00S2) for the naive cotangent
complex.  Let `A → B → C` be ring maps, let `α : A[x_s] → B` and `β : B[y_t] → C` be
presentations and let `γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C` be the induced presentation of `C` over `A`.
Then
```
H₁(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₁(NL(γ)) → H₁(NL(β)) --δ--> H₀(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₀(NL(γ)) → H₀(NL(β)) → 0
```
is exact at each of its five interior nodes, `δ` being
`NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariskiConnecting`.  In the notation of the source this is
`H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H₁(L_{C/A}) → H₁(L_{C/B}) → C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact (Q : Generators S T ι) (P : Generators R S σ) :
    Exact (nlToComp Q P).onH₁ (nlOfComp Q P).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlOfComp Q P).onH₁ (jacobiZariskiConnecting Q P) ∧
      Exact (jacobiZariskiConnecting Q P) (nlToComp Q P).onH₀ ∧
      Exact (nlToComp Q P).onH₀ (nlOfComp Q P).onH₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp Q P).onH₀
declarations.comment:
The six-term exact sequence for the naive cotangent complex, over the three
presentations of the source's own proof; `Stacks.KaehlerDifferential.JacobiZariski` records
only exactness at `H₁(L_{C/A})`, and for the full cotangent complex.

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.exists_jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00S2** in the form in which the source states it: there *exists* a six-term
exact sequence
```
H₁(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₁(NL(γ)) → H₁(NL(β)) → H₀(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₀(NL(γ)) → H₀(NL(β)) → 0
```
of `C`-modules, for ring maps `A → B → C`, presentations `α : A[x_s] → B`,
`β : B[y_t] → C` and the induced presentation `γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_jacobiZariski_sixTerm_exact (Q : Generators S T ι)
    (P : Generators R S σ) :
    ∃ δ : H₁ (NL Q) →ₗ[T] H₀ (nlBaseChange T P),
      Exact (nlToComp Q P).onH₁ (nlOfComp Q P).onH₁ ∧
        Exact (nlOfComp Q P).onH₁ δ ∧
        Exact δ (nlToComp Q P).onH₀ ∧
        Exact (nlToComp Q P).onH₀ (nlOfComp Q P).onH₀ ∧
        Surjective (nlOfComp Q P).onH₀
declarations.comment:
The existential form of the six-term sequence for the naive cotangent
complex.

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.bijective_h1BaseChangeMap_of_tor
declarations.doc:
**The `Tor` clause of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence** (Stacks 00S2, final assertion).  Let
`A → B → C` be ring maps and let `α : A[x_s] → B` be a presentation of `B` over `A`.  If
`Tor₁^B(Ω_{B/A}, C) = 0` and `Tor₂^B(Ω_{B/A}, C) = 0`, then the canonical map
`C ⊗_B H₁(NL(α)) → H₁(NL(α) ⊗_B C)` is bijective, that is
`H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C) = H₁(L_{B/A}) ⊗_B C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_h1BaseChangeMap_of_tor {T : Type u} [CommRing T] [Algebra S T]
    (P : Generators R S σ)
    (h₁ : Limits.IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} S) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of S Ω[S⁄R])).obj
      (ModuleCat.of S T)))
    (h₂ : Limits.IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} S) 2).obj (ModuleCat.of S Ω[S⁄R])).obj
      (ModuleCat.of S T))) :
    Bijective (h1BaseChangeMap T P)
declarations.comment: The final assertion: if `Tor₁^B(Ω_{B/A}, C)` and `Tor₂^B(Ω_{B/A}, C)` vanish then the canonical map `C ⊗_B H₁(NL_{B/A}) → H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C)` is an isomorphism; `Tor` is Mathlib's `Tor'` on `ModuleCat B`, with `B` and `C` in one universe as `Tor` requires.

declarations.name: main_theorem_00s3
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00S3 (Lemma 10.134.14).** Let `R` be a ring and let
`A_• : A_1 →[d_A] A_0` and `B_• : B_1 →[d_B] B_0` be two term complexes of
`R`-modules. Suppose there are morphisms of complexes `φ : A_• → B_•` and
`ψ : B_• → A_•` such that `φ ∘ ψ` is homotopic to `id_{B_•}` and `ψ ∘ φ` is
homotopic to `id_{A_•}`. Then there is an isomorphism of `R`-modules
`A_1 ⊕ B_0 ≅ B_1 ⊕ A_0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_00s3 (A B : TwoComplex R)
    (φ : ComplexHom A B) (ψ : ComplexHom B A)
    (hB : Homotopic (φ.comp ψ) (ComplexHom.id B))
    (hA : Homotopic (ψ.comp φ) (ComplexHom.id A)) :
    Nonempty ((A.A1 × B.A0) ≃ₗ[R] (B.A1 × A.A0))

declarations.name: FlatBaseChangeNL.statement2_complex_iso
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2, part (b): the canonical comparison is an isomorphism.**

If `R → R'` is flat, the canonical comparison `NL(α) ⊗_S S' → NL(α')` is an isomorphism of
two-term complexes of `S' = R' ⊗_R S`-modules, with degree-`1` component `cotComparison1`
(bijective by flatness) and degree-`0` component `cotComparison0` (always bijective).
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2_complex_iso [Module.Flat R R'] (P : Algebra.Extension R S) :
    ∃ iso : TwoComplexEquiv (cotDiffBaseChangeS R' P)
        (P.baseChange (T := R')).cotangentComplex,
      (iso.e1 : _ →ₗ[R' ⊗[R] S] _) = cotComparison1 R' P ∧
        (iso.e0 : _ →ₗ[R' ⊗[R] S] _) = cotComparison0 R' P

declarations.name: FlatBaseChangeNL.statement3_homotopy_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3**: under flatness of `R → R'`, the canonical comparison chain map of
naive cotangent complexes `NL_{S/R} ⊗_S S' → NL_{S'/R'}` (with `NL_{S'/R'}` the
canonical presentation of `S' = R' ⊗_R S` over `R'`) is a homotopy equivalence of
two-term complexes of `S'`-modules; in particular a quasi-isomorphism.

The asserted homotopy equivalence has as its forward chain map the canonical comparison,
i.e. the `ChainMap` whose degree-`1`/`0` components are the canonical comparisons
`statement3_f1`/`statement3_f0` (the `S'`-linear lifts of `Cotangent.map (canHom)`,
`CotangentSpace.map (canHom)`).
declarations.statement:
theorem statement3_homotopy_equiv [Module.Flat R R'] :
    ∃ he : HtpyEquiv (nlCanDiffBaseChange R')
        ((Algebra.Generators.self R' (R' ⊗[R] S)).toExtension).cotangentComplex,
      he.toFun.f1 = statement3_f1 R' ∧ he.toFun.f0 = statement3_f0 R'

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.Conormal.conormal_stable_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 00S5 (Lemma 10.134.15).** Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite
type, and let
  `P : Algebra.Generators R S (Fin n)` (with kernel `I`) and
  `Q : Algebra.Generators R S (Fin m)` (with kernel `J`)
be two finite-type presentations of `S` over `R`. Then there is an isomorphism
of `S`-modules
  `I/I² ⊕ S^{⊕m} ≅ J/J² ⊕ S^{⊕n}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormal_stable_iso [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    {n m : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Generators R S (Fin n)) (Q : Algebra.Generators R S (Fin m)) :
    Nonempty ((Conormal P × FreeModule S m) ≃ₗ[S] (Conormal Q × FreeModule S n))

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.nonempty_cotangent_baseChange_prod_linearEquiv_of_isLocalizationAway
declarations.doc:
**The conormal module up to free summands, after localizing at an element**: let `R → S` be
a ring map, let `g ∈ S` and let `S_g` be a localization of `S` away from `g`. Let
`α : R[x₁, …, xₙ] → S` be a presentation of `S` over `R` with kernel `I` and let
`β : R[y₁, …, y_m] → S_g` be a presentation of `S_g` over `R` with kernel `J`. Then there is an
isomorphism of `S_g`-modules `(I/I²)_g ⊕ S_g^{⊕m} ≅ J/J² ⊕ S_g^{⊕n}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_cotangent_baseChange_prod_linearEquiv_of_isLocalizationAway
    (g : S) [IsLocalization.Away g T] {n m : ℕ}
    (P : Generators R S (Fin n)) (Q : Generators R T (Fin m)) :
    Nonempty (((T ⊗[S] P.toExtension.Cotangent) × (Fin m → T)) ≃ₗ[T]
      (Q.toExtension.Cotangent × (Fin n → T)))
declarations.comment:
The isomorphism is non-canonical: `Nonempty` of a linear equivalence is the whole
statement. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.bijOn_ker_liftBaseChange_map_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**The naive cotangent complex commutes with localization**, on `H₁`: let `A → B` be a ring
map, let `M ⊆ B` be a multiplicative subset with localization `M⁻¹B`, and let `α`, `β` be
presentations of `B` and of `M⁻¹B` over `A` with a compatible map `f` between them. Then the map
`M⁻¹B ⊗_B I/I² → J/J²` induced by `f` carries the kernel of the base changed differential of
`NL(α)` bijectively onto the kernel of the differential of `NL(β)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.bijOn_ker_liftBaseChange_map_of_isLocalization
    {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T] [Algebra S T] [IsScalarTower R S T]
    (M : Submonoid S) [IsLocalization M T] {ι κ : Type*} {P : Algebra.Generators R S ι}
    {Q : Algebra.Generators R T κ} (f : P.toExtension.Hom Q.toExtension) :
    Set.BijOn ((Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map f).liftBaseChange T)
      (LinearMap.ker (P.toExtension.cotangentComplex.baseChange T))
      (LinearMap.ker Q.toExtension.cotangentComplex)
declarations.comment:
The `H₁` half at the level of the complexes, where the homology is `ker (d ⊗ T)`
rather than `T ⊗ ker d`. The `H₀` half is `KaehlerDifferential.isLocalizedModule_map` and the
`H¹(L)`-level `H₁` half is `Algebra.H1Cotangent.isLocalizedModule`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.isQuasiIso_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Localizing the target**: for a localization `T = M⁻¹S` of `S` at a multiplicative subset
`M ⊆ S`, the canonical map of two-term complexes `NL_{S/R} ⊗_S T ⟶ NL_{T/R}` is a
quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiIso_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_isLocalization (M : Submonoid S) [IsLocalization M T]
    (h : (Generators.self R S).toExtension.Hom (Generators.self R T).toExtension) :
    IsQuasiIso (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := T) h)
declarations.comment:
the whole lemma at the level of the complexes: the canonical map
`NL_{S/R} ⊗_S T ⟶ NL_{T/R}` is a quasi-isomorphism. The `H₁` half alone is
`Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.bijOn_ker_liftBaseChange_map_of_isLocalization`.

declarations.name: IsGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field. A `k`-algebra `S` is a *global complete intersection over `k`* if either
`S` is the zero ring (`Subsingleton S`), or there are `n, c ≥ 0` and an isomorphism of
`k`-algebras `S ≃ₐ[k] k[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` with `dim S = n - c`.

Here `k[x_1, …, x_n]` is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) k`, the relations `(f_1, …, f_c)` are the ideal
`Ideal.span (Set.range f)` for `f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) k`, and the dimension condition
is `c ≤ n` together with `ringKrullDim S = ((n - c : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)`.
declarations.statement:
public def IsGlobalCompleteIntersection (k : Type*) [Field k] (S : Type*) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] : Prop

declarations.name: IsLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field. A `k`-algebra `S` is a *local complete intersection over `k`* if there is
a set `s ⊆ S` whose standard opens `D(g)` cover `Spec S`, and such that `S_g = Localization.Away g`
is a global complete intersection over `k` for every `g ∈ s`.

The covering condition is recorded algebraically as `Ideal.span s = ⊤`;
`localCompleteIntersection_cover_iff` is its equivalence with `⨆ g ∈ s, D(g) = ⊤`.
declarations.statement:
public def IsLocalCompleteIntersection (k : Type*) [Field k] (S : Type*) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] : Prop

registrations.name: isGlobalCompleteIntersection_localization
registrations.comment:
part (1): a localization of a global complete intersection over a field is a
global complete intersection over that field

registrations.name: isLocalCompleteIntersection_localization
registrations.comment:
part (2): a localization of a local complete intersection over a field is a
local complete intersection over that field

declarations.name: IsCompleteIntersection.isMaximalCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**A complete intersection over a field is a Cohen–Macaulay local ring.** Writing the ring as
`R/(f_1, …, f_c)` with `R` regular local and `f_1, …, f_c` a regular sequence, `R` is
Cohen–Macaulay (Lemma 00NQ) and the quotient of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring by a regular sequence
is again Cohen–Macaulay (Proposition 02JN).
declarations.comment:
The pointwise half of the lemma: Cohen-Macaulayness of a single complete
intersection local ring over `k`, stated as `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay` over itself as in
00ND.

declarations.name: IsLocalCompleteIntersection.isMaximalCohenMacaulay_localization
declarations.doc:
**A local complete intersection over a field is Cohen–Macaulay.** Let `k` be a field and let
`S` be a local complete intersection over `k`. Then every local ring `S_𝔮` of `S` at a prime is a
Cohen–Macaulay local ring, `depth(S_𝔮) = dim(S_𝔮)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalCompleteIntersection.isMaximalCohenMacaulay_localization
    {k : Type*} [Field k] {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (h : IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S) (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (Localization.AtPrime q) (Localization.AtPrime q)
declarations.comment:
Cohen-Macaulayness of the Noetherian ring `S` (Definition 00NC) is spelled out as a
condition on its localizations at primes, each being `Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay` over itself,
as in 00ND. The finite type hypothesis is omitted, being a consequence of
`IsLocalCompleteIntersection`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.tfae_isGlobalCompleteIntersection_away
declarations.doc:
**The complete intersection criterion at a prime.** Let `k` be a field, let `S = k[x_i]/I` be a
presented `k`-algebra with finitely many variables, let `q` be a prime of `S`, let `q'` be the
corresponding prime of `k[x_i]` and let `c` be the codimension, `height q' = height q + c`. Write
`A = k[x_i]_{q'}` and `I_A = I_{q'}`. Then the following are equivalent:

1. there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, such that `S_g` is a global complete intersection over `k`;
2. the ideal `I_A` can be generated by `c` elements;
3. the conormal module `I_A/I_A²` can be generated by `c` elements over `A/I_A`;
4. the conormal module `I_A/I_A²` is a free `A/I_A`-module of rank `c`;
5. the ideal `I_A` can be generated by a regular sequence in the regular local ring `A`.

Items (3) and (4) are stated for the conormal module of `I_A` over `A/I_A`, which agrees with
`(I/I²)_q` over `S_q`: `A/I_A` is the localization `S_q` (this is
`ringKrullDim_quotient_map_ker_eq_height`), and `I_A/I_A²` is `(I/I²)_q`, localization being flat.

The closing assertion of the lemma, that any `c` elements of `I_A` generating `I_A/q'I_A` form a
regular sequence in `A`, is the second conjunct of
`Algebra.Generators.spanFinrank_ker_map_le_iff_exists_isRegular`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Generators.tfae_isGlobalCompleteIntersection_away
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    {ι : Type w} [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι)
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (c : ℕ)
    (hc : (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c)
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra P.Ring A]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ g ∉ q, IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g),
        Submodule.spanFinrank (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)) ≤ c,
        (⊤ : Submodule (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
            (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent).spanFinrank ≤ c,
        Module.Free (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
              (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent ∧
          Module.finrank (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
            (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent = c,
        ∃ rs : List A, IsRegular A rs ∧
          Ideal.ofList rs = P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)]
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(5) are the five entries of the `List.TFAE`, in order. The source's `c`,
defined there as `height 𝔮' - height 𝔮`, is the hypothesis `height 𝔮' = height 𝔮 + c`, the
additive form (see the module docstring); the source's parenthetical `dim_𝔮(S) = n - c` is a
consequence of it, by Stacks 00P2. Items (3) and (4) are stated for the conormal module of
`I_A = I_{𝔮'}` over `A/I_A` rather than for `(I/I²)_𝔮` over `S_𝔮`; the two agree under the
canonical identification of `A/I_A` with `S_𝔮`, localization being flat. The closing assertion of
the lemma is the second conjunct of
`Algebra.Generators.spanFinrank_ker_map_le_iff_exists_isRegular`, which carries this tag as
well.

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.spanFinrank_ker_map_le_iff_exists_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of items (2) and (5), together with the closing assertion.**

Let `k` be a field, let `S = k[x_i]/I` be a presented `k`-algebra with finitely many variables, let
`q` be a prime of `S`, let `q'` be the corresponding prime of `k[x_i]`, and let `c` be the
codimension, `height q' = height q + c`. Then the ideal `I_{q'}` of `A = k[x_i]_{q'}` can be
generated by `c` elements if and only if it can be generated by a regular sequence; and any `c`
elements of `I_{q'}` generating `I_{q'}/q'I_{q'}` form a regular sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Generators.spanFinrank_ker_map_le_iff_exists_isRegular
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    {ι : Type w} [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι)
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (c : ℕ)
    (hc : (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c)
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra P.Ring A]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] :
    (Submodule.spanFinrank (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)) ≤ c ↔
        ∃ rs : List A, IsRegular A rs ∧
          Ideal.ofList rs = P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)) ∧
      ∀ rs : List A, rs.length = c →
        Ideal.ofList rs ⊔ (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).map (algebraMap P.Ring A) *
            P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A) = P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A) →
          IsRegular A rs
declarations.comment:
The equivalence of items (2) and (5) is the first conjunct, and the closing
assertion of the lemma — that any `c` elements of `I_{𝔮'}` generating `I_{𝔮'}/𝔮'I_{𝔮'}` form a
regular sequence — is the second. The five equivalent conditions themselves are
`Algebra.Generators.tfae_isGlobalCompleteIntersection_away`, which carries this tag as well; this
declaration is on the covering set for the closing assertion.

declarations.name: IsCompleteIntersectionLocalRing
declarations.doc:
A `k`-algebra `S` is a *complete intersection over `k`* if there exist a `k`-algebra `R` and
a list `f = f₁, …, f_c` of elements of `R` such that

* `R` is a regular local ring,
* `R` is essentially of finite type over `k`,
* every `fᵢ` lies in the maximal ideal of `R`,
* `f₁, …, f_c` is a regular sequence in `R`, and
* `S ≅ R/(f₁, …, f_c)` as `k`-algebras.

The source states this for a local `k`-algebra `S` essentially of finite type over `k`; both
hypotheses are consequences here, see `IsCompleteIntersectionLocalRing.isLocalRing` and
`IsCompleteIntersectionLocalRing.essFiniteType`. The length `c` of `f` is unconstrained, and is
forced to be the codimension `dim R - dim S` by
`IsCompleteIntersectionLocalRing.exists_witness`.
declarations.statement:
def IsCompleteIntersectionLocalRing (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] : Prop

declarations.name: IsCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field. A `k`-algebra `S` is a *complete intersection over `k`* if there are a
regular local `k`-algebra `R`, essentially of finite type over `k`, and a regular sequence
`f_1, …, f_c` in `R` such that `S ≃ₐ[k] R/(f_1, …, f_c)`. The condition `f_1, …, f_c ∈ 𝔪_R` is
contained in `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, which asks the quotient `R/(f_1, …, f_c)` to be
nonzero.
declarations.statement:
public def IsCompleteIntersection (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] : Prop
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(4) are the four clauses of the body, in order. The source's condition
`f_1, …, f_c ∈ 𝔪_R` is not stated separately: over the local ring `R` it is equivalent, given
item (3), to the nonvanishing of `R/(f_1, …, f_c)` that Mathlib's `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`
already carries. The source's hypotheses that `S` be local and essentially of finite type over
`k` are omitted, both being consequences of the existence of `R`, as with the finite type
hypothesis in Definition 00S9. The witness `R` is quantified in the universe of `k`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.exists_isRegular_ker_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00SE.** Let `A → B → C` be surjective local ring homomorphisms with `A` and `B`
regular local rings. Then the following are equivalent: `Ker(A → C)` is generated by a regular
sequence; `Ker(A → C)` is generated by `dim A - dim C` elements; `Ker(B → C)` is generated by a
regular sequence; `Ker(B → C)` is generated by `dim B - dim C` elements.

Being generated by `n` elements is `Submodule.spanFinrank ≤ n`, stated here in the equivalent
additive form `dim C + spanFinrank (Ker) = dim A` (respectively `= dim B`), since the reverse
inequality is Krull's height theorem. See the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.exists_isRegular_ker_tfae
    {A B C : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing B] [Nontrivial C]
    {f : A →+* B} {g : B →+* C} (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ rs : List A, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A rs ∧
          Ideal.ofList rs = RingHom.ker (g.comp f),
        ringKrullDim C + (RingHom.ker (g.comp f)).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim A,
        ∃ rs : List B, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular B rs ∧ Ideal.ofList rs = RingHom.ker g,
        ringKrullDim C + (RingHom.ker g).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim B]
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(4) are the four items of the list, in the source's order. `Ker(A → C)`
is `RingHom.ker (g.comp f)`. `Generated by dim A - dim C elements` is the equality
`ringKrullDim C + (RingHom.ker (g.comp f)).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim A`: subtraction in
`WithBot ℕ∞` is truncated, while the inequality `≤` always holds here by Krull's height theorem,
so the equality says exactly that the minimal number of generators attains `dim A - dim C`. The
source's hypotheses that the maps be local homomorphisms and that `C` be local are omitted, all
three being consequences of surjectivity. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsCompleteIntersection.tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a local `k`-algebra essentially of finite
type over `k`. The following are equivalent: `S` is a complete intersection over `k`; for every
surjection `f : R →ₐ[k] S` with `R` a regular local `k`-algebra essentially of finite type over
`k` the ideal `Ker f` is generated by a regular sequence; for some such surjection `Ker f` is
generated by `dim R - dim S` elements; `S` is a localization of a global complete intersection
over `k` at a prime; and `S` is a localization of a local complete intersection over `k` at a
prime.

`Generated by dim R - dim S elements` is the additive equality
`dim S + spanFinrank (Ker f) = dim R`, and items (4) and (5) exhibit `S` as a localization by an
instance rather than by an isomorphism with `Localization.AtPrime`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsCompleteIntersection.tfae (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k S] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsCompleteIntersection k S,
        ∀ (R : Type (max u w)) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : Algebra k R) (_ : IsRegularLocalRing R)
          (_ : Algebra.EssFiniteType k R) (f : R →ₐ[k] S),
          Function.Surjective f →
            ∃ rs : List R, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R rs ∧ Ideal.ofList rs = RingHom.ker f,
        ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : Algebra k R) (_ : IsRegularLocalRing R) (_ :
          Algebra.EssFiniteType k R) (f : R →ₐ[k] S),
          Function.Surjective f ∧ ringKrullDim S + (RingHom.ker f).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R,
        ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : Algebra k A) (_ : Algebra A S) (_ :
          IsScalarTower k A S) (a : Ideal A) (_ : a.IsPrime),
          IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k A ∧ IsLocalization.AtPrime S a,
        ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : Algebra k A) (_ : Algebra A S) (_ :
          IsScalarTower k A S) (a : Ideal A) (_ : a.IsPrime),
          IsLocalCompleteIntersection k A ∧ IsLocalization.AtPrime S a]
declarations.comment:
Items (1)-(5) are the five items of the list, in the source's order. `Essentially
of finite presentation over k` is `Algebra.EssFiniteType k R`, the two notions agreeing over a
field; the source's proof states item (2) with `essentially of finite type` as well. `Generated
by dim R - dim S elements` is `ringKrullDim S + (RingHom.ker f).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R`,
the reading of Lemma 00SE: subtraction in `WithBot ℕ∞` is truncated while the inequality `≥`
holds unconditionally, so the equality says the minimal number of generators attains
`dim R - dim S`. In items (4) and (5) the isomorphism `S ≅ A_𝔞` is stated abstractly, as
`IsLocalization.AtPrime S a` for an `A`-algebra structure on `S` compatible with `k`. Item (2)
quantifies over rings in `Type (max u w)` for a universe parameter `w`: that asserts it in every
universe and still lets it be instantiated at the localization `k[x_1, …, x_n]_𝔮` of the source's
proof of (2) ⇒ (1), which a free `Type w` would not. The existential items (3)-(5) put their
witnesses in the universe of `k`, where the source's are. The hypothesis that the surjections be
local ring homomorphisms is omitted, being a consequence of surjectivity. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: IsCompleteIntersection.localization_atPrime_tfae_generators
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra and let `q` be a prime of `S`. The
