following are equivalent:

1. the local ring `S_q` is a complete intersection over `k`;
2. `S_g` is a local complete intersection over `k` for some `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`;
3. `S_g` is a global complete intersection over `k` for some `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`;
4. for every presentation `S = k[x_i]/I` in finitely many variables, with `q' ⊆ k[x_i]` the prime
   corresponding to `q` and `c` the codimension, `height q' = height q + c`, all of the equivalent
   conditions (1)-(5) of Stacks 00SC hold: `S_g` is a global complete intersection for some
   `g ∉ q`; `I_{q'}` is generated by `c` elements; the conormal module of `I_{q'}` is generated
   by `c` elements; it is free of rank `c`; and `I_{q'}` is generated by a regular sequence in
   `k[x_i]_{q'}`.

Entries 5-9 of the list are item (4) with a single one of the conditions (1)-(5) of 00SC, in
order: for every presentation, that one condition holds.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsCompleteIntersection.localization_atPrime_tfae_generators (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [Algebra k Sq]
    [IsScalarTower k S Sq] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsCompleteIntersection k Sq, ∃ g ∉ q, IsLocalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g),
        ∃ g ∉ q, IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g),
        ∀ (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι) (A : Type (max u w)) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra P.Ring A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] (c : ℕ),
          (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c →
            (∃ g ∉ q, IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g)) ∧
            Submodule.spanFinrank (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)) ≤ c ∧
            (⊤ : Submodule (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
                (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent).spanFinrank ≤ c ∧
            (Module.Free (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
                (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent ∧
              Module.finrank (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
                (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent = c) ∧
            ∃ rs : List A,
              RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A rs ∧
                Ideal.ofList rs = P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A),
        ∀ (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι) (A : Type (max u w)) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra P.Ring A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] (c : ℕ),
          (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c →
            ∃ g ∉ q, IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g),
        ∀ (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι) (A : Type (max u w)) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra P.Ring A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] (c : ℕ),
          (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c →
            Submodule.spanFinrank (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)) ≤ c,
        ∀ (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι) (A : Type (max u w)) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra P.Ring A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] (c : ℕ),
          (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c →
            (⊤ : Submodule (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
                (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent).spanFinrank ≤ c,
        ∀ (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι) (A : Type (max u w)) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra P.Ring A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] (c : ℕ),
          (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c →
            Module.Free (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
                (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent ∧
              Module.finrank (A ⧸ P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A))
                (P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)).Cotangent = c,
        ∀ (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (P : Algebra.Generators k S ι) (A : Type (max u w)) [CommRing A]
          [Algebra P.Ring A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))] (c : ℕ),
          (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)).height = q.height + c →
            ∃ rs : List A,
              RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A rs ∧
                Ideal.ofList rs = P.ker.map (algebraMap P.Ring A)]
declarations.comment:
Item (1) is `IsCompleteIntersection k Sq` for an abstract localization `Sq` of `S`
at `q`, with the `k`-algebra structure induced from `S`; items (2) and (3) use
`Localization.Away g`, as Definition 00S9 does. Item (4) is entry 4 of the `List.TFAE`: for every
presentation `Algebra.Generators k S ι` with `ι` finite, every localization `A` of `k[x_i]` at
`q'` and every `c : ℕ` with `height q' = height q + c` (the source's `c`, which exists by
`Algebra.Generators.exists_height_comap_eq`), the conjunction of conditions (1)-(5) of Lemma 00SC
in the form of `Algebra.Generators.tfae_isGlobalCompleteIntersection_away`. Entries 5-9 state
item (4) for each one of the conditions (1)-(5) of 00SC separately, so item (4) holds whichever
of the equivalent conditions is chosen. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalCompleteIntersection.tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra. Then: `S` is a
local complete intersection over `k`; every local ring of `S` is a complete intersection over
`k`; and every localization of `S` at a maximal ideal is a complete intersection over `k` — are
all equivalent. The local rings in the last two items are abstract localizations of `S`, carrying
the `k`-algebra structure induced from `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalCompleteIntersection.tfae (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S,
        ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (Sq : Type v) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
          [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [Algebra k Sq] [IsScalarTower k S Sq],
          IsCompleteIntersection k Sq,
        ∀ (m : Ideal S) [m.IsMaximal] (Sm : Type v) [CommRing Sm] [Algebra S Sm]
          [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sm m] [Algebra k Sm] [IsScalarTower k S Sm],
          IsCompleteIntersection k Sm]
declarations.comment:
Item (1) is `IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S` (Definition 00S9 (2)), and items (2)
and (3) say that `IsCompleteIntersection k Sq` (Definition 00SD) holds for every localization of
`S` at a prime, resp. at a maximal ideal, quantified over abstract localizations `Sq` in the
universe of `S` with the `k`-algebra structure induced from `S` — the hypothesis block of item
(1) of Lemma 00SG. The source's finite type hypothesis is kept: items (2) and (3) do not imply
it, as `ℚ(x)` over `ℚ` shows. The source's appeal to quasi-compactness of `Spec S` is absent,
`IsLocalCompleteIntersection` asking for a covering by an arbitrary set of elements generating
the unit ideal. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.isCompleteIntersection_localization_atPrime_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a field extension, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra and let
`S'` be the base change of `S` along `k → K`, so `S' = K ⊗_k S`. Let `q'` be a prime of `S'` and
let `q` be the prime of `S` it lies over. Then the local ring `S'_{q'}` is a complete intersection
over `K` if and only if the local ring `S_q` is a complete intersection over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsPushout.isCompleteIntersection_localization_atPrime_iff
    (k : Type*) [Field k] (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (S' : Type*) [CommRing S'] [Algebra k S'] [Algebra K S'] [Algebra S S']
    [IsScalarTower k K S'] [IsScalarTower k S S'] [Algebra.IsPushout k K S S']
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (q' : Ideal S') [q'.IsPrime] [q'.LiesOver q]
    (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q]
    [Algebra k Sq] [IsScalarTower k S Sq]
    (S'q' : Type*) [CommRing S'q'] [Algebra S' S'q'] [IsLocalization.AtPrime S'q' q']
    [Algebra K S'q'] [IsScalarTower K S' S'q'] :
    IsCompleteIntersection K S'q' ↔ IsCompleteIntersection k Sq
declarations.comment:
The base change `S' = K ⊗_k S` is an arbitrary pushout square
`Algebra.IsPushout k K S S'`, the shape of the sibling 00SJ; the source's literal form satisfies
it. The source's corresponding prime `q` is the contraction of `q'`, spelled `Ideal.LiesOver`, and
the two local rings are abstract localizations at `q`, resp. `q'`, with the `k`-, resp.
`K`-algebra structure induced from `S`, resp. `S'`, as in item (1) of Lemma 00SG. A complete
intersection over a field (Definition 00SD) is `IsCompleteIntersection`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.isLocalCompleteIntersection_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `k → K` be a field extension, let `S` be a `k`-algebra and let `S'` be
the base change of `S` along `k → K`, so `S' = S ⊗_k K`. Then `S'` is a local complete
intersection over `K` if and only if `S` is a local complete intersection over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsPushout.isLocalCompleteIntersection_iff (k K S S' : Type*) [Field k]
    [Field K] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k S'] [Algebra K S']
    [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower k K S'] [IsScalarTower k S S'] [Algebra.IsPushout k K S S'] :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection K S' ↔ IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S
declarations.comment:
The base change `S' = S ⊗_k K` is an arbitrary pushout square
`Algebra.IsPushout k K S S'`, the orientation of the sibling 00SM; the source's literal form is
`inferInstance`. The source's finite type hypothesis on `S` is omitted: each side of the
equivalence implies it. A local complete intersection over a field (Definition 00S9 (2)) is
`IsLocalCompleteIntersection`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.Syntomic
declarations.doc:
A ring map `R → S` is **syntomic**, and `S` is a **flat local complete intersection over
`R`**, if it is flat, of finite presentation, and if all of its fibre rings `S ⊗_R κ(p)` are
local complete intersections over `κ(p)` (`IsLocalCompleteIntersection`).
declarations.statement:
public class Algebra.Syntomic (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    Prop
declarations.comment:
Stated for an `R`-algebra `S`, as Mathlib states `Algebra.Smooth`; for a ring map
`f : R →+* S` it is `Algebra.Syntomic R S` at `f.toAlgebra`. The fibre ring is Mathlib's
`Ideal.Fiber p S = κ(p) ⊗[R] S`, the source's `S ⊗_R κ(p)` with the factors exchanged so that the
`κ(p)`-algebra structure is the one Mathlib puts on a tensor product. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.syntomic_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `R → R'` be faithfully flat and let `S'` be the base change of
`S` along `R → R'`, so `S' = R' ⊗_R S`. Then `R' → S'` is syntomic if and only if `R → S` is
syntomic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsPushout.syntomic_iff (R R' S S' : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra R' S']
    [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R R' S S'] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R R'] :
    Algebra.Syntomic R' S' ↔ Algebra.Syntomic R S
declarations.comment:
The base change `S' = R' ⊗_R S` is an arbitrary pushout square
`Algebra.IsPushout R R' S S'`; the source's literal form is `inferInstance` once
`Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra` is a local instance. Faithful flatness is
`Module.FaithfullyFlat R R'`, the module-level form Mathlib's descent lemmas use. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.syntomic
declarations.doc:
Any base change of a syntomic ring map is syntomic: if `R → S` is syntomic and `S'` is the base
change of `S` along an arbitrary ring map `R → R'`, so `S' = S ⊗_R R'`, then `R' → S'` is
syntomic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsPushout.syntomic (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (R' S' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S']
    [Algebra R' S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'] [Algebra.Syntomic R S] :
    Algebra.Syntomic R' S'
declarations.comment:
The base change is an arbitrary pushout square `Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'`, the
square `RingHom.IsStableUnderBaseChange` quantifies over and the orientation of Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsPushout.isIntegral`; the source's literal `S' = S ⊗_R R'` is `TensorProduct.isPushout`.
Nothing is assumed about `R → R'`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isSyntomic_of_isSyntomic_localization_away
declarations.doc:
Syntomic is local on the source: let `R → S` be a ring map and suppose there are
elements `g_1, …, g_m ∈ S` generating the unit ideal of `S` such that for each `i` the
composite `R → S_{g_i}` is syntomic. Then `R → S` is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSyntomic_of_isSyntomic_localization_away
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → S) (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    (h : ∀ i, IsSyntomic R (Localization.Away (g i))) :
    IsSyntomic R S

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A presentation `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` of `S` over `R` **is a relative global
complete intersection** if every nonempty fibre of `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` has dimension `n - c`.

The number of variables is `n = Nat.card ι` and the number of relations is `c = Nat.card σ`, the
fibre over a prime `p` of `R` is the spectrum of `p.Fiber S = κ(p) ⊗_R S`, it is nonempty exactly
when that ring is nonzero, and `dim = n - c` is written as the equation
`ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) + c = n` in `WithBot ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
public class Algebra.Presentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ]
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ) : Prop
declarations.comment:
The source's displayed `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, a presentation together
with the dimension property of its fibres; `Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection` is the
property of the ring map, defined through this one. Stated for arbitrary finite index types, with
`n = Nat.card ι` and `c = Nat.card σ`. The fibre ring is `Ideal.Fiber p S = κ(p) ⊗[R] S`, and
`dim = n - c` is written additively as `ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) + Nat.card σ = Nat.card ι` in
`WithBot ℕ∞` rather than with the truncated subtraction `Algebra.Presentation.dimension`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A ring map `R → S` is a **relative global complete intersection** if there is a presentation
`S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` such that every nonempty fibre of `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` has
dimension `n - c`, that is, a presentation satisfying
`Algebra.Presentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection`.
declarations.statement:
public class Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Type*)
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] : Prop
declarations.comment:
Stated for an `R`-algebra `S`, as Mathlib states `Algebra.Smooth` and as the
sibling `Algebra.Syntomic` (00SL) is stated; for a ring map `f : R →+* S` it is
`Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R S` at `f.toAlgebra`. The presentation
`S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` is `Algebra.Presentation R S (Fin n) (Fin c)` and the dimension
condition on it is `Algebra.Presentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection`, through which this
one is defined, as Mathlib defines `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension` through
`Algebra.SubmersivePresentation`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.universalFactorizationMapBaseChangeAlgHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
`K`-algebra maps from the fibre ring `K ⊗_{R[a]} S` of the universal factorization map
`φ : R[a] → S` to a `K`-algebra `L` correspond to factorizations over `L` of the image
`x^n + α_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ⋯ + α_0` of the free monic polynomial into monic polynomials of degrees
`m` and `k`. The factorization attached to `f` consists of the images under `f` of the two factors
of the free monic polynomial over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def universalFactorizationMapBaseChangeAlgHomEquiv (K L : Type*) [CommRing K]
    [CommRing L] [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) K] [Algebra K L]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) L] [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) K L] :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    (K ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin n) R] (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⊗[R] MvPolynomial (Fin k) R) →ₐ[K] L) ≃
      {q : MonicDegreeEq L m × MonicDegreeEq L k //
        q.1.1 * q.2.1 = (freeMonic R n).map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) L)}
declarations.comment:
the source's `k`-algebra maps `S_k → K` are tuples `β, γ` with
`x^{n+m} + α_1 x^{n+m-1} + … = (x^n + β_1 x^{n-1} + …)(x^m + γ_1 x^{m-1} + …)` in `K`; here for any
`K`-algebra `L` over any base ring, the tuples being the monic factors of degrees `m` and `k`, the
total degree being `n = m + k`

declarations.name: Polynomial.finite_monicDegreeEq_mul_eq
declarations.doc:
Over a field `L`, a polynomial has only finitely many factorizations into monic polynomials of
given degrees `m` and `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_monicDegreeEq_mul_eq (L : Type*) [Field L] (m k : ℕ) (p : L[X]) :
    Finite {q : MonicDegreeEq L m × MonicDegreeEq L k // q.1.1 * q.2.1 = p}
declarations.comment:
the source's finiteness of the set of tuples `β, γ` in a field `K` with
`x^{n+m} + α_1 x^{n+m-1} + … = (x^n + β_1 x^{n-1} + …)(x^m + γ_1 x^{m-1} + …)`; here for any
polynomial over any field, with factor degrees `m` and `k`

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.isIntegral_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc: Every element of `S` is integral over `R[a]` under the universal factorization map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_universalFactorizationMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsIntegral (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
      (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⊗[R] MvPolynomial (Fin k) R)
declarations.comment:
the source's last paragraph: each of `b_i, c_j` is integral over `R`; here every
element of `S`, over any base ring, the total degree being `n = m + k`

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.finite_primeSpectrum_tensorProduct_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc:
Every fibre `K ⊗_{R[a]} S` of the universal factorization map `R[a] → S` over a field `K` has
finitely many points.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_primeSpectrum_tensorProduct_universalFactorizationMap (K : Type*) [Field K]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) K] :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Finite (PrimeSpectrum
      (K ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin n) R] (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⊗[R] MvPolynomial (Fin k) R)))
declarations.comment:
the source's statement that all fibres have finitely many closed points; here all
points, over any base ring, the total degree being `n = m + k`

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_tensorProduct_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc:
Every nonempty fibre `K ⊗_{R[a]} S` of the universal factorization map `R[a] → S` over a field
`K` has dimension `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_tensorProduct_universalFactorizationMap (K : Type*) [Field K]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) K] :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Nontrivial
        (K ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin n) R] (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⊗[R] MvPolynomial (Fin k) R)) →
      ringKrullDim
        (K ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin n) R] (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⊗[R] MvPolynomial (Fin k) R)) = 0
declarations.comment:
the source's statement that all fibres have dimension `0`, over any base ring, the
total degree being `n = m + k`; the fibre over a prime `p` is the case `K = κ(p)`

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.universalFactorizationMapPresentation_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
The canonical presentation `S = R[a][b, c]/(a_l - a_l(b, c))` of the universal factorization
map, with `m + k` variables and `n = m + k` relations, is a relative global complete
intersection.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalFactorizationMapPresentation_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Algebra.Presentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
      (universalFactorizationMapPresentation R n m k hn).toPresentation
declarations.comment:
the source's `S` is a relative global complete intersection over `R`, for the
presentation by the `b_i, c_j` and the equations `a_k = a_k(b_i, c_j)`, over any base ring, the
total degree being `n = m + k`

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc:
The universal factorization map `R[a_0, …, a_{n-1}] → R[b] ⊗_R R[c]` is a relative global
complete intersection.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_universalFactorizationMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
      (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R ⊗[R] MvPolynomial (Fin k) R)
declarations.comment:
the source's `R → S` is a relative global complete intersection, as a property of
the ring map, over any base ring, the total degree being `n = m + k`

registrations.name: MvPolynomial.universalFactorizationMapPresentation
registrations.comment:
the source's `S` generated over `R` by the `n + m` elements `b_i, c_j`, with the
`n + m` equations `a_k = a_k(b_i, c_j)`: a presentation with variables `Fin m ⊕ Fin k` and relations
`Fin n`, over any base ring, the total degree being `n = m + k`

registrations.name: MvPolynomial.finite_universalFactorizationMap
registrations.comment:
the source's last paragraph: `R → S` is a finite ring map, over any base ring,
the total degree being `n = m + k`

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection.baseChange_and_localizationAwayComp_and_localizationBase
declarations.doc:
Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` be a relative global complete intersection, presented
by `P` with `n` variables and `c` relations. Then

1. for any ring map `R → R'` the presentation `R' ⊗_R S = R'[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` with `n`
   variables and `c` relations is a relative global complete intersection over `R'`;
2. for any `g ∈ S` which is the image of `h ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n]`, the presentation
   `S_g = R[x_1, …, x_n, x_{n+1}]/(f_1, …, f_c, h x_{n+1} - 1)` with `n + 1` variables and `c + 1`
   relations is a relative global complete intersection over `R`;
3. if `R → S` factors as `R → Rₘ → S` through a localization `Rₘ` of `R`, the presentation
   `S = Rₘ[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` with `n` variables and `c` relations is a relative global
   complete intersection over `Rₘ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_and_localizationAwayComp_and_localizationBase :
    (∀ (R' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'],
        (P.baseChange R').IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection) ∧
      (∀ (h : P.Ring) (T : Type*) [CommRing T] [Algebra S T] [Algebra R T] [IsScalarTower R S T]
        [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap P.Ring S h) T],
          (P.localizationAwayComp h T).IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection) ∧
      (∀ (M : Submonoid R) (Rₘ : Type*) [CommRing Rₘ] [Algebra R Rₘ] [IsLocalization M Rₘ]
        [Algebra Rₘ S] [IsScalarTower R Rₘ S],
          (P.localizationBase M Rₘ).IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection)
declarations.comment:
The given relative global complete intersection
`S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` is a presentation `P` with
`P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection`, the numbers of variables and relations being
`Nat.card ι` and `Nat.card σ`, and each conclusion is that the named presentation is a relative
global complete intersection. (1) is `P.baseChange R'`, the presentation
`R'[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` of `R' ⊗_R S`; the version along an arbitrary pushout square is
`baseChange_ofAlgEquiv_isPushoutEquiv`. (2) is `P.localizationAwayComp h T`, with variables
`Unit ⊕ ι` and relations `Unit ⊕ σ`, the new relation being `h x_{n+1} - 1`, for any localization
`T` of `S` away from the image `g` of `h`. (3) is `P.localizationBase M Rₘ`, with the same variables
(`localizationBase_val`) and the images of the same relations (`localizationBase_relation`), for a
localization `Rₘ` of `R` at an arbitrary submonoid `M`, not only at the powers of one `f ∈ R`; the
factorization `R → Rₘ → S` is `[Algebra Rₘ S]` with `[IsScalarTower R Rₘ S]`. The auxiliary rings
are quantified inside the statement; each part is also stated separately.

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.exists_sub_one_mem_map_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, presented by `P`, and let `I ⊆ R`
be an ideal such that the fibres of `Spec(S/IS) → Spec(R/I)` have dimension `n - c`, that is, every
nonempty fibre of `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` over a prime `𝔭 ⊇ I` has dimension `n - c`. Then there is an
`h ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n]` whose image `g ∈ S` maps to `1 ∈ S/IS`, such that
`S_g = R[x_1, …, x_n, x_{n+1}]/(f_1, …, f_c, h x_{n+1} - 1)` is a relative global complete
intersection with this presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Presentation.exists_sub_one_mem_map_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ]
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ) (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], I ≤ p → Nontrivial (p.Fiber S) →
      ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) + ((Nat.card σ : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
        ((Nat.card ι : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ h : P.Ring, algebraMap P.Ring S h - 1 ∈ I.map (algebraMap R S) ∧
      (P.localizationAwayComp h
        (Localization.Away (algebraMap P.Ring S h))).IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.comment:
(1): the fibre of `Spec(S/IS) → Spec(R/I)` over `𝔭/I` is the fibre
`κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S = 𝔭.Fiber S` of `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` over `𝔭 ⊇ I`, and only nonempty fibres are
constrained, as in Definition 00SP; `g ↦ 1 ∈ S/IS` is `g - 1 ∈ IS`. The presentation of `S_g` is
`Algebra.Presentation.localizationAwayComp`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.exists_isUnit_fiber_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, presented by `P`, and let `𝔭` be a
prime of `R` with `dim(S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)) = n - c`. Then there is an `h ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n]` whose image
`g ∈ S` maps to a unit of `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)`, such that
`S_g = R[x_1, …, x_n, x_{n+1}]/(f_1, …, f_c, h x_{n+1} - 1)` is a relative global complete
intersection with this presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Presentation.exists_isUnit_fiber_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ]
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) + ((Nat.card σ : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      ((Nat.card ι : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ h : P.Ring, IsUnit (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField)
        (algebraMap P.Ring S h)) ∧
      (P.localizationAwayComp h
        (Localization.Away (algebraMap P.Ring S h))).IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.comment:
(2): the fibre `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is `𝔭.Fiber S = κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S`, in which `g` is
`1 ⊗ g`, and `dim = n - c` is written additively as in Definition 00SP. The presentation of `S_g`
is `Algebra.Presentation.localizationAwayComp`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.exists_notMem_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, presented by `P`, and let `𝔮` be a
prime of `S` with `dim_𝔮(S/R) = n - c`. Then there is an `h ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n]` whose image `g ∈ S`
is not in `𝔮`, such that
`S_g = R[x_1, …, x_n, x_{n+1}]/(f_1, …, f_c, h x_{n+1} - 1)` is a relative global complete
intersection with this presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Presentation.exists_notMem_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ]
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ) (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R q + ((Nat.card σ : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      ((Nat.card ι : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ h : P.Ring, algebraMap P.Ring S h ∉ q ∧
      (P.localizationAwayComp h
        (Localization.Away (algebraMap P.Ring S h))).IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.comment:
(3): the presentation of `S_g` is `Algebra.Presentation.localizationAwayComp`, the
source's `R[x_1, …, x_n, x_{n+1}]/(f_1, …, f_c, h x_{n+1} - 1)`, and `dim_𝔮(S/R) = n - c` is
`Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R 𝔮 + c = n` (tag 00QD), written additively as in Definition 00SP.
The numbers of variables and relations are `Nat.card ι` and `Nat.card σ`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.exists_fg_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_naive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00SU.** Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` be a relative global complete
intersection. There is a finite type `ℤ`-subalgebra `R₀ ⊆ R` with `f_k ∈ R₀[x_1, …, x_n]` such
that `S₀ = R₀[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` is a relative global complete intersection.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Presentation.exists_fg_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_naive
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ]
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ) [P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection] :
    ∃ (R₀ : Subalgebra ℤ R) (_ : R₀.FG) (f₀ : σ → MvPolynomial ι R₀),
      (∀ j, MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R₀ R) (f₀ j) = P.relation j) ∧
        (Algebra.Presentation.naive (v := f₀)).IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.comment:
The subalgebra is a finitely generated `Subalgebra ℤ R`, the relations over it
are `f₀` with `MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R₀ R) (f₀ k) = f_k`, and `S₀` is presented by
`Algebra.Presentation.naive`. Stated for arbitrary finite index types.

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.isRegular_localization_relation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00SV (1).** Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, presented by `P`, be a relative
global complete intersection (Definition 00SP). For every prime `𝔮` of `S`, with corresponding
prime `𝔮'` of `R[x_1, …, x_n]`, the relations `f_1, …, f_c` form a regular sequence in the local
ring `R[x_1, …, x_n]_{𝔮'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Presentation.isRegular_localization_relation {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {S : Type*}
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {c : ℕ}
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι (Fin c)) [P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)))
      ((List.ofFn P.relation).map
        (algebraMap P.Ring (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)))))
declarations.comment:
(1): `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular` is Definition 00LF verbatim, nonvanishing
clause included, for the list of images of `f_1, …, f_c` in `Localization.AtPrime 𝔮'`,
`𝔮' = 𝔮 ∩ R[x_1, …, x_n]`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.flat_localization_quotient_relation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00SV (2).** Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, presented by `P`, be a relative
global complete intersection (Definition 00SP). For every prime `𝔮` of `S`, with corresponding
prime `𝔮'` of `R[x_1, …, x_n]`, each of the rings `R[x_1, …, x_n]_{𝔮'}/(f_1, …, f_i)` is flat
over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Presentation.flat_localization_quotient_relation {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {c : ℕ}
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι (Fin c)) [P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (i : ℕ) :
    Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S)) ⧸
      Ideal.ofList (((List.ofFn P.relation).map
        (algebraMap P.Ring (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (algebraMap P.Ring S))))).take i))
declarations.comment:
(2): `R[x_1, …, x_n]_{𝔮'}/(f_1, …, f_i)` is the quotient of
`Localization.AtPrime 𝔮'` by the ideal generated by the first `i` images of the relations, for
every `i : ℕ` (`List.take` saturates at `c`).

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.exists_basis_cotangent_relation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00SV (3).** Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`, presented by `P`, be a relative
global complete intersection (Definition 00SP). Then the conormal module `I/I²` of
`I = (f_1, …, f_c)` is free over `S` on the classes of `f_1, …, f_c`.
declarations.comment:
(3): the conormal module `I/I²` is `P.toExtension.Cotangent`, and the basis is
pinned: its `i`-th vector is the class of the relation `f_i`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Syntomic.of_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A relative global complete intersection is syntomic: if `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)`
is a relative global complete intersection over `R`, then `R → S` is flat, of finite
presentation, and its fibres are local complete intersections over the residue fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Syntomic.of_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection (R S : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R S] :
    Algebra.Syntomic R S
declarations.comment:
Stated for the class `Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R S` and
concluding `Algebra.Syntomic R S`: flatness, finite presentation and local complete intersection
fibres, the three clauses of Definition 00SL. Flatness is the clause the source's proof
singles out as needing an argument.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_notMem_syntomic_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `𝔮` be a prime of `S` lying over the prime `𝔭` of `R`. The
following are equivalent:

1. there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ 𝔮`, such that `R → S_g` is syntomic;
2. there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ 𝔮`, such that `S_g` is a relative global complete intersection over
   `R`;
3. there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ 𝔮`, such that `R → S_g` is of finite presentation, the local ring map
   `R_𝔭 → S_𝔮` is flat, and `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` is a complete intersection over `κ(𝔭)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_notMem_syntomic_tfae {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Syntomic R (Localization.Away g),
        ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R (Localization.Away g),
        ∃ g ∉ q,
          Algebra.FinitePresentation R (Localization.Away g) ∧
            (letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q) :=
              (Localization.localRingHom p q (algebraMap R S) (q.over_def p)).toAlgebra
             Module.Flat (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)) ∧
              IsCompleteIntersection p.ResidueField (p.Fiber (Localization.AtPrime q))]
declarations.comment:
The principal localization `S_g` is `Localization.Away g`, the local ring map
`R_𝔭 → S_𝔮` is `Localization.localRingHom` for the lying-over relation, and `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` is the
fibre `𝔭.Fiber S_𝔮 = κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S_𝔮`, canonically a `κ(𝔭)`-algebra, which is `S_𝔮/𝔭S_𝔮` because
`S_𝔮` is an `R_𝔭`-algebra.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00SZ (2).** If `R → S` and `S → S'` are relative global complete intersections,
then so is `R → S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection.comp (R S S' : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R S]
    [Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection S S'] :
    Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R S'
declarations.comment:
(2). Stated for the class `Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection`
along a scalar tower `R → S → S'`; the composite presentation is
`Algebra.Presentation.isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_comp`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Syntomic.comp
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00SZ (1).** If `R → S` and `S → S'` are syntomic, then so is `R → S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Syntomic.comp (R S S' : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S'] [Algebra.Syntomic R S]
    [Algebra.Syntomic S S'] : Algebra.Syntomic R S'
declarations.comment:
(1). Stated for the class `Algebra.Syntomic` along a scalar tower
`R → S → S'`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Syntomic.exists_span_eq_top_algEquiv_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00T0.** Let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal and let `R/I → S̄` be syntomic. There are
elements `ḡ_i ∈ S̄` generating the unit ideal such that every `S̄_{ḡ_i}` is isomorphic to
`S_i/IS_i` for a relative global complete intersection `S_i` over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Syntomic.exists_span_eq_top_algEquiv_quotient {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra (R ⧸ I) S]
    [IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ I) S] [Algebra.Syntomic (R ⧸ I) S] :
    ∃ s : Set S, Ideal.span s = ⊤ ∧ ∀ g ∈ s, ∃ (T : Type u) (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra R T),
      Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R T ∧
        Nonempty ((T ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R T)) ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
The syntomic `R/I`-algebra `S̄` is an `R`-algebra through `R → R/I`, the
elements `ḡ_i` are a set `s` with `Ideal.span s = ⊤`, and `S̄_{ḡ_i} ≅ S_i/IS_i` is an isomorphism
of `R`-algebras.

declarations.name: Algebra.Smooth.localization_away
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a smooth ring map and let `S'` be a localization of `S` away from an element
`g : S`. Then `S'` is smooth over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Smooth.localization_away {R S S' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.Smooth R S] (g : S) [IsLocalization.Away g S'] :
    Algebra.Smooth R S'
declarations.comment:
First assertion: any localization `S_g` is smooth over `R`. `Algebra.Smooth` is
Definition 00T2 (Mathlib's formal smoothness is the cotangent condition, plus finite presentation).
The localization is an abstract `IsLocalization.Away g S'`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.Smooth.localization_base
declarations.doc:
Let `M` be a multiplicative subset of `R` and `Rₘ` a localization of `R` at `M`. Let `Sₘ` be
an `R`-algebra which is smooth over `R` and which is an `Rₘ`-algebra compatibly with its
`R`-algebra structure — for `M` the powers of `f ∈ R` this last condition says that `f` maps to an
invertible element of `Sₘ`. Then `Sₘ` is smooth over `Rₘ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Smooth.localization_base {R Rₘ Sₘ : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing Rₘ]
    [CommRing Sₘ] [Algebra R Rₘ] [Algebra R Sₘ] [Algebra Rₘ Sₘ] [IsScalarTower R Rₘ Sₘ]
    (M : Submonoid R) [IsLocalization M Rₘ] [Algebra.Smooth R Sₘ] :
    Algebra.Smooth Rₘ Sₘ
declarations.comment:
Second assertion: if `f ∈ R` maps to an invertible element of `S` then `R_f → S`
is smooth. Stated as the `Algebra.Smooth` analogue of `Algebra.FormallySmooth.localization_base`:
the base is localized at an arbitrary submonoid `M`, and the hypothesis on `f` is the pair
`[Algebra Rₘ Sₘ] [IsScalarTower R Rₘ Sₘ]`. `Algebra.Smooth` is Definition 00T2 (Mathlib's
formal smoothness is the cotangent condition, plus finite presentation). See the module docstring.

registrations.name: Algebra.Smooth.baseChange
registrations.comment: smoothness is stable under base change

declarations.name: isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**A smooth algebra over a field is a local complete intersection.** Let `k` be a field and let
`S` be a smooth `k`-algebra. Then `S` is a local complete intersection over `k`: there is a family
of elements of `S` generating the unit ideal — equivalently, whose standard opens cover
`Spec S` — each of whose localizations `S_g` admits a presentation `k[x₁, …, xₙ]/(f₁, …, f_c)`
with `dim S_g = n - c`.
declarations.comment:
The source's `smooth` (Definition 00T2) is `Algebra.Smooth`, whose
`FormallySmooth` is the cotangent condition of 00T2;
its finite type hypothesis on `S` is not repeated, being `Algebra.Smooth.finitePresentation`.
A local complete intersection over `k` (Definition 00S9 (2)) is `IsLocalCompleteIntersection`.
See the module docstring.

registrations.name: Algebra.SubmersivePresentation
registrations.comment: standard smooth presentation (with [Finite ι])

registrations.name: Algebra.IsStandardSmooth
registrations.comment: S is standard smooth over R

declarations.name: Algebra.SubmersivePresentation.smooth_and_free_and_isStandardSmooth_and_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` be standard smooth, via a submersive presentation `P`.
Then (1) `R → S` is smooth; (2) `Ω_{S/R}` is free on the `dx_i` for the variables `x_i` not paired
with a relation; (3) `I/I²` is free on the classes of the `f_j`; (4) `S_g` is standard smooth over
`R` for every `g ∈ S`; (5) `R' ⊗_R S` is standard smooth over `R'` for every `R`-algebra `R'`; (6)
if `f ∈ R` maps to a unit of `S`, then `S` is standard smooth over `R_f`; (7) `S` is a relative
global complete intersection over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_and_free_and_isStandardSmooth_and_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection :
    Algebra.Smooth R S ∧
    (∃ b : Module.Basis ((Set.range P.map)ᶜ : Set ι) S Ω[S⁄R],
      ∀ i, b i = KaehlerDifferential.D R S (P.val i)) ∧
    (∃ b : Module.Basis σ S P.toExtension.Cotangent,
      ∀ j, b j = Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation j, P.relation_mem_ker j⟩) ∧
    (∀ g : S, IsStandardSmooth R (Localization.Away g)) ∧
    (∀ (R' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'], IsStandardSmooth R' (R' ⊗[R] S)) ∧
    (∀ (f : R) (hf : IsUnit (algebraMap R S f)),
      letI := (IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hf).toAlgebra
      IsStandardSmooth (Localization.Away f) S) ∧
    P.toPresentation.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.comment:
The standard smooth algebra is a submersive presentation `P` (Definition 00T6 is
Mathlib's `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth`). The source's `x_1, …, x_c` are the variables `P.map j`
paired with the relations, so its `dx_{c+1}, …, dx_n` are the `dx_i` for `i ∉ range P.map`.
`I/I²` is `P.toExtension.Cotangent`. In (6) the `R_f`-algebra structure on `S` is the one
factoring `R → S`. (7) is stated for the presentation `P` itself.

declarations.name: Stacks.StandardSmooth.isStandardSmooth_SAlg
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 00T8).**  With `f : Fin c → R[x_0, ..., x_{n-1}]`,
`h = det(jacobianFirst f)`, and
`S = R[x_0, ..., x_n] / (f_0, ..., f_{c-1}, x_n * h - 1)`, the algebra `S` is
standard smooth over `R`.  The witnessing presentation reorders the variables so
that the first `c + 1` variables (in the chosen order) are
`x_0, ..., x_{c-1}, x_n`, and uses the relations `g_0, ..., g_c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardSmooth_SAlg {n c : ℕ} (hc : c ≤ n) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) :
    IsStandardSmooth (R := R) (SAlg hc f)

registrations.name: RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.comp
registrations.comment: standard smoothness is stable under composition

declarations.name: Algebra.Smooth.exists_span_eq_top_isStandardSmooth_and_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00TA.** Let `R → S` be a smooth ring map. There are `g ∈ S` whose standard opens
`D(g)` cover `Spec(S)` and such that each `S_g` is standard smooth over `R`. In particular
`R → S` is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_span_eq_top_isStandardSmooth_and_syntomic [Smooth R S] :
    (∃ s : Set S, Ideal.span s = ⊤ ∧ ∀ g ∈ s, IsStandardSmooth R (Localization.Away g)) ∧
      Syntomic R S
declarations.comment:
The cover by standard opens `D(g)`, `g ∈ s`, is `Ideal.span s = ⊤`. Syntomic is
`Algebra.Syntomic` (Definition 00SL); it is derived here directly from Lemma 00T5 on the fibres
rather than through Lemmas 00T7, 00SW and 00SO.

declarations.name: Algebra.SmoothAt
declarations.doc:
A ring map `R → S` is *smooth at a prime* `q` of `S` if there exists
some `g ∈ S` with `g ∉ q` such that the induced map `R → S_g` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
def Algebra.SmoothAt (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.smooth_iff_forall_exists_notMem_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness is detected at the primes of the target.** A ring map `R → S` is smooth if and
only if it is smooth at every prime `q` of `S`, that is, if and only if for every prime `q ⊂ S`
there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, with `R → S_g` smooth (Definition 00TB).

Beware that the right-hand side is the Stacks project's notion of smoothness at `q`, which is
strictly stronger than Mathlib's `Algebra.IsSmoothAt R q = Algebra.FormallySmooth R S_q` when `S`
is not of finite presentation over `R`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.smooth_iff_forall_exists_notMem_smooth (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Type*)
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    Algebra.Smooth R S ↔
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Smooth R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Smoothness at a prime `q` (Definition 00TB) is spelled out as `∃ g ∉ q`, with
`Localization.Away g` smooth over `R` — as in Mathlib's `Algebra.IsSmoothAt.exists_notMem_smooth`
— and not as Mathlib's `Algebra.IsSmoothAt`, which is formal smoothness of `S_q` and makes the
equivalence false for `S` not of finite presentation over `R` (witness: `k[x_i : i ∈ ℕ]` over `k`).
Producing the finite presentation of `S` from the pointwise hypothesis is precisely the content of
this lemma. Stated for algebras; `RingHom.smooth_algebraMap` gives the form for a bundled ring map.
See the module docstring.

registrations.name: RingHom.Smooth.comp
registrations.comment: smoothness is stable under composition

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.isSmoothAt_iff_exists_jacobian_notMem
declarations.doc:
**Jacobian criterion for smoothness at a prime.** Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` be a
presentation of `S` over `R` such that every nonempty fibre of `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` has dimension
`n - c`, i.e. a relative global complete intersection (Definition 00SP). Then `R → S` is smooth at
a prime `q ⊂ S` if and only if there is a subset `I ⊆ {1, …, n}` of cardinality `c` such that
`g_I = det (∂f_j/∂x_i)_{j = 1, …, c, i ∈ I}` does not map into `q`.

The subset `I` is an injection `f : σ ↪ ι` from the relations to the variables, and the image of
`g_I` in `S` is the `Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation.jacobian` of `P` equipped with `f`. See the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Presentation.isSmoothAt_iff_exists_jacobian_notMem {R S : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {ι σ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite σ]
    (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι σ)
    (hP : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], Nontrivial (p.Fiber S) →
      ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) + Nat.card σ = Nat.card ι)
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    Algebra.IsSmoothAt R q ↔
      ∃ f : σ ↪ ι, (Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation.mk P f f.injective).jacobian ∉ q
declarations.comment:
The subset `I ⊆ {1, …, n}` of cardinality `c` is an injection `σ ↪ ι` from the
relations to the variables — that is, the extra datum of an
`Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation` — and the image of `g_I` in `S` is its `jacobian`. The
hypothesis is placed on the given presentation `P`, not on the class
`Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection` (00SP), since the criterion depends on `P`; it is
verbatim the condition that class asserts of its chosen presentation. Index types are arbitrary
finite ones rather than `Fin n`, `Fin c`, and smoothness at `q` is `Algebra.IsSmoothAt`
(00TB). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_notMem_smooth_of_isSmoothAt_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Flat with a smooth fibre implies smooth, at a prime.** Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `q` be
a prime of `S` and let `Q` be the prime of the fibre `κ(p) ⊗_R S` corresponding to `q`, where `p`
is the prime of `R` under `q`. Assume that `R → S_g` is of finite presentation for some `g ∉ q`,
that `S_q` is flat over `R` — equivalently, that the local homomorphism `R_p → S_q` is flat — and
that the fibre is smooth over `κ(p)` at `Q`. Then `R → S` is smooth at `q`: there is a `g ∈ S`,
`g ∉ q`, with `R → S_g` smooth (Definition 00TB).

Note that `q` lies over `p` automatically, this being part of `hq`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_notMem_smooth_of_isSmoothAt_fiber {R S : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (Q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [Q.IsPrime]
    [Algebra.IsSmoothAt p.ResidueField Q] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    [Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    (hq : Q.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : S →ₐ[R] p.Fiber S) = q)
    (hfp : ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.FinitePresentation R (Localization.Away g)) :
    ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Smooth R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Smoothness at `q` in the conclusion is spelled out as Definition 00TB, `∃ g ∉ q`
with `Localization.Away g` smooth over `R`, while smoothness of the fibre at `Q` is Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsSmoothAt`; the two notions agree under hypothesis (1), so this is the weakest hypothesis
with the strongest conclusion. The fibre is `Ideal.Fiber` and `Q` is pinned as the prime
corresponding to `q` by `hq`, the inverse of `PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber`. Flatness of
`R_p → S_q` is stated over `R`, which for the `R_p`-algebra `S_q` is the same condition
(`Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization`). This is the full generality of the tag; upstream's
`Algebra.IsSmoothAt.of_formallySmooth_fiber` is the case of all three hypotheses imposed globally.
See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.smoothLocus_comap_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**The smooth locus is stable under flat base change** (Stacks 00TG). Let `R → S` be of finite
presentation, let `R → R'` be flat and let `S'` be the base change `R' ⊗_R S`. Then the set of
primes of `S'` at which `R' → S'` is smooth is the inverse image, under
`f : Spec(S') → Spec(S)`, of the set of primes of `S` at which `R → S` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.smoothLocus_comap_of_isPushout (R S R' S' : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S']
    [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R R'] :
    PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S') ⁻¹' Algebra.smoothLocus R S
      = Algebra.smoothLocus R' S'
declarations.comment:
The base change is the abstract one, `Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'`, and the two
smooth loci are Mathlib's `Algebra.smoothLocus`, which for a finitely presented algebra is the
source's set of primes at which the map is smooth (Definition 00TB, via Lemma 07BU). The equality
is oriented as `f⁻¹(U) = V`, as in `Algebra.smoothLocus_comap_of_isLocalization`. See the module
docstring.

registrations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.instTensorProduct
registrations.comment: formal smoothness is stable under base change

declarations.name: Algebra.finitePresentation_and_lifting_iff_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00TN.** Let `R → S` be a ring map. Then `R → S` is of finite presentation and formally
smooth in the sense of Stacks 00TI (every `R`-algebra map `S → B ⧸ I`, for `I` an ideal of square
zero in an `R`-algebra `B`, lifts to an `R`-algebra map `S → B`) if and only if `R → S` is smooth
in the sense of Stacks 00T2.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_and_lifting_iff_smooth {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    (FinitePresentation R S ∧ ∀ (B : Type (max u w)) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] (I : Ideal B),
      I ^ 2 = ⊥ → ∀ g : S →ₐ[R] B ⧸ I, ∃ f : S →ₐ[R] B, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp f = g) ↔
      Smooth R S
declarations.comment:
The lifting property (Definition 00TI) is spelled out, not Mathlib's
`FormallySmooth`, which is defined by the cotangent condition. The test rings `B` range over
`Type (max u w)` for an arbitrary universe `w`, with `R : Type u`: every universe containing
`R`'s. `Algebra.Smooth` is Definition 00T2: finite presentation, `Ω[S⁄R]` projective (finite by
finite presentation) and `H¹(L_{S/R}) = 0`.

declarations.name: finrank_kaehler_baseChange_eq_finrank_cotangent
declarations.doc:
For an algebraically closed field $k$, a finite type $k$-algebra $S$, and a maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m} \subset S$, the dimension over the residue field
$\kappa(\mathfrak{m}) = S/\mathfrak{m}$ of the cotangent space
$\Omega_{S/k} \otimes_S \kappa(\mathfrak{m})$ equals the dimension of
$\mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_kaehler_baseChange_eq_finrank_cotangent
    (k S : Type*) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (𝔪 : Ideal S) [𝔪.IsMaximal] :
    Module.finrank (S ⧸ 𝔪) ((S ⧸ 𝔪) ⊗[S] KaehlerDifferential k S) =
      Module.finrank (S ⧸ 𝔪) 𝔪.Cotangent

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_of_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**Regularity at a closed point equals smoothness, over an algebraically closed field**
(Stacks 00TS). For an algebraically closed field `k`, a finite type `k`-algebra `S`, a maximal
ideal `𝔪 ⊆ S` and a model `Sₘ` of `S_𝔪`, the following are equivalent: (1) `S_𝔪` is a regular
local ring; (2) `dim_{κ(𝔪)} Ω_{S/k} ⊗_S κ(𝔪) ≤ dim S_𝔪`; (3) the same with equality;
(4) there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ 𝔪`, with `S_g` smooth over `k`; (5) in other words, `S/k` is smooth
at `𝔪`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_of_isAlgClosed {k S : Type*} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (𝔪 : Ideal S) [𝔪.IsMaximal]
    (Sₘ : Type*) [CommRing Sₘ] [Algebra S Sₘ] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sₘ 𝔪] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRegularLocalRing Sₘ,
       (Module.finrank (S ⧸ 𝔪) ((S ⧸ 𝔪) ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄k]) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim Sₘ,
       (Module.finrank (S ⧸ 𝔪) ((S ⧸ 𝔪) ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄k]) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim Sₘ,
       ∃ g ∉ 𝔪, Algebra.Smooth k (Localization.Away g),
       Algebra.IsSmoothAt k 𝔪]
declarations.comment:
The residue field `κ(𝔪)` is `S ⧸ 𝔪`, and the fibre `Ω_{S/k} ⊗_S κ(𝔪)` is the
base change `(S ⧸ 𝔪) ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄k]`, whose factors are transposed so that the left one carries the
scalar action making it a `κ(𝔪)`-vector space. `dim S_𝔪` is `ringKrullDim Sₘ` for an arbitrary
model `Sₘ` of the localization, matching Mathlib's `IsRegularLocalRing`. The source's item (4) is
stated twice, as the existential and as Mathlib's `Algebra.IsSmoothAt`; those are items 4 and 5.
See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_localKrullDim_and_isRegularLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness at a point is the differential fibre having the local dimension**
(Stacks 00TT). Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `X = Spec S`, let
`x ∈ X` be a point with prime ideal `𝔮 = x.asIdeal`, and let `Sq` be a model of `S_𝔮`. The
following are equivalent: (1) `S` is smooth at `𝔮` over `k`; (2)
`dim_{κ(𝔮)} Ω_{S/k} ⊗_S κ(𝔮) ≤ dim_x X`; (3) the same with equality. Moreover, in this case the
local ring `S_𝔮` is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_localKrullDim_and_isRegularLocalRing
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (x : PrimeSpectrum S) (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq x.asIdeal] :
    List.TFAE
      [Algebra.IsSmoothAt k x.asIdeal,
       (Module.finrank x.asIdeal.ResidueField (x.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄k]) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
         localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) x,
       (Module.finrank x.asIdeal.ResidueField (x.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄k]) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
         localKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum S) x] ∧
      (Algebra.IsSmoothAt k x.asIdeal → IsRegularLocalRing Sq)
declarations.comment:
`𝔮` and `x` are one datum `x : PrimeSpectrum S` with `𝔮 = x.asIdeal`; `dim_x X` is
`TopologicalSpace.localKrullDim`, Topology Definition 0055 (4); `κ(𝔮)` is
`Ideal.ResidueField x.asIdeal` and the fibre `Ω_{S/k} ⊗_S κ(𝔮)` is the base change
`κ(𝔮) ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄k]`, whose factors are transposed so that the left one carries the scalar action
making it a `κ(𝔮)`-vector space; `S_𝔮` is an arbitrary model `Sq`. The source's `moreover` is the
final conjunct and not a fourth equivalent item, regularity being strictly weaker than smoothness
over a nonperfect field. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor_injective_of_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
**The differential is injective on `I/I²` for a separable field quotient** (Stacks 00TU).
Let `k` be a field, let `R` be a `k`-algebra and let `R → B` be a surjection onto a field `B`
which is a finitely generated separable extension of `k`. Then `d : I/I² → Ω_{R/k} ⊗_R B`,
`x ↦ 1 ⊗ dx`, is injective, where `I = ker(R → B)`. For `R` local and `B = R/𝔪` this is
injectivity of `d` on `𝔪/𝔪²`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor_injective_of_isSeparableExtension
    (k R B : Type*) [Field k] [CommRing R] [Field B] [Algebra k R] [Algebra R B] [Algebra k B]
    [IsScalarTower k R B] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k B] [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k B]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R B)) :
    Function.Injective (kerCotangentToTensor k R B)
declarations.comment:
`d` is `KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor k R B`, whose domain
`(RingHom.ker (algebraMap R B)).Cotangent` is `I/I²` and whose codomain `B ⊗[R] Ω[R⁄k]` has the
factors of the source's `Ω_{R/k} ⊗_R κ` transposed, so that the left one carries the `B`-vector
space structure. Finitely generated separable is `Algebra.EssFiniteType` together with the notion
of Stacks 030O (2). Generalized: the quotient is an arbitrary surjection onto a field rather than
the residue field of a local ring, and `R` is not assumed Noetherian; the source's statement is
the case `B := IsLocalRing.ResidueField R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_iff_isRegularLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness at a prime with separable residue field is regularity** (Stacks 00TV). Let `k` be
a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `𝔮 ⊆ S` be a prime whose residue field `κ(𝔮)`
is separable over `k`, and let `Sq` be a model of `S_𝔮`. Then `S` is smooth at `𝔮` over `k` if and
only if `S_𝔮` is a regular local ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSmoothAt_iff_isRegularLocalRing
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k q.ResidueField]
    (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] :
    Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q ↔ IsRegularLocalRing Sq
declarations.comment:
`κ(𝔮)` is `Ideal.ResidueField q`, and its separability over `k` is
`Algebra.IsSeparableExtension`, Definition 030O (2); that does not presuppose algebraicity, so it
is not `Algebra.IsSeparable`. `S_𝔮` is an arbitrary model `Sq`, pinned by
`IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q`; regularity is `IsRegularLocalRing` (Definition 00KU) and smoothness
at `𝔮` is `Algebra.IsSmoothAt`. The two-item enumeration is an `Iff`. Finite generation of
`κ(𝔮)/k` is not assumed, being a consequence of `Algebra.FiniteType k S`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: not_isNilpotent_of_hasFreeSummandDifferential
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a map of `ℚ`-algebras with `S` nonzero, and let `f ∈ S` be such that
`Ω[S⁄R] = S·df ⊕ C` with `df` a free generator of `S·df`. Then `f` is not nilpotent.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isNilpotent_of_hasFreeSummandDifferential
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra ℚ R] [Algebra ℚ S] [Algebra R S] [IsScalarTower ℚ R S] [Nontrivial S]
    (f : S) (hf : HasFreeSummandDifferential R S f) :
    ¬ IsNilpotent f

declarations.name: nonzerodivisor_of_hasFreeSummandDifferential
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a map of `ℚ`-algebras with `S` a Noetherian local ring, and let `f ∈ S` be such
that `Ω[S⁄R] = S·df ⊕ C` with `df` a free generator of `S·df`. Then `f` is a nonzerodivisor:
`f * a = 0 → a = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonzerodivisor_of_hasFreeSummandDifferential
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra ℚ R] [Algebra ℚ S] [Algebra R S] [IsScalarTower ℚ R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing S]
    (f : S) (hf : HasFreeSummandDifferential R S f) :
    ∀ a : S, f * a = 0 → a = 0

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_free_kaehlerDifferential_isRegularLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness, free differentials and regularity agree in characteristic zero**
(Stacks 00TX). Let `k` be a field of characteristic `0`, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let
`𝔮 ⊆ S` be a prime and let `Sq` be a model of `S_𝔮`. The following are equivalent: (1) `S` is
smooth at `𝔮` over `k`; (2) the `S_𝔮`-module `Ω_{S/k, 𝔮}` is free; (3) the local ring `S_𝔮` is
regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_free_kaehlerDifferential_isRegularLocalRing
    {k S : Type*} [Field k] [CharZero k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra k Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
    [IsScalarTower k S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] :
    List.TFAE
      [Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q,
       Module.Free Sq Ω[Sq⁄k],
       IsRegularLocalRing Sq]
declarations.comment:
The localized module `Ω_{S/k, 𝔮}` is `Ω[Sq⁄k]`, which by
`KaehlerDifferential.isLocalizedModule_map` is the localization of `Ω[S⁄k]` at `q.primeCompl`, the
identification the source's own proof uses. The source's parenthetical `(finite)` is not a
conjunct: `Module.Finite Sq Ω[Sq⁄k]` holds unconditionally here. `S_𝔮` is an arbitrary model `Sq`,
pinned by `IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q` and `IsScalarTower k S Sq`, as in the siblings 00TT and
00TV; regularity is `IsRegularLocalRing` (Definition 00KU (2)) and smoothness at `𝔮` is
`Algebra.IsSmoothAt`. The three-item enumeration is a `List.TFAE`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.EtaleAtPrime
declarations.doc:
A ring map `R → S` is *étale at a prime* `q ⊂ S` if there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, such that
`R → S_g` is étale. Here `S_g` is `Localization.Away g`, an `R`-algebra through `R → S → S_g`.
declarations.statement: def EtaleAtPrime (q : Ideal S) : Prop
declarations.comment:
Second half of the definition: étale at a prime `q`, stated verbatim as
`∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away g)`. Mathlib's `Algebra.IsEtaleAt` is formal
étaleness of `S_q` and agrees with this notion for `S` of finite presentation over `R`
(`Algebra.etaleAtPrime_iff_isEtaleAt`).

declarations.name: Algebra.etale_iff_finitePresentation_and_naiveCotangent
declarations.doc:
A ring map `R → S` is étale if and only if it is of finite presentation and the naive
cotangent complex `NL_{S/R}` is quasi-isomorphic to zero, that is, `H_1(NL_{S/R}) = 0` and
`Ω_{S/R} = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_iff_finitePresentation_and_naiveCotangent :
    Algebra.Etale R S ↔ Algebra.FinitePresentation R S ∧
      Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R S) ∧ Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R]
declarations.comment:
First half of the definition: étale ring maps. `Algebra.Etale R S` is
`Algebra.FormallyEtale R S` (which is `Ω[S⁄R] = 0` together with `H1Cotangent R S = 0`, the first
homology of the naive cotangent complex) plus `Algebra.FinitePresentation R S`; this is the
source's definition literally.

declarations.name: Algebra.etaleLocus_eq_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `R → R'` be flat and let `S'` be the base change of `S` along
`R → R'`. Then the set of primes of `S'` where `R' → S'` is étale is the inverse image, under
`Spec S' → Spec S`, of the set of primes of `S` where `R → S` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.etaleLocus_eq_of_isPushout
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (R' S' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S']
    [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'] [Module.Flat R R'] :
    Algebra.etaleLocus R' S' =
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S') ⁻¹' Algebra.etaleLocus R S
declarations.comment:
(5). Stated for `Algebra.etaleLocus`, hence without the tag's hypothesis that
`R → S` be of finite presentation, which neither the conclusion nor the proof uses; with that
hypothesis the two loci are the tag's. The base change is the abstract `Algebra.IsPushout`. See
the module docstring. All eleven items of the tag, this one included, are stated together in
`Algebra.Etale.results_on_etale_ring_maps`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Etale.exists_etale_stage_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Item (9) of Stacks 00U2.** Let `A = colim_{i ∈ J} A_i` be a filtered colimit of rings,
computed on underlying sets, and let `B` be an étale `A`-algebra. Then there are an index `i` and
an étale `A_i`-algebra `B_i` with `B ≅ A ⊗_{A_i} B_i` as `A`-algebras, the `A_i`-algebra structure
of `A` being the comparison map `A_i → A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Etale.exists_etale_stage_of_isColimit {J : Type w} [Category.{t} J] [IsFiltered J]
    (F : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c)
    [PreservesColimit F (forget CommRingCat)]
    (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra (c.pt : Type u) B] [Algebra.Etale (c.pt : Type u) B] :
    ∃ (i : J) (Bᵢ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Bᵢ) (_ : Algebra (F.obj i : Type u) Bᵢ),
      Algebra.Etale (F.obj i : Type u) Bᵢ ∧
        (letI : Algebra (F.obj i : Type u) (c.pt : Type u) := (c.ι.app i).hom.toAlgebra;
          Nonempty (B ≃ₐ[(c.pt : Type u)] (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type u)] Bᵢ))
declarations.comment:
(9) The filtered colimit `A = colim A_i` is an arbitrary filtered diagram
`F : J ⥤ CommRingCat` together with a colimiting cocone `c` with vertex `A`, plus the instance
saying the colimit is computed on underlying sets; the stages `A_i` are `F.obj i` and the
comparison maps are the legs `c.ι.app i`, which are also the `A_i`-algebra structure of `A` in the
conclusion. The isomorphism `B ≅ A ⊗_{A_i} B_i` is one of `A`-algebras, with the tensor product as
the model of the base change. The existing registration of item (5) is
`Algebra.etaleLocus_eq_of_isPushout`; item (8), which this is deduced from, is Mathlib's
`Algebra.Etale.exists_subalgebra_fg`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.Etale.results_on_etale_ring_maps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00U2, results on étale ring maps.**
1. The ring map `R → R_f` is étale for any ring `R` and any `f ∈ R`.
2. Compositions of étale ring maps are étale.
3. A base change of an étale ring map is étale.
4. Being étale is local: given `R → S` and `g₁, …, gₘ ∈ S` generating the unit ideal with each
   `R → S_{gⱼ}` étale, `R → S` is étale.
5. Given `R → S` of finite presentation and a flat `R → R'`, with `S' = R' ⊗_R S`, the set of
   primes where `R' → S'` is étale is the inverse image under `Spec S' → Spec S` of the set of
   primes where `R → S` is étale.
6. An étale ring map is syntomic, in particular flat.
7. If `S` is of finite type over a field `k`, then `S` is étale over `k` if and only if
   `Ω_{S/k} = 0`.
8. Any étale `R → S` is the base change of an étale `R₀ → S₀` with `R₀` of finite type over `ℤ`.
9. If `A = colim Aᵢ` is a filtered colimit of rings and `A → B` is étale, there are an `i` and an
   étale `Aᵢ → Bᵢ` with `B ≅ A ⊗_{Aᵢ} Bᵢ`.
10. If `S ⊆ A` is multiplicative and `S⁻¹A → B'` is étale, there is an étale `A → B` with
   `B' ≅ S⁻¹B`.
11. A product `B' × B''` of `A`-algebras is étale over `A` if and only if both factors are.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Etale.results_on_etale_ring_maps :
    -- (1)
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (f : R), Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away f)) ∧
    -- (2)
    (∀ (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C]
        [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C], Algebra.Etale A B → Algebra.Etale B C →
        Algebra.Etale A C) ∧
    -- (3)
    (∀ (R S R' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'],
        Algebra.Etale R S → Algebra.Etale R' (R' ⊗[R] S)) ∧
    -- (4)
    (∀ (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → S),
        Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ → (∀ j, Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away (g j))) →
        Algebra.Etale R S) ∧
    -- (5)
    (∀ (R S R' S' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S']
        [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S']
        [IsScalarTower R S S'] [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'], Algebra.FinitePresentation R S →
        Module.Flat R R' →
        {q : PrimeSpectrum S' | ∃ g ∉ q.asIdeal, Algebra.Etale R' (Localization.Away g)} =
          PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S S') ⁻¹'
            {q : PrimeSpectrum S | ∃ g ∉ q.asIdeal, Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away g)}) ∧
    -- (6)
    (∀ (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S], Algebra.Etale R S →
        Algebra.Syntomic R S ∧ Module.Flat R S) ∧
    -- (7)
    (∀ (k S : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S], Algebra.FiniteType k S →
        (Algebra.Etale k S ↔ Subsingleton Ω[S⁄k])) ∧
    -- (8)
    (∀ (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S], Algebra.Etale R S →
        ∃ (R₀ : Subalgebra ℤ R) (S₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀),
          Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ Algebra.Etale R₀ S₀ ∧ Nonempty (S ≃ₐ[R] R ⊗[R₀] S₀)) ∧
    -- (9)
    (∀ (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone F),
        IsColimit c → ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra (c.pt : Type u) B],
        Algebra.Etale (c.pt : Type u) B →
        ∃ (i : J) (Bᵢ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Bᵢ) (_ : Algebra (F.obj i : Type u) Bᵢ),
          Algebra.Etale (F.obj i : Type u) Bᵢ ∧
            (letI : Algebra (F.obj i : Type u) (c.pt : Type u) := (c.ι.app i).hom.toAlgebra;
              Nonempty (B ≃ₐ[(c.pt : Type u)] (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type u)] Bᵢ))) ∧
    -- (10)
    (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (M : Submonoid A) (L : Type u) [CommRing L] [Algebra A L]
        [IsLocalization M L] (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra L B'] [Algebra A B']
        [IsScalarTower A L B'], Algebra.Etale L B' →
        ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra B B'),
          Algebra.Etale A B ∧ IsScalarTower A B B' ∧
            IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid B M) B') ∧
    -- (11)
    (∀ (A B' B'' : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B'] [CommRing B''] [Algebra A B']
        [Algebra A B''],
        Algebra.Etale A (B' × B'') ↔ Algebra.Etale A B' ∧ Algebra.Etale A B'')
declarations.comment:
Items (1)–(11) in order, as one conjunction; all rings in one universe. (1) is
for `Localization.Away f`. (4) has the generators as `g : Fin m → S` with
`Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤`. (5): `S' = R' ⊗_R S` is the abstract `Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'`,
and 'the set of primes where `R → S` is étale' is Definition 00U1's
`{q | ∃ g ∉ q, R → S_g étale}`. (6): syntomic is `Algebra.Syntomic` (Definition 00SL). (7):
`Ω_{S/k} = 0` is `Subsingleton Ω[S⁄k]`. (8): `R₀` is a `ℤ`-subalgebra of `R` of finite type and
`S ≅ R ⊗_{R₀} S₀` as `R`-algebras. (9): the colimit is a filtered diagram over a small category
with a colimiting cocone `c`, the `Aᵢ`-algebra structure of `A` being the leg `c.ι.app i`, and the
isomorphism is one of `A`-algebras. (10): `S⁻¹A` is any `L` with `IsLocalization M L`, and
`B' ≅ S⁻¹B` is an `A`-algebra map `B → B'` exhibiting `B'` as the localization of `B` at the image
of `M`, compatibly with `L → B'`. (11): the product carries the componentwise structure. Mathlib
also registers item (8) on `Algebra.Etale.exists_subalgebra_fg`.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsEtaleAt.map_eq_maximalIdeal_and_finite_isSeparable_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00U4.** Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over a prime
`p` of `R`. If `R → S` is étale at `q` then (1) the ideal `p S_q` is the maximal ideal of the
local ring `S_q`, hence equals `q S_q`, and (2) the residue field extension `κ(q)/κ(p)` is finite
separable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsEtaleAt.map_eq_maximalIdeal_and_finite_isSeparable_residueField
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [IsScalarTower R (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType R (Localization.AtPrime q)] [Algebra.IsEtaleAt R q] :
    p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) = maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q) ∧
      Module.Finite p.ResidueField q.ResidueField ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField q.ResidueField
declarations.comment:
The source's hypothesis that `R → S` be étale at `q` is taken in the weaker form of
its two consequences: `Algebra.IsEtaleAt R q`, and `S_q` essentially of finite type over `R`
(rather than finite presentation of `S` over `R`). Item (1) is recorded as `p S_q = m_{S_q}`; the
source's other half `q S_q = m_{S_q}` holds for any prime and is
`Localization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal`. See the module docstring, which also records that the
unramified version of this statement is the separate tag 00UW.

declarations.name: RingHom.Etale.quasiFinite
declarations.doc: An étale ring map is quasi-finite: every fibre `κ(P) ⊗ S` is a finite `κ(P)`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.Etale.quasiFinite
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.Etale) :
    f.QuasiFinite

declarations.name: Algebra.IsEtaleAt.of_flat_of_map_eq_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over a prime `p` of `R`. If (1)
`R → S` is of finite presentation, (2) `R_p → S_q` is flat, (3) `p S_q` is the maximal ideal of the
local ring `S_q`, and (4) the field extension `κ(q)/κ(p)` is finite separable, then `R → S` is
étale at `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.IsEtaleAt.of_flat_of_map_eq_maximalIdeal
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [IsScalarTower R (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Module.Flat (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Module.Finite p.ResidueField q.ResidueField]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField q.ResidueField]
    (h : p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) :
    Algebra.IsEtaleAt R q
declarations.comment:
"Étale at `q`" is `Algebra.IsEtaleAt R q`, which under
hypothesis (1) is the source's Definition 00U1 (`Algebra.exists_etale_of_isEtaleAt` in one
direction, `Algebra.basicOpen_subset_etaleLocus_iff_etale` in the other). Hypothesis (3) is
recorded as `p S_q = m_{S_q}`; the source's `p S_q = q S_q` follows by
`Localization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal`. The finiteness half of (4) is stated because the
source states it, and is implied by the rest; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: RingHom.Etale.of_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `f : R →+* S` and `g : S →+* T` be ring maps, so that `g` is a map of `R`-algebras for the
`R`-algebra structure `g ∘ f` on `T`. If `f` is formally unramified and of finite type and `g ∘ f`
is étale, then `g` is étale. In particular a map between two étale `R`-algebras is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.Etale.of_comp {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    {f : R →+* S} {g : S →+* T} (hf : f.FormallyUnramified) (hf' : f.FiniteType)
    (h : (g.comp f).Etale) : g.Etale
declarations.comment:
Stated for ring maps and their composite rather than for a tower of algebras: the
source quantifies over `R`-algebra maps `S → T`, for which `RingHom.Etale` is the predicate, and
the sibling `RingHom.FormallyEtale.of_comp` is stated that way. The hypothesis that `R → S` be
étale is weakened to the two properties the mathematics uses, formal unramifiedness and finite
type; see the module docstring for a witness that the generalization is strict.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_isIdempotentElem_isLocalizationAway_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
A surjective, flat, finitely presented ring map `R → S` exhibits `S` as the localization of
`R` at an idempotent `e`: the kernel of `algebraMap R S` is the ideal `(1 - e)`, and `S` is the
localization of `R` away from `e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_isIdempotentElem_isLocalizationAway_of_surjective
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S))
    [Module.Flat R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] :
    ∃ e : R, IsIdempotentElem e ∧
      RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S) = Ideal.span {1 - e} ∧
      IsLocalization.Away e S

registrations.name: Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero
registrations.comment:
An étale algebra is standard smooth of relative dimension `0`, that is, it
  admits a presentation with as many equations as variables whose Jacobian determinant is
  invertible. Mathlib proves the equivalence, of which the tag is the forward implication.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.surjective_aeval_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc: The `R[a]`-algebra map `R[a][b, c] → S` sending `bᵢ ↦ bᵢ` and `cⱼ ↦ cⱼ` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_aeval_universalFactorizationMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Function.Surjective (aeval (R := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (S₁ := 𝓢)
      (Sum.elim (fun i ↦ X i ⊗ₜ[R] 1) fun j ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ[R] X j))
declarations.comment:
The symbolic presentation `S = R[b, c]/(a_k(b, c) - a_k)`: the map from
`R[b, c]` is surjective.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.ker_aeval_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc:
The kernel of `R[a][b, c] → S` is generated by the relations `aⱼ(b, c) - aⱼ`, where
`aⱼ(b, c)` is the image of `aⱼ` written as a polynomial in the `b`'s and `c`'s.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_aeval_universalFactorizationMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    RingHom.ker (aeval (R := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (S₁ := 𝓢)
      (Sum.elim (fun i ↦ X i ⊗ₜ[R] 1) fun j ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ[R] X j)) =
    Ideal.span (Set.range fun j : Fin n ↦
      (tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn (X j))).map C -
        C (X j))
declarations.comment:
The symbolic presentation `S = R[b, c]/(a_k(b, c) - a_k)`: the kernel. The
polynomial `a_k(b, c)` is the image of `a_k` under `R[a] → S ≃ R[b, c]`.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.pderiv_universalFactorizationMap_eq_sylvester
declarations.doc:
The matrix of partial derivatives of the relations `aⱼ(b, c) - aⱼ` with respect to the
variables `bᵢ`, `cⱼ` is the transpose of the Sylvester matrix of the generic monic polynomials
`g` and `h` over `R[a][b, c]`. Its rows are indexed by the variables and its columns by the
relations.
declarations.statement:
theorem pderiv_universalFactorizationMap_eq_sylvester :
    (Matrix.of fun (i : Fin m ⊕ Fin k) (j : Fin n) ↦ pderiv i
