      ((tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn (X j))).map C -
        C (X j))) =
    ((Polynomial.sylvester
      ((Polynomial.freeMonic R m).map ((mapAlgHom (Algebra.ofId R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R))).comp
        (rename Sum.inl)).toRingHom)
      ((Polynomial.freeMonic R k).map ((mapAlgHom (Algebra.ofId R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R))).comp
        (rename Sum.inr)).toRingHom) m k).submatrix (finCongr hn) finSumFinEquiv)ᵀ
declarations.comment:
The matrix of partial derivatives is the Sylvester matrix of `g` and `h`.
Mathlib's `Polynomial.sylvester` is the transpose of the source's matrix, and the variables are
ordered by increasing degree; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.aeval_pderiv_universalFactorizationMap_eq_transpose_toMatrix_sylvesterMap
declarations.doc:
In `S`, the matrix of partial derivatives of the relations `aⱼ(b, c) - aⱼ` is the transpose
of the matrix of the `S`-linear map `S[x]_{<m} × S[x]_{<k} → S[x]_{<m+k}`,
`(p, q) ↦ g q + h p`, in the monomial bases.
declarations.statement:
theorem aeval_pderiv_universalFactorizationMap_eq_transpose_toMatrix_sylvesterMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    (Matrix.of fun (i : Fin m ⊕ Fin k) (j : Fin n) ↦
      aeval (R := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (S₁ := 𝓢)
        (Sum.elim (fun i ↦ X i ⊗ₜ[R] 1) fun j ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ[R] X j) (pderiv i
          ((tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R
            (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn (X j))).map C - C (X j)))) =
    ((LinearMap.toMatrix
      (((Polynomial.degreeLT.basis 𝓢 m).prod (Polynomial.degreeLT.basis 𝓢 k)).reindex
        finSumFinEquiv)
      (Polynomial.degreeLT.basis 𝓢 (m + k))
      (Polynomial.sylvesterMap 𝐠 𝐡 (Polynomial.natDegree_map_freeMonic_le m _)
        (Polynomial.natDegree_map_freeMonic_le k _))).submatrix (finCongr hn) finSumFinEquiv)ᵀ
declarations.comment:
The Sylvester matrix is the transpose of the matrix of the linear map
`S[x]_{<m} ⊕ S[x]_{<n} → S[x]_{<n+m}`, `a ⊕ b ↦ ag + bh`, stated for the matrix of partial
derivatives with entries in `S`. Mathlib's `Polynomial.sylvesterMap` lists the two summands in
the other order; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.aeval_det_pderiv_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc:
The determinant `Δ` of the matrix of partial derivatives of the relations `aⱼ(b, c) - aⱼ`,
with the variables `b₀, …, bₘ₋₁, c₀, …, cₖ₋₁` in this order, is in `S` the resultant
`Res(g, h)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem aeval_det_pderiv_universalFactorizationMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    aeval (R := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (S₁ := 𝓢)
      (Sum.elim (fun i ↦ X i ⊗ₜ[R] 1) fun j ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ[R] X j)
      (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n ↦ pderiv (finSumFinEquiv.symm (finCongr hn i))
        ((tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R
          (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn (X j))).map C - C (X j))).det =
    Polynomial.resultant 𝐠 𝐡
declarations.comment:
The determinant `Δ` of the matrix of partial derivatives is the resultant
`Res_x(g, h)`.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.etale_localizationAway_resultant_universalFactorizationMap
declarations.doc: `R[a] → S[1/Δ]` is étale, where `Δ = Res(g, h)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_localizationAway_resultant_universalFactorizationMap :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Algebra.Etale (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away (Polynomial.resultant 𝐠 𝐡))
declarations.comment: The conclusion: `R → S[1/Δ] = S[1/Res_x(g, h)]` is étale.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.tfae_universalFactorizationMap_etale
declarations.doc:
For a prime `q` of `S` the following are equivalent: `R[a] → S` is étale at `q`, that is,
`R[a] → S_f` is étale for some `f ∉ q`; `Δ = Res(g, h) ∉ q`; the images of `g` and `h` in
`κ(q)[x]` are coprime.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_universalFactorizationMap_etale (q : Ideal 𝓢) [q.IsPrime] :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    List.TFAE [∃ f ∉ q, Algebra.Etale (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away f),
      Polynomial.resultant 𝐠 𝐡 ∉ q,
      IsCoprime (𝐠.map (algebraMap 𝓢 q.ResidueField)) (𝐡.map (algebraMap 𝓢 q.ResidueField))]
declarations.comment:
For a prime `q ⊂ S`: (1) `R → S` is étale at `q`, (2) `Δ = Res_x(g, h) ∉ q`,
(3) the images of `g, h` in `κ(q)[x]` are relatively prime, are equivalent. Étale at `q` is the
source's definition, `∃ f ∉ q, Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away f)`.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.exists_mulVec_sylvester_map_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
For a prime `q` of `S`, the Sylvester matrix of the images of `g` and `h` in `κ(q)[x]` has a
nonzero kernel if and only if these images have a common factor which is not a unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mulVec_sylvester_map_eq_zero_iff (q : Ideal 𝓢) [q.IsPrime] :
    (∃ v ≠ 0, Polynomial.sylvester (𝐠.map (algebraMap 𝓢 q.ResidueField))
      (𝐡.map (algebraMap 𝓢 q.ResidueField)) m k *ᵥ v = 0) ↔
    ∃ d, d ∣ 𝐠.map (algebraMap 𝓢 q.ResidueField) ∧ d ∣ 𝐡.map (algebraMap 𝓢 q.ResidueField) ∧
      ¬IsUnit d
declarations.comment:
The reason given for (2) ⇔ (3): the image of the Sylvester matrix in
`Mat(n + m, κ(q))` has a kernel if and only if `ḡ, h̄` have a factor in common. Mathlib's
`Polynomial.sylvester` is the transpose of the source's matrix; a square matrix over a field and
its transpose have a nonzero kernel simultaneously.

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.isEtaleAt_universalFactorizationMap_iff
declarations.doc:
`R[a] → S` is étale at a prime `q` of `S` in the sense of `Algebra.IsEtaleAt` if and only if
`Δ = Res(g, h) ∉ q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleAt_universalFactorizationMap_iff (q : Ideal 𝓢) [q.IsPrime] :
    letI := (universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn).toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsEtaleAt (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) q ↔ Polynomial.resultant 𝐠 𝐡 ∉ q
declarations.comment:
(1) ⇔ (2), with étale at `q` read as Mathlib's `Algebra.IsEtaleAt`, which agrees
with the source's definition since `S` is of finite presentation over `R`.

registrations.name: Algebra.IsStandardEtale
registrations.comment: the property of an `R`-algebra

registrations.name: StandardEtalePair
registrations.comment: the pair `(f, g)`

registrations.name: StandardEtalePair.equivAwayQuotient
registrations.comment: its ring, as `R[x]_g/(f)`

declarations.name: standardEtalePair_isEtale
declarations.doc:
For an explicit standard étale pair `(f, g)` over `R`, the canonical map
`R → R[x]_g/(f)` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem standardEtalePair_isEtale {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (P : StandardEtalePair R) :
    Algebra.Etale R P.Ring

declarations.name: standardEtalePair_baseChange_isStandardEtale
declarations.doc: The base change `T ⊗[R] (R[x]_g/(f))` is standard étale over `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem standardEtalePair_baseChange_isStandardEtale {R T : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing T] [Algebra R T] (P : StandardEtalePair R) :
    Algebra.IsStandardEtale T (T ⊗[R] P.Ring)

declarations.name: standardEtalePair_localizationAway
declarations.doc:
For a standard étale pair `(f, g)` over `R` with ring `A = R[x]_g/(f)` and any `α : A`, the
composite `R → A → A[1/α]` is standard étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem standardEtalePair_localizationAway {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (P : StandardEtalePair R) (α : P.Ring)
    (Aα : Type*) [CommRing Aα] [Algebra P.Ring Aα] [Algebra R Aα]
    [IsScalarTower R P.Ring Aα] [IsLocalization.Away α Aα] :
    Algebra.IsStandardEtale R Aα

declarations.name: standardEtale_not_isStableUnderComposition
declarations.doc:
There exist commutative rings `R, S, T` with algebra structures forming a scalar tower
`R → S → T` such that `R → S` and `S → T` are standard étale but the composite `R → T` is not.
declarations.statement:
theorem standardEtale_not_isStableUnderComposition :
    ∃ (R S T : Type) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : CommRing T)
      (_ : Algebra R S) (_ : Algebra S T) (_ : Algebra R T) (_ : IsScalarTower R S T),
      Algebra.IsStandardEtale R S ∧ Algebra.IsStandardEtale S T ∧
        ¬ Algebra.IsStandardEtale R T

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_liesOver_residueFieldRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UD.** Let `R` be a ring, `p` a prime of `R` and `L/κ(p)` a finite separable field
extension. Then there are an étale ring map `R → R'` and a prime `p'` of `R'` lying over `p`
together with an isomorphism `κ(p') ≃ L` of extensions of `κ(p)`, i.e. one carrying the canonical
map `κ(p) → κ(p')` induced by `R → R'` to the structure map `κ(p) → L`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_liesOver_residueFieldRingEquiv {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R)
    [p.IsPrime] (L : Type v) [Field L] [Algebra p.ResidueField L]
    [Module.Finite p.ResidueField L] [Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField L] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R')
      (p' : Ideal R') (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p) (e : p'.ResidueField ≃+* L),
      (e : p'.ResidueField →+* L).comp
        (Ideal.ResidueField.map p p' (algebraMap R R') (p'.over_def p)) =
          algebraMap p.ResidueField L
declarations.comment:
The isomorphism of extensions `κ(p')/κ(p) ≅ κ(p) ⊂ L` is pinned as a ring
isomorphism `e : κ(p') ≃+* L` with `e ∘ Ideal.ResidueField.map p p' (algebraMap R R') = algebraMap
κ(p) L`. Only `Algebra.Etale R R'` is asserted, as in the source's statement; that `R'` may be
taken standard étale is Proposition 00UE. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_isStandardEtale_of_exists_etale
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map and `q ⊂ S` a prime. If `R → S` is étale at `q`, that is, if
`R → S_g` is étale for some `g ∈ S` with `g ∉ q`, then there is a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`,
such that `R → S_g` is standard étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_isStandardEtale_of_exists_etale {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime]
    (hQ : ∃ g ∉ Q, Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away g)) :
    ∃ g ∉ Q, Algebra.IsStandardEtale R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
The hypothesis "étale at `q`" is Definition 00U1 verbatim,
`∃ g ∉ Q, Algebra.Etale R (Localization.Away g)`, rather than Mathlib's `Algebra.IsEtaleAt`, which
is `Algebra.FormallyEtale R S_Q` and agrees with it only for `S` finitely presented over `R`; the
source assumes no finiteness on `S`, so this is strictly more general than Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsEtaleAt.exists_isStandardEtale` and implies it. `S_g` is `Localization.Away g` with its
`R`-algebra structure the composite `R → S → S_g`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsStandardEtale.exists_finite_faithfullyFlat_forall_exists_comp_eq_comap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UF.** Let `R → S` be a standard étale ring map. Then there is a finite, finitely
presented, faithfully flat `R`-algebra `S'` — equivalently, `S'` is finite projective over `R` and
`Spec(S') → Spec(R)` is surjective — such that for every prime `q ⊂ S` and every prime `q' ⊂ S'`
lying over the same prime of `R` there are `g' ∈ S'`, `g' ∉ q'`, and a factorization of the
canonical map `R → S'_{g'}` through a ring map `φ : S → S'_{g'}` with `φ⁻¹(q'S'_{g'}) = q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsStandardEtale.exists_finite_faithfullyFlat_forall_exists_comp_eq_comap_eq
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.IsStandardEtale R S] :
    ∃ (S' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra R S') (_ : Module.Finite R S')
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R S') (_ : Module.FaithfullyFlat R S'),
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) (_ : q.IsPrime) (q' : Ideal S') (_ : q'.IsPrime),
        q.under R = q'.under R → ∃ g' ∉ q', ∀ (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra S' B)
          (_ : IsLocalization.Away g' B), ∃ φ : S →+* B,
            φ.comp (algebraMap R S) = (algebraMap S' B).comp (algebraMap R S') ∧
              (q'.map (algebraMap S' B)).comap φ = q
declarations.comment:
Conditions (1) and (2) are `Module.Finite`, `Algebra.FinitePresentation` and
`Module.FaithfullyFlat` over `R`, faithful flatness being flatness plus surjectivity of
`Spec(S') → Spec(R)`; `S'_{g'}` is an arbitrary localization of `S'` away from `g'`; lying over a
common prime is the equation between contractions, and the factorization is pinned by an equation
between the canonical maps `R → S'_{g'}`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.Etale.exists_finite_faithfullyFlat_forall_exists_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UG.** Let `R → S` be a ring map which is étale and surjective on spectra. Then
there is a finite, finitely presented, faithfully flat `R`-algebra `S'` — equivalently, `S'` is
finite projective over `R` and `Spec(S') → Spec(R)` is surjective — such that for every prime
`q' ⊂ S'` there is a `g' ∈ S'`, `g' ∉ q'`, for which the canonical map `R → S'_{g'}` factors as
`R → S → S'_{g'}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Etale.exists_finite_faithfullyFlat_forall_exists_comp_eq
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.Etale R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S] :
    ∃ (S' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra R S') (_ : Module.Finite R S')
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R S') (_ : Module.FaithfullyFlat R S'),
      ∀ (q' : Ideal S') (_ : q'.IsPrime), ∃ g' ∉ q', ∀ (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B)
        (_ : Algebra S' B) (_ : IsLocalization.Away g' B), ∃ φ : S →+* B,
          φ.comp (algebraMap R S) = (algebraMap S' B).comp (algebraMap R S')
declarations.comment:
Hypotheses (1) and (2) are `Algebra.Etale` and `Module.FaithfullyFlat` over `R`,
faithful flatness being flatness — which étale supplies — plus surjectivity of
`Spec(S) → Spec(R)`; conclusions (1) and (2) are likewise `Module.Finite`,
`Algebra.FinitePresentation` and `Module.FaithfullyFlat` over `R`. `S'_{g'}` is an arbitrary
localization of `S'` away from `g'`, and the factorization in (3) is pinned by an equation between
the canonical maps `R → S'_{g'}`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_bijective_residueFieldMap_lift_isCoprime_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UH.** Let `p ∈ R[X]` be monic and `P ⊂ R` a prime. If `p mod P = f g` in
`κ(P)[X]` with `f` and `g` coprime, then there are an étale ring map `R → R'`, a prime `Q ⊂ R'`
lying over `P` with `κ(P) = κ(Q)`, and a factorization `p = f' g'` in `R'[X]` such that
`f = f' mod Q`, `g = g' mod Q` and `f'`, `g'` generate the unit ideal of `R'[X]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_bijective_residueFieldMap_lift_isCoprime_factorization.{u}
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (P : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime] (p : R[X])
    (f g : P.ResidueField[X]) (hp : p.Monic)
    (H : p.map (algebraMap R _) = f * g) (Hpq : IsCoprime f g) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R')
      (Q : Ideal R') (_ : Q.IsPrime) (_ : Q.LiesOver P) (f' g' : R'[X]),
    Function.Bijective (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ P Q (Algebra.ofId _ _) (Ideal.over_def Q P)) ∧
    p.map (algebraMap R R') = f' * g' ∧ IsCoprime f' g' ∧
    f.map (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ P Q (Algebra.ofId _ _) (Ideal.over_def Q P)).toRingHom =
      f'.map (algebraMap _ _) ∧
    g.map (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ P Q (Algebra.ofId _ _) (Ideal.over_def Q P)).toRingHom =
      g'.map (algebraMap _ _)

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_quasiFiniteAt_five_properties
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UJ.** Let `S` be a finite type `R`-algebra and `q` a prime of `S` lying over the
prime `p` of `R` such that `S` is quasi-finite at `q`. There are an étale `R`-algebra `R'`, a prime
`p'` of `R'` lying over `p` and an idempotent `e` of `R' ⊗[R] S` — the product decomposition
`R' ⊗[R] S = A × B` with `A = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e]` and `B = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/(1 - e)]` — such that
1. `κ(p) → κ(p')` is bijective,
2. `A` is finite over `R'`,
3. there is exactly one prime `r` of `A` (a prime of `R' ⊗[R] S` not containing `e`) lying over
   `p'`,
4. `r` lies over `q`, and
5. no prime of `B` lies over both `p'` and `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_quasiFiniteAt_five_properties
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R') (P : Ideal R')
      (_ : P.IsPrime) (_ : P.LiesOver p) (e : R' ⊗[R] S) (_ : IsIdempotentElem e)
      (P' : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)) (_ : P'.IsPrime) (_ : P'.LiesOver P),
      Function.Bijective (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p P (Algebra.ofId _ _) (P.over_def p)) ∧
      Module.Finite R' (Localization.Away e) ∧
      e ∉ P' ∧
      (∀ P'' : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S), P''.IsPrime → P''.LiesOver P → e ∉ P'' → P'' = P') ∧
      P'.comap Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom = q ∧
      ¬ ∃ Q : Ideal (Localization.Away (1 - e)), Q.IsPrime ∧ Q.LiesOver P ∧
        Q.comap ((algebraMap (R' ⊗[R] S) (Localization.Away (1 - e))).comp
          Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom) = q
declarations.comment:
The decomposition `R' ⊗_R S = A × B` is given by an idempotent `e`, with
`A = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e]` and `B = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/(1 - e)]`; the primes of `A` in (3) and (4) are
the primes of `R' ⊗[R] S` not containing `e`. Properties (1)–(4) are Mathlib's
`Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_forall_liesOver_eq`; (5) is the last conjunct.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_finite_not_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Étale local structure of a finite type algebra along a fibre** (Stacks 00UK). Let `S` be a
finite type `R`-algebra and `p` a prime of `R`. There are an étale `R`-algebra `R'`, a prime `p'`
of `R'` lying over `p` with `κ(p) = κ(p')`, and a decomposition
`R' ⊗[R] S = A₁ × ⋯ × Aₙ × B` — given by complete orthogonal idempotents `e 0, …, e n`, with
`Aᵢ = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e i]` and `B = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e n]` — such that each `Aᵢ` is finite over `R'`
and has exactly one prime `r i` lying over `p'`, while `R' → B` is quasi-finite at no prime lying
over `p'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_finite_not_quasiFiniteAt
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R') (p' : Ideal R')
      (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p) (n : ℕ) (e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S)
      (_ : CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents e) (r : Fin n → Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S))
      (_ : ∀ i, (r i).IsPrime) (_ : ∀ i, (r i).LiesOver p'),
      Function.Bijective (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p p' (Algebra.ofId _ _) (p'.over_def p)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, Module.Finite R' (Localization.Away (e i.castSucc))) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, e i.castSucc ∉ r i) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (q : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)), q.IsPrime → q.LiesOver p' →
        e i.castSucc ∉ q → q = r i) ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)) [q.IsPrime], q.LiesOver p' → e (Fin.last n) ∉ q →
        ¬ Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R' q
declarations.comment:
The product decomposition is given by complete orthogonal idempotents
`e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S`, the factors being `(R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e i]`, and the primes of a factor
are named by the primes of `R' ⊗[R] S` avoiding the corresponding idempotent. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_finite_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**Étale local structure of a finite type algebra along a fibre** (Stacks 00UL). Let `S` be a
finite type `R`-algebra and `p` a prime of `R`. There are an étale `R`-algebra `R'`, a prime `p'`
of `R'` lying over `p`, and a decomposition `R' ⊗[R] S = A₁ × ⋯ × Aₙ × B` — given by complete
orthogonal idempotents `e 0, …, e n`, with `Aᵢ = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e i]` and `B = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e n]`
— such that each `Aᵢ` is finite over `R'` and has exactly one prime `r i` lying over `p'`, each
residue field extension `κ(r i)/κ(p')` is finite purely inseparable, and `R' → B` is quasi-finite
at no prime lying over `p'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_finite_isPurelyInseparable
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R') (p' : Ideal R')
      (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p) (n : ℕ) (e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S)
      (_ : CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents e) (r : Fin n → Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S))
      (_ : ∀ i, (r i).IsPrime) (_ : ∀ i, (r i).LiesOver p'),
      (∀ i : Fin n, Module.Finite R' (Localization.Away (e i.castSucc))) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, e i.castSucc ∉ r i) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (q : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)), q.IsPrime → q.LiesOver p' →
        e i.castSucc ∉ q → q = r i) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p' (r i)
        Module.Finite p'.ResidueField (r i).ResidueField ∧
          IsPurelyInseparable p'.ResidueField (r i).ResidueField) ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)) [q.IsPrime], q.LiesOver p' → e (Fin.last n) ∉ q →
        ¬ Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R' q
declarations.comment:
The product decomposition is given by complete orthogonal idempotents
`e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S`, the factors being `(R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e i]`, and the primes of a factor
are named by the primes of `R' ⊗[R] S` avoiding the corresponding idempotent. Unlike Tag 00UK
this does not assert `κ(p) = κ(p')`, which the source's proof gives up in order to control the
residue fields. See the module docstring.

registrations.name: Algebra.FormallyUnramified
registrations.comment: formally unramified ring maps

registrations.name: Algebra.FormallyUnramified.iff_comp_injective
registrations.comment: at most one dotted arrow, as injectivity of post-composition

declarations.name: Algebra.forall_comp_injective_iff_subsingleton_kaehlerDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UO.** Let `R → S` be a ring map. Then `R → S` is formally unramified in the sense
of Definition 00UN — for every `R`-algebra `A` and every ideal `I` of `A` with `I² = 0`, the map
`Hom_R(S, A) → Hom_R(S, A/I)` given by composition with the quotient map is injective — if and
only if the module of differentials `Ω_{S/R}` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.forall_comp_injective_iff_subsingleton_kaehlerDifferential
    (R : Type*) (S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    (∀ ⦃A : Type u⦄ [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ →
      Function.Injective ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp : (S →ₐ[R] A) → S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I)) ↔
      Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R]
declarations.comment:
(1) is the lifting property of Definition 00UN, stated as injectivity of
`Hom_R(S, A) → Hom_R(S, A/I)` for every `R`-algebra `A` in the universe of `S` and every ideal `I`
with `I ^ 2 = ⊥`; (2) is `Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R]`. Proved from Mathlib's
`Algebra.FormallyUnramified.iff_comp_injective`.

declarations.name: Algebra.existsUnique_lift_iff_finitePresentation_and_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite presentation. Then `S` is formally étale over `R` in the
sense of unique infinitesimal lifting (for every `R`-algebra `A`, every ideal `I ⊆ A` with
`I ^ 2 = 0` and every `R`-algebra map `f : S → A ⧸ I` there is exactly one `R`-algebra map
`g : S → A` with `A → A ⧸ I` composed with `g` equal to `f`) if and only if `R → S` is étale: of
finite presentation with `H₁(NL_{S/R}) = 0` and `Ω_{S/R} = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.existsUnique_lift_iff_finitePresentation_and_subsingleton.{u, v}
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hfp : Algebra.FinitePresentation R S) :
    (∀ ⦃A : Type (max u v)⦄ [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ →
        ∀ f : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I, ∃! g : S →ₐ[R] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp g = f) ↔
      Algebra.FinitePresentation R S ∧ Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R S) ∧
        Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R]
declarations.comment:
Formally étale (1) is the unique-lifting property of Definition 00UQ, stated for
test rings `A` in the universe `max u v` of `R` and `S` (`Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I` is
`A → A ⧸ I`; an `R`-algebra map `g` makes the lower triangle commute). Étale (2) is
Definition 00U1 verbatim: finite presentation, and `NL_{S/R}` quasi-isomorphic to zero, which the
source spells out as `H₁(NL_{S/R}) = 0` (`Algebra.H1Cotangent R S`) and `Ω_{S/R} = 0`.

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified
declarations.doc:
A ring map `R → S` is **G-unramified** if it is of finite presentation and `Ω_{S/R} = 0`
(Stacks 00UT (2)); the vanishing of the differentials is recorded as formal unramifiedness, which
is the same condition by Lemma 00UO. This is the notion of EGA; dropping finite presentation to
finite type gives `Algebra.Unramified`, item (1) of the same definition.
declarations.statement:
public class Algebra.GUnramified (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    Prop
declarations.comment:
Item (2). `Ω_{S/R} = 0` is `Algebra.FormallyUnramified` (Lemma 00UO,
`Algebra.formallyUnramified_iff`), as in Mathlib's `Algebra.Unramified`, `Algebra.Smooth` and
`Algebra.Etale`. Item (1) is `Algebra.Unramified`, item (3) is
`∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Unramified R (Localization.Away g)` and item (4) is
`∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.GUnramified R (Localization.Away g)`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.unramified_iff_and_gUnramified_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UU.** A ring map `R → S` is unramified if and only if it is of finite type and
`Ω_{S/R} = 0`, and G-unramified if and only if it is of finite presentation and `Ω_{S/R} = 0`.
Both equivalences come from the identification of the vanishing of `Ω_{S/R}` with formal
unramifiedness (Lemma 00UO, `Algebra.formallyUnramified_iff`), which is the condition that
`Algebra.Unramified` and `Algebra.GUnramified` pair with their finiteness conditions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.unramified_iff_and_gUnramified_iff (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] :
    (Algebra.Unramified R S ↔ Algebra.FiniteType R S ∧ Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R]) ∧
      (Algebra.GUnramified R S ↔ Algebra.FinitePresentation R S ∧ Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R])
declarations.comment:
Both equivalences, as one lemma. `Ω_{S/R} = 0` is written out as
`Subsingleton Ω[S⁄R]` on the right of each; on the left, `Algebra.Unramified` and
`Algebra.GUnramified` (Definition 00UT) are formal unramifiedness together with finite type
resp. finite presentation, so the literal reading of the lemma would be structure eta. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UV.** Properties of unramified and G-unramified ring maps: (1) base change,
(2) composition, (3) a principal localization, (4) a quotient, (5) an étale map, (6)–(9) four
criteria at a prime in terms of the vanishing of the differentials, (10) descent along a principal
open cover, (11) unramifiedness at every prime, (12)–(13) descent to a finite type `ℤ`-algebra.
Each item has a version for `Algebra.Unramified` and one for `Algebra.GUnramified`, the source's
"resp.", differing only in whether the finiteness condition is finite type or finite
presentation. Cite the items by the names listed in the module docstring, not by projecting.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties :
    -- (1) base change
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (R' : Type w)
        [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'], (Unramified R S → Unramified R' (R' ⊗[R] S)) ∧
          (GUnramified R S → GUnramified R' (R' ⊗[R] S))) ∧
    -- (2) composition
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {T : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra R S]
        [Algebra S T] [Algebra R T] [IsScalarTower R S T],
        (Unramified R S → Unramified S T → Unramified R T) ∧
          (GUnramified R S → GUnramified S T → GUnramified R T)) ∧
    -- (3) a principal localization
    (∀ {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f : R) (Rf : Type v) [CommRing Rf] [Algebra R Rf]
        [IsLocalization.Away f Rf], GUnramified R Rf ∧ Unramified R Rf) ∧
    -- (4) a quotient
    (∀ {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R),
        Unramified R (R ⧸ I) ∧ (I.FG → GUnramified R (R ⧸ I))) ∧
    -- (5) an étale map
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Etale R S],
        GUnramified R S ∧ Unramified R S) ∧
    -- (6) the stalk of the differentials at the prime vanishes
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl Ω[S⁄R]) →
          (FiniteType R S → ∃ g ∉ q, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) ∧
            (FinitePresentation R S → ∃ g ∉ q, GUnramified R (Localization.Away g))) ∧
    -- (7) the fibre of the differentials at the prime vanishes
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
        Subsingleton (q.Fiber Ω[S⁄R]) →
          (FiniteType R S → ∃ g ∉ q, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) ∧
            (FinitePresentation R S → ∃ g ∉ q, GUnramified R (Localization.Away g))) ∧
    -- (8) the stalk of the differentials of the fibre over `𝔭` vanishes
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
        (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime],
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl Ω[p.Fiber S⁄p.ResidueField]) →
          (FiniteType R S → ∃ g : S,
              Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
                Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) ∧
            (FinitePresentation R S → ∃ g : S,
              Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
                GUnramified R (Localization.Away g))) ∧
    -- (9) the fibre at `q` of the differentials of the fibre over `𝔭` vanishes
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
        (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime],
        Subsingleton (q.Fiber Ω[p.Fiber S⁄p.ResidueField]) →
          (FiniteType R S → ∃ g : S,
              Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
                Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) ∧
            (FinitePresentation R S → ∃ g : S,
              Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
                GUnramified R (Localization.Away g))) ∧
    -- (10) descent along a cover of `Spec S` by principal opens
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (s : Set S),
        Ideal.span s = ⊤ →
        ((∀ g ∈ s, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) → Unramified R S) ∧
          ((∀ g ∈ s, GUnramified R (Localization.Away g)) → GUnramified R S)) ∧
    -- (11) unramified at every prime
    (∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S],
        ((∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], ∃ g ∉ q, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) →
            Unramified R S) ∧
          ((∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], ∃ g ∉ q, GUnramified R (Localization.Away g)) →
            GUnramified R S)) ∧
    -- (12) a G-unramified map is a base change of one over a finite type `ℤ`-algebra
    (∀ {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S], GUnramified R S →
        ∃ (R₀ : Subring R) (S₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀),
          FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ GUnramified R₀ S₀ ∧ Nonempty (S ≃ₐ[R] R ⊗[R₀] S₀)) ∧
    -- (13) an unramified map is a quotient of a base change of one over a finite type `ℤ`-algebra
    (∀ {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S], Unramified R S →
        ∃ (R₀ : Subring R) (S₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀)
          (f : (R ⊗[R₀] S₀) →ₐ[R] S),
          FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ Unramified R₀ S₀ ∧ Function.Surjective f)
declarations.comment:
All thirteen items, both variants of each, as one conjunction in the source's
order; item `n` is the `n`-th conjunct and its `(resp. G-unramified)` reading is that conjunct's
second component. The conjuncts share the universe variables `u`, `v`, `w`, and each item is
exported under its own name; a proof should cite those names. Items (8) and (9) quantify over a
prime of the fibre `κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S` rather than over a prime of `S` lying over `𝔭`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**The base change of a G-unramified ring map is G-unramified** (Stacks 00UV (1)); item (1) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`. This is `Algebra.Unramified.baseChange`, whose
statement is the other half of the item, with finite type replaced by finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.GUnramified.baseChange (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (B : Type w) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [GUnramified R A] :
    GUnramified B (B ⊗[R] A)
declarations.comment:
Item (1), the `G-unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`; the `unramified` version is Mathlib's
`Algebra.Unramified.baseChange`.

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified.comp
declarations.doc:
**The composition of G-unramified ring maps is G-unramified** (Stacks 00UV (2)); item (2) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`. This is `Algebra.Unramified.comp`, whose statement
is the other half of the item, with finite type replaced by finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.GUnramified.comp (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (B : Type w) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [GUnramified R A] [GUnramified A B] : GUnramified R B
declarations.comment:
Item (2), the `G-unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`; the `unramified` version is Mathlib's
`Algebra.Unramified.comp`.

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified.of_isLocalization_Away
declarations.doc:
**A principal localization `R → R_r` is G-unramified** (Stacks 00UV (3)), stated for an
arbitrary model `A` of `R_r`; item (3) of `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`. This is
`Algebra.Unramified.of_isLocalization_Away`, whose statement is the other half of the item, with
finite type replaced by finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.GUnramified.of_isLocalization_Away {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (r : R) [IsLocalization.Away r A] : GUnramified R A
declarations.comment:
Item (3), the `G-unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`; the `unramified` version is Mathlib's
`Algebra.Unramified.of_isLocalization_Away`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Unramified.quotient
declarations.doc:
**A quotient `R → R ⧸ I` is unramified** (Stacks 00UV (4), first sentence); item (4) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Unramified.quotient {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) :
    Unramified R (R ⧸ I)
declarations.comment:
Item (4), first sentence, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified.quotient_of_fg
declarations.doc:
**A quotient `R → R ⧸ I` by a finitely generated ideal is G-unramified** (Stacks 00UV (4),
second sentence); item (4) of `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.GUnramified.quotient_of_fg {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {I : Ideal R}
    (hI : I.FG) : GUnramified R (R ⧸ I)
declarations.comment:
Item (4), second sentence, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified.of_etale
declarations.doc:
**An étale ring map is G-unramified** (Stacks 00UV (5)); item (5) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`. This is `Algebra.Etale.instUnramified`, whose
statement is the other half of the item, with finite type replaced by finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.GUnramified.of_etale {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Etale R S] : GUnramified R S
declarations.comment:
Item (5), the `G-unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`; the `unramified` version is Mathlib's
`Algebra.Etale.instUnramified`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
**A finite type ring map whose differentials have vanishing stalk at a prime `q` is unramified
at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (6)): there is a `g ∉ q` with `R → S_g` unramified. Item (6) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FiniteType R S] (q : Ideal S)
    [q.IsPrime] (hq : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl Ω[S⁄R])) :
    ∃ g ∉ q, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Item (6), the `unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
**A finite presentation ring map whose differentials have vanishing stalk at a prime `q` is
G-unramified at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (6)): there is a `g ∉ q` with `R → S_g` G-unramified. Item (6)
of `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FinitePresentation R S] (q : Ideal S)
    [q.IsPrime] (hq : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl Ω[S⁄R])) :
    ∃ g ∉ q, GUnramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Item (6), the `G-unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite type ring map whose differentials have vanishing fibre at a prime `q` is unramified
at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (7)): there is a `g ∉ q` with `R → S_g` unramified. Item (7) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FiniteType R S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Subsingleton (q.Fiber Ω[S⁄R])) : ∃ g ∉ q, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Item (7), the `unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite presentation ring map whose differentials have vanishing fibre at a prime `q` is
G-unramified at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (7)): there is a `g ∉ q` with `R → S_g` G-unramified. Item (7)
of `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FinitePresentation R S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Subsingleton (q.Fiber Ω[S⁄R])) : ∃ g ∉ q, GUnramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Item (7), the `G-unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule_of_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite type ring map whose fibre over `p` has differentials with vanishing stalk at a prime
`q` of that fibre is unramified at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (8)): there is a `g` in `S` whose image in
`κ(p) ⊗_R S` avoids `q` and with `R → S_g` unramified. Item (8) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule_of_fiber
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FiniteType R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl Ω[p.Fiber S⁄p.ResidueField])) :
    ∃ g : S, Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
      Unramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Item (8), the `unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule_of_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite presentation ring map whose fibre over `p` has differentials with vanishing stalk at
a prime `q` of that fibre is G-unramified at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (8)): there is a `g` in `S` whose
image in `κ(p) ⊗_R S` avoids `q` and with `R → S_g` G-unramified. Item (8) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_localizedModule_of_fiber
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FinitePresentation R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl Ω[p.Fiber S⁄p.ResidueField])) :
    ∃ g : S, Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
      GUnramified R (Localization.Away g)

Item (8), the `G-unramified` version, exported from

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber_of_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite type ring map whose fibre over `p` has differentials with vanishing fibre at a prime
`q` of that fibre is unramified at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (9)): there is a `g` in `S` whose image in
`κ(p) ⊗_R S` avoids `q` and with `R → S_g` unramified. Item (9) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_unramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber_of_fiber {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FiniteType R S] (p : Ideal R)
    [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Subsingleton (q.Fiber Ω[p.Fiber S⁄p.ResidueField])) :
    ∃ g : S, Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := p.ResidueField) g ∉ q ∧
      Unramified R (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment:
Item (9), the `unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber_of_fiber
declarations.doc:
**A finite presentation ring map whose fibre over `p` has differentials with vanishing fibre at
a prime `q` of that fibre is G-unramified at `q`** (Stacks 00UV (9)): there is a `g` in `S` whose
image in `κ(p) ⊗_R S` avoids `q` and with `R → S_g` G-unramified. Item (9) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_gUnramified_away_of_subsingleton_fiber_of_fiber {R : Type u}

declarations.name: Algebra.Unramified.of_span_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Being unramified is local on the target**: if `s ⊆ S` generates the unit ideal and `R → S_g`
is unramified for every `g ∈ s`, then `R → S` is unramified (Stacks 00UV (10)); item (10) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.comment:
Item (10), the `unramified` version, exported from
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Unramified.of_forall_prime
declarations.doc:
**A ring map unramified at every prime of the target is unramified** (Stacks 00UV (11));
item (11) of `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Unramified.of_forall_prime {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v}

    (H : ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], ∃ g ∉ q, Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) :

declarations.name: Algebra.GUnramified.exists_finiteType_int_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**A G-unramified ring map is a base change of a G-unramified map over a finite type
`ℤ`-algebra** (Stacks 00UV (12)): there are a subring `R₀ ⊆ R` of finite type over `ℤ` and a
G-unramified `R₀`-algebra `S₀` with `S ≃ R ⊗_{R₀} S₀` as `R`-algebras. Item (12) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.GUnramified.exists_finiteType_int_baseChange {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [GUnramified R S] :
    ∃ (R₀ : Subring R) (S₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀),
      FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ GUnramified R₀ S₀ ∧ Nonempty (S ≃ₐ[R] R ⊗[R₀] S₀)
declarations.comment: Item (12), exported from `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Unramified.exists_finiteType_int_surjective
declarations.doc:
**An unramified ring map is a quotient of a base change of an unramified map over a finite type
`ℤ`-algebra** (Stacks 00UV (13)): there are a subring `R₀ ⊆ R` of finite type over `ℤ` and an
unramified `R₀`-algebra `S₀` with a surjection `R ⊗_{R₀} S₀ → S` of `R`-algebras. Item (13) of
`Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Unramified.exists_finiteType_int_surjective {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Unramified R S] :
    ∃ (R₀ : Subring R) (S₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀)
      (f : (R ⊗[R₀] S₀) →ₐ[R] S),
      FiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ Unramified R₀ S₀ ∧ Function.Surjective f
declarations.comment: Item (13), exported from `Algebra.unramified_and_gUnramified_properties`.

declarations.name: Algebra.map_eq_maximalIdeal_and_finite_isSeparable_of_unramified_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00UW.** Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over a prime
`p` of `R`. If `R → S` is unramified at `q` — some `g ∉ q` has `R → S_g` unramified — then
(1) `p S_q = q S_q`, the maximal ideal of the local ring `S_q`, and (2) the residue field extension
`κ(q)/κ(p)` is finite separable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.map_eq_maximalIdeal_and_finite_isSeparable_of_unramified_away
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Localization.AtPrime.IsLiesOverAlgebra p q]
    (h : ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) :
    (p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) =
        q.map (algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime q)) ∧
      q.map (algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime q)) = maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) ∧
      Module.Finite p.ResidueField q.ResidueField ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField q.ResidueField
declarations.comment:
Unramified at `q` is the source's Definition 00UT(3),
`∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Unramified R (Localization.Away g)`. Item (1) is both equalities
`p S_q = q S_q` and `q S_q = m_{S_q}`; item (2) is `Module.Finite` and `Algebra.IsSeparable` for
`κ(p) → κ(q)`, Mathlib's `Ideal.ResidueField` with the canonical map induced by `R_p → S_q`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_surjective_of_isUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Étale local structure of a ring map unramified at a prime.** Let `S` be a finite type
`R`-algebra and let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over the prime `p` of `R` at which `S` is
unramified over `R`. There are an étale `R`-algebra `R'`, a prime `p'` of `R'` lying over `p` and
an idempotent `e` of `R' ⊗[R] S` — the product decomposition `R' ⊗[R] S = A × B` with
`A = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e]` and `B = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/(1 - e)]` — such that `R' → A` is surjective and
`p'A` is a prime of `A` lying over `p'` and, along `S → R' ⊗[R] S → A`, over `q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_surjective_of_isUnramifiedAt
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt R q] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R')
      (p' : Ideal R') (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p) (e : R' ⊗[R] S)
      (_ : IsIdempotentElem e),
      Function.Surjective (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away e)) ∧
      (p'.map (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away e))).IsPrime ∧
      (p'.map (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away e))).LiesOver p' ∧
      (p'.map (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away e))).comap
        ((algebraMap (R' ⊗[R] S) (Localization.Away e)).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : S →ₐ[R] R' ⊗[R] S).toRingHom) = q
declarations.comment:
The product decomposition `R' ⊗_R S = A × B` is given by an idempotent `e`, with
`A = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e]`, as in Mathlib's `Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_forall_liesOver_eq`
(Tag 00UJ); `p'A` lying over `q` is read along `S → R' ⊗[R] S → A`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_surjective_not_liesOver
declarations.doc:
**Separating the points of a fibre of an unramified ring map** (Stacks 00UY). Let `S` be an
unramified `R`-algebra and `p` a prime of `R`. There are an étale `R`-algebra `R'`, a prime `p'`
of `R'` lying over `p`, and a decomposition `R' ⊗[R] S = A₁ × ⋯ × Aₙ × B` — given by complete
orthogonal idempotents `e 0, …, e n`, with `Aᵢ = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e i]` and `B = (R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e n]`
— such that each `R' → Aᵢ` is surjective, each `p'Aᵢ` is a prime of `Aᵢ` lying over `p'`, and no
prime of `B` lies over `p'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_surjective_not_liesOver
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.Unramified R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R') (p' : Ideal R')
      (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p) (n : ℕ) (e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S)
      (_ : CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents e),
      (∀ i : Fin n, Function.Surjective (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away (e i.castSucc)))) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, (p'.map (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away (e i.castSucc)))).IsPrime) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, (p'.map (algebraMap R' (Localization.Away (e i.castSucc)))).LiesOver p') ∧
      ∀ q : Ideal (Localization.Away (e (Fin.last n))), q.IsPrime → ¬ q.LiesOver p'
declarations.comment:
The product decomposition is given by complete orthogonal idempotents
`e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S`, the factors being `(R' ⊗[R] S)[1/e i]`. The prime of `Aᵢ` lying
over `p'` is named as the source names it, namely `p'Aᵢ`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_bot
declarations.doc:
A morphism of presheaves is locally injective with respect to the trivial topology if and only
if it is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_bot {C : Type*} [Category* C] {A : Type*} [Category* A]
    {FA : A → A → Type*} {CA : A → Type*} [(X Y : A) → FunLike (FA X Y) (CA X) (CA Y)]
    [ConcreteCategory A FA] {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} {f : F ⟶ G} :
    IsLocallyInjective ⊥ f ↔ ∀ X, Function.Injective (f.app X)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_bot
declarations.doc:
A morphism of presheaves is locally surjective with respect to the trivial topology if and only
if it is surjective.
declarations.statement:
lemma Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_bot {C : Type*} [Category* C] {A : Type*} [Category* A]
    {FA : A → A → Type*} {CA : A → Type*} [(X Y : A) → FunLike (FA X Y) (CA X) (CA Y)]
    [ConcreteCategory A FA] {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} {f : F ⟶ G} :
    IsLocallySurjective ⊥ f ↔ ∀ X, Function.Surjective (f.app X)

declarations.statement:
lemma Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_bot_iff_mono {C : Type*} [Category* C] {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w}
    {f : F ⟶ G} : IsLocallyInjective ⊥ f ↔ Mono f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isIso_iff_isLocallyBijective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of presheaves of types is an isomorphism if and only if it is both injective and
surjective.
declarations.statement:
lemma Presheaf.isIso_iff_isLocallyBijective {C : Type*} [Category* C] {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w}
    {f : F ⟶ G} : IsIso f ↔ IsLocallyInjective ⊥ f ∧ IsLocallySurjective ⊥ f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.existsUnique_subfunctor_surjective_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00V9.** A map of presheaves of sets `φ : F ⟶ G` factors as `F ⟶ G' ⟶ G` with
`G' ⊆ G` a subpresheaf and the first map surjective on sections over every object, and the
subpresheaf `G'` doing this is unique: it is the pointwise image `U ↦ φ_U (F(U))` of `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_subfunctor_surjective_factorization (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    ∃! G' : Subfunctor G, ∃ ψ : F ⟶ G'.toFunctor,
      (∀ U, Function.Surjective (ψ.app U)) ∧ ψ ≫ G'.ι = φ
declarations.comment:
The unique subpresheaf `G' ⊆ G` through which `φ : F ⟶ G` factors with
  objectwise surjective first map, stated as `∃!` over `Subfunctor G`; the witness is the
  pointwise image `Subfunctor.range φ` with `Subfunctor.toRange φ`.

declarations.name: IsSite
declarations.doc:
A class of coverings is a *site* if it satisfies the isomorphism, composition and base
change axioms: these are axioms (1), (2) and (3) of Stacks 00VH, as `IsoCond`, `CompositionCond`
and `BaseChangeCond`. The set `Cov(𝒞)` is the predicate `IsCov`. The coverings are families of
morphisms with fixed target, indexed by a type (Stacks 0396), not presieves, so a family may
repeat a morphism. Following the clarification after 00VH, axiom (3) asks for the fibre products
`Uᵢ ×_U V` of the members of a covering only, and for the covering property of *some* choice of
them; no other fibre products are assumed to exist.

Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Pretopology`, which also carries Stacks 00VH, is the special case of a
category with all pullbacks, with coverings recorded as presieves and base change taken along
the chosen pullbacks; `IsSite.pretopologyBigFppfPretopology` produces it from a site when `C` has
pullbacks. Conversely `CategoryTheory.Precoverage.isSite_presieve₀_mem` produces a site from a
Mathlib precoverage with `HasIsos`, `IsStableUnderComposition`, `IsStableUnderBaseChange` and
`HasPullbacks`.
declarations.statement: def IsSite (IsCov : Covering.{u, v, w} C → Prop) : Prop
declarations.comment: Stacks' definition of a site: no fibre products beyond those of axiom (3).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.HomOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VT (1)**: a *morphism of families of morphisms with fixed target* from
`𝒰 = {U i ⟶ S}` to `𝒱 = {V j ⟶ T}` over a morphism `g : S ⟶ T` of the targets. It consists
of a map of index sets `s₀`, and for each index `i` a morphism `h₀ i : U i ⟶ V (s₀ i)`,
subject to commutativity of the square

```
U i          ⟶  V (s₀ i)
 |                 |
 v                 v
 S           ⟶     T
```

Mathlib's `PreZeroHypercover.Hom` is the special case in which the two families have the
same target and `g` is the identity; see `homOverIdEquivHom`.
declarations.statement:
structure HomOver {S T : C} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} S) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} T)
    (g : S ⟶ T)
declarations.comment: (1) A morphism of families of morphisms with fixed target.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.homOverIdEquivHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VT (2)**: a *refinement* is a morphism of families with fixed target whose
morphism of targets is the identity. Such morphisms are exactly Mathlib's
`PreZeroHypercover.Hom`, the morphisms of the category of families of morphisms with the
given fixed target.
declarations.statement:
def homOverIdEquivHom (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} S) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} S) :
    E.HomOver F (𝟙 S) ≃ E.Hom F
declarations.comment: (2) The special case `U = V` with `U ⟶ V` the identity: a refinement.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.Hom
registrations.comment:
(2) Refinements of a family of morphisms with fixed target are the
  morphisms of Mathlib's category of such families; `homOverIdEquivHom` identifies them with
  the morphisms of 00VT (1) whose morphism of targets is the identity.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.CombinatoriallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VU (1).** Two families of morphisms with the same fixed target `U` are
*combinatorially equivalent* if there are maps `α : I → J` and `β : J → I` with
`φ_i = ψ_{α i}` and `ψ_j = φ_{β j}`.

An equality of morphisms `φ_i = ψ_{α i}` presupposes an equality of their sources
`U_i = V_{α i}`, which is the `h` below; `eqToHom` transports along it.
declarations.statement:
def CombinatoriallyEquivalent
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.TautologicallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VU (2).** Two families of morphisms with the same fixed target `U` are
*tautologically equivalent* if there are maps `α : I → J` and `β : J → I` together with, for
every index, a commutative triangle over `U` whose horizontal arrow is an *isomorphism*:
`U_i ≅ V_{α i}` over `U`, and `V_j ≅ U_{β j}` over `U`.
declarations.statement:
def TautologicallyEquivalent
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.tautologicallyEquivalent_of_combinatoriallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (1).** Combinatorially equivalent families are tautologically equivalent: an
equality of sources gives an isomorphism between them, via `eqToIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tautologicallyEquivalent_of_combinatoriallyEquivalent
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U) :
    CombinatoriallyEquivalent E F → TautologicallyEquivalent E F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.nonempty_hom_and_nonempty_hom_of_tautologicallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (2).** Tautologically equivalent families refine each other: the horizontal
isomorphism of each triangle is in particular a morphism over the common target, so the
triangles assemble into a `PreZeroHypercover.Hom` in each direction.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_hom_and_nonempty_hom_of_tautologicallyEquivalent
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U) :
    TautologicallyEquivalent E F → Nonempty (E.Hom F) ∧ Nonempty (F.Hom E)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.combinatoriallyEquivalent_refl
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00VV (3).** Combinatorial equivalence is reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem combinatoriallyEquivalent_refl (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) :
    CombinatoriallyEquivalent E E

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.combinatoriallyEquivalent_trans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (3).** Combinatorial equivalence is transitive: compose the index maps and
the source equalities, and `eqToHom_trans` composes the transports.
declarations.statement:

    (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U) (G : PreZeroHypercover.{w''} U) :
    CombinatoriallyEquivalent E F → CombinatoriallyEquivalent F G →
      CombinatoriallyEquivalent E G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.combinatoriallyEquivalent_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (3)** as stated there: combinatorial equivalence *is* an equivalence relation
on the families of morphisms with fixed target `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem combinatoriallyEquivalent_equivalence :
    _root_.Equivalence (fun E F : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U => CombinatoriallyEquivalent E F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.tautologicallyEquivalent_refl
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00VV (4).** Tautological equivalence is reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem tautologicallyEquivalent_refl (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) :
    TautologicallyEquivalent E E

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.tautologicallyEquivalent_trans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (4).** Tautological equivalence is transitive: compose the index maps, and
compose the triangles' horizontal isomorphisms with `Iso.trans`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tautologicallyEquivalent_trans (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U)
    (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U) (G : PreZeroHypercover.{w''} U) :
    TautologicallyEquivalent E F → TautologicallyEquivalent F G →
      TautologicallyEquivalent E G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.tautologicallyEquivalent_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (4)** as stated there: tautological equivalence *is* an equivalence relation
on the families of morphisms with fixed target `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tautologicallyEquivalent_equivalence :
    _root_.Equivalence (fun E F : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U => TautologicallyEquivalent E F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.nonempty_hom_refl
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00VV (5).** Every family refines itself, by the identity refinement.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_hom_refl (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) :
    Nonempty (E.Hom E) ∧ Nonempty (E.Hom E)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.nonempty_hom_trans
declarations.doc: **Stacks 00VV (5).** Mutual refinement is transitive, by composing refinements.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_hom_trans (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U)
    (G : PreZeroHypercover.{w''} U) :
    (Nonempty (E.Hom F) ∧ Nonempty (F.Hom E)) → (Nonempty (F.Hom G) ∧ Nonempty (G.Hom F)) →
      (Nonempty (E.Hom G) ∧ Nonempty (G.Hom E))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.nonempty_hom_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VV (5)** as stated there: mutual refinement *is* an equivalence relation on the
families of morphisms with fixed target `U`. Symmetry is the swap.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_hom_equivalence :
    _root_.Equivalence
      (fun E F : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U => Nonempty (E.Hom F) ∧ Nonempty (F.Hom E))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.isSheafFor_presieve₀_iff_of_tautologicallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VW.** Tautologically equivalent families of morphisms with a fixed target
generate the same sieve, hence impose the same sheaf condition on every presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_presieve₀_iff_of_tautologicallyEquivalent
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U)

    Presieve.IsSheafFor P E.presieve₀ ↔ Presieve.IsSheafFor P F.presieve₀

declarations.name: Covering.isSheaf_of_tautologicallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VX (1)**, the inclusion: if every covering of the site `IsCov₁` is tautologically
equivalent to some covering of the site `IsCov₂`, then `Sh(C, IsCov₂) ⊆ Sh(C, IsCov₁)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_of_tautologicallyEquivalent {IsCov₁ : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C → Prop}
    {IsCov₂ : Covering.{u, v, w₂} C → Prop} (_h₁ : IsSite IsCov₁) (_h₂ : IsSite IsCov₂)
    (h : ∀ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C, IsCov₁ 𝒰 → ∃ 𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w₂} 𝒰.1,
      IsCov₂ ⟨𝒰.1, 𝒱⟩ ∧ PreZeroHypercover.TautologicallyEquivalent 𝒰.2 𝒱)
    (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type t) (hP : IsSheaf IsCov₂ P) : IsSheaf IsCov₁ P

declarations.name: Covering.isSheaf_iff_of_tautologicallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VX (1)**, the equality: if moreover every covering of `IsCov₂` is tautologically
equivalent to some covering of `IsCov₁`, then the two sites have the same sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_iff_of_tautologicallyEquivalent {IsCov₁ : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C → Prop}
    {IsCov₂ : Covering.{u, v, w₂} C → Prop} (h₁ : IsSite IsCov₁) (h₂ : IsSite IsCov₂)
    (h₁₂ : ∀ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C, IsCov₁ 𝒰 → ∃ 𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w₂} 𝒰.1,
      IsCov₂ ⟨𝒰.1, 𝒱⟩ ∧ PreZeroHypercover.TautologicallyEquivalent 𝒰.2 𝒱)
    (h₂₁ : ∀ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w₂} C, IsCov₂ 𝒰 → ∃ 𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w₁} 𝒰.1,
      IsCov₁ ⟨𝒰.1, 𝒱⟩ ∧ PreZeroHypercover.TautologicallyEquivalent 𝒰.2 𝒱)
    (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type t) : IsSheaf IsCov₁ P ↔ IsSheaf IsCov₂ P

declarations.name: Covering.isSheaf_of_factorsThru
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VX (2)**, the inclusion: if every covering of the site `IsCov₁` is refined by some
covering of the site `IsCov₂`, then `Sh(C, IsCov₂) ⊆ Sh(C, IsCov₁)`.

As in the source, a sheaf for `IsCov₂` is a sheaf for the refining covering `{Vⱼ ⟶ U}` and,
by the base change axiom of `IsCov₂`, separated for each `{Vⱼ ×_U Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ}`; this is the input
of Stacks 0G1L, here `Presieve.isSheafFor_of_factorsThru`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_of_factorsThru {IsCov₁ : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C → Prop}
    {IsCov₂ : Covering.{u, v, w₂} C → Prop} (_h₁ : IsSite IsCov₁) (h₂ : IsSite IsCov₂)
    (h : ∀ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C, IsCov₁ 𝒰 → ∃ 𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w₂} 𝒰.1,
      IsCov₂ ⟨𝒰.1, 𝒱⟩ ∧ 𝒱.presieve₀.FactorsThru 𝒰.2.presieve₀)
    (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type t) (hP : IsSheaf IsCov₂ P) : IsSheaf IsCov₁ P

declarations.name: Covering.isSheaf_iff_of_factorsThru
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VX (2)**, the equality: if moreover every covering of `IsCov₂` is refined by some
covering of `IsCov₁`, then the two sites have the same sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_iff_of_factorsThru {IsCov₁ : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C → Prop}
    {IsCov₂ : Covering.{u, v, w₂} C → Prop} (h₁ : IsSite IsCov₁) (h₂ : IsSite IsCov₂)
    (h₁₂ : ∀ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w₁} C, IsCov₁ 𝒰 → ∃ 𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w₂} 𝒰.1,
      IsCov₂ ⟨𝒰.1, 𝒱⟩ ∧ 𝒱.presieve₀.FactorsThru 𝒰.2.presieve₀)
    (h₂₁ : ∀ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w₂} C, IsCov₂ 𝒰 → ∃ 𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w₁} 𝒰.1,
      IsCov₁ ⟨𝒰.1, 𝒱⟩ ∧ 𝒱.presieve₀.FactorsThru 𝒰.2.presieve₀)
    (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type t) : IsSheaf IsCov₁ P ↔ IsSheaf IsCov₂ P

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.sh_eq_of_forall_combinatoriallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00VY**: if `Cov₁ ⊆ Cov` and `Cov₂ ⊆ Cov` and every covering in `Cov` is
combinatorially equivalent to a covering in `Cov₁` and to a covering in `Cov₂`, then
`Sh(𝒞, Cov₁) = Sh(𝒞, Cov₂)`. The source assumes that `Cov` satisfies the axioms of 00VH and that
`Cov₁`, `Cov₂` are sites; the conclusion holds for arbitrary covering data, so this statement
takes no site axiom and no fibre products and contains the source's as a special case. Here
`Sh Cov` is the category of sheaves for the topology generated by `Cov`;
`forall_isSheafFor_iff_of_forall_combinatoriallyEquivalent` gives the same conclusion for the
sheaf condition taken family by family.
declarations.statement:
theorem sh_eq_of_forall_combinatoriallyEquivalent (Cov Cov₁ Cov₂ : CovData.{w, v, u} C)
    (hCov₁_sub : CovData.Subset Cov₁ Cov) (hCov₂_sub : CovData.Subset Cov₂ Cov)
    (h₁ : ∀ ⦃U : C⦄ ⦃E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U⦄, E ∈ Cov U →
      ∃ F : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U, F ∈ Cov₁ U ∧ CombinatoriallyEquivalent E F)
    (h₂ : ∀ ⦃U : C⦄ ⦃E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U⦄, E ∈ Cov U →
      ∃ F : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U, F ∈ Cov₂ U ∧ CombinatoriallyEquivalent E F) :
    Sh Cov₁ = Sh Cov₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.Sheaf.Action.exists_equivalence_sheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00W0**. Sheaves on `𝒯_G` are `G`-sets: let `G` be a monoid and let `J` be a
Grothendieck topology on a full subcategory `ι : T ⥤ Action (Type u) G` of the category of `G`-sets
whose essential image contains the left regular `G`-set `{}_G G` and whose covering sieves are
exactly the jointly surjective ones. Then `G`-sets are equivalent to the sheaves of sets on
`(T, J)` by an equivalence whose forward functor sends a `G`-set `S` to the sheaf
`U ↦ Hom_G(ι U, S)`; the quasi-inverse is `F ↦ F({}_G G)`. The source states this for a group.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Action.exists_equivalence_sheaf {T : Type w} [Category.{v} T] {G : Type u}
    [Monoid G] (ι : T ⥤ Action (Type u) G) [ι.Full] [ι.Faithful]
    (hreg : ι.essImage (Action.leftRegular G)) (J : GrothendieckTopology T)
    (hJ :
      ∀ (U : T) (S : Sieve U),
        S ∈ J U ↔
          ∀ a : Action.leftRegular G ⟶ ι.obj U,
            ∃ (V : T) (f : V ⟶ U) (b : Action.leftRegular G ⟶ ι.obj V),
              S.arrows f ∧ b ≫ ι.map f = a) :
    ∃ e : Action (Type u) G ≌ Sheaf J (Type u),
      e.functor ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J (Type u) =
        yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft Tᵒᵖ (Action (Type u) G)ᵒᵖ (Type u)).obj ι.op

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.createsLimitsOfShape

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.terminal
registrations.comment:

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isTerminalTerminal

  limit of the empty diagram of sheaves

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plusObj
registrations.comment:
The presheaf `F⁺`. Mathlib builds the colimit over covering sieves
  rather than over covering families, i.e. the functor `L` of Stacks section 7.49; the
  functoriality in the object that 00W4 asserts is the `map` field of this functor, and its
  compatibility with composition `F⁺(U) → F⁺(V) → F⁺(W)` is `Functor.map_comp`, which is
  exactly what the proof of 00W4 verifies.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.toPlus
registrations.comment: The canonical map of presheaves `F → F⁺` of 00W4.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.toPlus_naturality
registrations.comment:

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.intersection_covering
registrations.comment: common refinement

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.H0.mapOver_eq_of_homOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00W7.** Any two morphisms of families `𝒰 → 𝒱` inducing the same morphism of
targets induce the same map `H⁰(𝒱, F) → H⁰(𝒰, F)`.

Because `HomOver` carries the base morphism as a parameter, "inducing the same morphism of
targets" is expressed by the two morphisms having the same type, and the statement is that the
induced map depends on `g` alone. The proof applies the matching property of `s` at the single
cone `(U_i, φ.h₀ i, ψ.h₀ i)`, which commutes over `V` precisely because both morphisms lie
over `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem H0.mapOver_eq_of_homOver {E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U} {G : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} V}
    {g : U ⟶ V} (φ ψ : E.HomOver G g) : H0.mapOver F φ = H0.mapOver F ψ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.H0.mapOver_bijective_of_mutual_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00W8.** If `𝒰` refines `𝒱` and `𝒱` refines `𝒰`, the two induced pullback maps on
`H⁰` are mutually inverse bijections, so there is a canonical identification
`H⁰(𝒰, F) = H⁰(𝒱, F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem H0.mapOver_bijective_of_mutual_refinement {E G : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U}
    (φ : E.HomOver G (𝟙 U)) (ψ : G.HomOver E (𝟙 U)) :
    (∀ s : H0 F E, H0.mapOver F φ (H0.mapOver F ψ s) = s) ∧
      (∀ t : H0 F G, H0.mapOver F ψ (H0.mapOver F φ t) = t)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.H0.refinementEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00W8**, packaged as the bijection `H⁰(𝒱, F) ≃ H⁰(𝒰, F)` determined by mutual
refinements. By 00W7 it does not depend on which refinements are chosen.
declarations.statement:
def H0.refinementEquiv {E G : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U}
    (φ : E.HomOver G (𝟙 U)) (ψ : G.HomOver E (𝟙 U)) : H0 F G ≃ H0 F E

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.H0.refinementEquiv_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00W8**, the independence clause: the identification above is canonical, since any
two refinements `𝒰 → 𝒱` induce the same map. This is 00W7 at `g = 𝟙 U`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
Sheafification `presheafToSheaf J A : PSh(C) ⥤ Sh(C)`, `F ↦ F^#`, preserves finite colimits,
for sheaves with values in any category `A` in which sheafification exists.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (A : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂} A] [HasWeakSheafify J A] :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (presheafToSheaf J A)
declarations.comment:
Sheafification `PSh(C) → Sh(C)`, `F ↦ F^#`, is exact: it commutes with finite limits
  and with finite colimits. This is the right-exact half; the left-exact half is
  `presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteLimits`.

declarations.name: presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WJ**, left-exact half. Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `A` be a concrete category in
which the plus construction `F ↦ F^+` can be carried out and whose finite limits and coverings
colimits are computed on underlying sets. Then sheafification
`presheafToSheaf J A : PSh(C) ⥤ Sh(C)`, `F ↦ F^#`, preserves finite limits. Together with
`CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits`, which holds because `F ↦ F^#` is a left
adjoint, this says that sheafification is exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteLimits
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type w) [Category.{t} A]
    {FA : A → A → Type*} {CA : A → Type t} [∀ X Y, FunLike (FA X Y) (CA X) (CA Y)]
    [ConcreteCategory.{t} A FA]
    [∀ (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (X : C) (S : J.Cover X), HasMultiequalizer (S.index P)]
    [∀ X : C, HasColimitsOfShape (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ A]
    [∀ X : C, PreservesColimitsOfShape (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ (forget A)]
    [∀ {X : C} (S : J.Cover X), PreservesLimitsOfShape (WalkingMulticospan S.shape) (forget A)]
    [∀ X : C, Small.{t, max u v} (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ]
    [(forget A).ReflectsIsomorphisms] [HasFiniteLimits A] [PreservesFiniteLimits (forget A)] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (presheafToSheaf J A)
declarations.comment:
Sheafification `PSh(C) → Sh(C)`, `F ↦ F^#`, is exact: it commutes with finite limits
  and with finite colimits. This is the left-exact half; the right-exact half is
  `CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits`.

declarations.name: sheafify_local_description
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WK.** Let `P` be a presheaf of sets on a site, `θ² : P → P♯` the canonical map.
Every `s ∈ P♯(U)` admits a covering `{U_i → U}` and `s_i ∈ P(U_i)` with (1)
`s|_{U_i} = θ²(s_i)` and (2) for all `i, j`, the pullbacks of `s_i` and `s_j` agree on a
covering of `U_i ×_U U_j`. Conversely, for any covering and `s_i` satisfying (2) there is a
unique `s ∈ P♯(U)` satisfying (1). Coverings are covering sieves of `J`, indexed by their
arrows; `P` takes values in `Type (max u v)`, the universe of Mathlib's `J.sheafify`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafify_local_description :
    (∀ {U : C} (s : (J.sheafify P).obj (op U)),
      ∃ (𝒰 : J.Cover U) (s_ : ∀ I : 𝒰.Arrow, P.obj (op I.Y)),
        IsLocalDescription J P 𝒰 s s_ ∧ LocallyAgreeOnOverlaps J P 𝒰 s_) ∧
    (∀ {U : C} (𝒰 : J.Cover U) (s_ : ∀ I : 𝒰.Arrow, P.obj (op I.Y)),
      LocallyAgreeOnOverlaps J P 𝒰 s_ →
        ∃! s : (J.sheafify P).obj (op U), IsLocalDescription J P 𝒰 s s_)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLocallyInjective_iff_injective
registrations.comment:
(1) A map of sheaves is injective, in the sense of 00WM (1) that it is
  injective on the sections over every object, exactly when it is locally injective in
  Mathlib's sense. Mathlib's class is stated for an arbitrary concrete category of values;
  this lemma is what identifies it with the pointwise-injectivity definition of 00WM (1).

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
registrations.comment:
(2) The predicate of 00WM (2): every section of the target is locally, on
  a covering, in the image. Mathlib's single field `imageSieve_mem` is that condition.

declarations.name: mono_iff_isInjective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of sheaves of sets is a monomorphism in the category of sheaves if and only if it
is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff_isInjective {F G : Sheaf J (Type max v u)} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    Mono φ ↔ IsInjective J φ

declarations.name: epi_iff_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of sheaves of sets is an epimorphism in the category of sheaves if and only if it
is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_iff_isSurjective {F G : Sheaf J (Type max v u)} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    Epi φ ↔ IsSurjectiveSheafType J φ

declarations.name: isIso_iff_isInjective_and_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism if and only if it is both injective and
surjective.

declarations.name: StacksEffectiveEpi.IsEffectiveEpiFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WP.** A family `{X i ⟶ B}` in a category `C` is an *effective epimorphic
family* if it is representable and if for every object `Y` the diagram
`Mor(B, Y) → ∏ᵢ Mor(X i, Y) ⇉ ∏₍ᵢ,ⱼ₎ Mor(X i ×_B X j, Y)` is an equalizer.

The equalizer condition is spelled out as: a family `g i : X i ⟶ Y` whose two restrictions
to any fibre product `X i ×_B X j` agree extends uniquely to `B`.  Both halves of the
equalizer property are contained in the `∃!`: uniqueness says that
`Mor(B, Y) → ∏ᵢ Mor(X i, Y)` is injective, existence says that its image is the set of
compatible families.  Fibre products are referred to through `IsPullback`, so that the
condition does not depend on a choice of pullbacks; representability guarantees that at
least one such square exists for every pair `(i, j)`.
declarations.statement: def IsEffectiveEpiFamily : Prop

declarations.name: StacksEffectiveEpi.IsUniversalEffectiveEpiFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WP.** A family `{X i ⟶ B}` is a *universal effective epimorphic family* if it
is representable and if for every morphism `h : V ⟶ B` the base-changed family
`{X i ×_B V ⟶ V}` is an effective epimorphic family.
declarations.statement: def IsUniversalEffectiveEpiFamily : Prop

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical
registrations.comment:
a topology is subcanonical when every representable presheaf is a sheaf
  for it

declarations.name: IsRepresentableSheaf
declarations.doc:
A sheaf `F` on a site whose topology `J` is subcanonical is *representable* if it is
isomorphic to the sheaf `h_U = J.yoneda.obj U` for some object `U`. This is
`(GrothendieckTopology.yoneda J).essImage` with the witnessing isomorphism written the other way
round.
declarations.statement:
def IsRepresentableSheaf {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [J.Subcanonical]
    (F : Sheaf J (Type v)) : Prop

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.yonedaFullyFaithful
registrations.comment: full subcategory of sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.CoveredByRepresentables.exists_isColimit_cofork_sigma_sheafifiedYoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WS.** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `E ⊆ Ob(C)` be such that every object of `C`
has a covering by elements of `E` (`IsCoveringSubset J E`). Let `F00WS` be a sheaf of sets.
Then there is a diagram of sheaves of sets `F₁ ⇉ F₀ → F00WS` exhibiting `F00WS` as a
coequalizer, where `F₀ = ∐_{i ∈ I₀} h_{U₀ i}^♯` and `F₁ = ∐_{i ∈ I₁} h_{U₁ i}^♯` are coproducts
(in the category of sheaves) of sheafified representables `h_U^♯` with `U ∈ E`.

Proof as in Stacks: `σ : F₀ ⟶ F00WS` is an epimorphism (`epi_σ`), and so is the analogous map
`F₁ ⟶ F₀ ×_{F00WS} F₀` onto the kernel pair; an epimorphism of sheaves of sets is the
coequalizer of its kernel pair, and precomposing with an epimorphism keeps it a coequalizer.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isColimit_cofork_sigma_sheafifiedYoneda {E : Set C} (hE : IsCoveringSubset J E)
    (F00WS : Sheaf J (Type max v u)) :
    ∃ (I₀ I₁ : Type max v u) (U₀ : I₀ → E) (U₁ : I₁ → E)
      (f g : (∐ fun i => sheafifiedYoneda J (U₁ i).val) ⟶
        ∐ fun i => sheafifiedYoneda J (U₀ i).val)
      (p : (∐ fun i => sheafifiedYoneda J (U₀ i).val) ⟶ F00WS) (w : f ≫ p = g ≫ p),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ p w))

declarations.name: isLocallySurjective_coprodYonedaDesc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WT.** Let `(C, J)` be a site. If `{f_i : U_i ⟶ U}_{i ∈ I}` is a covering of `U`,
then the canonical map `∐_i h_{U_i} ⟶ h_U` of presheaves of sets is locally surjective for
`J`; equivalently, it becomes an epimorphism after sheafification.
declarations.statement:
