theorem isLocallySurjective_coprodYonedaDesc
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    {I : Type v} (U : I → C) (X : C) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X)
    (hf : Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows U f) ∈ J X) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (coprodYonedaDesc U X f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Site.IsContinuous
declarations.doc:
A functor `u : C ⥤ D` between sites is *continuous* (Stacks 00WV) if for every covering
`{V_i → V}_{i ∈ I}` of `C`
1. the family `{u(V_i) → u(V)}_{i ∈ I}` is a covering of `D`, and
2. for every morphism `T → V` of `C` the morphism `u(T ×_V V_i) → u(T) ×_{u(V)} u(V_i)` is an
   isomorphism.

The fibre products in clause (2) exist by axiom (3) of `C`, resp. of `D` applied to the covering
of clause (1).
declarations.statement: structure IsContinuous (SC : Site.{w} C) (SD : Site.{w} D) (u : C ⥤ D) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isSheafFor_op_comp_of_preservesLimit_cospan
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WW.** Let `J` and `K` be precoverages on `C` and `D` such that the fibre products
`T ×_V Vᵢ` of a `J`-covering `{Vᵢ ⟶ V}` with any `T ⟶ V` exist (axiom (3) of a site, Stacks
00VH), and let `u : C ⥤ D` be continuous in the sense of Stacks 00WV:
`hcov` says that the image `{u(Vᵢ) ⟶ u(V)}` of a `J`-covering is a `K`-covering, and `hpb` that
`u` carries each fibre product `T ×_V Vᵢ` to a fibre product. If a presheaf of sets `F` on `D`
satisfies the sheaf condition for every `K`-covering, then `u^p F = u.op ⋙ F` satisfies it for
every `J`-covering.

The remaining axioms of a site (isomorphisms and composites of coverings are coverings, and
coverings are stable under base change) are not used, so they are not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_op_comp_of_preservesLimit_cospan (J : Precoverage C) (K : Precoverage D)
    [J.HasPullbacks] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (hcov : ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ ⦃R : Presieve V⦄, R ∈ J V → R.map u ∈ K (u.obj V))
    (hpb : ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ ⦃R : Presieve V⦄, R ∈ J V → ∀ ⦃Vᵢ : C⦄ ⦃f : Vᵢ ⟶ V⦄, R f →
      ∀ ⦃T : C⦄ (g : T ⟶ V), PreservesLimit (cospan g f) u)
    (F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) (hF : ∀ ⦃U : D⦄ (S : Presieve U), S ∈ K U → Presieve.IsSheafFor F S)
    ⦃V : C⦄ (R : Presieve V) (hR : R ∈ J V) : Presieve.IsSheafFor (u.op ⋙ F) R
declarations.comment: u^p of a sheaf is a sheaf, for the sheaf condition on the coverings of the sites

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_toGrothendieck_of_preservesLimit_cospan
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WW**, for the Grothendieck topologies generated by the coverings. Let `J` and `K`
be precoverages on `C` and `D` whose coverings have fibre products with arbitrary morphisms and
are stable under base change (axiom (3) of a site, Stacks 00VH), and let `u : C ⥤ D` be
continuous in the sense of Stacks 00WV (`hcov`, `hpb`, as in
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isSheafFor_op_comp_of_preservesLimit_cospan`). Then restriction along `u`
carries sheaves for the topology generated by `K` to sheaves for the topology generated by `J`,
that is, `u` is `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_toGrothendieck_of_preservesLimit_cospan (J : Precoverage C)
    (K : Precoverage D) [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] [K.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [K.HasPullbacks] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (hcov : ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ ⦃R : Presieve V⦄, R ∈ J V → R.map u ∈ K (u.obj V))
    (hpb : ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ ⦃R : Presieve V⦄, R ∈ J V → ∀ ⦃Vᵢ : C⦄ ⦃f : Vᵢ ⟶ V⦄, R f →
      ∀ ⦃T : C⦄ (g : T ⟶ V), PreservesLimit (cospan g f) u) :
    u.IsContinuous J.toGrothendieck K.toGrothendieck
declarations.comment: u^p of a sheaf is a sheaf, for the generated Grothendieck topologies

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous
registrations.comment: the sheaf pushforward `u^s : Sh(D) ⥤ Sh(C)` along a continuous functor

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
registrations.comment: the sheafified pushforward `u_s : G ↦ (u_p G)^#`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
registrations.comment: the sheafified pushforward is left adjoint to the sheaf pushforward

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.lanCompPresheafToSheafIsoSheafPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WY**.
For a continuous functor `u : C ⥤ D` between sites and a presheaf `G` on `C`,
`(u_p G)^# ≅ (u_p (G^#))^# = u_s (G^#)`, naturally in `G`: the composite of
`u_p = u.op.lan` with sheafification on `D` is isomorphic to sheafification on `C` followed by
the sheaf pullback `u_s = u.sheafPullback`. The right adjointness of `u^s` needed to form
`u.sheafPullback` is Mathlib's instance built from `u_p` and sheafification on `D`, so it is
not a hypothesis here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lanCompPresheafToSheafIsoSheafPullback
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (A : Type u₃)
    [Category.{v₃} A] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (u : C ⥤ D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K] [HasWeakSheafify J A] [HasWeakSheafify K A]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasLeftKanExtension F] :
    u.op.lan ⋙ presheafToSheaf K A ≅ presheafToSheaf J A ⋙ u.sheafPullback A J K

declarations.name: QuasiMorphismOfSites.IsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WZ (definition).** A functor `u : C ⥤ D` between sites, presented by precoverages
`JC` and `JD`, is *quasi-continuous* if for every covering `𝒱 = {V_i → V}` of `C`:
* (1') the image family `{u(V_i) → u(V)}` is tautologically equivalent to a covering of `D`; and
* (2) for every morphism `T → V` of `C` the canonical morphism
  `u(T ×_V V_i) → u(T) ×_{u(V)} u(V_i)` is an isomorphism, i.e. `u` carries the fibre square
  `T ×_V V_i` (which exists when `JC` has pullbacks along coverings) to a fibre square of `D`.

Unlike `IsQuasiContinuous`, nothing here asks `C` or `D` to have all fibre products; the two
notions agree for pretopologies on categories with fibre products
(`isQuasiContinuousPrecoverage_toPrecoverage_iff`).
declarations.statement:
def IsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D]
    (u : C ⥤ D) (JC : Precoverage C) (JD : Precoverage D) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition of quasi-continuous, for sites given by precoverages

declarations.name: QuasiMorphismOfSites.isContinuous_of_isQuasiContinuousPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WZ (Lemma 00WW for quasi-continuous functors).** Let `C` and `D` be sites in the
sense of Stacks, given by precoverages `JC` and `JD`, where `JC` has the fibre products along its
coverings and is stable under base change. If `u : C ⥤ D` is quasi-continuous
(`IsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage`), then `u^p F` is a sheaf for every sheaf of sets `F` on `D`,
i.e. `u` is continuous for the associated topologies. No global fibre products are assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_of_isQuasiContinuousPrecoverage
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (JC : Precoverage C) (JD : Precoverage D) [JC.HasPullbacks] [JC.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hu : IsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage u JC JD) :
    u.IsContinuous JC.toGrothendieck JD.toGrothendieck
declarations.comment: Lemma 00WW holds for quasi-continuous functors

declarations.name: QuasiMorphismOfSites.sheafAdjunctionOfIsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00WZ (Lemma 00WX for quasi-continuous functors).** In the situation of
`isContinuous_of_isQuasiContinuousPrecoverage`, the functor `u_s : 𝒢 ↦ (u_p 𝒢)^#` (left Kan
extension along `u` followed by sheafification) is left adjoint to restriction
`u^s : Sh(D) → Sh(C)` of sheaves of sets.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafAdjunctionOfIsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (JC : Precoverage C) (JD : Precoverage D) [JC.HasPullbacks] [JC.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hu : IsQuasiContinuousPrecoverage u JC JD) :
    letI := isContinuous_of_isQuasiContinuousPrecoverage u JC JD hu
    Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback u (Type u) JC.toGrothendieck
        JD.toGrothendieck ⊣
      u.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) JC.toGrothendieck JD.toGrothendieck
declarations.comment: Lemma 00WX holds for quasi-continuous functors

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Site.IsMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
A *morphism of sites* `f : D → C` (Stacks 00X1) is given by a continuous functor
`u : C ⥤ D` (Stacks 00WV) such that the functor `u_s : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(D)`, `G ↦ (u_p G)^#`, on
sheaves of sets is exact, i.e. preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Here `u_s` is
`Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback`, the restriction to sheaves of the left Kan
extension along `u.op` followed by sheafification.
declarations.statement: structure IsMorphismOfSites (SC : Site.{w} C) (SD : Site.{w} D) (u : C ⥤ D) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksZariskiSite.topPushforward_eq_sheafPushforwardContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00X2.** The site-theoretic pushforward `u^s` along `u = Opens.map f` is the usual
topological pushforward `f_*` on sheaves of sets: Mathlib's `TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward` is defined
to be precisely `(Opens.map f).sheafPushforwardContinuous`, so the identification asserted by the
example holds on the nose.
declarations.statement:
theorem topPushforward_eq_sheafPushforwardContinuous :
    TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) f =
      (Opens.map f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)

declarations.name: StacksZariskiSite.topPullback_eq_sheafPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00X2.** The site-theoretic pullback `u_s` along `u = Opens.map f` is the usual
topological pullback `f⁻¹` on sheaves of sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem topPullback_eq_sheafPullback :
    TopCat.Sheaf.pullback (Type u) f =
      (Opens.map f).sheafPullback (Type u) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)

declarations.name: StacksZariskiSite.topAdjunction_eq_sheafAdjunctionContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00X2.** Consequently the topological adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*` is the site-theoretic
adjunction `u_s ⊣ u^s`; this is the step by which the example concludes `f⁻¹ ≅ u_s` from
uniqueness of adjoints.
declarations.statement:
theorem topAdjunction_eq_sheafAdjunctionContinuous :
    TopCat.Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Type u) f =
      (Opens.map f).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type u) (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)

declarations.name: StacksZariskiSite.isMorphismOfSites_opensMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00X2.** The functor `u = Opens.map f : Y_Zar ⥤ X_Zar`, `V ↦ f⁻¹(V)`, defines a
morphism of sites `X_Zar → Y_Zar`: it is continuous, and the induced pullback `u_s = f⁻¹` on
sheaves of sets is exact.

Continuity is Mathlib's instance for `Opens.map f` and the Zariski topologies.  For exactness the
example argues that `u_s ≅ f⁻¹` is exact because `f⁻¹` is; here it is obtained from the criterion
of Stacks 00X5 (`CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_representablyFlat`), whose hypothesis
`RepresentablyFlat (Opens.map f)` holds because the categories `I_V^u` of Stacks 00VC are the
lattices of open `W ⊆ Y` with `V ⊆ f⁻¹(W)`, which are closed under intersection and contain
`W = Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_opensMap :
    (Opens.map f).IsMorphismOfSites (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)

declarations.name: isFiltered_op_structuredArrow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00X3.** Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a functor. Suppose `C` has a terminal
object whose image under `u` is terminal in `D`, and `C` has fibre products
which `u` preserves. Then for every `V : D` the opposite of the comma category
`StructuredArrow V u` is filtered.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_op_structuredArrow
    (u : C ⥤ D) [HasTerminal C] [HasPullbacks C]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) u]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u] (V : D) :
    IsFiltered (StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.structuredArrow_op_span_and_parallelPair_completion
declarations.doc:
If `C` has fibre products and equalizers and `u : C ⥤ D` preserves them, then for every
`V : D`, in `(StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ` every span can be completed to a commutative square and every
parallel pair can be coequalized.
declarations.statement:
theorem structuredArrow_op_span_and_parallelPair_completion
    (u : C ⥤ D) [HasPullbacks C] [HasEqualizers C]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair u]
    (V : D) :
    (∀ (w x y : (StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ) (a : w ⟶ x) (b : w ⟶ y),
        ∃ (z : (StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ) (c : x ⟶ z) (d : y ⟶ z),
          a ≫ c = b ≫ d) ∧
    (∀ (x y : (StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ) (a b : x ⟶ y),
        ∃ (z : (StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ) (c : y ⟶ z),
          a ≫ c = b ≫ c)

declarations.name: isMorphismOfSites_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00X5 at the universe of a small model.**  A continuous representably flat functor
between two sites that are essentially small at `u` defines a morphism of sites for sheaves of
sets valued in `Type u`, one universe below the objects of the sites.

The left exact left adjoint of the direct image is the pullback along the transported functor on
the small models, which is left exact by Stacks 00X5 at the universe of a genuinely small site,
conjugated by the two restriction equivalences along the comparisons with the small models.
declarations.comment: the site condition at the universe of a small model

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_isFiltered_op
declarations.doc:
Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between sites and assume that all the
categories `(I_V^u)ᵒᵖ` of Stacks 00VC are filtered. Then `u` defines a morphism of sites `D → C`,
in other words `u_s` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_of_isFiltered_op (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) [u.IsContinuous J K]
    (h : ∀ V : D, IsFiltered (StructuredArrow V u)ᵒᵖ) : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K
declarations.comment:
A continuous functor all of whose index categories `(I_V^u)ᵒᵖ` are filtered defines
  a morphism of sites; equivalently a continuous representably flat functor does.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_isTerminal
declarations.doc:
Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between sites. Assume furthermore that

1. the category `C` has a final object `X` and `u(X)` is a final object of `D`, and
2. the category `C` has fibre products and `u` commutes with them.

Then `u` defines a morphism of sites `D → C`, in other words `u_s` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_of_isTerminal (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) [u.IsContinuous J K] [HasPullbacks C]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u] {X : C} (hX : IsTerminal X)
    (huX : IsTerminal (u.obj X)) : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K
declarations.comment:
A continuous functor `u` such that `C` has a final object sent by `u` to a final
  object and has fibre products preserved by `u` defines a morphism of sites; this is the criterion
  under which `u` induces a morphism of topoi with exact pullback.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesTerminal_and_pullbacks
registrations.comment:
If the category has a final object and fibre products, a functor preserving the
  final object and fibre products is left exact (preserves finite limits).

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits.preservesFiniteLimits
registrations.comment:
Conversely, a left exact functor preserves limits of every finite shape, in
  particular final objects and fibre products.

declarations.name: QuasiMorphismOfSites.IsQuasiMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Definition 5 (Quasi-morphism of sites).** Given a quasi-continuous functor
`u : C → D` (witnessed by `hqc`), `u` defines a quasi-morphism of sites
`f : D → C` if the induced left adjoint `u_s : Sh(C) → Sh(D)` on set-valued
sheaves is exact. The continuity instance needed to form
`u_s = u.sheafPullback` is derived from `hqc` via Background Lemma A, not
assumed.
declarations.statement:
def IsQuasiMorphismOfSites
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D]
    [HasPullbacks C] [HasPullbacks D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (PC : Pretopology C) (PD : Pretopology D)
    (hqc : IsQuasiContinuous u PC PD) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition of quasi-morphism of sites

declarations.name: QuasiMorphismOfSites.isQuasiMorphismOfSites_of_isQuasiContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.** A quasi-continuous functor `u : C → D` between sites that
preserves the terminal object and preserves fibre products (pullbacks) defines a
quasi-morphism of sites: the induced functor `u_s : Sh(C) → Sh(D)` on set-valued
sheaves is exact. Continuity is derived internally from quasi-continuity via
Background Lemma A and is not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiMorphismOfSites_of_isQuasiContinuous
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D]
    [HasPullbacks C] [HasPullbacks D] [HasTerminal C]
    (u : C ⥤ D) (PC : Pretopology C) (PD : Pretopology D)
    (hqc : IsQuasiContinuous u PC PD)
    -- Hypothesis (1): `u` sends the final object of `C` to a final object of `D`.
    (hterminal : PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) u)
    -- Hypothesis (2): `u` commutes with fibre products.
    (hpullbacks : PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u) :
    IsQuasiMorphismOfSites u PC PD hqc

declarations.name: SheafToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XA (1).** Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites. A *morphism of topoi* `f` from
`Sh(D)` to `Sh(C)` is a pair of functors `f_* : Sh(D) ⥤ Sh(C)` and `f⁻¹ : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(D)`
together with an adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*` (that is, `Mor(f⁻¹ G, F) = Mor(G, f_* F)` bifunctorially)
such that `f⁻¹` commutes with finite limits. Here `Sh(C)` is the category of sheaves of sets
`Sheaf J (Type w)`; the fields are `pushforward` (`f_*`), `inverseImage` (`f⁻¹`), `adj` and
`preservesFiniteLimits` of `MorphismOfTopoi`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SheafToposMorphism {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
declarations.comment: (1); the composition (2) is `SheafToposMorphism.comp`

declarations.name: SheafToposMorphism.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XA (2).** Given morphisms of topoi `f : Sh(D) → Sh(C)` and `g : Sh(E) → Sh(D)`,
the composition `f ∘ g : Sh(E) → Sh(C)` is the morphism of topoi given by the functors
`(f ∘ g)_* = f_* ∘ g_*` and `(f ∘ g)⁻¹ = g⁻¹ ∘ f⁻¹` (see `pushforward_comp` and
`inverseImage_comp`).
declarations.statement:
abbrev comp (f : SheafToposMorphism.{w} J K) (g : SheafToposMorphism.{w} K L) :
    SheafToposMorphism.{w} J L

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites.morphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
Given a morphism of sites `f : D → C`, i.e. a continuous functor `u : C ⥤ D` whose associated
functor `u_s` on sheaves of sets is exact, the pair `(f⁻¹ = u_s, f_* = u^s)` is a morphism of topoi
`Sh(D) → Sh(C)`. Here `u_s` is `Functor.sheafPullback`, `u^s` is
`Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous` and the adjunction is `Functor.sheafAdjunctionContinuous`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites.morphismOfTopoi
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type w} [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {u : C ⥤ D}
    (h : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf K (Type w)) (Sheaf J (Type w))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.objEquiv
declarations.doc:
The objects of the category `{}_T I = CostructuredArrow S T` are the pairs `(U, ψ)` of an
object `U` of `C` and a morphism `ψ : S U ⟶ T`.
declarations.statement: def objEquiv : CostructuredArrow S T ≃ Σ U : C, (S.obj U ⟶ T)
declarations.comment: the objects of the category `{}_V I` are the pairs `(U, ψ : u U ⟶ V)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
The morphisms `(U, ψ) ⟶ (U', ψ')` of `{}_T I = CostructuredArrow S T` are the morphisms
`α : U ⟶ U'` of `C` with `ψ = ψ' ∘ S α`.
declarations.statement:
def homEquiv (X Y : CostructuredArrow S T) :
    (X ⟶ Y) ≃ { α : X.left ⟶ Y.left // S.map α ≫ Y.hom = X.hom }
declarations.comment:
a morphism `(U, ψ) ⟶ (U', ψ')` of `{}_V I` is a morphism `α : U ⟶ U'` with
`ψ = ψ' ∘ u(α)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.lanRanAdjunctionTriple
declarations.doc:
The restriction functor `u^p : PSh(D) ⥤ PSh(C)` has a left adjoint `u_p`, the left Kan
extension along `u.op`, and a right adjoint `{}_pu`, the right Kan extension along `u.op`: the
functors `u_p, u^p, {}_pu` form an adjoint triple.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lanRanAdjunctionTriple [HasLimitsOfSize.{v₁, max u₁ v₂} A]
    [HasColimitsOfSize.{v₁, max u₁ v₂} A] :
    Adjunction.Triple u.op.lan ((whiskeringLeft Cᵒᵖ Dᵒᵖ A).obj u.op) u.op.ran
declarations.comment:
`u^p` has the left adjoint `u_p` and also a right adjoint `{}_pu`; in the sequence
`u_p, u^p, {}_pu` each consecutive pair is an adjoint pair

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranObjIsoLimitCostructuredArrow
declarations.doc:
The value `{}_pu F (V)` of the right Kan extension of a presheaf `F` along `u.op` is the limit
over `{}_V Iᵒᵖ = (CostructuredArrow u V)ᵒᵖ` of the functor `{}_V F : (U, ψ) ↦ F(U)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ranObjIsoLimitCostructuredArrow (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (V : D) :
    (u.op.ran.obj F).obj (op V) ≅ limit ((CostructuredArrow.proj u V).op ⋙ F)
declarations.comment: `{}_pu F (V)` is the limit over `{}_V Iᵒᵖ` of `{}_V F : (U, ψ) ↦ F(U)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranObjIsoLimitCostructuredArrow_hom_π
declarations.doc:
The projection map `c(ψ) : {}_pu F (V) ⟶ F(U)` of the limit at an object `(U, ψ)` of `{}_V I`
is the restriction along `ψ` followed by the canonical map `{}_pu F (u U) ⟶ F(U)` of Stacks 00XG,
the counit of `u^p ⊣ {}_pu`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ranObjIsoLimitCostructuredArrow_hom_π (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (V : D)
    (X : CostructuredArrow u V) :
    (u.ranObjIsoLimitCostructuredArrow F V).hom ≫ limit.π _ (op X) =
      (u.op.ran.obj F).map X.hom.op ≫ (u.op.ranCounit.app F).app (op X.left)
declarations.comment:
the projection maps `c(ψ) : {}_pu F (V) ⟶ F(U)` of the
limit

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies
declarations.doc:
For a presheaf of sets `F` on `C`, the set `{}_pu F (V)` is the set of collections
`s_{(U, ψ)} ∈ F(U)`, indexed by the objects `(U, ψ)` of `{}_V I`, such that
`β^* s_{(U₂, ψ₂)} = s_{(U₁, ψ₁)}` for every morphism `β : (U₁, ψ₁) ⟶ (U₂, ψ₂)` of `{}_V I`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies :
    (u.op.ran.obj F).obj (op V) ≃
      { s : ∀ X : CostructuredArrow u V, F.obj (op X.left) //
        ∀ ⦃X Y : CostructuredArrow u V⦄ (β : X ⟶ Y), F.map β.left.op (s Y) = s X }
declarations.comment:
`{}_pu F (V)` is the set of collections `s_{(U, ψ)} ∈ F(U)` with
`β^* s_{(U₂, ψ₂)} = s_{(U₁, ψ₁)}` for all `β : (U₁, ψ₁) ⟶ (U₂, ψ₂)` in `{}_V I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies_apply
declarations.doc:
The correspondence `ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies` is `s ↦ s_{(U, ψ)} = c(ψ)(s)`, where
`c(ψ)` is the projection map of the limit.
declarations.statement:
lemma ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies_apply (s : (u.op.ran.obj F).obj (op V))
    (X : CostructuredArrow u V) :
    (u.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies F V s).1 X =
      limit.π ((CostructuredArrow.proj u V).op ⋙ F) (op X)
        ((u.ranObjIsoLimitCostructuredArrow F V).hom s)
declarations.comment: the correspondence is given by `s ↦ s_{(U, ψ)} = c(ψ)(s)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies_map
declarations.doc:
The restriction mapping `{}_pu F (V) ⟶ {}_pu F (V')` along `g : V' ⟶ V` sends a collection
`s` to the collection `(U, ψ') ↦ s_{(U, g ∘ ψ')}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies_map {V' : D} (g : V' ⟶ V) (s : (u.op.ran.obj F).obj (op V))
    (X : CostructuredArrow u V') :
    (u.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies F V' ((u.op.ran.obj F).map g.op s)).1 X =
      (u.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies F V s).1 ((CostructuredArrow.map g).obj X)
declarations.comment: the restriction mappings `{}_pu F (V) ⟶ {}_pu F (V')` along `V' ⟶ V`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies_ran_map
declarations.doc:
A map of presheaves `φ : F ⟶ F'` induces the map `{}_pu F ⟶ {}_pu F'` acting componentwise:
`s_{(U, ψ)} ↦ φ_U(s_{(U, ψ)})`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies_ran_map {F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (φ : F ⟶ F')
    (s : (u.op.ran.obj F).obj (op V)) (X : CostructuredArrow u V) :
    (u.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies F' V ((u.op.ran.map φ).app (op V) s)).1 X =
      φ.app (op X.left) ((u.ranObjEquivCompatibleFamilies F V s).1 X)
declarations.comment: a map of presheaves `F ⟶ F'` gives the map `{}_pu F ⟶ {}_pu F'` componentwise

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringLeft_obj_obj
registrations.comment: `u^p : PSh(D) ⥤ PSh(C)` sends `G` to `G ∘ u`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranCounit
registrations.comment: the canonical map `{}_p u F (u U) ⟶ F(U)` is the counit of `u^p ⊣ {}_p u`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.NatTrans.naturality
registrations.comment: compatibility with the restriction maps is naturality of that counit

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringLeft
registrations.comment: the restriction functor `u^p : PSh(D) ⥤ PSh(C)` is precomposition with `u.op`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ran
registrations.comment: the functor `{}_pu : PSh(C) ⥤ PSh(D)` is right Kan extension along `u.op`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranAdjunction
registrations.comment: `{}_pu` is right adjoint to `u^p`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCocontinuous
registrations.comment:
a functor between sites is cocontinuous when every covering of `u U` in `D` is
  refined by the image of a covering of `U` in `C`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionPullbackCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XL**, the adjunction. For a cocontinuous functor `u : C ⥤ D` between
sites, the functor `Sh(D) ⥤ Sh(C)`, `G ↦ (u^p G)^#`, is left adjoint to the pushforward
`{}_s u = u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous`.

This is Stacks' chain of bijections: restriction along `u.op` is left adjoint to the
right Kan extension `u.op.ran`, whose restriction to sheaves is
`u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous`, and sheafification is left adjoint to the inclusion of
sheaves into presheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafAdjunctionPullbackCocontinuous :
    u.sheafPullbackCocontinuous A J K ⊣ u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_sheafPullbackCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XL**, right exactness. `G ↦ (u^p G)^#` is a left adjoint, hence preserves
all colimits; in particular it is right exact.
declarations.statement:
instance preservesFiniteColimits_sheafPullbackCocontinuous :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (u.sheafPullbackCocontinuous A J K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_sheafPullbackCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XL**, left exactness. `G ↦ (u^p G)^#` is the composite of three left exact
functors: the inclusion `Sh(D) ⥤ PSh(D)` (which creates limits), restriction along `u.op`
(limits of presheaves are computed pointwise), and sheafification, which is left exact by
Stacks 00WJ — here the `HasSheafify J A` hypothesis, whose `isLeftExact` field is exactly
that statement.
declarations.statement:
instance preservesFiniteLimits_sheafPullbackCocontinuous
    [HasFiniteLimits A] [HasSheafify J A] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (u.sheafPullbackCocontinuous A J K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.morphismOfTopoi_of_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XL at the universe of a small model.**  A functor between two sites essentially
small at `u` which is both cocontinuous and continuous induces a morphism of topoi on sheaves of
sets in `Type u`, in the same direction as the functor.

Its direct image is the right Kan extension along `v.op`, and its inverse image is *restriction*
along `v`, which Stacks 00XR (1) identifies with the sheafified pullback and which Stacks
00XR (3) shows to be left exact.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def morphismOfTopoi_of_isCocontinuous (v : C ⥤ D)
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) [v.IsCocontinuous J K]
    [v.IsContinuous J K] :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf J (Type u)) (Sheaf K (Type u))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi of a cocontinuous functor, at the universe of a small model

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafifyRestrictionIsoOfIsCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XM.** For a cocontinuous functor `u : C ⥤ D` between sites and any presheaf `G`
on `D`, `(u^p G)^# = (u^p (G^#))^#`: the sheafification of the restricted unit
`whiskerLeft u.op (toSheafify K G) : u^p G ⟶ u^p (G^#)` is an isomorphism of sheaves on `C`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafifyRestrictionIsoOfIsCocontinuous (G : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    (presheafToSheaf J A).obj (u.op ⋙ G) ≅
      (presheafToSheaf J A).obj
        (u.op ⋙ (sheafToPresheaf K A).obj ((presheafToSheaf K A).obj G))

declarations.name: main_adjunction00XO
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XO.** For a cocontinuous functor `u`, the functor `g^{-1}` is left adjoint
to `g_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_adjunction00XO :
    Nonempty (gInv C D J K u ⊣ gStar C D J K u)

declarations.name: main_left_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XO.** The functor `g^{-1}` is left exact; together with the adjunction this makes
`(g_*, g^{-1})` a morphism of topoi `Sh(C) ⟶ Sh(D)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_left_exact :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (gInv C D J K u)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
The morphism of topoi attached to a functor of sites that is both continuous and
cocontinuous (Stacks 00XO): its inverse image is restriction along `F.op` and its direct image is
the right Kan extension along `F.op`.

Each field is a single application, so that projecting out of it stays cheap: an inline proof of
left exactness here makes every later unification that has to see through this definition
expensive. Left exactness is the instance
`CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous` (Stacks 04J4).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous {A : Type ua}
    [Category.{va} A] {B : Type ub} [Category.{vb} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) (JA : GrothendieckTopology A) (JB : GrothendieckTopology B)
    [F.IsContinuous JA JB] [F.IsCocontinuous JA JB]
    [∀ (G : Aᵒᵖ ⥤ Type ww), F.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf JA (Type ww)) (Sheaf JB (Type ww))
declarations.comment:
for a functor that is also continuous, with inverse image the restriction
  along F.op

declarations.name: StacksOpenMapSite.isCocontinuous_isOpenMapFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XQ.** For an open continuous map `f : X ⟶ Y` the functor
`v : X_Zar ⥤ Y_Zar`, `U ↦ f(U)`, is cocontinuous: if `f(U) = ⋃ V j` is an open covering then
`U = ⋃ (f⁻¹(V j) ∩ U)` is an open covering refining it.

Formally, `v` is a left adjoint of the continuous functor `u = Opens.map f`
(`IsOpenMap.adjunction`), and a left adjoint is cocontinuous exactly when its right adjoint
preserves covering sieves (`Adjunction.isCocontinuous_iff_coverPreserving`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCocontinuous_isOpenMapFunctor :
    (IsOpenMap.functor hf).IsCocontinuous (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)

declarations.name: StacksOpenMapSite.sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoTopPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XQ.** The pullback `(v^p)^#` of the morphism of topoi attached to the cocontinuous
functor `v = IsOpenMap.functor` is the usual topological pullback `f⁻¹` on sheaves of sets.

By Stacks 00XX (2) the presheaf restriction along `v` is the left Kan extension along
`u = Opens.map f`, so sheafifying identifies `(v^p)^#` with the construction of `f⁻¹` as
`(u_p)^#`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoTopPullback :
    (IsOpenMap.functor hf).sheafPullbackCocontinuous (Type u) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) ≅
      TopCat.Sheaf.pullback (Type u) f

declarations.name: StacksOpenMapSite.sheafPushforwardCocontinuousIsoTopPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XQ.** The pushforward `{}_sv` of the morphism of topoi attached to the cocontinuous
functor `v = IsOpenMap.functor` is the usual topological pushforward `f_*` on sheaves of sets.

Both are right adjoint to `f⁻¹`: for `{}_sv` this is Stacks 00XL
(`CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionPullbackCocontinuous`) transported along
`sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoTopPullback`, and for `f_*` it is
`TopCat.Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardCocontinuousIsoTopPushforward :
    haveI := isCocontinuous_isOpenMapFunctor hf
    (IsOpenMap.functor hf).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) ≅
      TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoSheafPushforwardContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XR (1).** If `u` is both cocontinuous and continuous then the
sheafification in `g^{-1} = (u^p\ )^#` is unnecessary: the sheaf pullback is naturally
isomorphic to plain restriction along `u.op`, so `g^{-1}(G)(U) = G(u(U))`.

Both functors are left adjoint to `u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous` — the first by
`sheafAdjunctionPullbackCocontinuous` (Stacks 00XL), the second by Mathlib's
`sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous` — so they agree by uniqueness of left adjoints.

See `sheafPullbackCocontinuousObjObjIso` for the displayed formula itself. Mathlib's
`CoverLifting.lean` records this comparison as a `TODO`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoSheafPushforwardContinuous :
    u.sheafPullbackCocontinuous A J K ≅ u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackCocontinuousObjObjIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XR (1)**, the displayed formula `g^{-1}(G)(U) = G(u(U))`.

Composing `sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoSheafPushforwardContinuous` — which removes the
sheafification — with the fact that `u.sheafPushforwardContinuous` is restriction along
`u.op`, so that its sections over `U` are literally `G(u(U))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackCocontinuousObjObjIso (G : Sheaf K A) (U : C) :
    ((u.sheafPullbackCocontinuous A J K).obj G).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) ≅
      G.obj.obj (Opposite.op (u.obj U))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesColimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XR (3)**, colimits. `g^{-1}` commutes with arbitrary colimits: by
Mathlib's `sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous` it is a left adjoint, its right adjoint being
`{}_s u = u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous`.
declarations.statement:
instance preservesColimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous :
    PreservesColimits (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XR (2).** `g^{-1}` has a left adjoint `g_! = (u_p\ )^#`.

The left adjoint is Mathlib's `sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback`, which is
literally `(u_p\ )^#`: the left Kan extension `u.op.lan = u_p` followed by
sheafification.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafAdjunctionLowerShriek :
    sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback u A J K ⊣ u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesLimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XR (3)**, limits. `g^{-1}` commutes with arbitrary limits: it is a right
adjoint, its left adjoint being `g_! = (u_p\ )^#`.
declarations.statement:
instance preservesLimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous :
    PreservesLimits (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XR (3) at the universe of a small model.**  Restriction of sheaves of sets in
`Type u` along a continuous functor between sites essentially small at `u` is left exact: it is
the right adjoint of the lower shriek functor.
declarations.comment: (3) at the universe of a small model

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesLimitsOfShape_sheafPullback
declarations.doc:
Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor of sites such that `C` has fibre products and
equalizers and `u` preserves them. Then `g_! = u.sheafPullback` preserves limits of every finite
connected shape, in particular fibre products and equalizers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesLimitsOfShape_sheafPullback
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
    (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K] [HasPullbacks C] [HasEqualizers C]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u] [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair u]
    [HasSheafify K (Type w)] [∀ Y : Dᵒᵖ, Small.{w} (CostructuredArrow u.op Y)]
    (I : Type t) [SmallCategory I] [FinCategory I] [IsConnected I] :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape I (u.sheafPullback (Type w) J K)
declarations.comment:
If `u` is continuous and `C` has fibre products and equalizers which `u` preserves,
  then `g_!` commutes with fibre products and equalizers, and more generally with finite connected
  limits.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous_counit
declarations.doc:
If `u : C ⥤ D` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful, the counit
`g^{-1}g_*F ⟶ F` of `g^{-1} ⊣ g_*` is an isomorphism; equivalently `g_*` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public instance isIso_sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous_counit
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (A : Type w) [Category.{w'} A]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [u.IsContinuous J K] [u.Full] [u.Faithful]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    IsIso (u.sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous A J K).counit
declarations.comment:
If `u` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful, the canonical map
  `g^{-1}g_*F → F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf `F` on `C`. Existence of `g_!` is not needed
  for this half.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_unit_of_sheafPushforwardContinuous
declarations.doc:
If `u : C ⥤ D` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful, then for every left adjoint `L`
of `g^{-1} = u^s` the unit `F ⟶ g^{-1}LF` of `L ⊣ g^{-1}` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_unit_of_sheafPushforwardContinuous
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (A : Type w) [Category.{w'} A]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [u.IsContinuous J K] [u.Full] [u.Faithful]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    {L : Sheaf J A ⥤ Sheaf K A} (adj : L ⊣ u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K) :
    IsIso adj.unit
declarations.comment:
If `u` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful, the canonical map
  `F → g^{-1}g_!F` is an isomorphism, for every left adjoint `g_!` of `g^{-1}`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_sheafAdjunctionContinuous_unit
declarations.doc:
If `u : C ⥤ D` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful and `g^{-1}` has a left adjoint
`g_!`, the unit `F ⟶ g^{-1}g_!F` of `g_! ⊣ g^{-1}` is an isomorphism; equivalently `g_!` is fully
faithful.
declarations.statement:
public instance isIso_sheafAdjunctionContinuous_unit
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (A : Type w) [Category.{w'} A]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [u.IsContinuous J K] [u.Full] [u.Faithful]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    [(u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K).IsRightAdjoint] :
    IsIso (u.sheafAdjunctionContinuous A J K).unit
declarations.comment:
If `u` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful, the canonical map
  `F → g^{-1}g_!F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf `F` on `C`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isMorphismOfSites_comp_iso_id_of_isTerminal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XU.** Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites and let `u : C ⥤ D` be a functor such that
(a) `u` is cocontinuous, (b) `u` is continuous, (c) `u` is fully faithful, (d) fibre products
exist in `C` and `u` commutes with them, and (e) there are final objects `e` of `C` and `u(e)` of
`D`. Let `g : Sh(C) → Sh(D)` be the morphism of topoi of the cocontinuous functor `u`
(`morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous`), with `g^{-1} = u^s` and `g_! = (u^s).leftAdjoint` the left
adjoint of `g^{-1}`.

Then `u` defines a morphism of sites `f : D → C` with `f_* = g^{-1}` and `f^{-1} = g_!`, the
latter both as an equality with the chosen left adjoint `(u^s).leftAdjoint` and as an adjunction
`f^{-1} ⊣ g^{-1}`; the
composition `f ∘ g : Sh(C) → Sh(D) → Sh(C)` is isomorphic to the identity morphism of `Sh(C)`,
both on pushforwards (an invertible 2-morphism of topoi) and on inverse images; and `f^{-1}` is
fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isMorphismOfSites_comp_iso_id_of_isTerminal
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [u.IsContinuous J K] [u.Full] [u.Faithful]
    [HasPullbacks C] [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u]
    {e : C} (he : IsTerminal e) (hue : IsTerminal (u.obj e)) :
    ∃ h : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K,
      h.morphismOfTopoi.pushforward = (u.morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous J K).inverseImage ∧
      h.morphismOfTopoi.inverseImage = (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) J K).leftAdjoint ∧
      Nonempty (h.morphismOfTopoi.inverseImage ⊣
        (u.morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous J K).inverseImage) ∧
      Nonempty ((h.morphismOfTopoi.comp (u.morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous J K)).pushforward ≅
        (MorphismOfTopoi.id (Sheaf J (Type u))).pushforward) ∧
      Nonempty ((h.morphismOfTopoi.comp (u.morphismOfTopoiOfCocontinuous J K)).inverseImage ≅
        (MorphismOfTopoi.id (Sheaf J (Type u))).inverseImage) ∧
      h.morphismOfTopoi.inverseImage.Full ∧ h.morphismOfTopoi.inverseImage.Faithful
declarations.comment:
`f ∘ g ≅ id` is an invertible 2-morphism of topoi, an isomorphism of pushforwards
  `(f ∘ g)_* ≅ id`; the isomorphism `(f ∘ g)^{-1} ≅ id` of inverse images is also stated. Here
  `g^{-1}` is restriction along `u` (Stacks 00XR (1)) and `g_!` is the left adjoint of `g^{-1}`.

declarations.name: real_punctured_uOpens_not_cocontinuous
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 00XV (Example 7.21.9): for `X = ℝ` and `Z = ℝ \ {0}` (with the subspace
topology), the functor `u : X_Zar → Z_Zar`, `U ↦ Z ∩ U`, is NOT cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem real_punctured_uOpens_not_cocontinuous :
    ¬ CocontinuousZar (X := ℝ) {x : ℝ | x ≠ 0}

declarations.name: uOpens_cocontinuous_inter_nonempty_and_not_sufficient
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 00XV (Example 7.21.9), both claims. For a topological space `X` and a subset
`Z ⊆ X` with the induced topology, if the functor `u : X_Zar → Z_Zar`, `U ↦ Z ∩ U`, is
cocontinuous then every nonempty open `U` of `X` has nonempty intersection with `Z`. This
condition is not sufficient: for `X = ℝ` and `Z = ℝ \ {0}` every nonempty open of `ℝ` meets `Z`,
yet `u` is not cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem uOpens_cocontinuous_inter_nonempty_and_not_sufficient :
    (∀ (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (Z : Set X), CocontinuousZar Z →
        ∀ U : Opens X, (U : Set X).Nonempty → (Z ∩ U).Nonempty) ∧
      (∀ U : Opens ℝ, (U : Set ℝ).Nonempty → ({x : ℝ | x ≠ 0} ∩ U).Nonempty) ∧
      ¬ CocontinuousZar (X := ℝ) {x : ℝ | x ≠ 0}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuousIsoRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XX (1).** Let `u : C ⥤ D` be cocontinuous with right adjoint `v : D ⥤ C`,
and let `g : Sh(C) → Sh(D)` be the associated morphism of topoi. Then for a sheaf `F` on
`C` the sheaf `g_*F` is the presheaf `v^p F`, in other words `(g_*F)(V) = F(v(V))`.

Underlying presheaves are compared because `g_* = {}_s u` lands in sheaves on `D` while
`v^p F = F ∘ v` is a priori only a presheaf; the isomorphism says the latter is the
former, hence a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardCocontinuousIsoRestriction
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A J K ⋙ sheafToPresheaf K A ≅
      sheafToPresheaf J A ⋙ (whiskeringLeft Dᵒᵖ Cᵒᵖ A).obj v.op

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoLan
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XX (2).** In the situation of `sheafPushforwardCocontinuousIsoRestriction`,
for a sheaf `G` on `D` we have `g^{-1}G = (v_p G)^#`: the sheaf pullback
`G ↦ (u^p G)^#` agrees with the sheafified left Kan extension along `v.op`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoLan
    [HasWeakSheafify J A] [∀ F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ A, v.op.HasLeftKanExtension F] :
    u.sheafPullbackCocontinuous A J K ≅
      sheafToPresheaf K A ⋙ v.op.lan ⋙ presheafToSheaf J A

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VR, final assertion.** A continuous functor `v : D ⥤ C` which admits a left adjoint
defines a morphism of sites `f : C → D`, i.e. `v` is continuous and the induced pullback
`v_s = f⁻¹` on sheaves of sets is exact.

Indeed a right adjoint is representably flat (`RepresentablyFlat.of_isRightAdjoint`: the comma
category `StructuredArrow X v` has an initial object, namely the unit of the adjunction), so this
is the criterion of Stacks 00X5 recorded as
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_representablyFlat`.

This is also the first assertion of Stacks 00XY, where the left adjoint `u` is assumed
cocontinuous: that hypothesis is not needed for it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint (adj : u ⊣ v) [v.IsContinuous K J] :
    v.IsMorphismOfSites K J
declarations.comment: v defines a morphism of sites (cocontinuity of u is not needed)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.morphismOfTopoiPushforwardIsoOfIsCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XY**, `f_* = g_*`. Let `u : C ⥤ D` be cocontinuous with continuous right adjoint
`v : D ⥤ C`. Then `v` defines a morphism of sites `f : C → D`
(`Adjunction.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint`), and the pushforward `f_* = v^s` of its
morphism of topoi (Stacks 00XC) is identified with the pushforward `g_* = {}_su` of the morphism
of topoi `g` of the cocontinuous functor `u` (Stacks 00XO), by the canonical isomorphism
`(g_*F)(V) = F(v(V))` of Stacks 00XX (1).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morphismOfTopoiPushforwardIsoOfIsCocontinuous :
    (adj.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint (J := J) (K := K)).morphismOfTopoi.pushforward ≅
      (u.sheafMorphismOfTopoiCocontinuous J K).pushforward
declarations.comment:
f_* = g_*, where f is the morphism of topoi of the morphism of sites defined by
  v (constructed by Adjunction.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint) and g that of the
  cocontinuous u; together with morphismOfTopoiInverseImageIsoOfIsCocontinuous and
  morphismOfTopoi_adj_compatible_of_isCocontinuous this is the equality f = g

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.morphismOfTopoiInverseImageIsoOfIsCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XY**, `f^{-1} = g^{-1}`. In the situation of
`morphismOfTopoiPushforwardIsoOfIsCocontinuous`, the inverse image `g^{-1} = (u^p-)^#` of the
morphism of topoi of `u` is identified with the inverse image `f^{-1} = v_s = (v_p-)^#` of the
morphism of topoi of the morphism of sites defined by `v`, by the isomorphism conjugate to the
identification `f_* ≅ g_*` of pushforwards under the adjunctions `f^{-1} ⊣ f_*` and
`g^{-1} ⊣ g_*`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morphismOfTopoiInverseImageIsoOfIsCocontinuous :
    (u.sheafMorphismOfTopoiCocontinuous J K).inverseImage ≅
      (adj.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint (J := J) (K := K)).morphismOfTopoi.inverseImage
declarations.comment: f^{-1} = v_s = g^{-1}, the conjugate of the identification f_* = g_*

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.morphismOfTopoi_adj_compatible_of_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00XY**, `f = g` as morphisms of topoi. Let `u : C ⥤ D` be cocontinuous with
continuous right adjoint `v : D ⥤ C`, let `f` be the morphism of topoi of the morphism of sites
defined by `v` and `g` that of the cocontinuous functor `u`. The identifications `f_* ≅ g_*`
(`morphismOfTopoiPushforwardIsoOfIsCocontinuous`) and `g^{-1} ≅ f^{-1}`
(`morphismOfTopoiInverseImageIsoOfIsCocontinuous`) identify the adjunctions as well: for sheaves
`𝒢` on `D` and `ℱ` on `C`, the bijection `Mor(𝒢, f_*ℱ) = Mor(f^{-1}𝒢, ℱ)` of `f` corresponds to
the bijection `Mor(𝒢, g_*ℱ) = Mor(g^{-1}𝒢, ℱ)` of `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem morphismOfTopoi_adj_compatible_of_isCocontinuous (𝒢 : Sheaf K (Type u))
    (ℱ : Sheaf J (Type u))
    (α : 𝒢 ⟶
      (adj.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint (J := J) (K := K)).morphismOfTopoi.pushforward.obj
        ℱ) :
    ((u.sheafMorphismOfTopoiCocontinuous J K).adj.homEquiv 𝒢 ℱ).symm
        (α ≫ (adj.morphismOfTopoiPushforwardIsoOfIsCocontinuous (J := J)).hom.app ℱ) =
      (adj.morphismOfTopoiInverseImageIsoOfIsCocontinuous (J := J)).hom.app 𝒢 ≫
        ((adj.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint (J := J) (K := K)).morphismOfTopoi.adj.homEquiv
          𝒢 ℱ).symm α
declarations.comment:
f = g: the identifications of pushforwards and inverse images are compatible
  with the adjunctions of f and g

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.isEquivalence_sheafFunctorToOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y1.** The functor `Φ_sh : Sh(C/U) ⥤ Sh(C)/h_U^#` induced by `j_{U!}` is full,
faithful and essentially surjective, i.e. an equivalence.
declarations.statement: instance isEquivalence_sheafFunctorToOver : (sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the functor j_{U!} : Sh(C/U) ⥤ Sh(C)/h_U^# is an equivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y1**, as an equivalence of categories `Sh(C/U) ≌ Sh(C)/h_U^#`. Its functor is
`sheafFunctorToOver`, the sheaf level `j_{U!}` viewed as a functor into the slice
(`sheafEquivalence_functor`), and its inverse is isomorphic to the fibre functor
`(F, φ) ↦ F_φ`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafEquivalence :
    Sheaf (J.over U) (Type v) ≌ Over ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).obj (yoneda.obj U))
declarations.comment: the resulting equivalence of categories Sh(C/U) ≌ Sh(C)/h_U^#

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafFunctorToOverForgetIsoOfAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y1, in the form the source restates it in**: `j_{U!}` *is* the equivalence
`Φ : Sh(C/U) ≌ Sh(C)/h_U^#` followed by `Over.forget : Sh(C)/h_U^# ⥤ Sh(C)`.

Here `j_{U!}` is an arbitrary left adjoint `L` of the restriction functor `j_U^{-1}`, so this is a
statement about `j_{U!}` rather than about one model of it: `sheafFunctorToOverForgetIso` identifies
`Φ ⋙ Over.forget` with the left adjoint obtained from `Over.forget U`, and two left adjoints of one
functor are canonically isomorphic.

The adjunction `adj` is also what makes that left adjoint exist (`J.overPullback` being the
pushforward along `Over.forget U`), so no adjointness hypothesis beyond `adj` is assumed.
declarations.statement:
def sheafFunctorToOverForgetIsoOfAdjunction
    {L : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type v) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type v)} (adj : L ⊣ J.overPullback (Type v) U) :
    sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ⋙ Over.forget _ ≅ L
declarations.comment: j_{U!} is Sh(C/U) ≌ Sh(C)/h_U^# followed by Over.forget, for any left adjoint

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isIso_unit_and_sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous_counit_of_isSubterminal
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a site, and let `U` be an object of `C` such that every object of `C` has at most
one morphism to `U`, i.e. `U` is subterminal. Let `L` be a left adjoint of
`j_U^{-1} = J.overPullback A U : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(C/U)`, i.e. let `L` be `j_{U!}`, and let
`j_{U*} = {}_pj_U` be the pushforward along the cocontinuous localization functor. Then the
canonical maps `F ⟶ j_U^{-1}j_{U!}F` and `j_U^{-1}j_{U*}F ⟶ F` are isomorphisms for every sheaf
`F` on `C/U`: they are the unit of `j_{U!} ⊣ j_U^{-1}` and the counit of `j_U^{-1} ⊣ j_{U*}`.
Equivalently, `j_{U!}` and `j_{U*}` are fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_unit_and_sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous_counit_of_isSubterminal {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (U : C) (hU : IsSubterminal U) (A : Type w)
    [Category.{w'} A] [∀ (F : (Over U)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A), (Over.forget U).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    {L : Sheaf (J.over U) A ⥤ Sheaf J A} (adj : L ⊣ J.overPullback A U) :
    IsIso adj.unit ∧
      IsIso ((Over.forget U).sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous A (J.over U) J).counit
declarations.comment: if every object of `C` has at most one morphism to `U`, the canonical maps `F ⟶ j_U^{-1}j_{U!}F` and `j_U^{-1}j_{U*}F ⟶ F` are isomorphisms, for coefficients in an arbitrary category `A`

declarations.name: PointOfTopos
declarations.doc:
A *point of the topos* `Sh(C, J)` is a morphism of topoi `p : Sh(pt) → Sh(C, J)`, where
`Sh(pt) = Sets` is modelled by `Type w`. Concretely, a point is an adjoint pair `p⁻¹ ⊣ p_*` with
`p⁻¹ : Sh(C, J) ⥤ Type w` (the stalk functor) and `p_* : Type w ⥤ Sh(C, J)` (the skyscraper
functor), such that `p⁻¹` is left exact.
declarations.statement: def PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Type _

declarations.name: Stacks.IsSitePoint.toPoint
declarations.doc:
**A point in the sense of Stacks 00Y5 is a point in the sense of Mathlib**, with the same
fibre functor `u`. Its category of elements is cofiltered because the stalk functor is left
exact (condition (3)).
declarations.statement: def toPoint : K.toGrothendieck.Point.{w}
declarations.comment: a Stacks point gives a Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology.Point` with fibre `u`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsPointOfSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y5.** A *point* of the site `(C, J)` is a functor `u : C ⥤ Set` such that

1. for every covering `{U_i → U}` the map `∐ u(U_i) → u(U)` is surjective;
2. for every covering `{U_i → U}` and every morphism `V → U` the maps
   `u(U_i ×_U V) → u(U_i) ×_{u(U)} u(V)` are bijective;
3. the stalk functor `Sh(C) ⥤ Set`, `F ↦ F_p`, is left exact, where `F_p` is the colimit of the
   sections `F(U)` over the opposite of the category of neighbourhoods `(U, x)`, `x ∈ u(U)`
   (`PresheafPushforwardStalkAdjunction.presheafStalk`, Stacks 04EH).

A covering is a family `{U_i → U}` whose generated sieve is `J`-covering. That this is the same
notion as Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology.Point` is `Functor.isPointOfSite_iff_exists_point`.
declarations.statement: structure Functor.IsPointOfSite (u : C ⥤ Type w) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Prop
declarations.comment:
Stacks' definition, with conditions (1), (2) and (3) as fields; it is
  identified with Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology.Point` by
  `Functor.isPointOfSite_iff_exists_point` and `Functor.pointOfSiteEquiv`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Precoverage.Point
declarations.doc:
A *point* of the site `(C, K)` (Stacks 00Y5): a functor `u : C ⥤ Type u` such that

1. for every covering `R` of `X` the elements of `u(X)` all come from the members of `R`, i.e.
   `∐ u(U_i) → u(X)` is surjective;
2. for every covering `R` of `X`, every member `f : Y ⟶ X` of `R` and every `g : Z ⟶ X`, the map
   `u(Y ×_X Z) → u(Y) ×_{u(X)} u(Z)` is bijective;
3. the stalk functor `F ↦ F_p` on sheaves of sets is left exact, the stalk being the colimit
   `PresheafPushforwardStalkAdjunction.presheafStalk u` of the sections of `F` over the opposite
   of the category of elements of `u` (Stacks 04EH).
declarations.statement: structure Point
declarations.comment: The source's definition, for a site given by its covering families.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.SitePoint
declarations.statement: structure SitePoint

declarations.name: Phi_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y6.** The canonical map `Φ_U : p U ⟶ (h_U)_p` from the value of the point at `U`
to the stalk of the representable presheaf `h_U` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem Phi_bijective (p : C ⥤ Type u) (U : C) :
    Function.Bijective (theta p U)
declarations.comment: isomorphism

declarations.name: Phi_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y6.** The maps `Φ_U` are natural in `U`: they commute with `p.map g` on the source
and with the stalk of `yoneda.map g` on the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem Phi_naturality (p : C ⥤ Type u) {U U' : C} (g : U ⟶ U') (x : p.obj U) :
    theta p U' (p.map g x) = (presheafStalk p).map (yoneda.map g) (theta p U x)
declarations.comment: functoriality

declarations.name: PresheafPushforwardStalkAdjunction.presheafStalk_adjoint_presheafPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y7.** For any functor `u : C ⥤ Type w` such that the
appropriate colimits exist, the pushforward functor `presheafPushforward u`
is a right adjoint to the stalk functor `presheafStalk u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafStalk_adjoint_presheafPushforward
    (u : C ⥤ Type w)
    [HasColimitsOfShape u.Elementsᵒᵖ (Type w)] :
    Nonempty (presheafStalk u ⊣ presheafPushforward u)

declarations.name: PresheafPushforwardStalkAdjunction.isSheaf_presheafPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y8 (1).** If `u : C ⥤ Type w` satisfies conditions (a) and (b) for every covering
of the site, then the presheaf `u^p E : U ↦ Map(u(U), E)` is a sheaf for every set `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_presheafPushforward (h : StalkConditions K u) (E : Type w) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf K.toGrothendieck ((presheafPushforward u).obj E)
declarations.comment: (1): `u^p E` is a sheaf for every set `E`

declarations.name: PresheafPushforwardStalkAdjunction.sheafStalk_adjoint_skyscraper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y8 (2).** If `u : C ⥤ Type w` satisfies conditions (a) and (b) for every covering
of the site, then the stalk functor `Sh(C) → Sets`, `F ↦ F_p`, is left adjoint to
`u^s : Sets → Sh(C)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafStalk_adjoint_skyscraper [Limits.HasColimitsOfShape u.Elementsᵒᵖ (Type w)]
    (h : StalkConditions K u) : Nonempty (sheafStalk K u ⊣ skyscraper h)
declarations.comment: (2): the stalk functor on sheaves is left adjoint to `u^s`

declarations.name: PresheafPushforwardStalkAdjunction.isIso_presheafStalk_map_toSheafify
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y8 (3).** If `u : C ⥤ Type w` satisfies conditions (a) and (b) for every covering
of the site, then for every presheaf of sets `F` the canonical map `F_p → (F^#)_p`, the stalk of
the sheafification map `F → F^#`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_presheafStalk_map_toSheafify [Limits.HasColimitsOfShape u.Elementsᵒᵖ (Type w)]
    [HasWeakSheafify K.toGrothendieck (Type w)] (h : StalkConditions K u)
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) :
    IsIso ((presheafStalk u).map (toSheafify K.toGrothendieck F))
declarations.comment: (3): the canonical map `F_p → (F^#)_p` is an isomorphism

declarations.name: pushforwardPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00Y9.** The pushforward `p_* E` of an object `E` along a point `p` of the site
`(C, J)`: the skyscraper sheaf at `p` with value `E`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardPoint
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (p : J.Point) {A : Type*} [Category A] [Limits.HasProducts A] (E : A) :
    Sheaf J A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.targetSitePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YA (2) along a morphism of ringed topoi.** The point of the target site `(D, K)`
whose stalk functor is the inverse image along `f` followed by the stalk functor of the point
`Φ` of the source site.
declarations.statement: def targetSitePoint (f : RingedToposHom X Y) (Φ : X.J.Point.{w}) : Y.J.Point.{w}
declarations.comment:
(2), applied to the composite of a point of the source site with a morphism of
  ringed topoi

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.pointOfTopos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YA (1).** Let `p` be a point of the site `C`, given by a fibre functor
`u = Φ.fiber`. Then the pair of functors `(p_*, p^{-1}) = (Φ.skyscraperSheafFunctor,
Φ.sheafFiber)` is a morphism of topoi `Sh(pt) → Sh(C)`, i.e. a point of the topos `Sh(C)` in
the sense of Stacks 00Y4.

The two functors are adjoint by `Point.skyscraperSheafAdjunction`, and `p^{-1}` is left exact
by `Point.sheafFiber_leftExact` (Stacks 00Y5 (3)), which are exactly the two conditions in the
definition of a morphism of topoi (Stacks 00XA).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pointOfTopos (Φ : Point.{w} J) : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J
declarations.comment: (1): a point of the site defines a morphism of topoi `Sh(pt) → Sh(C)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiberComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison from the stalk functor to `F`, induced by a natural
transformation on the sheafified representables. On a germ `(U, x, σ)` it is
`F(σ)(α_U(x))`, viewing the section `σ` as a map out of `h_U^#`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sheafFiberComparison : Φ.sheafFiber ⟶ F
declarations.comment: (2): the canonical comparison from the reconstructed stalk functor

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.exists_sitePoint_fiber_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YA (2).** Every point `p` of the topos arises from a point of the site
whose fiber functor is `U ↦ p⁻¹(h_U^#)` on the nose.

`PointOfTopos.exists_sitePoint` is the same reconstruction stated up to isomorphism of stalk
functors; this form is the one consumers need when they have to transport along the identity of
fibre functors with `eqToIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sitePoint_fiber_eq {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (p : PointOfTopos.{max u v, v, u} J) :
    ∃ Φ : GrothendieckTopology.Point.{max u v} J,
      Φ.fiber = Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J ⋙ p.inverseImage
declarations.comment: (2): reconstruction of the site point

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.isIso_sheafFiberComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YA (2).** The canonical comparison identifies the reconstructed stalk
functor with `p.inverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafFiberComparison :
    IsIso (Φ.sheafFiberComparison p.inverseImage e.hom)
declarations.comment: (2): the canonical inverse-image comparison is an isomorphism

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.isIso_conjugate_sheafFiberComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YA (2).** The adjoint mate of the canonical comparison is an isomorphism
`p.pushforward ⟶ Φ.skyscraperSheafFunctor`, recovering the pushforward compatibly with
the given adjunctions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conjugate_sheafFiberComparison :
    IsIso (conjugateEquiv p.adj Φ.skyscraperSheafAdjunction
      (Φ.sheafFiberComparison p.inverseImage e.hom))
declarations.comment: (2): recovery of the pushforward by the adjoint mate

declarations.name: StacksStalk.nbh_isCofiltered
declarations.doc:
Statement 1 (Main, tag `00YB`): under the hypotheses, the category of
neighbourhoods `Nbh(p)` of `p` is cofiltered.
declarations.statement:
theorem nbh_isCofiltered [HasTerminal C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (u : C ⥤ Type w) (hu : IsPoint u) : IsCofiltered u.Elements

declarations.name: StacksStalk.sheafStalkFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
Statement 2 (Consequence, tag `00YB`): under the hypotheses, the stalk
functor on sheaves commutes with finite limits, i.e. it is left exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafStalkFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits
    [HasTerminal C] [HasPullbacks C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (u : C ⥤ Type w) (hu : IsPoint u) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      (sheafToPresheaf J (Type w) ⋙ CategoryTheory.elementColimit u (Type w))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.ofPreservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
On a site in which finite limits exist, the point with fiber functor `u : C ⥤ Type w`, for
`u` commuting with finite limits, with initially small category of elements, and jointly
surjective on covering sieves.

This is the direction "(1) and (2) imply a point" of Stacks 00YC for points in Mathlib's sense;
the equivalence for the points of Stacks 00Y5 is
`GrothendieckTopology.SitePoint.exists_fiber_eq_iff`.
declarations.statement:
def ofPreservesFiniteLimits (u : C ⥤ Type w) [PreservesFiniteLimits u]
    [InitiallySmall.{w} u.Elements] (hu : u.CoveringJointlySurjective J) :
    Point.{w} J
declarations.comment:
the direction (1) and (2) ⇒ point, for Mathlib's points; the equivalence for
  the points of 00Y5 is `SitePoint.exists_fiber_eq_iff`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.equivFiber
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a site in which finite limits exist. Then the points of `C`
correspond bijectively to the functors `u : C ⥤ Type w` such that

1. `u` commutes with finite limits, and
2. `∐ u(U_i) → u(U)` is surjective for every covering `{U_i → U}`
   (in the sieve form `Functor.CoveringJointlySurjective`), and whose category of elements is
   initially small,

the bijection being `Φ ↦ Φ.fiber` in one direction and `ofPreservesFiniteLimits` in the
other. This is Stacks 00YC for points in Mathlib's sense; for the points of Stacks 00Y5 see
`GrothendieckTopology.SitePoint.exists_fiber_eq_iff` and
`GrothendieckTopology.SitePoint.equivFiber`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivFiber :
    Point.{w} J ≃ {u : C ⥤ Type w //
      InitiallySmall.{w} u.Elements ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits u ∧
        u.CoveringJointlySurjective J}
declarations.comment: the bijection, for Mathlib's points (with initially small category of elements)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.SitePoint.exists_fiber_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YC.** Let `C` be a site in which finite limits exist. A functor
`u : C ⥤ Type w` is a point of `C` (Stacks 00Y5) if and only if

1. `u` commutes with finite limits, and
2. for every covering `{U_i → U}` the map `∐ u(U_i) → u(U)` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fiber_eq_iff (u : C ⥤ Type w) :
    (∃ p : J.SitePoint, p.fiber = u) ↔
      PreservesFiniteLimits u ∧
        ∀ {I : Type w} {U : C} {Ui : I → C} (f : ∀ i, Ui i ⟶ U),
          Sieve.ofArrows Ui f ∈ J U → ∀ x : u.obj U,
            ∃ (i : I) (y : u.obj (Ui i)), u.map (f i) y = x
declarations.comment: the equivalence, for the points of Stacks 00Y5

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.SitePoint.equivFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YC.** On a site in which finite limits exist, the points of Stacks 00Y5
correspond bijectively, by `p ↦ u`, to the functors `u : C ⥤ Type w` which commute with finite
limits and for which `∐ u(U_i) → u(U)` is surjective for every covering `{U_i → U}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivFiber :
    J.SitePoint ≃ {u : C ⥤ Type w // PreservesFiniteLimits u ∧
        ∀ {I : Type w} {U : C} {Ui : I → C} (f : ∀ i, Ui i ⟶ U),
          Sieve.ofArrows Ui f ∈ J U → ∀ x : u.obj U,
            ∃ (i : I) (y : u.obj (Ui i)), u.map (f i) y = x}
declarations.comment: the bijection between points and the functors satisfying (1) and (2)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.WeakPullbacksNotPoint.exists_site_weakly_left_exact_not_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YD.** There is a site `C` with a final object and fibre products, and a functor
`u : C ⥤ Set` such that

1. `u(⊤) = {*}` is a singleton,
2. for every pair `U → W ← V` the map `u(U ×_W V) → u(U) ×_{u(W)} u(V)` is surjective,
3. for every covering `{U_i → U}` the map `∐ u(U_i) → u(U)` is surjective,

but `u` is not a point: no point of `C` (Stacks 00Y5) has fiber functor `u`, and the stalk
functor `Sh(C) ⥤ Set`, `F ↦ F_p` (Stacks 04EH), is not left exact.

The example is the skeleton of the category of finite sets with the trivial topology and `u` the
nonempty-subsets functor; the example given in the source fails (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_site_weakly_left_exact_not_point :
    ∃ (C : Type) (_ : SmallCategory C) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (_ : HasTerminal C)
      (_ : HasPullbacks C) (u : C ⥤ Type),
      Nonempty (Unique (u.obj (⊤_ C))) ∧
      (∀ {U V W : C} (f : U ⟶ W) (g : V ⟶ W), Function.Surjective (pullbackComparison u f g)) ∧
      (∀ {I : Type} {U : C} {Ui : I → C} (f : ∀ i, Ui i ⟶ U), Sieve.ofArrows Ui f ∈ J U →
        ∀ x : u.obj U, ∃ (i : I) (y : u.obj (Ui i)), u.map (f i) y = x) ∧
      (¬ ∃ Φ : J.Point.{0}, Nonempty (Φ.fiber ≅ u)) ∧
      ¬ PreservesFiniteLimits (sheafToPresheaf J Type ⋙ presheafStalk u)
declarations.comment:
the remark's assertion. The source's example (two objects `U → X`, `u(U)` with two
  elements) fails (2) at `U ×_X U = U`; corrected example: finite sets with the trivial topology and
  `u` the nonempty-subsets functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.PointStalk.tStalk
declarations.doc:
Tag 00YH, Lemma 7.37.1: the canonical natural transformation of stalk
functors `t_stalk : (-)_{p'} ⟹ (-)_p` induced by `t : u' → u`.  Its components are
`tStalkApp`; naturality is `tStalk_naturality` (part 2).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tStalk (uu uu' : C ⥤ Type u) (t : uu' ⟶ uu) :
    presheafStalk uu' ⟶ presheafStalk uu

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.PointStalk.tStalkApp_stalkMk
declarations.doc:
Part 1 (Well-defined + defining formula). The stalk transformation acts on a
representative `[(U, x', s)]` by `[(U, x', s)] ↦ [(U, t_U(x'), s)]`; this is `ι_tStalkApp`
at `op ⟨U, x'⟩` applied to `s`, since `(map t).op.obj (op ⟨U, x'⟩)` is `op ⟨U, t.app U x'⟩`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tStalkApp_stalkMk (uu uu' : C ⥤ Type u) (t : uu' ⟶ uu) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (U : C) (x' : uu'.obj U) (s : F.obj (Opposite.op U)) :
    tStalkApp uu uu' t F (stalkMk uu' F U x' s) = stalkMk uu F U (t.app U x') s

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.PointStalk.tStalkApp_theta
declarations.doc:
Part 3 (Compatibility with `t`, the agreement of Tag 00Y6).  Under the
canonical identifications `θ^{u'}_U : u'(U) ≅ (h_U)_{p'}` and
`θ^u_U : u(U) ≅ (h_U)_p`, the map `(t_stalk)_{h_U} : (h_U)_{p'} → (h_U)_p`
corresponds to `t_U : u'(U) → u(U)`.  Since `θ` is `stalkMk … (𝟙 U)`, this is the case
`F := yoneda.obj U`, `s := 𝟙 U` of `tStalkApp_stalkMk`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tStalkApp_theta (uu uu' : C ⥤ Type u) (t : uu' ⟶ uu) (U : C) (x' : uu'.obj U) :
    tStalkApp uu uu' t (yoneda.obj U) (theta uu' U x') = theta uu U (t.app U x')

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.Hom
registrations.comment:
a morphism of points of a site is a transformation of the fibre functors in
  the opposite direction

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsConservativeFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YK (1).** A family of points `{p_i}_{i ∈ I}` of a site `(C, J)` is *conservative* if
every map of sheaves of sets `φ : F ⟶ G` which is an isomorphism on all the fibres
`F_{p_i} ⟶ G_{p_i}` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: def IsConservativeFamily {ι : Type t} (p : ι → Point.{w} J) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YK (2).** A site `(C, J)` *has enough points* if there exists a conservative family
of points. No smallness is required of the family; contrast
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints`, which asks for a `w`-small one.
declarations.statement: def HasConservativeFamily (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.nonempty_isLimit_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YL (4).** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `P` be a conservative family of points of
it. Let `G : K ⥤ Sh(C)` be a finite diagram of sheaves with values in `A`. Then a cone over `G` is
a limit if and only if its image under every stalk functor `F ↦ F_{p_i}`, `p_i ∈ P`, is a limit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_isLimit_iff {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {P : ObjectProperty (GrothendieckTopology.Point.{w} J)}
    (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints) {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] [LocallySmall.{w} C]
    [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} A] [HasFiniteLimits A] [AB5OfSize.{w, w} A]
    {FC : A → A → Type*} {CC : A → Type w}
    [∀ X Y : A, FunLike (FC X Y) (CC X) (CC Y)] [ConcreteCategory.{w} A FC]
    [(forget A).ReflectsIsomorphisms] [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} (forget A)]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget A)]
    {K : Type u''} [SmallCategory K] [FinCategory K] {G : K ⥤ Sheaf J A} (c : Cone G) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit c) ↔
      ∀ Φ : P.FullSubcategory, Nonempty (IsLimit ((Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := A)).mapCone c))
declarations.comment:
(4): a cone over a finite diagram of sheaves is a limit if and only if it is one in
  every stalk at a conservative family of points.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.injective_app_of_forall_injective_sheafFiber_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YL (1).** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `P` be a conservative family of points of
it. Let `φ : F ⟶ G` be a map of sheaves of sets. If every stalk map `φ_{p_i}`, `p_i ∈ P`, is
injective, then `φ` is injective, that is, injective on the sections over every object `U`
(Stacks 00WM (1)).
declarations.comment:
(1): a map of sheaves of sets which is injective on the stalks at a conservative
  family of points is injective.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.isLocallySurjective_of_forall_surjective_sheafFiber_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YL (2).** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `P` be a conservative family of points of
it. Let `φ : F ⟶ G` be a map of sheaves of sets. If every stalk map `φ_{p_i}`, `p_i ∈ P`, is
surjective, then `φ` is surjective, that is, every section of `G` is locally in the image of `φ`
(Stacks 00WM (2); `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective`).
declarations.comment:
(2): a map of sheaves of sets which is surjective on the stalks at a conservative
  family of points is surjective.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.eq_of_forall_sheafFiber_map_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YL (3).** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `P` be a conservative family of points of
it. Two maps of sheaves `φ₁ φ₂ : F ⟶ G` which agree on the stalks at every `p_i ∈ P` are
equal.
declarations.comment:
(3): two maps of sheaves which agree on the stalks at a conservative family of
  points are equal.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.nonempty_isColimit_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YL (5).** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `P` be a conservative family of points of
it. Let `G : K ⥤ Sh(C)` be a finite diagram of sheaves with values in `A`. Then a cocone under `G`
is a colimit if and only if its image under every stalk functor `F ↦ F_{p_i}`, `p_i ∈ P`, is a
colimit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_isColimit_iff {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {P : ObjectProperty (GrothendieckTopology.Point.{w} J)}
    (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints) {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] [LocallySmall.{w} C]
    [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} A] [HasWeakSheafify J A] [HasProducts.{w} A]
    {FC : A → A → Type*} {CC : A → Type w}
    [∀ X Y : A, FunLike (FC X Y) (CC X) (CC Y)] [ConcreteCategory.{w} A FC]
    [(forget A).ReflectsIsomorphisms] [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} (forget A)]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget A)]
    {K : Type u''} [SmallCategory K] [FinCategory K] {G : K ⥤ Sheaf J A} (c : Cocone G) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit c) ↔
      ∀ Φ : P.FullSubcategory, Nonempty (IsColimit ((Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := A)).mapCocone c))
declarations.comment:
(5): a cocone under a finite diagram of sheaves is a colimit if and only if it is
  one in every stalk at a conservative family of points.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isConservativeFamily_iff_exists_toPresheafFiber_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YM.** Let `(C, J)` be a site and `{p_i}_{i ∈ I}` a family of points. The family is
conservative if and only if for every sheaf of sets `F`, every object `U` of `C` and every pair of
distinct sections `s ≠ s'` of `F` over `U`, there are an index `i` and `x ∈ u_i(U)` such that the
triples `(U, x, s)` and `(U, x, s')` define distinct elements of the stalk `F_{p_i}`; that element
is the germ `(p i).toPresheafFiber U x F.obj s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConservativeFamily_iff_exists_toPresheafFiber_ne {ι : Type t}
    (p : ι → Point.{w} J) :
    IsConservativeFamily p ↔
      ∀ (F : Sheaf J (Type w)) (U : C) (s s' : F.obj.obj (op U)), s ≠ s' →
        ∃ (i : ι) (x : (p i).fiber.obj U),
          (p i).toPresheafFiber U x F.obj s ≠ (p i).toPresheafFiber U x F.obj s'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.exists_refinement_of_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YO.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, let `F` be a separated presheaf of sets on `C` and let
`p : N ⥤ C` be a cofiltered system in `C`, with associated fibre functor
`u'(X) = colim_j Mor(p j, X)` and stalk functor `F ↦ F_{p'} = colim_j F(p j)`. Let `s ≠ s'` be two
germs in `F_{p'}`, represented by `a, a' : F(p j₀)`, let `{g k : Y k ⟶ W}` be a finite covering of
the site and let `f : p j₀ ⟶ W` represent a section of `u'(W)`.

Then the system can be refined — there are a cofiltered system `q : M ⥤ C`, a fully faithful
`e : N ⥤ M` and an isomorphism `ε : e ⋙ q ≅ p` exhibiting `p` as the restriction of `q` — in such a
way that the two germs stay distinct in `F_p` and that the image of `f` in `u(W)` lies in the image
of `u(Y k)` for one of the members `g k : Y k ⟶ W` of the covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_refinement_of_ne {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (hF : Presieve.IsSeparated J F) {N : Type u₁} [SmallCategory N]
    [IsCofiltered N] (p : N ⥤ C) (j₀ : N) (a a' : F.obj (op (p.obj j₀)))
    (haa' : ∀ (j : N) (φ : j ⟶ j₀), F.map (p.map φ).op a ≠ F.map (p.map φ).op a') {W : C}
    {ι : Type t} [Finite ι] {Y : ι → C} (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ W) (hg : Sieve.ofArrows Y g ∈ J W)
    [∀ (X : C) (h : X ⟶ W) (k : ι), HasPullback h (g k)] (f : p.obj j₀ ⟶ W) :
    ∃ (M : Type u₁) (_ : SmallCategory M) (_ : IsCofiltered M) (q : M ⥤ C) (e : N ⥤ M) (_ : e.Full)
      (_ : e.Faithful) (ε : e ⋙ q ≅ p),
      (∀ (i : M) (ψ : i ⟶ e.obj j₀),
          F.map (q.map ψ ≫ ε.hom.app j₀).op a ≠ F.map (q.map ψ ≫ ε.hom.app j₀).op a') ∧
        ∃ (k : ι) (i : M) (ψ : i ⟶ e.obj j₀) (h : q.obj i ⟶ Y k),
          h ≫ g k = q.map ψ ≫ ε.hom.app j₀ ≫ f
declarations.comment:
The inductive step of Deligne's criterion: a cofiltered system can be refined so as
  to keep two germs of a separated presheaf distinct while a given section of `u'(W)` becomes
  covered by a given finite covering of `W`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.exists_refinement_forall_covering_of_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YP.** Let `(C, J)` be a site in which the members of a finite covering admit fibre
