products along arbitrary morphisms to its base (`hpb`), let `F` be a separated presheaf of sets on
`C` and let `p : N ⥤ C` be a cofiltered system in `C`, with associated fibre functor
`u'(X) = colim_j Mor(p j, X)` and stalk functor `F ↦ F_{p'} = colim_j F(p j)`. Let `s ≠ s'` be two
germs in `F_{p'}`, represented by `a, a' : F(p j₀)`.

Then the system can be refined — there are a cofiltered system `q : M ⥤ C`, a fully faithful
`e : N ⥤ M` and an isomorphism `ε : e ⋙ q ≅ p` exhibiting `p` as the restriction of `q` — in such a
way that the two germs stay distinct in `F_p` and that, for every finite covering `{g k : Y k ⟶ W}`
of the site and every section `f : p j ⟶ W` of `u'(W)`, the image of `f` in `u(W)` lies in the
image of `u(Y k)` for one of the members `g k` of the covering. Moreover the refined index category
is no larger than the data it is assembled from: if `C` is `w'`-small with `w'`-small hom types and
`N` is essentially `w'`-small, then so is `M`, so the refinement can in turn be fed back into the
construction of a point of the site and the lemma iterated.

Unlike `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.exists_refinement_of_ne` (Stacks 00YO), the covering
and the section are not fixed in advance: one refinement works for all of them at once.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_refinement_forall_covering_of_ne {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Small.{w'} C]
    [LocallySmall.{w'} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w}
    (hF : Presieve.IsSeparated J F)
    (hpb :
      ∀ {W : C} {ι : Type t} [Finite ι] {Y : ι → C} (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ W),
        Sieve.ofArrows Y g ∈ J W → ∀ (X : C) (h : X ⟶ W) (k : ι), HasPullback h (g k))
    {N : Type u₁} [SmallCategory N] [IsCofiltered N] [EssentiallySmall.{w'} N] (p : N ⥤ C) (j₀ : N)
    (a a' : F.obj (op (p.obj j₀)))
    (haa' : ∀ (j : N) (φ : j ⟶ j₀), F.map (p.map φ).op a ≠ F.map (p.map φ).op a') :
    ∃ (M : Type (max u₁ u v)) (_ : SmallCategory M) (_ : IsCofiltered M) (_ :
      EssentiallySmall.{w'} M) (q : M ⥤ C) (e : N ⥤ M) (_ : e.Full) (_ : e.Faithful) (ε :
      e ⋙ q ≅ p),
      (∀ (i : M) (ψ : i ⟶ e.obj j₀),
          F.map (q.map ψ ≫ ε.hom.app j₀).op a ≠ F.map (q.map ψ ≫ ε.hom.app j₀).op a') ∧
        ∀ {W : C} {ι : Type t} [Finite ι] {Y : ι → C} (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ W),
          Sieve.ofArrows Y g ∈ J W →
            ∀ (j : N) (f : p.obj j ⟶ W),
              ∃ (k : ι) (i : M) (ψ : i ⟶ e.obj j) (h : q.obj i ⟶ Y k),
                h ≫ g k = q.map ψ ≫ ε.hom.app j ≫ f
declarations.comment:
The main step of Deligne's criterion: a cofiltered system can be refined so as to
  keep two germs of a separated presheaf distinct while every section of `u'` becomes covered by
  every finite covering of the site.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasEnoughPoints_of_exists_finite_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YQ** (Deligne's criterion for the existence of enough points). Let `(C, J)` be a
site in which fibre products exist and in which every covering sieve `S` of an object `X` admits a
refinement by a finite covering — a finite family `g k : Y k ⟶ X` of morphisms of `S` which is
again a covering of `X`. Then the site has enough points: there is a small family of points of
`(C, J)` whose fibre functors jointly reflect isomorphisms of sheaves of sets.

The source asks for all finite limits in `C`; only the fibre products of the members of a finite
covering along an arbitrary morphism are used, whence `HasPullbacks C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasEnoughPoints_of_exists_finite_refinement {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    [HasPullbacks C] [Small.{w} C] [LocallySmall.{w} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J (Type w)]
    (h :
      ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Sieve X),
        S ∈ J X →
          ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Finite ι) (Y : ι → C) (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ X),
            Sieve.ofArrows Y g ≤ S ∧ Sieve.ofArrows Y g ∈ J X) :
    HasEnoughPoints.{w} J
declarations.comment:
Deligne's criterion: a site with fibre products in which every covering has a finite
  refinement has enough points.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringLeft
registrations.comment: `u^p F (U) = F(u U)` on presheaves, i.e. precomposition with `u.op`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes
declarations.doc:
On the small étale sites of the objects of `B` over `X`, inverse image along small étale base
change to any `T ⟶ X` commutes with passing from an abelian sheaf to its underlying sheaf of
sets.
declarations.statement: public theorem smallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor from abelian groups to sets, on the small étale sites over X: inverse image along small étale base change commutes with passing to the underlying sheaf of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_mateEquiv_sheafAdjunctionContinuous
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites, let `u : C ⥤ D` be continuous and representably flat —
the latter holds under the hypotheses of Stacks 00X6 — and let `s : A ⥤ B` be a functor such that
`A` and `B` have filtered colimits, `s` preserves them, `A`- and `B`-valued presheaves on `D` can
be sheafified, sheafification commutes with `s`, and an `A`-valued presheaf is a sheaf as soon as
its image under `s` is.

Then the pullback functor `f^{-1}` on `A`-valued sheaves commutes with postcomposition by `s`:
the mate, under the adjunction `f^{-1} ⊣ f_*`, of the identity square expressing that the
pushforward `f_* = u^s` is restriction along `u.op` on both sides, namely the canonical map
`f^{-1}(s ∘ F) ⟶ s ∘ (f^{-1} F)`, is an isomorphism.

For `B = Type u` and `s` the underlying-set functor of a type of algebraic structure, this says
that the pullback of sheaves of algebraic structures commutes with taking the underlying sheaf of
sets.

At the level of presheaves the corresponding assertion, that `u_p` commutes with postcomposition
by `s`, is `Functor.lanCompIsoOfPreserves` for `L = u.op`, which needs neither topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_mateEquiv_sheafAdjunctionContinuous {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) [u.IsContinuous J K] [RepresentablyFlat u] {A : Type w}
    [Category.{v} A] {B : Type w'} [Category.{v'} B] (s : A ⥤ B)
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{u, u} A] [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{u, u} B]
    [PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{u, u} s] [HasWeakSheafify K A] [HasWeakSheafify K B]
    [J.HasSheafCompose s] [K.HasSheafCompose s] [K.PreservesSheafification s] :
    IsIso
      ((mateEquiv (u.sheafAdjunctionContinuous A J K) (u.sheafAdjunctionContinuous B J K)).symm
          (TwoSquare.mk (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K) (sheafCompose K s) (sheafCompose J s)
            (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous B J K) (𝟙 _)))
declarations.comment:
The sheaf level, for an arbitrary `s : A ⥤ B`: for a continuous, representably flat
  `u : C ⥤ D` and a functor `s` preserving filtered colimits and sheafification, the pullback
  `f^{-1}` of `A`-valued sheaves commutes with postcomposition by `s`, in that the canonical mate
  `f^{-1}(s ∘ F) ⟶ s ∘ (f^{-1} F)` of the pushforward square is an isomorphism. The tag is the
  case `B = Type u`, `s` the underlying-set functor of a type of algebraic structure. The presheaf
  level, `u_p (F ⋙ s) ≅ (u_p F) ⋙ s`, is `lanCompIsoOfPreserves` at `L = u.op`, which mentions no
  topology.

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.AbelianVersusSets.uShriekAb
declarations.doc:
**Definition 4 (the functor `u_p^{ab}` on presheaves of abelian groups).**
The left adjoint of `u^p` on abelian presheaves, equivalently the left Kan
extension along `uᵒᵖ`; its pointwise value is the *same* colimit diagram, now
taken in `Ab`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def uShriekAb (u' : C ⥤ D) :
    (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤ (Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
declarations.comment:
`u_p^{ab}` is defined on abelian presheaves by the same colimits as `u_p` on
  presheaves of sets: both are the pointwise left Kan extension along `uᵒᵖ`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.AbelianVersusSets.uShriekAbAdjunction
declarations.doc:
Adjointness `u_p^{ab} ⊣ u^p` on presheaves of abelian groups (Stacks
Remark 00VF, and Stacks 00YU).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def uShriekAbAdjunction (u' : C ⥤ D) :
    uShriekAb u' ⊣ uPullbackAb u'
declarations.comment: `u_p^{ab}` is left adjoint to `u^p` on the categories of abelian presheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.AbelianVersusSets.exists_isMorphismOfSites_not_bijective_theta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YU (Remark 7.44.4).** Even for a continuous functor defining a morphism of sites,
`u_p^{ab}` need not agree with `u_p` on underlying presheaves of sets: there exist sites
`(C, J)` and `(D, K)`, a continuous functor `u : C ⥤ D` which defines a morphism of sites
(`u_s` exact, Stacks 00X1), a presheaf of abelian groups `F` on `C` and an object `V` of `D`
such that the comparison map `θ_{F,V} : (u_p F^set)(V) → (u_p^{ab} F)(V)` is not a bijection.

The witness is the empty functor from the empty category to the one-point category `PUnit`,
which carries the topology `⊤` in which the empty family covers the point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isMorphismOfSites_not_bijective_theta :
    ∃ (C D : Type) (_ : SmallCategory C) (_ : SmallCategory D)
      (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (u' : C ⥤ D),
      u'.IsMorphismOfSites J K ∧
        ∃ (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{0}) (V : Dᵒᵖ),
          ¬ Function.Bijective ((theta u' F).app V)
declarations.comment:
Under the remark's hypothesis: a continuous functor defining a morphism of
  sites for which `u_p^{ab}` does not agree with `u_p` on underlying sets.

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.toposAlgebraicStructureAdjunctions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YV.** Let `C`, `D` be sites and let `f = (f⁻¹, f_*)` be a morphism of topoi
`Sh(C) → Sh(D)`. Then `f` gives an adjoint pair of functors `(f⁻¹, f_*)` on sheaves of algebraic
structures compatible with taking the underlying sheaves of sets, for pointed sets, abelian
groups, groups, monoids, rings, modules over a fixed ring `R` and Lie algebras over a fixed field
`k`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposAlgebraicStructureAdjunctions
    (f : MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf J (Type u)) (Sheaf K (Type u))) (R : Type u) [Ring R]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] : AlgebraicStructureAdjunctions f R k
declarations.comment:
The adjoint pairs for the seven listed types, each compatible with the underlying
  sheaves of sets: the underlying sheaf of sets of `f⁻¹ F`, resp. `f_* G`, is `f⁻¹`, resp. `f_*`,
  of the underlying sheaf of sets, and the unit is the unit of `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*` on sheaves of sets.
  Rings are commutative rings; the module case is stated for an arbitrary ring `R`. The final
  assertion, (α)–(ζ) for each type, is `Stacks.Topos.algebraicStructureSheafification`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.algebraicStructureSheafification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YV, final assertion.** On any site, for each of the seven types of algebraic
structures of Stacks 00YV, the properties (α)–(ζ) of sheafification hold: a presheaf is a sheaf
if and only if its underlying presheaf of sets is; `P# = (P⁺)⁺` is a sheaf; sheafification
commutes with taking underlying presheaves of sets; `P ⟶ P#` is an isomorphism exactly when `P`
is a sheaf; sheafification is left adjoint to the inclusion; and sheafification is left exact.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def algebraicStructureSheafification (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Type u)
    [Ring R] (k : Type u) [Field k] : AlgebraicStructureSheafification J R k
declarations.comment:
The final assertion: (α)–(ζ) hold for each of the seven listed types, on any
  site (`Stacks.Sites.SheafificationProperties`). The adjoint pairs themselves are
  `Stacks.Topos.toposAlgebraicStructureAdjunctions`.

registrations.comment: a sieve on `U`, i.e. a subpresheaf of `h_U`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.downward_closed
registrations.comment:
the closure condition that makes a collection of arrows into `U` a sieve:

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.sieveSetEmbedding
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (1).** A sieve on `U` is a subpresheaf of `h_U`, so it is determined by the
family of subsets `{f : V ⟶ U | f ∈ S}` of `h_U(V) = Hom(V, U)`. Thus the collection of sieves on
`U` injects into `∏_V 𝒫(Hom(V, U))`, which is the source's proof that it is a set.
declarations.statement: def sieveSetEmbedding (U : C) : Sieve U ↪ ∀ V : C, Set (V ⟶ U)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.le_iff_forall_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (2).** The partial order on sieves on `U` is inclusion: `S ≤ T` holds exactly
when the subset of `Hom(V, U)` cut out by `S` is contained in the one cut out by `T`, for every
`V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_iff_forall_subset {S T : Sieve U} :
    S ≤ T ↔ ∀ V : C, sieveSetEmbedding U S V ⊆ sieveSetEmbedding U T V

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.iSup_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (3).** The union of a family of sieves on `U` is a sieve, namely their
supremum: an arrow lies in `⨆ i, S i` exactly when it lies in some `S i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_apply {I : Type w} (S : I → Sieve U) {V : C} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    (⨆ i, S i) f ↔ ∃ i, S i f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.iInf_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (3).** The intersection of a family of sieves on `U` is a sieve, namely their
infimum: an arrow lies in `⨅ i, S i` exactly when it lies in every `S i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iInf_apply {I : Type w} (S : I → Sieve U) {V : C} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    (⨅ i, S i) f ↔ ∀ i, S i f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.isLeast_ofArrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (4).** Given a family `{Y i ⟶ U}` of morphisms with target `U`, the sieve
`Sieve.ofArrows` it generates — the union of the images of the maps `h_{Y i} → h_U` — is the
smallest sieve on `U` containing every `f i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeast_ofArrows {I : Type w} (Y : I → C) (f : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ U) :
    IsLeast {S : Sieve U | ∀ i, S (f i)} (Sieve.ofArrows Y f)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.existsUnique_isLeast_arrows_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (4).** The smallest sieve on `U` containing a given family `{Y i ⟶ U}` of
morphisms with target `U` is unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isLeast_arrows_mem {I : Type w} (Y : I → C) (f : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ U) :
    ∃! S : Sieve U, IsLeast {S : Sieve U | ∀ i, S (f i)} S

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.isGreatest_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (5).** The sieve `h_U`, which contains every arrow with target `U`
(`CategoryTheory.Sieve.top_apply`), is the maximal sieve on `U`.
declarations.statement: theorem isGreatest_top : IsGreatest (Set.univ : Set (Sieve U)) ⊤

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sieve.isLeast_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00YZ (6).** The empty subpresheaf of `h_U`, which contains no arrow at all
(`CategoryTheory.Sieve.bot_apply`), is the minimal sieve on `U`.
declarations.statement: theorem isLeast_bot : IsLeast (Set.univ : Set (Sieve U)) ⊥

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.mem_finestTopology_of_forall_isSheafFor
registrations.comment:
Every sieve whose pullbacks along all V → U satisfy the sheaf condition for

declarations.name: IsSite.exists_topology_and_isSheaf_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZC.** Let `C` be a site with coverings `IsCov`. For `U : C`, let `J(U)` be the
set of sieves `S` on `U` such that some covering `{fᵢ : Uᵢ ⟶ U}` of the site generates a sieve
contained in `S`. Then (1) `J` is a Grothendieck topology on `C`, and (2) a presheaf of sets
is a sheaf for `J` if and only if it is a sheaf on the site, that is, for every covering the
fork `F(U) ⟶ ∏ F(Uᵢ) ⇉ ∏ F(Uᵢ ×_U Uⱼ)` is an equalizer (Stacks 00VM). The topology is
`IsSite.topology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_topology_and_isSheaf_iff (h : IsSite IsCov) :
    ∃ J : GrothendieckTopology C,
      (∀ (U : C) (S : Sieve U),
        S ∈ J U ↔ ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U, IsCov ⟨U, E⟩ ∧ Sieve.generate E.presieve₀ ≤ S) ∧
      ∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w,
        Presieve.IsSheaf J F ↔
          ∀ (𝒰 : Covering.{u, v, w} C) (h𝒰 : IsCov 𝒰),
            haveI := h.hasPairwisePullbacks h𝒰
            Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι (Equalizer.Presieve.Arrows.forkMap F 𝒰.2.X 𝒰.2.f)
              (Equalizer.Presieve.Arrows.w F 𝒰.2.X 𝒰.2.f)))
declarations.comment:
Both parts for a site as in 00VH (no fibre products assumed in `C`); the sheaf
  condition is the equalizer of 00VM. Mathlib's own 00ZC tag on `Pretopology.toGrothendieck`
  only names the topology of a pretopology in a category with all fibre products.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Coverage.toGrothendieck
registrations.comment:
the Grothendieck topology associated to a site, i.e. the smallest topology for
  which every covering of the site generates a covering sieve

declarations.name: statement1_map_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (1)**, identity law: restriction in `F⁺` along an identity arrow is the
identity, one half of `F⁺` being a presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1_map_id (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (U : Cᵒᵖ) :
    (J.plusObj F).map (𝟙 U) = 𝟙 ((J.plusObj F).obj U)

declarations.name: statement1_map_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (1)**, composition law: restricting in `F⁺` along `f ≫ g` is restricting
along `f` and then along `g`, the other half of `F⁺` being a presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1_map_comp (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    {U V W : Cᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V) (g : V ⟶ W) :
    (J.plusObj F).map (f ≫ g) = (J.plusObj F).map f ≫ (J.plusObj F).map g

declarations.name: statement2_ell_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (2)**: `ℓ : F ⟶ F⁺` is a morphism of presheaves, i.e. its components commute
with restriction along any arrow `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2_ell_natural (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) {U V : Cᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    F.map f ≫ (J.toPlus F).app V = (J.toPlus F).app U ≫ (J.plusObj F).map f

declarations.name: statement3a_map_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (3)**, identity law for `F ↦ F⁺` as an operation on presheaves:
`(𝟙 F)⁺ = 𝟙 F⁺`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement3a_map_id (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) :
    (J.plusFunctor (Type u)).map (𝟙 F) = 𝟙 ((J.plusFunctor (Type u)).obj F)

declarations.name: statement3a_map_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (3)**, composition law for `F ↦ F⁺` as an operation on presheaves:
`(α ≫ β)⁺ = α⁺ ≫ β⁺`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement3a_map_comp {F G H : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H) :
    (J.plusFunctor (Type u)).map (α ≫ β) =
      (J.plusFunctor (Type u)).map α ≫ (J.plusFunctor (Type u)).map β

declarations.name: statement3b_ell_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (3)**, naturality of `ℓ` in the presheaf variable: the square
`α ≫ ℓ G = ℓ F ≫ α⁺` commutes, so `ℓ` is a natural transformation `𝟭 ⟶ plusFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement3b_ell_natural {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (α : F ⟶ G) :
    α ≫ J.toPlus G = J.toPlus F ≫ J.plusMap α

declarations.name: statement4_preserves_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (4)**: if `α : F ⟶ G` is injective on sections over every object, then so is
`α⁺`. The sections of `F⁺` over `U` form a filtered colimit of multiequalizers, and
injectivity survives both `diagramNatTrans` and the filtered colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement4_preserves_mono
    {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (α : F ⟶ G)
    (hα : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (α.app U)) :
    ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective ((J.plusMap α).app U)

declarations.name: statement5_local_representability
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZH (5)**: every section `s` of `F⁺` over `U` is locally in the image of `ℓ` —
there is a covering sieve `S ∈ J U` and a `φ : S.functor ⟶ F` with `φ ≫ J.toPlus F` equal to the
restriction of `s` to `S`, expressed via `S.functorInclusion` and `yonedaEquiv.symm s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement5_local_representability
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (U : C) (s : (J.plusObj F).obj (op U)) :
    ∃ (S : Sieve U) (_ : S ∈ J U) (φ : S.functor ⟶ F),
      φ ≫ J.toPlus F =
        S.functorInclusion ≫ (CategoryTheory.yonedaEquiv.symm s)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.existsUnique_toSheafify_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
The universal property of the sheaf `F^# = L L F` associated to a presheaf of sets `F`:
every map `φ : F ⟶ G` into a sheaf of sets `G` factors uniquely through the canonical map
`F ⟶ F^#`, i.e. there is a unique `ψ : F^# ⟶ G` with `(F ⟶ F^#) ≫ ψ = φ`.

Here `J.sheafify F` is by definition `J.plusObj (J.plusObj F)`, the plus construction applied
twice, and `J.toSheafify F` is the canonical map; the factorization is Mathlib's
`GrothendieckTopology.sheafifyLift`, with `toSheafify_sheafifyLift` and `sheafifyLift_unique`.

declarations.name: sieve_sheafification_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZO.** A sieve `S` on `U` is a covering sieve for the topology `J` if and only if
the sheafification `S^# ⟶ h_U^#` of its inclusion `S ↪ h_U` (i.e. the image under the
associated-sheaf functor of `S.functorInclusion`) is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem sieve_sheafification_iff {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (U : C) (S : Sieve U) :
    S ∈ J U ↔ IsIso ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).map S.functorInclusion)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.topology_eq_iff_same_sheaves
registrations.comment:
two topologies are equal exactly when they have the same `Type`-valued
  sheaves

declarations.name: le_iff_isSheaf_imp_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZQ.** For Grothendieck topologies `J`, `J'` on a category `C`, we have `J ≤ J'`
(every `J`-covering sieve is `J'`-covering) if and only if every sheaf for `J'` is a sheaf
for `J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_iff_isSheaf_imp_isSheaf :
    J ≤ J' ↔
      ∀ (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u v)),
        Presheaf.IsSheaf J' P → Presheaf.IsSheaf J P

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsPointOfTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 00ZT.** A *point of the topology* `J` on `C` is a functor `u : C ⥤ Type w` such
that

1. for every covering sieve `S` on `U`, the map `S_p → (h_U)_p` induced on stalks by the
   inclusion `S ⟶ h_U` is surjective;
2. the stalk functor `Sh(C) ⥤ Sets`, `F ↦ F_p`, on sheaves of sets `Type w`, is exact: it
   commutes with finite limits and with finite colimits (Stacks 0034).

The stalk is `Functor.pointStalk u`, the colimit over the neighbourhoods of `p = u`.
declarations.statement: structure IsPointOfTopology (u : C ⥤ Type w) : Prop
declarations.comment:
Stacks' definition of a point of a topology, on `u : C ⥤ Type w` with the
  stalk taken as the colimit over the category of elements of `u`; a Mathlib point gives one,
  see `GrothendieckTopology.Point.isPointOfTopology`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.factors_through_zero_iff_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `Z` is a zero object, then a morphism `α : y ⟶ z` factors through `Z` if
and only if `α = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem factors_through_zero_iff_eq_zero
    (Z : C) (hZ : Limits.IsZero Z) {y z : C} (α : y ⟶ z) :
    (∃ (f : y ⟶ Z) (g : Z ⟶ z), α = f ≫ g) ↔ α = 0
declarations.comment: part 2
